title: Conditional κ = 0.001593667716067094: two compatible cold kernels in all 72 calls
body:
Raises the conditional bound from [PR564](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/564)'s **κ = 0.001593134158181640** to **κ = 0.001593667716067094**, an improvement of **0.03349108314035%**. The native complex rate is **b = 0.001596211546877366844000**. The separately checked conservative complex model gives κ = 0.001593667713327391, also above PR564.

The change adds a compatible second cold kernel on helper 294 after reconstructing PR564's first kernel on helper 270. Its suffix relation is recomputed on the already modified word, and cleanup is rebuilt. All 72 calls use actual zero/four/eight-promotion providers with the existing 15/2/55 dispatch. A literal reassignment changes 798 of 36,288 owner records; live stock remains 7168 and physical stock 7682. The complete paid profile is:

```text
{1:166640,2:31072,3:35604,4:13696,5:4032,6:4032,
 7:136,8:576,12:1,48:1675}
```

The verifier reconstructs all scalar words, dirty-helper restoration, reflected frame ledgers, exact phases and wrappers, then checks the owner schedule and a fresh finite invoice. It charges all 4,168 positive idle remainders, including the rank-12 child. Generated-artifact identities tolerate gzip serialization differences while retaining fresh raw-hash bindings and every mathematical field.

**Validation:** two independent clean reconstructions of the same source manifest passed all 47 stages each on Windows Python 3.14 and Linux Python 3.12. Both produce the exact native and conservative results above. This covers both reflected operators and dirty-helper restoration, all phase edges and endpoint adapters, 17 controller mutants, 57 malformed-admission controls, seven bootstrap levels and all 47 strict outer constraints. Both rational moment engines reject the adjacent supplier endpoint. Compression controls accept equivalent recompressions and reject altered proof contents or stale references.

All 18 required repository baseline groups also passed, including the Gen4 bank construction, after the documented SymPy-version, compiler-header and Git-worktree environment corrections. Initial failed attempts and their successful recoveries are preserved. Source-bound receipts, environment details and stage logs are in `research/complex-doublecold-validation/`. A Python 3.11/3.14 Linux CI workflow is included.

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-doublecold/verify.py --work /tmp/doublecold-replay
```

The result retains the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, analytic-transfer and bit H1–H5 assumptions. [PR543](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/543) remains the cited bit supplier; its pinned profile is repriced. This is conditional finite evidence, with no unconditional theorem or practical-speed claim.

Credits: PR564 and its PR561/PR562/PR558 ancestry supply the retained construction; [Rohan Arun's PR559](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/559) supplies the native exact-cover recurrence. title: Conditional κ = 0.001596133352130093: seven more cold-kernel helpers on PR564
body:
## Summary

This is a small extension of eumemic's PR564. It raises the conditional κ from 0.001593134158181640 to **0.001596133352130093** (+2.999e-6). Nearly all of the construction and all of the verification machinery come from the earlier PRs credited below.

PR564 (following PR561) makes one width-nine helper per complex call "cold". An exact dyadic donor relation cancels its dirty response, so it enters at rank one and its residual width drops from nine to eight. This PR finds **seven more such helpers per provider**, for eight in total. Then it re-solves the owner packing for the new width inventory. Most of the gain comes from the repacking, as in PR564.

This PR adds a single self-contained package, `research/complex-multicold/`, on top of current `main`. It vendors PR558 and PR559 unchanged, as PR564 does. Its new and changed parts relative to PR564's `research/complex-allcold/` are these 16 files:
- **New:**
  - `code/build_multicut_kernels.py`
  - `code/audit_multicold_controls.py`
  - `data/{ZERO,FOUR,EIGHT}-MULTICOLD.json`
- **Changed:**
  - `verify.py`
  - `code/assemble.py`
  - `code/assembly_controls.py`
  - `code/audit_allcold.py`
  - `code/bind_providers_portable.py`
  - `data/OWNERS.json.gz`
  - `data/PLAN.json`
  - `proof/CONSTRUCTION.md`
  - `README.md`, `NOTICE.md`, `MANIFEST.json`

All other files are byte-identical to PR564's package.

## Construction

A B-first width-nine helper is untouched before its first original gate. Up to that point it holds only its initial dirt. Its cancelling gates `donor += -q·pivot @E` can therefore sit at **different cuts**, with each donor at a cut where its frame fits (cur ⊆ E ⊆ next). The dirty response is zero exactly when the sum, over donors, of q times that donor's suffix column at its cut equals the pivot's column. PR564's search used a single cut and finds no new relations. The multi-cut search finds seven:

- **Helper-donor kernels:** helpers 282, 294 and 306 (registers 506@[24], 518@[30], 530@[30]). Local profile delta: `{1:+1,2:+2,3:-2}`.
- **Target-donor kernels:** helpers 271, 283, 295 and 307 (registers 495@[24], 507@[24], 519@[30], 531@[30]). These are placed only after the centre scatter, mirroring the post-centre gauge compensation. Local profile delta: `{1:+3,2:+1,3:-2}`.

Each of the 16 post-centre helpers needs one specific partner as its split donor. They pair up as (494,566), (506,578), (518,542), (530,554), (495,567), (507,579), (519,543) and (531,555). So this family supports at most eight cold helpers per word. We found no kernel by any of these mechanisms for the 276 helpers first touched before the centre.

**Overlap with PR567.** PR567 (jon314159), opened shortly before this PR, independently found one of these seven kernels: helper 294 (register 518@[30], split donor 542). It places that kernel at a single cut, where we use multiple cuts. The other six kernels and the eight-helper owner repacking are not in PR567.


PR562's 15/2/55 dispatch is unchanged. The width inventory becomes `{4:p,5:56-p,8:164,9:284}`. The owner assignment was found as follows:
- an aggregate CP-SAT model with per-call Hall conditions, adapted from higherbeing's open allocator;
- then a per-pattern Kőnig edge colouring, as in the existing `partial-own-coordinated` script.

Neither tool is an admission dependency; the verifier checks the literal assignment. The idle profile is `{1:93,2:93,3:2118,7:1,48:1713}`, compared with PR564's `{3:2364,7:172,48:1668}`.

The paid profile is `{1:167741,2:31741,3:34502,4:13696,5:4032,6:4032,7:1,8:576,48:1713}`. The figures are: live stock 7168, physical stock 7682, rank mass 520704, deficit 2560. The complex rate is b = 0.00159868506668458107128. eumemic's unchanged PR543 bit supplier gives c = 0.001653826988146798944268, so the complex side binds. A conservative complex model gives κ = 0.001596133349380077.

## Verification methodology

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-multicold/verify.py --work /tmp/multicold-replay
```

The verifier is PR564's, extended to cover the new kernels. It uses the standard library only, and assertions must stay enabled. In order, it:
1. Rebuilds frozen PR558, the four-pivot source and PR564's three one-cold words, with their cold-kernel omission controls.
2. Applies the seven multi-cut kernels to each provider word. It checks:
   - exact zero dirty response by forward replay;
   - legal frame chains;
   - the pinned profile delta.
   It runs 32 omission controls per provider: every new gate alone and every whole kernel, in both orientations. Each must fail.
3. Re-runs the inherited 44-kernel and promotion omission audits on each final word, then checks:
   - all 728 scalar columns in both orientations;
   - all 504 dirty helpers restored;
   - both reflected ledgers;
   - all 2929 phase edges and 224 endpoint adapters per provider;
   - the normalized wrappers.
4. Binds the three providers and checks the physical owner assignment:
   - all 36,288 helpers have a single whole owner;
   - 3,209 chart types;
   - 27,679 cross-replica roles;
   - 4,018 idle remainders;
   - 16 controller mutants, each of which must be rejected.
5. Emits a fresh invoice and runs both exact assembly models with 54 malformed-receipt controls. Two rational moment engines reject the adjacent supplier endpoint. It also runs seven bootstrap levels and 47 strict outer inequalities, with next-grid and parameter controls.

## Verification results

All runs were local, on Windows with Python 3.11.

| Run | Tree | Status | κ | Steps | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | stacked on PR564 (`aa70965`) | `PASS_THREE_PROVIDER_048_MULTICOLD_NATIVE_COMPLEX_AND_CITED_BIT` | 1596133352130093/10^18 | 42/42 exit 0 | 357 s |
| 2 | same package, independent worktree | same PASS | same | 42/42 exit 0 | 356 s |
| 3 | this PR's tree (`main` `db0e57b` + `71c99ac`) | same PASS, process exit 0 | 1596133352130093/10^18 | 42/42 exit 0 | 353 s |

The paid profile in every run equals the one stated above. GitHub CI has not run, and I make no claim about it.

## Credits

This builds directly on:
- **eumemic**:
  - PR564 (all-call cold kernels, `c18417b`), the base of this work.
  - PR561 (the cold-kernel idea).
  - PR562 (zero/four/eight providers and owners).
  - PR558 (rank-five pivots).
  - PR550 (rank-five trace expansion).
  - PR543 (bit supplier, cited).
  - PR507 (partial-own factory).
- **jon314159**: PR567 (independently found the register-518 cold kernel, posted first).
- **rohanarun**: PR559 (native complex moment).
- **Dugongue**: PR552 (collective hyperplane waves) and PR514 (asynchronous whole owners).
- **chafreaky**: PR551 (subspace16 complex).
- **icekylinx**: PR535 (post-centre rank-four kernels), PR531, and the compiler and controller.
- **DreamingOfClouds**: PR484 (shared-donor kernels and entrance gauges).
- **higherbeing**: the open allocator.
- **lydakis**: PR275 (finite assembly and E8 verification).
- **Douglas Colkitt / CrocSwap**: maintenance and the review framework.
- **The authors of the original OpenAI #109 framework**, on which all of this is conditional.

All vendored packages, notices, licenses and AI disclosures are unchanged.

**AI disclosure and authorship:** Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), running in the omp coding harness, did the work for this PR. A small team of Claude agents found the seven multi-cut kernels, wrote the constructor and omission audit, solved the new owner assignment, built and verified the package, and drafted this description. Jeremy Kothe (jeremykothe2) directed and reviewed the work and is submitting it.

## Scope

The result is conditional on the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape/exact recovery, analytic transfer and the bit H1–H5 assumptions. It is finite exact evidence. It is not an unconditional theorem, a complete Lean proof, or a practical speedup.

title: [Lean] Compute a binary ceiling-log parameter on explicit tapes
body:
# A binary ceiling-log parameter on explicit tapes

This package adds two unchanged accepted Lean sources, `BinaryCeilLogTokens.lean` and `BinaryParameterCount.lean`. A five-state, two-tape machine scans a binary word into zero tokens. A concrete fifteen-state, three-tape machine then counts those tokens into an actual binary record. On normalized input the stored number is the least natural exponent whose power of two bounds the represented value. Fourteen external sources retain their immutable PR origins.

## Exact physical and numeric contracts

For an arbitrary finite Boolean word w, let m=w.length and

b=w.dropLast.length + indicator(w.dropLast.any id).

The token machine starts with canonical Tape.ofWord w and one pristine blank tape. In exactly m+1 elapsed transitions it reaches halted state 4 with input <w.reverse.map bitSymbol,blank,[]> and token tape <replicate b zero,blank,[]>. The output head is at the represented right blank. This exact elapsed identity does not assert first completion.

The binary-parameter machine starts with canonical Tape.ofWord w on slot 0 and pristine Tape.blank on slots 1 and 2. One actual tape-preserving bridge joins the scan to the unchanged automatic-width counter. At some t<=13m+6 it reaches halted state 14. Let u=replicate b false and r=(CarryTape.pass b (replicate b false)).1. The complete final tapes are:

- Slot 0: <w.reverse.map bitSymbol,blank,[]>.
- Slot 1: <u.reverse.map bitSymbol ++ [blank],blank,[]>.
- Slot 2: <[],blank,r.map bitSymbol ++ [blank]>.

The counter bits satisfy r.length=b and wordValue r=b. This is a marked width-b binary record with the head at its home blank, not a canonical compact representation of b. The source ends at its right blank; the token tape also ends at its right blank, retaining the additional represented left blank. The record's home and end blanks are distinct represented cells, including b=0. The theorem gives an existential elapsed upper bound; no first-halting-time claim is made.

Numeric identification uses w=compact bits and v=wordValue bits. The accepted facts identify the stored value with ceilLog2 v and prove, for every natural k,

b<=k if and only if v<=2^k.

The explicit definition is ceilLog2 0=0; for positive v it is v.log2 plus zero when v=2^(v.log2), and one otherwise. Thus zero and one produce b=0, powers of two have their exact exponent, and other positive values use the next exponent. Positive canonical bit length is not silently substituted for this ceiling parameter. The physical theorems hold for arbitrary words; the ceiling identification is only for normalized input. For example the noncanonical word [false,false] emits one token although its numeric value is zero.

For empty input, slot 0 remains the canonical blank, while slot 1 is <[blank],blank,[]> and slot 2 is <[],blank,[blank]>. A normalized one also produces the width-zero marked record. No singleton-zero output encoding is introduced.

## Reuse and verification boundary

The sixteen-source scientific closure has 122 complete standard-only axiom probes, with 28 in the two included sources. The accepted token check took 3.619026548 compiler seconds and 1,730,854,912 bytes peak VM. The binary-parameter machine passed its first check in 3.545301435 seconds with 1,774,333,952 bytes peak VM. These are historical research checks. The token module's preserved initial ordinary elaboration failure is not accepted evidence.

The public reproduction passed after verifying and retaining PR526's twelve exact public outputs, PR565's physical-copy output and PR566's numeric-normalization output, then freshly checking only these two new sources. The two fresh checks used 4.468479126 compiler seconds and 0.001146350 FIFO seconds, with peak VM 1,774,305,280 bytes. All sixteen reference objects and full logs match exactly, and all 122 complete probes pass. REPLAY_SUMMARY.json records this fourteen-retained/two-fresh measurement; its accumulated records are not one fresh sixteen-source replay.

PR488 supplies the two explicit-model foundations; PR511 supplies the carry/dispatcher interfaces; PR519 supplies automatic width allocation/counting; PR526 supplies the PR64 arithmetic transport and accepted 12n+4 counter bound. PR565 already proves the physical compact copy. PR566 already proves numeric compact normalization and the six-tape preparation/count/copy composition. This package consumes only PR566's normalization module. It does not include or republish BinaryPreparedCompactCount, BinaryPreparedInputCount, BinaryInputPreparation or BinaryWordReversal. Its new contribution is the actual lookahead-token table and the token-to-binary-counter handoff. No new generic counter, potential or logarithm theory is asserted.

Immutable dependencies include PR565 at b5766e15ab1c9f5c86e994aa7754a7750c6af76c and PR566 at 86d39f3247a5a1df4f040ed71d8251bed77b91ec. Repaired branch heads are not substituted, and no merger is assumed. DEPENDENCIES.json gives all six source-package origins and exact paths.

The public arithmetic dependency is PR526's reviewed CounterArithmeticPure public variant, with a 1,092-byte attribution/modification comment relative to the research source. Its public object is separately accepted and differs from the research object. The public reproduction retained that exact public artifact and independently measured both new objects against their research references. PR64 attribution, Apache-2.0 LICENSE and applicable NOTICE remain explicit through the unchanged dependencies.

EXTERNAL_OBJECTS_REFERENCE.json points directly to PR526's exact 797,008-byte runtime inventory; this package does not duplicate it or require PR530 solely for that inventory. The unchanged external closure has 1,366 nodes: 1,300 official Lean core modules and 66 cached Mathlib/dependency nodes. No download, import expansion or dependency rebuild is proposed. Central reproduction tooling must retain the established 60-second/4-GiB hard limits and 40-second/3.5-GiB review stops.

The separately accepted Nat.clog equality is outside this package. Including it would add one API fact and expand the combined closure by 256 external nodes, without changing the physical endpoint. The wider literal Real.logb ceiling bridge and the 48-state/eight-tape two-operand composition are also separate. This package begins with one canonical record and two pristine work tapes; it does not claim the selected one-string x#y caller, physical p=6b setup, source-specific parameter-record/head layout, compact-b output, radix/carry Plan, represented-list Gaussian Budget or a multiplier theorem.

## Author-checked conditional project context

At pinned selected-result context f19cb621be2caf3a7291a37c343c1c55afe935e0, certificates/selected-result.json reports

kappa = 1517760977820331 / 1000000000000000000 = 0.001517760977820331.

The author checked this exact rational/decimal equality and the selected-result-to-research/community-pr531-audit/direct-ASSEMBLY.json hash linkage. The intended publication-base pin is db0e57bc7f36b5ac0fc844ad7ce1396165ee6647, as reported by the publisher. The f19 selected record and delivered proof/review packet retain all-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-basis, normalized residual realization, correlated whole-owner hosting, restored-row, precision/tape and analytic-transfer interfaces. Reported finite-package replays are source-attributed; they are not a local replay or proof of the selected construction. The delivered text does not supply a selected scalar caller/parameter-record/head layout.

Both generic modules are independent of kappa and establish no multiplier or kappa theorem. This explicit parameter is conditional project context only. The prior 12a/4d source contexts and accepted research history remain preserved; no later selected hypothesis is imported into these proofs.

## Repository checks and AI disclosure

Substantial AI assistance was used to develop and check this contribution. Exact accepted sources, full axiom probes, predecessor attribution and independent reviews are retained. These two sources and their dependency bytes are unchanged; this packet adds no upstream source, generator or certificate repair.

The affected public Lean measurement passed the guarded 14-retained/2-fresh sequence described above. Current CONTRIBUTING requirements also include make verify and make gen4-bank-verify. Their exact new-publication-head results must be recorded separately. Historical research checks and predecessor reproductions are not fresh repository-wide aggregate results; no aggregate PASS is claimed here.

## Offline reproduction

The supported fresh sixteen-source command requires the six exact dependency packages in DEPENDENCIES.json, official Lean 4.21.0 and an already-built Mathlib checkout at 308445d7985027f538e281e18df29ca16ede2ba3. From this flat package directory:

```sh
python3 check.py --lean /path/to/lean-4.21.0-linux/bin/lean \
  --mathlib-root /path/to/mathlib4 \
  --input-foundation-root /path/to/PR488/research/lean-binary-input-preparation \
  --dispatcher-foundation-root /path/to/PR511/research/lean-binary-count-dispatcher \
  --automatic-width-root /path/to/PR519/research/lean-automatic-width-count \
  --amortization-root /path/to/PR526/research/lean-count-receipt-amortization \
  --compact-copy-root /path/to/PR565/research/lean-compact-counter-copy \
  --prepared-compact-root /path/to/PR566/research/lean-prepared-compact-count \

```

The build directory must not exist. The checker validates the exact PR526 runtime-manifest reference, its 797,008 bytes and all 1,366 runtime source/object/import rows with first-match resolution. It validates all sixteen proof source hashes, sizes and imports, copies sources into a fresh isolated directory, and permits only its fresh object directory plus eight validated cache paths in Lean's search path. No dependency download or rebuild is performed. Inherited Lean paths/sysroot are ignored. Every receipt/full log and all 122 expected standard-only probes are retained. Hard caps are 60 seconds/4 GiB per root, with review stops at 40 seconds/3.5 GiB. An optional existing --slot-service supplies FIFO admission without changing proof inputs.

The approved measurement instead retains and verifies PR526's twelve public outputs, PR565's compact-copy output and PR566's normalization output, then checks only BinaryCeilLogTokens followed by BinaryParameterCount. That fourteen-retained/two-fresh sequence passed, with complete source/object/receipt/log identities and the shared runtime inventory verified before and after the two fresh checks. Its accumulated reference records are distinct from running the supported fresh sixteen-source command above.

This PR additionally carries the one-entry mixed-point source-provenance correction already reviewed in PR565 (commit 890b2906). It updates only the rational_span_frames.py digest; mathematical certificate data and scripts are unchanged. On exact candidate 9278e39baec4f23267336c7d212306d0c0003d08, the scoped static provenance preflight matched 204/204 declared checks, and make -j1 verify-research passed all 28 auditors under Python 3.13.5 with byte-identical regenerated certificates and clean tracked/untracked state. The scientific run took 598.877 seconds under the reviewed 35-minute wall and 4-GiB per-process address-space limits. title: [Lean] Connect eight-tape parameter setup to the real ceiling logarithm
body:
# Prepared binary parameters with a real-ceiling identity

This package adds four unchanged accepted Lean sources. `BinaryPreparedParameters.lean` supplies the actual forty-eight-state, eight-tape composition of the previously published preparation/compact-count and binary-parameter machines. `BinaryCeilLogNatBinding.lean`, `BinaryCeilLogRealBinding.lean` and `BinaryPreparedParametersRealBinding.lean` reuse installed logarithm APIs and attach their identities to that same execution. Twenty public predecessor sources retain their immutable origins; none is republished here.

## Entry, full endpoint and time bound

Let x and y be arbitrary finite Boolean operand words, n=max(x.length,y.length), w=widthBits x y, m=w.length and b=ceilLog2 n. Bits are little-endian under the explicit model's wordValue. Entry is canonical Tape.ofWord x on slot0, Tape.ofWord y on slot1, and pristine Tape.blank on slots2 through7. No arbitrary initial work-tape contents are admitted.

The machine starts in state0. The accepted six-tape prepared compact count runs on slots0 through5; one actual halt-interception transition then runs the accepted three-tape binary-parameter machine on slots5 through7. Slots0 through4 are preserved during this second phase with their actual first-phase endpoint footprints. They are not asserted to remain equal to their original entry tapes.

At some elapsed t<=22*n+13*m+24<=35*n+24 the machine reaches the exact finalConfiguration x y, halted in state47. These are existential elapsed upper bounds, not a first-completion or exact elapsed-count claim.

Write L=leftPad x y and R=rightPad x y for the accepted equal-length zero-padded operand lists, and r=parameterBits x y. Using <left,head,right> for the explicit finite tape, the complete final slots are:

- Slot0: BinaryWordReversal.finalInput L.
- Slot1: BinaryWordReversal.finalInput R.
- Slot2: <L.map bitSymbol ++ [blank],blank,[]>.
- Slot3: <R.map bitSymbol,blank,[]>.
- Slot4: <[],blank,w.map bitSymbol ++ replicate (n-m+1) blank>.
- Slot5: <w.reverse.map bitSymbol,blank,[]>.
- Slot6: <(replicate b false).reverse.map bitSymbol ++ [blank],blank,[]>.
- Slot7: <[],blank,r.map bitSymbol ++ [blank]>.

The reversal's finalInput definition fixes the represented boundary cells on slots0/1; no quotient by trailing blanks is used. The normalized n record w has value n, is empty when n=0, and otherwise has length n.log2+1. Its length is at most n. In the final configuration its head has been scanned to the right blank on slot5. The parameter record r has both length b and value b. It is a marked-home width-b binary record, not a compact binary-b output. Both its home and end blanks are represented, including b=0. The retained slot4 footprint is not shrunk by clearing cells.

For x=y=[], w=[] and r=[]. Visited blanks on the other tapes are retained exactly by the endpoint definitions; this is not a claim that all eight tapes are canonical blanks. Width one also gives b=0. No singleton-zero word is introduced.

## Exact logarithm interface

The published PR570 token theorem already supplies the least-power characterization. The new Nat adapter reuses the installed Mathlib theorem to identify tokenCount(compact bits) with Nat.clog 2 (wordValue bits), without a new logarithm induction or numeric hypothesis.

The Real adapter then reuses Real.natCeil_logb_natCast. For every width n, the stored b equals the natural ceiling of Real.logb (2 : Nat) (n : Real), under the library's explicit zero extension. For 0<n, the stored b cast to Int equals the integer ceiling of that same real logarithm. Zero and one are explicitly recorded as b=0. At powers of two the exact exponent is used; positive binary length is not substituted for the ceiling.

The final two run theorems conjoin the exact existing physical endpoint and t<=35*n+24 with, respectively, the totalized natural-ceiling identity or the integer-ceiling identity under the explicit premise 0<n. The three adapter sources do not alter the machine, entry, endpoint, assumptions on work tapes, or time bound. The positive hypothesis belongs to the integer-ceiling statement; it is not silently added to the underlying physical run.

## New contribution and predecessor overlap

PR565 already publishes the physical compact-copy helper. PR566 already publishes compact value/length normalization and the six-tape prepared compact-n count. PR570 already publishes the five-state token scan/least-power certificate and fifteen-state binary-b machine. This package reuses those bytes as exact external dependencies. Its new physical contribution is their real eight-tape handoff from two operands plus six pristine tapes. Its remaining three sources provide the thin Nat.clog/Real.logb API transport and the full physical/Real identity join.

PR488 supplies reversal, input preparation and the two explicit-model foundations; PR511 supplies carry/dispatcher interfaces; PR519 supplies width allocation/counting; PR526 supplies the PR64 arithmetic transport and 12n+4 count bound; PR530 supplies the five-tape prepared count. All eight immutable source-package origins are listed in DEPENDENCIES.json. In particular PR565 remains pinned to b5766e15ab1c9f5c86e994aa7754a7750c6af76c, PR566 to 86d39f3247a5a1df4f040ed71d8251bed77b91ec, and PR570 to 9278e39baec4f23267336c7d212306d0c0003d08. Later repaired branch heads are not substituted and no merger is assumed.

The public arithmetic dependency is PR526's already reviewed CounterArithmeticPure variant 7fea5026, whose 1,092-byte attribution/modification notice differs from the accepted research source 1ad26524. Its public object fbeef132 and research object 3d3ef802 are intentionally distinct. The retained public prefix uses the public object; all four newly included roots have now passed their isolated reproduction against that exact prefix, with object bytes identical to their research references. No new generic counter, amortization potential, normalization or real-logarithm theory is claimed. Apache-2.0 LICENSE and applicable NOTICE, including predecessor attribution, are retained.

## Exact source and verification boundary

The complete closure contains 24 proof sources, 256,978 source bytes and 194 complete standard-only axiom probes. These four included files total 27,934 bytes and 33 probes. The 20 public reference outputs contribute 161 probes. The accepted research passes used only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, with some facts axiom-free. The Nat adapter's first name-resolution failure is preserved in development evidence and is not accepted evidence; the included file is the accepted repaired source.

title: Document exact lookup for triple-line source complements
body:
## Scope

This adds a computer-assisted, exact-rational lookup result for the one-line and intersection-one two-line triple complements in the original OpenAI manuscript preserved in the repository Douglas Colkitt maintains. Its motif section credits the underlying degree-one intersection construction to Alon. A paper adjacent-exterior contraction reduces every valid ordered elimination to one of 1,936 support/gap skeletons of height at most 11. The included standard-library checker enumerates those normal forms exactly and verifies a fixed table of 20 matrix values and 17 nonzero operation coefficients. The reference has `h-r` pivots in `h` row iterations, including every valid `h=100` source instance.

The note derives the correct coefficient `(3*1_{j in L}-1)/6` from `G=I-J/9`, proves the all-retained-row contraction at complete pivot blocks, and distinguishes the paper induction from the finite certificate. It credits the upstream source form and records a bounded current-source overlap check, with no priority claim. The local Tintagel audit packet is unpublished provenance; the proof and checker needed for the scoped claim are in this PR. The patch was prepared with substantial AI assistance.

python3 -I -B research/tintagel-source-lookup/replay.py --stress

The all-height claim rests on a paper induction plus finite computation; the induction is not mechanically checked. title: [Lean] Verify selected rational certificate arithmetic
body:
# Selected rational certificate arithmetic

Five unchanged, kernel-checked Lean sources reconstruct finite rational calculations from the pinned f19 PR531 `direct-ASSEMBLY.json` and its source engines. The package checks 34 complete axiom probes. Its contribution is a source-bound finite certificate bridge, not a new multiplication algorithm or an all-size analytic theorem.

## Explicit author-checked conditional parameter

The selected source context is commit `f19cb621be2caf3a7291a37c343c1c55afe935e0`. Its exact conditional project value is

`κ = 1517760977820331 / 1000000000000000000 = 0.001517760977820331`.

The author checked this rational/decimal identity and the linkage from `certificates/selected-result.json` (SHA256 `0bca96caf2da6fe14c3f69b0560b6185de1c8238d2b361dec8e9786c91f585ed`) to `research/community-pr531-audit/direct-ASSEMBLY.json` (SHA256 `b352aad19ea2f23d70f9913e497b2588d7352d68816bf201cbc35bba2aa71698`). The intended publication base is separately pinned to `db0e57bc7f36b5ac0fc844ad7ce1396165ee6647`.

This package proves exact rational comparisons involving that κ. It does not establish the full integer-multiplication theorem at κ. The selected construction's operator, realization, precision/tape, common-label/mutable-basis, hosting, compiler and all-size transfer conditions remain separate.

## Checked finite statements

1. **Final grid.** `SelectedOuterGridCertificate` evaluates the source q formula and compact-layer slack, then proves `κ < selectedMargin ≤ κ + 10⁻¹⁸`. The upper inequality is the strict-margin failure at the next grid tick. This module initially names the recorded bootstrap endpoint; the bootstrap module below derives that same endpoint.
2. **Log-expression checkpoints.** `SelectedMomentLogCheckpoints` connects 50 contiguous eight-term checkpoint transitions to five complete 80-term rational expressions at z = 1/3, 9/137, 25/121, 33/113 and 17/129. These are exact finite sums with the source's rational tail expressions. No Real logarithm enclosure is asserted.
3. **Nine-profile aggregation.** `SelectedMomentUpperAggregate` reuses those exact expressions, checks the source domains and binary-reduction data, and connects 27 four-step exponential recurrence checkpoints to the nine source tail expressions. The profile counts sum to 256,224; the rank-one fallback count is exactly `32 × 73² × 256224 = 43,693,366,272`. Rounding is kept in source order: each combined log expression is rounded on the 10³⁰ grid; the ordinary nine-profile sum and the fallback are then ceiling-rounded separately; only the fallback is scaled by 10⁻¹⁶. For the supplied `bMinus = 304013615566499291631 / 200000000000000000000000`, the resulting rational `selectedUpper` satisfies

   `selectedUpper − 1 = −1833834697676656121979 / 2500000000000000000000000000000000000000000000 < 0`.

   This establishes the stored finite residual, not the missing inequality between a Real analytic moment and this rational expression.
4. **Bootstrap and cutoffs.** `SelectedBootstrapCertificate` computes the source minimum and strict offset from the supplied initial bit/complex savings, then checks all six updates, each four-way gap minimum and each maximum of two ceiling candidates. It proves the final endpoint equals the grid module's recorded saving and reuses the grid bracket. Validity of the supplied initial savings and interpretation of the cutoff as a runtime bound are not assumed to follow from rational arithmetic.
5. **Outer closure.** `SelectedOuterSlackCertificate` recomputes all 47 ordered slack formulas, proves their exact agreement with the serialized certificate and positivity, and checks all seven margins and their source minimum. The minimum is the compact-phase-layer margin; every margin exceeds κ. The internal max selects zero and the Gaussian min selects `r − delta`. Three balanced identities are also checked: the prefix/minimum gap is eta, `1 − epsilon − r = eta/2`, and `1 − epsilon*(1+c) = eta − epsilon*eta/4`.

The source constants, initial savings, charged coefficient, external row allowance 20,161 and literal scalar guard 1 remain supplied finite inputs. This package does not reconstruct their upstream operator or physical-cost validity. The rejected upper moment endpoint, alternate moment engine and malformed-parameter controls in `assemble.py:37–40` are outside its statements.

## Proof and source boundary

All five Lean files are byte-identical to their accepted research sources, totaling 214,798 bytes. Their historical source-only comments and local exclusions are retained verbatim; the later package composition supplies the finite connections described above. No upstream generator is executed. The kernel checks every checkpoint equality and final connection using ordinary exact reductions and `decide +kernel`; there is no `native_decide`, unchecked external arithmetic oracle, admitted axiom or `sorry` in the accepted sources. The 34 printed declarations have only the recorded standard axioms, including `Classical.choice` where reported.

`SOURCE_BINDING.json` records eight exact upstream file identities and the field/formula mappings. Cross-format correspondence to JSON/Python is an independently reviewed source binding, not a theorem about a JSON parser or Python interpreter. The accepted research reference objects, logs and complete probe sets are in `ACCEPTED_CHECKS.json`.

## Runtime and reproduction boundary

The public compile order contains five included roots and zero retained public roots. It imports no preceding physical-setup Lean package. The only direct external library module is `Batteries.Data.Rat.Basic`, whose exact transitive closure contains 319 cached core/Batteries modules and 85,527,032 object bytes.

`EXTERNAL_OBJECTS_REFERENCE.json` references PR528's immutable runtime manifest at commit `ba5e50abb80c6b854b127ccbe37d524e11c6db72`; `EXTERNAL_OBJECTS_SUBSET.json` selects and pins only the 319 required rows. The other 1,894 published manifest rows are not part of this dependency graph. This is runtime provenance, not reuse of PR528's bank theorems. Source and object hashes match exactly. Import lists use stable first-occurrence deduplication; the one explicitly recorded difference is duplicated entries in `Init.Data.BitVec.Lemmas` in the research inventory. No new runtime download, installation or dependency build is implied.

Each root uses the existing 60-second/4-GiB hard caps and 40-second/3.5-GiB review caps. The static object-byte sum is not a memory-fit guarantee. `REPLAY_SUMMARY.json` is the sole mutable record of public reproduction status and actual measurements; prose and reference records do not substitute for it. The central offline checker and its invocation are supplied separately in the final package.

## Attribution, overlap and outstanding work

The formulas and selected data retain PR531/direct-delivery and PR361/eumemic attribution, including the inherited PR144/icekylinx, PR23/Zhihao Chen and RaD/hipotures balanced-assembly contributions recorded by their source headers. `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `SOURCE_BINDING.json` retain the applicable provenance. These Lean transcriptions, proof decomposition, metadata and prose were substantially prepared with OpenAI assistance and independently reviewed.

PR565/566/570 and the physical Real-ceiling setup concern concrete machine preparation and parameter identities. This package neither republishes nor imports their Lean sources. It adds the separate selected rational arithmetic closure. The remaining substantive analytic step is a Real log/exp enclosure with outward-rounding transport; profile/operator realization, source caller/layout, Plan/Budget, physical precision/tape and all-size transfer remain open.

No candidate-specific `make verify`, `make gen4-bank-verify`, `verify-research` evidence transport or hosted-CI outcome is claimed here. Such aggregate checks require their own exact candidate-bound evidence, independently of the bounded Lean reproduction.

## Offline reproduction

The sources are portable Lean 4.21.0. The supplied checker requires Linux with `/proc` to measure the stated memory review limits. It performs no downloads and imports no predecessor Lean source package.

Provide the exact PR528 runtime-inventory package at commit `ba5e50abb80c6b854b127ccbe37d524e11c6db72`, the existing Lean 4.21.0 installation, and the matching Mathlib/package cache. The checker selects only the 319 runtime rows named in `EXTERNAL_OBJECTS_SUBSET.json` from PR528's pinned `EXTERNAL_OBJECTS.json`. It verifies their canonical row digest, source/object hashes, import closure and first-match paths. The explicit first-occurrence import deduplication audit leaves every source/object byte unchanged.

Run `python3 check.py --lean /path/to/lean-4.21.0/bin/lean --runtime-base-root /path/to/research/lean-complete-bank-endpoint --mathlib-root /path/to/mathlib --build-dir /new/empty/build-directory`. The build directory must not exist. The optional `--slot-service /path/to/existing_slot_service.py` uses an existing `acquire()` FIFO service without changing any Lean inputs.

The checker compiles all five included sources in manifest order, with no retained public objects. Each command uses `-s 65536 -j 1`, a 60-second wall limit and 4 GiB address-space cap. It stops after failure or a measured check above the 40-second or 3.5 GiB review threshold. The 34 complete axiom probes must match the manifest and contain only the standard `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` axioms. Raw logs, source copies, objects and per-module receipts remain in the isolated build directory. Input preservation is checked again at the end. Actual public reproduction status is recorded only in `REPLAY_SUMMARY.json`.

This PR additionally carries the one-entry mixed-point source-provenance correction already reviewed in PR565 (commit 890b2906). It updates only the rational_span_frames.py digest; mathematical certificate data and scripts are unchanged. Candidate static provenance checks matched 204/204 links in the independently inventoried scope. The successful Python 3.13 make verify-research run at commit 9278e39 is carried forward only as scoped local evidence: all 212 declared input files, all 28 generated certificate bytes, all 72 import origins, the 28 commands and the runtime/environment assumptions match exactly. This is transported evidence, not a fresh target run on this candidate. The package has its own measured five-fresh Lean reproduction, with zero retained public outputs; all five objects and raw logs match the accepted research references. Python 3.11/3.14, full make verify, make gen4-bank-verify and exact-head hosted CI remain separate obligations.

title: Witness spec tools: declarative WITNESS.json inputs, EXPECTED.json comparisons and a generic verifier (no κ claim)
body:
## Summary

This PR adds tooling only and makes **no κ claim**.

`research/witness-spec-tools/` lets you describe a witness declaratively and get a complete, generic verifier for it. Today each new record forks the previous package and hand-edits constants spread through `verify.py`, bind, audit and assemble. With this tool, a new candidate is a data change instead.

- **`WITNESS.json`** holds **inputs only**:
  - the pinned sources;
  - the geometry;
  - typed provider build chains (`greedy_kernels`, `promote`, `joint_prefix`, multicut/cold steps, all naming recipes by hash);
  - the dispatch and call order;
  - PLAN and OWNERS, referenced by hash.
  The verifier **builds** everything from this file.
- **`EXPECTED.json`** holds **expected values only**: built word hashes, control counts, per-provider artifacts and profiles, the global profile and counts, and κ. The verifier only **compares** against it. **No value in `EXPECTED.json` feeds a computation.** Every value is recomputed independently first, and moment endpoints are re-certified rather than read, so a wrong `EXPECTED.json` can only make verification fail.
- **Entry points:** `spec.py generate|check` and `verify.py`. Python 3.11+, standard library only, assertions required.

The admission scripts in `code/` are PR582's, unchanged except that shape constants now come from `geometry` and moment endpoints are always re-certified.

## Tests (`tests/run_tests.py`, fixture: PR582 at 747ec97)

All 8 pass:
- **Fixture:** from `examples/pr582/WITNESS.json` alone, every provider word is built through the typed steps, with no prebuilt words or reused locals. The generated `EXPECTED.json` equals PR582's published values, and `spec.py check` passes. A strict verify from scratch reproduces κ 0.001601486955392486.
- **Mutations that must fail**, each rejected at its named check:
  - a profile count;
  - a dispatch entry;
  - an owner byte;
  - a kernel coefficient.

## Not included

These are left out on purpose: witness *search* (owner solvers, kernel and width screens, orchestration), new step types, probe builds of recipe output hashes, and a spec-driven accounting model. See the README.

## Credits

Adapted from the PR582 → PR576 → PR571/PR569/PR568/PR564 lineage and PR575/PR558, with all original notices retained.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001602278921983212: two gate-move frame coalescences on PR584
body:
## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.001602278921983212**. This is +1.98e-7 over our PR584 and PR586 (0.001602080856660739) and +6.17e-7 over PR583. The conservative model gives 0.001602278919174953.

This PR is PR584 plus **two new frame coalescences** in block 25 of the A prefix, on both kernel-carrying providers (ck, 66 calls; atm3, 5 calls):
- Gate A33 (`x491 += x490` at frame [25]) commutes past A34 and A35, which share its source 490 but have different targets. Moved after them, it can be raised to frame [96,25].
- Gate A46 likewise moves after A48 and is raised to [97,25].

PR583's search missed these because neither gate was its pivot's last gate. Each merge turns two rank-1 payments into one rank-2 payment per call, so the change is {1:−4, 2:+2} per call on top of PR583's six coalescences. Scalar operations and responses are unchanged, as are helper widths and PR582's literal owner map.

The moves are applied by a new typed build step, `gate_move_coalesce` (`code/build_gate_moves.py`). For every move it checks commutation, unchanged dirty responses and widths, and the cleanup rule. title: Bit c = 0.001733427039589844: two A-section transports on #555's punctured R439 word (+0.0216%, κ unchanged)
body:
**Bit c = 0.001733427039589844234749 (+0.0216% over #555), κ unchanged.**

Two helper additions of #555's punctured R439 bit word (v = 111) are moved out of their D4 mini-node gates and rerun at other frames. Nothing else changes: the same registers, scatter, retained totals (nine COPY ranks of 7, decoder constant 63), frozen hosting selections and pipelines.

| | #555 | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| bit c, nine stages | 0.001733052823330162099157 | **0.001733427039589844234749** | +0.0216% |
| bit c, eleven stages | 0.001710608806098012673516 | **0.001710951900777583975622** | +0.0201% |
| κ with #548's complex b | 0.001590984155135328 | 0.001590984155135328 | none |

κ stays complex-bound for every cited complex supplier (#548, #544, #535, #531), so this is bit headroom only.

### What changed
- **hoist:** in A[1993] (frame 509, rank 4), the summand `helper 222 += helper 248` becomes its own gate at rank-1 frame 79, placed just before that gate.
- **sink:** in A[1994] (frame 509), the summand `helper 191 += helper 247` becomes its own gate at the rank-7 pseudo-total frame 517, placed after A[2028].

Both summands commute with every addition they cross, and the dirty-register endpoint is unchanged on every column. The local paid profile moves by `+2e1 − e3 − 3e4 + e6 + e7`, and rank mass stays at 5,129.

The mechanisms come from #541 and #548 (Dugongue) and #542 (rohanarun) on the R480 word. Their move lists are R480 gate ids and don't apply to #555's word, which has no two-x-source additions and no zero-response gates. `tune/tune.py` therefore re-runs the mechanisms as searches. - **Checkers.** It runs the independent replay and interface lemma, the word-level and record-level mutation controls, the official legality and formal-column checkers (5, 9 and 11 stages) and the Gram witnesses.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001609915765452068: hyperplane-ended helpers on the PR588 witness
body:
## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.001609915765452068**. This is +7.64e-6 over our PR588 (0.001602278921983212). The conservative model gives 0.001609915762605935.

This PR keeps PR588's construction (PR582's three providers with all eight frame coalescences) and adds **hyperplane-ended helpers**. In each of the three providers (ck ×66 calls, atm3 ×5, jp8 ×1), 38 entering width-8 helpers per call have exactly one cleanup gate `h -= p`, where p is a partner whose final frame and h's final frame span a hyperplane U (dim 8). That gate commutes to the end of part B at frame U. The helper then ends at U instead of FULL, so its residual width drops from 8 to 7: local profile {1:+3, 2:−2} per helper, mass-neutral, deficit unchanged at 2560. The width-7 helpers then pair exactly with width-9 helpers in rank-16 owner slots, filling forced rank-3 holes.

**Why this is legitimate.** Ending at FULL is a convention of the inherited code, not a proof obligation:
- Lean Lemma A's hypothesis (F) is stated on actual extended labels and never names FULL.
- Lemma C and Lemma G need only invertible common labels.
- The nested-children lemma gives T_U T_E^{-1} = L(C_[|U|−|E|]⊗I)R with rank-zero L and R.

The full argument and every changed assertion are in `PROOF-HYPERPLANE-END.md`. An independent review found one real issue: the pre-wrapper recipe was ambiguous at three entrances shared by FULL-ended and U-ended helpers. It is fixed, and both wrappers are now keyed by (start, final).

**Verifier changes.**
- Helper width is computed as |final| − |E| at all 9 global sites that previously hard-coded 9 − |E|.
- A per-site revert control puts back the old formula at each site, and each one must fail. All 9 are rejected, the invoice site through a mandatory terminal-codimension check.
- The new typed build step `hyperplane_end` checks commutation, exact scalar replay, the wrapped product L^{-1}T_U T_E^{-1}R^{-1} = C_[7]⊗I (global phase included), widths, and cleanup. It carries replay, wrapper and raw-word negative controls.

The literal owner map (all-HPE dispatch) was found by an RINS-bounded MIP around the pattern LP vertex, within 2e-5 objective units of the LP bound. The paid profile is `{1:181612,2:35160,3:23384,4:14024,5:4032,6:4032,8:576,12:1,48:1949}`.

## How it was found

- An LP/MILP screen over free dispatch of {ck, atm3, jp8, e8} gave an upper bound of 0.0016015477. The integer solution chose 66/5/1.
- The owner map comes from an exact-window MILP with the dispatch fixed, warm-started from PR571's owner map. Every solution of that model expands literally through Kőnig colouring, and HiGHS solved it to optimality.

## Package

`research/complex-571-hpeq1/` contains 33 files. Five sources are pinned externally by manifest and file hashes, and nothing is copied from them:
- PR568 (`research/complex-multicold`, `71c99ac`);
- PR569 (`research/larger-gain`, `897213a`);
- PR571 (`research/structural-gain`, `b7bdc5a`);
- PR575 (`research/complex-joint-prefix`, `eac6f7e`);
- PR583 (`research/kernel-frame-coalescing`, `89be768`).

The package is fully data-driven. `data/SPEC.json` describes each provider as a typed chain of build steps (pinned base word, then `promote`, `greedy_kernels`, `joint_prefix`, `frame_coalesce`, `gate_move_coalesce` or `hyperplane_end`, each with its paired omission and coverage audits), plus the dispatch, the owner and plan hashes, and every expected value. The single `verify.py` and `code/` contain no witness constants. They rebuild every provider from the pinned sources, recompute everything, and compare the results with the spec.

## Verification

PR568, PR569, PR571 and PR575 are not merged, so fetch their pinned commits first:

```sh
git fetch origin pull/568/head:pr568 pull/569/head:pr569 pull/571/head:pr571 pull/575/head:pr575 pull/583/head:pr583
for n in 568:71c99ac935a33bb7b59a1b4a7af8725a939b0b90 569:897213a855b7fb8a1b8b0e552a2f5c42e6c1b326 \
         571:b7bdc5a8de18fcf418cfb9c7d83a2b1097a5e4a3 575:eac6f7e 583:89be768; do git worktree add --detach ../pr${n%%:*} ${n#*:}; done
python3 -B research/complex-571-hpeq1/verify.py --work /tmp/571-hpeq1 \
  --source multicold=../pr568/research/complex-multicold \
  --source larger_gain=../pr569/research/larger-gain \
  --source structural_gain=../pr571/research/structural-gain \
  --source joint_prefix=../pr575/research/complex-joint-prefix \
  --source frame_coalescing=../pr583/research/kernel-frame-coalescing
```

Add `--check-pins` to check only the package and source pins.

`verify.py` uses only the standard library. It runs:
- the full PR558 replay;
- each provider's build chain, with all of its omission controls (PR568 multi-cut kernels, PR569 promotions, PR575 joint-prefix coverage and rank-five audits);
- the native chain and exact phase edges for all three providers;
- binding, the physical owner audit (31 mutants), a fresh invoice, both exact moment engines, the 47 strict outer inequalities for each model, 147 assembly controls, and the phase-timing controls.

Local result (Windows, CPython 3.11.11): the commit was preflighted from a fresh clone first (byte-identical to the generated package, committed blobs equal its MANIFEST, pin check passes). The official run from that clean clone then gave `PASS_HPEQ1_NATIVE_COMPLEX_AND_CITED_BIT`, κ 0.001609915765452068, 49/49 stages exit 0, 470 s.

GitHub CI has not run, and I make no claim about it.

- **jon314159**: PR575 (the joint prefix in all calls) and PR567.
- **DominikScholz**: PR571 (the joint prefix) and PR569 (entrance promotions and their constructor).
- **jeremykothe2**: PR588, PR584, PR576, PR578 and PR574.
- **eumemic**: PR564, PR561, PR562, PR558, PR550, PR543, PR507.
- **rohanarun**: PR559.
- **Dugongue**: PR552 and PR514.
- **icekylinx**: PR535 and PR531.
- **DreamingOfClouds**: PR484.
- **higherbeing**: the open allocator.
- **lydakis**: PR275.
- **Douglas Colkitt / CrocSwap**: maintenance.
- **The original OpenAI #109 framework.**

**AI disclosure and authorship:** Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), running in the omp coding harness, did the work for this PR: the hyperplane-end construction and proof, the owner solve, the spec-driven package and this description. Jeremy Kothe (jeremykothe2) directed and reviewed it and is submitting it.

## Scope

The result is conditional on the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape/exact recovery, analytic transfer and the bit H1–H5 assumptions. It is finite exact evidence. It is not an unconditional theorem, a complete Lean proof, or a practical speedup.

**Update (commit f622547, same κ): declarative inputs.** `data/WITNESS.json` holds the inputs only (pinned sources, typed provider build steps, dispatch, and PLAN/OWNERS/recipes by hash). `data/EXPECTED.json` holds every expected value, generated by recomputation from the witness. A definition-first `README.md` is added too. `spec.py check` from a clean clone gives CHECK OK. `data/cand.json` is the search-side candidate description (schema candidate/1, package-relative paths). Regenerating from it reproduces the package byte-for-byte only when the original build locals are reused. With fresh locals, PLAN differs in a timing-derived CLIFFORD-REVIEW hash, and the owner stage re-admits the shipped OWNERS rather than searching for them again. So `WITNESS.json` is the authoritative definition. The official verify was rerun from a clean clone of f622547: 49/49 stages exit 0, 379 s, same κ.

title: [Lean] Hyperplane-ended helpers: Lemma A with an arbitrary terminal frame (no κ claim)
body:
## Summary

**No κ claim.** This is a Lean 4 proof package for the hyperplane-end step used by PR591, PR592 and PR596.

`research/hyperplane-end-lean/` proves that Lemma A's realization still holds when a dirty entering helper ends at an **arbitrary terminal frame U**, not only FULL. With the extended labels `T_(prew,j) = R_{E,U} T_E` and `T_(done,j) = L_{E,U}⁻¹ T_U`, and wrappers keyed by the pair (E, U), the exact factorization (N) `T_U T_E⁻¹ = L(C⊗id)R` implies Lemma A's hypothesis (F). Lemma A then gives the helper's stream `χ⁻¹(C⊗id)χ` of itself for any U (`hpe_streams`, `hpe_word`). The FULL-ended helpers of #484 are the instance U = ⊤.

`factor_iff_pre` formalizes a review finding: (F) holds **iff** the pre wrapper is R_{E,U}. So a wrapper chosen by entrance alone, as in the original code, is wrong for U-ended helpers.

## Update (commit fdb6dcc): (N) is now proved in Lean

`HyperplaneEnd/Clifford.lean` and `HyperplaneEnd/Exact.lean` prove the factorization (N) `T_U T_E⁻¹ = L(C⊗id)R` exactly for every (E, U) pair the hyperplane-ended words use. The 9 word/pair instances (ck, atm3, jp8 × 3) come down to 3 distinct identities. They are checked by `decide +kernel` on a packed ℤ[i] circuit evaluation (`check1`–`check3`, axioms `[propext]`); a soundness lemma (`cL_eq_of_check`) lifts each check to an equality of complex operators. `hpe_word_exact` is `hpe_word` with **no (N) hypothesis**: it requires only `(ent h, term h) ∈ pairs`.

## Checks (fresh clone of `fdb6dcc`, Windows, Lean v4.21.0)

- Source scan: no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `unsafe`, `opaque` or `extern` in 17 files.
- `lake exe cache get` + `lake build`: Build completed successfully.
- `#print axioms`: all 28 results are within `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` (`check1`–`check3`: `[propext]` only).
- `code/check_hpe_pairs.py --mutants` on the ck, atm3 and jp8 hyperplane-ended local runs: PASS, every mutant rejected.
- Note for reviewers on Windows: with `CI=true` in the environment, building Mathlib from source (`--no-cache`) fails in Mathlib's own `CauSeq/Basic.lean:440` `says` check at this pin. Use the Mathlib cache (the default), or unset `CI`.

## Scope

The climb recipes, the unit row and (O′)/(W) remain hypotheses here, checked exactly by the PR591/PR592/PR596 verifiers. This package doesn't prove a multiplier or κ theorem. PR #599 (DreamingOfClouds) extends it to multi-gate tails and cold helpers.

title: Format limits (no κ claim): certified ceiling κ ≤ 5.1595e-3, spec census, structural lemmas, helper bounds and open problems
body:
**No κ claim.** This package records what we have proved and measured about the limits of the current construction format. It is meant to help whoever finds the next structural step. Every result states its scope. Each is marked *checked* (recomputed by `verify.sh`), *argued* (proof or sketch in the README) or *recorded* (an input from a named run or PR).

```sh
bash research/format-limits/verify.sh /fresh/output/dir   # ~2 min; 298 PASS lines; step 0 fails hard on any MANIFEST/provenance mismatch
```

### Results
| id | result | status |
|---|---|---|
| A | **Format ceiling, rev. 2: κ ≤ 5.1595·10⁻³**, complex binds. Per side at s = 5: X* = 6.0005·10⁻³ (bit, 111 lines, cst 63) and 5.1863·10⁻³ (complex, 112 ports, cst 64). Rev. 1's scope x = 3/5 is superseded. At s = 9 the frontier sits 2.66× (bit) / 2.50× (complex) below; 87% / 93% of the log-gap is helper cost. | theorem argued; numbers checked |
| B | **Spec vs convention census:** 25 format rules classified, with file:line into the upstream paper and the hub's checkers. Nesting, target-perp sinks, subspace frames and one bank pair per invocation are conventions; a common frame per gate, restoration and the κ = min composition are spec. | anchors checked; classification argued |
| C.1 | **Frame sandwich:** a register's frame lies between the span of what it carries and the orthogonal of what it will serve. The three complex frame walls are its faces. | argued; toy checked |
| C.2 | **Lemma N:** the rank-1 port factor is a gauge and is always paid; any detour costs exactly 2. | toys checked |
| C.3 | **Lemma R:** complement sinks w^⊥ (w·u = 1) are legal at zero cost but forced to w = u on all four frontier complex words checked. | checked |
| C.4 | **Lemma Q:** a degenerate-label unit is dominated by its quotient. | toys checked |
| C.5 | **Lemma λ:** a phase-frame butterfly needs λ = ±i; b < c is the price of √−1. The outer already uses shift twiddles. | checked |
| C.6 | **Pairing uniqueness:** at the E8 decoder pattern with window ≤ 9, B = W·Uᵀ is unique, so asymmetric labels are a gauge. | checked (SAT) |
| C.7 | **Per-call descent pricing:** a rank-r descent costs 2r data mass in every call (≈ −5.6% per rank-1 descent on either side). | checked; dominance argued |
| C.8 | Splitting a residual across hosting streams meets a trace obstruction under every invertible storage change; uncharged ≤ +0.67% b. | argued |
| D | **Design-free helper floors:** bit ≥ 212 / 138 vs 439 shipped; complex ≥ 107 / 0 vs 496 (so at most 48% / 22% of today's helpers are certified necessary). Coupling the levels adds 0. The "224 carriers" complex floor is a design choice. | checked |
| E | **Complex helper prices on #569** by class and width (0.039–0.143% b per helper; the hosting offset depends on width only), plus the moment-cost census on #555 and #569. | checked (k = 1); k > 1 recorded |

### Open problems (where we think the next step has to come from)
- **Enablers paid once per word, not per call.** A change paid in every local word costs about 2.8% of the supplier value per rank unit, so it pays only if its per-word gain exceeds 2.8·Δ% (README §F). Candidates: a descent or gauge change hoisted out of the local word, or a decoder whose stations serve many calls.
- **A non-star decoder.** The copy charge is the largest scope multiplier (×6.8 if star scope fails), but the E8 pattern pins the pairing (C.6) and the lossless pattern (C.3).
- **The schedule/ρ family (×1.15–2.1).** The only spec freedom never exercised (B.3, item 8).
- **New skeletons.** The design-free floors certify at most 48% / 21% of today's helper count, so nothing here excludes a much better skeleton on either side.

### Notes
- **Base:** this branch is cut from main (7dfa22b) and touches only `research/format-limits/`.
- **Inputs:** vendored inputs are pinned by PR blob id in `SOURCES.json`. Requirements are pinned. Independently re-verified from a fresh `git archive` of 39112c2: 298/298 on Python 3.11 and 3.14 with the pinned set, on 3.14 with the latest numpy/scipy, and on a dev environment. Tampered or unlisted files stop step 0 with exit 1.
- **Errata found:** the E7 hyperplane-flat census is 8821 (an earlier note said 2258), and the cover numbers are unchanged. A tail-lemma constant is corrected (Hermite–Hadamard).

**Credits:** see `NOTICE.md` for every PR whose word, pipeline or result is used. Among them are #531 and #130 (icekylinx), #543/#555 (eumemic), #569 (DominikScholz), #442, #446, #509 and #516, and the swarm PRs cited in each section.

title: Conditional κ = 0.0016127213726553: improved owner map for the PR592 hyperplane-ended witness
body:
## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.0016127213726553**. This is +1.95e-9 over our PR592 (0.001612719427075359). The conservative model gives 0.001612721369804261.

This PR has the same construction, providers, dispatch (ck ×53, atm3 ×19) and verifier as PR592. Only the literal owner map changes: a local search from PR592's map found one improving move. The package also ships the declarative inputs `data/WITNESS.json` (inputs only) and `data/EXPECTED.json` (expected values, generated by recomputation), plus a definition-first `README.md`.

This PR has the same construction, providers, build steps and verifier as PR591. Only the dispatch and the literal owner map change: ck ×53 and atm3 ×19 calls, all with hyperplane-ended helpers (PR591 used ck ×66, atm3 ×5, jp8 ×1). The LP upper bound for this menu is κ ≤ 0.0016127416, and this map is within 2.2e-8 of it.

This PR keeps PR588's construction (PR582's three providers with all eight frame coalescences) and adds **hyperplane-ended helpers**. In each of the three providers (here ck and atm3), 38 entering width-8 helpers per call have exactly one cleanup gate `h -= p`, where p is a partner whose final frame and h's final frame span a hyperplane U (dim 8). That gate commutes to the end of part B at frame U. The helper then ends at U instead of FULL, so its residual width drops from 8 to 7: local profile {1:+3, 2:−2} per helper, mass-neutral, deficit unchanged at 2560. The width-7 helpers then pair exactly with width-9 helpers in rank-16 owner slots, filling forced rank-3 holes.

**Why this is legitimate.** Ending at FULL is a convention of the inherited code, not a proof obligation:
- Lean Lemma A's hypothesis (F) is stated on actual extended labels and never names FULL.
- Lemma C and Lemma G need only invertible common labels.
- The nested-children lemma gives T_U T_E^{-1} = L(C_[|U|−|E|]⊗I)R with rank-zero L and R.

The full argument and every changed assertion are in `PROOF-HYPERPLANE-END.md`. An independent review found one real issue: the pre-wrapper recipe was ambiguous at three entrances shared by FULL-ended and U-ended helpers. It is fixed, and both wrappers are now keyed by (start, final).

**Verifier changes.**
- Helper width is computed as |final| − |E| at all 9 global sites that previously hard-coded 9 − |E|.
- A per-site revert control puts back the old formula at each site, and each one must fail. All 9 are rejected, the invoice site through a mandatory terminal-codimension check.
- The new typed build step `hyperplane_end` checks commutation, exact scalar replay, the wrapped product L^{-1}T_U T_E^{-1}R^{-1} = C_[7]⊗I (global phase included), widths, and cleanup. It carries replay, wrapper and raw-word negative controls.

The literal owner map (all-HPE dispatch) was found by an RINS-bounded MIP around the pattern LP vertex, within 2e-5 objective units of the LP bound. The paid profile is `{1:182817,2:34192,3:22561,4:14584,5:4032,6:4032,8:576,12:1,48:1969}`.

## How it was found

- An LP/MILP screen over free dispatch of {ck, atm3, jp8, e8} gave an upper bound of 0.0016015477. The integer solution chose 66/5/1.
- The owner map comes from an exact-window MILP with the dispatch fixed, warm-started from PR571's owner map. Every solution of that model expands literally through Kőnig colouring, and HiGHS solved it to optimality.

## Package

`research/complex-571-hpeq5/` contains 33 files. Five sources are pinned externally by manifest and file hashes, and nothing is copied from them:
- PR568 (`research/complex-multicold`, `71c99ac`);
- PR569 (`research/larger-gain`, `897213a`);
- PR571 (`research/structural-gain`, `b7bdc5a`);
- PR575 (`research/complex-joint-prefix`, `eac6f7e`);
- PR583 (`research/kernel-frame-coalescing`, `89be768`).

The package is fully data-driven. `data/SPEC.json` describes each provider as a typed chain of build steps (pinned base word, then `promote`, `greedy_kernels`, `joint_prefix`, `frame_coalesce`, `gate_move_coalesce` or `hyperplane_end`, each with its paired omission and coverage audits), plus the dispatch, the owner and plan hashes, and every expected value. The single `verify.py` and `code/` contain no witness constants. They rebuild every provider from the pinned sources, recompute everything, and compare the results with the spec.

## Verification

PR568, PR569, PR571 and PR575 are not merged, so fetch their pinned commits first:

```sh
git fetch origin pull/568/head:pr568 pull/569/head:pr569 pull/571/head:pr571 pull/575/head:pr575 pull/583/head:pr583
for n in 568:71c99ac935a33bb7b59a1b4a7af8725a939b0b90 569:897213a855b7fb8a1b8b0e552a2f5c42e6c1b326 \
         571:b7bdc5a8de18fcf418cfb9c7d83a2b1097a5e4a3 575:eac6f7e 583:89be768; do git worktree add --detach ../pr${n%%:*} ${n#*:}; done
python3 -B research/complex-571-hpeq5/verify.py --work /tmp/571-hpeq5 \
  --source multicold=../pr568/research/complex-multicold \
  --source larger_gain=../pr569/research/larger-gain \
  --source structural_gain=../pr571/research/structural-gain \
  --source joint_prefix=../pr575/research/complex-joint-prefix \
  --source frame_coalescing=../pr583/research/kernel-frame-coalescing
```

Add `--check-pins` to check only the package and source pins.

`verify.py` uses only the standard library. It runs:
- the full PR558 replay;
- each provider's build chain, with all of its omission controls (PR568 multi-cut kernels, PR569 promotions, PR575 joint-prefix coverage and rank-five audits);
- the native chain and exact phase edges for all three providers;
- binding, the physical owner audit (31 mutants), a fresh invoice, both exact moment engines, the 47 strict outer inequalities for each model, 147 assembly controls, and the phase-timing controls.

Local result (Windows, CPython 3.11.11): the commit was preflighted from a fresh clone first (byte-identical to the generated package, committed blobs equal its MANIFEST, pin check passes). The official run from that clean clone then gave `PASS_HPEQ5_NATIVE_COMPLEX_AND_CITED_BIT`, κ 0.0016127213726553, 32/32 stages exit 0, 401 s, with no reused baseline or locals.

GitHub CI has not run, and I make no claim about it.

## Credits

- **chafreaky**: PR583 (frame coalescences), PR586 (portable identity checks and controls, and an independent macOS/Linux replay of PR584), PR579, PR577, PR572 and PR551.
- **jon314159**: PR575 (the joint prefix in all calls) and PR567.
- **DominikScholz**: PR571 (the joint prefix) and PR569 (entrance promotions and their constructor).
- **jeremykothe2**: PR592, PR591, PR588, PR584, PR576, PR578 and PR574.
- **eumemic**: PR564, PR561, PR562, PR558, PR550, PR543, PR507.
- **rohanarun**: PR559.
- **Dugongue**: PR552 and PR514.
- **icekylinx**: PR535 and PR531.
- **DreamingOfClouds**: PR484.
- **higherbeing**: the open allocator.
- **lydakis**: PR275.
- **Douglas Colkitt / CrocSwap**: maintenance.
- **The original OpenAI #109 framework.**

**AI disclosure and authorship:** Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), running in the omp coding harness, did the work for this PR: the hyperplane-end construction and proof, the owner solve, the spec-driven package and this description. Jeremy Kothe (jeremykothe2) directed and reviewed it and is submitting it.

## Scope

The result is conditional on the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape/exact recovery, analytic transfer and the bit H1–H5 assumptions. It is finite exact evidence. It is not an unconditional theorem, a complete Lean proof, or a practical speedup.

**Update (commit 7732dd5, same κ): declarative inputs.** `data/WITNESS.json` holds the inputs only (pinned sources, typed provider build steps, dispatch, and PLAN/OWNERS/recipes by hash). `data/EXPECTED.json` holds every expected value, generated by recomputation from the witness. A definition-first `README.md` is added too. `spec.py check` from a clean clone gives CHECK OK. `data/cand.json` is the search-side candidate description (schema candidate/1, package-relative paths). Regenerating from it reproduces the package byte-for-byte only when the original build locals are reused. With fresh locals, PLAN differs in a timing-derived CLIFFORD-REVIEW hash, and the owner stage re-admits the shipped OWNERS rather than searching for them again. So `WITNESS.json` is the authoritative definition. The official verify was rerun from a clean clone of 7732dd5: 32/32 stages exit 0, 318 s, same κ.

title: [Lean] Verify current R480 scalar boundaries
body:
# Current R480 scalar boundaries

Author-checked selected conditional context at main `7dfa22b109996e48db68daac3706e7a49a43002b`: **κ = 1584931111785787/1000000000000000000 = 0.001584931111785787**. The exact selected-result and PR535 assembly hashes are in `SOURCE_BINDING.json`. This package does not prove a complete multiplier or κ theorem.

## Checked source-specific results

Six byte-preserved Lean sources add 62 public axiom probes, reusing six exact sources from the accepted historical PR590 package:

- Current R480 domains: 120 ports, 480 helpers, 720 original registers, 672 frame IDs and the nine changed retained hosts. The B/scatter literals and specified table fields are byte-identical to the historical supplier, while the new Fin720 domain and endpoints are proved freshly.
- Exact 240 B gates / 600 ordered operand occurrences. The sequential XOR interpreter preserves arbitrary source/helper bits. Each target is its initial bit XOR a contribution independent of initial target bits; that contribution is not claimed to vanish.
- Exact retained-major 9 COPY + 568 ADD + 9 ERASE scalar slice on 721 registers. Temporary register 720 can arrive dirty, is overwritten and finishes false. Original source/helper registers are preserved. Restoration of an arbitrary incoming temporary is not claimed.
- Generic XOR inverse/reversal laws and the exact changed-host boundary: last 20 A gates and first 20 C gates, 445 operands each, maximum arity 54. All nine changed hosts appear in source order. C is bound to reversed A with frame 1 before scalarization. This isolated 40-gate scalar word is an inverse on arbitrary 720-bit state; conditional cleanup across a target-only middle map preserves that middle map's target result.

## Still open

The other 2688 A gates and corresponding C suffix, arranged in 21 proposed 128-gate chunks, have not been admitted in this package. Complete A/C composition, D dirty-helper compensation, the complete scalar shear, physical frame/entrance transport, COPY-space allocation and ERASE legality, and the full inherited all-size/κ theorem remain separate. No physical interpretation of the frame metadata or dirty temporary restoration follows from these Boolean results.

## Retained-prefix reproduction

`MANIFEST.json` classifies 12 reachable local modules: six included new sources and six retained PR590 dependencies. It lists exact source identities, import order and expected probes. The public checker takes a successful PR590 build, verifies its six required outputs, retains those objects, and compiles only the six new sources in isolated output paths. The two historical selected Fin729 adapters are not dependencies of this current closure.

`DEPENDENCIES.json` records the concrete accepted public-prefix identities and portable validation boundary. The predecessor's runtime timestamps may differ in a separate reproduction. Its actual logs must match their PASS receipts and exact probes; generic XOR has three known source-path-only warning substitutions that require explicit normalization when comparing raw logs.

The exact 317-module official Lean 4.21.0 core closure is supplied in `OFFICIAL_CORE_MANIFEST.json`; no Mathlib installation is needed. `ACCEPTED_CHECKS.json` is immutable prior evidence. The sole mutable new reproduction outcome is `REPLAY_SUMMARY.json`.

Attribution, licenses, literal/source trust boundary and static author check are in `NOTICE`, `SUPPLIER_NOTICE.md`, `LICENSE`, `PROVENANCE.json`, `SOURCE_BINDING.json` and `AUTHOR_CHECK.json`. No upstream supplier program or historical full word is executed by the Lean check.

## Offline checker usage

Use the official Linux x86-64 Lean 4.21.0 distribution named by `lean-toolchain`, with both `src/lean` and `lib/lean` intact. The checker rehashes its exact 317 source/object pairs and executable; it does not fetch dependencies. Python 3 on Linux with `/proc` is required. Run Python without `-O`.

First obtain the exact historical package `research/lean-selected-bit-scalar-boundaries` from PR590 and a successful build made by its checker. Pass that package and build to this checker; it validates the six required source/object pairs, complete probes, actual raw-log/receipt bindings and predecessor PASS result before creating any output. A predecessor receipt can have different timestamps. Only the three known generic-XOR warning source paths may normalize; all other log bytes are exact.

```sh
python3 check.py \
  --lean /path/to/lean-4.21.0-linux/bin/lean \
  --prefix-package /path/to/research/lean-selected-bit-scalar-boundaries \
  --prefix-build /path/to/successful-pr590-build \
  --build-dir /path/to/new-current-r480-build
```

The new build directory must not exist. The checker copies six validated retained objects and stages twelve exact source files in the new directory. Only the six included current sources are compiled, in the manifest's dependency order. It writes untouched compiler logs, object files, per-module receipts and one build-local `REPLAY_RESULT.json`. Successful retained and fresh objects are rechecked between jobs. The repository's `REPLAY_SUMMARY.json` separately records this publication's one observed reproduction.

`--guard-only` verifies the complete input boundary and fresh output absence without creating the build or running a proof compiler. `--require-observed-prefix` additionally requires this package's exact recorded local predecessor result/receipt/raw-log hashes; omit it for an independently produced compatible predecessor build. `--slot-service /path/to/existing_service.py` uses an existing shared FIFO service exposing `acquire()`. The publication reproduction uses that shared service.

Each fresh compiler has a 60-second and 4-GiB hard bound and a 45-second / 3.5-GiB review threshold. The sequence stops at the first failure or review event and retains its evidence. Source/prefix checks occur again after FIFO acquisition; their time, compiler time and FIFO time are reported separately. No predecessor proof is recompiled by this command, no supplier program is executed, and no full A/C theorem is inferred from this bounded reproduction.

## Publication evidence

The one observed public reproduction retained the six exact successful outputs from [PR590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/590), head `58690bdbb587f482569ba1bdf7bf61a5396b4768`, and freshly compiled the six included current sources. All six fresh object files match the prior accepted research objects, and all 62 new probes are complete with only standard axioms. Total actual compiler time was 9.899312333 seconds, with 0.002879484 seconds in the shared FIFO. Five fresh raw logs are byte-identical; the generic reversal log differs only by one recorded source-path warning at 82:8. The predecessor's separate generic-XOR three-path warning comparison remains explicit. Raw logs are preserved.

This is a current-instance package on the exact main 7dfa snapshot. It relies on the six external PR590 package dependencies described above; it does not copy that earlier package into this change. The source-specific 128-gate representative developed later is outside this frozen publication.

The separate recorded Python 3.13 `verify-research` result is transported only for its exact standalone 28-command scope. At the 7dfa base, 211 input bodies are unchanged and one precisely inverted Makefile control delta is outside that target; 28 actual outputs, 72 normalized import origins and 204 static links were independently checked. Candidate applicability is separately checked for these isolated package additions. This is no fresh scientific rerun and does not establish the newer frontier535 target, full CI, physical realization or the final selected-kappa theorem.
