title: Leech/Turyn research (no κ claim): scoped fitting bounds and cost screens
body:
**No κ claim.** This PR records exact Leech/Turyn constructions, tested transformations, and scoped obstructions to smaller binary fitting dimensions. It preserves the failed directions as reproducible research and identifies the freedom that remains open. No production supplier or selected exponent certificate changes.

### Results and scope

| Result | Evidence and limitation |
|---|---|
| A Turyn product kernel with 23,040 ports, real rank 512, and a valid 27-bit fitting representation | Exact generation and all 530,841,600 ordered pair checks. Within each fixed profile, a dyadic change of basis reduces the kernel to 64 E8 copies. Sharing the real centers across profiles remains relevant. |
| Glue-class-constant fitting dimension is exactly 27 | Nine 24-cliques with even vertex incidences give a characteristic-two rank bound, including normalized block fits. This does **not** assume those quotient cliques lift simultaneously to individual ports. |
| Each individual full profile needs symmetric binary dimension nine | A 24-port witness is exhausted without a SAT solver in 43 search nodes; cyclic copies cover all three profiles. This alone does not add to a global 27-dimensional bound. |
| Several full-port transformations cannot reduce the dimension | Four actual edges obstruct independent source/target block-sign choices. Exact finite constraints rule out an improvement from affine Leech coordinates and the tested 168-feature nonlinear family. The latter permits separate affine glue maps for all eight high-line positions and quadratic glue terms. |
| Real basis changes alone cannot reduce the existing full-port encoder bill | Every nonzero real linear tensor encoder has support rank 27 under the existing labels; rank-minimal 512-feature factorizations therefore cost at least 13,824. Redundant encoders outside the tensor column space are excluded from this bound. |
| Full Leech-shell alternatives and scoped moment budgets | The 98,280-line cubic kernel has a 2,600-center dyadic factorization. Norm-six directions reduce the tested encoder support rank to 24, but their dyadic decoder and complete word remain unbuilt. Cost relaxations are explicitly separated from constructed suppliers. |

The hosting-aware accounting relaxation gives nominal κ ≈ 0.00142611820 for the full 27-bit Turyn recipe, about 11.6% below the **reported** PR592 frontier. The punctured recipe has about 1.06% optimistic headroom before the omitted construction obligations. These are bounds within stated scheduling and center-cost assumptions, **not universal limits on dimension 27**. Neither PR592's supplier nor PR595's complete structural analysis is freshly replayed here.

### Packages and reproduction

The branch starts from `main` at `7dfa22b` and adds only:

- `research/leech-lattice/`: geometry, transformations, factorizations, support calculations, and initial screens.
- `research/turyn-code-space/`: the exact glue-quotient rank obstruction and affine/quadratic search spaces.
- `research/turyn-port-labels/`: full-port finite certificates, encoder-support bound, and updated scoped costs.

Requirements: Python ≥ 3.10, NumPy, and a C++17 compiler for the complete code-space replay. No SAT solver is required. Each package pins its files and inherited inputs.

```sh
python3 -I -O research/leech-lattice/verify.py --output /tmp/leech-replay
python3 -I -O research/turyn-code-space/verify.py --output /tmp/turyn-code-replay
python3 -I -O research/turyn-port-labels/verify.py --output /tmp/turyn-port-replay
```

All three packages have passed their exact replay, including optimized Python checks. The frozen first two packages retain their corruption controls; the full-port package includes the known nine-bit fit and a relaxed eight-bit fitting control. No GitHub CI result or formal code review is claimed.

### What remains open

An arbitrary global 25-dimensional full-port fit is still open. The finite family obstructions do not exclude richer nonlinear labels, other scalar kernels, redundant factorizations, or different paid controllers. Even a compatible labeling would still need a charged scalar circuit, frame moves, helper clearing and hosting, and the inherited outer checks. Nothing here establishes worst-case O(1) indexing or an improved multiplication exponent.

title: [Lean] Hyperplane-end helpers: multi-gate cleanup tails and the cold specialisation (stacked on #593, no κ claim)
body:
**No κ claim.** This PR extends #593's hyperplane-end Lean (jeremykothe2) in two directions:
- multi-gate cleanup tails, with several helpers at once;
- the cold specialisation, where the helper enters at E = ⊥.

It is stacked on #593 and adds one commit, touching only `research/hyperplane-end-lean/`.

### What is proved (`HyperplaneEnd/Multi.lean`)
- **`hpe_labels_multi`**: the word `a ++ mtail ++ b ++ posts` is well labelled, and every hyperplane-ended helper ends at `(done, j)`. This holds for a general `cleanup_tail`: any number of gates `t += q • s` or `t *= q`, each at its own frame, where each operand climbs to that frame unless it is already there. A helper may be target or partner of several tail gates, and several helpers may interleave. Hypotheses:
  - the last tail gate touching `j` runs at `term j`;
  - the rest of the cleanup never moves `j`;
  - the entrance frame is arbitrary.
- **`hpe_word_multi`**: Lemma A on streams for every such helper, given the per-helper (N), as in #593.
- **`hpe_labels_tail`**: `Tail.lean`'s one-gate word is the one-gate instance when both operands start away from `U`.
- **`exact_cold`, `cold_hyperplane_width`**: given `T_E = id`, which holds for the canonical frame of `E = ⊥`, (N) reduces to `T_U = L (C ⊗ id) R`, and `⊥ ≤ U` with `dim U = 8` gives width 8. #593's `hpe_word` already accepts an arbitrary entrance frame, so the Lean content specific to E = ⊥ is just this specialisation.

### Scope
- **Not checked against emitted words:** the shipped hyperplane-ended helpers of #591/#592 have one tail gate each. Multi-gate and `scale` tails are not checked here against emitted words. This PR does not change the instance checker `check_hpe_pairs.py`.
- **Hypotheses outside Lean:** as in #593 §4, (N) for each pair (E, U) used, the unit row `hS`, `hrec`, and (O′)/(W) are hypotheses checked outside Lean.
- **E = ⊥ check:** (N) was checked locally on all 511 hyperplanes of F₂⁹ with `clifford_exact` from main's `direct-delivery504-global/vendor` (tableau and global phase). That script is not shipped here.
- **Possible clash:** `Multi.lean` derives `DecidableEq` for `XLab`. If #593 later derives it in `Labels.lean`, delete this line.

### Checks
- **Verify:** `python3 research/hyperplane-end-lean/verify.py` passes. All 27 named results (#593's 13 plus 14 new) depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. There is no `sorry`, `admit` or `axiom`.
- **Fresh build:** an independent audit rebuilt LemmaG, LemmaA and HyperplaneEnd from a fresh `git archive`, reusing prebuilt Mathlib, and `verify.py` passed there.

**Credit:** #593 (jeremykothe2) is the base package and the single-gate theorem; #509 / #516 (DreamingOfClouds) are the Lemma G / Lemma A packages it builds on.

Prepared by DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code; Apache-2.0.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001612722852614221: improved owner map for the PR596 hyperplane-ended witness
body:
## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.001612722852614221**. This is +1.48e-9 over our PR596 (0.0016127213726553). The conservative model gives 0.001612722849763179.

This PR has the same construction, providers, dispatch (ck ×53, atm3 ×19) and verifier as PR596. Only the literal owner map changes: a 2-swap ejection chain on idle remainders turns {1:1,3:281,12:1} into {1:2,3:279,5:1,12:1}. The concave moment cost favours uneven holes. The package also ships the declarative inputs `data/WITNESS.json` (inputs only) and `data/EXPECTED.json` (expected values, generated by recomputation), plus a definition-first `README.md`. `data/cand.json` is the search-side candidate description; its warm-start owner map is shipped as `data/search/WARM-OWNERS.json.gz` (a search input that the verifiers do not read).

This PR has the same construction, providers, build steps and verifier as PR591. Only the dispatch and the literal owner map change: ck ×53 and atm3 ×19 calls, all with hyperplane-ended helpers (PR591 used ck ×66, atm3 ×5, jp8 ×1). The LP upper bound for this menu is κ ≤ 0.0016127416, and this map is within 2.2e-8 of it.

This PR keeps PR588's construction (PR582's three providers with all eight frame coalescences) and adds **hyperplane-ended helpers**. In each of the three providers (here ck and atm3), 38 entering width-8 helpers per call have exactly one cleanup gate `h -= p`, where p is a partner whose final frame and h's final frame span a hyperplane U (dim 8). That gate commutes to the end of part B at frame U. The helper then ends at U instead of FULL, so its residual width drops from 8 to 7: local profile {1:+3, 2:−2} per helper, mass-neutral, deficit unchanged at 2560. The width-7 helpers then pair exactly with width-9 helpers in rank-16 owner slots, filling forced rank-3 holes.

**Why this is legitimate.** Ending at FULL is a convention of the inherited code, not a proof obligation:
- Lean Lemma A's hypothesis (F) is stated on actual extended labels and never names FULL.
- Lemma C and Lemma G need only invertible common labels.
- The nested-children lemma gives T_U T_E^{-1} = L(C_[|U|−|E|]⊗I)R with rank-zero L and R.

The full argument and every changed assertion are in `PROOF-HYPERPLANE-END.md`. An independent review found one real issue: the pre-wrapper recipe was ambiguous at three entrances shared by FULL-ended and U-ended helpers. It is fixed, and both wrappers are now keyed by (start, final).

**Verifier changes.**
- Helper width is computed as |final| − |E| at all 9 global sites that previously hard-coded 9 − |E|.
- A per-site revert control puts back the old formula at each site, and each one must fail. All 9 are rejected, the invoice site through a mandatory terminal-codimension check.
- The new typed build step `hyperplane_end` checks commutation, exact scalar replay, the wrapped product L^{-1}T_U T_E^{-1}R^{-1} = C_[7]⊗I (global phase included), widths, and cleanup. It carries replay, wrapper and raw-word negative controls.

The literal owner map (all-HPE dispatch) was found by an RINS-bounded MIP around the pattern LP vertex, within 2e-5 objective units of the LP bound. The paid profile is the global profile recorded in `data/EXPECTED.json`.

## How it was found

- An LP/MILP screen over free dispatch of {ck, atm3, jp8, e8} gave an upper bound of 0.0016015477. The integer solution chose 66/5/1.
- The owner map comes from an exact-window MILP with the dispatch fixed, warm-started from PR571's owner map. Every solution of that model expands literally through Kőnig colouring, and HiGHS solved it to optimality.

## Package

`research/complex-571-hpeq6/` contains 33 files. Five sources are pinned externally by manifest and file hashes, and nothing is copied from them:
- PR568 (`research/complex-multicold`, `71c99ac`);
- PR569 (`research/larger-gain`, `897213a`);
- PR571 (`research/structural-gain`, `b7bdc5a`);
- PR575 (`research/complex-joint-prefix`, `eac6f7e`);
- PR583 (`research/kernel-frame-coalescing`, `89be768`).

The package is fully data-driven. `data/SPEC.json` describes each provider as a typed chain of build steps (pinned base word, then `promote`, `greedy_kernels`, `joint_prefix`, `frame_coalesce`, `gate_move_coalesce` or `hyperplane_end`, each with its paired omission and coverage audits), plus the dispatch, the owner and plan hashes, and every expected value. The single `verify.py` and `code/` contain no witness constants. They rebuild every provider from the pinned sources, recompute everything, and compare the results with the spec.

## Verification

PR568, PR569, PR571 and PR575 are not merged, so fetch their pinned commits first:

```sh
git fetch origin pull/568/head:pr568 pull/569/head:pr569 pull/571/head:pr571 pull/575/head:pr575 pull/583/head:pr583
for n in 568:71c99ac935a33bb7b59a1b4a7af8725a939b0b90 569:897213a855b7fb8a1b8b0e552a2f5c42e6c1b326 \
         571:b7bdc5a8de18fcf418cfb9c7d83a2b1097a5e4a3 575:eac6f7e 583:89be768; do git worktree add --detach ../pr${n%%:*} ${n#*:}; done
python3 -B research/complex-571-hpeq6/verify.py --work /tmp/571-hpeq6 \
  --source multicold=../pr568/research/complex-multicold \
  --source larger_gain=../pr569/research/larger-gain \
  --source structural_gain=../pr571/research/structural-gain \
  --source joint_prefix=../pr575/research/complex-joint-prefix \
  --source frame_coalescing=../pr583/research/kernel-frame-coalescing
```

`verify.py` uses only the standard library. It runs:
- the full PR558 replay;
- each provider's build chain, with all of its omission controls (PR568 multi-cut kernels, PR569 promotions, PR575 joint-prefix coverage and rank-five audits);
- the native chain and exact phase edges for all three providers;
- binding, the physical owner audit (31 mutants), a fresh invoice, both exact moment engines, the 47 strict outer inequalities for each model, 147 assembly controls, and the phase-timing controls.

Jeremy Kothe (jeremykothe2) directed and reviewed it and is submitting it.

## Scope

The result is conditional on the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape/exact recovery, analytic transfer and the bit H1–H5 assumptions. title: Conditional κ = 0.001614202339036103: 46 hyperplane-ended helpers per call via commuting-prefix cleanup

## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.001614202339036103**. This is +1.479e-6 over PR600 (0.001612722852614221) and +1.481e-6 over PR596. The conservative model gives 0.001614202336182603.

**Controls.** Each word's `hyperplane_end` step runs 21 controls, all of which must behave as stated:
- a partner gate that **writes** `p` (or scales it) is rejected by the commutation assert, with a pinned message;

title: Conditional κ = 0.00162128508944984: cold factory-scratch helpers end at 4-dimensional frames on the PR601 witness (+0.439%)
body:
**Conditional κ = 0.00162128508944984, +0.439% over #601** (0.001614202339036103). The conservative model gives 0.001621285086572193. The dispatch is ck ×44, atm3 ×22, jp8 ×6. The value comes from `ASSEMBLY.json` of the strict `verify.py` run on this package's literal owner map. **Stacked on #601** (open); the diff includes #601's package until it merges.

The complex side binds. The bit supplier value (#543, 0.0016538) is above the complex bound, so κ is the same with or without the bit cap.

### What changes relative to #601
In every call, **14 cold factory-scratch helpers** (`S b.10`, one per factory block) end at a **4-dimensional frame** instead of FULL, so their residual width drops from 9 to 4. One typed step, `cold_end`, is appended to each provider chain (ck, atm3, jp8) after `hyperplane_end`. It has three parts:
1. **Premix:** 142 rank-0 gates at frame `[]` at the head of section A, after the entry adapters and paid wrappers. They swap `S b.0`/`S b.10` dirt and fan the candidate's initial value out over `S b.1…S b.7`. The compensation reads no cold-ended helper.
2. **Low-frame cleanup:** four multi-gate tail gates per candidate at its frame U_b (`h += −½·P_a`, `h += P_b`, `P_c += h`, `P_d += h`). After them, h's row and column of the state are unit vectors.
3. **Exact FULL remainder:** a dyadic Gauss–Jordan refactorisation of the rest of the inverse, touching no helper that ends below FULL.

The local profile changes by {1:+28, 5:+14, 6:−28} per call per provider. The literal owner map comes from an exact pattern-restricted CP-SAT model (one helper per port per call, expanded by Kőnig edge colouring, warm-started from an annealed map) under every inherited window, family and capacity constraint.

**Necessary condition used throughout:** h can end at U only if, at the end of B, the supports of its row in the inverse state map and of its dirt column both lie in the registers whose end-of-B frames lie in U. The premix collapses each candidate's dirt column to three low-frame registers.

### Why the cold ends are legitimate
- **Lean:** #599 (`hpe_labels_multi`, `hpe_word_multi`, `exact_cold`) covers multi-gate tails and an unrestricted entrance (E = ⊥), building on #593. It is now merged.
- **(N) for every (0, U_b) pair** is checked exactly, global phase included (`hpe_adapters_local.py`), with wrapper mutants rejected.
- **The refactored cleanup is not trusted.** It is accepted only for words marked `refactored_cleanup`: non-target registers only, dyadic additions with signed binary scales, and the arbitrary-dirt endpoint replay of the full program exact in both orientations. The transport also checks the row and column cone conditions.
- **Wrapper order** is enforced twice: by the transport's zero-frame assertion, and by an event-level check in `hpe_audit_local.py` with a negative control (a premix gate hoisted before the pre-wrapper).
- **The verifier changes are inert** for words without cold ends.

### Checks
```sh
research/complex-571-cold14/verify.sh /tmp/complex-571-cold14 ..   # kappa 0.00162128508944984
```
- **Fresh-archive receipt:** strict `verify.py` from a fresh `git archive` of this head, with no baseline reuse, gives `PASS_COLD14_NATIVE_COMPLEX_AND_CITED_BIT` and κ 0.00162128508944984 (exit 0).
- **Full rebuild:** `verify.py` rebuilds the three provider words through their typed chains, with pinned hashes and paired controls.
- **Local replay:** it runs exact scalar replay with the cone pre-check, both reflected ledgers, the independent local replay with mutants, exact wrappers and all phase edges.
- **Global:** it runs binding with the physical owner audit, a fresh finite invoice with both moment engines, and the assembly, phase-timing and generated-identity controls.
- **Independent audit (a separate Claude agent's re-implementation):** the three cold words replay exactly (forward, dual, inverse-reverse and random-dirt). There are 0 nesting violations, and the cone fits are tight at 60/60 per word. The compensation reads no wrapped helper. The chain-derived profile reproduces the conservative κ via `b_exact`. Every word-level mutant is rejected, with one exception: declaring a candidate FULL-ended is legal but unpriced, so only the profile/report check catches it.
- **Extra scalar work (disclosed):** the scalar primitive bound per call rises by about 31%; prefix bits are 41/46 of the 192 limit; and the FULL remainder has 4 addition numerators that are not powers of two.

### Future optimization
| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| LP ceiling, #601's dispatch, all three providers cold | ≈ +0.49% |
| LP ceiling, free dispatch over {ck, atm3, jp8} cold (jp8-heavy; packager's estimate, not independently checked) | ≈ +0.71% |
| this package's literal map (fixed dispatch ck 44 / atm3 22 / jp8 6) | +0.439% |

- **A jp8-heavy dispatch is the main open lever:** an exact LP with one-helper-per-port-per-call constraints matches the aggregate LP, so time-refinability does not bind at the LP level, and the remaining gap is integrality and search. On this dispatch the owner-map headroom is ≈ 0.06 pt.
- **End dimension:** d = 4 is the best end dimension for these units. Raising it lifts one partner and adds 2ψ(d−4) + ψ(9−d) − ψ(5) to the local cost (ψ(r) = r·ln(73/r)), which exceeds the remaining hosting headroom.
- **Unit supply:** the 14 units per word are not certified optimal here.

**Credits:**
- **jeremykothe2:** #591, #592, #593, #596, #600 and #601 (the hyperplane-end mechanism, verifier, Lean and the base packages).
- **icekylinx:** #531 and #535.
- **DreamingOfClouds:** #509, #516 and #599 (Lean).
- The pinned #568, #569, #571, #575 and #583 packages and their authors are listed in NOTICE.md.

The approach borrows from the uncomputation literature: Bennett 1989; Gidney 2015; Häner–Roetteler–Svore 2017.

DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code.

title: [Lean] Prove the pinned PR588 native Real moment bound
body:
## Historical PR588 native Real moment, exact source-bound publication

This package publishes seven already accepted Lean sources and retains two public PR585 moment prerequisites. The resulting nine-source closure has 31 complete axiom probes: 20 from the seven fresh public roots and 11 from the two retained roots. All included Lean bytes match the accepted research sources.

The author-checked historical source context is main `9594b61042164a27a31e44d8c3197f231470eda0`, whose conditional selected κ is **400569730495803 / 250000000000000000 = 0.001602278921983212**. This is the source-matched context for the PR588 data proved here.

The intended publication base is current main `5996f9043c27bafa90b23e1c937de92a738f1a76`, subject to the publisher's final main recheck. Its separately author-read conditional selected κ is **16127213726553 / 10000000000000000 = 0.0016127213726553**, from the PR596 selection. The package does not replace its historical PR588 inputs with that newer profile or prove the newer selected endpoint.

The accepted theorem bounds the exact nine-term native expression Σ (r·c)/(73·7168) · exp(b·log(73/r)), at b = 802425169927850686731 / 500000000000000000000000, by the source's single outward-ceiling rational upper. The upper minus one is exactly −696193 / 250000000000000000000000000000, so the finite Real moment is strictly below one. The selected native branch has no fallback summand. Conservative-complex and bit branches retain their own surcharge models and are outside this package.

Four PR588 files provide the rank-30 finite/Real logarithm unit and native rational/Real aggregate. Three unchanged, previously unpublished support files provide generic exponential enclosure, logarithm units, and executable outward rounding. PR585 at `809915a264d4fbe1f7597cc13da3610dc4d52f15` supplies the two retained rational moment modules. Runtime inventory provenance comes from the exact PR526 base, the selected PR573 extension subset, and 158 additional rows, forming the accepted 3,260-module cache.

The isolated public reproduction passed with exactly two retained outputs and seven serial fresh roots. Fresh compiler time totaled 50.832447741 seconds; actual FIFO wait totaled 33.034372293 seconds. Peak VM was 3,095,539,712 bytes. All nine objects match their references, and all 31 complete probes are clean. Five raw logs match byte-for-byte; four logs differ only by 16 explicitly checked source-path substitutions in preserved warning lines. The measured public status and receipt references live in REPLAY_SUMMARY.json. Every root met the existing 60-second/4-GiB hard and 40-second/3.5-GiB review limits.

Bootstrap and outer-parameter/slack proofs are outside this package. title: Niemeier research (no κ claim): operator factors and paid spinor circuits
body:
**No κ claim.** This PR records the Niemeier follow-up to #598: exact lattice factorizations, transformations of the scalar computation, constructed compensation subwords, and scoped explanations of why the tested routes do not yet improve the exponent. It adds only `research/niemeier-lattices/`; the production suppliers and selected exponent certificate are unchanged.

### Results and scope

| Result | Evidence and limitation |
|---|---|
| Census of all 23 rooted Niemeier systems; explicit D24+, E8³ and E8² scalar factors | Exact shell counts and identities. The symmetric Pauli factor for E8² has 816 centers and support bill 12,752. The remaining 21 glue-dependent systems are still open. |
| Rational 16-dimensional bit addresses for E8² and D16+ | Each full shell has 30,960 ports and binary decoder rank 815. The complex E8² compensation `I-K` has full rank 30,960, so small kernel rank does not make compensation free. |
| A D16 spinor computation in a square-zero algebra | The transformed operator factors into 35 commuting shears, totaling 2,240 additions **in that basis**. Exact frame propagation and scoped all-stage bounds show why the direct full Möbius round trip consumes the saving. Partial and fused transforms are not excluded. |
| Fused clique/matching compensation with earlier cleanup | Exact dirty-state and frame replay lowers local rank mass from 1,024 to 832 per clique: **18.75% in this subword, not in κ**. The final replay checks all 1,056 input columns of a representative 256-port block and rejects an omitted cleanup operation. Proper-endpoint wrappers, spectator banks and full supplier admission remain open. |
| Explicit native E8 tensor lift and paid invoice | Exact checks cover 224 embeddings, signed port transport, spectator complements and center descents. The native scalar word is inherited, not freshly replayed. Using pinned #600 profiles, the best tested odd stage count gives nominal κ ≈ 0.000872182222, about 46% below that historical comparison. |
| Scoped residual and alternative-kernel obstructions | The rank-1,268 residual needs at least 11,412 descent ranks under the specified rank-minimal/private-copy implementation, exceeding the 7,168 surplus. The fused alternative decoder has rank 1,024 with full-dimensional nonzero image columns and no center surplus. The full-shell hybrid has rank 1,851 and an exact all-odd-stage pressure bound below 0.000448646990529330. These are not universal exclusions of Niemeier suppliers. |

The package also retains exact section and cross-factor experiments, a 135-clique E8 edge partition, conditional helper budgets, and bounded searches that failed. Sampled intermediate ranks are distinguished from final certificates. Zero-helper screens are explicitly conditional and are not presented as exponent improvements.

### Package and reproduction

Based on `main` at `5996f9043c27bafa90b23e1c937de92a738f1a76`. Requirements: Python ≥ 3.11, NumPy and SymPy. Z3 is only for optional clique discovery; it is not needed to replay the committed certificates.

```sh
python3 -B research/niemeier-lattices/verify.py --workbench
python3 -B -I -O research/niemeier-lattices/verify.py --workbench
```

Omit `--workbench` for the census, geometric factors and initial cost screens. The full driver checks the package manifest and inherited source pins, regenerates coordinate inputs, and compares saved receipts without modifying the checkout. NPZ equality is checked by arrays, not ZIP bytes; only the recorded elapsed-seconds field is excluded from JSON comparisons.

Validation: normal and optimized combined replays passed from a relocated package with only its six pinned external files; the final staged export was also replayed. The manifest inventory and corruption rejection passed, as did `git diff --cached --check`. `make gen4-bank-verify` passed all nine fresh stages and its omission controls (273 seconds). The broader `make verify`, run in an isolated checkout of the unchanged base, passed through the bank checks but **did not complete**: `frontier596-verify` / `bit543` stopped because the C++ compiler could not find `boost/multiprecision/cpp_int.hpp`. Boost headers are absent from this machine's standard include locations. This is an environment prerequisite for the inherited verifier; no full-suite pass is claimed. No formal review or full multiplication-theorem verification is claimed.

### What remains open

A gain still requires a joint routing/restoration word whose actual frame histories retain a positive center surplus, with all wrappers, spectator banks, dirty-helper cleanup and outer inequalities paid. The negative results leave redundant factorizations, shared arithmetic circuits, other endpoints and the glue-dependent Niemeier systems open. Nothing here proves worst-case O(1) indexing.

Comparison inputs are pinned historical claims, not a declaration of the current frontier: the initial costs use #592/#543; the native tensor invoice uses #600 at `dfb7b827990d7b586b3cd778e3d750c050dd4778`. The contemporary #604 proper-endpoint work is explicitly credited and is not claimed as a new idea here.

### Credits and AI disclosure

The direction follows **DominikScholz's** guidance and the suggestion attributed to **David Ryan / @davidryan59** in the supplied image. Classical lattice and code background credits **J. H. Conway, N. J. A. Sloane, Gabriele Nebe, Shoyu Nagaoka, Sho Takemori**, and the related authors listed in `SOURCES.txt`; their papers are not represented as proving these supplier deductions.

Inherited frame and Hamming-coordinate work credits **icekylinx**, with the OpenAI GPT-6 Astra assistance recorded in those sources. The accounting and helper profiles credit **Jeremy Kothe / jeremykothe2**, with disclosed Claude Opus 5.5 assistance in the omp harness, and **DreamingOfClouds**, with disclosed Claude Opus 5.5 assistance via Claude Code. The retained bit comparison credits **eumemic** and its disclosed Anthropic Claude assistance. `NOTICE` and the pinned source notices preserve the earlier lineage, including **Zhihao Chen / jacklightChen, Jacob Sussman**, the original OpenAI #109 framework, and community work maintained by **Douglas Colkitt / CrocSwap**.

**AI disclosure and authorship:** OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, running in T3 Code, developed the research, certificates, code and write-up under **DominikScholz's** direction. Apache-2.0, following the repository license. Inherited source files retain their attribution and are not presented as new authorship.

title: Independent construction: 46 hyperplane-ended helpers per call via the exact commutation condition, conditional κ = 0.001613569610580215 (below #601)
body:
**Independent construction of the 46-helper hyperplane end; no record claimed.** Conditional κ = **0.001613569610580215** (conservative model 0.001613569607722207). This is the same mechanism as #601 (jeremykothe2), which was posted first: both replace #591's first-gate rule by the exact commutation condition and end 46 helpers per call. #601 re-optimises the dispatch (ck × 45, atm3 × 21, jp8 × 6) and its RINS owner map reaches 0.001614202; this package keeps #592's dispatch (ck × 53, atm3 × 19) with its own owner map, so its value is 0.04 % lower. It is offered as a second, independently built and strictly verified witness, together with the owner-allocation tools it used (HiGHS pattern MILP, lazy cross-time Hall cuts, per-window matching; the PR520 allocator extended to per-call widths).

**Mechanism.** #591 (jeremykothe2) ends 38 entering width-8 helpers per call on a hyperplane U instead of the full frame. Its candidate rule requires the helper's single cleanup gate to be the *first* cleanup gate on both of its registers, so that it trivially commutes with the skipped cleanup prefix. Eight more helpers per call fail that rule only because their partner register is **read** by an earlier cleanup gate; two additions that merely share a source commute, so nothing obstructs the move. Replacing the rule by the exact condition (the helper's cleanup gates plus the non-commuting closure of what they pass run right after part B at the minimal common frames; here the closure is the gate itself) ends **46 helpers per call** on every provider word (ck, atm3, and jp8, which this dispatch does not use). The local paid Φ is unchanged to within 1 Φ; each call has eight more width-7 residuals.

| | #592/#596 | this PR | #601 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hyperplane-ended helpers per call | 38 | 46 | 46 |
| ck width inventory | {4:8, 5:48, 7:70, 8:102, 9:276} | {4:8, 5:48, 7:78, 8:94, 9:276} | same |
| idle remainders | {1:2, 2:1, 3:280, 12:1, 48:1969} | {3:197, 25:1, 48:1986} | dispatch 45/21/6 |
| paid profile | {1:182818, 2:34193, 3:22560, 4:14584, 5:4032, 6:4032, 8:576, 12:1, 48:1969} | {1:183968, 2:33616, 3:23053, 4:14008, 5:4032, 6:4032, 8:576, 25:1, 48:1986} | see #601 |
| LP bound on remainders for the menu (dispatch 53/19) | 42,321.7 Φ (attained within 37 Φ) | 41,862.3 Φ (attained within 28 Φ) | — |
| κ | 0.0016127213726553 (#596) | 0.001613569610580215 | 0.001614202339036103 |

Dispatch (ck × 53, atm3 × 19), call order, pinned sources (PR568 `71c99ac`, PR569 `897213a`, PR571 `b7bdc5a`, PR575 `eac6f7e`, PR583 `89be768`), the other build steps and #592's verifier code are unchanged. The owner map is renominated for the new width inventory: an exact-window MILP over port patterns (HiGHS) with lazy cross-time Hall cuts and a per-window literal matching (CP-SAT); the nominator and the allocation tools are included.

**Package** `research/complex-571-hpe46/`, a copy of #592's with: one new allowlisted step type `hyperplane_end_closure` (`code/build_hpe_closure.py`; the chosen helpers and the tail are recomputed from the input word and must equal the recipe, then #592's unchanged raw-word control audit runs and the same independent comparison as `hyperplane_end`), new `data/PLAN.json`, `data/OWNERS.json.gz`, `data/SPEC.json` and recipes, and `code/witness.py` recording pins in discovery mode (strict mode unchanged). Everything else is byte-identical to #592.

**Verification.** `verify.py` rebuilds both provider words from the pinned sources through all typed steps, localises them with #592's HPE native chain (all columns, both reflected ledgers, local controls, normalised wrappers, all phase edges), binds, emits and audits the owner map with mutation controls, prices a fresh invoice and runs both exact moment engines with the 47 outer constraints and the assembly, timing and recompression controls. The strict run passed locally with the frozen558 baseline reused from a fresh #588 replay; `RECEIPT.json`, `RESULT.json` and `STAGES.json` are in `research/complex-571-hpe46-validation/` (31 stages; 23 controller and 114 assembly mutations rejected). The README was reworded after that run, so the receipt's package manifest hash predates the final README.

**Scope.** Conditional on the same inherited assumptions as #592 (all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, analytic transfer, and Lemma A for hyperplane-ended helpers as stated in #592's PROOF-HYPERPLANE-END.md and #593's Lean). body:
# Current R420 boundary and B-XOR interfaces

Author-checked selected context: κ = 16127213726553 / 10000000000000000 = 0.0016127213726553 at main `5996f9043c27bafa90b23e1c937de92a738f1a76`. The selected bit supplier is PR543, commit `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`. This is a conditional source context, not a proved κ or integer-multiplication theorem.

## What is checked

Seven new source files consume four byte-exact public PR590 dependencies. The complete closure is 317 official Lean 4.21.0 core modules plus 11 local modules. Mathlib is not required. No PR597 module or unpublished generic helper is imported.

- `CurrentR420BoundaryData`: current ordered literal data, a bound-carrying frame-table permutation, and fresh Fin660/Fin661 interfaces.
- `CurrentR420FrameIndexCheck`: three shape/index facts. A finite `isPerm` certificate and public list theorems derive the original sorted-equality interface without evaluating merge sort.
- `CurrentR420FrameBoundaryCheck`: seven frame/entrance/final/retained-host facts. Frame-row bounds reuse the accepted historical table symbolically.
- `CurrentR420BBandCheck`: eleven facts for the exact 120/597/120 B bands, all 837 gates and 1,077 ordered operand occurrences.
- `CurrentR420ScatterFacts`: six finite facts for 120 scatter rows, 568 retained indices, nine helpers and temporary index 660 in Fin661.
- `CurrentR420BoundaryCheck`: import-only restoration of all 27 original public facts. It evaluates no theorem body or finite predicate.
- `CurrentR420PhaseBXor`: exact ordered Boolean decoding, helper preservation and target-translation semantics for B.

There are 61 printed probe records for the new files, representing 34 distinct declarations: the import-only wrapper deliberately prints the 27 finite facts again. The four retained dependencies contribute 14 additional probe records. Every recorded axiom set is standard-only; no rejected or partial module is accepted.

## The semantic boundary

Original registers are Fin660: sources 0–119, targets 120–239 and helpers 240–659. The middle 597 B gates write source registers. Their operands consist of 477 source reads followed by 120 helper reads. The last 120 gates contain 120 source and 240 helper operand occurrences.

The scalar interpreter retains gate and operand order, multiplicity and frame IDs. It applies sequential Boolean XOR updates. For arbitrary original input bits, B preserves every helper bit. Each output target equals its initial target bit XOR the contribution computed from the same state with targets erased. That contribution is independent of the initial target bits and need not be zero. Source registers are allowed to change.

The scalar interpreter carries frame metadata but does not prove physical frame transport. The Fin661 temporary facts are only domain/exclusion facts. No current COPY/ERASE lifecycle or restoration of an initially dirty temporary is claimed here.

## Source binding and reuse

The current source is `research/e8-bit-r420/data/bitE8mut-r420.json.gz`, compressed SHA256 `9721a3819efd68307f66f00d84a952eb28eb7c3ad2ce79653ce295c98a764784`; its decoded SHA256 is `e597e3885c0a8daa262afa5985ee2930443329126aece76d33159d81882bdcc2`. All 49 selected R420 package files agree between the original 9594 snapshot and selected 5996. The current 672-frame order is proved to permute the accepted old table; the current typed domains and endpoint/host facts are checked afresh.

The required PR590 modules are `SelectedBitCarrierBoundaryData`, `SelectedBitCarrierBoundaryCheck`, `SelectedBitCarrierPhaseBData` and `BitXorTargetTranslation`. Their source/object identities and public probe/log requirements are in `DEPENDENCIES.json`. A successful predecessor build supplies these four accepted objects. They are retained rather than compiled again. No historical R489/R480 typed theorem is renamed into a current instance.

`MANIFEST.json` lists every origin, exact source hash, import and ordered probe. `ACCEPTED_CHECKS.json` records the immutable local and public-prefix kernel evidence. `REPLAY_SUMMARY.json` owns the single mutable reproduction result. The standalone retained-prefix checker and its concrete offline instructions are supplied in the reviewed publication completion.

## Preserved failures and costs

The original combined 27-fact module failed allocation at 25.649962 seconds and 4,272,771,072 bytes VM, without an accepted object. Three later index attempts failed on kernel sort reduction or import syntax. Their exact evidence remains preserved. The successful recovery uses separate roots and a symbolic permutation proof, retaining the original public statements. It is not an equivalent whole-check speedup measurement.

The seven included source modules have independently reviewed local passes totaling 32.303836 compiler seconds; the largest observed VM was 1,260,244,992 bytes. These are prior research measurements, not a prediction of a public replay. Compiler, FIFO and post-slot guard times remain separately recorded. The intended bounds remain 60 seconds / 4 GiB hard and 45 seconds / 3.5 GiB review per root, stopping on the first failure or review event.

- Actual full A/C typed bindings and the selected cleanup composition
- D parity/compensation equality
- The current 661-register COPY/scatter lifecycle instance
- Physical/common-frame transport, provider and hosting conditions, and all-size multiplication transfer

Generic reversal/chunk/two-level cleanup results are separate and are not needed by this package. This completed boundary does not wait on those remaining source-specific instances.

Apache-2.0. The R420 supplier was prepared by eumemic with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance. Complete current and carrier-ancestry notices are preserved in `SUPPLIER_NOTICE.md` and `PR493_NOTICE.md`. These Lean certificates were prepared with OpenAI assistance, reusing the exact public PR590 proofs and official Lean core APIs.

## Offline retained-prefix reproduction

Use the exact PR590 package and a successful eight-root PR590 public build. This checker validates four required source/object/probe records and preserves all eight predecessor roots, including the four that are not imported here. It compiles only the seven included sources in the manifest's order.

With the existing official Lean 4.21.0 Linux distribution, run from this package:

```sh
python3 check.py --lean /path/to/lean-4.21.0-linux/bin/lean \

```

The local profile changes by {1:+6, 2:−4} per word. The ends reuse PR604's `cold_end` machinery, extended to entering helpers: a premix at frame E, multi-gate tails at U, and the exact dyadic Gauss–Jordan remainder. - The (E, U) pair is Lean pair 3 of PR593 (`exact_N_pair3`), so (N) is proved, global phase included. Multi-gate tails with an arbitrary entrance are PR599's `hpe_word_multi`.

title: Prove uniform prime-power cyclic inverse bounds (no κ claim)
body:
The prior cyclic inverse notes establish finite invertibility at roots of unity. That does not give a conditioning bound independent of the cyclic length. This package proves such a bound for every prime-power kernel order, including dyadic orders, and every primitive root choice.

For `n=r-1`, `D=phi(r)`, and `H=2^r-1`, it proves `|P(z)| >= delta = 1/(2rn H^(nD-1))` on the entire unit circle. For every unit scalar `tau`, cyclic length `L`, and integer shift step `w`, it then proves `||P(tau Z_L^w)^-1||_infinity <= delta^-1 + 2nH/(r delta^2)`. Finite products and unit diagonal gauges retain the stated bound. Radix two has a separate bound of two.

The proof uses integral tail coefficients, prime-power residue reduction, a nonzero Sylvester determinant, paired field embeddings, cofactor bounds, and an absolutely convergent Fourier series. The logarithm of the inverse upper bound is `O(r^2 phi(r))`; no dependency on cyclic length remains.

Validation:
- The written proof passed a separate AI-assisted mathematical review.
- The standard-library engine checks eight exact cyclotomic cases; isolated optimized Python gives the committed deterministic record.
- An independent SymPy engine matches all eight determinants and norms, checks an extra primitive choice, and verifies 36 actual cyclic inverse products. Both engines reject the intended unit-root and omitted-conjugation controls.
- Both engines pass from a relocated standalone package with no historical workspace inputs.
- `make verify` passed on pinned main `5996f9043c27bafa90b23e1c937de92a738f1a76`, including `make gen4-bank-verify`, `make frontier596-verify`, all remaining tests, and patch applicability checks. `git diff --cached --check` passed.

This is a scoped analytic contribution, with **no new integer kappa, complex b, BIT c, or paid inversion algorithm**. Efficient preparation, combined precision and rounded execution, restoration, and tape costs remain open. The scalar theorem uses standard mathematical facts; any multiplication application still needs the original algorithmic interfaces. No all-composite, full multiplication theorem, practical speedup, literature priority, or maintainer acceptance claim is made.

Credits and exact pins are in `SOURCE.json` and `NOTICE.md`: OpenAI's exact-DFT kernel, classical q-Pochhammer/Newton factorization (Alexey Kuznetsov), and prior unpublished local cyclic inverse work. title: Uniform rounded prime-power cyclic inversion (no κ claim)
body:
Supplies a rounded inverse for the prime-power cyclic kernels of PR621. Stable first-order factors use two scans, including the periodic closure. The full neighboring-shift inverse uses `O(r)` array passes and `p+O(r^4)` precision, independent of cyclic length. The proof charges approximate factor preparation, coefficient verification and unit-phase approximation. The extension to independently varying unit phases at every position has the same length-independent precision bound, with every phase oracle charged.

The standard bit-model bound is `soft-O((Lr+r^3)(p+r^4))`. Its preparation argument uses the cited Pan factorization and fast elementary-function algorithms. The reference root finder only nominates candidates; exact coefficient enclosures, factor products and rounding budgets certify them. Those worst-case preparation algorithms are not implemented here.

A separate inverse-shear construction now restores the source and `ceil(log2(r-1))` borrowed dirty arrays exactly. Causal integer lifts implement each stable factor; balanced commutators compose them. It uses `O(r^2)` factor calls and `O(p+log(D+1)+r^5)` precision for initial magnitude bound `D`, independent of cyclic length. It permits charged clean scalar arithmetic and read-only phase access; reversible bit arithmetic and a common-label word are not supplied. The rounded target increment may depend on the initial dirt within the proved error bound.

Arbitrary strides have an explicit two-sort reduction, with `O(L(B+log L)log L)` routing cost. That can become `O(Lp^2)`, so the package exposes the remaining layout requirement. Scheduling the borrowed arrays in the complete transform, full-transform composition, normalization, bit compilation and the multiplication reduction remain open. **No new integer κ, complex b, BIT c, practical speedup or literature-priority claim.**

title: Research notes (no κ claim): #109 and lower bounds, the coding gap, a Lorentzian minrank obstruction, and a loss chain
body:
**No κ claim.** This PR adds only `research/lower-bounds-coding-gap/`, which contains four notes, their scripts and
DRUP proofs. No supplier, certificate or existing file changes. Based on `main` at `17ce0c7`.

## Summary

| # | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #109 contradicts no unconditional lower bound for multiplication. Each bound fails on a stated hypothesis (on-line, bounded coefficients, well-conditioning, or Li–Li). | audit |
| 1 | **Lemma B′:** #109's machine can be made oblivious at the same κ: fixed-width scalars, compute-both branches, and an oblivious Schönhage–Strassen whose log log factor fits the p^κ margin that `08-assembly.tex` already reserves. So **if #109's Theorem 1 holds, multiplication has bounded-degree Boolean circuits of size O(n(log n)^{1−κ})**. | proved, given a procedure-by-procedure audit (included) |
| 1 | **If #109 holds, on-line multitape multiplication is slower than off-line by Ω((log n)^κ)** (Paterson–Fischer–Meyer). So no relaxed variant of #109's transforms can have (log n)^{o(1)} overhead. | proved, given #109 |
| 2 | **The rank saving is a coding gap.** On #109's labelled exchange network, weighted by rank or subspace distance, coding achieves rate 1 while flow ≤ (s + 2W)/(Wm + 2W). This is < 1 exactly when s < Wm. It reproduces the paper's η exactly, and it is the same mechanism as dysfunctor's 33-vertex Li–Li counterexample, whose flow we re-certify as exactly 149/150. | proved (analytic LP dual) + exact |
| 3 | **I_{11,1} and I_{13,1} (triples + pairs) have fitting minrank n, not n − 1**, over every field of characteristic ≠ 2. E8 = I_{9,1} is the case n − 9 = 0. | proved; SAT step exhaustive with drat-trim-checked DRUP proofs; exact ranks over Q |
| 4 | **Loss chain**: a ≈ (1/m)(D/W)/L_ent, with L_ent = ln m − E ln r. It reproduces gen4, #493, #501, #589 and the selected #596 supplier to < 10⁻⁸; the #596 row gives main's κ. There is also a piece-count remark: under H1–H6 no label family reaches κ → 1 (copy-free windows give a ≲ 0.31/(h − 1)). | exact; Theorems 1 and 4 proved; H6 assumed |

## What is new compared with prior work

- **Li–Li is already refuted** (2026-10-07), by Zhang–B. Li–Z. Li (arXiv 2610.09367, already cited in
  `docs/research/stronger-rank-screens.md`), by Braverman–He (arXiv 2610.10108), and by
  [dysfunctor/network-coding-counterexample](https://github.com/dysfunctor/network-coding-counterexample), which
  builds its network from #109's XOR swap. So "#109 ⇒ ¬Li–Li" (via AFKL) is moot and gives no error signal in either
  direction. Note 1 says this explicitly. **What is new is Lemma B′, the circuit corollary and the on-line/off-line
  separation.** We found neither in the preprint, the hub (PRs and comments through #633), openai/math, AFKL,
  HvdH 2021/2025 or the public discussion.
- Note 2 generalises dysfunctor's observation from the XOR swap to the rank-weighted motif with any η > 0, as an
  identity. The 33-vertex flow value is an independent re-check, not a new result.
- Note 1's Ailon row cites #621 and #628 (chafreaky): their length-independent but exponential-in-r conditioning
  bounds for the prime-power cyclic inverses are consistent with the row.
- Note 3 covers a family that #446, #595 (C.6), #598 and #606 (DominikScholz), #620 (GamingPuzzled; ADE and number-field label screens, with #630's E6 → D6 correction by vectorsss), hipotures' lattice screen and
  Sussman's notes do not cover. Unlike #595 C.6, its SAT step ships proof logs.
- Note 4 is complementary to #595 (DreamingOfClouds) and #602 (artuskg). #595's κ ≤ 5.1595·10⁻³ is much tighter
  inside its scope, and its §A.5/§C.7/§E already price helpers, descents and the log-gap. The note claims only the
  four-factor identity and a hypothesis-light piece-count bound. It also lists the route-specific ceilings it sits
  beside: #183, #458, #203, #201 and Swapnil Jain's P1/P2.
- **Dropped as duplicate:** our "a saving needs different scalar and label characteristics" lemma (Swapnil Jain's
  closed ideas; Sussman's mod-2 argument), our frozen-word and E8-architecture ceilings (superseded by #595), and
  our fixed-word retiming optimality results (#556, #557).

## Scope

- Notes 1–2 concern consequences of #109's Theorem 1 *if it holds*. They neither support nor refute it.
- Note 3 is a minrank statement about two graphs. It bounds no supplier, and the general odd-n claim is a conjecture.
- Note 4's remark assumes H1–H6. H6 is checked on the certified words but not proved in general, and the remark is
  not a universal ceiling.
- "Proved" means a written argument checked only by its authors. Nothing here is formalised in Lean, and certificate
  success is not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/lower-bounds-coding-gap/requirements.txt
DYSFUNCTOR=/path/to/network-coding-counterexample DRAT_TRIM=/path/to/drat-trim \
  bash research/lower-bounds-coding-gap/verify.sh /fresh/out
```

The run took about 75 s from a fresh venv (Python 3.14.4, WSL Ubuntu) on the rebased branch, and every step printed PASS:

- manifest;
- η exact;
- flow 149/150 exact;
- 10,395 cliques;
- final span 7/10/12;
- σ-model 0/130 violations;
- N = 6, 8, 10, 12 UNSAT with drat-trim `s VERIFIED` (fresh and shipped proofs);
- loss chain roots;
- piece-count certificates.

Without `DYSFUNCTOR` the flow check prints SKIP. Without `DRAT_TRIM` the proofs are written and the CNFs compared
byte-for-byte, but the proofs are not checked.

## Attribution and AI disclosure

Prepared by @ShikeChen01 with substantial assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code. AI agents
drafted the arguments, the audit and the scripts. Apache-2.0. Upstream: OpenAI #109. Prior work used or cited:
dysfunctor; Zhang, B. Li and Z. Li; Braverman and He; Afshani, Freksen, Kamma and Larsen; Harvey and van der Hoeven;
Jacob Sussman (wht-power-saving-lean); Swapnil Jain; hipotures; DreamingOfClouds (#446, #589, #595); artuskg (#602);
DominikScholz (#598, #606); GamingPuzzled (#620); vectorsss (#630); chafreaky (#621, #628); jeremykothe2 (#596); eumemic (#493, #501). Details are in `NOTICE.md`.

This extends the pinned [#635](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/635) construction with a changed arbitrary-helper-input factory and 44 rank-four cold endpoints. It is one new commit based on main at `17ce0c79b7b51c2634b439ea5a2b754f09909693`.

T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1649483702558979}{10^{18}}=0.001649483702558979.
$$

The saving is **0.80931% above #635**. This compares exponent savings, not practical runtime. The conservative complex model separately certifies κ `0.001649483699681650`.

This changes how arbitrary initial helper values propagate while preserving the clean operands. The resulting protected-column and inverse-support calculation exposes 44 rank-four cold directions. Exact dyadic input premixes, low-frame tails and a recomputed FULL inverse realize them. title: Research: the complex delivery layer is rigid — target hosting and raw-face sharing closed exactly
body:
**Research note; no κ claim.** Adds only `research/complex-delivery-rigidity/` (README, scripts, results, manifest). No supplier, certificate, verifier or existing file changes. Based on `main` at `17ce0c7`.

## Two exact negative results on the K-triangle word (#622 lineage)

Slot copies and the in-place mixing of the 8-sums are about 15 % of the complex local rank mass. Two proposed ways to remove them, "group delivery" (my #520 §3) and target-hosted / output-borrowed registers (#571's open list), are closed on this word family:

1. **No target can host a face or 8-sum for other targets.** Checked on all 14 blocks from the pinned constructor, executed unchanged with a role dump: a target's cap contains an 8-sum's span iff it consumes it (112/112); two consumers have consistent coefficient ratios only in opposite tetrads (ratio `σ_x[p0]σ_z[p0]`, constant on their 3 shared keys), while same-tetrad pairs share 2 keys with opposite ratios; a target's own-row frame lies only in same-tetrad caps; and the own read cannot be deferred (own registers are never written after their last target read, but the module's next read lifts the frame out of the cap in all 112 cases). Hence every cross-tetrad target-to-target read is frame-illegal and same-tetrad sharing is the existing butterfly, once per target. A CP-SAT read-ordering model with exact atom flow confirms the 8-sum-level floor: pure registers need 20 copies per block (bound 12) against the 8 the word uses with 2×2 mixes.

2. **No read order of face registers removes the slot copies.** In the raw word no register is read by two targets of the same block; all 120 multi-reader registers are #531's cross-block raw reads. The pollution-tolerance census over all 168 (key, consumer-block) incidences shows a target's frame after the butterfly, or after its own row plus the selected faces, is inside the caps of no consumer group (0/1344 each); only the bare own-row frame is tolerated: 160/448 foreign cases for selected incidences (56 are used by #531), 64/896 for non-selected ones, and 96 of the 112 non-selected incidences have no tolerated foreign target at any stage.

So under the hub's rules (monotone frames, target frames inside `u_t^⊥`, helpers never reading targets, own row first) the delivery layer is at its floor; #646's measured loss from more skeleton atoms and #645's gain in the factory layer point the same way. The README states what a rule-level change would have to touch.

## Reproduction

```sh
sh research/complex-delivery-rigidity/reproduce.sh /tmp/delivery-rigidity
```

Standard library only; `order_model.py` needs `ortools` and is skipped otherwise (its recorded runs are in `results/`). The constructor from `research/complex-571-cold14-k492` and the inputs from `research/direct-delivery504-global` are read in place and not modified.

icekylinx (#425/#433/#531 construction, SAME504 factory), jeremykothe2 (#622 constructor and schedule, hyperplane ends), DreamingOfClouds (#604 cold ends), DominikScholz (#571 factory floor and open list), chafreaky, eumemic and the #446 authors. title: No new κ: the square-root wall — every current assembly has κ < 1/2 (checked)
body:
**No new κ.** This adds a structural ceiling that applies to the manuscript and to every assembly in the repository.

**Theorem.** An algorithm built on the shared framework runs in time Ω(n·√(log n)), so κ ≤ 1/2. Each assembly's own accounting makes this strict: κ < (1 − δ)/2 < 1/2.

## Change and mathematical scope

The package is `research/sqrt-log-wall/`: `README.md` (statement and proof), `wall_check.py` (standard library only), `NOTICE.md` and `LICENSE`, plus one path-filtered workflow. No existing file changes.

Every assembly keeps the manuscript's reduction (`upstream/build/sections/08-assembly.tex`):

- **The box.** A d-axis cyclic transform with `Tp = Θ(n)` stored bits and axis lengths `t_i ≤ r = 2^ℓ`, so `dℓ ≥ log₂ T`.
- **One pass per butterfly level.** ℓ simultaneous rounds.
- **One pass per axis.** d Gaussian line passes, applied axis by axis.
- **Two cost rows.** The dimension row with margin ε (packed products) and the scalar-work row with margin 1 − ε − δ (chirps, twists and scalar products).

**Proof.**
- Each pass reads every stored bit, so the time is at least (d + ℓ)V ≥ 2√(dℓ)·V ≥ 2√(log₂ T)·V = Ω(n√log n). Hence κ ≤ 1/2.
- The rows require κ < ε and κ < 1 − ε − δ. Since max_ε min(ε, 1 − ε − δ) = (1 − δ)/2 and every assembly has δ > 0, the bound is strict.
- **Network side.** The butterfly row's margin is εq with q = 1 − λ′ < 1 − τ = a, so κ < min(εa, 1 − ε) ≤ a/(1 + a) < 1/2.

**Escaping the wall** needs a different skeleton: several butterfly levels per pass, fewer than d axis sweeps, or a reduction other than the d-axis box. Better networks, frames, recurrences, constants or parameters cannot cross it.

## Where things stand

| assembly | κ | below 1/2 by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| selected record (`certificates/selected-result.json`, research outer engine) | 1.635527·10⁻³ | 306× |
| best tex assembly (`notes/paired-cube-assembly.tex`) | 4.609169·10⁻⁴ | 1085× |
| manuscript (`08-assembly.tex`; its εC₁ < 1 with C₁ = 20 caps it at 1/20) | 2⁻¹⁸² | — |

- **Selected record.** The certificate's margin gaps give ε = 0.998364 and δ = 1.25·10⁻²⁵. The binding rows are εq and 1 − ε − δ ≈ q, so κ ≈ a, the bit-network saving.
- **Inside the wall.** The real limit is the network saving a, and no all-network bound on a is known.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/sqrt-log-wall/wall_check.py` prints `PASS_SQUARE_ROOT_WALL_REDUCTION` (about 9 s). It passed locally on Python 3.12 and 3.14 against main at `17ce0c79`. It checks, from source text and the certificate:

1. 11 verbatim facts of the manuscript's reduction, rows and parameters;
2. both margins and the boxed κ in each of the nine assembly notes;
3. `dimension=eps`, `scalar_work=1-eps-delta` and the margin-above-κ slacks in all 122 research outer engines that define margins;
4. ε, δ and q for the selected record, recovered exactly from its certificate's outer table, with κ < min(ε, 1 − ε − δ) ≤ (1 − δ)/2 and κ < εq < q/(1 + q) < 1/2 in rational arithmetic;
5. d + ⌈log₂T/d⌉ ≥ 2√(log₂ T) for every log₂ T ≤ 4096 and every d.

As a negative control, changing the manuscript's `g_7=\epsilon` makes the check fail with exit status 1. CI runs the check on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Scope

- This is a statement about the framework's schedule and accounting, not a lower bound for integer multiplication in general.
- The pass bound assumes each level round and axis pass reads the whole box, as every current assembly does.
- No Lean proof is claimed.

## Credits and AI disclosure

Prepared by DaysSky with assistance from Claude. The manuscript, the assembly notes, the research engines and the selected certificate are read unchanged and keep their own credits.

title: Composite cyclic inverses: exact certificates and modular lifting
body:
Ali Romman's #621 proves uniform cyclic-kernel conditioning for prime-power radices and leaves other composites outside its claim. This package adds an **integral seed-certificate lifting mechanism for specified composite families**, together with six stronger fixed-radix certificates. **No new κ is claimed.**

If `A f_s+B f_s*=d` is an integral Bézout identity and p is prime with p not dividing s*d, the written proof establishes nonvanishing for `r=s*p^a` for **every a>=1 and every primitive root choice**. Reduction modulo p sends the two integral kernels to `z^(r-s) f_s` and `f_s*`; modular coprimality then lifts back to characteristic zero. Independently checked seeds give:

| Family | Condition on prime p |
|---|---|
| `r=2*p^a` | p not in {2,3} |
| `r=3*p^a` | p not in {3,43} |
| `r=4*p^a` | p not in {2,37} |

The proof handles reciprocal degree loss explicitly. #621's inherited norm/cofactor and Fourier arguments supply quantitative circle and inverse-norm bounds uniform in cyclic length, integer stride and unit scalar gauge. Excluded primes limit this modular route; they are not characteristic-zero counterexamples. This is not a theorem for all composite radices.

Separate exact certificates at **6, 10, 12, 14, 15 and 18** cover all 30 primitive embeddings symbolically and give sharper explicit rational bounds. The standard-library checker reconstructs cyclotomic polynomials and tail-product kernels without importing the SymPy generator or either predecessor checker. title: Independent verification: exact CRT resultants through radix 27
body:
This independently checks the nonzero conjugate-reciprocal Sylvester determinant, complete Bezout identity and integral norm used in Ali Romman's incorporated #621 prime-power inverse proof. A new standard-library implementation evaluates every primitive embedding in split finite fields, then reconstructs exact integer coefficients using CRT and a proved coefficient bound. Integer polynomial replay and a separate Bareiss norm calculation check the reconstructed data.

Completed finite coverage: radices 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 16, 25 and 27; 80 primitive embeddings; 193 split-prime runs; 2,918 determinant/adjugate evaluations. All eight published determinant/norm examples match exactly. This changes both arithmetic method and coverage beyond the rational-field/SymPy engines through radix 11. Concurrent #628's rounded inverse and radix-16 kernel evidence are credited; radix-25/27 exact resultant evidence and bounded CRT are distinct. No new kappa or uniform theorem is claimed.

Base: `17ce0c79b7b51c2634b439ea5a2b754f09909693`. Reviewed #621 source head: `520774462b19b29af41554b74def31f9d01e997e`. Upstream's refreshed `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60` changes only CONTRIBUTING.md. The selected frontier and upstream/ are unchanged. Assignment seed 83 and the local claim/result are retained.

Reproduce with Python 3.9+ and no external dependencies:
```sh
python3 -B research/prime-power-resultant-crt/verify.py --check research/prime-power-resultant-crt/RESULTS.json
```
Expected: `PASS 80 primitive embeddings; 8 predecessor matches; 8 negative controls`.

Validation: identical receipts on Python 3.9/3.11/3.13, including isolated optimized execution; six additional tests against permutation/minor determinants and all 1,000 trace dual-basis identities; meaningful CRT, conjugation, cofactor, source-pin and singular-root controls. The original primary checker, selected-record binding and complete historical `make gen4-bank-verify` pass. One full `make verify` passed its earlier groups and gen4, then stopped at the unchanged bit543 C++ cohort because Boost headers are missing locally; no full-suite pass is claimed. The scoped Linux Python 3.11/3.13 workflow passed on this exact commit: [CI run](https://github.com/swbiggart/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38340969484). Wider inherited CI is separate. See VALIDATION.md for exact evidence and limits.

Changes are confined to one new research package and its scoped workflow. The finite checks do not prove the all-prime-power analytic theorem, paid preparation, rounding/restoration, tape/compiler interfaces or multiplication theorem. Preserves predecessor and kernel attribution under Apache-2.0. Contribution by Scott Woolsey Biggart (swbiggart), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No delegated or human review is claimed.

title: Research: exact star-decoder hierarchies, target budgets, and COPY bounds
body:
This research contribution determines sharp information thresholds for signed proper-star decoders and proves physical COPY obstructions for explicitly defined classes. It adds uniform proofs, exact prescribed-target criteria, and independent finite certificates. **There is no new multiplication coefficient or claimed physical supplier.**

For `q=p-k>=3`, the first five generalized weights are now exactly
`(2q+2,4q+3,6q+3,8q+2,10q)`. At the boundary `q=2,k>=4`, an affine cube gives `(6,11,14,15,16)`: three, four, or five selectable targets all require eleven deletions. These deletion counts measure information recovery; the physical notes separately charge copied frame dimensions and inherited endpoint schedules.

### Results and review entry points

Only `research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/` changes. Start with its README.

- **Uniform higher weights:** `HIGHER-WEIGHTS.md`, `FOURTH-WEIGHT.md`, and `FIFTH-WEIGHT.md` prove the first five weights for every `k>=2,q>=3`. Every second-weight word is a sum of two adjacent minimum stars. Every rank-three and rank-four optimum is a star clique; every rank-five optimum is a five-star clique for `q>=4`. The notes give exact counts and prescribed-target independence criteria. The `q=3` rank-five equality classification remains open.
- **Exceptional cube geometry:** `CUBE-OPTIMIZERS.md` proves exact ordinary-cube shortening and classifies all rank-three through rank-five optima for `q=2,k>=4`. Prescribed target sets of those sizes attain eleven deletions exactly when they use the same original pairs and have affinely independent signs.
- **Arbitrary graph targets:** `HIGHER-GRAPH.md` gives the complete `k=2` generalized-weight hierarchies. `GRAPH-TARGETS.md` adds exact partition formulations for arbitrary target sets, a capacity-matching formula for every forest in the nonempty-star code, and every prescribed triple budget in both codes. These results go beyond choosing a favorable target set.
- **Core shortening:** `CORE-SHORTENING.md` identifies the full unrestricted-sign shortening on `k-2` original pairs at `q=3`, its exact dimension, and the sharp weight-sixteen threshold of the additional polynomial layers. Simply repeating the fixed-sign graph code omits these layers.
- **Recoding and sequential copying obstruction:** `COPY-OBSTRUCTION.md` proves that an integral separating pairing with odd diagonal forces total copied frame rank `C>=v`, including arbitrary linear observation recodings, exact nonlinear postprocessing, individually readable corrections, and chronological copy-to-zero innovations under the stated monotone-frame model. Every even-size paired-port geometry with overlap-one readability satisfies the hypothesis. The inherited odd-stage ledger then has no positive deficit. The selected E8 geometry has even diagonal and is outside this result.
- **Native odd-star cost:** `ODD-NATIVE-COST.md` proves a bit-saving ceiling `c<107/66606` for every odd `k>=5` in the inherited schedule with at least five stages, accounting for source/target climbs, idle hosting, and whole banks even while granting other work free. A separately stated conditional three-stage extension excludes odd `k>=7`. Both ceilings are below the campaign-start selected coefficient. Arbitrary recoding and COPY-assisted innovations are outside this particular theorem.

Earlier uniform minimum-word rigidity, all optimal two-dimensional subcodes, and exact prescribed-pair budgets remain included. A generalized weight `d_r` yields `d_r-r` deletions for **some selectable r-target set**, not every prescribed set. Code statements cover both proper-star spaces; the original uniform overlap corrections are absorbed only at power-of-two `k`.

### Reproduction and evidence

Python 3.10+; standard library only:

```sh
for check in shortening optimizer block copy_obstruction core_shortening graph_targets; do
  python3 -I -O -B "research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/${check}_verify.py" --self-test || exit
done
for check in higher cube boundary; do
  python3 -I -O -B "research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/${check}_verify.py" --self-test || exit
done
python3 -I -O -B research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/global_verify.py --self-test
python3 -I -O -B research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/verify.py --negative-controls
```

The current campaign checkers cover 42 full-generator cube shortenings; all 187 relevant `RM(1,4)` subspaces and 6,748 target sets; complete small complementary-block models; eight exact binary/rational COPY matrix cases and a sequential-innovation fragment; full-generator original-core shortenings at `k=3,...,6` with all 1,048,576 words of the smallest code; and 4,112 complete graph target sets plus 73 triple/quadruple orbits covering 12,650 sets at `p=4`. The graph oracle directly checks 4,329,472 decoder assignments. Receipts distinguish exhaustive domains, overlapping case instances, and logical meet-in-the-middle candidate counts.

All six campaign self-tests passed isolated optimized execution, relocation, corruption rejection and failure-output preservation. The graph checker also tests atomic replacement failure cleanup. Proofs and implementations received separate AI-assisted reviews; the lead reviewed the resulting proofs and code. Earlier higher-target receipts were reproduced under Python 3.11.13 and 3.14.5; campaign receipts currently record Python 3.14.5. No human or proof-assistant verification is claimed. Finite enumeration supports the separate uniform proofs. Selected supplier cold replay, unrelated regeneration, and hosted CI are not claimed.

### Provenance and remaining work

Original base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Campaign continuation base: `7d526020fc368ce4157cd436995c2f4fcf683318`. Latest inspected main snapshot: `007664306fff84fbb1c9a1b4053b69f439764034`, whose selected record and actual #890 integration review report conditional κ `1661957774647029/10^18`; its #589-on-#555 bit supplier is unchanged. `upstream/` and selected certificates are untouched. Seed **48**, structural decoder research.

Credit **Luke Mansoor (#732)** for uniform minimum distance, **Sagar Thakrar (#725)** for the `q=1` exception, **Alishan Ladhani (#747)** for the finite `(6,4)` minimum-word classification, **ellipsi2 (#772)** for uniform ranks, and **Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (#231)** with **icekylinx/eumemic** for the paired-cube decoder lineage. The graph incidence-code/cut bridge is credited to Martínez-Bernal, Valencia-Bucio, and Villarreal, [arXiv:1812.04106v2, Corollary 2.13](https://arxiv.org/html/1812.04106v2). Physical notes retain the inherited odd-stage/hosting and rank-product credits and immutable source pins.

Overlap was refreshed through #958. **Ross Richardson's #958** studies a distinct five-port point-only decoder with quadratic labels and both overlap-one and overlap-three corrections; our native odd-star result uses incidence labels, additional proper-star observations, and overlap-one corrections. #939/#954 concern E8 geometry outside our integral odd-diagonal hypothesis. No literature-wide priority claim is made.

`CAMPAIGN-18H.json` records the active minimum eighteen-hour campaign, reviewed milestones, exact receipts and remaining obligations. The present checkpoint does not complete that campaign. Higher-rank classification, remaining odd-size observation classes, and fully priced source/helper/frame/restoration/recursive schedules remain under investigation. No deletion count is promoted to a physical supplier invoice.

Prepared by **Sam Sung (@the-missionary-company)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, including proof development, implementation, and independent AI-assisted review. Apache-2.0.

title: Research: simplify one R420 block from 50 to 33 XOR gates (no new kappa)
body:
This reduces one finite circuit in eumemic's PR543 R420 bit word from **50 to 33 binary XOR gates**, preserving its exact ordered 12-register F2 map. The matching literal reverse cleanup saves another 17 gates: **34 fewer scalar ADDs overall (26916 to 26882)**. This is a **research contribution / finite local circuit improvement, with no new kappa claim**.

Both forward and reversed nonnegative transfer matrices are entrywise dominated by the originals. Every register's physical frame path, the paid histogram, 420 helpers, nine retained copies and rank mass 5112 remain unchanged. The local cohort forward prefix stays 144651; its reverse prefix drops from 2270064 to 2185964. The payload allowance remains 100 bits. No hosted supplier invoice is claimed.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. PR543 reviewed dependency: `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`. `SOURCES.json` pins the input and relevant predecessor files. Only `research/r420-block3-xor/` is added; upstream and the selected frontier are unchanged.

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/r420-block3-xor/requirements.txt
python -B research/r420-block3-xor/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_R420_BLOCK3_XOR gates=50->33 saved_with_cleanup=34 columns=660 rank_mass=5112 controls=10`.

Passed on Windows/Python 3.12.14 with SymPy 1.14.0 and mpmath 1.3.0:

- Pinned PR543 labels, frames, all 660 symbolic dirty-input columns, H1-H5 and their decomposed conclusion.
- Independent set-based column replay and reconstruction; exact frame paths, positive transfers and prefix quantities agree.
- Ten corruption controls, including F2-neutral positive-bill inflation and F2-correct cleanup that fails literal-reversal H4.
- Actual inherited record exporter: 29874 to 29840 records, with scalar streams and paid histogram checked exactly.
- Frozen seed-13 search reproduction; Windows launcher; optimized Python; existing-output protection; selected-record binding; staged whitespace check.

Full C++ multistage replay, hosted invoices, frontier assembly, repository-wide `make verify`, Lean and remote CI were not run for this standalone local addition. No signed endpoint, optimal gate count, practical speedup or complete multiplication theorem is asserted. The README gives the precise positive-prefix argument, inherited assumptions, search domain/stopping rule and remaining integration work.

The assignment seed was 13, selecting block 3 by `13 mod 10`. Search stopped after 50 x 400 attempts. No pinned coordination issue existed; `CLAIM.json` records the narrow local claim and completed result. PR metadata was refreshed through #669. PR661 fixes the scalar gates/order and explicitly excludes resynthesis; PR612 formalizes the original word's literal interfaces; PR589 transports gates in a different punctured word. This contribution is distinct and depends on none of them.

Credit: eumemic's PR543/493 circuit and interface; Dylan Crow, DreamingOfClouds, Zhihao Chen, Chafik Boukhalfa, DaysSky and the cumulative predecessor lineage detailed in the README. Prepared for **yongjae321 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, including separate nomination, checking and review workers. Apache-2.0; no independent human peer review claimed.

title: Tooling: exact integer exponential intervals with pinned replay evidence
body:
The independent PR626 owner checker evaluates exponential bounds through repeated rational reductions. This adds an opt-in integer kernel that returns **exactly the same bounds**: degree-16 Taylor polynomial, identical tail, and identical 200-bit outward rounding. The unchanged complete checker runs through a source-pinned adapter on the archived PR622 native inputs.

**Status: tooling improvement; no new κ.** The kernel is approximately **13× faster**, but the full checker improves only modestly: final 15-pair runs measured **2–3% less wall time**, and an earlier run showed only 0.5%. All raw runs are retained. No substantial full-check or frontier-replay speedup is claimed.

- Five polynomial/tail/rounding negative mechanisms and 32 whole-check subprocess controls pass. Repinned owner/plan/native corruptions and both failed moment thresholds are rejected by the original checker in both engines.
