title: Research: dirty echo, verifier repair, and priced bit-sharing boundaries
body:
PR628's binary dirty commutator has quadratic factor-call growth and an executable phase-alias admission defect. This contribution adds a subquadratic multiway echo, a one-line alias guard, an exact full-transform/bit integration experiment, and bit-sharing cost gates that include physical owner restoration. The integration works functionally, but its complete recursive bill rejects this direct adapter as a route to larger κ. This is a construction refinement, executable repair and scoped negative research result.

### Local construction and verifier repair

The multiway echo composes noncommuting factor shears while restoring arbitrary borrowed data. Fixed fanout 8 reduces the leaf-call exponent from 2 to approximately 1.602452 with O(log n) borrowed arrays. At 512 factors the exact count falls from 262,144 to 21,952, using 21 arrays instead of 9. The flat variant takes 4n−4 calls and n−1 arrays. The complete inherited error recurrence is included; this is a classical local primitive, not an admitted multiplication supplier.

At pinned PR628, `phases is x` passes admission even though phases must remain read-only. For `x=phases=[1,1]`, outer b=1/4 and eight fractional bits, execution returns x=[1,15/16]. The submitted patch rejects source/target/scratch phase aliases before mutation. Replay applies the actual patch to the pinned Git source. More precision does not repair this exact counterexample.

### Full-transform and bit integration

`research/dirty-echo-integration/` implements:

- An all-role complex adapter and Boolean address-chunk interchange, including outputs on every role borrowed during execution.
- Complete normalized synthetic Fourier transforms over C[y]/(y^r+1), stored bit-reversed frequency order, signed monomial twiddles, opposite transforms and correctly normalized convolution.
- Independent exact references, instruction/interface corruption controls, source pins and deterministic evidence.

Three shears per pair complete the all-role adapter. Even granting one recursive child per additive leaf and making routing, phases, storage, preparation and precision free, its moment is `3 N(n)/(2 n^(1-b))`. Since `N(n) >= 4n-4`, its moment at saving zero is at least `6-6/n >= 3`. This rejects **this adapter's** bill for every nonnegative saving; it is not a lower bound for other integrations or suppliers.

Two exact counterexamples prevent silently substituting different operators: replacing the triangular Newton factor by its cyclic counterpart fails at radix 4, with a rank-r−1 boundary correction; the radix-3 cyclic kernel is singular on a length-5 cycle over GF(4). The latter rules out the unrestricted finite-field analogue, not restricted lengths or Boolean address permutations.

At κ=0.01, both retained supplier savings must exceed 1/99. With unchanged widths and volumes, uniform reductions of all paid terms would need to exceed approximately 2.70% for pinned #589 and 2.47% for pinned #659. These are exact-moment diagnostic targets, not feasible fractional deletions or replacement suppliers. No κ gain is attributed to the echo integration.

### Bit sharing priced before construction

`research/bit-role-sharing-budget/` extracts the actual PR589 local paid profile and all 661 Boolean columns, retains the complete frozen hosting remainder and fallback, and compares role-sharing budgets at the necessary bit saving 1/99 for κ=0.01.

- Equal-call pooling saves dispatches but not volume-weighted recursive work. A fixed-address-permutation rank argument also excludes fewer queried role volumes under arbitrary invertible XOR row charts and restored private dirt. Different address-dependent charts and native primitives are outside this model.
- Even ideal rank-8 consolidation of every local rank unit fails the target. Making all retained-total copies free still fails. The corresponding bit-only outer ceilings are below 0.002644610326897 and 0.007315906873875; neither is an achieved supplier.
- With the original rank mass and boundary remainder, cap 55 fails and cap 56 is the first passing relaxation. A hypothetical integer rank-57 invoice allows 431 extra rank-1 repair calls globally and needs over 98.48% of local rank mass fused. The eight-stage interpretation applies only to one port's active spaces; cross-port sharing has a larger span.
- A different arithmetic target is ideal rank-8 consolidation plus 100 **net paid rank units** removed per invocation after hosting: 99 fails, 100 passes. This is not achieved by simply deleting helpers or XORs.

No replacement supplier was built: the simple sharing classes fail even under favorable complete-cost bounds, and the passing high-rank/mass-reduction targets still lack an operator and hosting plan. No new κ is claimed. The independent positive-atanh engine reproduces the current bit root and agrees with the inherited Mercator engine on 133 complete invoices. Normal/optimized evidence is byte-identical; 108 small coded-query programs, 384 positive-control basis columns, source/scatter/expected-evidence mutations and a relocated minimal replay are checked.

Standalone command: `sh research/bit-role-sharing-budget/replay.sh /tmp/bit-role-sharing-budget`. Expected final line: `PASS_BIT_ROLE_SHARING_REPLAY`. The combined command below now includes this screen. Final overlap review through #716 distinguishes #705/#708/#714/#715; no new pinned coordination issue was found.

### Concrete bit-sharing candidate and physical hosting gate

`research/bit-sharing-hosting-gate/` follows the 100-net-unit arithmetic target with an exact scalar candidate and a source-bound reconstruction of all **126,432** frozen helper reservations. Neither candidate is admitted as a supplier.

- The nine-stage source-bank masks have one exact dependence: the last source is the XOR of the preceding eight. Nine running accumulators per replica can therefore share the source part of the retained decoder totals at the scalar level. The actual snapshots have rank-nine dirty contamination. The proposed owned-storage plan adds 288 persistent rows and nine temporary rows; source extraction, copy, clear and XOR costs are listed. ADDRESS-chart alignment is still unproved. Even gifting it, the maximum COPY credit is only **7 rank units per invocation**, with target moment 1.026605906228685.
- A hypothetical free producer eliminating 13 helper paths removes **104 local rank units**, but the explicit idle owners must complete all 104 vacated directions: **zero net credit**. The new complete profile is priced after coalescing those directions at the owners' original boundaries. Every one of the 439 single-helper eliminations has the same mass conservation. These favorable screens do not assert a replacement producer exists.
- The previous 100-unit screen granted rank-8 consolidation everywhere. Keeping the 222 rank-7 data climbs makes 100 and 101 fail; **102 first passes that narrower relaxation**. More fundamentally, under the current data/cover boundary identity, even zero COPY cost saves only 63 per invocation. Reaching 100 requires a changed boundary term.
- A scope control changes the hosting remainder: free elimination of all helper work plus perfect data consolidation still fails with COPY retained, but passes if COPY is also granted free. Thus 100 is not a universal necessary condition for other suppliers; the complete moment remains decisive.

The package verifies all 888 source-bank columns, retained source/dirty ranks and reflected copy forms, reconstructs chronological windows and disjoint owners independently of the parent allocator, and compares **449 complete invoices with two exact rational engines**. Normal, optimized and relocated minimal replays agree; six ownership/admission controls plus source/receipt corruption controls are rejected. No new supplier, physical cache realization, all-size transfer or κ is claimed. The construction goal remains unmet.

Standalone: `sh research/bit-sharing-hosting-gate/replay.sh /tmp/bit-sharing-hosting-gate`. The combined replay includes it. The final overlap refresh through #762 distinguishes the fixed P111 COPY-floor proofs #757/#761 and R420 ghost-return audit #760; these are credited context, not imported dependencies.

### Paired boundary target and exact owner plan

`research/bit-paired-boundary-gate/` changes the boundary contract instead of withdrawing helper paths from fixed owners. For orthogonal P and Q, incoming source/target frames P/Q and outgoing Q-perp/P-perp give the exact local operator with diagonal D_(I-P-Q) and off-diagonal D_I. The existing nine-stage bank schedule composes it to the full all-role exchange. Rational charts at all 111 ports, the complete permutation algebra and all 18 omitted-bridge controls are checked.

An explicit realization by wrapping the old word is priced, including two rank-two endpoint children per port, 439 owned zero-initialized helper rows, every new idle boundary and ordinary padding to preserve m=64 and W=28416. Its moment exceeds 1.7015, so it is rejected before supplier construction.

A different, **unrealized local word** with rank(Q)=2 would have rank-five data climbs. The package gives a concrete chronological plan for 296 whole width-eight helpers: 85,248 exclusive global reservations and all owner remainders. Charging every local rank unit as its own rank-one child gives moment 0.9947928245644905 at c=1/99+10^-9 and conditional net saving 197 1/3 units per invocation. Adding 31 rank-one repair children per invocation still passes at 0.9999126541717095, with net saving 166 1/3; 32 fails the rate test. These are conditional construction targets, not achieved improvements.

The actual PR589 scalar order cannot realize the new endpoints by monotone re-framing: its least frame closure forces all 111 sources to full rank eight during cleanup. A new local source/read/restoration topology is required. The Gaussian appendix separately shows that the reported 80-rational-rank COPY floor, under the stated B_K slot model, bounds every stage count below c=0.0078; it does not re-prove that external floor or exclude other delivery models.

Standalone: `sh research/bit-paired-boundary-gate/replay.sh /tmp/paired-boundary-new-output`. Normal and optimized evidence agree; relocated minimal replay, source/receipt corruption controls, owner timing/collision controls, two exact price engines and selected-record integrity pass. The combined driver includes this package; its unchanged older stages were not repeated in this increment. The full goal remains unachieved: no paired local supplier, finite controller admission or new kappa is claimed. Final overlap metadata was checked through #802, including #791/#801 and the updated #717.

### Reproduce and validation

Full contribution, after fetching the exact dependencies listed in the README:


title: Conditional κ = 0.001659319032684569: six dim-8 cold ends and three entrance promotions on the PR659 no-triangle word

## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.001659319032684569** (conservative 0.001659319029797309). This is +6.04×10⁻⁷ over PR671 (0.001658714981837397). The complex side binds; PR589's bit supplier gives 0.0017334.

**Construction**, on PR659's no-triangle layered word (sha a9de804f):
1. **p6n: six dim-8 cold ends** in three pairs, [512,513] at U66_34_16, [311,510] at U72_40 and [522,327] at U66_34_18, each with one dim-6 partner split. Δ{1:+6, 2:+12, 3:−12}, width −6. This is the p123 lane re-chosen so that no end needs a second split on the no-triangle word.
2. **Three entrance promotions** (as in PR664) on top, using a *minimal* deterministic recipe that raises only each group's entry gates (36 gate frames). Δ{1:+24, 2:−24, 3:−12, 4:+12}, width −12.

title: Scoped negative result: volume-aware selector batching of complex children
body:
An attempted replacement of two equal-rank complex children by one selector-batched call gives a false moment saving if the joined array's volume is omitted. This **scoped negative result** supplies the exact circuit, restoration of arbitrary dirty padding, and the complete volume-weighted budget on a source-pinned pair of rank-2 calls from the accepted #626 `jp8` supplier. **No new κ or supplier is claimed.**

At the accepted supplier's complex exponent, the unweighted `2 C_2 -> C_3 + C_1` comparison gives ratio **0.999786029497691095**. The actual joined array has twice the volume, giving **1.999572058995382190**. Even granting the inverse selector and all routing/frame work for free leaves ratio **1.499003977340941911**. Exact rational enclosures are included.

The note distinguishes the two uniform scaling regimes: a fixed pair uses one selector bit and has the same leading asymptotic moment; a selector slot scaled by `f` requires `2^f` lanes and cannot retain the two-stream volume. A support argument excludes replacing selector correction by monomial routing alone. These are comparisons of the inherited cost bounds, not lower bounds on arbitrary algorithms or a defect claim against production admission.

title: Research audit: tensor E8 rate and finite-depth center-copy correction
body:

```
9^n k_n = 28/(2739 log 3) * (1 - (3/2)(3/5)^n) + O(n/9^n),
```

- Stress: 480 prescribed pairs, lengths through 32, precisions through 64 fractional bits, zero inputs, cancellation, carry boundaries and seed-derived mixed values. Numerators reach 128 bits; packed operands reach 8,219 bits.

The oracle uses neither packing nor source `rounded()`, Gaussian factors, `bits=None`, or the original Fraction-matrix checker. Its upper-triangle oracle directly sums upper entries. `PROOF.md` separately gives an elementary all-length radix argument, including the zero-input case and the necessity of rounding only completed coordinates. At one fractional bit, H=(1,1), X=(1,-2) has degree-one output zero; separately rounding positive/negative products incorrectly gives -1/2. title: Independent verification: weighted-stride closures and bilinear dual (no kappa)
body:
## Result and scope

**Independent verification / research note; no new kappa.** This adds an independent finite-geometric-sum oracle for `(W-rho I)^(-1)`, where `(Wx)_i=tau_i*x_(i-s mod L)`, and checks the bilinear inverse transpose. It compares exact results with the neighboring rounded single-factor primitive from Chafik Boukhalfa / chafreaky's PR628, after cycle-local gathering and scattering.

For a stride cycle C of length m and phase product h_C, the written identity is

`(W_C-rho I)^(-1) = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} rho^(m-1-j) W_C^j / (h_C-rho^m)`.

The oracle uses exact rational complex arithmetic, not the predecessor's affine two-pass scan or Gaussian elimination. It checks both inverse products on every matrix entry. The dual independently reverses the stride and shifts phases by s, **without conjugation**, then checks the result against the actual inverse transpose.

A concrete length-6 / stride-2 witness rejects using one global phase product or the global length in place of each cycle's own closure. These are counterexamples to deliberately incorrect extensions, **not a defect in PR628's stated neighboring scope**. No such defect was found in the tested domain.

**Predecessor credit:** PR628 already provides constant-gauge arbitrary-stride sorting and the direct-sum infinity-norm argument. Neither is claimed new. The additional evidence covers independently varying phase products on multiple cycles and the bilinear dual through a different exact algorithm. Gather/scatter routing, phase reads, storage and restoration are not declared free or newly improved.

## Pins and package

- Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`.
- Contribution: `c5b53a5e80372a1fae9830d8dcf21aaabce3f729`.

The adapter executes the unchanged `scan` and `apply` function ASTs from pinned `weighted.py`, using its original `scan.py` arithmetic. Unrelated kernel setup is not executed. Setting the initial scalar to one isolates a single factor; it is **not** a radix-1 kernel certificate or a full cascade replay.

## Reproduce

Python 3.9+ and Git; standard library only. Fetch the exact pending source object once if absent:

```sh
git fetch --no-tags https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds.git 0768f97d06c623b8211e651543c66135796b62bf
python3 -B -I research/cyclic-stride-independent/verify.py --check research/cyclic-stride-independent/EXPECTED.json
```

Expected: `PASS_STRIDE_RESOLVENT_AND_DUAL`.

Completed fixed domain: lengths 1-12, 16, 18 and 21; every stride residue; two separated inner/outer roots; seed-derived rational unit phases and RHS values. No adaptive search or early-success stopping rule.

- **266 exact cases; 252,730 matrix-entry obligations**, including forward and dual; 122 multi-cycle cases and 30 zero-stride cases; signed-stride and zero-root edge checks.

body:

title: Research: determinant obstruction for rank-homogeneous register paths (no kappa)
body:
Eight fixed four-block Clifford words at m=3, W=3, s=8 remained unresolved by bounded support and polynomial searches. A determinant argument now excludes every invertible complex scalar realization of those words: when paths with the same interior group product have the same accumulated unary rank, the total unary rank must be at least W*m.

The written theorem allows arbitrary width and any number of scalar mixing blocks, subject to that explicit path-homogeneity hypothesis. The finite checker specializes to three-qubit, three-register formal projective Clifford words. This does not settle the full register problem or claim a new primitive or kappa.

The standalone corpus contains 73 literal words:
- Eight newly closed four-block follow-ups.
- Twenty-three further exclusions among 32 evolved words; nine fail the hypothesis and remain unclassified by this criterion.
- All 33 PR #680 words as regressions, recovered without support/torus solving.

The search consequence is concrete: repeated products alone are insufficient. A successful word below the W*m cost needs coincident interior products with different accumulated ranks.

Validation: `python3 -I -B research/graded-path-obstruction/verify.py` prints `PASS_GRADED_PATH_OBSTRUCTION`. Signed tableaus and exact Gaussian matrices agree on 1,377 paths; 73 polynomial determinant checks and exact nine-call positive controls pass. Forged homogeneity and rank certificates, damaged payload/expected data, and optimized execution are rejected. An isolated relocated package and a recompressed input reproduce identical results in about 0.63 seconds locally. The package uses only the Python standard library and writes no files.

The general claim rests on PROOF.md, not extrapolation from tests. No independent human review, proof assistant, full supplier/repository replay, remote CI, or multiplication theorem is claimed. title: Research: optimal clean root checkpoint saves 25–40% of binary product-shear calls
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Research note / scoped interface construction; no new kappa.

A genuinely clean root checkpoint removes one right-subtree cancellation from PR628's product-shear recursion. Keeping both child recursions balanced and all-dirty, an exact root-split formula saves 25–40% of primitive leaf calls with the same total scratch-array count. One array must now start clean. At the seed-selected generic factor count 54, split 22+32 uses 2,112 calls instead of 3,136 and one clean plus five dirty arrays instead of six dirty arrays.

The package includes the all-n proof, complete weighted/dispatch/preparation/storage/routing cost recurrence, executable adapter, source pins, deterministic certificate and meaningful negative controls. title: Scoped negative result: minimal E8 mixed-port extension is saturated
body:
## Result

Scoped negative result; no new kappa. Every compatible non-root port added after at most 14 E8 root-line deletions, with the inherited nine-dimensional labels, forces the same D7 equality case up to Weyl symmetry. Exactly one non-root port type fits. Adding it makes every nonzero reader span all eight physical dimensions, so no further nonzero port can be added within this model.

The exact star copy cost rises from 64 on 106 root ports to **72 on 107 mixed ports**. This rules out improving the copied-information ratio by the minimum-puncture mixed-port mechanism before implementing helper or restoration work.

This extends Chi Zhao's #631 sharp threshold with equality classification and saturation. GamingPuzzled's #620 already computed the coordinate-axis example's approximate ratio; that example is credited, not claimed as new. #669's paired-hypercube result and #703's quaternionic result have different scopes.

Changes are confined to four files in `research/e8-minimal-mixed-port/`: proof, independent standard-library checker, exact receipt, and source pins. The checker uses a Gram-row basis instead of the predecessor's orthonormal factorization. The written Weyl-chamber reduction separates exhaustive coverage from finite replay.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-minimal-mixed-port/verify.py
```

Expected: PASS for 8 maximal flats, all 511 nonzero readers before and after augmentation, one non-root candidate, and 5 negative-control categories; star costs 64 and 72. Every run compares the complete regenerated receipt with the checked-in JSON.

Validation passed on Python 3.14.8 and Python 3.11.15 with optimized mode. Controls reject duplicate non-root ports, even labels, each of the 14 forbidden root restorations, a full-rank normal request, and a malformed simple system. A separate AI-assisted implementation generated the signed roots in a different order, chose another binary basis, and checked ranks over GF(3), with exact annihilators for deficient spans. It independently confirmed costs 64 and 72. Selected-record integrity, source hashes, and staged whitespace checks pass.

The expensive repository-wide and selected supplier cold replays were not repeated. No existing supplier, generator, assembly, `upstream/` file, or selected-frontier pointer changes.

## Scope, pins and credit

- Exact base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`; OS-random seed **40**, structural decoder research. Source pins and claim details are in `SOURCES.json`.
- #631 head: `fb893b5ee1317c2da3b297e6fe78eca0857d1a76`. #620 head: `e9cf03bbdf7094b5a83f6dbd1d74bfd77a05fb87`. The relevant imported source bytes have explicit hashes.
- The theorem keeps the original labels, nine binary dimensions, nonzero rational physical vectors, and the Euclidean ambient form. More than 14 punctures, relabelling, extra label dimensions, and other decoder families are outside scope. Helper-saving tradeoffs and complete paid suppliers remain unpriced.
- The accepted conditional kappa remains `51110230636731/31250000000000000`. All inherited all-size, realization, restoration, precision and analytic obligations remain. This is not formal verification of the multiplication theorem.
- No pinned coordination issue existed, so the claim was local. The final overlap scan covered 528 open PRs through #709 and found no competing equality-classification result.
- Prepared by **Sagar Thakrar / @thakrarsagar**, with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in research, implementation, proof review and documentation. Apache-2.0. Predecessor credit includes GamingPuzzled, Chi Zhao, DreamingOfClouds, artuskg, eumemic, OpenAI #109 and the cumulative community work.

title: Research: optimal disjoint R420 target pairs save 3,250 XORs (no new kappa)
body:
This **research construction with a restricted optimality certificate** saves **3,250 binary XOR additions** in eumemic's PR543 R420 bit word: **26,916 → 23,666** overall, with frame-zero D **19,922 → 16,672**. It uses 60 disjoint target pairs and includes every preparation and restoration operation. **No new kappa is claimed.**

A small independent certificate proves 3,250 is the **exact optimum within the disjoint target-pair substitution class**. Its 120 nonnegative doubled vertex prices satisfy `q_i+q_j >= 2*w_ij` for all **7,140 unordered pairs** and sum to 6,500. Every disjoint pairing therefore saves at most 3,250. The frozen 60-pair circuit attains that bound. The shipped standard-library checker verifies the inequalities and construction without a matching solver.

**Concurrent #713, by Scott Woolsey Biggart, is credited.** It appeared during the final refresh and independently achieved the original 3,150-addition greedy saving. This final submission adds **100 saved additions and the exact upper-bound certificate**. No priority for target-row factoring is claimed. The result concerns this four-operation pair identity only, not arbitrary D circuits.

Every helper remains untouched during D. The complete dirty-input operator, physical frame paths, 420 helpers, nine copies and rank mass 5,112 are preserved. The reverse positive-prefix bound rises from 2,270,064 to 3,703,810; the local payload allowance rises from 100 to 102 bits, below the inherited 104-bit cap. No hosted invoice is reused.

The original H2 syntax and literal K extractor reject this word as expected. The package records both rejections and proves the semantic replacement: D executes at frame zero and has exactly `(x,s,y) -> (x,s,y+Ks)`. Predecessor checkers are unchanged.

```sh
python3 -B research/r420-target-pairs/verify.py
# Optional unchanged native cohort checks, with C++17 and Boost headers:
BOOST_INCLUDE=/path/containing/boost python3 -B research/r420-target-pairs/verify.py --native
```

- Fresh unchanged native legality and 5/9/11-stage checks on 900/1,380/1,620 formal columns, with 6/18/24 omitted-bridge controls, for both source and final word. Records fall from 29,874 to 26,624.
- Nine local circuit rejection controls, an underpriced-dual rejection control and a paid neutral-pair positive control. Two native corruptions pass legality but fail every stage's formal-column check.
- Independent endpoint/frame/dual checks, gzip recompression acceptance, altered-payload rejection, selected-record integrity, documentation links and whitespace checks.

title: Format limits part 2 (no κ claim): erratum to #595, exact invoice prices, frontier-word censuses, decoder floors, spec requirements, centre and fragmentation walls
body:
**No κ claim.** This continues the merged #595. It records what we have proved and measured about the limits of the construction format and of the shipped #656 word, including an erratum to #595. Every result states its scope. Each is marked *CHECKED* (recomputed by `verify.sh`; *CHECKED (log)* = a shipped, sha256-pinned log is compared), *ARGUED* (proof or file:line argument in the README) or *RECORDED* (an earlier run that is not repeated; notes are shipped where the row names them).

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/format-limits-2/requirements.txt          # sections 5-9 only
bash research/format-limits-2/verify.sh /fresh/output/dir                    # 233 PASS lines, ~22 s; step 0 fails hard on any MANIFEST/provenance mismatch
E1_FULL=1 bash research/format-limits-2/verify.sh /fresh/output/dir          # also re-runs #595's a5 unchanged: 228 PASS lines, ~62 s
```

### Results
| id | result | status |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | **ERRATUM to #595.** The ×1.15–2.15 "schedule/ρ family" multipliers (#595 census item 8, open problem 3) come from dropping idle-frame rules, not from a ρ family: idle changes free ×2.15, one-child batching ×1.55, no split pre-stretch ×1.18 at s = 9 (×1.15 best, s = 5), both sides. | numbers CHECKED; reading ARGUED |
| E2 | ρ is not a verifier input (it is the hard-coded final bank swap). Over all pair-preserving ρ at P ≤ 3 (reachable set exactly Sp(4,2) = 720 and Sp(6,2) = 1,451,520) none beats B_K: multiplier 1.000. | (b) CHECKED (log, re-run and compared); (a) ARGUED |
| P1 | Complex invoice calculus on #626 (reproduced to 16+ digits): centre −1 = +22.6% b; one cst unit +2.81%; one port +2.15%; one w9 helper +0.068% (+0.137% if its width merges). | CHECKED |
| P2 | Bit invoice calculus on #555: c reproduced to 24 digits; cst unit ±2.80% c, port 2.15%. Word-level helper knobs (0.06–0.11% c) not re-run. | root, mass, cst rows CHECKED; rest RECORDED |
| P3 | Helper exchange rate by width on #649: w9 0.070% (no merge) / 0.140% (merged), down to w4 0.026 / 0.072; explains the old 0.027–0.143 spread. | CHECKED |
| P4 | Stage count s = 9 → 7 is worse at every R: hosting overflows 8.7%, b₇ only +0.21% over b₉ at equal R. | CHECKED (model) |
| P5 | The climb mass is a forced cover (mass = mW − deficit): mass padding is illegal, frame annealing on the #626 ck/jp8 words gains 0.0% b (fixed op order; jump-merging frame raises as in #741 were not in the move set), "fewer helpers" is not a gain. | identity CHECKED; SA outcome RECORDED |
| C1 | Provenance census of #656: 492 helpers born at 4 allocation sites: S1 scratch 224, S3 packet copy 156, S4 slot copy 112; κ identity exact. | CHECKED (tags from a recorded rebuild) |
| C2 | The shipped word is a dirty-borrow program, not a clean SLP: 2056 distinct read rows (minimum chain cover 2056), 268 of 422 B-phase helpers are pure dirt, equal to the S3 + S4 sites. | CHECKED |
| C3 | The 112 ports form a cap in F₂⁹ (no three XOR to 0, every hyperplane misses ≥ 48); 8-port blocks sit at dimension ≤ 5. | cap CHECKED; corollary ARGUED |
| G1 | Gauge-free cold-end bound N_cold ≤ Σ_b(\|Q_b\| − rank C[Q_b]); #645 attains 44. | CHECKED on #645; 504 / K480 values RECORDED |
| G2 | Gauge44 is gauge-optimal at 44 for its frame schedule; read-order ceiling 48 (+0.13–0.16% b), home-first legal ceiling 46. | 44 = bound CHECKED; ceilings RECORDED |
| G3 | **Theorem.** A helper can end at a hyperplane U only if the supports of its row of M⁻¹ and its column of M lie in Q_U; covers every reordering and relay strategy. | ARGUED (Lean on #593's package RECORDED) |
| D1 | Complex decoder floor on P112: exactly 8 costly terms give cst ≥ 64 (9 label spans over 440,880 supports); all costly terms β ≥ 8 and n ≥ 9 give cst ≥ 72; n = 8 is infinitesimally rigid up to gauge. Open: mixed β ≤ 7 terms with n ≥ 9. | counts, spans, rigidity CHECKED; step (b), (c) ARGUED; flip-walk logs CHECKED (log) |
| D2 | Any n = 8 exact P112 decoder is D = XA, T = XA⁻ᵀ; absorbing one frame line costs exactly +1 cst, a pair +2 (≈ 272k and 951k sampled cases). | ARGUED; census CHECKED (log) |
| D3 | Non-star complex decoders exist: exact cst 63 on all six single-line P111 punctures, cst 56 on P104. Their buildability price is negative (net −0.1 to −10% b). | hits CHECKED (exact); walks CHECKED (log); price RECORDED |
| D4 | Structured classical decoders cost more than coordinate (64): rotations, WHT, halves 72; coset 4-split 192. | CHECKED |
| S1 | In-place elimination is dead under the shipped frame rules: 0 of 12,432 cross-port in-place pairs legal; 33 illegal reads in every row of M (41.2% of the off-diagonal support). | CHECKED |
| S2 | Spec dependencies of the sink wall: the endpoint operator holds on every role, so target sinks cannot be shared; a full sink forces M_in(X) = 0 only for idempotent labels (non-projection labels open). | ARGUED (citations CHECKED) |
| S3 | R2 (one identical exact representative per gate) is specification; relaxing it to a fixed finite set is unsound as a drop-in (h = 3 toy: 4 of 8 addresses moved). | CHECKED (toy) |
| S4 | Centre descents exist only for the 8 barrier centres of the shipped verifier; the "once per word" premise is false (centre −1 = +22.6% b). | ARGUED (file:line CHECKED) |
| Y1 | Centre/cut facts for M = I − G/2 on 112 D₈-root ports: rank G = 8, cut ranks 6/7/7/8, no weight-4 total in the span of the centres; rank 7 occurs at 8 coordinate splits. | CHECKED |
| Y2 | Full centre delivery is frame-illegal (448 of 456 reads); a 7+1 time-split barrier saves 0%. | rank part CHECKED (8 splits); rest ARGUED / RECORDED |
| F1 | Target fragmentation at the shipped op order: legal ceiling 950 of 1096 ops, loose format bound 229 psi/call (HiGHS-proved maximum 36), S3/S4 reader sets admit no modular chain (0/156, 0/112). | CHECKED for the stated parts; rest RECORDED |
| F2 | Tight-frames wall: legal iff G ⊆ U; slack arises only by deleting ops, time shifts, descents or equal-value re-threading; +1 dimension on any helper pushes 2–8 target frames 8 → 9. | ARGUED; instances RECORDED |
| F3 | S1 block scratch cannot be shared or shortened inside the format: 16 distinct sparse forms per block, 0 of 16 equal twins retireable. | RECORDED |
| F4 | Twin substitution for the 73 frame-insulator helpers fails on #656: all 111 twin reads are value-exact, 0 of 111 are legal one at a time (each raises 2–6 final caps), 0 of 73 helpers deletable. | RECORDED (exact oracle, not shipped) |
| F5 | Re-ordering reads of read-only S3 faces fails on #656: for 27 of the 32 structurally clean faces every B slot from the last write to the copy slot (window ≈ 740–860 ops), in given and reversed reader order, gives 0 legal reads. | RECORDED (exact oracle, not shipped) |
| F6 | The opening miner on the rebuilt #664 word finds 2534 disjoint-lifetime helper pairs; all 2534 need frame growth and none is frame-nested, so 0 register-reuse openings: the same rigidity as #656. | CHECKED (log) |
| O1 | Cross-block totals ("X4" faces): 2688 reach-10 quads all span 4 blocks; ledger 12.21% b (hypothetical design) does not close. | faces CHECKED; ledger RECORDED |
| O2 | #617 → #622 K-triangle ledger on the moment engine: ideal gross +0.52% b for 12 helpers, net +0.0146% after 6 lost cold ends and rewired climbs. | RECORDED |
| App. | **Appendix: conditional candidates** (5 items, each with one blocking condition; none is a result). | unverified |

31 rows by primary status: 21 CHECKED, 6 ARGUED, 4 RECORDED.

### Open problems
- **Mixed-beta decoders with n >= 9** (D1): a cst below 64 on P112 would have to mix terms with beta <= 7.
- **An order-free fragmentation ceiling** (F1, F2): the loose order-free bound (2478 psi/call) is uncalibrated.
- **Non-projection rational labels** (S2) and **a frame schedule with |I| > 8 per block** (G1, G2).
- **Value-exact re-threading beyond the fixed order and DAG** (F2).

### Appendix
README, "Conditional candidates (unverified: could work IF...)": 5 items, each with one measured fact and one blocking condition (S1 scratch never read, single-packet S4, order-free frame slack, radix-4 first climb, partner-merge of pure-dirt helpers). None is a result. Two earlier candidates were tested and failed (F4, F5).

*Update after submission:* single-packet S4 (item 2) is answered negatively: 18 of the 28 deferred S4 adds are illegal even when deferred alone, checked on cycles 0–1. The never-read S1 drop (item 1) is mostly answered negatively: given the shipped end-of-A frames, each of the 11 eight-line S1 blocks needs all 16 registers (forced-matching argument). Blocks (0,1,*) and the true-cap case remain open. See the README appendix.

### Notes
- **Base:** cut from main (`66849e14`); touches only `research/format-limits-2/`.
- **Check:** independently run from a fresh `git archive` of the head commit: 233 PASS in 22 s (Python 3.14.7 and 3.11.17 with the pinned set, 3.14.7 with the latest numpy/scipy); with `E1_FULL=1`, 228 PASS in 61 s. Tampering with any file stops step 0 with exit 1. Sections 1-4 use the standard library only.
- **Inputs:** vendored inputs are byte copies pinned by PR blob id and sha256 in `SOURCES.json`; existing logs and card records are shipped unchanged (six had absolute local paths, a personal name or CRLF endings removed, listed in `SOURCES.json`). No Lean, SAT, CP-SAT or DRAT artefact is claimed.
- **Errata found in our own earlier claims:** the "schedule/rho family" of #595 (census item 8 / open problem 3) (E1); S1's 4164/8960 legal reads (a port-indexing mismatch; the same word gives 5264 with its own ports, 33 illegal reads per row); "rank 8 at every cut" (rank 7 at 8 coordinate splits); "all 56|56 splits" (only the 8 coordinate splits were run); F1's provider words; P3's random-draw rate table (exact means 0.070 / 0.140).
- **Overlap:** #703, #705 and #711 are related (D1/D3, S2/F2, F2) and duplicate no row; see README Notes. #698 (fixed-order frame optimality) is cited in P5, F1 and F2, which keep only the distinct parts; #683 and #687 study different objects and are credited in `NOTICE.md`.

**Credits:** see `NOTICE.md` for every PR whose word, pipeline or result is used, including #531 (icekylinx), #555 (eumemic), #595 and #604 (DreamingOfClouds), #622, #623, #635, #649, #656 (jeremykothe2), #626 (chafreaky), #645 (icekylinx) and #646 (jeremydiviney).

title: Scoped negative result: R420 split target reads cannot lower the paid moment
body:

title: Research theorem: nine-call bound for arbitrary invertible three-register targets
body:
PR468 proves that three invertible lower-triangular rational 3×3 targets need nine rank-one calls in the abelian three-register bit model. This research theorem removes the target-triangularity assumption: the minimum remains nine for **arbitrary invertible rational targets**.

The new connection is to extract a dimension-independent disjoint-subset lemma from PR468's low-corank argument. With at most two frame relations, every target is a sum of a disjoint subset of paid frames. This gives a six-call bound for arbitrary invertible 2×2 target triples and closes the formerly flagged block case in address span four. The other reductions and the complete span-five search remain unchanged. The note expands the proof, including the associated-graded common-J argument, rather than extrapolating from a bounded word test.

The extension covers strictly more targets: the package exhibits I, C, C² with characteristic polynomial of C equal to x³−2. These cannot be made jointly lower triangular by any common rational left/right coordinate changes. Their nine-call construction is checked as an exact formal group-algebra identity.

title: Research note: sharp off-target proper-star puncture threshold
body:
PR669 proves the sharp puncture threshold for target-local stars and explicitly leaves punctured decoders using arbitrary off-target stars open. This **research note / scoped negative result** closes that larger scalar class: for every power-of-two k >= 2 and p >= k, decoding one retained target requires exactly **2(p-k)+1** deleted ports. **No new kappa or paid supplier is claimed.**

The written elementary proof establishes the stronger identity d(C_{p,k}) = 2(p-k+1) for the global degree-<k star evaluation code, including the empty star, for every k >= 2. It uses generalized-cube parity, an even-face lemma and restriction induction. At a power-of-two k, permitted target overlap-class corrections add no functions to that code. The attaining witness uses one nonempty (k-1)-star.

A ten-star p=5,k=4 example reaches the same threshold while all 16 target intersection cells survive. Thus PR669's **minimum threshold** extends globally, while its **local cell feasibility criterion** does not. Exact elimination checks local infeasibility for this example.

Changes are limited to research/global-star-puncture/ and one scoped workflow. The accepted conditional kappa remains 51110230636731/31250000000000000; selected-result, existing suppliers, generators and upstream/ are unchanged.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/global-star-puncture/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_GLOBAL_STAR_PUNCTURE: sharp deletion thresholds 3/5; 2 independent F2 engines; 960 correction rows; 12 negative controls`.

The complete deterministic receipt is compared on every run. A packed row-space quotient and a separately written list-RREF/nullspace implementation agree on 80/240-port domains, ranks 65/155 and distances 4/6. All 28,680 pair syndromes in the second domain are distinct. Coverage also includes all 38,344 codewords in seven small domains, exhaustive even-face support checks in dimensions 1–4, valid generalized-face cubes, and a non-power-of-two positive escape control. Finite replay supports the written proof; it is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

- Python 3.13.5 on Windows: normal and isolated optimized exact replays pass.
- Four harness tests pass: relocated minimal replay/export, corrupted receipt rejection with output preserved, changed contextual source rejection, and changed source-pin rejection.

- Selected-record/source integrity and staged whitespace checks pass; the final checkout is clean.

Both jobs passed the exact receipt, four failure-detection tests, selected-result integrity and clean-checkout check. Upstream PR-triggered workflows await maintainer approval (`action_required`).
- Full make verify and frontier626-verify were not repeated for this isolated additive research package.

The theorem concerns one specified retained target, arbitrary global proper-star coefficients and fixed coefficients within each overlap class. title: Research consolidation: uniform proof of the archived 2P+1 stage bound
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The archived campaign report M claims that exchanging P bank pairs requires at least 2P + 1 stages. Its discussion mixes a four-call rank argument with finite searches for P <= 3. This research consolidation supplies a self-contained uniform argument and confirms the same bound; it does not claim a new kappa or controller.

For two blocks of dimension P*v, consider calls that add a rank-at-most-v linear function of one block to the other, with arbitrary invertible block-diagonal bridges. The potential rank(A) + rank(D) starts at 2P*v and ends at zero. The first call cannot lower it, and every later call lowers it by at most v. Thus at least 2P + 1 calls are needed, over every field. The existing Sussman borrowing chain attains the count. The endpoint is measured before the designated terminal exchange; physical frames, helper contracts, restoration and all-size/analytic interfaces remain separate obligations.

Additions are one self-contained research package and a path-filtered verification workflow. The original report and its notice are preserved byte for byte. title: Research: Gaussian E8 weighted maximal-clique ceiling 40 and independent replay
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The Gaussian E8 copy floor is 40, but can changing clique weights improve that certificate? This **research note and independent verification** proves that **40 is the exact optimum for all nonnegative weighted inclusion-maximal-clique certificates**, including nonuniform weights and mixtures of maximal cliques of different sizes.

Concurrent #738 already establishes the decoder lower bound 40, closure reduction and uniform maximum-clique sharpness. It was discovered during the final overlap refresh, after this package's proof and implementations were developed. This submission credits that result and adds the stronger method ceiling: #738's inspected proof gives a general ceiling of 48; here 40 suffices for the specified maximal-clique class. Certificates using non-maximal cliques remain outside this extension. **No new kappa or physical supplier is claimed.**

The short ceiling argument sums the local certificate constraints over the 900 ordered orthogonal-root hyperplane pairs. Each pair has Gaussian pairing rank two. A maximal clique of size k meets both hyperplanes in exactly 900-30k cases, which is at least 45k because k<=12. Therefore every such weighted certificate has value at most 1800/45=40. Uniform weights 1/192 on the 640 maximum cliques attain it.

Two separately implemented exact replays independently confirm the lower bound on all **2,582,128 unordered pairs of 2,272 flats**. The primary uses eight rational coordinates and exact pairing ranks; the second uses four Gaussian-integer coordinates, cofactor-based flat generation and nonzero-minor certificates. It also enumerates all 8,704 inclusion-maximal cliques. Adding empty-support pairs explains the count difference from #738 and is not claimed as a stronger mathematical domain. The abstract decoder optimum remains in [40,60].

title: Research: certify R420 forest cuts under the 104-bit cap
body:
This **finite bit-circuit construction with exact scoped certificates and a generic Lean proof** saves **4,897 binary XORs** in PR543's R420 word: **26,916 → 22,019** overall, with compensation D **19,922 → 15,025**. Every preparation and restoration operation is charged. The unchanged native **104-bit** prefix cap passes. **No new κ is claimed.**

**Concurrent #759 by Oscar Fennell is credited.** It appeared during final validation with the same forest class and 14,921-XOR unconstrained floor. This independently corroborates that floor and adds an exact coefficient-constrained cut optimization, **113 fewer XORs** than its submitted 15,138-XOR D circuit, independent verification and a generic Lean proof. No priority for forest factoring or the floor is claimed. The package uses the distinct path `research/r420-forest-cut-budget/` to avoid colliding with #759.

The contribution has three linked parts:

- A minimum spanning tree and all **7,140 non-tree cycle inequalities** certify the **14,921** unconstrained optimum for the explicitly defined single-parent forest recipe. The particular seed-6 optimum needs **106 payload bits**; all three unchanged native column checkers reject it. It is an explicit failing calibration.
- An exact dynamic program checks **all 2^116 cut subsets of the fixed oriented tree** using **724 ancestor states**. Cutting at targets **5, 34, 39, 57, 78** attains the exact minimum D cost **15,025** in this class. The independently reimplemented recurrence agrees. Its complete positive-prefix maxima are **F=144651**, **B=9800790**, with `64 F^3 B^2 = 18606576056688220135806852422400 < 2^104`.
- Lean **4.21.0** proves generic XOR-circuit linearity/reversal, children-before-parent forest execution, and compensation for arbitrary helpers and arbitrary initial targets. Seven axiom reports contain only `propext` and `Quot.sound`; no `sorry` or extra axioms. Lean does not bind the concrete word or prove MST/DP, physical, or asymptotic claims.

Optimality is deliberately narrow. A positive scope-control test changes only `parent[32]` from 37 to 34 and obtains **15,023** D XORs with the same exact scalar prefix bound and valid 660-column/frame replay. title: Scoped negative result: PR626 jp8 and ck A/B frames admit no next complex tick at fixed order (exact duals, no new κ)
body:
# Fixed-order A/B frame exclusion for the selected PR626 complex providers

**Scoped negative result; no new κ.** Base `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Sprint track: complex supplier (OS seed 23).

## Claim

Take the emitted programs of the two selected #626 complex providers: **jp8**, used in 64 of the 72 calls, and **ck**, used in 8. Use both orientations. The macro list, order and operands stay fixed, as do every start frame, final frame and target level, each centre chain, and the frame of every macro outside phases A and B. Any frame in F_2^9 may then be assigned to any A or B scalar macro, simultaneously. No assignment that is legal under `hpe_audit_local.py`'s frame rules yields a native complex moment below one at

    b_next = 102387919519255428911/62500000000000000000000

This is the next 10^-24 grid point above #626's accepted endpoint. With owners, widths, the bit supplier and the outer assembly unchanged, frame-only reassignment therefore cannot raise the binding complex endpoint, and so cannot raise the selected κ.

## Proof (finite, exact)

1. **Domains.** Forward joins from the fixed starts and pins give `lo_i`, and backward meets from the finals and pins give `hi_i`. Every legal frame satisfies `lo_i <= G_i <= hi_i`. In these words `dim(hi/lo) <= 3`. The verifier enumerates every subspace in each interval and checks completeness: 2, 5 or 16 choices per macro (`model.py`).
2. **LP.** For each component of free macros, the local-polytope LP uses variables x(i,G), plus nested pair variables y on consecutive macros of a register (counted with multiplicity). Every legal assignment is a 0/1 point of this LP. Each register's total climb is fixed, so the paid local moment equals sum n_k c_k plus a constant, where c_k = k^(1-b) - k. The common positive factor m^b/(mW) is dropped.
3. **Duals.** Each component has a rational dual whose entries are linear forms in c_2..c_9. The verifier checks two things. First, every reduced cost is >= 0 at b_next, using two rational engines: its own atanh/alternating-series engine, and the pinned repository `moment.py`. Second, the dual objective equals the literal #626 baseline as an exact coefficient-vector identity. By weak duality, every legal assignment costs at least as much as the baseline.
4. **Global step.** Using the pinned #626 `ASSEMBLY.json` profile, both engines put the baseline global moment minus one at about +6.49e-25 at b_next. Every child term increases with b. So for each call, each reassignment has a local moment at least the baseline's at b_next, and the reassigned supplier is rejected at b_next and above.

Small components (63 for jp8 and 96 for ck, per orientation) are also brute-forced over all legal assignments as an independent cross-check.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-k492-frame-bound/verify.py            # committed inputs, ~30 s, stdlib only
python3 -B research/complex-k492-frame-bound/verify.py --controls # six controls must be rejected
```

Expected: `PASS_FIXED_ORDER_AB_FRAME_EXCLUSION_PR626` and `PASS_CONTROLS 6 of 6 rejected`. `--work DIR` checks fresh outputs of `research/complex-k492-owner-repair/verify.sh DIR` instead.

The inputs are the jp8/ck `CANONICAL-WORD` and `LOCAL-PROGRAMS` files. Their gzip SHA-256 equals the hashes recorded in `research/community-k492-audit/pr626/replay/mixed-global/base/providers/*/INDEPENDENT-LOCAL-REPLAY.json`, and the decompressed payload hashes are pinned in `SOURCES.json`.

This was validated in two ways: the full #626 provider replay was run fresh on macOS with Python 3.12, and its outputs matched; and the verifier was run on Python 3.11 and 3.15. Running with `-O` is refused.

The six controls are:
- a dropped component
- an inflated dual
- an incomplete domain
- the accepted (rather than next) endpoint
- a legal but worse baseline, which the duals must not certify
- the wrong word

`gen_duals.py` (needs highspy/scipy) nominates the duals; it is deterministic, reproducing the pinned payload hash. `explore/exact.py` (needs ortools) solves the same exact model with CP-SAT and reports the baseline objective as optimal for both words. It is a solver cross-check, not part of the proof.

## Exploratory findings (not shipped as checks)

- A per-register rank-path relaxation, which drops shared geometry, leaves gaps on 410 jp8 registers.
- A coupled dimension-only relaxation claims a large spurious gain, which shrinks after pair-span cuts but does not vanish.
- Greedy and annealed block moves and a flag-structured frame family all found no improvement.

So the geometric subspace constraints are what close the gap, which is why the full subspace LP is needed.

## Scope

Not covered:
- scalar rewrites, reordering, or changed cuts or centres
- frames of zero-frame precondition, cleanup-tail and full-frame-cleanup macros
- changed starts or finals (and so widths), owners, hosting or the invoice
- the bit supplier, other words (for example the open #645/#659/#685 lineages), or other outer theorems

The result holds at the fixed exponent b_next, not for all exponents. All inherited all-size, compiler, realization, hosting, precision, tape and analytic assumptions remain. This is a finite certificate, not a Lean proof.

## Credit

The method follows chafreaky's #557 (`research/frame-domain-ceiling`, PR551 word): complete F_2 domains, an LP relaxation and symbolic exact duals. This package is a new implementation against the emitted #626 programs. Concurrent #698 (thakrarsagar) proves ck B-phase optimality at fixed end-of-B frames for all exponents; this result independently corroborates it at b_next and adds jp8, joint A/B freedom and the global next-tick exclusion. #661 (yuj1r0) is the bit analogue.

The suppliers and their lineage are Jeremy Kothe (#622), Chafik Boukhalfa (#626), DreamingOfClouds, icekylinx and the selected-record contributors. Prepared with substantial AI assistance (Anthropic Claude). Apache-2.0.

---
Status: **negative result** (scoped). Only `research/complex-k492-frame-bound/` is added; selected record and `upstream/` untouched. Overlap refresh done before submission: #698 (ck B-phase, fixed end-of-B) is the closest work and is credited above; this adds jp8, joint A/B freedom and a global exclusion at the next grid point. No pinned coordination issue existed; claim recorded locally. Full repository suite and Linux CI not run.

Independently verifies **Agastya Sondhi / @TMM2009’s PR727** at `71ba94c981477b3527ef21dd0f8140e795a7664d`, using a third footprint algorithm: sorted interval endpoints. **Status: independent verification and scoped tooling evidence; no new optimization or κ claim.**

```text
owner intervals → sort endpoints → reject overlap → sum lengths → check prefix/idle width
```

The new oracle uses neither bit masks nor per-coordinate occupancy sets. It reconstructs all **16,128 owner bins**, **280,592 occupied coordinates** and the complete idle histogram for **35,424 helper roles**. Original sets, PR727 masks and the endpoint oracle agree. The entire inherited checker receipt and relevant internal states are compared, including exact moment fractions.

This adds a different verification method, invalid interval enumeration, stateful sequence checks and same-input replay evidence. PR727 already supplied its own set/mask tests; this package credits that work and vendors four exact source/provenance files with their original notice. Only `research/owner-footprint-crosscheck/` is added, so it can be reviewed independently of PR727’s package.

Exact base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. The selected #626/#543 result remains `51110230636731/31250000000000000`. `SOURCES.json` pins the 17 original inputs and four PR727 files with SHA-256 and Git blob identities. Native artifacts are archived PR622 outputs, not a fresh reconstruction.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -I -B research/owner-footprint-crosscheck/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_OWNER_FOOTPRINT_CROSSCHECK ... sweep_owners=16128`.

- Complete-map replay; **21,500 exhaustive cases**, **6,000 sequential operations**, nine full-map corruptions, five actual-code mutations and four source-pin controls. Both complete engines reject with matching diagnostics; the independent oracle rejects all four footprint corruptions.
- Normal and optimized Python 3.12.12/3.14.7 checks pass. A minimal export replays from a path with spaces and an unrelated working directory. The four vendored files match PR727’s exact remote Git blobs.
- Fifteen alternating fresh-process pairs per interpreter: full-check median wall time **0.303022 → 0.274185 s (9.52% less)** on Python 3.12 and **0.297138 → 0.272085 s (8.43% less)** on Python 3.14. All 60 timed receipts match byte for byte. Both modes include the same source-admission harness, unlike the author’s direct-CLI reference setup; no claim to reproduce their absolute timings or percentages. Raw samples are retained. No RSS reduction or full-frontier speedup is claimed.
- Selected-record binding, all five existing selected-record tests, seven historical source inventories and staged whitespace checks pass. A final inventory check caught one agent-generated `.pyc`; only that cache was removed, with no reviewed source changes. Details are in `VALIDATION.md`.

No full repository suite, cold supplier replay, full controller/47-inequality assembly, Lean or remote CI pass is claimed. The oracle checks footprint accounting, not physical legality of its input windows. All inherited compiler/common-label/mutable-basis/hosting/residual/precision/tape/analytic assumptions remain.

Seed **89**, verification engineering. The final overlap refresh found PR727, so the overlapping optimization was retired and this independent audit was completed instead. No pinned coordination issue existed; the local claim contains the result and source link. Refresh through #767 found no endpoint-sweep audit of PR727; its pinned head and base main were unchanged.

Credit Agastya Sondhi/TMM2009 for the mask optimization; Chafik Boukhalfa/chafreaky for the independent checker; Jeremy Kothe/jeremykothe2, DreamingOfClouds, Rohan Arun, icekylinx, eumemic and the retained construction lineage. Prepared by **Brian / JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, Apache-2.0. “Independent” describes the endpoint algorithm and replay, not independent human review.

**Door:** two-way. **Blast Radius:** isolated research package. No existing source, default command, selected-frontier pointer or `upstream/` file changes.

title: Construction: one coded helper for all-K packet delivery
body:
A six-source all-K packet cell can share partial sums through one coded helper while preserving arbitrary dirty inputs. This PR adds an explicit circuit, a strict paid-profile comparison, and a rebuild inside the native complex word. It also retains the analytic single-pair obstruction and resolves the broader positive no-helper search that previously timed out.

The selected cell is pair `(6,7)`, sign `+1`, chosen from OS seed 23 and the recorded salt. Existing supplier files and the selected certificate are unchanged; the package is confined to `research/complex-packet-borrowing23/`.

## Constructive result

- The one-helper cell has 28 core additions, five zero-frame preconditioning additions and two full-frame cleanup additions. Exact rational replay checks all 13 arbitrary input columns in forward and inverse-transpose orientations, with the dirty helper restored.
- Its paid profile is `32 H1 + 17 H2 + 11 H3`. The specified direct circuit with the same helper left idle has `48 H1 + 12 H2 + 6 H3 + H9`. Both have rank mass 99.
- The difference `-16 H1 + 5 H2 + 5 H3 - H9` strictly improves every recursive moment `sum H_r r^s`, `0 < s < 1`; the README gives an analytic inequality, not a numerical scan. The local scalar operation count is 35 versus 30, so this is a recursive frame-cost comparison.
- Both circuits rebuild inside the pinned raw K492 constructor with 490 helpers. The unchanged native auditor independently derives dirty-input compensation and verifies every one of the 714 columns in both orientations, all native frame chains and dyadic primitives. Both have rank mass 6,266, and their full native profiles have exactly the same difference as the cell.

## Exclusions and solver follow-up

The analytic proposition excludes source-dependent interactions on a single target pair without helpers, allowing arbitrary signed coefficients, read order and repeated pair operations. It binds to all eight signed all-K cells through explicit XOR-span checks and finite ordering controls.

An event-clock reformulation resolves the six-source no-helper search with arbitrary target-sharing graphs in the narrower positive unit-addition, disjoint-support domain. Z3 5.1.0 and CVC5 1.4.2 both return UNSAT on the same exported formula, in approximately 12.4 and 130.7 seconds. Direct-only and omitted-frame controls return SAT. The optional model, formula hash and solver receipts are included; no independently checked UNSAT proof object is claimed. The explicit constructive witness is verified without solver dependencies.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-packet-borrowing23/verify.py
```

Passed on Python 3.13.5 and 3.14.0, including `-I -O` and a relocated minimal checkout with `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=2`; inherited workers always run with assertions enabled. Changed source pins, corrupted expected evidence and altered assignment data are rejected. Circuit controls reject missing compensation, cleanup and helper delivery. The packaged optional model reproduces the exact formula hash checked by both solvers.

## Scope and credit

**No new κ, globally admitted supplier, optimal circuit or general coding barrier is claimed.** The native words are changed raw constructions; the later supplier transformations, phase lowering, wrappers, global owners and assembly have not been rebuilt for them. The comparison is against the specified matched-stock direct control, not the admitted incumbent.

The constructor, native auditor, source data and routing word are pinned and retain their upstream attribution. The package credits the #425/#433/#484/#531/#552/#622/#626 lineage and distinguishes the related scopes of #651 and #683. Prepared by NeoKazuya with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance (GPT-6-Astra), under Apache-2.0.

title: independent verification: r420 lattice parity and 480 added incidences
body:
**independent finite verification; no new kappa.** this certifies the selected #543 roots in the intrinsic lattice quotient `L/2L` and exhausts all 672 frames' binary-span root memberships. all dimensions agree with the rational frames, but 180 dimension-six frames gain two root classes each and 120 dimension-seven frames gain one: **300 changed closures and 480 extra memberships**.

every extra membership has an explicit integral lift, a nonzero rational minor, and an independently checked orthogonality witness. the 120 root lines correspond bijectively to the 120 quadratic-value-one classes among all 256 quotient classes. reducing the displayed coordinates directly modulo two instead gives only 15 root residues, so the checker first certifies an integral lattice basis and every root coordinate.

this adds the intrinsic characteristic-two census and lift witnesses beyond sagar thakrar's #737 (`b41e73169430641be18c988c659d2855a6a6218a`), which certifies rational/odd-prime geometry. it does not challenge #737 or allege a supplier defect. eumemic's existing p111 use of lattice classes for decoder affine rank is explicitly credited; that idea is not claimed new. no predecessor arithmetic is imported.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r420-lattice-parity/verify.py
```

- a separate direct-pairing encoding with modular elimination matches every parity closure. permutation determinants check the arithmetic, and original-coordinate lifts plus positive norm/orthogonality independently check every extra witness.

body:
Independent audit of #696 by Sagar Thakrar (`thakrarsagar`) at head `5a3f983715027c4fd83f50bc9001d4b18463bed1`. **Verdict: the 22–25% primitive claim is confirmed exactly. It does not change κ.**

Exact base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60` (current `main`, also the base of #696). Only `research/community-pr696-audit/` is added. Credit for the construction belongs to #696.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/community-pr696-audit/recount.py
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_PR696_INDEPENDENT_RECOUNT savings=55320,55352,56852,56884 percent=22.10-24.60 kappa_inputs_unchanged=True
```

The recount uses the standard library, runs offline, writes nothing and takes about 3 minutes. It imports no #696 code.

### Findings

| Program | Old | New | Saved | % |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CK forward | 224,938 | 169,618 | 55,320 | 24.59 |
| CK backward | 224,986 | 169,634 | 55,352 | 24.60 |
| JP8 forward | 257,232 | 200,380 | 56,852 | 22.10 |
| JP8 backward | 257,280 | 200,396 | 56,884 | 22.11 |

- The re-derived Horner baseline equals each emitter's `real_component_primitive_bound`. The re-implemented copy-init and unit rules match every #696 count. The saving equals `2·(additions + units)` in every program.
- A separate randomized replay checks every complete program twice per real component, with dirty private work. After every macro the old and new states are equal, and `W = 0` after each addition. Every value the new word writes to a register also occurs in that register in the old trace.
- **κ:** the selected assembly (`complex-k492-owner-repair/code/assemble.py`) computes κ from the paid profile, `m = 73`, `live`, the deficit and the PR543 bit profile. Scalar primitives enter only the finite per-vertex invoice and its pass/fail inequalities, which already pass. Over the 72 selected calls, the lowering saves 4,082,112 of 18,263,888 scalar primitives, or 8.7·10⁻¹⁰ of the per-vertex allowance. This cannot feed a κ gain in the current model.

### Limits

`make verify`, the cold selected replay and Lean were not run. The inherited geometric, compiler, hosting, precision and tape contracts were not audited. Open #681, which consolidates #696, was not audited.

title: Research theorem: sharp scratch-dependent call bound for dirty echoes
body:
Proves a sharp call bound for ordered dirty-echo trees: `N >= 2^(s+1)n - 4^s`, with an explicit attaining family for every `s >= 2` and `3*2^(s-2) <= n <= 2^s`. In particular, 50 factors with six arbitrary dirty arrays have exact minimum **2,304 complete leaf calls**, versus 2,752 for the pinned balanced binary word. All inverse and restoration work is included.

**Status: research note / independent verification; no new kappa.** The theorem is scoped to static ordered echo trees with reserved parent scratch. It is not a minimum over arbitrary reversible programs or a multiplication improvement.

Concurrent #758 already supplies all-arity weighted optimization; #730 supplies mixed binary/ternary optimization and #744 a strict-ternary audit. This contribution credits them and adds the analytic scratch-dependent bound and equality family. Its independent uniform-cost implementation also corroborates #758 at nine pinned instances. The echo itself is #673's, the stronger balanced comparator is #689's, and the rounded leaves are #628's.

[Proof](https://github.com/AlexS-scale/integer-mult-bounds/blob/548e42022b37a300f8bf745e848c38baccbce056/research/dirty-echo-space-budget/PROOF.md) · [Exact certificate](https://github.com/AlexS-scale/integer-mult-bounds/blob/548e42022b37a300f8bf745e848c38baccbce056/research/dirty-echo-space-budget/EXPECTED.json) · [Source pins](https://github.com/AlexS-scale/integer-mult-bounds/blob/548e42022b37a300f8bf745e848c38baccbce056/research/dirty-echo-space-budget/SOURCES.json) · [Validation](https://github.com/AlexS-scale/integer-mult-bounds/blob/548e42022b37a300f8bf745e848c38baccbce056/research/dirty-echo-space-budget/VALIDATION.md)

- 2,904 signed noncommutative identities/inverse checks, 1,530 nonlinear round trips, and 186 rounded compositions with dense exact references and counted phase reads.
- Instruction and interface negative controls, relocated replay, seven artifact-corruption/overwrite controls, 13 exact Git source bindings, and selected-record integrity.

title: Scoped negative result: Hurwitz copy floor for fixed-support nonlinear messages
body:
Scoped negative result; **no new kappa**. On the ten Hurwitz E8 lines, fixed-support, deterministic, zero-error messages have minimum charge **10b quaternionic / 40b rational units** for b independent bits per port, even with nonlinear encoding and joint decoding. The essential premise is explicit: a q-bit message is charged q times its reader/source pairing rank, additively across messages. This note does not establish that physical pricing premise for arbitrary nonlinear circuits.

The proof extends Douglas R. Colkitt's scalar-total result in #703 by replacing binary rank with conditional transcript injectivity. It retains the predecessor's geometry, charge table and weighted transversals. Arbitrary finite block widths, unequal demands and any finite number of messages are allowed. An explicitly nonlinear code attains the bound. Under the additional inherited Dfc accounting, even zero helper, access, frame, restoration and recursive expenses give `D/T <= -40b`, so no paid construction or assembly improvement is claimed.

Only `research/hurwitz-nonlinear-copy-floor/` is added. Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. The selected construction and `upstream/` are unchanged. Seed **42**, structural decoder research. The local claim records three candidates, the exact scope and result; no pinned sprint issue exists.

Reproduce with CPython 3.10+ and the standard library:

```sh
uv run --offline python -B research/hurwitz-nonlinear-copy-floor/verify.py
uv run --offline python -B research/hurwitz-nonlinear-copy-floor/test_verify.py
```

Expected main receipt:

```text
PASS_HURWITZ_NONLINEAR_COPY: 1048576 support pairs; 3 attaining codes; 12 rejection controls; conditional floor 10b
```

Validation passes on CPython 3.10.21, 3.13.15 and optimized 3.14.7. The package checks all 240 roots, 100 singleton pairing ranks, 45 two-line spans, all 1,048,576 support pairs and 33,856 conditional transcripts. Four additional tests compare all 145 geometric obligations with an independent Fraction column algorithm, explicitly invert the nonlinear examples, exhaust all 65,536 one-bit encoders on four ports, and reject receipt/manifest mutations in a relocated isolated optimized replay. A clean committed `git archive` passes from an unrelated working directory. Selected-record integrity and whitespace checks pass. The unchanged expensive repository-wide and selected cold-replay suites were not repeated; no remote CI or proof-assistant pass is claimed.

The physical width-pricing and stage-accounting assumptions remain unresolved outside the declared model. Adaptive or interactive supports, correlated inputs, errors, cheaper sharing between coordinates and extra nonorthogonal side information are excluded. An explicit boundary example demonstrates why the last restriction matters. Finite replay is not the all-width proof.

Pre-submission overlap checks covered the full live queue through #775, then recent arrivals through #782. They inspected #765's tensor factorization result, #767's Gaussian subclass obstructions and #770's Gaussian weighted-clique ceiling, which have distinct model or geometry scope. Exact predecessor pins and credit are included for #703, Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled's #620, DreamingOfClouds' #446/accounting work and Sagar Thakrar's related #738. No predecessor implementation is imported.

Prepared by Alexander Templeton (@azide0x37) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof development, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0. No independent human review is claimed.

title: Research: factor center quarters and certify the adapter-cost limit (no kappa)
body:
The selected #626 CK and JP8 programs each use 224 signed quarter-coefficient center taps. Factoring the quarter once into each of the eight private centers saves **864 real scalar primitives per orientation**, with exact recursive-call inputs, dirty-input restoration and prefix bounds preserved.

**Status: finite circuit construction and scoped cost audit / research note; no new kappa.** The complete accounting matters: the literal rewrite adds eight scale macros, increasing the generic adapter allowance by 128. The conservative local bound therefore **increases by 3,319,594,144** for each provider. This is not a net supplier-cost improvement; the package certifies both the scalar identity and that integration limit.

| Scalar program | Original primitives | Factored primitives |
|---|---:|---:|
| CK forward | 224,938 | 224,074 |
| CK inverse-transpose | 224,986 | 224,122 |
| JP8 forward | 257,232 | 256,368 |
| JP8 inverse-transpose | 257,280 | 256,416 |

The scale occurs after the forward center descent and before the reverse ascent. No commutation with a recursive operator is assumed. A negative control preserves scalar endpoints while changing a recursive-call input, and is rejected. Every source copy, coefficient preparation, scale, clear and recursive child remains charged. Coefficient work is still cleared after each addition. The complete local invoices, original source bindings and unchanged paid profiles are included in the exact receipt.

Only `research/complex-center-quarter/` is added: proof, deterministic construction, exact receipt, 14 source pins, integer-matrix crosscheck, focused failure tests, validation record and local sprint claim. The selected frontier and `upstream/` are unchanged.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-center-quarter/verify.py
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_COMPLEX_CENTER_QUARTER programs=4 centers=32 saving=864_each columns=724 controls=32+50 invoice_delta=+3319594144 kappa=unchanged
```

Passed on Windows, CPython 3.12.10, standard library only. Verification covers all 724 formal input columns in each original/candidate program; arbitrary private work at every changed block; the unchanged native frame/wrapper auditor and its 50 controls; and 32 new block controls. A separate integer implementation checks 57,600 matrix entries and 32 clear omissions. Five focused tests, isolated optimized execution, a minimal relocated checkout with spaces, gzip repackaging, source/receipt corruption, output preservation, selected-record verification and staged whitespace checks pass.

### Provenance, overlap and limits

Base: **`66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`**. OS seed **35**, complex supplier; JP8 first and center 3 for the initial witness/controls. Selected #626 is pinned at `660de893d27bb7abd1d5b01b1640207528a5c851`, with #622/#623 and #543 dependencies recorded. No pinned coordination issue exists, so the claim is local.

The pre-submission refresh covered 602 open PRs through #783; upstream main still equals the exact base. New #776's fixed-order A/B frame exclusion leaves scalar rewrites and changed centers outside its scope and does not overlap this experiment.

Concurrent **#755 by @taizaki69** is explicitly credited: its coefficient reuse also covers the 224 forward JP8 center taps. This adds the reverse common-target gather, CK coverage, recursive-input equality and the complete extra-macro cost audit. It claims no priority or stronger primitive saving for forward JP8 centers. #745 motivates arbitrary private-center coverage; #750 relocates a live cleanup scale; #696/#723/#734, #722/#739/#751 and #769 use different coefficient lowerings or reuse classes. No pending implementation is imported and no additive saving is asserted.

Credit to icekylinx, Jeremy Kothe/AtomScout, Chafik Boukhalfa, DreamingOfClouds, Dominik Scholz, Dugongue, Rohan Arun, eumemic and the retained predecessor notices. Prepared for **@ssteeper with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, Apache-2.0. Both checking implementations were written in one AI session; no independent human review is claimed.

The experiment stops at this verified local circuit and cost result. A grouped center-microcircuit admission rule, global invoice/hosting replay and production integration are separate work. All inherited compiler, realization, precision/tape, recovery and analytic assumptions remain. Full `make verify`, cold supplier regeneration, Lean and remote Linux CI were not run or claimed. title: Research: reusable clean checkpoint lowers weighted binary leaf bill 20 to 16 (no new kappa)
body:
For four ordered complete signed-leaf prices `(1,3,1,1)` and two scratch arrays, reusing one initially clean array across successive subtrees lowers the exact weighted leaf bill from **20 to 16**, with the same twelve leaf calls and full dirty restoration. An interval dynamic program optimizes this explicitly defined ordered binary/reserved-connector class.
