title: Research note: factor R420 block 9 from 38 to 24 XORs (28 fewer native ADDs, no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research note with a finite circuit construction and exact verification. No new κ.** The selected certificate, its κ (`51110230636731/31250000000000000`) and `upstream/` are unchanged. All files are new, under `research/r420-block9-factorization/`.

In eumemic's #543 R420 bit word, phase-B block 9 is the 38-XOR slice `B[559:597]` at frame 551 (rational rank four), on the twelve source registers `8, 13, 33, 39, 42, 47, 80, 85, 88, 94, 114, 119`. This PR replaces it with 24 XORs. Regenerating the literal reverse cleanup saves 14 more, at the rank-eight full frame. D, A, the scatter, the retained totals and every other B gate are unchanged.

| Quantity | Original | Replacement |
|---|---:|---:|
| Block 9 XORs | 38 | 24 |
| Literal cleanup gate records | 2,661 | 2,647 |
| Complete native scalar ADDs | 26,916 | 26,888 |
| Local reverse positive prefix bound | 2,270,064 | 2,234,964 |
| Local forward positive prefix bound | 144,651 | 144,651 |
| Paid rank mass | 5,112 | 5,112 |

- **Exact block identity.** Write `T_ab = I + e_a e_b^T`. The old and new chronological gate lists have the same positive integer transfer matrix, so block 9 computes the same linear map over every commutative ring, F2 included, on arbitrary register contents. The signed inverse is also identical, and the ordered physical output assignment is kept. The complete dirty-restored word is certified over F2; its defining endpoint is not claimed over the integers.
- **Positive bounds do not grow.** The positive reverse transfer is entrywise no larger, with 22 strict entries. Block followed by positive reverse improves 102 entries, and its unit-input maximum falls from 973 to 137. The unchanged exterior operations are monotone on nonnegative bounds, so the domination carries through the whole word and no prefix bound increases. The five-stage payload stays at 100 bits and the nine-stage charge at 192 bits.
- **No hidden cost.** The change adds no helper, source access, copy, frame change or recursive child. Every register keeps its frame path, and the paid histogram `{1:1320, 2:1440, 4:60, 5:120, 8:9}` is unchanged. The interface is #543's original H1–H5, including literal cleanup reversal (H4).
- **Search.** A seeded walk factors the block's 12-by-12 transfer matrix from both ends: subtracting a dominated row removes a final gate, subtracting a column removes a first gate, and entries stay nonnegative. With OS seed 19 it ran a fixed 2,000 trials. 372 reached the identity, 236 of those had a dominated positive reverse, and the best has 24 gates. 24 is not claimed minimal.

**Predecessor work.** Details and pins are in the README and SOURCES.json.
- eumemic's #543, reviewed at `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`, supplies the R420 word, source plan, integer norm objective, interleaved interface and exact checker, building on #493.
- The exporter, checker and pricing lineage is credited in the README: Dylan Crow (#370 word and exporter), DaysSky (bridged cohort checker), DreamingOfClouds (#503/#510 and #463 nine-stage pricing), Zhihao Chen (#425 interface), Chafik Boukhalfa (common-label and hosting/emitter work), and the cumulative authors in the selected maintainer review.
- #661 (yuj1r0) proves the R420 phase-B frames moment-optimal at fixed gate order and excludes resynthesis. This PR changes the gate list instead of reopening that class.

**Open obligations.**
- Build the globally hosted owner program, physical invoice and outer assembly for the changed word, and update the supplier bindings. In the nine-stage invoice's scalar term, `9 * 32 * local_additions + bridge_additions`, the local saving would remove 8,064 ADDs; nothing hosted is regenerated here.
- Settle whether 24 gates is minimal for this block.
- Discharge the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-basis realization, pooled hosting, normalized residual, precision/tape/exact-recovery and analytic-transfer assumptions.

No κ change follows from the local count: the recursive profile and rounded prefix budgets are unchanged, and the selected assembly is complex-bound.

[Research note and proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/README.md), [frozen circuit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/CANDIDATE.json), [certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/CERTIFICATE.json), [source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/SOURCES.json), [validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/VALIDATION.json), [verifier](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/verify.py) and [search](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/search.py).

**Overlap.** The pre-submission refresh at 05:31 UTC on 13 October searched the titles and bodies of the 320 most recent PRs (#462–#782, all states) and read every R420 circuit PR among them; none changes block 9's gates. `main` is still at base `66849e1`, so no merged change touches the word. #670 (yongjae321) and #674 (x0hu) resynthesize blocks 3 and 5, by local F2 rewrites and explicit sum sharing. #688 (Ali Romman) composes those two, and #681 (alluri-ritual) consolidates #688 with phase-A, D, decoder and complex-supplier work; none of the four touches block 9, and no composition with them is certified here. The one direct interaction is #754 (namredips), which keeps B fixed and rewrites four-wire cleanup windows under a semantic H4′. Two of its 101 windows, `[120,124)` and `[126,130)` of the expanded original cleanup (one XOR each), lie inside block 9's reversed segment `[120,158)`, which this PR replaces wholesale, so the two savings are not additive. #710's conjugation lies outside that segment, and #691 (mtpsl) applies the same forward-equality and reverse-domination test to phase-A quad 13. #686, #694, #713, #716, #733, #742, #759 and #774 change the frame-zero compensation D, and #708, #748 and #753 change the phase-A decoder totals; each saves more than 28 ADDs. This PR is the only change to block 9, and unlike several of those D and decoder changes it raises no positive prefix bound.

## Validation

From the repository root, with Python 3.11+, a C++17 compiler and Boost headers (no Python packages):

```sh
python3 -B research/r420-block9-factorization/verify.py
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_R420_BLOCK9_FACTORIZATION gates=38->24 native_adds=26916->26888 columns=660/900/1380/1620 rank_mass=5112
```

The driver writes the rebuilt word, exported records, checker receipts and logs to a fresh directory under `build/`, and compares every proof-relevant field with CERTIFICATE.json. It compares regenerated gzip output by canonical decompressed JSON. The lane's run passed on Linux x86-64 with Python 3.12.3 and GCC 13.3.0.

- **Finite checks.**
  - Exact integer transfer, signed inverse and entrywise positive-bound comparisons for the block, in unbounded Python integers.
  - #543's own E8 label, rational-frame, all-column and H1–H5 checks on both complete words.
  - A separate standard-library interpreter replays all 660 dirty-input columns one at a time in both orientations, and reconstructs every exported MOVE/ADD/COPY/ERASE record, frame path, paid profile and positive prefix. It imports no predecessor checker or search code.
  - The unchanged C++ legality checker and five-, nine- and eleven-stage column checkers run on both words: 900, 1,380 and 1,620 physical columns, with 6, 18 and 24 omitted-bridge controls per word. The C++ and Python prefix and profile results must agree.
  - The checker rejects all 15 new negative controls. They include an integer-correct 25-gate factorization with a worse positive reverse, and a stale literal cleanup that passes the F2 endpoint replay but fails H4.
- **Proof arguments.** Equality over every commutative ring follows from the equal integer transfer matrices. The README gives the written argument that reverse domination propagates through the monotone exterior to every prefix of the whole word; the finite prefix replays agree with it but do not replace it.
- **Search reproduction.** `python3 -B research/r420-block9-factorization/search.py --seed 19 --trials 2000 --output NEW-candidate.json` regenerates the frozen candidate in the recorded environment. Verification neither imports the search nor trusts its trace.
- **Repository checks.** `make selected-record-check` passes: `PASS selected record, exact kappa, original source inventory and proof supplement: 51110230636731/31250000000000000`. `git diff --check` is clean, and no existing file or `upstream/` byte changes. The verifier above was re-run on the submitted commit.
- **Not claimed.** This is not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem, not a hosted, invoice or outer-assembly replay, and not a full repository suite, Linux CI or Lean pass. No composition with a concurrent PR is certified, and 24 gates is not claimed minimal.

Sprint: bit-supplier track, OS seed 19. The claim and its result update are recorded locally. title: Research audit: exact path penalties for general idempotent labels (no new kappa)
body:
The historical cancellation audit's two-unit path bound is correct for its diagonal/common-form rank-one endpoints. Carrying that rule over to arbitrary idempotent or block labels needs a more precise penalty: **rank(PQ) + rank(QP)**. This research audit proves the sharp endpoint identity, gives exact boundary examples, and verifies the retained compiler's complementary-block rank-additivity argument. **No new kappa and no counterexample to the selected construction.**

The useful distinction is concrete: a one-sided rank-one pair has excess **1**; common-form rank-two labels can have excess **2**, not automatically 4. An arbitrary common additive offset can erase the original excess, while the compiler's actual `prior` / `I-prior` split preserves it. Original side-edge checkers correctly reject both one-sided orientations.

## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research construction with exact verification. No new κ.** The selected certificate, its κ (`51110230636731/31250000000000000`) and `upstream/` are unchanged. All files are new, under `research/r420-target-compensation/`.

eumemic's #543 R420 bit word implements its frame-zero dirty-helper compensation D, `y <- y + K s` for a fixed binary 120-by-420 matrix `K`, with 19,922 XORs. This PR factors `K` through a reversible target basis. D first applies 205 target transvections `y[a] ^= y[b]`, whose product is `E`. It then adds helpers along the 11,633 nonzero entries of `R = E K`, and finally repeats the 205 transvections in reverse order. Over F2 the result is `E^-1 (E y + R s) = y + K s` for arbitrary incoming targets and helpers. D never writes a helper or a source and needs no workspace.

| Quantity | #543 | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| D XORs (entrance + helper injections + exit) | 19,922 | 12,043 (205 + 11,633 + 205) |
| Complete native word, XORs | 26,916 | 19,037 |
| Hosted instructions, 288 local calls | 8,603,712 | 6,334,560 |
| Forward / reverse positive bounds F / B | 144,651 / 2,270,064 | 144,651 / 4,409,580 |
| Local payload `64 F^3 B^2`, bits (cap 104) | 100 | 102 |
| Nine-stage prefix `2^18 F^5 B^4` / charge, bits | 189 / 192 | 192 / 192 |
| Two-level coefficient / charge, bits | 416 / 512 | 424 / 512 |

- **Unchanged.** Only D changes. The 420 helpers, the nine COPY/ERASE pairs, every register's frame path, the paid profile `{1:1320, 2:1440, 4:60, 5:120, 8:9}` with rank mass 5,112, and the recursive children stay as they are. The bit lower bound and the selected κ reproduce exactly.
- **Prefix.** The reverse bound grows. The search admitted a row step only if F stayed at most 144,651 and B at most 4,409,638, the largest B with `2^18 F^5 B^4 < 2^192`, so the existing 192-bit nine-stage and 512-bit two-level charges still hold. The unrounded invoice coefficient increases. The claim is fewer instructions under unchanged charges, not a measured speedup.
- **Changed hypothesis.** The new D breaks #543's gate-local H2, under which D gates read only helpers, and #543's direct `K_equals_D` extraction no longer applies. The verifier records both predicates as false and keeps every other H1–H5 check. In their place, README.md proves a semantic D-boundary lemma: D runs at frame zero and implements exactly `(x, y, s) -> (x, y + K s, s)`, so the unchanged remainder of the word sees identical values and frames. The verifier checks that boundary on all 660 symbolic columns.
- **Search.** OS seed 18 chose this object (`18 mod 3 = 0` among three candidates). At each step a greedy pass scored every ordered pair of target rows, kept only steps that passed an exact incremental prefix check, and broke ties with the seed. It stopped after 205 steps and 2,941,680 pair evaluations, when no admissible positive-gain pair remained; the cap was 1,000 steps. An unrestricted control with the same seed reached 10,384 D XORs but needed 201 nine-stage bits and broke the 104-bit payload cap, so it is kept only as a rejected control. 12,043 is not claimed optimal.

**Predecessor work.** Details and pins for 39 source files are in README.md and SOURCES.json.
- eumemic's #543, reviewed at `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535` and building on #493, supplies the word, the compensation matrix, the interleaved interface and the checker this package reuses.
- Credit carried from #543's lineage: Dylan Crow (E8 word, record and checker lineage), DreamingOfClouds (#503/#510, generalized nine-stage accounting), DaysSky (bridged columns, whole-call hosting), Zhihao Chen (mutable-source/common-label and compressed geometry) and Chafik Boukhalfa (physical routes, templates and audits). Chafik Boukhalfa's selected #626 supplies the complex lower bound that the hosted replay cites.
- Dugongue's #476 and #478 used the reversible donor-receiver target identity on R715 phase B. Each transvection pair here is that identity, applied to the compensation.
- Mikhail R. Gadelha's concurrent #686 published the semantic D-boundary substitution first. This PR claims no priority for it or for basis factoring.

**Open obligations.**
- A maintainer must accept the semantic D-boundary lemma in place of the gate-local H2 and update the supplier's source bindings.
- B sits 58 below the nine-stage cutoff, so combining this D with any change that raises F or B needs a fresh prefix recount.
- The all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-basis realization, pooled hosting, normalized residual, precision/tape recovery and analytic-transfer assumptions remain inherited.

[Research note and proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/README.md), [frozen recipe](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/candidate.json), [certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/CERTIFICATE.json), [hosted certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/HOSTED-CERTIFICATE.json), [source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/SOURCES.json), [validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/VALIDATION.json), [seed, search and overlap record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/RESEARCH.json), [verifier](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/verify.py) and [search](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/search.py).

**Overlap.** No coordination issue exists; the only open issue, #650, asks about Discussions. The circuit was nominated and frozen locally before any concurrent D PR was read (RESEARCH.json records the freeze at 04:19 UTC on 13 October), and nothing from those PRs is imported. The package README records the overlap as of 04:25 UTC, when only #686 and #694 had appeared. A refresh between 05:28 and 05:37 UTC searched PR titles and bodies through #788 and read every PR among them that changes D. `main` is still `66849e1`, so nothing on D has merged. Many open PRs now change this D, and two reach lower counts:

| PR | Basis and recipe class | D XORs | Native XORs | Nine-stage bits |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| This PR | target; 205 successive steps | 12,043 | 19,037 | 192 |
| #686 | helper; one pair | 19,814 | 26,808 | 189 |
| #694 | helper; 201 disjoint pairs | 12,988 | 19,982 | 192 |
| #713 | target; 57 disjoint pairs | 16,772 | 23,766 | 191 |
| #716 | target; 60 disjoint pairs, optimal among disjoint pairs | 16,672 | 23,666 | 191 |
| #742 | target; shared donors | 16,634 | 23,628 | 192 |
| #759 | target; rooted forest | 15,138 | 22,132 | 197 |
| #774 | target; forest with optimized cuts | 15,025 | 22,019 | 197 |
| #733 | #694's helper basis, then 57 target pairs | 11,554 | 18,548 | 195 |
| #681 | #694's helper basis, then 56 target pairs, in a six-PR consolidation | 11,562 | 18,378 | 196 |

The last column applies this package's nine-stage formula to each PR's reported F and B. The other D PRs check the local payload against 2^104 and leave the hosted prefix to integration; #681 reports 196 bits itself, and the formula reproduces it. #681's native count includes its phase-A, phase-B and decoder changes.

- **Lower counts.** Scott Woolsey Biggart's #733 and the D stage of Alluri's #681 use 489 and 481 fewer D XORs than this PR. Both exceed the 192-bit nine-stage charge: #681 raises its allocation to 256 bits and replays the hosted invoice at that charge, and #733 leaves global invoices open. This PR does not settle whether their extra savings are worth the larger allocation.
- **What this adds.** Of the D constructions that keep the existing 192-bit charge, this one saves the most, 945 XORs more than Greer Guthrie's #694. Apart from #681's consolidation, it is the only D package that replays the complete nine-stage hosted invoice. Its D of 12,043 lies below the 14,921-XOR floor that Oscar Fennell's #759 certifies for rooted target forests, a floor Anthony's #774 corroborates, so this circuit lies outside that class, as it lies outside the disjoint pairs of Sagar Thakrar's #716. Scott Woolsey Biggart's #713 published the first target-side circuit, at 04:40 UTC, followed by #716 and ellipsi2's #742.
- **Composition and conflict.** These PRs replace the same D subword, so they are alternatives; no file paths collide. #733 shows that a helper basis and a target basis compose. At #694's F = 202,699, however, the 192-bit charge allows B only up to 2,892,279, against #694's own 2,446,788, so this PR attempts no such composition. cxnmai's #748 changes K itself through a decoder-total representation, which would require recomputing this recipe on the new matrix. #731 (Joshua Snider) and #762 (Sagar Thakrar) verify the baseline K and complement this work. #749 (Sricharan Vagvala) takes target pairs to the JP8 complex supplier. The phase-A, phase-B and cleanup PRs (#670, #674, #688, #691, #708, #710, #753, #754) change other subwords; combining any of them with this D needs the prefix recount above.

## Validation

From the repository root (Python 3.11+, standard library only):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r420-target-compensation/verify.py
```

Output, re-run on base `66849e1` with this package before submission (Linux, Python 3.12.3, about 3 seconds):

```text
PASS_R420_TARGET_COMPENSATION D=19922->12043 total=26916->19037 columns=660 rank_mass=5112 nine_bits=192 controls=13
```

`python3 -I -B research/r420-target-compensation/search.py` reruns both seed-18 trials and compares the full result with the frozen recipe. It printed `PASS_REPRODUCIBLE_SEARCH guarded_steps=205 D_adds=12043 trials=2 seed=18` in the same pre-submission run.

The optional complete hosted replay needs a C++17 compiler, Boost headers, and `requirements.txt` (SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.3.0) in a virtual environment. It writes a fresh directory under `build/`:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r420-target-compensation/replay_hosted.py
```

Expected final status:

```text
PASS_R420_TARGET_COMPENSATION_HOSTED local_adds=19037 hosted_events=6334560 prefix_charge=192 coefficient_charge=512 kappa=unchanged
```

- **Finite checks.**
  - `verify.py` runs #543's exact lattice, frame and symbolic-row engine, plus a separate Boolean walk of all 660 columns in each direction. It checks the frozen recipe without trusting or rerunning the search, and rejects all 13 negative controls. One control omits the whole entrance basis: it passes when targets start at zero but fails the arbitrary-target boundary.
  - The hosted replay freshly compiles the predecessor C++ engines. It checks 900 five-stage and 1,380 nine-stage formal columns with 6 and 18 omitted-bridge controls, and 4,740 unbanked parent columns; the parent and hosted audits reject 17 and 16 mutations. Four record controls omit a basis ADD, a helper ADD or a COPY, or understate a MOVE rank. All 47 outer assembly inequalities reproduce the selected κ from #626's pinned complex lower bound. The recorded run, on Linux with Python 3.12.3, SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.3.0 and GCC 13.3.0, produced a full report equal to HOSTED-CERTIFICATE.json. It was not re-run for this submission.
- **Proof arguments.** README.md proves the D-boundary lemma, its substitution into the unchanged word, and the exact incremental formula the search uses to admit steps. None of these is inferred from the finite replay. The identity holds over F2; the positive integer bounds are recomputed from the literal instructions in both orientations.
- **Repository checks.** `make selected-record-check` passes: `PASS selected record, exact kappa, original source inventory and proof supplement: 51110230636731/31250000000000000`. `git diff --check` is clean, and no existing file or `upstream/` byte changes. The verifier above was re-run on the submitted commit.
- **Not claimed.** This is not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem or a cold replay of the complex supplier; #626's complex bound is pinned and cited. It claims no circuit optimality, no measured speedup and no composition with any other D, phase-A, phase-B or cleanup change. No repository-wide suite, eleven-stage physical replay, remote CI or Lean pass was run.

Sprint: bit-supplier track, OS seed 18. The claim and its result update are recorded locally. Submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6-Astra) wrote the analysis, proof and checker, and Claude Code packaged the submission. No independent human peer review is claimed.

title: Independent exact certificate of PR741 owner-profile optimality
body:
This proves that PR741's idle profile `{48:2396,44:1,3:1,1:1}` is optimal for its fixed native supplier, 72 complete calls and capacity inventory. Every different idle profile fails the exact moment at the admitted PR741 endpoint; maps with the same profile tie. **No new κ is claimed.**

Five integer helper-width prices and four capacity bonuses exclude both the all-rank-48 profile and `{48:2396,44:1,4:1}`, with an integer contradiction of 25. Concavity and a positive eleven-step period reduce every remaining profile to 13 strict rational moment checks.

The independent checker uses count-vector enumeration, a separate base-two interval engine, and an integer dynamic program over all 115,057 possible non-48 masses. It directly covers every feasible number of rank-48 residuals without relying on the 13-case reduction. Eight mutations cover native widths and billing, ownership, chronology, dual prices and endpoint hypotheses.

```bash
python3 -B research/sw4-owner-optimality/verify.py --out /tmp/owner-proof
python3 -B research/sw4-owner-optimality/independent_check.py --out /tmp/owner-proof/INDEPENDENT.json
python3 -B research/sw4-owner-optimality/controls.py --out /tmp/owner-proof/CONTROLS.json
```

The package uses Python 3.11+ and the standard library. Fresh macOS 3.11/3.14 and Linux 3.14 runs pass in normal and optimized modes, with byte-identical mathematical artifacts. Sources and validation are pinned in the package and companion validation directory. The complete native scalar/phase/controller admission remains in PR741 and is not rerun here.

PR699 previously reported packing optimality for this shared width inventory. This supplies a solver-free proof for that packing shape, evaluated at PR741's stronger endpoint. Credits retain PR741/PR685/PR660's owner map and integer flow lineage; PR699's SW4 construction; PR676's p6n ends; PR664's promotions; the underlying gauge/no-triangle/native-audit lineages; and both unchanged interval checkers. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

The result does not constrain changed local programs or widths, provider mixtures, dispatch counts, capacity inventories, split helper invocations or different hosting contracts. All inherited all-size, physical-realization and analytic-transfer obligations remain. No unconditional multiplication theorem or κ = 1 is claimed.

title: Research audit: exact prime-power kernel root valuations (no new kappa)
body:
This **mathematical audit / research note** corroborates the nonunit-root lemma in Ali Romman's incorporated #621 and determines the complete p-adic root-valuation multiset of its prime-power kernel. No defect was found in that lemma, and no new κ is claimed.

For `r=p^a` and `v(1-u)=1`, the written proof gives root valuation `1+(k-1)(p-1)/p` with multiplicity `(p-1)p^(k-1)`, for every `k=1,...,a`. It supplies all Newton-polygon vertices and collinear coefficient contacts, handles radix two and every primitive root choice, and distinguishes this normalization from `v_p(p)=1`. These are nonarchimedean valuations, not complex root moduli or a sharper complex conditioning bound.

Only `research/prime-power-newton-audit/` is added. One implementation counts factor valuations; a separate implementation reconstructs the exact cyclotomic coefficients, changes to the uniformizer basis, and extracts their valuations without using the counting formula.

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/prime-power-newton-audit/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/prime-power-newton-audit/test_verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_NEWTON_NONUNIT_AUDIT: 28 radices; 697 primitive embeddings; 30224 coefficient obligations; 9 negative controls`, then eight tests pass. Python 3.9+; standard library only.

Validation passed on macOS arm64 / Python 3.9.6: normal and isolated optimized replay; dense-polynomial reference tests; exact Eisenstein checks; malformed-input, source-drift and receipt-corruption rejection; a complete minimal relocated replay; unchanged #621 replay matching its published receipt; selected-record integrity; and staged whitespace. A separate Codex reviewer found no correctness issue. Finite replay supports the written proof; neither is a formal proof of integer multiplication. Full repository/cold supplier suites, optional SymPy, Linux and remote CI were not run or claimed.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Audited #621 head: `520774462b19b29af41554b74def31f9d01e997e`. Source hashes, proof references, deterministic receipt, completed local claim and validation scope are included. OS assignment seed **68**, adversarial-audit track. No pinned sprint issue existed. The final overlap check through #757 distinguishes #668's CRT resultants, #666's composite lifting, #628/#692's inverse execution, and #736's replay optimization.

Credit Ali Romman, OpenAI's pinned exact-DFT kernel, the classical q-Pochhammer/Newton lineage, and the standard cyclotomic/Newton-polygon references. Prepared for **Hao Yan (@FanPUYen)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, under Apache-2.0. No literature-priority claim. The selected #626/#543 frontier and `upstream/` are unchanged; paid preparation, restoration, compiler/hosting, precision/tape and analytic multiplication obligations remain.

title: Tooling: filter default reclamation candidates before sorting
body:
Filter retired slots by exact frame containment before sorting them in the joint compiler. On the same historical [PR #55](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/55) inputs, three fresh alternating-order benchmark pairs give median complete-compilation speedups of **2.36× at h=23** and **2.69× at h=25**. All **12 runs** reproduce the accepted decompressed physical words and complete compiler receipts exactly.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b879e8472547bd820ce81b1b9c0463176fe5151c/research/reclaim-order-performance/README.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b879e8472547bd820ce81b1b9c0463176fe5151c/research/reclaim-order-performance/BENCHMARK.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b879e8472547bd820ce81b1b9c0463176fe5151c/research/reclaim-order-performance/SOURCES.json).

**Status: verification tooling improvement. No new κ or physical word.**

The production change is two lines. The eligible slot order remains descending current frame rank, then slot ID. Filtering commutes with sorting here: the predicate and key only read frames, and frame mutation begins only after the chosen dependence is found, followed immediately by return. The package gives this equivalence argument, retains the exact original compiler for comparison, and supplies a source-pinned benchmark with no timing threshold.

| Input | Reference median | Filtered median |
|---|---:|---:|
| h=23 | 72.876 s | 30.901 s |
| h=25 | 135.037 s | 50.220 s |

These measurements include complete scalar compilation, both input/dirty orientations, source admission and serialization on Python 3.14.7 / macOS arm64. They exclude setup copies, the independent CRT profiler and the full suite. OS caches were not flushed; the development machine was not an isolated benchmark host. They are not integer-multiplication runtime measurements or latest-frontier replay timings. The filter can evaluate more containment predicates when the old loop would stop early, so there is no universal speedup claim.

```sh
python3 -B research/reclaim-order-performance/benchmark.py --pairs 3 --out /tmp/reclaim-order-benchmark.json
```

Use a new output path. Expected: `PASS_IDENTICAL_RECLAIM_WORDS_AND_RECEIPTS`.

All **18 required verification groups passed** across the initial run and resumption. The initial `make verify` passed the first 14 groups, then a historical positive-skip build could not find Boost. A retry refused the output directory left by that failed attempt. After preserving that directory and supplying GCC's standard `CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH`, `make verify-positive verify-joint verify-pair verify-tests` exited 0. No source change or omitted check was needed. The complete selected cold replay, original C++ CRT profiles, 47 strict inequalities, seven margins, all 16 joint controls, isolated tests and patch checks are covered. **No uninterrupted `make verify` pass is claimed.** Exact attempt log hashes and environment details are in [VALIDATION.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b879e8472547bd820ce81b1b9c0463176fe5151c/research/reclaim-order-performance/VALIDATION.json).

The four benchmark admission controls pass. After timing, the receipt comparison was tightened to preserve JSON types; all 12 timed receipt hashes match retained bytes that pass the typed comparison. The timed commands and compiler inputs did not change. No remote-CI or proof-assistant claim is made for this branch.

Only the compiler source hash and derived historical certificate bindings change. All numerical certificate fields, word payloads, profiles and existing mutation tests remain unchanged. There is no new cache, compiler mode, dependency or test-only interface. [upstream/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/b879e8472547bd820ce81b1b9c0463176fe5151c/upstream) and the historical selected [PR #626](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/626) / [PR #543](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/543) frontier at the original base are unchanged; all inherited compiler, common-label, physical, hosting, precision, tape and analytic assumptions remain.

Base: [66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60). OS-random seed **85**, verification-engineering track. No pinned sprint coordination issue existed, so the three candidates and narrow claim are recorded locally and in [CLAIM.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b879e8472547bd820ce81b1b9c0463176fe5151c/research/reclaim-order-performance/CLAIM.json).

Credit @gupt1156's [PR #55](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/55) producer, @eumemic's [PR #57](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/57) compiler and Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky)'s ranked reclamation. [PR154](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/154), at `f571bcbd6e06618aeae0b8279da48060032dc74b`, identified this sorting bottleneck and explicitly left it unchanged. This change follows that lead and supplies exact-output and performance evidence. The measured [PR #55](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/55) source is pinned at [03e991aa79f9df1a935726213bb6a8631cd0d823](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/03e991aa79f9df1a935726213bb6a8631cd0d823); full source and dependency hashes are retained in [SOURCES.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b879e8472547bd820ce81b1b9c0463176fe5151c/research/reclaim-order-performance/SOURCES.json). Other frame/arithmetic/profiler acceleration work is credited in the package.

The final overlap review covered **614 open PRs through [PR #795](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/795)**. Concurrent [PR779](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/779), Peter Carpenter (@PeterCarp320), at `daa9b0e773b53f36d5b4c3f1c7524600e5714deb`, maintains exact eligibility indexes in a separate adapter and reports larger speedups. It follows Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky)'s [PR175](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/175) (`f1081fabbfadaaaaf7292a40d428dbbb865ce920`), which maintains sorted rank buckets and is incorporated in a historical source archive. The default compiler at this base still uses the full sort. **This PR is a two-line option for that default path, with no maintained index, update hook or adapter, plus exact-output and integration evidence.** It claims neither priority nor best performance. [PR #175](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/175), [PR #779](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/779) were not benchmarked on this machine; their code is not imported or changed.

Prepared by **Ali Romman (@aliromman) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**. Apache-2.0. Finite certificate checks are not a formal proof of the full multiplication theorem.

The [2026-10-14 follow-up review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/366a24008d621170f680d8971bc4f0fae90db494/research/reclaim-order-performance/FOLLOWUP-REVIEW.md) addresses the maintainer's compiler/regression request. Fresh sequential compilations at both `h=23` and `h=25` reproduce the complete accepted words and type-preserving receipts. The [receipt](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/366a24008d621170f680d8971bc4f0fae90db494/research/reclaim-order-performance/FOLLOWUP-REVIEW.json) records the four changed source-binding fields and confirms that the original compiler is unchanged on refreshed main `418e40eb2572d930b58c1cf9b82b41c0fc7ee08d`. The implementation, source pins and mathematical certificate fields needed no correction. The original timing runs, mutation suite and full-suite evidence were retained; no new timing comparison or full-suite run is claimed.

title: Research note: Eisenstein E8 copy cost ≥22 and sharp clique-method limit
body:
PR620's archived extension-ring screen leaves the asymmetric copy cost of the 40 Eisenstein E8 lines unresolved. This **research note** proves cost at least **22 Eisenstein pairing-rank units (44 rational units)** for any finite number of scalar binary totals. A matching dual certificate also proves that **22 is the exact limit of every nonnegative weighted-clique certificate**, including nonuniform weights on smaller cliques.

The actual decoder optimum remains in **[22,40]**. No cost-22 decoder, paid supplier or new κ is claimed. Under the inherited Dfc accounting, positive three-stage deficit would require integer copy cost 22–26; existence and all remaining implementation costs stay open.

title: Research: weighted path valuations exclude a remaining eight-call Clifford word (no kappa)
body:
PR705 leaves nine fixed eight-call Clifford register words unclassified when equal group products have different accumulated Fourier ranks. This extends its determinant argument by choosing arbitrary Laurent path weights and requiring homogeneity only for coefficients forbidden by the endpoint. The resulting exact certificate excludes **`evolved-27` for every invertible choice of its four 3-by-3 scalar blocks**, even without a shared final frame per input column.

The certificate has interior weights `(1,0,1), (-1,-1,0), (0,0,0)`, row potentials `(-1,0,0)` and column potentials `(0,1,1)`. Its scalar weighted determinant has degree zero, while every permitted determinant term has valuation at least one. `PROOF.md` gives the general argument over a formal group algebra, including why cancellation of forbidden coefficients is preserved.

Across all nine unresolved words, one global and 918 frame-specific certificates exclude 1,093 of 1,152 endpoint frame triples; **59 remain unclassified**. Of the exclusions, 865 already follow from the elementary allowed-entry matching test. The weighted criterion adds **228 exclusions beyond that baseline**. No exhaustive comparison against predecessor support/polynomial methods is claimed.

**No new κ or positive eight-call primitive.** This is a fixed-word obstruction and reusable search filter in the inherited formal projective Clifford model. It does not close the general m=3, W=3, s=8 problem, infer formal linear independence from concrete 8-by-8 matrices, or extend to arbitrary circuit representations. The eight other whole words remain unclassified here.

title: Research: certified format ceilings for Eisenstein/Gaussian/Hurwitz E8 copy floors (no κ claim)
body:
**Research note and tooling. No κ claim and no word.** Contributed by Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani), with substantial AI assistance.

Builds on the extension-ring E8 floors already proved: #620 (screen), #703 (Hurwitz cost exactly 10), #738/#770/#767 (Gaussian floor 40), #798 (Eisenstein cost ≥22, open in [22,40]) and #765. It does not re-prove them. It turns them into **certified B_K format ceilings** using the unchanged `research/format-limits-corrected` engine.

## Findings
- **The outer assembly is saturated.** The selected κ equals a/(1+a) for the binding complex supplier to a relative 1.4e-16. So ring, transform length, resampling and Fürer/SS/HvdH-type outer changes can gain at most a factor 1+a ≈ 1.0016.
- **Eisenstein bit side.** A decoder of cost ≤24 would give a ceiling above 1/99 (cost 24: X ≤ 1.150e-2; cost 25: X ≤ 1.0053e-2). Cost ≤28 still beats the realised E8 bit unit (6.000e-3). Coordinate-total decoders cost at least 28 (new exact clique bound), so only non-coordinate decoders inside #798's open interval could matter.
- **Gaussian floor 40** gives X ≤ 7.688e-3. **Hurwitz** gives no positive saving for s ≤ 13.
- **Complex side (argued).** An Eisenstein complex unit has an F₄ window of at least ω = 7, which gives X ≤ 8.07e-3 even at cost 22. The current complex unit caps at 5.19e-3. So the label-field route cannot give κ > 0.01 in the B_K format, though it could still give a several-fold ceiling rise if a cost ≤24 bit decoder exists.

## Reproduce
`python3 -B research/label-field-census/census.py --json out.json` runs in about 4 minutes with numpy only and reproduces `RESULT.json`. Not covered: s ≥ 15, non-coordinate decoders in the clique table, realisability of Q(ω) frames, and helper/hosting/analytic obligations.

title: Research: degree-controlled cyclic inverse bound by root reflection (no new kappa)
body:
PR621 proves a uniform circle gap for the prime-power cyclic kernels, but its Fourier-to-operator step pays an additional inverse-gap power. This contribution applies classical root reflection, the Dolzhenko-Spijker arc-length inequality, and Hardy coefficient control to obtain a degree-only multiplier.

For a degree-`n` polynomial `P` with `|P(z)| >= delta > 0` on the unit circle, the note proves

```text
||1/P||_W <= (1+4n)^2 / delta
||P(tau Z_L^w)^-1||_infinity <= (1+4n)^2 / delta.
```

The bound permits interior, exterior, repeated, and zero roots and is uniform in cyclic length, integer stride, and unit phase. A degree-one family shows that the inverse-gap exponent one is necessary; the quadratic degree factor is not claimed optimal. The proof includes elementary derivations with explicit constants and distinguishes the analytic argument from finite tests.

For PR621's notation, the constant changes from `A(1+4X^2)` to `A(1+4n)^2`, where `A=delta^-1` and `X=n H^(nD/2)`. The dominant logarithmic term is halved asymptotically. At radix 71, the exact ceiling of `log2` of the sufficient norm bound changes from 695,757 to 347,859. These are norm overestimates, not working-precision or runtime measurements. The previous unpublished local weighted-Fourier audit gave 521,801; its proof and notice are retained for comparison.

### Source and analytic review follow-up

Revision `a0f15ce84f0951f69b39795f229cb854307ca52b` addresses the continuation at the reviewed head `d213ac12d4a1ab8f717d942e844df318ceb395fb`. The [source and analytic audit](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a0f15ce84f0951f69b39795f229cb854307ca52b/research/rational-circle-bound/audit/README.md) maps the proof obligations to the expanded argument and exact classical-source locators. It checks normalization, Hardy-factorization limits, the degree-2d level polynomial, both Fourier directions, and absolute convergence of the operator inverse.

The theorem and hypotheses are unchanged. PR692's attribution is corrected to **Ryan Pinto (@Ambassators)**. The six immutable source/context inputs, executable scripts, finite receipt, and historical evidence are preserved. The existing exact verifier and all eight package controls pass on the revised package; these are regression checks, not proof of the analytic theorem. This is author/AI review; independent analytic acceptance, the inherited PR621 foundation and full multiplication obligations remain separately scoped.

### Reproduce

Python 3.10+ and the standard library:

```sh
python -B research/rational-circle-bound/verify.py
python -B research/rational-circle-bound/test_package.py
```

Expected markers: `PASS_RATIONAL_CIRCLE_BOUND` and `PASS_PACKAGE_CONTROLS`.

Executed on Windows 11 / Python 3.12.2, including a relocated offline copy under isolated optimized Python:

- 126 exact reflection families and 756 boundary identities.
- 546 dense-versus-finite-geometric cyclic inverse comparisons, covering 9,516 inverse entries and including zero/noncoprime strides.
- 6,565 finite Hilbert-matrix inequalities and 128 exact near-circle parameter instances.
- 14 exact prime-power budget comparisons, 21 mathematical/admission controls, and eight package fault tests.

The finite cyclic tests use supplied rational root families, not newly computed cyclotomic kernel inverses. No proof assistant, independent human review, full repository replay, second-platform replay, or remote CI result is claimed. The unchanged PR621 foundation replay was not repeated.

### Scope and attribution

Only `research/rational-circle-bound/` is added. Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. The source package was prepared in a partial pinned-input worktree; the published commit uses the complete upstream tree and that upstream commit as its parent. Credit Ali Romman for PR621's kernel setting, nonvanishing theorem and circle certificate; Dolzhenko, Spijker, Hardy and the classical Blaschke theory for the analytic tools; and Baranov-Zarouf for the inspected normalized arc-length statement and historical attribution. Source notices and six immutable source/context files are preserved. The standard finite-geometric oracle also appears in Ryan Pinto's PR692; it is not claimed as a new solver here. PR628 and PR764 address distinct rounded-scan questions.

This is an application relative to the inspected repository work, not a literature-priority claim. title: Tooling: pack cyclic routing states with identical exhaustive receipts
body:
The historical cyclic routing checker stores more than half a million nested scalar/routing states. This replaces those state keys with an injective, order-preserving integer encoding, reducing verification time and Python allocation peaks while retaining every original exhaustive-search receipt. **Tooling improvement; no new κ or negative result.**

## Contributor

**4RchYMing** ([GitHub](https://github.com/4RchYMing), authenticated account ID 275918740). Git author: `4RchYMing <275918740+4RchYMing@users.noreply.github.com>`, explicitly specified by the contributor. The predecessor's authorship and notices remain intact.

## AI Assistance

Prepared with **substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** for implementation, mathematical reasoning, independent test implementation, experiments, documentation, and delivery. No independent human peer review is claimed.

## Base Commit

`66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60` is the original implementation and benchmark baseline. Upstream subsequently advanced to `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`; all 19 relevant original checker/certificate, pinned dependency, test-runner and CI input files there are byte-identical. The compatibility receipt is retained in `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json`. OS-cryptographic assignment seed **87**, verification-engineering track. Three candidates, measurements, the local claim, and overlap review are recorded in `research/cyclic-routing-performance/SELECTION.json`. There is no pinned coordination issue.

## Research Scope

Only `audit_cyclic_topology.routing_state_search`: two-port XOR words on 2, 3, or 4 arbitrary-input roles, with the existing depth cap of seven. Preserve scalar/routing joint-state distinctions, full-routing saturation pruning, stopping rules, terminal tests, every frontier digest, and all eight cyclic seed controls. Selected-frontier records, `upstream/`, and the contributor list are unchanged. The #741 frontier selected by newer upstream commits is outside this contribution.

## Method

Place each scalar row in a separate fixed-width integer lane and the complete routing bit set in the low bits. The encoding is injective and preserves the original tuple ordering. XOR updates affect only the target lane; the routing extension remains unchanged. Decode sorted keys to preserve the exact original hash input. The README proves these invariants and explains why the permutation lookup agrees with the old predicate on reachable invertible matrices.

Only the historical certificate's changed checker-source binding is regenerated. Benchmark processes load the original implementation from its pinned Git object and compare the **entire** certificate after restoring that one binding. Source dependencies and the original certificate are hash-pinned.

## Results

- **529,066 four-role states**, all frontier digests, terminal counts, saturation counts, and complete historical certificate fields are preserved.
- Final seven alternating fresh-process pairs on Windows 10 / CPython 3.12.14: complete-process median **3.788324 s → 2.680431 s**, **1.413× faster / 29.24% less elapsed time**. The earlier seven-pair run is retained too: **1.368×**. All 80 receipts across five benchmark series, including the separate memory runs, agree.
- Separately traced Python allocation peak: **131,099,209 → 80,510,849 bytes**, **38.59% lower**. This is not RSS; tracing is disabled in timing runs.
- **Full independent coverage:** the dense-F2/literal-permutation-set oracle checks every cap 0–7 for all three widths, including all 529,066 four-role states. Every receipt field agrees. A scalar-only merge control loses coverage despite retaining the same negative Boolean and is detected.
- **14 tests pass on each of CPython 3.11.16, 3.13.15 and 3.14.7**, plus all 14 under 3.14.7 `-O` (56 successful test executions). `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json` retains command output and source hashes.
- Minimal offline replays in a path with spaces pass. Modified dependencies, reused output paths, and invalid parameters are rejected. Selected-record/source-inventory and staged whitespace checks pass. `VALIDATION.txt` retains command output.

Additional same-host, same-input pairs on the CI interpreter versions show that the speedup varies by interpreter:

| CPython | Original process median | Packed process median | Speedup | Python allocation peak reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3.11.16 | 3.436026 s | 2.553110 s | 1.346x | 38.59% |
| 3.13.15 | 3.628811 s | 2.902232 s | 1.250x | 38.61% |
| 3.14.7 | 3.842965 s | 3.198651 s | 1.201x | 42.42% |

Each row uses seven alternating fresh-process pairs and separate memory runs. All samples, including the more variable 3.14 timings, are retained. These are within-version comparisons; **1.413x is not a universal guarantee**.

## Reproduction

Python 3.11+ standard library and Git; use a full clone containing the base commit and a fresh output path:

```sh
python3 -B research/cyclic-routing-performance/benchmark.py --pairs 7 --out routing-benchmark.json
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_cyclic_routing_packed.py -v
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_finite_bit_contract.py -v
```

Expected: `PASS_IDENTICAL_COMPLETE_ROUTING_RECEIPTS`; five and nine tests pass. `SOURCE.json`, `RESULT.json`, `INITIAL-RESULT.json`, `RESULT-python311.json`, `RESULT-python313.json`, `RESULT-python314.json`, `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json`, and `EXPLORATION.json` retain pins, exact dependency versions, all measurements, and exploratory evidence. Repeat the commands under each Python interpreter with fresh benchmark output paths; add `-O` before `-m` to reproduce the optimized-mode tests. The README gives the argument and review map.

## Limitations

This measures one historical verifier, not selected-supplier replay or multiplication runtime. OS caches were not flushed; absolute timings vary. There is one separately traced memory run per mode in each benchmark series. The four-role frontier remains unclosed; no claim extends beyond depth seven. The independent implementation shares the documented joint-state reduction and saturation rule; it does not independently prove those reductions. This is not a Lean formalization or a new multiplication theorem, and all inherited transfer/physical/compiler/precision/tape/analytic assumptions remain.

Full `make verify`, the selected cold replay, Lean, and remote Linux CI were not run locally. This Windows environment lacks `make` and a C++ compiler. The local version matrix ran on Windows. Upstream Actions returned `action_required`, requiring maintainer approval; Linux CI and maintainer review are separate from this local evidence.

## Prior Work

Douglas R. Colkitt's original checker, certificate, and `docs/research/cyclic-topology-audit.md` provide the routing obstruction and finite-state reduction (historical source commit `d55bcd62ceb8f322bcf311a5a66e94c3ac7724f0`). Original notices and Apache-2.0 licensing remain.

eumemic's pending [#154](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/154) profiles other verifier hotspots; Victor Li's pending [#756](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/756) optimizes the distinct balanced-Fano search. Neither supplies code here. The original overlap refresh covered 614 open PRs through #795 and fresh arrivals through #799. The follow-up checked the 100 latest open PRs through #820; only this PR matched the cyclic-routing optimization scope. Earlier original-hash inventories and frozen supplier copies are preserved as historical provenance.

title: Research circuit: lower historical dyadic center bill with one basis shear (no new kappa)
body:
A single unimodular center-basis shear lowers the **historical h=26 dyadic central factor's** gather/scatter bill from **45,381 to 43,909** counted scalar operations. The complete signed invocation saves **2,944** operations after charging its increased scatter cost, both gathers, both scatters and all unchanged side work. title: Research construction: shorten R420 phase-B block 8 from 47 to 30 XORs (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This finite bit-circuit construction replaces **phase-B block 8 of the selected PR543 R420 word** (frame 550, `B[512:559)`, ordered registers `[2,4,16,18,20,22,96,98,101,103,112,118]`) with a schedule of **30 gates instead of 47**. The literal reverse cleanup `C` is regenerated from the changed `A`/`B`, so it saves 17 more gates. The complete local record stream falls **26,916 → 26,882 scalar additions** (34 fewer). **No new κ is claimed.**

- The ordered positive integer forward matrix of the block is identical in all 144 entries, so every arbitrary block input gives the same exit values.
- The positive reverse matrix is entrywise no larger: 32 entries are strictly smaller, the entry sum falls 321 → 103 and the largest row sum falls 134 → 26.
- All 660 register frame paths, the paid histogram `{1:1320, 2:1440, 4:60, 5:120, 8:9}`, rank mass 5,112, and the nine copies and nine erasures are unchanged.
- The original R420 checker `xcheck.py` reports all hypotheses H1-H5 and all four interface conclusions true on the changed word.
- Python positive-prefix replay: forward 144,651 (unchanged), reverse 2,270,064 → 2,212,684. The five-stage local payload stays at 100 bits, below the existing `2^104` cap.

Only `research/r420-block8-schedule/` is added: the circuit (`CANDIDATE.json`), its search (`search.py`), an exact verifier (`verify.py`) with `CERTIFICATE.json`, source pins (`SOURCES.json`), a native replay harness (`native.py`) and the local claim (`CLAIM.json`). `upstream/`, the selected sources, the selected record and the frontier are unchanged.

**Search record.** Seeded two-sided nonnegative elementary-factor reduction on the fixed 12×12 forward matrix. The OS-random assignment seed 18 (bit-supplier track) selects block 18 mod 10 = 8. The search seed 801018 was fixed before the first trial. 10,000 trials, each stopped at the current best length: 144 reached the identity, 10 of these also had a dominated reverse matrix, and improvements came at trial 21 (33 gates) and trial 318 (30 gates). A separate seed-18 run was interrupted, found no improvement and was not used. No minimality or exhaustive-coverage claim is made.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/r420-block8-schedule/verify.py
```

Expected output (Python standard library only, about 2 s; checked with Python 3.14.6 on macOS arm64):

```text
PASS_R420_BLOCK8_SCHEDULE gates=47->30 ADDs=26916->26882 columns=660 controls=10 rank_mass=5112 kappa=not_recomputed
```

The verifier does not import the search. It requires and checks the SHA-256 pins of the source word and `xcheck.py` (and the other files in `SOURCES.json`); binds the recipe to its block index, frame, slice and ordered registers; checks forward matrix equality and reverse domination; rebuilds the record stream independently of the predecessor exporter; replays all 660 columns forward and in reverse over F2 with copy-lifecycle checks; replays both positive prefixes; requires equal frame paths, an equal paid profile, the exact 2 × 17 saving, frame ranks equal to the original checker's, and true interface flags on both words; and compares the full report with `CERTIFICATE.json`.

Ten negative controls are checked: equal forward maps without reverse domination (three-wire calibration), a dropped gate, a self-addition, a boolean wire index, a wrong frame, a swapped register binding, an unpriced cancelled pair, a missing cleanup gate, a stale cleanup that passes the F2 endpoint but fails H4, and an illegal frame descent. A separate temporary test confirmed that an empty pin map, a map without `xcheck.py` and a wrong source hash are rejected.

**Not run:** native C++ replay of the candidate word. `native.py` is included for that replay, but only a calibration run (the original word as both inputs, on a pre-final revision of the harness) has been done. No repository-wide suite, selected cold replay, hosted or outer assembly, or CI result is claimed. Inherited obligations remain open: signed decoder evidence beyond F2 column replay, mutable-basis common-label realization and exact-bank completion, and hosted replay, routing, pricing and outer assembly. Finite replay is not a proof of the full multiplication theorem.

## Pins, overlap and attribution

- Base commit **66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60**. PR543 source `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535` (git confirms the source word blob matches it); selected consumer PR626 `660de893d27bb7abd1d5b01b1640207528a5c851`.

Composition with these or any other pending PR is not checked.

title: Research audit: literal binary spectra and moment-preserving corruption control (no new kappa)
body:
The historical single-intersection screen checks two integer spectral moments, but those checks can miss a wrong modular characteristic polynomial. This research audit adds an independent exact calculation from literal subset-intersection matrices. **No new kappa is claimed.**

All 41 cases with `4 <= h <= 10`, `2 <= k <= min(4, floor(h/2))`, and `0 <= j < k` match the claimed binary polynomial and rank lower bound. The largest matrix has order 210. The bound is strict in 21 cases, so the evidence preserves the distinction between a lower bound and a binary diagonalization.

The useful negative control is a two-edge switch at `(h,k,j)=(7,3,0)`: it preserves every row degree, integer trace 35 and squared trace 175, but changes the characteristic polynomial. The independent audit rejects it. A complementary-subset nilpotent example and a wrong odd-multiplicity control document the other failure boundaries.

Reproduce from the repository root with standard-library Python:

python3 -B research/single-intersection-spectrum-audit/spectrum_audit.py

title: Research: Eisenstein nonlinear message copy floor 22b under explicit width pricing
body:

Unequal demands satisfy `C >= max(ceil(11*sum(b_t)/20), max_clique sum(b_t))`.

title: Research: exact frame search certifies #741 and #626 providers frame-optimal (rediscovers #741; negative result)
body:
**Update: current selected word (#741).** Rebased on main after #741 merged. I gave CP-SAT PR699's SW4 word (`d232183f…`), using the admissible model with the audit's hpe cone caps and fixed tail frames. In 27 s it returned `OPTIMAL` with exactly #741's profile `{1:2556,2:334,3:430,4:194,5:56,8:8}`, so the solver rediscovers #741's gain without guidance. `check_sw4.py` applies #741's recipe and reproduces its pinned output hash `e7804702…`. The LP optimum over all frame assignments then equals #741's weight: 18155.950422 linear and 18219.665540 exact-root at #741's complex root, with gaps under 1e-9. So **no frame-only change of the selected word can raise κ**; PR699's frame slack (6.90 units) is exactly what #741 recovered. Six commuting-reorder restarts on #741, each re-solved by the LP, gave no gain. The receipt is `RESULT-SW4.json`. This work does not touch the R420/R439 bit or E8 lines (#789/#790/#792, #765/#767/#770).

**Negative result, scoped. No κ change.** By Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani), with substantial AI assistance (an AI coding agent wrote the search code and ran the experiments).

The complex side binds the selected κ. In the 64 jp8 calls, unit climbs make up 160,768 of the 181,659 rank-1 children. Paid children are exactly the frame climbs that `hpe_audit_and_transport.py::climb` counts, and the scalar program never reads frames. So I treated every A/B/tail gate frame of the selected provider words as a variable and searched all of them exactly.

**Result.** For #626's `jp8` and `ck` words (content hashes pinned in `complex-k492-owner-repair/data/SPEC.json`, rebuilt fresh by the package's `verify.py`), the paid profile is optimal over every frame assignment of the fixed gate sequence:

| word | gates | input weight | LP optimum (HiGHS) | CP-SAT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| jp8 | 4471 | 18475.029780700 | 18475.029780701 | OPTIMAL, same value |
| ck | 4507 | 18568.580702034 | 18568.580702035 | OPTIMAL, same value |

The weight is the linearised moment, Σ d·ln(48/d). Each word's rank mass is fixed by its widths, so at the selected root a* the exact criterion is Σ d·(73/d)^a*. That weight is also LP-optimal at the input (gap below 1e-9). The model relaxes the audit: it omits the hpe cone caps and cold_end conditions and leaves tail frames free. So no frame regroup, coalescence or promotion recipe of any size can raise κ on these words. Lifting every frame to its greatest feasible value costs +3.8%. Annealing over commuting reorders (the `build_gate_moves.py` rule), followed by an exact frame re-solve, gave no gain in 11 restarts (`ORDER-SEARCH.json`). That is a sample, not a proof for all orders.

**Context for κ > 0.01.** Jensen's inequality gives a ≤ −ln p / E_mass[ln(73/r)]. At the current deficit (2560 / 523264), a ≥ 0.01 needs a mass-weighted geometric-mean child rank of at least 44.7; today it is 3.66. At today's child ranks it would instead need a deficit of at least 15,425 (6.0×). Reaching it needs new scalar structure, not frame bookkeeping. About 1,700 of jp8's 2,512 rank-1 climbs are helper unit climbs.

**Files.** `research/frame-lift-search/` contains the model, the LP/CP-SAT solvers, the order search, `RESULT.json` and `ORDER-SEARCH.json`. `tests/test_frame_lift_search.py` checks the lattice model on the in-repo #571 prefix word. There is also a one-line experiment-log link.

**Verification.** `check.py` ran on a fresh `complex-k492-owner-repair/verify.py` rebuild (Linux, Python 3.13) and reports `PASS_FRAME_ONLY_LP_OPTIMAL_FOR_SELECTED_PROVIDERS`. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_frame_lift_search` passes. I did not run `make verify`: no generator, certificate or selected-record file changed.

**Limits.** HiGHS is a floating-point LP, not an exact rational dual certificate, and CP-SAT's `OPTIMAL` comes without a proof log. The scalar program, helper count, dispatch, hosting and bit supplier are out of scope.

title: Tooling: 1.13x faster exact stage-pair audit with identical receipts
body:
The historical stage-pair audit spends most of its runtime in exact rational arithmetic. This replaces two wasteful patterns with identical operations, preserving every receipt and rejection check. **Tooling improvement; no new kappa.**

## Changes

1. `scripts/audit_fused_block.py` — `rational_rank` skips redundant `Q(x)` construction when an entry is already a `Fraction`. `Q(Q)` returns the same value after needless normalization.
2. `scripts/audit_stage_pair.py` — `modular_rank` converts denominators through a cached `_mod_inv(d, prime)` helper (same `pow(d, -1, prime)` call) instead of one fresh `pow()` per matrix entry. `lru_cache` does not cache exceptions, so a non-invertible denominator raises the same `ValueError`.

No matrix, pivot order, stopping rule, candidate list, or rejection predicate was touched.

## Measurements

Fresh-process timings of `certificate()` (compute only), CPython 3.12.14 / Windows, stdlib only. OS caches not flushed; host not isolated. Timing is descriptive, not a pass threshold.

| run | original (s) | optimized (s) |
|-----|---:|---:|
| 1 | 16.63 | 14.31 |
| 2 | 15.79 | 13.96 |
| 3 | 15.57 | 13.64 |
| median | 15.79 | 13.96 |

Median 15.79 s to 13.96 s: 1.13x faster, 11.6% less wall time. Microbenchmarks: `rational_rank` 3.05x on 50 sampled frames; modular conversion 1.42x on 20 sampled matrices.

```sh
python3 -B research/stage-pair-performance/benchmark.py --rounds 3
```

Expected: `PASS_IDENTICAL_STAGE_PAIR_RECEIPTS`.

## Validation

- Full `certificate()` output identical to `certificates/stage-pair-audit.json` in every field except the single expected `source_sha256` entry for the edited `audit_stage_pair.py` (rank sum 8684, 64 candidates, 6 local improvements).
- `audit_fused_block` and `audit_joint_frames` certificates regenerate byte-identical.
- New `tests/test_stage_pair_performance.py`: 6 tests compare optimized helpers against verbatim base-commit references on edge cases (empty, zero, singular, non-square, ints vs Fractions, 30-digit numerators, primes 101/103), including the `ValueError` path. Existing suites pass: `test_stage_pair` (8), `test_fused_block` (7), `test_joint_frames` (8), `test_quadratic_affine` (4).
- Full `make verify` and the selected-supplier cold replay were not rerun for this isolated historical-checker change. `upstream/` untouched; selected frontier unchanged.

## Change and mathematical scope

PR621's uniform circle gap and derivative bound imply the valid cyclic inverse estimate `delta^-1 + 2 M delta^-2`. This independently prepared audit gives an elementary periodic Sobolev/Fourier proof of

```text
||P(tau Z_L^w)^-1||_infinity^2 <= delta^-2 + (44/7) M delta^-3.
```

The finite Fourier-polynomial argument establishes absolute summability before matrix transfer. It covers every cyclic length, integer stride (including zero and noncoprime strides), unit scalar and constant polynomial. The bound improves the inherited expression when `M/delta > 4/7`, including the prime-power kernels covered by PR621. For fixed positive M, its inverse-gap dependence is `delta^-3/2`.

**Concurrent work:** Rafael Guevara (@alephnan)'s #803, inspected at `d213ac12d4a1ab8f717d942e844df318ceb395fb`, proposes the stronger degree-controlled bound `(1+4 degree(P))^2 / delta` for the same conditioning step, using root reflection, arc-length and Hardy arguments. This submission preserves a separate Sobolev proof and exact regression evidence; it does **not** claim priority or the best currently proposed conditioning bound. No PR803 code is imported and its pending result is not independently certified here. #820 separately audits radix-9 coefficient enclosures and factor residuals. The publication overlap refresh covered the recent queue through #824.

Relative to PR621's original estimate, the radix-9 ceiling of log2 of the analytic upper bound falls from 870 to 651. These are bound ceilings, not actual required precision or runtime speedups. title: Research: signed rank transport excludes unitary register mixers (no new kappa)
body:
A forward/inverse coefficient potential gives a general search constraint: **unitary scalar register mixing cannot save paid rank**, regardless of word length, mixing locations or noncommuting frames. The same obstruction holds for scalar multiples of unitaries and for mixers jointly made unitary by the supplied positive diagonal metrics. In particular, the three-stream rank-three endpoint needs nine calls throughout this subclass.

For arbitrary nonunitary mixers, the argument becomes a quantitative necessary condition. Define

`p_ij(g) = Re(S_ij[g] (S^-1)_ji[g^-1])` and `Phi(S) = sum rank(g) p_ij(g)`.

Scalar mixing preserves Phi exactly. A paid call of cost c on row i changes it by at most `c(1+2*N_i)`, where N_i is the negative mass of that row's pairing immediately before the call. A full-rank three-stream endpoint has Phi=9. Thus **an eight-call solution requires accumulated paid-row negative mass at least 1/2**. A Cauchy–Schwarz version requires a local coefficient-row/inverse-column norm product of at least 9/8 at some paid prefix.

`PROOF.md` proves the identities for any symmetric subadditive group metric and derives the positive-diagonal-gauge corollary. A matrix-sparsity metric extends the scalar-unitary obstruction to formal words with arbitrary invertible matrix frames, free monomial maps and two-sparse butterflies, including non-Clifford frames. The finite implementation specializes to the pinned three-qubit Clifford model.

**No new kappa or positive eight-call primitive.** The general nonunitary problem remains open. Potential and negativity are necessary diagnostics, not endpoint certificates. The theorem is in a formal complex group algebra; it does not infer formal linear independence from a concrete matrix representation, import an FFT lower bound into the multiplication model, or cover clean ancillas without an independent-stream argument.

Validation:

- Exact standard-library Q(omega) arithmetic, with omega²+omega+1=0. All 71 named prefixes and their actual inverses agree with independent dense Gaussian Clifford multiplication; both formal inverse identities are checked.
- Seven named controls include valid nine-call endpoints, eight-call deletions, complex positive diagonal gauges, and an exact two-call example attaining the local excess bound: one call gains 5/3 using negative mass 1/3.
- Two explicit false-positive controls matter for search: a five-call word has Phi=9 but fails the endpoint; an eight-call amplification trap has 200/201 correct coefficient mass in its deficient column while Phi stays 8.
- 126 paid/free inverse controls, exact squared norm inequalities and invalid-metric mutations pass. Relocation, source corruption, false endpoint receipts, wrong phase inverses, corrupted pairings and optimized-mode rejection are replayed by `validate.py`.
- The isolated replay takes about 3.1 seconds locally. `make selected-record-check` passes on base `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`, selecting #799 at `1661634653669567/10^18`. No full `make verify` or selected supplier cold replay is claimed for this standalone addition.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3 -B -I -S research/signed-rank-transport/verify.py
python3 -B -S research/signed-rank-transport/validate.py
```

Expected: `PASS_SIGNED_RANK_TRANSPORT` and `PASS_SIGNED_RANK_CLI_CONTROLS`.

Only `research/signed-rank-transport/` is added. Credits: Nir Ailon's [2014 quasi-probability/conditioning work](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.1307v5) and [paraunitary follow-up](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03278v6) supply the mathematical inspiration; eumemic's PR288 and its retained Swapnil Jain/upstream lineage supply the register framework; littleBro's PR680/705 supply two unchanged model/dense modules, byte-pinned in ORIGINS.json. title: Research: fuse native BIT dyadic shear pairs with three children (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The completed DATA-target shears of PR677 normally pay four native queries to produce `x ^= (h^a+h^-a)y`. For PR521's exact unipotent ADDRESS map and `a=+/-2^j`, this supplies the literal fused word `h^-a; XOR_y; h^(2a); XOR_y; h^-a`. A six-affine/one-child lowering of every signed dyadic query works over every odd residue ring. The completed pair pays **3 ordinary children instead of 4, 18 affine events instead of 24, and 2 XOR scans instead of 4**, with arbitrary dirty DATA/spectators and no full private row.

**Status: recursive-interface research construction; no new kappa.** The written proof also establishes a sharp **three-query** minimum in the stated power-query/XOR model, even with arbitrary dirty row spectators and integer query powers. This is not a minimum over arbitrary tape programs or a physical runtime comparison. The first-difference two-query theorem of PR677 remains intact.

The complete typed recurrence prices actual full-row children at volume `V/3` and width `N/3`, coefficient preparation, all affine/XOR scans, primitive temporary streams, source access, routing and head returns. The target requires exclusive access until completion; the source never changes. The new middle coefficient differs from the baseline and streaming constants depend on fixed j. The seed-selected `a=2^54` fixture is exact coefficient evidence, not a practical speedup. A centered DATA shear cannot replace ordinary ADDRESS interchange without a separate compiler; supplier/frame/owner invoices and all-size/tape/analytic transfer remain open.

Only `research/dyadic-query-pair/` is added. Exact task base: `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`. Consumed source heads are PR521 `a190fdb39f31647fc6f651625353710624627348` and PR677 `613c02b8b4411f991f108dcc1481b3f9100b996f`, plus the original tape sections at `5996e33ecad6a0ccd578aec58831457829d75575`. Seven original source/license/notice files are retained byte for byte with Git blob and SHA-256 pins.

OS-random assignment seed **54**, recursive interfaces. No pinned coordination issue exists, so the claim is local. Upstream advanced to PR799 (`f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`) during the sprint; its selected record, review and actual X4 construction were read. The two consumed PR heads and tape sections remain unchanged. The selected frontier is not edited.

**Concrete non-overlap:** PR756 changes the historical balanced-Fano enumeration's performance; this adds no such checker or replay. PR805 builds real rational cyclic leaves and restores one dirty array plus a scalar; this instead concerns exact odd-ring ADDRESS permutations acting on F2 VALUE arrays with queries on the genuine DATA target and no full private row. Neither PR's branch/worktree, construction, restoration interface, code or verification is consumed or changed. Concurrent dirty/clean echo, Clifford valuation and newer supplier work are separate objects; inspected heads and attribution are retained.

Credit **Karl Appel / applecrusher (PR521)**, **commdata2338 (PR677)**, OpenAI's imported tape framework, Douglas Colkitt and the retained projector/group-algebra lineage. python3 -I -O -B research/dyadic-query-pair/verify.py

- 112 signed dyadic lowerings through index 55 (including the doubled seed-54 query), 1,792 rational columns and 16,128 modular columns, with literal inverses and ADDRESS spectators.
- 110 signed symbolic program pairs; separate outer-product/literal-matrix projector catalogues; all 91,320 declared balanced-power two-query products reject the centered target. The universal exclusion is the written proof, not an extrapolation from this census.
- Separate coordinate interpreter/direct push formula and sparse-set replay of the full six-field domains mod 3 and mod 5: 154,160 dirty four-role basis columns per program, 7,552 further prime-power orbit columns, complete baseline/fused/inverse checks and 92 simultaneous dirty-row cases.

title: Tooling: bind selected primary-proof pointers to verified digests (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

**Status: Tooling improvement / provenance audit. No new κ.**

Found and fixed a provenance-validation gap in `scripts/verify_selected_result.py`.

The original checker verifies the selected certificate, exact κ, source inventories, and proof supplements, but only checks that the primary `proof` path exists. Changing that pointer to an existing, unverified file containing `NO PROOF` still passes, without modifying any mathematical inputs or verified digests.

The fix requires the resolved primary-proof path to belong to the set of files whose SHA-256 digests have already been verified.

This preserves:
- Both legacy package-relative and newer repository-relative source manifests.
- Primary proofs covered by the source inventory or by a proof supplement.
- Existing arithmetic, certificate, inventory, and supplement checks.
- Mutable review/validation receipts when they are not otherwise digest-pinned.
- Existing normalized-path and resolved-symlink semantics.

**This is a concrete metadata-validation gap, not evidence of an incorrect mathematical construction or published proof.**

## Reproduction and evidence

From the repository root (Python 3.11+, standard library only):

```bash
python3 -I -B research/selected-proof-binding/reproduce.py
```

Expected output:

```text
PASS_SELECTED_PROOF_BINDING 11 reproduced gaps; 11 repaired rejections; 12 tests
```

The reproducer imports the original checker from a byte-identical, Git-blob-pinned copy and compares it with the patched implementation.

**Validation results:**
- 11 detached-proof mutations accepted by the original checker and rejected by the patched checker.
- 6 valid proof/path cases accepted by both implementations.
- 12 regression tests pass under normal and optimized Python.
- Baseline corruption, expected-receipt corruption, and removal of the repair are detected.
- Relocated source-bundle and clean patch-application checks pass.

The package includes a deterministic evidence receipt (`EXPECTED.json`), the original checker, regression tests, source references, and a reproduction guide.

## Scope and limitations

This verifies provenance coverage, not the semantic correctness of the referenced proof. A coherently modified record/inventory or a pointer to another already-verified but irrelevant file remains outside this check's guarantees.

Full `make verify`, selected cold-supplier replays, complete repository inventory checks, Lean, and remote CI were not run. Direct cloning was blocked by DNS resolution in the execution environment; pinned source files were inspected through the GitHub connector and the focused tests ran in an isolated source snapshot.

No selected certificate, supplier, construction, research ledger, or `upstream/` files are modified.

## Provenance and overlap

- **Exact base commit:** `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`
- **OS-random assignment seed:** 96 (research consolidation)
- **Original checker Git blob:** `4f0e4bded003a48b5122cbff597af4282f4d6329`

The original experimental base selected PR741/PR589 at κ = 0.001661202643272239. During verification, main advanced to PR799 at κ = 0.001661634653669567. The affected checker remained byte-identical, and the new selected primary proof is also digest-covered. No new κ is claimed.

Related work: PR704 strengthens review-ledger metadata, while PR474 binds fresh gen4 replay certificates. PR746 and PR828 address separate historical source-reconciliation gaps. None is duplicated or imported here.

The local sprint claim, candidate selection, source pins, results, and limitations are recorded in `research/selected-proof-binding/`.
