title: Scoped negative result: one added P112 total cannot reduce fixed-reader copy cost
body:
## Scoped negative result — no new kappa

PR717 leaves open whether mixed pairing-rank totals can improve the P112 complex decoder. This package rules out one exact family: **adding one total while retaining the eight coordinate reader columns cannot lower copy-rank cost below 64**, even with arbitrary real coefficients and an arbitrary 112-component source correction outside the coordinate column space.

For `X X^T = 2G`, the family is

```text
X X^T = sum_j x_j (x_j-a_j z)^T + (Xa) z^T,
a in R^8, z in R^112.
```

It includes every exact nine-term factorization retaining those reader columns, up to nonzero column scaling, and the transposed class. It does **not** cover arbitrary changes of the reader columns, masked completions with extra free terms, multiple additional totals, other geometries, or arbitrary physical delivery programs.

The proof uses annihilator dimensions. Exact premises cover 511 binary functionals and all 3,272 sign classes. At full eight-coordinate support, the linear system has rank 63 rather than 64: each of its 128 nonzero kernels forces contradictory correction values at 56 ports. That extra compatibility check is included explicitly. This is a written theorem with exact finite certificates, not an inference from failed searches or a proof-assistant multiplication theorem.

## Reproduce and validation

```sh
python -B research/p112-single-lift/verify.py
python -B research/p112-single-lift/independent_check.py
```

Expected: `PASS_P112_SINGLE_LIFT` and `PASS_P112_SINGLE_LIFT_INDEPENDENT`.

- Standard library only; Windows/Python 3.12.0 normal and optimized checks pass.
- A relocated Git archive passes on Python 3.11.9 with `-O -S -B`; regenerated certificate is byte-identical.
- The independent implementation imports neither the main verifier nor its geometry module. It checks 511 integer minors with Bareiss elimination and repeats all binary ranks using set elimination.
- Nine mathematical negative controls, four independent arithmetic controls, and four additional source/certificate corruption controls pass.
- Original-base selected-record integrity and staged whitespace pass. `upstream/`, existing generators, and the selected frontier are unchanged.
- Repository-wide `make verify`, selected-supplier cold replay, and proof-assistant verification were not run. The new package has not run in hosted CI: the GitHub token lacks `workflow` permission, so the proposed scoped workflow was removed after a rejected push. Account permissions were not changed. Existing repository CI is separate from these local results.

At submitted head `125ce25bdae421627b56077adc14940c2d0aa52f`, all five existing upstream workflows report `action_required`; [Verify research artifacts](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38362262287) has no passing result. No hosted CI pass is claimed. GitHub reports the PR mergeable. The exported patch also passed application checking against an isolated index at the exact base, and the final portable ZIP passed its verifier after fresh extraction.

## Provenance, overlap and accounting

Exact base: `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`. Seed **40**, structural decoder research, drawn once from OS randomness. The local claim, full coverage, source pins and validation receipt are in the package. Only this isolated research package is added.

Credit **Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled's PR620** for the existing cost 64; **DreamingOfClouds' PR717** at `4150829a2cb66b823f4282da98985959ee448a90` for the model/open problem, and **PR446** at `309482849b6ddf34db998f53612d34c19f6e3233` for the inherited separate-total copy-tree interpretation. Their review scopes are preserved, and the original model/notice are retained. This adds a proof for a nine-term subclass beyond the prior eight-term/gauge and finite flip-walk evidence.

The final refresh inspected 639 open PRs through #842 and found no duplicate. Main advanced to `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`, selecting #799; that integration does not overlap these files or alter this pinned research model. There was no pinned coordination issue, so the claim is local.

Improvements to other costs or to rank distributions at the same sum remain possible. title: Research: pay for preparation, execution, restoration and tape for #621's cyclic inverse at every stride (no κ claim)
body:
The [K492 review](docs/research/community-k492-review.md) leaves one obligation open for #621 (Ali Romman). That PR's `L`-uniform inverse bound still needs paid costs for efficient preparation, rounded execution, restoration and tape. #628 (Chafik Boukhalfa) pays for preparation and neighbouring-stride execution. #764 (Charles Bethin) sharpens the scan rounding. For any stride other than ±1, #628 routes cycles through two merge sorts costing `O(L(B+log L) log L)`. Those sorts bring back the `log L` factor that the inverse bound removed.

This PR adds `research/cyclic-inverse-stride-bridge/` and one CI workflow. **No existing file changes. No new integer κ, complex b, or BIT c.**

## Result

- **Theorem 1.** A Euclidean chain/closure recursion solves `y_i = x_i + b_i y_(i-w)` for any stride. A lag-`w` FIFO built from two stacks gives every pass its predecessor in natural order. Each level at least halves the length. A single stable factor then costs:
  - at most `40L` sequential record moves (largest observed: 29.68 per entry through `L=131072`);
  - `O(L)` rounded operations;
  - an error of at most `min(K,1/β)(u/β)(5+4B/β)+u`.

  The error bound holds for every `L`. The proof reuses #764's shared-suffix identity `1-Q ≥ βG`. A concavity argument shows that coefficient margins never fall below `β` at any recursion depth.
- **Theorem 2.** Composing the solver with #628's certified factorization gives `P(τZ_L^w)^{-1}` at precision `p+(n+2)g+O(log r) = p+O(r^4)`, with no `L` term. One admission condition, `p ≥ log2(log2 L+2)`, depends on `L`.
- **Verdict.** For one kernel inverse on fixed sequential tapes, the cost with all four obligations paid is `soft-O(r^3(p+r^4)) + O(rL)·M(p+r^4) + O(rL(p+r^4))`. That cost per entry does not depend on `L`, so **#621's gain survives payment at the single-kernel level**. Restoration in this model is cheap: the input tape is never written, and scratch tapes are erased at linear cost.

## Validation

`python3 -B -I -O research/cyclic-inverse-stride-bridge/verify.py --check` prints `PASS_CYCLIC_INVERSE_STRIDE_BRIDGE generic=2052 kernel_cases=300 controls=4 max_records_per_entry=29.671875`. It passed under system Python and the repository venv (Python 3.13, Linux). It needs only the standard library and takes about 100 seconds.

- **Generic cases (2052).** `L=1..18`, every stride in `[-L,L)`, three margins and two grids. Each case is compared exactly with an independent per-cycle geometric-closure oracle. The margin invariant is checked at every recursion level.
- **Kernel cases (300).** These use all ten #628 certified kernels (radix 3 through 16), two gauges, `L ∈ {1,2,3,5,8}` and all strides for `L≤5`. Each case checks Theorem 2's exact budget together with #628's perturbation bound and the expanded residual. 81 cases are also compared with a dense Gauss–Jordan solve.
- **Controls.** The replay rejects a rotated closure reseed, too little precision, a unit coefficient and a wrong inner-shift direction.
- **Vendored sources.** The #628 files are byte-identical to head `0768f97d` and are hash-pinned; the verifier refuses drift.
- **Repository checks (Linux, base `66849e1`).** I did not complete a full `make verify`.
  - `make verify` passed seven targets with no failures: `verify-community`, `verify-producers`, `verify-partial-gauge`, `verify-three-stage-cover`, `verify-paired-cube`, `verify-recycled-bit` and `verify-entrance-banks`. My one-hour local limit then stopped the run during `gen4-bank-verify`.
  - `make selected-record-check` and `make verify-tests` passed separately: 549 tests, 0 failures, exit 0.
  - I did not run `frontier626-verify` or the later targets. This PR changes no existing file and does not affect the selected construction.
  - `git diff --cached --check` passed.

## Still open

- A borrowed-array (dirty) form of the stride solver for the exact-width model. #628's dirty route still covers that model, at `O(p+log(D+1)+r^5)` precision.
- Composition across the complete transform, phase collection and normalization.
- The multiplication reduction.
- The `O(r^4)` guard is a proof bound. Numerical probes put the true `min|P|` near `2^-10` for `r≤32`; those probe values are not certified here.

This is not a formal verification. The written proof carries the all-`L` claims, and the finite cases support the reference implementation.

## Credits

- **#621, Ali Romman (@aliromman).** Kernel and the `L`-uniform bounds.
- **#628, Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky).** Factorization, preparation, phase and dirty-shear budgets, and the vendored certificates.
- **#764, Charles Bethin (@cbethin).** The shared-suffix identity and the inverse-square scan bound.

New work by **Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani)**, prepared with substantial AI assistance. Apache-2.0. No literature-priority claim is made.

title: Research audit: sharp linear inverse bounds for balanced weighted cycles (no new kappa)
body:
This research audit gives the exact worst-case infinity norm of a linear inverse on a balanced weighted cycle with bounded local weight magnitudes. It supplies rational attaining weights and a scoped negative result: exact unit cycle products, unit-circle spectrum, and arbitrarily small local weight deviations do not preserve a length-independent unit-weight inverse estimate.

**Status: research note / scoped negative result with independent exact verification.**

For `P(z)=z-33/32`, cycle length 256 and every weight within 1/16 of one, the simple two-block witness has inverse norm strictly between 1936 and 1937. The exact maximum over the admitted class lies between 2164 and 2165. The inherited unit-weight estimates would be 800, or 160 using the interior-root count. **This does not contradict PR803:** those matrices violate its explicit all-integer-power norm-one assumption. No new kappa or rounded implementation is claimed.

The written proof gives the exact cycle-local power factor K, transfer with one factor K, a sharp extremal inverse formula, the constant/linear/exponential local-error regimes for a linear polynomial, and a sufficient strict perturbation guard. The universal arguments are separate from the finite checks. The analytic Wiener bound from Rafael Guevara's PR803 is an explicit inherited premise; the cycle criterion and counterexample/extremal formulas have their own elementary proofs.

Reproduce offline with Python 3.10+ and its standard library:

```sh
python -B research/weighted-cycle-power-audit/verify.py
python -B -m unittest discover -s research/weighted-cycle-power-audit -p test_package.py -v
```

Expected: `PASS: exact weighted-cycle power audit` and 11 tests passing. Evidence covers:

- 1,377 generated weighted-permutation cases and 9,990 exact signed-power samples, plus 18 admission/failure controls.
- 72 dense inverses checked against 504 independent affine basis solves; 96 sharp-inverse attainments; 108 complex-phase inverses; three exact length-256 extremal solves; ten near-unit threshold certificates.
- 48 sharp power-cap witnesses / 2,600 direct path products and 240 polynomial perturbation cases (155 admitted, 85 inconclusive).

Normal and optimized replays from a clean export of staged Git blobs passed, as did the source/tamper/mutation checks and the selected-record check at the starting base. Full `make verify` and supplier cold replays were not run: only the new `research/weighted-cycle-power-audit/` package is added, with no existing generator, selected certificate, schedule or `upstream/` changes. title: Tooling: 1.54-1.71x faster #741 complex replay by running independent pinned stages concurrently
body:
**Status: tooling improvement.** No κ, construction, predicate, pinned file or selected record changes. `make frontier741-verify` is unchanged and remains the reference replay.

Base: `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261` (main). Track: verification engineering (sprint seed 85).

## What changed

The complex half of `make frontier741-verify` (874 s of 1158 s in the c290b7b receipt) runs the 22 stages of `research/complex-sw4-frame8/verify.py` one after another. Many are independent. For example, the fresh PR558 ancestor replay shares nothing with the gauge44 → p6n → SW4 → frames chain, and three control stages read only the final word.

`scripts/verify_complex741_parallel.py` (opt-in `make complex741-parallel-verify`) executes the pinned `verify.py` itself, statement by statement, after checking its SHA-256 (`7706065e…`, the value in the package `MANIFEST.json`):

- The prelude runs unchanged: manifest check, vendored source pins, environment.
- Each `run(...)` call goes to `verify.py`'s own `run` function on a worker thread once its prerequisites in `STAGE_DEPS` have passed. Command line, environment, `run_portable.py`, logs and failure handling are the original code.
- Statements that read stage output (ancestral linkage loop, all count assertions, `RESULT.json`, `RECEIPT.json`) run unchanged, in their original order, after all stages pass.
- It refuses a changed `verify.py` or a stage list that differs from the table.

## Evidence

**Schedule against a recorded trace.** `research/complex741-parallel-replay/record_access.py --record DIR` runs the unchanged sequential `verify.py` under a Python audit hook loaded through a `.pth` file, so it also covers the `-I` children. The hook logs every open, listing, rename, delete and mkdir per stage. `ACCESS.json` covers 83 processes. No stage writes outside the work directory except into fresh `tempfile` directories. No pair of stages left unordered by `STAGE_DEPS` has a write/read, write/write, write/list or mkdir/list conflict, and deferring the ancestral linkage loop conflicts with no later stage. Two independent recordings gave identical access sets. The table keeps argument-derived edges, which are stricter than the trace requires, because audit hooks do not see `stat`.

**Equivalence.** Three full replays on one machine, each in the same absolute work directory:

| Replay | Result | Total |
|---|---|---:|
| sequential `verify.py` | PASS κ = 1661202643272239/10^18 | 594.7 s |
| driver `--jobs 8` (default) | PASS, same κ | 386.4 s (1.54×) |
| driver `--jobs 3` | PASS, same κ | 347.7 s (1.71×) |

`compare_replays.py` checked all 304 files of each tree pair. Sequential vs `--jobs 8`: 233 byte-identical, 50 JSON files differ only under `seconds`/`elapsed_seconds` or in SHA-256 digests of the same file where that file is itself accepted (checked to a fixed point), and 21 logs differ only in decimal elapsed times or such digests. Nothing else differs, and the other two pairs give the same result. Every generated word is byte-identical. Masking floats in logs is a relaxation; the JSON outputs are compared without masking. Negative control: changing the last digit of κ in `global-replay/ASSEMBLY.json` and one integer in a log produces exactly those two rejections.

The parallel time equals the dependency chain gauge44 → … → `all-native-phase-edges` → global admission, so more workers cannot shorten it. Applying that chain to the Linux stage times in c290b7b gives 457 of 874 s. That is an estimate, not a measurement.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_complex741_parallel.py   # 15 tests
make complex741-parallel-verify                                         # PASS 0.001661202643272239
python3 research/complex741-parallel-replay/compare_replays.py SEQ_DIR PAR_DIR   # exit 0, "0 other differences"
```

(`SEQ_DIR` and `PAR_DIR` must be replays made at the same path, one after the other.)

## Scope and limits

- Measured on Windows 11 (16 logical CPUs, CPython 3.12.14), one run each, host not isolated. **Linux was not run for this change.** The sequential package replay also passed on this Windows machine.
- Covers the complex supplier only. The bit replay (`tune/verify.sh`, needs C++17 and Boost) could not be run here and is unchanged. Running it beside this driver would hide most of its 284 s; I leave that for someone who can test it.
- The trace and comparison are evidence for this pinned `verify.py`; the SHA-256 pin forces re-derivation after any package change.
- Finite replay does not prove the multiplication theorem; inherited assumptions are unchanged.

## Credit and overlap

Replays chafreaky's #741 package and the contributors credited in its `PROVENANCE.md`. eumemic's #154 proposed concurrent execution of the `make verify` groups; this applies the idea inside the selected complex replay, with a recorded trace. It does not overlap #824 (stage-pair audit), #818 (R420 RREF) or #838 (binding audit).

Prepared by navinor (Aaron Wang) with substantial AI assistance (Claude) in design, code, measurement and prose.

title: Research audit: kernel102 packing ceiling holds without fallback charges
body:
PR525's fixed kernel102 packing ceiling still holds after removing every positive fallback charge: the ideal rank moment alone exceeds one. This adds a standalone exact proof of that stronger cost statement, using two small pinned inputs and neither upstream moment engine.

- Enumerates all 112 packing patterns, with exact rational log/exp lower bounds and no solver or third-party dependencies.
- Verifies a dual whose minimum slack exceeds `2/10^11`; its ideal-moment lower bound exceeds `1 + 7/10^10` at `b = 6981767/5000000000`.
- Includes the weak-duality proof, exact deterministic result, source SHA-256/Git blob pins, and semantic negative controls that bypass file hashes.

The numerical ceiling is unchanged: under the original outer relation, `kappa < 6981767/5006981767`. The frozen local profile, helper widths, idle stocks, whole-helper assignment and paid-remainder model are explicit hypotheses. This does not reconstruct PR525's supplier, improve the selected frontier, or close its scalar/physical/all-size obligations.

Validation in a network-disabled, read-only Python container: `python -B verify.py`, plus 10 tests (26 negative cases) normally and under `-O`. An additional Codex review independently corroborated the inequalities using exact alternating Mercator/Taylor arithmetic; this is not human review or a Lean proof. No full supplier replay or GitHub CI result is claimed.

Reproduce from `research/kernel102-ideal-dual-audit/`:

```sh
python -B verify.py
python -B -m unittest -v test_verify.py
python -O -B -m unittest -v test_verify.py
```

Base: `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`. PR525 source head: `71acd0c35ee81de848316b3f2b4c3bd15b219c51`. The package can be copied and run outside the repository. Recent PRs were checked for overlap through #852.

Prepared by Chinmay (@chinmayarvind23) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky) supplied the model, source profile, original dual and numerical ceiling in #525; the new contribution is independent arithmetic verification and removal of the fallback-charge assumption. Upstream notices and Apache-2.0 attribution are retained.

title: Tooling: exact modular rank fast path for historical joint-frame verification
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This contribution adds an opt-in verification package under
`research/joint-frame-modular-screen/` for the historical
`scripts/audit_joint_frames.py` certificate.

The adapter uses exact elimination modulo 101 to certify full rational
rank. If the modular reduction is rank-deficient, or a denominator is
divisible by 101, it falls back to the unchanged original rational
elimination routine. No approximate rank decision is used.

The supplied benchmark records a reduction in median complete-certificate
wall time from 1.952577 s to 1.701918 s (12.8% lower) across seven
alternating fresh-process A/B pairs. All fourteen timed certificates
are byte-identical. One individual pair was slower; the timing result
is specific to the recorded environment, not a universal speedup claim.

This is a tooling improvement, not a new construction or conditional
bound. No improved kappa or practical integer-multiplication speedup
is claimed.

- Exact investigation base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`

- `NOTICE.md` credits predecessor and related concurrent work.

The supplied patch adds only this research package and leaves existing

The supplied verification record reports:

  original rational routine: 752 modular full-rank certificates and

- 12 focused test groups, including an independent determinant/minor
  oracle over 530 binary matrices and 240 seed-85 rational matrices.
- Four deliberately incorrect kernels detected by counterexamples.

```

`PROOF.md` supplies the algebraic equivalence argument for the fast path.
The finite test campaign and certificate replays are not a formal proof
of the full multiplication theorem.

title: Research audit: sharp physical counter costs with direction reversals (no new kappa)
body:
The existing physical ripple-counter theorem correctly bounds calls in one fixed direction. This **research note / adversarial mathematical audit** supplies an exact signed-potential identity for arbitrary directions and a sharp run-based invoice: for width `w >= 1`, `N` calls in `K` maximal constant-direction runs cost at most `4N + 2(w-1)K` literal transitions. If `H` runs contain wraps, the sharper bound is `4N + 2(w-2)K + 2H`.

Alternating wraparound calls attain the uniform bound; alternating nonwrapping calls across the middle edge attain the no-wrap bound. At width 4 and seven calls, these cost 70 and 56 transitions respectively, whereas an invalid extension of the old fixed-direction bound gives 36. This establishes that excluding wraps alone does not justify arbitrary-direction `O(N+w)` for this primitive. It identifies **no error in the existing fixed-direction theorem or selected multiplication construction**, and claims **no new kappa**.

Eight isolated files under `research/counter-reversal-audit/` contain the handwritten uniform proof, an independent single-cell tape interpreter, exact deterministic receipt, source pins, fault-injection tests, scope/attribution, validation and local sprint claim. The primitive invoice excludes controller dispatch, preparation, payload, reset/restoration and recursive scheduling; those remain explicit obligations. Finite replay is not a formal proof of the universal statement or full multiplication theorem.

Reproduce with Python 3.10+ (standard library):

```sh
python3 -I -B -O research/counter-reversal-audit/verify.py
# PASS_COUNTER_REVERSAL_AUDIT schedules=130305 literal_executions=16376 controls=10
python3 -I -B -O research/counter-reversal-audit/test_audit.py
# Six tests pass.
make selected-record-check machine-transfer-check
```

All commands pass on Linux / Python 3.14.7; the audit and tests also pass without `-O`. Six source SHA256/Git-blob pins are checked. Exhaustive coverage is all words of widths 0..10 in both directions with four exterior patterns, plus all words of widths 0..7 and all direction strings of lengths 0..8. Another 256 seeded length-257 schedules are sampled. The fixed domain and stopping rule are recorded. Fault injection checks omitted head returns, suppressed wraps, incorrect endpoints and source drift under optimized Python. `git diff --cached --check` passed. No full `make verify`, selected supplier cold replay, Lean rebuild or remote CI pass is claimed for this isolated addition.

Base: `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631` (still upstream main at submission). Assignment seed **67**, drawn with OS-backed `secrets.randbelow(100)`. The accepted result was followed through the #799 certificate, construction and review; selected κ remains `1661634653669567/10^18`. No existing files or `upstream/` changed. No coordination issue exists, so the claim and its result are local. A final scan of 656 open PRs through #859 found no matching reversal audit; #565 is distinct counter-copying work and is not a dependency.

Credit **rfu08** for the physical counter, fixed-direction formalization and already documented direction limitation, published at `2d970ab3ca0271cfb2b609dc9aae1b7073b7774d`, and the repository manuscript authors for the scan argument. Contribution by **Kairos Ess (@Kairos-Ess)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in derivation, implementation, verification and writing. title: Research: cubic precision and exact coarse-grid recovery for cyclic inverses (no κ)
body:
Reduces the growing-radix precision guard for PR628's neighboring cyclic inverse from **O(r^4) to O(r^3)**. Every partial inverse is bounded by the full inverse and its complementary polynomial, using the standard Mahler-measure inequality. Bounding all rounded prefixes together avoids multiplying the worst reciprocal margin once per factor. PR621's circle bound is unchanged.

The written proof gives `W <= max(p,w)+12r^3+m` fractional bits for a source of norm at most `2^m`, including exact coarse-grid source recovery, and a factor-preparation budget `b <= p+6r^3+m`. Integer magnitude bits have the same cubic order. With the inherited preparation algorithms, neighboring-layout execution and setup cost `soft-O((Lr+r^3)(max(p,w)+r^3+m))`, plus charged phase access and longer phase descriptions.

The new in-place schedule evaluates the inverse, adds its result to a target, applies the forward factors, and rounds the source back to its original grid exactly. This requires **owned widened words with reserved low zero bits**, whose capacity is explicitly charged. Rounding the target increment to the original grid also gives signed shears that compose and cancel exactly with one fixed precision budget for a planned word.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.11+:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/cubic-cyclic-inverse/run.py --out /absolute/fresh/output
```

Validation:

- 5,220 exact integer budget cases across all 116 prime-power radices from 3 through 512.
- 120 actual kernel executions; 60 compare every prefix with independent dense solves. All check expanded polynomial residuals, recovery bounds, exact source restoration and total kernel error at most `2^-128`.
- 20 interacting shear-word cases, including 12 dense comparisons and exact whole-word cancellation; ten rejection controls across both suites.
- Complete fresh runs passed on macOS/Python 3.11 and 3.14 and Linux aarch64/Python 3.14, in approximately 66–72 seconds. All three generated mathematical artifacts are byte-identical. Receipts, logs, source manifests and artifact hashes are included. Scoped Python 3.11/3.14 CI is added.

**No new κ, complex b, BIT c or measured multiplication speedup.** The asymptotic claim comes from the written argument; finite tests do not implement Pan's worst-case factorizer. Arbitrary dirty-bit restoration, common-label/Clifford compilation, arbitrary-stride restored-source scheduling, complete-transform accounting and the multiplication reduction remain open. The full repository suite and selected supplier were not rerun for this isolated package.

Credit Ali Romman for #621, Chafik Boukhalfa for #628, and the standard Mahler-measure, periodic-filtering and approximate-factorization methods. Exact predecessor heads, blobs, notices and mathematical sources are retained. Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human or delegated-agent review, formal verification or literature-priority claim.

title: Scoped negative result: no frame reassignment of the selected X4 complex word admits the next tick (exact duals, no new kappa)
body:
**Scoped negative result. No new κ.** Only `research/complex-x4-frame-bound/` is added. The selected record, `upstream/` and every supplier file are unchanged.

## Claim

Take the selected complex word, PR799's X4 word (content `1e1d99ba…`, all 72 complex calls), and fix its scalar program, start and end frames (so all widths), cut, centres, target levels, precondition, FULL cleanup and early-cleanup membership. Let each of its 6,364 A, B and early-cleanup gate frames be any F₂⁹ subspace allowed by the frame contract that `research/gauge44-frames-x/independent/audit_local.py` checks: nested frames along every register, centre and target levels at the start of B, and the inverse-row and dirt-column cone conditions of all 126 low ends.

No such assignment admits b_next = 0.001664400278850482327914, the next 10⁻²⁴ tick above the selected complex endpoint. The pinned `outer.py` gives κ < b/(1+b) (`compact_phase_layer` with `complex_above_bit`), and b_next/(1+b_next) lies below the next κ tick. Frame reassignment alone cannot raise the selected κ.

## Method and evidence

- Forward joins and backward meets give complete frame intervals: 5,163 gates are forced and 1,201 have 2, 5 or 16 choices. The verifier enumerates every interval and checks each size against the Gaussian-binomial count.
- 140 components, with a local-polytope LP of 9,483 rows and 12,019 columns in total. Dual entries are integer linear forms in C₂…C₉ (C_d = M_d − d·M₁). Of the reduced costs, 8,582 are identically zero and 3,437 are strictly positive under outward bounds from both pinned engines (`moment.py` and `base_two_moment.py`). Each component's dual objective equals the selected cost as an exact coefficient identity.
- Global step: 72 × local + {1:1, 3:1, 44:1, 48:2396} equals the pinned global profile. Both engines put the moment above 1 at b_next and below 1 at the selected endpoint.
- The start-of-B centre equality is relaxed to a charged climb, and native-chain conditions beyond `audit_local.py` are not imposed. Both only enlarge the feasible set.
- Cross-check without duality: 12 random legal reassignments (40 frame changes each) pass the pinned `audit_local.py` unchanged, with exactly the profile the model predicts, and each is strictly costlier at b_next. The auditor refuses a frame below the forward join and a mismatched profile.
- Six rejection controls: a dropped component, an inflated dual, an omitted frame choice, the accepted endpoint in place of b_next, a legal but costlier baseline, and a changed word.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-x4-frame-bound/verify.py --controls
```

Expected final line: `PASS_X4_FRAME_ASSIGNMENT_EXCLUSION controls=6/6`. This takes about 5 s, uses the standard library only and refuses `-O`. Optional: `crosscheck.py` (about 1 min), and `verify.py --word <fresh X4 FULL-WORD.json.gz>` for a rebuilt word. `gen_duals.py` (HiGHS) only nominates the duals and reproduces `data/DUALS.json.gz` byte for byte.

## Validation run

- Windows 11, CPython 3.12.14 and 3.14.7: verifier with all six controls passes.
- A minimal closure of 21 committed files, extracted with `git archive` into an empty directory, passes the verifier and the cross-check.
- `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` passes, and so does the staged whitespace check.
- Not run: full `make verify`, the native cold replay `make frontier799-verify`, Linux CI and Lean. The word comes from the retained `pr799-replay.tar.gz`, whose hash the integration receipt records; its content hash matches `RECIPE-X4.json` and `INDEPENDENT-LOCAL.json`.

## What it leaves for the complex track

Per call, 1,745 of the 2,548 rank-1 children, all 56 rank-5 children and the eight centre descents lie on edges between forced frames. A κ gain from this supplier needs a scalar change (read sets, order, tail membership), new start or end frames, or an owner and hosting change.

## Scope

Not covered: scalar rewrites, reordering, read-set exchanges, early-cleanup membership, entrance promotions or other width changes, owners, hosting and the invoice, the bit supplier, and other outer theorems. The exclusion holds at b_next for this fixed word. Inherited all-size, realization, hosting, precision, tape and analytic hypotheses remain. This is a finite certificate, not a Lean proof.

## Prior and concurrent work

The method is chafreaky's #557 (PR551 word). ntedvs's #776 applies it to #626's jp8 and ck words without tail frames. Rohansguliani's #815 solves PR699's SW4 and #626's words with floating-point LP and CP-SAT, with tail frames fixed. JointXF's FrameCoal report in #799 (X4 frame-optimal for its moves) is a search report in the #799 review; this package corroborates it with an exact certificate. New here: the selected X4 word in native gauge44 format, free early-cleanup frames and cone ceilings derived from the exact prefix map. Related: #850 (owner packing at the current inventory) and #775 (partial read exchanges on P6k4). #858 (closed) changed owners, which is outside this fixed-owner scope. Overlap was refreshed through #863.

Construction credit for the X4 word belongs to Jeremy Kothe (#799), chafreaky (#741, #685), BRoute, BlockInvert, icekylinx (#645) and the lineage in `research/gauge44-frames-x/README.md`.

title: Research audit: CK Horner reversal raises scalar-grid guard from 3 to 5 bits (no new kappa)
body:
The bidirectional Horner circuits in #837 preserve their exact endpoint maps and gate savings, but can need a finer intermediate fixed-point grid. This **mathematical audit** establishes the exact fractional guard requirements of all six pinned scalar programs and supplies a complete-word rounding counterexample. **No new κ.**

For inputs on `2^-p Z^N`, with an unbounded integer part and working grid `2^-(p+g) Z`, exact representability of every intermediate for every input is equivalent to `g` being at least the largest reduced binary denominator exponent of any prefix-map coefficient. The package gives the proof, complete prefix replays, and sharpness witnesses.

| Scalar projection | Forward binary/NAF baseline | #837 bidirectional |
|---|---:|---:|
| CK forward | 3 | **5** |
| CK backward | 8 | 8 |
| JP8 forward | 4 | 4 |
| JP8 backward | 27 | 27 |
| SW4 forward | 3 | 3 |
| SW4 backward | 19 | 19 |

The shared forward/backward guard stays **8 for CK, 27 for JP8, 19 for SW4**. Eighteen of the 962 individual coefficients require one or two additional bits in the chosen reversed circuits, occurring in 21 CK, 4 JP8 and 5 SW4 additions per orientation.

For `t += (31/8)*s`, reverse NAF saves one real primitive but raises local depth from three to five. With `s=1`, halving rounded toward minus infinity at three fractional bits gives **4 instead of 31/8**. In the complete CK forward scalar program, native basis input 16 at three bits leaves errors `L43=-1/8`, `L422=+1/8`, `L425=+1/8`; four bits still fail, and five restore the exact endpoint. The original forward-only program is exact at three bits.

## Reproduce and validation

python3 -B -I research/dyadic-fractional-grid/verify.py
python3 -B -I research/dyadic-fractional-grid/crosscheck.py
python3 -B -I research/dyadic-fractional-grid/test_grid.py
```

PASS_DYADIC_FRACTIONAL_GRID programs=6 coefficients=962 extra_grid_coefficients=18 kappa=unchanged

- Arbitrary 716+9 or 728+9 native/private columns, macro boundaries, private erasure, event inventory and paid profiles are retained.
- Python 3.12.3 and 3.14.4 passed; nine tests passed on each. A minimal checkout with spaces in its path also passed in isolated, optimized Python without site packages.

title: Research: Gaussian E8 all-clique certificate ceiling is 40 (no new kappa)
body:
**Research note / scoped negative result. No new kappa.** Nonnegative weighted-clique certificates on the fixed 60-line Gaussian E8 configuration cannot certify more than **40 Gaussian pairing-rank units**, even when every nonempty nonorthogonal clique is allowed.

PR770 proves ceiling 40 for inclusion-maximal cliques and expressly leaves non-maximal cliques outside its theorem. This package closes that certificate-domain gap. It preserves PR738's existing scalar decoder interval **[40,60]**; a cost-40 decoder remains unconstructed.

## New evidence

- The initial attempt to extend PR770's 900-pair dual fails on a singleton: 42 hits rather than the required 45. This is a failed extension hypothesis, not a defect in the predecessor's scoped theorem.
- An exact repaired dual retains the **180 ordered orthogonal-normal hyperplane pairs with six-line intersection**, each of Gaussian pairing rank two. Every nonempty clique Q meets both hyperplanes in at least `9 |Q|` of these pairs. Summing their local constraints gives `9 sum_Q |Q| w_Q <= 360`, hence ceiling 40 for arbitrary nonnegative clique weights.
- Complete enumeration covers **2,068,372 cliques**, without a size cutoff. A separately implemented Gaussian geometry/rank checker and Bron–Kerbosch/submask traversal agree on all counts, size minima, pairs and the complete clique-set digest.

The matching feasible value-40 certificate is inherited from pinned PR738/PR770 sources. Their unchanged full primal flat-pair coverage is **not rerun or claimed as new evidence** here. This result closes the specified proof method, not all possible decoder mechanisms.

## Reproduce and validation

python -B research/gaussian-all-clique-dual/verify.py
python -B research/gaussian-all-clique-dual/independent.py

PASS_GAUSSIAN_ALL_CLIQUE_DUAL cliques=2068372 ordered_pairs=180 ceiling=40 controls=6 no_new_kappa

The enumerators also match brute force on all **1,099 labelled graphs of orders 1–5**. `scripts/audit_joint_frames.py` certificate.

Rank-deficient modular reductions and denominators divisible by 101
fall back to the unchanged original rational elimination routine.

body:
# R439 phase-B block 508: 37 to 30 additions (no new kappa)

Finite bit-supplier construction. The tuned R439 phase-B block at frame 508
(`B[205:242]` of `research/e8-bit-p111-tuned/tune/bitE8mut-p111-tuned.json.gz`,
registers `[19, 27, 35, 43, 57, 65, 66, 74, 89, 97, 466]`) is replaced with a
30-addition program computing the identical forward integer map. Rebuilding its
literal reverse cleanup reduces the complete native word from **24,305 to
24,291 ADDs** (7 forward + 7 reverse).

| Quantity | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Block additions (frame 508) | 37 | **30** |
| Complete exported ADDs | 24,305 | **24,291** |
| Forward positive bound | 49,347 | 49,347 (equal) |
| Reverse positive bound | 1,113,070 | **1,086,054** |
| Payload | 93 bits | 93 bits (cap 104) |
| Local paid profile / rank mass | `{1:1323, 2:1342, 3:79, 4:44, 5:102, 6:11, 7:19}` / 5,129 | unchanged |
| Bit saving / kappa | conditional, complex-bound | unchanged, no new kappa |

## Method

The block is treated as an integer-linear straight-line program over its 11
registers. Discovery (`search.py`, deterministic, no randomness) runs a
forward dynamic program over realized-register subsets: each register is
realized once, in some order, from already-realized rows or entry singletons,
each donor used at most once (doubling-free positive-addition class). The
minimum is 30 and the recovered witness achieves it.

Verification (`verify.py`, imports no search code) rechecks the minimum with an
independently written backward Bellman recursion: 2,048 states, 11,264
state/destination pairs, 4,376 feasible edges, minimum 30. It further checks
forward integer-map equality, reverse-map entrywise domination (strict in 20
entries), all 2,048 Boolean input tables, the splice with literally rebuilt
cleanup, identical register frame paths, the unchanged paid profile and rank
mass, the exact F2 endpoint on all 661 columns, the inherited H1-H5 interface
and conclusions via the pinned `xcheck_p.py`, and the exported scalar bills
and positive/payload bounds via the pinned `export_records.py` (forward bound
equal, reverse bound reduced, payload 93 bits). Eight negative controls are
rejected.

This differs from the neighboring block results: PR #844 (block 4) optimizes
within a fixed two-factor split, PR #857 (block 8) searches whole-block
integer factorizations with randomized trials, and PR #843 (frame 509) reuses
one existing sum. The mechanism here is exact whole-block single-write
rescheduling with a certified class minimum. PRs #728/#792 change phase-A
mini-nodes (a different section); they report no improvement at frames 507/508
in their mini-node class, which does not cover this B-section block.

conditional kappa 0.001661634653669567). Only this directory is added;

title: Research audit: quartic precision for balanced dirty cyclic inverses (no new kappa)
body:
PR628's balanced dirty-array inverse uses a valid but conservative **O(p+d+r^5)** precision bound, charging growth across every leaf call. This **mathematical audit** gives a sufficient **O(p+d+r^4)** word-size bound for the **unchanged dispatcher and rounded leaves**, preserving arbitrary initial dirt, exact restoration, call count and storage. **No new κ.**

The improvement comes from complete recursive children restoring their workspace. Their ideal prefixes and inverse prefixes have norms at most `B=(1+K)^E(n)`, where

```text
E(1)=1
E(n)=n+max(floor(n/2)+E(ceil(n/2)), ceil(n/2)+E(floor(n/2))) <= 4n-3.
```

Every ideal interval then has norm at most `B^2`. For N complete leaf calls with error `a*u*(||source||+1)`, variation of constants gives execution error at most **`2*N*B^2*a*u*(B*D+1)`**, provided `N*B^2*a*u<=1/2`. The proof handles nonlinear rounded increments and arbitrary initial data; it does not assume rounded children are linear or their output is independent of dirt.

Using PR628's inherited root-gap and coefficient/phase preparation bounds gives the quartic sufficient guard. All leaf validation, three passes, inverse work, source access, borrowed storage, scalar arithmetic, phase access and routing remain paid. The neighboring-layout bill becomes `soft-O((L*r^2+r^3)*(p+d+r^4))` under the inherited preparation/arithmetic assumptions. Finer incoming grid precision must also be retained.

At **radix 64, p=128, d=20**, the certified fractional-bit budget is **73,245,212**, versus **516,978,511** after already crediting PR663's exact leaf count in the old proof. The same 63 factors still use **4,000 leaves and six dirty arrays**. These are conservative proof budgets, not minimum precision or measured performance. The old bound is tighter at small radices; the README records both.

## Reproduce and evidence

```sh
python3 -B -I research/dirty-prefix-precision/verify.py
python3 -B -I research/dirty-prefix-precision/test_precision.py
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_DIRTY_PREFIX_PRECISION budgets=1740 prefix_traces=18 rounded_generic=48 rounded_kernels=40 controls=10 kappa=unchanged
```

- All n=1..10,000 resource bounds checked; 128 signed words / 191,342 instructions agree with the frozen dispatcher.
- 18 dense integer traces check 11,142 prefix and inverse-prefix boundaries. Separate rational Gauss-Jordan inverses check 66 selected prefixes; 5,104 contiguous subwords are reconstructed directly and agree with their prefix products.
- 1,740 integer budgets cover every prime-power radix from 3 through 512, five target precisions and three magnitude bounds.
- 48 generic and 40 actual kernel executions use the unchanged rounded leaves. All ten pinned kernels are certified. Exact dense comparisons bound every nonzero rounding error; every borrowed array is restored, and every inverse word cancels exactly. All 6,304 observed leaf boundaries satisfy the magnitude bound. Kernel execution plus coefficient perturbation is at most `2^-128`.
- Ten mathematical controls, four focused tests including nonlinear perturbations, and six disposable-package controls passed. A deliberately incorrect inverse-prefix engine is rejected by the separate Gauss-Jordan path.
- Python 3.12.3 and 3.14.4 passed, including isolated optimized execution and a read-only standalone copy with spaces in its path. `make selected-record-check`, syntax, local documentation links and staged whitespace passed.

Only **23 new files under `research/dirty-prefix-precision/`** are added. The full repository suite, selected supplier cold replay, Lean and hosted CI are not claimed passed by these local results.

title: Scoped negative result: PR589's bit word is exactly frame-optimal (no new kappa)
body:
**Scoped negative result; no new κ.** PR589's bit word is **exactly frame-optimal**. Keep its gate sequence, scalar program, start/final frames and COPY frames (decoder constant 63) fixed. Then no reassignment of gate frames, however many gates change at once, raises c = 0.001733427039589844234749. PR555's base word is frame-optimal too. PR589's tuner was greedy and made no optimality claim; this settles the frame-only part of that question exactly.

**Method** (standard library only, about 16 s):
1. **Bounds.** Forward least-frame and backward greatest-frame passes bound every legal frame. Only **159 of 5,472 gates** have any slack.
2. **Components.** Free gates couple only when consecutive on a register, giving **133 independent components** (largest has 5 gates). Each is enumerated exhaustively: 398 assignments, of which 55 fail nesting.
3. **Exact objective.** At z = c the moment is *linear* in the paid profile, so the sign of Σ n_d·d·(64/d)^c decides exactly whether c rises. Every strictly different alternative loses by at least 9.1e−4. Ten alternatives tie on the same profile.

**Positive control:** drop every free gate to its least frame. The optimiser finds 37 improving components and recovers **exactly** PR589's profile `{1:1323,2:1342,3:79,4:44,5:102,6:11,7:19}`.

```sh
bash research/bit589-frame-optimum/verify.sh   # → PASS_BIT589_FRAME_OPTIMUM
```

**Scope**
- Frame-only search class. Transports, Steinberg rewrites and different retained-total frames are outside it.
- C-gate frames are relaxed beyond H4, which only enlarges the search.
- The bit side does not bind κ. The practical conclusion: further bit headroom on this word must come from gate-order or structural moves.
- "No improvement" is proven only within this finite search class.

title: [Lean] Prove reserved-scratch echo bounds and equality family (no new kappa)
body:
PR784's reserved-scratch echo theorem now has a standalone Lean 4.21.0 proof, including exact feasibility, the universal call lower bound, and the whole attaining family. In particular, Lean proves that **50 factors with six reserved dirty arrays need exactly 2,304 uniform leaf calls**. This is a scoped formalization of Alexander Schwartzman's existing theorem, not a new call-count improvement or κ claim.

For the explicit `Fits s n N` grammar, parents reserve `k-1` arrays throughout their children, endpoints run twice, and interior children four times. The new proof establishes:

```text
feasible(n,s) iff 1 <= n <= 2^s
N + 4^s >= 2^(s+1) n
min N = 2^(s+1) n - 4^s for s>=2 and 3*2^(s-2) <= n <= 2^s
```

title: No new κ: BW16 as a unit — window c ≥ 72 puts its ceiling at 0.649× E8's (checked)
body:
**No new κ.** This screens the Barnes–Wall lattice BW16 as a unit, using the screen main already applies to the ADE root systems, K12, Leech and the Niemeier lattices (`research/e8-decoder-floors-and-cold14-notes/ade_screen.py`, #620; #598; #606). BW16 has not been screened before. Its ceiling comes out 35% below E8's.

## Change and mathematical scope

One self-contained package, `research/bw16-unit-screen/`, plus one path-filtered workflow and one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

- **Lattice.** BW16 = RM(1,4) + 2·RM(3,4) + 4ℤ¹⁶ (Construction D). It is rebuilt from code generators. All 4320 minimal vectors are enumerated: the shapes (±2²) and (±1⁸) are proved to be the only norm-8 vectors. They give 2160 lines.
  - Every line has the same \|⟨x, y⟩\| profile: {0: 855, 2: 1024, 4: 280}.
- **Window.**
  - `data/clique72.json` holds 72 pairwise non-orthogonal lines. A deterministic greedy reproduces it exactly.
  - At the decoder pattern of `format-limits` §C.6 (#446 Theorem A), the clique forces B[K, K] = I, so the window is c ≥ 72. For comparison, E8 has c = 9, and its largest non-orthogonal set is exactly 8, which is also checked.
  - The pattern's natural decoder B₀ has F₂ rank 191, so 72 ≤ c_min ≤ 191.
- **Screen.**
  - The screen uses `ade_screen.py`'s proxy x = c·h/v = 8/15 and #595's certified `skel.X`, imported unchanged.
  - Result: X(s, 16, 1, 8/15) ≤ 3.8923·10⁻³ at every s = 3…39. That is 0.649× E8's bit ceiling (6.0005·10⁻³, reproduced) and below the full-E8 ceiling (5.1598·10⁻³).
- **Break-even.** BW16 loses at every s if and only if c ≥ 63. So the conclusion does not depend on finding the largest clique.
- **Cause of the loss.** It is entirely the copy charge. With free copies, X(3, 16, 1, 0) = 1.96·10⁻², more than 3× E8's ceiling.

**Scope.**
- This is a ranking screen of the same kind as main's ADE, Leech and Niemeier screens. It is not a κ bound.
- Only decoders on the §C.6 pattern are covered. k = 1, and helper cost is not priced (#620 §4). BW16 has 855 orthogonal neighbours per line against E8's 63, which points the same way.

**Duplicates.** Checked against main at `f567884a` and against the titles and bodies of every hub PR through #883: none screens BW16. The Gaussian E8 clique ceilings (#738, #770, #868) concern a different unit.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/bw16-unit-screen/bw16_check.py` uses the standard library only. It prints `PASS_BW16_UNIT_SCREEN (21 checks)` in about 2 min 40 s. It passed on Linux aarch64 with Python 3.12.3 and 3.11.16, against main at `f567884a`. CI runs it on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

- DreamingOfClouds: #595's certified ceiling and the `format-limits` decoder-pattern results.
- Joel Pulikkan (GamingPuzzled): #620's unit screen.
- The authors of #446, #598 and #606.
- BW16 and Construction D are classical (Barnes and Wall 1959; Conway and Sloane, *SPLAG*, ch. 4 and 8).
- Prepared by DaysSky with assistance from Claude.

title: [Lean] Prove nonlinear dirty-commutator restoration and ordered products (no new kappa)
body:
**Scoped formalization / independent verification; no new κ.** The nonlinear binary-commutator induction from PR628 and PR663 now has a Lean 4.21.0 proof for an explicit typed recursive evaluator. For every finite binary tree, array width, arbitrary initial dirt, and fixed deterministic nonlinear leaf maps, a complete call restores scratch, has a target-independent increment, and has an exact reverse-word inverse. Under the separate additive-leaf premise, Lean proves the ordered factor product without assuming the factors commute.

This formalizes an existing argument rather than claiming a new commutator, call-count improvement, or precision estimate. The evaluator passes actual intermediate scratch states between children. Its completed-leaf interface assumes source restoration and target-independent increments; the proof does not establish the numerical leaf's own correctness.

The package also supplies bounded source evidence:

- **12 audited formal statements**, using only standard `propext` and/or `Quot.sound`, including a concrete nonlinear dirt-dependence counterexample.
- **130 actual dispatcher traces / 206,830 instructions**, covering n=1..64 and n=83 in both signs. **34 kernel-checked equalities**, with no axiom dependencies, bind complete literal traces at n=1..16 and n=83 to the address compiler. Both 7,744-instruction n=83 words are included.
- **1,170 mutable source execution cases / 3,722,940 leaf calls including inverses**, compared with a functional evaluator and the independent increment recurrence. Widths 1..3 and floor, bounded-square, and noncommuting integer-shear leaves are covered.
- **2,364 additional cases** cover all 197 ordered binary trees through seven leaves with a separate word interpreter. Six proof/trace mutations, three disallowed-axiom inputs, and four alias/depth controls are rejected.

Reproduce with Python 3.12+ and the official Lean 4.21.0 core/Std toolchain:

```sh
python3 -B -I research/lean-nonlinear-commutator/verify.py --lean /path/to/lean-4.21.0/bin/lean
```

Expected: `PASS_NONLINEAR_ECHO: 12 formal statements; 34 kernel trace equalities; 1170 source cases; 2364 tree cases; 13 controls; kappa unchanged`.

The complete receipt matches on Python 3.14.4 and an isolated optimized Python 3.12.3 replay from a read-only standalone copy. Source drift, missing source, integer-to-boolean receipt corruption, and existing-output preservation checks pass. The verifier uses an explicit 64 MiB Lean thread stack for the expanded trace. Source-function identity uses exact extracted text, avoiding Python-version-specific AST debug serialization. Selected-record integrity and staged scope/whitespace checks pass.

Only `research/lean-nonlinear-commutator/` is added. Base `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`; subject PR628 `0768f97d06c623b8211e651543c66135796b62bf`; written audit PR663 `e0e546fd01b396478c68b6b6c5a16d87515983ba`. title: No new κ: covers of E7 by hyperplane flats are exactly the D4-frame triples; near-covers are the A3s (checked)
body:
**No new κ.** Main's cover numbers (`research/format-limits` §D, #595) establish that the 63 readers of a bit source (E7 = t⊥) need three hyperplane sections: two flats cover at most 52 lines, and some three D6 flats cover all 63. This package classifies the covers exactly.

## Change and mathematical scope

One self-contained package, `research/e7-flat-cover-classification/`, plus one path-filtered workflow and one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

1. **The covering triples are exactly the D4 frames through t.**
   - Three hyperplane flats cover E7 if and only if they are E7 ∩ a⊥, E7 ∩ b⊥, E7 ∩ c⊥ for an orthogonal frame {t, a, b, c} spanning a D4.
   - There are 315 such triples, one per D4 through t.
   - The other 3780 orthogonal frames span only 4A1, and their triples miss at least 8 lines.
2. **The near-covers are exactly the A3 subsystems through t.** A near-cover is a triple covering exactly 62 of the 63 lines.
   - Each near-cover is E6(A) + E6(B) + D6(m). Here A and B are the two A2s through t of the A3, and m is the A3's line orthogonal to t, which is the missed line.
   - There are 378 = 63 × 6, and no other type occurs.
3. **The cover count does not force 3 registers per D6 pool.**
   - In a covering triple, each D6 has 16 private lines, which span it.
   - Two rank-5 subflats never cover a whole D6 (at most 28 of 30). But they do cover its 16 private lines (75 pairs per D6), and six rank-5 flats, two per D6, cover all of E7.
   - So "two 5-dim subflats cover ≤ 28 of 30" does not alone give the proposed 180 × 3 = 540 count.

**Consequence for bit skeletons.**
- The D4 skeletons of #493, #510 and #543 read each target through the D6 triple of its 4-frame. By (1), every three-section top layer has this form.
- The only near-alternative is (2), with one line read separately.

**Scope.**
- These are statements about covers by flats, the model of §D. They do not price a skeleton.
- (3) does not construct a 2-per-pool design: frame nesting, the readers' frames and restoration are not modelled.

**Duplicates.**
- Main has the flat census, the best pair and the existence of a D6 cover. It does not classify covers or near-covers.
- #463 has the two-section carrier bound.
- Checked against main at `f567884a` and against the titles and bodies of every hub PR through #883.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/e7-flat-cover-classification/cover_check.py` uses the standard library only.

- **Run.** It prints `PASS_E7_FLAT_COVER_CLASSIFICATION (21 checks)` in about 6 minutes. It passed on Linux aarch64 with Python 3.12.3 and 3.11.16, against main at `f567884a`. CI runs Python 3.11 and 3.14.
- **Exact arithmetic.** Ranks are computed mod 2³¹ − 1. By Hadamard, minors of at most 8 norm-4 rows are at most 256 in absolute value, so these equal the rational ranks.
- **Exhaustive searches.** Every search is exhaustive.
- **Agreement with main.** The checker confirms main's pinned D1 values (8821 flats, the size histogram, the best pair 52, cover number 3) both from its own census and from the text of `d1_cover_numbers.py`.

## Credits and AI disclosure

- DreamingOfClouds: #595's cover-number census and #463's carrier bound.
- eumemic: the D4 skeleton of #493 and #543.
- Prepared by DaysSky with assistance from Claude.

title: Helper minimality (no κ claim): the shipped helper layers of #656 / #799 are minimal for their op multiset
body:
**No κ claim and no word.** Knowledge package `research/helper-minimality/`: frame-side lower bounds for the helper layers of the frontier words, each with its scope and hypotheses, plus a single `verify.sh` that rechecks them. It continues #717 (rows F3-F5 there are the value-side records) and the merged #595.

## What is shown (22 rows: 13 CHECKED, 4 ARGUED, 5 RECORDED)

| Layer | Result | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| S1 scratch | In each of the 11 eight-line blocks of #656, 15 registers are infeasible: whole-bound registers ≥ plane stoppers = 8, perfect matching forced, every whole-bound register (the "never read" ones too) is indispensable; the 38 "twin" couriers are whole-bound registers of this kind (38/38), none equal to its partner (value-forced, B176). CP-SAT (F₃ relaxation, dyadic coefficients, 4-level lemma argued in the card; any horizon) confirms for block (4,5,6,7): dropping 433 is INFEASIBLE. | given the shipped end-of-A frames as bounds (own 24 registers), FOM; true-cap case open |
| S3/S4 copies | No copy pair can be merged by any reordering: 268/268 FAIL on #656 and on #799 (Lawler 1973 backward rule, checked against exhaustive search); every copy already has a two-visit conflict. | FOM; shipped-order partner frames `g` (lower bound for arbitrary reorderings only where value-forced, B172 caveat); rerun skipping the 1921 / 2317 value-zero adds is still 268/268 FAIL on #656 / #799 |
| Bridges, holders | The 12 bridge registers 716..727: 12/12 FAIL; holder/entering copies 450..457 and 484..569: 94/94 FAIL. | #799, FOM |
| Cut | Under H-CUT (justified by the spec lines `03-motifs.tex:78-83` and the emitter line `hpe_emit_local.py:94`, which are checked at the quoted lines), the cut needs ≥ μ ≥ ω = 8 centres; both shipped words attain 8 = rank(F−F₀). | #656, #799 |
| Pre-read | Minimum touched pre-read targets on #799 within the 271-move family is 66 (CP-SAT OPTIMAL, bound 66) against threshold 62. | pairs / recorded triples only |
| Model | The oracle frames equal the AL frames on all 5726 A/B ops of the #656 word (B128). | #656 chain word |

The S1 bound (given the shipped end-of-A frames) and the Lawler bounds (under the `g` hypothesis in the table) are support/frame bounds, so they hold for cancelling programs of the same op multiset too (contrast Boyar–Find 2013); undo/redo ADDs change the multiset and are open.

## Open gaps, stated plainly

1. S1 blocks (0,1,2,3), (0,1,4,5), (0,1,6,7): the Hall bound is slack (21/21 matching with line registers alone); minimality of their 48 scratch registers is unproven, not refuted. B177 is running; no verdict yet.
2. Multiset-changing merges (undo/redo ADDs, holder merges) are outside every Lawler result.
3. S1 minimality is given the shipped end-of-A frames as bounds: the true-cap case (later readers' true caps replace them, as in #717) is open, as is an interface change; H-CUT is not enforced by AL (a centre-free toy is accepted by AL and flagged by the H-CUT check).
4. Decoder n ≥ 9 (#717 D1) is a separate question and not covered.
5. Pre-read is checked to singles, all pairs and recorded triple probes, not arbitrary k-sets.
6. The Lawler layers and the S1 lemma have no independent second-reader audit.

## Verification

`bash research/helper-minimality/verify.sh /fresh/dir` from a fresh `git archive`: 53 PASS lines (2 in step 0), 0 FAIL, exit 0, about 52 s. Step 0 checks every file against `MANIFEST.sha256` and every vendored input against `SOURCES.json` (git blob ids of the #799 / #635 / main files, hashes published by #656 / #799 for the rebuilt words) and stops on any mismatch (tamper test: a changed byte in a word or in a script exits 1 at step 0). `HM_FULL=1` also regenerates the 36,501-pair pre-read table. No absolute paths, no personal names, no κ claim.

Builds on #717 and #595 (DreamingOfClouds); the words and verifier are #656, #659, #664, #799, #741, #685 (jeremykothe2, chafreaky), #645 (icekylinx), #622/#623/#635 (jeremykothe2); related: #698 (thakrarsagar; fixed gate order, exact end-of-B frames, against the order-free bounds here), #719 (rank-two obstruction for the 78 CK cleanup pairs), #705 (littleBro; different model and argument), #687 (cbethin), #683 (Mister-Meeseeks), #869/#870 (jeremykothe2). The Gaussian decay term is unchanged. A written all-path proof and rationally certified Neumann residual counts are included. title: Research: cubic precision for cyclic inverses with arbitrary dirty arrays (no new kappa)
body:
PR628's balanced cyclic inverse can use **cubic sufficient precision with arbitrary dirty arrays**:

```text
max(p, incoming_grid_bits) + O(m + r^3)
```

The dispatcher, rounded leaves, quadratic leaf count and logarithmic number of borrowed arrays are unchanged. No reserved zero bits or clean length-L array are required. **No new κ.**

The new free-algebra induction shows that every ideal prefix and inverse prefix is a sum of ordered products with no repeated factor occurrence. Their coefficient row sum is at most `2*3^ceil(log2 n)`. Applying #862's common-isometry complementary-factor bound to these products, then #877's nonlinear perturbation argument, gives the cubic precision bound. Both source and borrowed arrays still restore exactly; the rounded increment may depend on the initial dirt.

At radix 64, p=128 and initial magnitude at most 2^20, the explicit fractional-bit budget is **1,162,553**, versus **73,245,212** in #877. Both schedules have **4,000 leaves and six dirty arrays**. These are conservative sufficient bounds, not minimum precision or measured performance. Cubic coefficient preparation uses #862's inherited full-inverse estimate; every leaf pass, inverse call, validation, source access, arithmetic and routing charge remains.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.11+:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-cubic-precision/verify.py

title: Research audit: exact carry-grade modulus admission for PR524 (no new kappa)
body:
PR524's mixed-radix carry filter is correct with `T=D`, but a smaller modulus is not safely chosen from active-axis count or by monotone search. This **research audit** gives an exact criterion: attainable internal carry counts are subset sums of the gaps between consecutive non-singleton axes, and a modulus is sound iff no positive attainable count is divisible by it.

For example, `(2,1,1,2)` admits `T=2` but rejects `T=3`. The fixed encoding occupies 19 potential product-coefficient slots at `T=2`, versus 47 at the inherited `T=4`; this is a layout observation, not a runtime or kappa improvement. The proof also shows `T=D` is sharp for all-active boxes and gives explicit delta-input aliases for unsound moduli. Singleton compaction or different weights are outside the negative result.

The standalone package contains the proof, exact admission adapter, an independent floor-based grade oracle, source pins, deterministic receipt, eight mutation/counterexample controls and validation evidence. All additions are under `research/graded-modulus-audit-seed74/`. It also records a separate pinned-source failed assertion for `apply([0], [5], (1,))`, without mislabeling that failure as a counterexample to the convolution identity.

python3 -B research/graded-modulus-audit-seed74/verify.py

title: Tooling: schedule isolated test modules concurrently with identical receipts (3.3-3.9x faster verify-tests, no new kappa)
body:
## Tooling: schedule isolated test modules concurrently with identical receipts

Status: **tooling improvement** (verification engineering, track 85–94, assignment seed 88). No new kappa claim. Prepared with help from opencode.

### What and why

`scripts/run_isolated_tests.py` (run by `make verify-tests`, hence `make verify`) runs every test module in a fresh interpreter to isolate colliding research-package module names. A timing survey of the `make verify` checks at base `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631` found this runner to be the single most expensive check: 298.5 s end to end (and over a 250 s sweep budget), while every other surveyed check was at most 144 s (`scripts/audit_quadratic_affine.py`), most under 10 s. No open PR (surveyed 703) targets the test runner or generic parallelism.

The runner now schedules the same per-module commands concurrently — one isolated interpreter per module; `--workers N` pins the width — and replays each module's captured bytes in sorted module order. The isolation design is unchanged; it is exactly what makes the modules independent and safely concurrent. A test-module audit found no writes outside `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` blocks, so concurrent modules share no mutable state.

### Measured result (same host, same input, 16 logical CPUs, CPython 3.13.15/Windows)

| Run | Modules | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-change runner, base commit, end to end | 87 | 298.5 s |
| Benchmark sequential pass (pre-change schedule) | 88 | 250.6 s |
| Benchmark concurrent pass (16 workers) | 88 | 75.9 s (3.30x) |
| Post-change runner end to end | 88 | 76.7 s (3.9x vs base) |

### Exactness (machine-checked, `research/agent-07-verifeng-seed88/benchmark.py`)

Per-module command is byte-identical to the pre-change one (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <module> -v`, same interpreter/cwd/env); only scheduling changes. Across 88 modules:

- exit codes identical for all 88; the failing-module sets of both schedules are equal (same 15 environmental Windows failures, e.g. `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'resource'`, present identically at base);
- stdout byte-identical for all 88; stderr byte-identical for 87 modulo the wall-clock field `unittest -v` embeds in `Ran N tests in T.TTTs`;
- `test_frontier799_bindings.py` is inherently nondeterministic across any two runs (its failing traceback embeds a machine-random temp path). The benchmark proves this automatically by re-running any mismatched module twice under the same schedule: `scheduling_driven_mismatches` is empty.

No certificate, patch, generator, proof supplement or hash-pinned source file is touched (`run_isolated_tests.py` is not pinned by `certificates/selected-result.json`, `SELECTED-SOURCE.json` or any checkpoint).

### Negative controls

`tests/test_isolated_test_runner.py` runs the real runner end to end in a sandbox: (1) a deliberately failing module must appear in the shared `Failed modules:` summary; (2) a barrier test — three modules each wait (8 s) for three markers, passing only if at least three module processes run concurrently — fails against the pre-change runner with "barrier timeout: test modules did not run concurrently" and passes with `--workers 3` after; (3) default-invocation summary lines and exit codes are unchanged.

### Reproduce

    python3 -B research/agent-07-verifeng-seed88/benchmark.py

Expected final line: `PASS identical exit codes (88 modules); receipts identical for 87 modules modulo the unittest timing field; 1 module(s) inherently nondeterministic across same-mode runs: ['test_frontier799_bindings.py']`

On a Unix host `python3 -B scripts/run_isolated_tests.py` should end `PASS all 88 test modules in isolated interpreters`; on this Windows host it exits 1 with the same 15-module environmental failing set as at base (documented in the package README).

### Scope and remaining obligations

Windows portability of the 15 pre-existing failing modules is out of scope; the claim is exact reproduction of the sequential runner's receipts, exit codes and failing set. Live interleaved output is replaced by sorted per-module replay. Related concurrent tooling on a different target: PR #853 (#741 pinned-stage concurrency) — independent of and not depended on by this change. Base commit, claim record and full evidence are in `research/agent-07-verifeng-seed88/` (README.md, SPRINT-CLAIM.md, evidence/benchmark.json).

title: Research: compose PR922 factory fusions with PR924 rescaling
body:
## Summary

PR922's factory contractions and PR924's coupled rescaling are compatible. Applying them in either order produces the same literal circuit: 32 scalar macros and 73 PR696 primitives per real-component block.

Either standalone contribution costs 77 primitives; their shared PR681 baseline costs 81. Fresh reconstruction and complete primitive replay establish that the savings add up across all fourteen raw-factory windows and inverse cleanups.

Finite construction and scoped exact verification. No new κ; the selected conditional κ remains 0.001661634653669567.

## Exact result

| Construction | Macros/block | PR696 primitives/block | Full forward | Full backward |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 34 | 81 | 123,768 | 123,784 |
| PR922 | 32 | 77 | 123,544 | 123,560 |
| PR924 | 34 | 77 | 123,544 | 123,560 |
| Combined | 32 | 73 | 123,320 | 123,336 |

The combination saves 448 primitives per orientation against baseline, or 224 beyond either PR alone. This is about 5.2% fewer primitives per block and 0.18% fewer across the full raw program compared with either standalone contribution.

The combined circuit retains PR922's 15,456 emitted macros and 319,104 adapter allowance. Its conservative local PR696 bound decreases from PR922's 8,275,750,478,504 to 8,275,750,478,280: another 224.

Helpers, registers, centers, recursive children and paid profile are unchanged. Positive prefix bounds remain PR922's 39,090 / 1,301,331; exact primitive prefix row-l1 maxima remain 124 / 107; fractional depth remains two bits.

These are operation counts and a retained local recount, not runtime measurements or a global invoice replay.

## What is new

The original contributions established their improvements separately and left compatibility untested. This follow-up:

- Reconstructs both pinned witnesses and verifies both application orders.
- Tracks original gate labels so deletions cannot silently shift splice sites.
- Rebuilds baseline, PR922, PR924 and the combination.

title: Research: four grouped cyclic inverse calls with one dirty connector (no new kappa)
body:
Replaces PR628/905's quadratic number of first-order dirty inverse calls with **four higher-order calls and one arbitrary dirty length-L connector**. Data scans use **O(rL)** scalar arithmetic for r-1 root factors. Source and connector restore bit for bit, and the signed inverse word cancels exactly, including when every incoming lowest working bit is nonzero. **No new κ.**

The construction splits the roots into two stable polynomials. Each group uses causal integer lifts, a periodic companion-state closure, a homogeneous correction, and reverse source lifts. A four-call dirty commutator combines the groups; both rounded inner calls have separate error charges because their increments may depend on the initial dirt.

The adjugate resolvent bounds the sum of companion-power norms. Together with #862's common-operator complement bound, this gives cubic data precision. Polynomial coefficients, phase windows, initial gauge, output multipliers and rounded binary powering all have explicit error budgets. The dyadic closure uses classical fraction-free integer elimination, with wider intermediates charged.

For prime-power r>=3, target precision p, incoming grid w and magnitude at most 2^m, let `A=max(p,w)+2m+48r^3`. With exactly supplied rational unit phases of bit size at most B_phi, the neighboring-cycle bill is

```text
soft-O(rL*(A+B_phi) + r^3 log L*(A+log L) + r^4*(A+log L)).
```

Clean scalar workspace is `O(r^3*(A+log L+log r))` bits, in addition to the data arrays. It can exceed a length-L array for short cycles. This trades the prior quadratic data term for a larger scalar preparation term; it is not an unconditional runtime or space improvement. The Python reference is an exact arithmetic verifier, not a measured implementation of the soft-O bound.

Reproduce offline with standard-library Python 3.11+:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/grouped-dirty-cyclic/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/grouped-dirty-cyclic/test_package.py
```

Validation on the final frozen source:

- macOS arm64 / Python 3.11.15 and Linux aarch64 / Python 3.14.8 produced **byte-identical complete mathematical receipts** under isolated optimized execution.
- 160 real, 40 weighted complex, 120 mixed-root and 48 original-kernel cases passed. All ten pinned prime-power fixtures through radix 16 meet the original 128-bit target.
- Repeated roots, zero inside roots, empty groups, both directions, L<k, odd lowest working bits, nonzero preparation rounding, exact restoration and inverse cancellation are exercised against separate dense rational oracles.
- 2,313 budget rows, three written all-size polynomial identities, 16 additional mathematical rejection controls and 36 independent fraction-free solver comparisons passed.
- Each platform passed 11 package rejection controls and a full read-only relocated replay in a path with spaces. Linux also ran the supplied package read-only outside a checkout. All 14 retained files match their pinned Git objects; selected-record consistency and staged whitespace passed.

Full receipts, environment records and logs are in `research/grouped-dirty-cyclic-validation`. They also record the corrected archive sidecars and read-only mutation-fixture issue; both final platform runs were repeated after the harness repair.

Sources are retained byte for byte with SHA256 and Git-object pins: Ali Romman's #621 kernel and uniform inverse proof, Chafik Boukhalfa's #628 lifts and fixtures, #862 complement bound, and #905 arbitrary-dirty cubic baseline. Classical state-space filtering, Mahler/Wiener arguments and Bareiss elimination are credited separately. No priority claim is made for those methods. Related #805 instead supplies determinant-balanced in-place leaves for real coefficients bounded by 1/2, with exact coefficient growth left open; its code is not imported and no savings are combined.

All factors use the same immutable unit-weighted cycle; phase data is distinct from mutable data. This supplies a local classical arithmetic construction. title: Scoped negative result: no relocation or Steinberg rewrite with exact reframing raises PR589's bit c (no new kappa)
body:
**Scoped negative result; no new κ.** PR589's selected R439 bit word cannot be improved by **one commuting relocation followed by an exact optimum over all frame assignments**. The relocation moves a phase-A or phase-B summand or gate within its phase, as an in-place split, or across the scatter. The same holds for **every Steinberg 3→2 rewrite of single-source gates** (PR548's mechanism): there are 659, each one F2-checked, and all are neutral under exact reframing. This settles the gate-order question that open #886 leaves open after proving frame-only optimality at fixed order. Over **891,589 interacting pairs** of relocations, the second enumerated on the word after the first, 685,524 are legal. 663,741 reproduce PR589's exact profile, and the rest have one of 58 distinct profiles, each certified below. None is better.

| outcome (10,886 relocation classes, 1,442,430 insertion indices) | count |
|---|---:|
| no legal frame assignment (least frames exceed a COPY or target hyperplane) | 2,805 |
| optimum = PR589's exact profile | 7,968 |
| optimum strictly worse (17 distinct profiles, each certified with exact rational moment bounds) | 113 |
| **optimum better** | **0** |

## Method

- For each gate order, `reframe.py` computes forward least frames and backward greatest frames. The COPY frames are pinned, so the COPY ranks stay 7×9 and the decoder constant stays 63. Free gates split into independent components, and each component is enumerated exhaustively over **all** closed frames between its bounds, from the catalogue or not.
- C is the literal reverse of the z-destination gates at the full frame (H4); D is unchanged.
- One representative is evaluated per slot. A slot is a run of insertion indices with identical per-register gate sequences.
- At z = c the moment is linear in the profile. Every distinct non-base profile is then certified exactly with the repository's rational moment engine, using the inherited fallback term and PR589's idle remainder.

## Controls

- **Positive control.** On PR555's untuned word, the search finds exactly five improving relocations, including PR589's hoist and sink. The interacting-pair search from the hoist reaches exactly PR589's published profile.
- **Explicit word.** The control word, rebuilt with its optimal frames, passes PR589's exact F2 replay on all 661 columns. It also passes the unchanged `xcheck_p.py` interface audit: H1–H5 and U/J/K/C⁻¹.
- **Independent implementation, no shared code.** It uses frozenset frames, fraction-free integer span tests and explicit D/C. It enumerates every insertion index and groups by any shared register. It reproduces the class count and the outcome of every class with **0 mismatches**. A seed-14 sample of 2,000 interacting pairs, rebuilt by the independent move builder, agrees on every pair.
- **Steinberg detection control.** On a word expanded by one inverse rewrite, the 3→2 search lists the cancelling triple and restores PR589's phase A gate for gate. Both implementations agree on all 659 Steinberg optima.
- **Negative controls.** A non-commuting swap breaks the exact F2 endpoint, and a frame lowered below its forced bound fails nesting.

## Reproduce

Standard library only; no numpy or compiler.

```sh
python3 -B research/bit589-transport-reframe/verify.py /fresh/output/dir
```

Expected (5 min 34 s with `--jobs 10` on a 12-thread Linux machine):

```text
PASS_BIT589_TRANSPORT_REFRAME classes=10886 legal=8081 improving=0 control_rediscovered=2 independent_mismatches=0 certified=17 steinberg=659 pair_sample_agree=2000 no_new_kappa
```

Add `--pairs` for the depth-two replay (30 min 34 s with `--jobs 10`), which ends with `... pair_sample_agree=2000 pairs=685524 no_new_kappa`.

## Scope

- **Covered:** the stated finite class only.
- **Not covered:** longer reorderings, non-interacting pairs, Steinberg rewrites combined with other moves or involving multi-source gates, other op-multiset changes, D/C/COPY/decoder/hosting changes, and other words.
- **Pricing:** PR589's `fastc` identity with the idle remainder held fixed. The C++ hosting pipeline was not rerun; it needs a compiler and Boost, and no new word arises.
- **κ:** the selected #799 assembly is complex-bound (bit 0.0017334 vs complex 0.0016644), so no bit-side result changes κ.
- **Assumptions:** all inherited assumptions remain. This is not a Lean proof.
- **Files:** only `research/bit589-transport-reframe/` is added. The selected record, the PR589 package and `upstream/` are unchanged.

## Provenance

- Base `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`. Merges cleanly with `main` at `91a2094f`; the only intervening commit is an unrelated review-batch freeze.

The new R439 work (#904, #906, #908, #914, #915, #923, #925, #926) consists of native ADD-count constructions, not paid-profile searches. Other relocation or reorder searches concern complex-side objects (#687, #698, #750, #815, #910). None searches gate order or Steinberg rewrites with reframing on the bit word.
