title: Finite complex construction: two-sided Markowitz LPR cleanup refactorization on U8 (-2,580 macros, -37,320 real prims per orientation, seed 30, no new kappa)
body:
## Summary

- **Status:** Construction (`no new kappa`) + scoped negative finding
- **Track & Seed:** `20–39: Complex supplier: improve one specific circuit, frame schedule, decoder, or paid recursive profile` (OS random seed: **`30`**)
- **Base Commit:** `abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf`
- **Selected Frontier Certificate:** `certificates/selected-result.json` ($\kappa = 1661960547713947 / 10^{18} = 0.001661960547713947$, PR #942 on PR #869/#870 and PR #890 / PR #858; **untouched**)
- **Package:** `research/u8-cleanup-markowitz-lpr-seed30/`

### What Changed and Was Learned

In the selected U8 complex supplier word (`native/barch/FULL-WORD.json.gz`, content SHA-256 `090fd574747fbf9628e70cb9beb792732914cfa52e1df147579fe4dbccc68c5a`; `native/local/CANONICAL-WORD.json.gz`, content SHA-256 `24db880b7dab31e6af4eec8a1aba1bbbae29cd50d9a7b77cf0e9b571b3e5ae7c`), the `full_frame_cleanup` section (`canonical['cleanup']`, running at frame `1` = `FULL` on the $490$ `FULL`-ended non-target registers) was synthesized by `cold44x.py` via one-sided (row-only) Gauss-Jordan elimination (`high_inverse = "dyadic_sparse_Gauss_Jordan"`) on $M_{\text{after}} = M_0^{-1}$ in fixed register index order $c = 0, 1, \dots, 727$.

While $M_{\text{after}}$ has $9,430$ off-diagonal nonzeros, the target cleanup operator $M_0 = M_{\text{after}}^{-1} \in GL_{728}(\mathbb{Z}[1/2])$ itself has **only $2,844$ off-diagonal nonzeros**, all with numerators in $\{\pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 3, \pm 4\}$ and denominators in $\{1, 2, 4\}$. One-sided elimination in fixed index order caused severe fill-in ($6,105$ scalar macros, $68,714$ real-component primitives per orientation), coefficient blowup up to $\max |\text{num}| = 131,646$, and a $72$-bit peak prefix $L_1$ coefficient norm (`48299247708521178587951/16`) in the backward orientation.

Replacing one-sided Gauss-Jordan elimination with a **two-sided Markowitz $R^{-1} P L^{-1}$ Schur-complement factorization and Weyl-group signed cycle realization** (`seed = 30`, `trial = 16`, `swap_pen = 6`, `scale_pen = 0`) achieves the following exact improvements across the U8 complex supplier word while preserving all $728$ columns, native frames, paid recursive profile, and residual adapter recipes:

| Metric | Baseline U8 (`dyadic_sparse_Gauss_Jordan`) | Refactored U8 (`two_sided_Markowitz_LPR_Weyl_seed30`) | Exact Change |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `full_frame_cleanup` scalar macros (per orientation) | `6,105` (`6,005 add + 100 scale`) | **`3,525`** (`3,355 add + 170 scale`) | **`-2,580` (`-42.26%`)** |
| `full_frame_cleanup` real primitives (per orientation) | `68,714` | **`31,394`** | **`-37,320` (`-54.31%`)** |
| `full_frame_cleanup` max $\|\text{numerator}\|$ | `131,646` | **`8`** | **`16,455.75x` smaller** |
| `full_frame_cleanup` max denominator | `64` | **`8`** | **`8x` smaller** |
| Total raw scalar operations (`SCALAR-FRAME-AUDIT`) | `19,189` | **`16,609`** | **`-2,580` (`-13.45%`)** |
| Emitted events per orientation (`LOCAL-CHECKS`) | `24,415` | **`21,835`** | **`-2,580` (`-5,160` pair)** |
| Emitted scalar macros per orientation (`LOCAL-CHECKS`) | `19,213` | **`16,633`** | **`-2,580` (`-13.43%`)** |
| Forward real-component primitive bound | `193,306` | **`155,986`** | **`-37,320` (`-19.31%`)** |
| Backward real-component primitive bound | `193,354` | **`156,034`** | **`-37,320` (`-19.30%`)** |
| Forward + backward pair real-component primitives | `386,660` | **`312,020`** | **`-74,640` (`-19.30%`)** |
| Forward `prefix_l1_upper` (`prefix_bits_upper`) | `6812058044968180837/256` (`55` bits) | **`1938756620440273` (`51` bits)** | **`-4` bits (`13.7x` smaller)** |
| Backward `prefix_l1_upper` (`prefix_bits_upper`) | `48299247708521178587951/16` (`72` bits) | **`57316408753392281/4` (`54` bits)** | **`-18` bits (`210,704x` smaller)** |
| Paid recursive child profile (`local_rank_mass = 5634`) | `{1:2548, 2:338, 3:446, 4:162, 5:72, 8:8}` | **`{1:2548, 2:338, 3:446, 4:162, 5:72, 8:8}`** | **Identical (`0` delta)** |
| `RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json` SHA-256 | `8b06181f6983...` | **`8b06181f6983...`** | **Byte-identical** |

### Scoped Negative Finding (Candidate 1)

We also prove and verify (in `PROOF.md` Section 5 and `verify.py`) why reverting $m \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ helpers of the 4-helper group $G = \{659, 661, 662, 663\}$ in U8 from entrance frame $E_5 = [298, 170, 102, 30, 1]$ (dim 5) back to $E_4 = [298, 170, 102, 30]$ (dim 4) to fill T37 rank-1 idle slots fails: the 12 bipartite delivery gates `B[420..431]` into $D_G = \{656, 657, 658, 660\}$ split between $E_4$ and $E_5$, splitting the single rank-4 climb $1 \to 5$ on $D_G$ into $1 \to 4 \to 5$ and producing local profile deltas $\Delta(m=1) = \{1:+2, 2:+1, 3:+3, 4:-3\}$, $\Delta(m=2) = \{1:+2, 2:+2, 3:+4, 4:-4\}$, and $\Delta(m=3) = \{1:-1, 2:+4, 3:+4, 4:-4\}$, strictly worsening the complex moment at $b_{\text{front}}$.

title: Research: local block splitting excludes 49 mixed-rank patterns
body:
Uniform mode 3 permits at most one regular anchor block. This closes all 28 four-exception and all 21 five-exception patterns left open by [research/kappa-nine/MIXED-RANK-TEST.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b084bc5bc7aaa4ee51aba7e3d668ea3da9af4934/research/kappa-nine/MIXED-RANK-TEST.md). These are regularity patterns inside one remainder-mode branch. The seven six-exception patterns, the all-exception pattern, and all 103 complete remainder-mode branch representatives remain open. No new kappa is claimed.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b084bc5bc7aaa4ee51aba7e3d668ea3da9af4934/research/kappa-nine/MIXED-GEOMETRY.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b084bc5bc7aaa4ee51aba7e3d668ea3da9af4934/research/kappa-nine/mixed-geometry-certificate.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b084bc5bc7aaa4ee51aba7e3d668ea3da9af4934/research/kappa-nine/MIXED-GEOMETRY.md).

The new algebraic result is a forced local decomposition on every anchor block: the distinguished Y restrictions for outside points 7 and 8 give complementary idempotents. Their paired A ranks and paired B ranks each sum to 2. Two regular blocks force both paired restrictions on a third block to have rank 2, by Douglas Colkitt (@Mister-Meeseeks)'s existing complementary-block lemma. This contradicts the new rank sum. No covariance, common form, positivity, finite-field inference, or nonlinear solver is used.

The six-file package adds the proof, source pins, a graph-certificate builder, an independent replay, a frozen copy of the experimental selection, and the local scope claim. The exact base is [abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf). A separate live-main note records [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042) at [ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262); the executable experiment keeps its original pins and does not read the mutable selected record.

```sh
python3 -B -O research/kappa-nine/verify_mixed_geometry.py
```

Expected output: 7 local block certificates, 378 sole-common-block edges, 21 excluded regular pairs, 49 newly excluded exception patterns, 8 remaining patterns, 3 rational controls, and 7 rejected mutations. The replay reconstructs the graph without importing the producer's graph helpers. It also checks all 128 exception sets, a full 42-label Y coordinate control, and exact root enclosures for the inherited optimistic cost profile.

Validation completed:

- Saved and rebuilt certificates are byte-identical; optimized replay passes.
- Twelve focused predecessor tests pass.
- Replay passes on the pinned source files from live main, with its live selection file absent.
- The coordinating AI agent independently replayed the certificate and reviewed the algebraic proof and inherited block-inverse obligation. This is not external human review.
- `git diff --check` passes. Repository-wide `make verify`, full supplier replay, hosted CI, and Lean were not run; no supplier or selected result changes.

The historical dimension-15/five-role relaxed profile passes `a=1/511` but fails `a=1/99`. It is not an implemented producer. A bit-only improvement cannot advance the outer grid while either recorded complex endpoint stays fixed. A useful full construction still needs the remaining geometry, extension to 16 points, a compact charged producer, the copied/ordered transfer interfaces, and a complex counterpart.

Credit: Douglas Colkitt (@Mister-Meeseeks)'s original `kappa-nine` work and complementary-block proof; [PR #1066](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1066) by @woklerx at `2e72784a7908d45511e953c182d42cdcb911e6cb` independently corroborates that inherited lemma. This contribution adds the forced local decomposition and 49 exclusions. The final overlap check at 2026-10-13 18:28 UTC found [PR #1066](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1066) unchanged and no competing extension. Ali Romman (@aliromman) prepared this package with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. New work is Apache-2.0.

title: Finite bit construction: compose R439 A/B/star D to 10,652 ADDs
body:
The frozen PR1062 B/star-D word costs 11,500 ADDs. Composing PR980's A preparation and rebuilding literal cleanup reduces it to **10,652**, a fully paid saving of **848** and **13,653 below PR589**. This is a **finite bit-circuit construction, with no new kappa**.

All eight combinations of the frozen A, B and D changes are retained and independently checked. The full composition reduces conservative positive bounds to **F = 15,223 and B = 3,910,388**, giving **92 local / 176 nine-stage bits** within the inherited 104/192 ceilings. D alone implements the right F2 map but requires 193 nine-stage bits and is rejected; either A or B makes that D admissible.

The contribution also closes PR1062's stated missing native check: its exact 11,500-ADD word is one of the eight freshly replayed corners. PR980's headline 872 saving includes 24 B/cleanup ADDs already covered by PR1062, so only 848 are additional; the verifier rejects the double-counted 10,628 invoice.

## Reproduce and evidence

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r439-abc-star-composition/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/r439-abc-star-composition/test_package.py -v
```

C++17 and Boost headers are required for native replay; `BOOST_INCLUDE` and `CXX` support nonstandard installations. Expected marker: `PASS_R439_ABC_STAR_COMPOSITION`.

- All 661 independent dirty input columns, phase maps and complete literal ADD/COPY/ERASE streams, forward and backward, for all eight words.
- Unchanged owning E8/frame checker and fresh native 5/9/11-stage checks: 883/1,327/1,549 physical columns per word; **384 omitted-bridge controls** rejected.
- Every register's ordered MOVE path, paid histogram/rank mass 5,129, nine rank-seven copies and all helper counts preserved. Complete scalar/bridge and precision bills checked separately.
- **17 semantic/accounting controls, 10 package tests and 14 existing selected-record/finite-contract tests** pass. Strict source pins and complete decoded gzip comparison.
- Linux CPython 3.14.4 and isolated optimized 3.12.3 from a relocated read-only tree produce byte-identical complete receipts. GCC 15.2.0 / Boost 1.83.0. The first driver attempt misread the reverse-stage COPY subtotal; the corrected totals are checked in both final replays, without changing a source checker.

## Scope and provenance

Only `research/r439-abc-star-composition/` is added. Base **ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262**; OS assignment seed **13**, bit track. Domain: exactly eight fixed combinations, no new synthesis or search restarts. Twenty-two source/context files have exact Git-object and SHA-256 pins. Pending PR1062 is frozen at **cd016e5dcd5ba28dafa3f3b4eeef003a38e6a11b**. Upstream/source pins were refreshed, and overlap checked through #1120; #1113 concerns a different historical matching neighborhood.

The changed D inherits **false syntactic H2 and literal K_equals_D**. Those original predicates remain intact; semantic D equality is checked separately. Adoption still needs acceptance of that interface, full hosted-supplier emission/audit, complete finite/precision bindings and outer assembly. All-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, hosting, precision/tape, recovery and analytic obligations remain. The paid profile is unchanged. title: Research audit: exact concave-cost reversal across four frozen T16 owner maps
body:
The four T16 owner maps admitted in the PR1047 review improve a particular
certified exponent, but their joint repacks need not improve every concave
cost. This audit reconstructs all 276,480 roles and proves that five of the
six map pairs are incomparable by majorization. Only PR1028 -> PR1031 has
the universal concave ordering.

For the selected PR1031 -> PR1042 change, exact rational bounds show that
`phi_b(r)=73^b*r^(1-b)-r` decreases at b=1/2 but increases at b=3/4. This
concrete reversal bounds the applicability of the inherited greedy exchange
proof; it does not contradict the reviewed selected small-exponent result
or change kappa. The source maps, classical majorization argument and T16
construction are fully credited.

Validation: source-pinned whole-role reconstruction; an independent dense-bin,
sorted-prefix and Fraction-bisection cross-check; eight mathematical checks,
six package rejections and a spaced-path relocation replay. All three
standard-library commands pass under isolated optimized Python. Physical
charts, native semantics, invoices and all-size admission remain upstream
obligations rather than claims of this narrow audit.

Fixed base: ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262, selected PR1042.
Prepared by @woklerx with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

title: Research: exact asynchronous P104 carrier bound across 7,168 decoders
body:
The P104 decoder saves eight COPY ranks, but its nonzero endpoints still need a delivery word. This scoped negative result extends [PR #1071](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1071) from one decoder and a common read order to all 7,168 mixed frame-pair decoders, with independent target orders, extra frame directions, and paid downward moves.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9f7c0679d64bab954b7161d8586dc626a59b92ee/research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9f7c0679d64bab954b7161d8586dc626a59b92ee/research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/CERTIFICATE.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9f7c0679d64bab954b7161d8586dc626a59b92ee/research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/SOURCES.json).

Every decoder has the same cube support family. Exact antichains and chain covers give width 32, or 26 after any one term is removed. The written terminal-read theorem gives

`L >= q + 2 max(0, width(F_K) - P_K)`.

Here `P` counts continuous fixed-term delivery paths, including the eight seeds; `q` counts terms whose survivor line is lost in a frame move; `K` contains the remaining terms; and `L` is excess frame-move rank. Thus `P <= 26` forces at least two extra ranks. The path count is not peak memory, and the chain covers do not construct a legal schedule.

Two exact moment engines show that two extra ranks per call already exceed both the base [PR #942](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/942)/T37 and refreshed [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042)/T16 budgets, even at price one per rank. This implication requires the remaining paid moment to retain or exceed the corresponding [PR #968](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968) P104 knob profile. The proof does not establish that cost premise for every new word. Term mixing, different COPY endpoints, larger path banks, and savings elsewhere remain open. No new kappa or physical supplier is claimed.

Only [research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/9f7c0679d64bab954b7161d8586dc626a59b92ee/research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound) is added. The exact base is [abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf). Source hashes, the refreshed selected record, proof, nine exact certificates, failed attempts, and the execution receipt are included. The selected frontier and [upstream/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/9f7c0679d64bab954b7161d8586dc626a59b92ee/upstream) are unchanged.

Validation:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/independent.py
```

Both pass. The separate checker constructs the roots and all 896 by eight dual partitions without importing the primary checker or [PR #968](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968). The primary check also proves that the reflection orbit equals the complete 2,025-frame set. Seven controls, an optimized relocated run, an actual changed-source rejection, and the base selected-record check pass. Full supplier replay, repository-wide regeneration, hosted CI, and Lean were not run.

Credit [PR #717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717) and [PR #968](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968) for the decoder model and family, [PR #1071](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1071) for the delivery question, [PR #1077](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1077) for the distinct coefficient-field floor, and the [PR #942](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/942), [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042) and bit supplier lineages. The final overlap scan covered open PRs through [PR #1120](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1120); [PR #1099](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1099) accelerates the earlier enumeration and does not duplicate this scheduling theorem. See [NOTICE.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9f7c0679d64bab954b7161d8586dc626a59b92ee/research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/NOTICE.md) for attribution and [SOURCES.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9f7c0679d64bab954b7161d8586dc626a59b92ee/research/p104-asynchronous-carrier-bound/SOURCES.json) for pins. title: Research: exact 3->2 z-program rewrites of the PR589 word, 24,305 -> 23,495 ADDs (no new kappa)
body:
Status: **finite bit construction / research note (no new kappa)**. Assignment seed 13, bit-supplier track. Base commit `abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf`. Prepared with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance, disclosed per CONTRIBUTING.md).

## What this is

405 exact single-edge triangle (Steinberg 3->2) rewrites of the **z-program** of the selected PR589 word (`research/e8-bit-p111-tuned/tune/bitE8mut-p111-tuned.json.gz`, DreamingOfClouds on eumemic's PR555): the A/B z-destination gates and their literal-reverse cleanup mirrors. One forward source edge is deleted per rewrite and two kept edges swap order; the rebuilt cleanup loses its mirror edge.

| complete local quantity | base | candidate | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| complete exported ADDs | 24,305 | 23,495 | **-810** |
| exported records | 27,234 | 26,424 | -810 |
| MOVEs / COPYs / ERASEs | 2,911 / 9 / 9 | unchanged | 0 |
| 661 register frame paths | reference | identical | unchanged |
| paid profile | reference | identical | unchanged |
| z-program product U (550x550 over F2) | reference | identical | unchanged |
| F2 endpoint, all 661 basis columns | pass | pass | unchanged |
| kappa | unchanged | unchanged | **no new kappa** |

Every accepted rewrite is gated on an exact replay of the F2 endpoint on all 661 columns, identical frame paths and an identical paid profile, so the frozen hosting and the whole pricing chain carry over exactly as in the prior phase-B block packages. This is a finite scalar circuit-size result only.

## Method and coverage

- The identity is exact over F2: `[b += x] [b += a] [a += x] == [a += x] [b += a]` (and the mirror order). A candidate is accepted only when every gate strictly between the three edges commutes with all three at the register level, so no observable intermediate state moves.
- Complete base census: 2,606 distinct triangles / 2,613 instances in the z-stream; 293 base instances have a fully commuting window. Greedy application in deterministic order to a fixed point: 7 rounds, 405 accepted, **zero endpoint rejections** (rounds 2-7 unlock new instances as windows open). Stopping rule: a full rescan with zero accepted rewrites. The greedy order is not an optimum over orders.
- Paired-transvection control class exhausted: only 17 duplicate edges exist in the whole z-program and every pair is dependency-blocked.
- Structural note: `rank(U - I) = 539` over F2 (`rank(U_A - I) = 439`), so any forward program and any exact cleanup need at least 539 transvections each against 2,224 each after these rewrites. The literal-reverse cleanup is not claimed optimal; that gap is recorded as headroom, not closed here.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r439-z3to2-seed13/verify.py
```

Expected (standard library only, CPython 3.11+):

```text
PASS_R439_Z3TO2 moves=405 ADDs=24305->23495 records=27234->26424 columns=661 paths=661 profile=identical U=identical controls=6/6 exporter=ok no_new_kappa
```

`verify.py` imports no search code: it re-applies the witness moves from the pinned base word (canonical SHA-256 `5642fd0e...eba0b`), re-checks each move's three-register identity and window commutation at its application state, compares the rebuilt word with the committed candidate (canonical SHA-256 `8aedb3be...539a`), replays base and candidate independently on all 661 columns, compares U, all frame paths and the paid profile, recomputes the full ADD/MOVE/COPY/ERASE invoice and cross-checks it against the repository exporter `export_records.py` run on both words, rejects six tamper controls (source corruption, deleted cleanup gate, truncated cleanup, tampered move list, non-commuting swap without cleanup rebuild, truncated dirt gate), and compares the summary with `CERTIFICATE.json` byte for byte. `search.py` regenerates the witness deterministically (same fixed point, byte-identical outputs).

## Scope

Finite replays of one word in one rewrite class; not an optimality proof and not a Lean multiplication theorem. H1-H5 of the interface lemma hold literally (D untouched, scatter unchanged, C the literal reverse at the full frame, V = I). Native 5/9/11-stage C++/Boost checkers were **not** run here (no such toolchain in this environment); this is an exact finite word-level certificate in the sense of PR1040/1047's semantic candidates, not a native hosted supplier admission. No new kappa and no new bit headroom (the profile is exactly unchanged and the bit side does not bind).

## Credit and positioning

Predecessors (not superseded): PR589/PR555 (the word), PR541/PR548 (Dugongue's transvection move families) and PR589's tuner, which optimizes the *moment* to a fixed point and records that its Steinberg step has "nothing to apply that lowers the moment"; equal-moment rewrites are outside its greedy objective, and this package's delta is the ADD-count objective with exact commutation windows. The phase-B block programs (PR873/973/986/1001/1002/989/980, `r439-bsection-survey`, `r439-frame524-seed13`, concurrent #1015/#1045/#1062) are orthogonal regions measured against the same base word; results are not additive across PRs. PR #933 and #1048 close *moment/reframing* classes; this package's rewrites keep the paid profile exactly identical, so they neither raise bit c nor contradict those claims. Concurrent #1122 (same track and a coincidentally identical assignment seed, different agent) composes the frozen PR980/PR1062 changes on the semantic-D word lineage (11,500 -> 10,652 ADDs there); its object, word and mechanism are different, its results are not additive to this one, and the 3->2 rewrites here are candidates for that lineage as future work. See `research/r439-z3to2-seed13/NOTICE.md` and `CLAIM.md` (local sprint claim; no pinned coordination issue exists).

title: Research: two-sided boundary obstruction for R439 width-seven helpers
body:
The selected [PR #589](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/589) word cannot obtain a width-seven helper by replacing cleanup C alone. An exact inverse-row certificate requires rank eight for all 439 helpers after B. A second necessary condition tracks every register that carries the helper's dirty input. At the earlier cut after D/A/scatter, the two conditions require rank eight for 433 helpers and leave six explicit rank-seven candidates.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/df29b159239b79d7e451d6ddda826a73e0e50a67/research/bit-width-seven-boundary/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/df29b159239b79d7e451d6ddda826a73e0e50a67/research/bit-width-seven-boundary/CERTIFICATE.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/df29b159239b79d7e451d6ddda826a73e0e50a67/research/bit-width-seven-boundary/SOURCES.json).

This is a **scoped negative result, with no new kappa**. It tests the physical boundary that is missing from [PR #1023](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1023)'s hypothetical width-seven hosting gains. The proof permits arbitrary finite reversible linear suffixes, arbitrary rational frames, target access, extra restored dirty registers, and simultaneous helper endpoint changes. Frames must move monotonically, all scalar operations must use a common frame, and the suffix cannot add a COPY or another transport operation. The six early-cut survivors are necessary-condition survivors, not constructions.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001674097969905390: an attaining T37 construction and fixed R480 owner optimum
body:
The seven-slot k8 R480 word has an exact owner optimum across all positive replica counts. This package proves that bound and gives a physical 37-replica construction that attains it, with conditional **κ = 0.001674097969905390**. It changes only the owner assignment and its finite admission. The local word, bit supplier, and selected-result pointers are unchanged.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a007dc2e1cc7ae7e8f7ec1343e8883fe43259f21/research/r480-owner-optimum/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a007dc2e1cc7ae7e8f7ec1343e8883fe43259f21/research/r480-owner-optimum/CERTIFICATE.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a007dc2e1cc7ae7e8f7ec1343e8883fe43259f21/research/r480-owner-optimum/SOURCES.json).

The signed bin inequality covers all 1,163 whole-helper patterns. Two exact rational engines certify its moment support over the complete root interval `[0.001676905273619680861300, 0.001676905273619680861301]`. Equality forces a multiple of 37 replicas. An integer pattern-flow certificate expands into 159,840 literal roles in 333 complete calls. The independent audit reconstructs source-event windows, 73-axis charts, and disjoint pending children on each physical family.

The full finite invoice charges 1024 complex prefix bits: the actual bound is 775. Its physical row coefficient is 17,495, below 20,161. The complete deficit stays 320 per replica; the gain changes the child-rank distribution. The complete native/bit composition passes all 47 outer inequalities. This is the maximum grid value for the fixed word, capacity inventory, and outer recipe. A changed local word or another assembly recipe lies outside that ceiling.

Reproduce from this branch with a new output directory:

```sh
python3 -B research/r480-owner-optimum/check.py --work /tmp/r480-owner-check
```

PASS_R480_ALL_REPLICA_OPTIMUM_AND_ATTAINING_CONSTRUCTION 0.00167409796990539

[evidence/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a007dc2e1cc7ae7e8f7ec1343e8883fe43259f21/research/r480-owner-optimum/evidence) contains the exact receipts. `git diff --check` passed. title: Research consolidation: rational support descent for fixed-reader single lifts (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For a rational matrix X, every complex fixed-reader single lift has a rational representative with identical support pairs in all rank-one terms. This extends @woklerx's #998 reciprocal-projection argument from complex-to-real descent to every infinite base field. The proof uses a linear functional on a finite span, avoiding finitely many polynomial roots. A 1 by 1 F4-to-F2 counterexample identifies a genuine boundary of the statement.

The P112 consequence is equality of the attainable ordered nine-term support-cost vectors over Q, R and C. Mihir Srivastava's #845 floor 64 remains inherited. There is no new kappa, physical supplier, coefficient-height bound, terminating rational search, or efficiency-preserving compiler claim. The proof allows arbitrary complex inputs, while the exact implementation demonstrates inputs with supplied quadratic-field coordinates. This differs from #998's already-effective Gaussian rational examples and #1098's Gram spectra.

Nine new files live only in `research/rational-lift-descent-seed95/`. Credit: @woklerx for reciprocal support transfer, @mihir-s-05 for the real obstruction, DreamingOfClouds for P112 geometry and the copy interpretation, and GamingPuzzled / Joel Pulikkan for the coordinate cost. title: Scoped obstruction: P111 query transport exceeds the frozen U8 host budget
body:
The P111 decoder's smaller local COPY cost does not by itself pay for delivery
of its changed query from the existing U8 gather rows. This adds a scoped
negative result for a query inserted after U8 section A, with the old rows,
later frame contracts, and helper widths fixed, and with no mixing between
new carriers before the query hyperplane.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ed5424aa3b6ca32fd5bb2c33a8e6afcd87170160/research/shared-carrier-host/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ed5424aa3b6ca32fd5bb2c33a8e6afcd87170160/research/shared-carrier-host/RESULT.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ed5424aa3b6ca32fd5bb2c33a8e6afcd87170160/research/shared-carrier-host/SOURCES.json).

For all 112 punctures, exact rational elimination gives a unique expression
in the eligible old rows. Their required frames are pairwise incomparable and
cannot advance inside the query hyperplane while preserving the old tail.
The minimum transport profiles are `10 H5 + 6 H6`, `8 H5 + 10 H6`, or `26 H6`.

A favorable complete moment bound gives free entrance frames, no separate
centre charge, free compensation and interface work, and pooled fractional
rank-48 idle space. It credits each puncture's actual source and target paths,
plus the `H8 -> H7` COPY saving. Every case still exceeds one at historical
[PR #942](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/942) b; the minimum is enclosed by
`1.00000864736369386816835926810620863001514` and
`1.00000864736369386816835926935824150131476`.
A linear volume argument covers every positive replica count and mixtures of
punctures. This fixed-U8 class also fails at the larger b selected by
[PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042) at the recorded refresh. The proof does not apply to [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042)'s word.

raw U8 from the pinned [PR #799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799) archive and U8 recipe. It checks all root/label
pairings, frame paths, unique row expressions, antichains, actual data-path
credits, and rational cost intervals. It compares power intervals against the
retained independent engine. Controls cover wrong query coefficients,

`090fd574747fbf9628e70cb9beb792732914cfa52e1df147579fe4dbccc68c5a`.
Only [research/shared-carrier-host/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/ed5424aa3b6ca32fd5bb2c33a8e6afcd87170160/research/shared-carrier-host) is added. The selected frontier and
[upstream/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/ed5424aa3b6ca32fd5bb2c33a8e6afcd87170160/upstream) stay unchanged. This is a scoped negative result, not a new kappa
or a complete multiplication theorem. Changed A/B words, early mixing,

title: Research: exact restoration contracts and resource bounds for rounded borrowing
body:
[PR #1057](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1057) proves exact restoration with three dirty arrays when every child is additive. The rounded leaves from [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) and the precision proof in [PR #1054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1054) do not supply that contract. This package identifies the actual borrowed boundary and proves its necessary and sufficient translation condition.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract/VALIDATION.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract/SOURCES.json).

The result is a scoped obstruction and resource tradeoff. It makes no new kappa claim.

- An exact additive wrapper on the same arbitrary fine grid has integer slope. It cannot approximate the valid [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) map `x -> 4x/3` with error below `1/3` on the physical interval `[-1,1]`, even with more guard bits or unlimited restored workspace. Restricted source grids and different output grids are explicit escapes.
- For componentwise nearest rounding of `Pz/q`, the safe translations are exactly `Ph=0 mod q`. A correction that cannot reread the old helper needs one saved state per quotient class. For a coprime scalar on L entries this gives `q^L` states when the admitted source and displacement ranges contain a complete residue domain. Smaller finite domains can need fewer states. Readable current data and displacement can recover the old helper without a saved summary; the proof accounts for that escape at the actual borrowing boundary.
- A nonzero additive result from fixed signed offset averaging needs at least q variable calls. The matching q-call construction returns the q-scaled integer map. A separate exact integer lift pays for denominator growth, initialized low bits, all local operations, source access, and inverse calls. It is a comparison construction, not a fast rounded supplier.

The written proof is supported by deterministic exact checks: 716 reduced scalar ratios, 3,495,180 residue responses, all 700 normalized functions on cyclic groups of orders 2 through 5 at the emitted child boundary, six matrix quotients, 380 pinned rounded leaf executions, 22 finite exact lifts, and nine mathematical controls. A read-only relocated replay under optimized Python passes. Three real subprocess controls reject a changed pinned source, a discarded residue, and an occupied output file.

Reproduce from the repository root with the Python standard library:

```sh
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 python3 -I -B research/rounded-borrowing-contract/test_package.py
```

Expected final markers:

```text
PASS_ROUNDED_BORROWING_CONTRACT ratios=716 responses=3495180 rounded_leaves=380 exact_lifts=22 controls=9
PASS_ROUNDED_BORROWING_PACKAGE controls=3 relocation=1
```

The selected-record check and all 25 selected unit tests passed on the exact experiment base. Full `make verify`, the selected cold replay, remote CI, and a physical tape compiler were not run. This change only adds the isolated research package. Finite replay is not a formal proof of the full multiplication theorem.

Experiment base: [abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf). Source pins: [PR #1057](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1057) [78a062df1dcab2bffea5ff4d8243f3da6e465414](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/78a062df1dcab2bffea5ff4d8243f3da6e465414); [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) [da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70); [PR #1054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1054) [6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a). The package freezes exact source and context bytes. During the work, main [ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262) selected [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042) at conditional `kappa=1672188119205421/10^18`; this package does not alter that selection or any supplier call moment.

The proof, failed approaches, finite domains, overlap checks, and validation receipt are in [research/rounded-borrowing-contract/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract). title: Research: two-block native-query encoding theorem and paid boundary obstructions
body:
[PR #840](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/840) gives a centered DATA shear with three ordinary children, but leaves its conversion to the ordinary BIT supplier boundary open. This contribution proves that one fused block cannot realize any positive number of whole ordinary-interchange rows under an arbitrary binary linear encoding and its inverse, with restored dirty helpers. It then proves that exactly two such blocks suffice algebraically for three genuine rows over every odd prime-power modulus m>=11. The latter result uses explicit complementary square-zero factors; it is not a search claim.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e6a8003673d55929be6925b22f9ee645d03c33c3/research/native-query-boundary/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e6a8003673d55929be6925b22f9ee645d03c33c3/research/native-query-boundary/CERTIFICATE.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e6a8003673d55929be6925b22f9ee645d03c33c3/research/native-query-boundary/SOURCES.json).

The proof counts the complete six-field native orbits, including short prime-power orbits and every spectator. It also gives an orbit-quotient charge for added adapters and treats different entry/exit frames separately. A literal two-block construction for one genuine row plus two restored dirty rows is compiled and checked on all 2,187 independent VALUE columns, then lifted to two spectator fibers and checked on all 4,374 columns. Its six full-volume children fail the recurrence even with free encoders. That failure applies only to this one-genuine-row construction.

For three genuine rows, the six children each have volume V/3 and width N/3, so the child-only coefficient is two. The full cost still includes affine streams, XOR scans, encoder generation/storage, every bit transfer, routing, head returns and child restoration. The supplied scan-per-bit encoder emission has a proved superlinear volume cost. A cheap uniform encoder, arbitrary-width layout and recursive hosting remain open. This is an enabling algebraic proof with scoped obstructions and an exact finite boundary construction; it is not an admitted supplier, a new kappa, or a formal proof of the full multiplication theorem.

Base: [abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf). [PR #840](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/840) is pinned at [da2cd0dd2229e08b61b174a8835a2c2bb99d2230](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/da2cd0dd2229e08b61b174a8835a2c2bb99d2230); [PR #521](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/521), [PR #677](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/677) and [PR #990](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/990) pins, copied sources and notices are in [research/native-query-boundary/SOURCES.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e6a8003673d55929be6925b22f9ee645d03c33c3/research/native-query-boundary/SOURCES.json). Main was rechecked at [ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262), which selects [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042). The selected BIT exponent is unchanged and the complex side still binds. Neither the selected record nor [upstream/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/e6a8003673d55929be6925b22f9ee645d03c33c3/upstream) is changed.

Validation:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/native-query-boundary/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/native-query-boundary/check_package.py
```

The first command reports `PASS_NATIVE_QUERY_BOUNDARY full_addresses=665444 prime_power_cases=13 dirty_columns=2187 escape_children=6 no_new_kappa`. The package check passes relocation and rejects changed source bytes, changed source identity, a false child volume and Boolean/integer substitution. The mathematical replay rejects missing children, XORs, decoder transfers, helper corruption and a lost spectator fiber. Nine large-domain direct-sum templates are checked; no full m=11 encoder matrix is allocated. The base selected-record gate and staged diff check also pass. The full repository `make verify` and selected cold replay were not run for this isolated package; the validation note states that limit.

The local claim records the three candidate approaches and the reason for each pivot. No pinned coordination issue exists at the final check. Recent open-PR metadata through [PR #1125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1125) and the predecessor heads were refreshed; no matching native-boundary result appeared in the inspected scope. Predecessor credit is retained for Karl Appel (@applecrusher), @commdata2338, Wentao Li (@VictorLiwentao), Sagar Thakrar (@thakrarsagar), the upstream framework and selected suppliers. Contributed by Ali Romman (@aliromman) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, mathematics, implementation, verification and writing. No independent human review is claimed.

title: Tooling: fast exact HPE transport audit for the layer-end controls, 2.53x, 480/480 trials cross-checked (seed 93, no new kappa)
body:
**Status: tooling improvement (verification engineering). No new κ. No check is changed, removed or weakened; the selected result is unchanged.**

- **Track and seed:** track 85–94 (verification engineering), assignment seed **93** from the OS CSPRNG (Python `secrets`).
- **Base commit:** `ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262`.
- **Adds:** this directory and two Makefile targets. No existing file is modified.

## What is slow

In the selected #1042 replay, the `chain` stage takes 711 s. Of that, 530 s is spent in its five layer-end control steps (`lec-p6n`, `lec-promo`, `lec-jx`, `lec-hyb`, `lec-frames`).

Each step runs the pinned `layer_end_controls_leaver.py`. That script calls PR635's `hpe_audit_and_transport.run` (sha256 `c9a05ff2…0aa3`) about 96 times: once on the honest word, then on each of 95 mutants, every one of which must be rejected at its pinned reason.

The cost is in exact arithmetic. On one audit, profiling shows:

| Share | Where |
|---|---|
| ~63% | `Fraction` operations in the row updates (endpoint replay in both orientations, plus the P and P⁻¹ state maps) |
| ~22% | `copy.deepcopy` of gates |

## What changes

`hpe_audit_fast.py` is the pinned file with four local changes. Its control flow, every assertion, every message and every output are kept.

1. **Integer rows.** Each scalar row is stored as integer numerators over one positive row denominator, instead of a dict of `Fraction`s.
   - Each gate coefficient is still built as `Fraction(a, b)`, in the same order as before. So the `assert target != source`, `assert q` and any `ZeroDivisionError` or `TypeError` are raised exactly as in the pinned file.
   - Zero entries are never stored. That makes every truth test (`if x`, `P[g].get(h)`) and every zero-pattern unchanged.
   - Rows are reduced by their content gcd only when a denominator exceeds 128 bits.
   - The dirty-compensation table is still built from normalized `Fraction`s, sorted as before.
   - The endpoint equality is evaluated entry by entry against the pinned expected `Fraction` matrix.
2. **Structural copies.** Gates are copied structurally instead of with `deepcopy`, and nested lists are never shared. Any shape other than a list of JSON scalars and integer lists falls back to `deepcopy`.
3. **Memoized frame bases.** `basis()` is memoized for tuples of integers, which is a pure function. Any other input takes the original uncached path.
4. **Shared coefficients.** `Fraction(a, b)` objects are shared for pairs of integers with b ≠ 0. They are immutable, so sharing cannot change any value.

### How it is used

`shim/hpe_audit_and_transport.py` stands in for the module. The **unchanged** controls script picks it up when `PR635_CODE` points at `shim/`, which is what `run_lec.py` sets.

`run_lec.py` repeats the chain's invocation exactly: same portable wrapper, routing word, reason-pin file and environment. It hash-pins the controls script, the wrapper, the routing word, both pin files and the reference audit. It has three modes:

- **`reference`:** the pinned audit, unchanged.
- **`fast`:** the fast audit only.
- **`crosscheck`:** every trial word is audited by **both** implementations. Any difference in outcome raises `RuntimeError`: exception type and arguments, output bytes, receipt without `seconds`, or printed output. It never raises `AssertionError`, so no `trial()` can absorb the mismatch. The reference result is what is returned, and each outcome is logged.

This is opt-in. Nothing in `make frontier1042-verify` changes. It composes with #1059, which parallelises the calls without changing the audit. This package makes each call cheaper.

## Evidence

All measurements were taken on one machine (macOS arm64, Python 3.12.3), with the same inputs, extracted from the committed `selected-replay.tar.gz`.

| Step | Reference | Fast | Speedup | Cross-check (96 trials) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `lec-p6n` | 75.2 s | 30.3 s | 2.48× | identical (99.9 s) |
| `lec-promo` | 76.2 s | 30.3 s | 2.51× | identical (101.0 s) |
| `lec-jx` | 76.0 s | 29.9 s | 2.54× | identical (99.9 s) |
| `lec-hyb` | 75.4 s | 29.7 s | 2.54× | identical (99.5 s) |
| `lec-frames` | 76.4 s | 29.8 s | 2.56× | identical (101.1 s) |
| **total** | **379.2 s** | **150.0 s** | **2.53×** | **480/480 identical** |

Each `crosscheck` row means:

- all trial words gave identical outcomes and identical outputs under both audits;
- the resulting `COLD-END-CONTROLS.json` is byte-identical to the `reference` run's;
- it equals the maintainer's archived receipt for that step, apart from the word path.

**Differential fuzz** (`verify.py`):

- The five honest words give byte-identical canonical and full words, receipts and printed output.
- The recorded run `FUZZ-300-SEED93.json` has 300 mutants with seed 93, and all 300 are identical under both audits. Their outcomes:

  | Outcome | Count |
  |---|---:|
  | rejected at the arbitrary-dirt endpoint | 168 |
  | accepted (the audit passes) | 53 |
  | rejected because the compensation reads an entering helper | 27 |
  | rejected because the precondition or compensation touches a cold helper | 23 |
  | `TypeError` from a non-integer coefficient | 12 |
  | rejected as `nonmonotone` | 10 |
  | empty `assert q` | 6 |
  | other | 1 |

  The total time was 135.0 s for the reference and 44.9 s for the fast audit.

The mutations are:

- coefficient changes, including non-dyadic values;
- edge values: 0, 3⁶⁰, −5⁵⁰, 2³⁰⁰, `'x'`, 1.5 and `None`. These exercise `ZeroDivisionError`, `TypeError`, the empty `assert q` and the 128-bit normalization;
- gate drops, swaps and duplicates;
- register changes;
- frame-vector bit flips.

**Unit tests:**

- 300 random gate programs give integer rows equal to the pinned `Fraction` rows;
- zero entries are dropped;
- `apply` raises the same errors on bad gates as the reference;
- copies never share nested lists;
- a deliberately wrong fast audit makes `crosscheck` raise `RuntimeError` (control).

## Reproduce

```sh
make hpe-audit-fast-verify            # about 1-2 min: 5 honest words, 40 seeded mutants, 7 unit tests
make hpe-audit-fast-crosscheck-lec    # about 2 min: all 96 lec-p6n trials under both audits
```

The first target prints:

```
PASS_HPE_AUDIT_FAST_EQUIVALENCE | honest 5/5 identical | fuzz 40 seed 93 identical | reference …s fast …s
```

Any single step can also be run directly:

```sh
python3 -B research/hpe-audit-fast-seed93/run_lec.py --archived hyb --pins LEC-REASON-PINS-STACK --out /tmp/x/lec-hyb --mode fast
```

For `lec-frames`, pass `--pins LEC-REASON-PINS`.

## Scope

- **What the evidence is.** Equivalence is shown by:
  - a line-by-line argument (the changes are local, and they preserve values, zero patterns and exception order);
  - finite differential evidence: every trial of the five selected steps, plus a seeded fuzz.

  It is not a formal proof of equivalence for every possible input. That is why `crosscheck` exists: anyone who wants the pinned semantics on new words can run both audits.
- **What it does not change.** No pinned file, reason pin, receipt or selected record is changed.
- **About the timings.** They describe one machine. They are not measurements of multiplication performance.

## Credit

- **Audited code:** `hpe_audit_and_transport.py` was prepared for icekylinx with GPT-6 Astra assistance. It was adapted from icekylinx's PR425/433, DreamingOfClouds' PR484 `audit_gk.py` and Round19's transport, and shipped in PR635. Its Apache-2.0 header is kept in the derived file.
- **Controls:** the layer-end controls are DreamingOfClouds' and LayerReviewer's. The leaver variant and its not-applicable handling come from LeaverSAT and Q6Reviewer, in Jeremy Kothe's #1004/#1005 chain.
- **Related work:** #1059 (thakrarsagar) parallelises the T37 layer-end controls; this package is complementary to it.
- **Precedents:** #367 applied the same `Fraction`-to-integer technique to PR364's frame verifier, and #824 to the stage-pair audit. Neither touches this audit.

Prepared by Wronskode (@Wronskode) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. New material is Apache-2.0.

title: Independent verification: exact dirt and label-span atlas for all leaver cell relabelings
body:

title: Research: sharp ten-coordinate threshold for doubly degenerate triple shared nodes
body:
PR920 gives an eight-dimensional shared-frame bound for general norm-one
labels and a ten-dimensional positive example for triples. This contribution
proves that the two-coordinate gap is necessary when both endpoint pairs
are degenerate: signed scalar rank one plus disjoint binary spans forces
the source and target triples onto disjoint five-coordinate supports.

The all-dimension classification gives the exact count
`225*C(h,5)*C(h-5,5)` with source/target sides distinguished, and a legal
dimension-four frame for every rectangle in the class. The existing PR920
positive fixtures and characteristic-vector argument are explicitly credited.
This is not an E8 puncture census, a new supplier, or a kappa improvement.

Validation: canonical bit-mask census h5..12; independent complete labeled
set/Fraction census h5..10 covering 6,930 source pairs and 615,060 eligible
rectangles; all 15 sharp canonical h10 frames with 60 explicit orthonormal
residual bases; ten semantic checks; six package rejections and spaced-path
relocation. All three commands pass with isolated optimized Python.

The theorem is scoped to one scalar-shared node, triple labels, two
degenerate endpoint pairs, and the historical orthonormal-residual interface.
It does not supply a physical word, paid invoice, global DAG labeling or
selected construction change. Fixed base ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262.

title: Research: sharp k8 factory register bound and target frame barriers (no new kappa)
body:
The retained k8 source-factory interface needs at least 224 helpers in addition to its 112 sources. This proof permits arbitrary rational scalar gates, cancellation, undo and redo, gate reordering, and operations between blocks. It does not fix the operation multiset. The 192 required values have 168 incomparable support frames; first formation requires two distinct registers at each frame. All 14 packet programs are executed to check the matching 224-helper upper witness, and all 192 values are bound to the actual final seven-slot word.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/8e2e18b93d8c6b302e540ad5edc767cb98cf1514/research/k8-frame-antichain/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/8e2e18b93d8c6b302e540ad5edc767cb98cf1514/research/k8-frame-antichain/CERTIFICATE.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/8e2e18b93d8c6b302e540ad5edc767cb98cf1514/research/k8-frame-antichain/SOURCES.json).

The package also proves that none of the 112 target end frames can contain any of the eight complete cold-block frames or any of the eight complete center frames. Exact replay shows why scalar restoration is insufficient: all 32 cold helpers can be restored after A on all 704 arbitrary input columns, but their frames still prevent whole-block target borrowing. A complete two-cap split calculation requires six or eight carriers. A four-cap, four-carrier algebraic witness shows the limit of that split result. A separate cost screen covers only descent between local formation jobs with the remaining invoice fixed.

This is a scoped negative result. It does not prove the full 480-helper word optimal, does not bound a fixed-count paid profile, and does not supply a new kappa. Target dirt, formation and restoration of mixed-cap carriers, new private queries, and changed interfaces remain open. No source guard was weakened.

Reproduce offline with Python 3.10+ and the standard library:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/k8-frame-antichain/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/k8-frame-antichain/independent.py
```

Both pass. The independent checker imports no primary code; it checks 112 scalar columns, all 192 value witnesses, 168 antichain frames, 112 split ranks by integer determinants, and 1,792 cap pairs. Five mathematical controls, normal and optimized relocation, an actual word corruption, a missing-certificate-value control, and whitespace checks pass. The separate unchanged seven-slot native rebuild passed all 2,896 exact phase edges. Its commands, pins, and limits are recorded. title: Add a reversible quadratic phase stream with linear scalar work
body:
[PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038) evaluates Machin and Taylor series at every data site. This package
replaces that phase interface with two reversible dyadic phase states.
It uses a fixed second difference, bounded three-shear rotations, and
`Q=W+2 bit_length(L+1)+20` state bits. Every pass reconstructs its phase
state backward. Seed and chart coefficients clear exactly. No phase
array or checkpoint list is stored.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/VALIDATION.md) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/SOURCE.json).

The proof gives a uniform quadratic drift bound and the same emitted
coefficient accuracy as [PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038). The retained dirty wrappers therefore
keep their large-target error bound, exact source and borrowed-array
restoration, original precision, and two-data-tape movement bill. One
prepared phase object serves all four passes of a complete dirty word.
Its stream uses `60L+6` real products and `24L` chart divisions. Exact
seed preparation and erasure add `O(P)` scalar operations on wider
rational operands, where `P=Q+24`.

Status: enabling construction. The elementary phase bit bound is
`O((A+V)^2+P S^2+L T^2)`, where `A` is the original numerator width,
`V` is the modulus width, `S=16(P+V+1)^2`, and `T` covers stream and
data widths. A direct reversible arithmetic compiler needs
`O((A+V)^2+S^2+T^2)` clean scratch bits. The Python reference implements
the scalar state and exact series cleanup; it does not emit a native
bit-gate program. No new kappa is claimed.

The base is [abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf). [PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038) is pinned
at [99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9); nine retained files have
Git-blob and SHA256 pins. No moving selected-result file is source-pinned.
[PR #1054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1054) and [PR #1025](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1025) are scope references, not combined theorems. The
inherited logarithmic borrowed-array pool stays fixed. Supplier hosting,
factor production, multi-axis composition, and outer assembly stay open.

Verification:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/test_package.py
```

The main receipt covers 98 phase cases, 1,474 rational interval samples,
16 dirty words, three same-input work comparisons, and seven input or
lifecycle controls. It executes and reverses all 16,384 steps of the
long case. The package check rejects seven semantic faults and source
corruption, then replays the full receipt from read-only relocated files.
It returned 0 in 245.149 seconds. The parent agent also completed the
optimized main replay. These checks are finite evidence for the written
proof, not independent human review or formal multiplication verification.

Timing results are mixed. Three alternating same-input trials give
[PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038)/new median seconds of `0.042217/0.191425` at `(L,W)=(32,16)`,
`0.689942/1.286691` at `(257,48)`, and `10.187936/9.092779` at
`(2048,96)`. New seed erasure is included. Seed operands reach 55,767
bits in the last case. All final trials and an earlier run's medians
are disclosed. The shared-host timings do not establish a general
speedup. The result is the proved interface and its separate work bill.

[NOTICE.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/NOTICE.md) preserves predecessor credit and discloses substantial OpenAI
Codex assistance. New material is by Ali Romman (@aliromman) under Apache-2.0.

title: Scoped negative result: scratch-free CK/JP8 boundaries need extra primitives
body:
The historical CK/JP8 2+3-cycle boundary costs eight real-component primitives with one temporary register. Removing that register cannot tie the price when the circuit may use exactly the five moved coordinates—even allowing arbitrary mixed dyadic intermediate rows. The scratch-free minimum is between nine and ten; the nine-versus-ten question remains open.

This is a **scoped negative result**, with no new kappa or supplier substitution. The complete census binds all 168 PR971 boundaries. The restricted scratch-free boundary invoice is at least 238 versus 224 primitives per real component, or at least 28 extra real primitives per orientation.

- Complete radius-four F3 balls: 509,157 states. Separate Python row-table and C++ bit-packed implementations agree on every state and shortest distance. The exact dyadic-to-F3 reduction makes the empty five-dimensional intersection a length-eight exclusion.
- Rational witnesses establish exact costs four and six for the two-/three-cycle cases and a ten-operation upper bound for the combined case. All 37 single-primitive omissions fail.
- Ten test groups pass on CPython 3.14.6 and 3.9.6, including source/receipt corruption and minimal offline relocation. Full receipt regeneration, source pins, selected-record check and five selected-result tests pass after rebase.

Reproduce with Python 3.9+ and a C++17 compiler:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/complex-scratch-free-boundaries/verify.py
```

Research base: `ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262`; refreshed submission base: `ce7ad1b6ab09452c3478723a2e96ed5ff212dc08`. All seven historical source inputs are unchanged. Upstream now selects PR1094; this patch does not edit selection or `upstream/`.

Credit ToikY/Eva Ayala #971, woklerx #1095, Sagar Thakrar #696, Chafik Boukhalfa #626, Jeremy Kothe #622 and the retained lineage. body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This proposes the conditional finite witness **κ = 0.001675560947524449**. Joint entrance choices replace eight local rank-one recursive children with four rank-two children while preserving the helper-width inventory. An exact within-call permutation therefore transfers the preceding T16 packing without another owner search.

The final local word uses demoted entrance groups **603, 611, and 635**, with local profile `{1:2364,2:498,3:412,4:130,5:82,8:8}`. It improves the preceding three-demotion witness, 0.001675121647789207, by **0.0262249453%**. Scalar operations, coefficients, and order are unchanged. The T16 assignment hosts **69,120 whole-helper roles in 144 calls**.

**Start review at `research/k8-joint-entrances/README.md`, `PROOF.md`, `CLAIM.json`, and `verify.py`.** The branch also includes its four additive predecessor packages: `k8-coordinated-owners`, `k8-eight-ends`, `k8-eight-ends-t16`, and `k8-three-demotions`. These retain the construction chain, eight rank-seven endpoints, source pins, unchanged admission engines, and intermediate evidence.

The new exact fixed-word, fixed-inventory all-replica grid upper bound is **0.001675568675201533**. It is an upper relaxation, not an achieved construction or a bound on other circuits, mixed suppliers, or recursion geometries.

The unchanged PR589 bit supplier, PR559 recurrence correction, and bit bad-residue surcharge remain. All-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, analytic-transfer, and bit H1–H5 assumptions remain. This is not an unconditional multiplication theorem or full Lean certification. The selected repository certificate is unchanged.

## Validation

The final package passed:

- Fresh native exact forward and dual replay of all **704 columns**, with **2,904 directed phase checks**.
- **27 new local semantic controls**.
- Unchanged admission engines: **69 assembly, 12 bit-supplier, 15 controller, and six independent T16 negative controls**; **47 strict outer inequalities**.
- Complete portable wrapper: `PASS_JOINT_ENTRANCES_COMPLETE_ADMISSION 0.001675560947524449`. Its explicit parent/native reuse uses completed fresh replays, with all consumed parent files and semantic identities rechecked, followed by local controls and full global admission.
- Two exact arithmetic engines for the fixed-family ceiling, with independent enumeration of all **1,163 bin patterns**.
- Source and manifest bindings, Python compilation, and whitespace checks. All **82 pinned source files shared with upstream main at `ce7ad1b6`** are unchanged; the remaining pinned files are predecessor packages added on this branch.

Fresh reproduction (Python 3.11+, C++ compiler, Boost; choose a new output directory outside the repository):

```sh
CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH=/path/to/boost python -B research/k8-joint-entrances/verify.py \
  --base "$BASE" --work /absolute/new/output-directory
```

`BASE` is the original R480 k8 + seven-slot word pinned in `research/k8-eight-ends/RECIPE.json`. No optimization solver runs during verification. Reproduction details and explicit replay-reuse options are in the README.

All **18 repository `make verify` groups completed across the initial and resumed runs**, including all **87 isolated test modules** and **20 patch applicability checks**. This was not one successful `make verify` invocation: the initial system-Python attempt stopped on missing `int.bit_count`, and the Python 3.11 run later stopped because Apple clang rejects `-fopenmp`. The failed and remaining stages then passed under Python 3.11.14 and GCC 16.2.0 (continuation exit 0). No guards, tests, or tracked upstream sources were changed. `evidence/REPOSITORY-VERIFICATION.json` and three archived logs record the complete coverage and both environment failures; this regression result is separate from the package-specific witness admission above.

The search covers all **64 subsets** of six individually selected entrance reductions, followed by **354 same-dimension rotation trials**, a joint fixed-dimension entrance/frame search over **68 helpers**, and a joint dimension-four/five plus aggregate-packing search over **56 helpers**. The latter searches found no further improvement. Another 145 trials removed one-dimensional entrances individually, by point cohort, or all together, again without improvement. Solver output is nomination data, not an exact optimality certificate. A broader formulation over 192 entrances and 1.8 million LP variables returned no solution before its numerical solve limit; it is recorded as inconclusive, not infeasible, and yields no stronger κ.

title: Tooling: opt-in parallel layer-end controls for the frontier1042 leaver chain, byte-identical receipts, 3.1x (extends #1059, no new kappa)
body:
**Tooling (verification engineering). No new κ, no change to any pinned file, and no check is weakened. Extends merged #1059 to the leaver variant of the frontier1042 chain.**

## What

A cold `make frontier1094-verify` (the selected verifier) runs `verify_frontier1042.py` as its `baseline1042-cold` stage. The recorded frontier1042 run took 1162 s, and **530 s of that are the chain's five layer-end-control steps** (`lec-p6n`, `lec-promo`, `lec-jx`, `lec-hyb`, `lec-frames`). Each step runs the Q6Reviewer-signed `layer_end_controls_leaver.py` v2 (`4ba676f1…`) through the pinned `run_portable.py` (`322d29d4…`). That script audits the unmutated word and 95 mutants with PR635's `hpe_audit_and_transport.run` (`c9a05ff2…`), one audit after another.

`research/frontier1042-lec-parallel/` adds an opt-in, drop-in parallel runner for these steps. Merged #1059's runner is hardcoded to the T37 variant `layers_p6n/layer_end_controls.py` (`fc58c569…`), so it cannot run these steps. This runner accepts both variants by digest, and checks the T37 one against the archived T37 receipt as well. Scripts are accepted by digest, so the 3 + 10 byte-identical copies on main are covered, as are the `4ba676f1` copies in open #1104 (`d8982686`) and #1107 (`6123fc5d`).

## How

The pinned launcher, the scripts and PR635's audit are run unedited, after a digest check.

1. **Record.** The pinned script runs once with a stand-in audit module that only records each trial word's exact bytes. That pass decides nothing, and its receipt is discarded.
2. **Evaluate.** The real audit evaluates every distinct word in a spawn pool, keyed by the sha256 of the exact bytes plus the routing path.
3. **Replay.** The pinned script runs again. Its own assertions see the real outcomes and the captured audit output for the identical bytes, and it writes the receipt. The trial sequence must match the recorded one.

`chain_lec.py` runs the five steps as `reproduce_leaver_chain.py`'s `lec()` does, sharing one outcome table. The k8 X4 exchange is the identity, so `lec-jx` re-audits exactly `lec-promo`'s words and audits nothing new. Before each step it binds the word to the chain's recipe pins. After each step it applies `lec()`'s `CHAIN-PINS-k8` checks: the pins-file digest, PASS status, 95 rejected controls and the not-applicable sites.

## Evidence (`verify.py`; the serial bullet needs `--serial`)

- **Archived receipts.** All five receipts equal the maintainer receipts in `community-frontier1042-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz` byte for byte. Only the recorded input path (`word`) is rewritten, and it must occur exactly once. The T37 receipt is checked the same way against `t37-replay.tar.gz`.
- **Pinned serial reference** (`--serial`). All six receipts are byte-identical to the pinned serial steps on the same paths. The logs are identical except for the audit's own wall-clock `"seconds"` value.
- **Controls.** No control leaves a receipt.
  - C1: a corrupted unmutated word fails at the script's own first assertion.
  - C2: a forged acceptance of one mutant fails with `cold-end mutation accepted`.
  - C3: a forged reason fails with `rejected for the wrong reason`.
  - C4: a one-byte change to the script or to the audit is refused before any work.
- **Unit tests (7).** They cover the placeholder, the pins, the recipe pin set and the jx == promo identity. They also check that `run_pinned` restores global state, that the portable gzip header reaches the trial words, that the routing key keeps a symlink's own suffix, that a killed worker fails the wait, and that the real audit accepts the word and rejects a corruption.

## Benchmark

macOS arm64, 10 cores, Python 3.14.8, `--jobs 10`, on a shared machine. The raw receipt from the committed code is `BENCHMARK-macos-arm64.json`. These numbers are descriptive only.

| | Recorded serial | Pinned serial | Parallel |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| five frontier1042 steps | 529.5 s | 314.3 s | **100.2 s (3.1×)** |
| T37 variant | 77.0 s | 81.2 s | **26.2 s (3.1×)** |

Two earlier runs of the same algorithm, before the review fixes, gave 266.7 → 97.1 s and 293.5 → 143.6 s. The remaining cost is the pinned script's own mutant construction, which by design runs twice: once in the record pass and once in the replay.

## Scope and honesty notes

- **Opt-in, not wired.** `reproduce_leaver_chain.py` and `verify_frontier1042.py` are manifest-pinned and unchanged. In `lec()`, wiring would mean running `lec_parallel.py WORD ROUTING OUT` instead of the launcher plus script. That is the maintainers' call.
- **Who benefits.** No pending claim reruns these steps, because claims reuse the k8 chain. The steps run when the chain is rebuilt, for a batch's shared candidate replay and for the selected replay, and in cold `frontier1042-verify` runs.
- **Phases steps.** The verifier's three `phases` steps (cells, chain and slots stages; 469 s) call the same pinned `phases_full.py` that merged #1041's runner accepts. This PR does not re-measure them.
- **No Makefile targets.** `research/community-batch1099-audit` pins the Makefile by exact digest, so an append would fail `scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py`. That check passes on this branch.
- **#1059 (merged).** It is a separate package, so #1059's pinned files and receipts stay untouched.
- **#1137 (Wronskode, open, head `e3b8fa39`) targets the same five steps differently.** It is a faster exact re-implementation of the audit, cross-checked against the pinned one, with 2.53× on a single process. This PR keeps PR635's pinned audit **unchanged** and spends cores instead. The two compose partly. Here the audits mostly overlap the record pass, with 0.8–2.2 s of wait per audited step. A faster audit would remove that wait and reduce CPU contention, but not the floor, which is the pinned script's own mutant construction and runs twice.
- **Recorded replay.** The recorded frontier1094 replay (58 s) reused the completed frontier1042 baseline. These steps run on cold verifies and on chain rebuilds.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/frontier1042-lec-parallel/verify.py --work NEW_DIR            # ~3 min
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s research/frontier1042-lec-parallel -p test_package.py
python3 -B research/frontier1042-lec-parallel/verify.py --work NEW_DIR --serial   # + pinned serial (~9 min)
```

The expected last line of `verify.py` is `PASS_FRONTIER1042_LEC_PARALLEL`. It needs standard-library Python 3.11+ and no network.

## Assignment, credit and disclosure

- **Assignment.** Track 85–94 (verification engineering), seed 89 (OS CSPRNG). Base `ce7ad1b6`.
- **Selection.** Six read-only scout subagents and three judges compared candidates: the T37 audit fast copy, emit, stage DAG, mid-size stages, cold #799, and a repo-wide sweep. A three-lens recheck against the new main then chose this one, and two adversarial review subagents checked the package. Their fixes are in the second commit.
- **Credit.**
  - Q6Reviewer: the signed layer-end scripts.
  - DreamingOfClouds: the original controls.
  - PR635's authors: the audit.
  - LeaverSAT and LeaverSAT2: the k8 cells and recipes.
  - ColdWitness: the chain driver.
  - icekylinx: gauge44.
  - Jeremy Kothe, Rohan Arun and Hao Yan: frontier1042.
  - Douglas Colkitt, with OpenAI Codex: maintainer orchestration and the archives.
  - Prior concurrency tooling: #853, #921 (navinor), #1101 (rcfc-jreed), #1041 and #1059.
  - Wronskode: #1137, the concurrent fast-audit approach.
- **AI disclosure.** Prepared by Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. New material is Apache-2.0.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001674340686401949: rank-seven helper ends with T37 owner packing
body:
Conditional **κ = 0.001674340686401949** (`1674340686401949/10^18`). This improves the currently selected #1094 result `0.001672660197076918` and the submitted #1121 value `0.001672965558289236` at the comparison snapshot. It improves our #1131 construction and the concurrent #1129 construction, both at `0.001674097969905390`.

The PR combines Jeremy Kothe's unchanged #1107 rank-seven-end seven-slot k8 supplier with a new 333-call order and an exact integer-flow construction of 159,840 whole-helper owners. The constructor expands the frozen flow through deterministic bipartite matching, without an owner optimizer. The idle profile is `{1:5424,48:11320}`; the independent owner checker and emitted-controller invoice agree. The charged prefix reserve is 1,024 bits (actual 775), and the row coefficient is 17,495 < 20,161.

title: Finite construction: PR1042 R480 sign normalization saves 408 primitives per orientation (no new kappa)
body:
On the frozen PR1042 R480 seven-slot word, Ross Richardson's retained sign compiler reduces the complete PR696 scalar comparison by **408 real-component primitives per orientation**: **149002 -> 148594** forward and **149018 -> 148610** backward. **Status: finite complex-supplier circuit construction. No new kappa.**

This adds only `research/selected-k8-sign-seed38/`. Both orientations, all 4,332 same-frame runs and all 713 arbitrary input columns are covered. A fresh basis at every run checks dirty-input boundary equality. Copies, clears, source-access order, shifts, per-register prefix envelopes and the complete paid profile remain unchanged. All final sign restorations are priced. A copy-fanout control demonstrates that the method can increase cost outside these pinned programs; no circuit-optimality claim is made.

Reproduce offline with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/selected-k8-sign-seed38/check.py
python3 -I -O -B research/selected-k8-sign-seed38/test_package.py
```

Separate Fraction and integer-dyadic implementations reproduce every receipt field and both full primitive streams. Validation includes 116 actual-run omissions/sign faults, four additional mathematical controls, 10,000 arithmetic differential steps, optimized minimal offline relocation, archive/source/receipt corruption, and rejection of both archived ancestors. `make selected-record-check`, 25 selected-record regressions and the whitespace check pass on Linux / CPython 3.12.3.

Exact base: **ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262**. OS assignment seed **38**, complex-supplier track. The selected result at that base is PR1042, kappa 0.001672188119205421. Source archive: `research/community-frontier1042-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz`, SHA256 `22c3f4dce4b897a1d423d1388801933e288b6a6b1906cb15e1b16a5eb68db754`. Source pins bind four repository inputs, five named archive members and the frozen selection. Upstream advanced to PR1094; all four input pins still match the refreshed main tree. No transport to later words is claimed.

Credit **Ross Richardson / PR919** for the method and retained compiler; **Sagar Thakrar / PR696** for the lowering; and **Jeremy Kothe, Rohan Arun, Hao Yan, Chafik Boukhalfa, icekylinx, DreamingOfClouds, eumemic** and the retained construction lineage. The overlap refresh through PR1152 found distinct commuting-ADD work in PR1143 and capsule closure in PR1142. **woklerx / PR1132** exposed the retained R492 evidence trap during final inspection; the input was corrected to the actual `slots/local/` R480 archive members before any submission. Native Clifford/frame execution, production integration, whole-call hosting, the global invoice and outer assembly were not rerun.
