title: Conditional kappa = 0.001673260706543984: adaptive joint kernel demotion on PR1117
body:
## Result

Conditional **kappa = 0.001673260706543984**, compared with the frozen [PR1117](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1117) claim **0.001672846995880185** at `342b67f23dfa8f41a520a0d58978b2875e9eb0dd`.

The absolute gain is **0.000000413710663799**, approximately **0.02473093 percent** relative. This is a concrete combined kernel-and-owner improvement under the inherited conditional interfaces. It is not an unconditional multiplication theorem or a claim that the full open-proposal queue has been accepted.

Only `research/adaptive-kernel-demotion/` is added. The selected certificate, upstream sources and existing submissions are unchanged.

## Mechanism: choose the kernel prefix to fit the actual pending stock

PR1117 supplies the rank-seven end word and its T16 owner schedule. PR1111 supplies a four-helper entrance-demotion recipe. Applying one fixed provider everywhere ignores the actual pending capacities. This package constructs and checks five joint local prefixes and chooses the prefix separately at every literal call:

1. Groups are ordered **635, 603, 611, 619, 627**. Their helper indices are respectively `(411,413,414,415)`, `(379,381,382,383)`, `(387,389,390,391)`, `(395,397,398,399)`, and `(403,405,406,407)`.
2. Prefix `k` changes exactly `4k` helper widths from four to five. The complete local profile change is `k * (-8H1 + 8H2 + 4H3 - 4H4)`, verified by recounting each actual joint word, rather than assuming recipe gains add.
3. Within a call, selected helper occurrences eligible to use their own slack remain in place. The remaining selected occurrences exchange owners bijectively with distinct width-four donor occurrences. Every extra width consumes an actual unused axis; all shared owner remainders are updated before the next insertion.
4. Every insertion uses a gap pattern `[1,1,1,r]`, with `r` equal to one, two or three. The resulting complete local-plus-remainder differences are respectively `-12H1+8H2+4H3-4H4`, `-10H1+7H2+4H3-4H4`, and `-11H1+9H2+3H3-4H4`. The written proof establishes strict moment improvement for every `0 < b < 1`.
5. Before these insertions, one legal three-owner cycle replaces two rank-six remainders by rank one and rank eleven: `+H1 - 2H6 + H11`. This preserves all literal helper occurrences and has a strict concavity saving for every `0 < b < 1`.

The realized assignment contains **359 group demotions across 103 of 144 calls**: 356 four-unit patterns, one `[1,1,1,2]` pattern and two `[1,1,1,3]` patterns. Prefixes zero through five occur **41, 24, 8, 15, 6 and 50 times**. These counts come from the final table and dispatch; no advertised kappa gains are added together.

## Complete paid profile and exact pricing

```text
{1:344363, 2:65097, 3:62855, 4:19012, 5:11808,
 7:8, 8:1152, 11:2, 48:4873}
```

Live stock remains **14,336**, paid rank mass **1,041,408**, and deficit **5,120**. The final map has **6,034 paid idle remainders**, 1,433 fewer than PR1117, and **9,898 actual 73-column chart types**, compared with 10,057. The complete literal difference contains **4,594 owner records**; unchanged rows are retained exactly.

Both retained exact rational moment engines certify the native and conservative endpoints. The complete outer assembly checks **all 47 strict inequalities**. The bit supplier remains the pinned inherited supplier; the complex side binds. Finite work, adapters, restoration and the six-provider dispatch are retained in the invoice instead of being treated as free.

## Reproduction and checked scope

Python 3.10+ and its standard library, from the repository root, using a fresh output directory outside this package:

```sh
python -I -B research/adaptive-kernel-demotion/verify.py --out ../adaptive-result
```

The delivered verifier binds the complete source inventory and checks:

- Every actual joint prefix on all **704 arbitrary input columns**, including dirty helpers, in forward and inverse-transpose orientations; native emitted words and **25 corruption controls per provider**.
- The changed phase edges and wrappers for each prefix. These are fresh checks of the changed local constructions, not a cold reconstruction of every unchanged ancestral phase.
- Every one of the **69,120 literal roles**, all 144 calls, their actual provider widths, independent source-derived inactivity windows, physical family uniqueness, chronological coordinate blocks and actual orthogonal 73-column charts.
- A complete remainder/profile recount, all nine finite invoice guards, exact native/conservative and inherited-bit moment brackets, and all 47 strict outer inequalities. Negative controls and source/manifest binding remain explicit.

The changed local constructions, adaptive dispatch and new owner map are concretely checked. The all-size/compiler, common-label and mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting interface, precision/tape and exact-recovery, analytic-transfer and inherited bit-contract assumptions remain conditional. No complete ancestral cold replay, new Lean certificate, hosted CI pass, independent human review or global packing optimum is claimed.

## Mathematical sources and future reuse

The package notes and source ledger in `research/adaptive-kernel-demotion/README.md` record two distinct OpenAI-proof mechanisms investigated by each of the four workers, including their exact source statements and their actual contribution or limitation. In the owner construction, alternating matching-layer switches provide the cycle replacement, and a disjoint first-hit projector partition supplies the canonical self-donor/external-donor separation. The other worker ledgers explain the local transfer, inventory, dispatch and arithmetic adaptations.

These are explicitly sourced adaptations. They are not eight independently additive exponent improvements or new priority claims for the underlying mathematics. The reusable contribution is the checked sufficient coupling: actual joint provider prefixes plus literal donor assignments and a uniform saving proof. The notes retain the one-group fallback, bounded allocation comparisons and routes that were not assigned numerical gains.

## Credit and disclosure

Direct construction inputs: **PR1117** (rank-seven ends and frozen T16 owners), **PR1111** (entrance demotion), and **PR1030** (the demotion/lowering context). Local and schedule ancestry: **PR1018/987** (seven slots), **PR1005/1004** (mutable-leaver cells), **PR1022/858** (T16 and whole-family owner scheduling), together with **PR869, PR799, PR741, PR685 and PR645**. **PR635** and its retained notices record the ported cold-end, frame, native compiler and source lineage; **PR589** supplies the inherited bit endpoint.

**PR1063/1094** provide neutral recolouring and owner-exchange context, and **PR1072** supplies the related promotion-to-gap construction. Their numerical gains are not copied or added to this result. Original author attribution, AI disclosures and the Apache-2.0 license are preserved in the vendored notices.

The new adaptive construction, proofs, independent checks and packaging were prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No name or email of the submitting user is added by this package, and the assistant did not publish or push anything.

The final self-contained replay passed from the delivered source inventory. It additionally rejects optimized Python and mutated source bytes before running the mathematical checks. The manual browser-upload batch contains 73 files (approximately 7.7 MB), with SHA-256 identity to that inventory.

title: Research note: restoration coalescing across a recursion batch (read-free + composable-family boundary; no new kappa)
body:
## Status: research note (scoped mechanism + complete cost recurrence; no new kappa)

Track **recursive-interfaces** (50-59), assignment seed **53** (OS CSPRNG). One
explicit way to eliminate boundary/restoration work with a complete cost
recurrence, a sufficient correctness condition (with the exact defect criterion
behind it), and a sharp cost boundary. Contributor:
**Navinor (Aaron Wang)**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

### What is learned

A recursion node that restores its borrowed dirty workspace after **every** child
pays `r` restoration passes. This note prices one operator-level rewrite: let the
workspace drift across the batch and replace the `r` restorations by the **one**
composed restoration `(G_r...G_1)^{-1}` at the node exit. Two independent
questions decide it, both decidable exactly:

- **Correctness (vanishing defect; read-free is sufficient, not necessary).**
  The single deferred restoration returns the same observables (final data and
  final workspace) exactly when the summed defect vanishes,
  `sum_i B_i (G_{i-1}...G_1 - I) = 0`. Read-free batches make every term vanish
  separately and are sufficient, but they are **not necessary**: nonzero readers
  can cancel (exact counterexamples:
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1199,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1203,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1205). The certificate's
  reader example shows only that one reader child *can* break deferral; a second
  case replays the exact nonzero-reader cancellation (5 restorations -> 1).
- **Cost (composable family; density is not application cost).** The rewrite
  removes passes only when the restoration operators stay cheap under
  composition: unit phases -> one phase pass, permutations -> one routing pass
  (`r -> 1`). A **heterogeneous** mix (phase + Walsh + permutation) composes to
  a dense product that *retains its cheap factorization*: applying the factors
  sequentially costs the eager sum (`16` = `16` multiplications at `N = 8`,
  verified against the exact dense product). Deferred application costs *more*
  only when no cheap factorization is retained and the dense product must be
  applied directly (`64` vs `16` multiplications at `N = 8` — a statement about
  direct dense application). Structure, not the count alone, decides.

### Reproduce

Standard library only, Python 3.10+ (verified on 3.12 and 3.13), from the repo root:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/restoration-coalescing/verify.py
```

Expected first line:

```
PASS_RESTORATION_COALESCING phase=3->1(x3) perm=3->1 hetero_dense=True reader_diverges=True reader_cancels_5to1=True hetero_mults=eager16|factorized16|dense64
```

The checker recomputes the certificate and compares every field with
`research/restoration-coalescing/CERTIFICATE.json`, failing on drift. It builds
every operator explicitly at `N = 8` over exact Gaussian rationals (no floating
point, no random tolerance, no imported supplier verifier), derives each composed
restoration from the exact dense product, and self-checks any cheap structured
application against that product on the standard basis before trusting its cost.

### Base commit and pins

- Base: `ce7ad1b6ab09452c3478723a2e96ed5ff212dc08` (current `origin/main`).
- Branch: `research/agent-13-recursive-seed53` (isolated research
  package under `research/restoration-coalescing/`; no generator, `upstream/`, or
  selected-construction file touched).
- Selected result at base unchanged: `kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000`
  (CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1094 on CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1087).
- Exact source/dependency pins and file digests: `research/restoration-coalescing/SOURCE-PINS.json`.

### Relationship to concurrent work

This is a second, independent treatment of the restoration question with a
meaningfully different method (exact operator algebra and structure detection,
standalone sub-second, versus assembly-level pricing on frozen payloads). It does
**not** claim priority on "restoration deferral" and does not reproduce others'
numbers.

- [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1012)
  (thakrarsagar, same track) prices restoration deferral of U8 helper rank/frame
  climbs at the hosted T37 assembly level and finds it mass-neutral. Different
  layer and cost unit (rank mass vs. phase/routing passes); complementary, not a
  contradiction.
- [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#974](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/974)
  (avirazza, same track) prices the same boundary classes with zero parent cost.

Where those notes give the assembly-level ceiling effect, this note gives the

title: Tooling: exact opt-in 2.3x acceleration of the transport audit behind the control suites (no new kappa)
body:
**Status: tooling improvement (verification engineering). No new κ. No mathematical check is changed, skipped or weakened, and no pinned file or orchestrator is edited.**

Track 85–94, OS-random seed **87**. Base: current main `ce7ad1b6`. The work started on `29218749`, and every pinned input is unchanged between the two. Only `research/fast-transport-audit-seed87/` is added.

## What it speeds up

PR635's `hpe_audit_and_transport.run` (sha `c9a05ff2…`) is the per-trial cost of every negative-control suite in the cold chain. Each suite runs 96 full audits:

- T37 layer-end, 77 s (recorded cold-chain time);
- #799 layer-end, 151 s;
- #741 p6n layer-end, 114 s; layered66, 64.5 s; inherited cold-end, 114 s;
- the five `layer_end_controls_leaver.py` runs that the selected #1094 lineage rebuilds.

`fast_controls.py` is a drop-in for `python3 <control script> <args>`. An import hook lets the script select `hpe_audit_and_transport.py` by its own rule and executes it from the hashed bytes, never a `.pyc`. Only for the validated sha256 does it rebind five exact primitives:

- `Q`: integral values as `int`;
- `apply`: integer and ±1 fast paths, with the same assertion order, lazy row access and zero-dropping;
- `copy`: structural copy of flat gate records only;
- `basis`: memoised on all-`int` inputs;
- `state_maps`: scaled-integer dyadic P and P⁻¹, falling back to the pinned code for anything else.

`run()` and every assertion and message remain the pinned code objects. An unvalidated module runs unaccelerated, or exits non-zero under `--require-fast`.

## Evidence

```sh
python3 -I -B research/fast-transport-audit-seed87/verify.py            # tests + 4 real suites (~10 min)
python3 -I -B research/fast-transport-audit-seed87/verify.py --quick    # tests + T37 suite (~2.5 min)
```

Expected final line: `PASS_FAST_HPE_TRANSPORT suites=4 audits=384 identical_receipts_logs_outcomes cpu=…`. Deterministic fields are compared with `EXPECTED.json`. An independent `--quick` rerun and a clean sparse clone of this branch both reproduced it.

- **Four archived suites, 384 audits.** Inputs, receipts and logs are read from the repo's own evidence tarballs. Each unchanged script runs directly, through `--pinned`, and through `--require-fast`:
  - `COLD-END-CONTROLS.json` is byte-identical across the three runs and matches the archived receipt apart from its absolute `word` path;
  - stdout is identical across the three runs and equal to the archived log for the three suites that have one, apart from the seconds line;
  - all 96 per-audit outcomes are identical (exception type, `repr(args)` and `run()` line, or receipt text plus both output-word hashes).
- **Differential tests, under both Fraction constructors.** Each primitive is compared with the pinned function on value, key order and exception type and message:
  - `apply`: 4,000 programs, including malformed gates;
  - `state_maps`: 300 programs (227 take the dyadic path) and the real 12,913-gate prefix;
  - `basis`: 3,000 inputs, including non-int and cached calls;
  - the copy, at nesting depths 1 to 2,000;
  - `run()` on two module instances, for the honest word plus four deep-nesting variants;
  - the import hook (it selects the script's own sibling over `$PR635_CODE`) and the hash guard.

  Negative controls: a sabotaged `apply` is detected, and a zero-coefficient gate matches the pinned code.
- **Current frontier.** On the #1094 lineage's final k8 word, `layer_end_controls_leaver.py` produced a byte-identical receipt (95 rejected plus 2 declared not-applicable substitutes) and identical stdout; user CPU fell 50.6 → 24.6 s. This was recorded manually because that word isn't archived.

## Adversarial review

Three reviewer subagents tried to break the claim: a primitive fuzzer (~600k `apply` gates), a word mutator (201 new corrupted U8 words, run in fresh processes), and a harness reviewer. They reproduced one real divergence: an earlier copy used one frame per nesting level, so a gate nested about 500–1,000 deep made the pinned audit raise `RecursionError` while the accelerated one passed. The copy now handles only flat records.

They also found that pre-importing from `$PR635_CODE` could substitute a different module for scripts that import a sibling; about 17 directories hold another version. That is why the import hook now leaves the choice to the script. Smaller fixes:

- bare asserts are now distinguished by the `run()` line;
- the receipt is compared as text;
- a `.pyc` can no longer bypass the hash guard;
- the wrapper's own directory is removed from `sys.path`;
- `--` is passed through to the script.

Each of these cases is now a test.

## Measurements

macOS arm64, CPython 3.14.8, concurrent load 8–22:

| measurement | direct | accelerated | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| honest U8 audit, best-of-9 process CPU | 0.766 s | 0.334 s | **2.29×** |
| four archived suites, CPU | 239.3 s | 106.0 s | **2.26×** |
| #1094-lineage leaver suite, user CPU | 50.6 s | 24.6 s | 2.06× |

Cumulative ablation: Q/apply 1.72×, +copy 1.72×, +basis 2.07×, +state_maps 2.29×. The copy step is roughly neutral now and can be dropped.

## Scope

- Composes multiplicatively with #1059 (process parallelism; its workers would install the hook) and with #1101 (stage overlap). Not wired into any orchestrator.
- The layered66 suite (`7829187b…`, input not archived) was not run.
- Exactness is claimed for `run()`. Helpers return `int` after installation, and behaviour within one frame of the recursion limit is not claimed identical.
- How this was chosen: five explorer subagents prototyped alternatives (exact audit arithmetic, cross-mutant prefix memo, bit589 dependency portability, T37 emit, open sweep), and three lens judges ranked them. The cross-mutant memo (about 2× more CPU, exact) composes with this and is left as a follow-up.

## Credit

- PR635 authors (icekylinx) for the audit.
- DreamingOfClouds / LayerReviewer for the control scripts.
- #869/#870, #741, #942, #1005 and #1094 for the archived and rebuilt replays.
- #1059 for the complementary parallel runner.

Prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial assistance from Anthropic Claude (Claude Code), including the explorer, judge and reviewer subagents.

**Status: research construction and exact finite census; no new κ.**

PR997 samples signed four-source/four-output Hadamard connector paths and finds a 22-query, 238-primitive word. This contribution exhausts its eight-source-call class, allows arbitrary repeated readouts, and finds a **24-query word with 222 primitive calls**, using the same four dirty scratch rows. The new word executes 66 internal echo nodes versus 72. Every child and literal inverse is included. This is an exact interface operation-count comparison, not a measured multiplication-runtime improvement.

The completed census covers all **40,320** signed source orders. Two independent integer algorithms agree on all 114 minimum-profile frequencies and 22 Pareto profiles. The scoped minimum query count is **22**. For positive complete A-query prices sorted a≤b≤c≤d, the exact readout-price envelope is `4a+4b+2c+2d+min(2c,4a)`; source queries add twice the sum of B prices. A 24-query word is optimal when `c>2a`. Higher dispatch or placement charges can change the winner, and the complete recurrence and an explicit reversal control retain that expense.

The domain fixes one positive and one negative B call per source, distinct sources and outputs, one arbitrary dirty connector, and exact linear additive children. The optimum requires the coefficient identity for independent formal operators; special maps with additional algebraic relations are excluded. The readout bound is justified by the four available coordinate differences, so arbitrary integer readout multiplicities are covered. Additional source calls, output borrowing, other query alphabets, rounded children and state/placement-dependent prices are outside the optimum. title: Research: exact modular borrowed-port echoes with endpoint-sized data
body:
This supplies an explicit finite-width modular backend for PR1057's borrowed-port echo. Integer matrix factors execute modulo `2^w`, restore every dirty bit pattern, and recover the exact signed output from input/output bounds. Large intermediate integer lifts need not fit the data registers. **Recursive-interface construction; no new kappa.**

For the 52-factor fixture, the existing plan still takes **1,376 complete leaf calls and three dirty length-two arrays**, using **56-bit data**. The inherited integer-prefix majorant gives 114 sufficient bits for entry values bounded by seven, or 167 for arbitrary signed 56-bit dirt. These are sufficient-bound comparisons, not integer-width minima. The retained arbitrary-dirt integer lift actually reaches **90 signed bits**.

The cost is explicit: **38 scalar/access commands per two-dimensional leaf instead of 28**, including ten reductions. The full kernel executes **52,292 commands**, of which **13,760 are reductions**. All five arrays occupy 560 model bits; the four private work registers occupy **283 bits**, including a 112-bit product register. Coefficient/input conversion, final decoding, original input storage, planning, metadata, routing and physical adapters have separate paid terms. No measured speedup follows from this invoice.

## Reproduce and evidence

```sh
python3 -I -B research/modular-port-borrowing/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/modular-port-borrowing/test_package.py -v
```

Python 3.10+ and standard library only. Expected marker: `PASS_MODULAR_PORT_BORROWING`.

- **5,280 exact matrix cases** covering all ten input columns: all 861 ordered binary/ternary trees through seven factors at three widths and both signs, plus each parent plan from eight through 64 in both directions.
- A separate control-stack and matrix implementation checks **528,302 leaf prefixes and 667,416 recursive returns**, including borrowed ancestor ports.
- **33,280 exhaustive scalar cases** over the declared small quotient rings execute **2,160,640 actual scalar/access commands**; another **144 dense cases** vary dimension, signs, zero factors and width.
- Four primary executions compare every leaf with the integer lift, restore arbitrary dirty bits and replay the literal inverse. Closed operation and address invoices agree with literal execution.
- **19 mathematical/admission controls, 12 package tests and 25 existing selected-record tests** pass. Final normal CPython 3.14.4 and read-only, relocated, isolated optimized 3.12.3 receipts are byte-identical.
- Recovery failure is explicit: residue 12 modulo 16 decodes as −4 when the true result is 12 and the bound is omitted. Saturation corrupts a helper; rounded division fails the quotient contract. The guard separately preserves input representability when a zero product makes the output small.

## Scope and credit

Only `research/modular-port-borrowing/` is added. Base **ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262**, OS seed **52**. Six exact Git-object/SHA-256 source/context pins include five unchanged PR1057 files at **78a062df1dcab2bffea5ff4d8243f3da6e465414**. The generator/planner and additive-group identity remain credited predecessor work; the contribution is their concrete quotient-register backend, recovery guard and full cost/validation evidence.

The all-tree argument applies to **integer linear factors** and residue-valued recursive boundaries. Rounded, irrational or general dyadic leaves need another interface. The Python interpreter models bounded registers; its host allocation is not the stated data-space bound. A physical fixed-tape compiler, supplier/frame adapters, hosting and outer analytic transfer remain open. Leaf multiplicities and the direct all-role obstruction are unchanged. No supplier admission, full repository suite, selected cold replay, CI success or formal multiplication theorem is claimed.

The final queue was checked through **#1157**. **Ali Romman's #1135** was read through its exact-lift proof: it studies rounded restoration and a common-denominator rational embedding with `q^D` initialization and numerator headroom. This integer modular backend does not remove its denominator costs or solve its rounded-leaf obstruction. #1103's rectangular batching, #1155's deferred batch restoration and #835/#1144's modular verification have different objects and are acknowledged. This backend restores every completed child boundary and does not defer those restorations. Upstream advanced to **ce7ad1b6ab09452c3478723a2e96ed5ff212dc08**, selecting conditional PR1094; the experimental context remains frozen.

Credit Gareth Davidson PR1057, shhxera PR822, androolloyd PR673, Sagar Thakrar PR730, Chafik Boukhalfa PR628 and the retained lineage. The Ben-Or–Cleve register principle and modular arithmetic are classical; no priority claim is made for them. title: Construction: cap unfinished outputs in dirty fanout
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a **construction and scheduling tool** for dirty fanout. Sharing a temporary row across output updates saves restoration work, but can leave several outputs partly updated. This scheduler caps the number of unfinished outputs. Once an output is committed, it is correct and is never touched again.

For five outputs with a cap of two:

| Schedule | Most outputs unfinished at once | Child calls |
|---|---:|---:|
| This construction | 2 | 404 |
| Unrestricted optimum | 3 | 300 |
| Compute and restore each output separately | 1 | 716 |

All three use four dirty rows. The 716-call baseline is separate restoration, not the optimal cap-one schedule, which costs 508 calls. These are exact operation counts, not measured speedups or memory savings.

For $k$ outputs and capacity $W$, the minimum query cost is

$$
Q_{\min}=2\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}c_{A_i}+2\left\lceil\frac{k}{2W}\right\rceil c_B.
$$

Here $c_{A_i}$ prices one complete output-readout call and $c_B$ one complete shared-source call. Prices must be positive, fixed and equal for a call and its inverse. The written lower bound covers arbitrary extra readouts in the declared query alphabet. It does not establish optimality over arbitrary circuits.

The [construction and paid recurrence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b53b07b5aed4e00358a0d0061ad99dbf5190ca2b/research/bounded-pending-fanout-seed53/README.md#complete-recurrence-and-fixture) also charge admission, preparation, control, source access and child restoration. Supplier placement, common-label realization, precision/tape integration and outer assembly remain open. **No new $\kappa$ is claimed.**

## Task and overlap

Scope key: `dirty-fanout/pending-cap/permanent-commit`. This follows the user's recursive-interface assignment, seed 53. The domain is $k\geq0$, $W\geq1$, with exact characteristic-zero linear maps, signed unit queries and arbitrary initial data. The [task card](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b53b07b5aed4e00358a0d0061ad99dbf5190ca2b/research/bounded-pending-fanout-seed53/CLAIM.md) records the bounded experiment and stopped earlier candidate.

Investigation base: `ce7ad1b6ab09452c3478723a2e96ed5ff212dc08`. Upstream advanced during the cycle; this remains the base used for the result.

| Predecessor | Exact dependency head | Result used |
|---|---|---|
| @CubeJerry, #889 | `e2021d1c9e06948528cbc0a8fd7079b671da981d` | Dirty fanout and its unrestricted weighted minimum |
| Ross Richardson, #938 | `df645942469e6a739ec94010a6068c398f4a6c86` | Coefficient states and all unrestricted minimum words |

The addition is the capacity-constrained scheduler, permanent-commit checker and lower bound for longer words below the unrestricted schedule's required capacity. #982 and #1103 instead borrow output rows; this construction reserves them throughout.

## Validation

Run from the repository root with standard-library Python 3.11 or later:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bounded-pending-fanout-seed53/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/bounded-pending-fanout-seed53/test_package.py
```

Expected results are `PASS_BOUNDED_PENDING_FANOUT` and `PASS_BOUNDED_PENDING_PACKAGE`. Both pass on macOS arm64 with CPython 3.11.15 and 3.14.8. The checks cover 529 capacity cases, exact dirty-state replay, every child return and five independently computed finite minima. A reordered word passes final-output checks but fails the child-restoration check. Actual file corruptions are rejected, and certificate regeneration is byte-identical.

The all-$k,W$ claim rests on the written proof. The tests provide finite evidence. [The validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b53b07b5aed4e00358a0d0061ad99dbf5190ca2b/research/bounded-pending-fanout-seed53/VALIDATION.md) gives commands, hashes and controls. Selected-record integrity and its 25 existing tests pass. Full repository/cold supplier replay, Linux execution and formalization were not run; hosted CI success is not claimed.

Prepared for Sagar Thakrar / @thakrarsagar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. @CubeJerry and Ross Richardson retain credit for the predecessor results above, including their attribution to Chafik Boukhalfa's #628 commutator work. Original source and notice files are preserved byte for byte. title: Research: all-puncture E8 star decoder exclusion and p=56 classification (seed 49, no new kappa)
body:
## Summary & Status

- **Status:** Research note / scoped negative result (**no new $\kappa$**; `certificates/selected-result.json` and `upstream/` are unchanged).
- **Track & Seed:** Track 40–49 (Structural decoder research), OS random seed `49`.
- **Base Commit:** `ce7ad1b6ab09452c3478723a2e96ed5ff212dc08`
- **Predecessors Extended:** PR #631 (Chi Zhao, `0 <= p <= 35`), PR #875 (Philipp / `@mightyOil`, `p = 36`), and PR #939 (Ross Richardson, `0 <= p <= 55`).

## What Changed / Was Learned

PR #939 excluded the $E_8$ root-only star label-decoder from improving on the 9-puncture ratio $63/111$ up to $p \le 55$ and stopped at $p = 55$ because at $p = 56$ a minimum-weight codeword $c_0 \in C$ ($\operatorname{wt}(c_0)=56$) can vanish on the 64 live ports $L = \{0,\dots,119\}\setminus P$, dropping the live binary label rank $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_2}(C|_L)$ from $9$ to $8$. Moreover, the pairwise ($k \le 2$) capacity inequality $M_a + M_b \ge 84 - p$ used in PR #939 fails at $p = 72$ ($27/48 = 9/16 < 63/111$) and across $78 \le p \le 119$ (collapsing to $0$ for $p \ge 84$).

This package (`research/e8-star-all-punctures-seed49/`) resolves the remaining range $56 \le p \le 119$ and classifies the $p = 56$ dimension-loss boundary:

1. **Proposition 1 (Live-Quotient Star Cost Equivalence under Dimension Loss):** For any puncture set $P$ with $0 \le p \le 119$ ($1 \le v = 120 - p \le 120$) and restriction kernel $K_P = \{c \in C : \operatorname{supp}(c) \subseteq P\}$ of dimension $k_0 = 9 - \dim_{\mathbb{F}_2}(C|_L) \in \{0,\dots,8\}$, surviving rational star rank $s_P(c)$ is constant on cosets of $C / K_P \cong C|_L$ and vanishes iff $c \in K_P$. Thus the minimum star cost over $(9-k_0)$-element bases of the live quotient $C|_L$ equals the minimum star cost $C_{\text{star}}(P)$ over 9-element bases of $C$.
2. **Proposition 2 (Complete Two-Orbit Classification at the $p=56$ Boundary):** The $255$ puncture sets of size $p = 56$ with $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_2}(C|_L) < 9$ are the supports of the $255$ weight-$56$ codewords of $C$ (all with $k_0 = 1$, $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_2}(C|_L) = 8$), which partition under $W(E_8)$ into two orbits:
   - **Orbit 1 ($135$ even-frame codewords):** 511-reader rank histogram $\{0:1,\; 7:112,\; 8:398\}$, cumulative $\mathbb{F}_2$-dimensions $(1,1,1,1,1,1,1,8,9)$, exact optimal basis $(0,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,8)$ of star cost **$57$ on $64$ ports** ($57/64 = 0.890625 > 63/111$). All $56$ single-port restorations ($p=55$) restore $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_2}(C|_L)=9$ with cost $58$.
   - **Orbit 2 ($120$ root-nonorthogonality supports $S_a = \{i : |\langle L_i, L_a \rangle| = 4\}$):** live ports $\{a\} \cup a^\perp$ ($1+63=64$ lines), 511-reader rank histogram $\{0:1,\; 6:56,\; 7:198,\; 8:256\}$, cumulative $\mathbb{F}_2$-dimensions $(1,1,1,1,1,1,8,8,9)$, exact optimal basis $(0,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,8)$ of star cost **$50$ on $64$ ports** ($50/64 = 25/32 = 0.78125 > 63/111$). All $56$ single-port restorations ($p=55$) restore $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_2}(C|_L)=9$ with cost $51$.
3. **Proposition 3 (Sharp Subspace Support-Union Hierarchy, $k=1,\dots,9$):** The minimum support union of a $k$-dimensional subspace $W_k \subseteq C$ is sharply
   $$(U_1, U_2, U_3, U_4, U_5, U_6, U_7, U_8, U_9) = (56, 84, 100, 108, 112, 116, 118, 119, 120),$$
   attained simultaneously by a single nested full flag $0 \subset W_1 \subset \dots \subset W_9 = C$.
4. **Theorem 4 (All-Puncture $0 \le p \le 119$ Ratio Exclusion):** Imposing $\delta_{d_i} \le p$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k M_{d_i} \ge U_k - p$ ($1 \le k \le 9$) across all $24{,}310$ sorted rank profiles (with PR #631's $72-p$ for $0 \le p \le 8$) proves $C_{\text{star}}^{\text{live}}(P)/(120-p) = C_{\text{star}}(P)/(120-p) \ge 63/111$ for all $0 \le p \le 119$, with equality possible only at $p = 9$.

## Reproducible Verification Commands

```bash
python3 -I -O -B research/e8-star-all-punctures-seed49/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/e8-star-all-punctures-seed49/independent_check.py
python3 -I -O -B research/e8-star-all-punctures-seed49/test_package.py
```

## Scope, Attribution & AI Disclosure

- **Scope:** Applies strictly to the real $E_8$ root-only star label-decoder cost model $C_{\text{star}}(P)$ defined in PR #631 and PR #939; does not claim a formal proof of the asymptotic multiplication theorem or exclude non-star/multi-stage decoders.
- **Attribution:** Credits Chi Zhao (PR #631), Philipp / `@mightyOil` (PR #875), and Ross Richardson (PR #939), with retained sources pinned in `SOURCES.json`.
- **AI Disclosure:** Prepared by `@3xcalibur-tech` with substantial AI assistance from **Antigravity (Google DeepMind / Gemini)**. Licensed under Apache-2.0.

That is +0.1095% over the chain's best and +0.7294% over the selected result. The complex side binds (lower endpoint 0.001676890737967805674397).

Why this is the ceiling of the family at eight replicas. The windowed aggregate LP over bin patterns per (owner replica, idle child) class and per-call width counts has optimum 1215.57 rank-1 remainders, equal to the time-free relaxation, so the owner windows do not bind. The integer optimum of the time-free pattern model is exactly {1:1214, 2:1, 32:1} (HiGHS, proved optimal), which this map attains. At any replica count the time-free bound is at least 151.95 rank-1 remainders per replica, so T = 16 or 37 could add at most about 1.5·10⁻⁸.

An exactly liftable MILP over pattern counts n(c,p) and per-pattern time incidences x(c,p,t,w) (each port takes at most one helper per call; Σ_t x = n·mult_p(w); every call's inventory is placed inside its windows) solves in seconds once the patterns are restricted to the LP support. Each pattern's times × positions multigraph has maximum degree n and is properly n-edge-coloured (König); every colour class is one literal port, offsets are the partial sums of the pattern. construction/owners/search_owners.py is a search input only; construction/owners/recount_owners.py (standard library) recounts the frozen map.

# PASS_ARCFLOW_OWNERS_ON_CHECKED_K8_SLOT_BASELINE 0.001674083482880778
python -I -B research/gauge44-slots-arcflow/construction/owners/recount_owners.py
# PASS_OWNERS_RECOUNT

All stages pass locally (Linux, Python 3.12): baseline pins, slot layer and its 34 controls, native locals, independent audit_local, and the strict global replay (restore-parent, bind, emit, audit with mutation controls, invoice, assembly, 69 admission controls, 12 bit-supplier controls). independent/price_profile.py gives the same κ (PASS_FROZEN_PROFILE_TWO_EXACT_ENGINE_AND_OUTER47_CROSSCHECK).

A finite conditional witness on a pending construction; every assumption of the #1005/#1018 chain is inherited (all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, exact recovery, analytic transfer, bit H1–H5). body:
## Result

Conditional **kappa = 0.001675224519162937**, improving the source-pinned [PR1148](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1148) value **0.001675121647789207** by **0.000000102871373730**, approximately **0.00614113 percent** relative.

The conservative endpoint gives **kappa = 0.001675224516317980**. The comparison is the frozen proposal snapshot through PR1153. This is a new finite conditional construction under the inherited interfaces; the selected certificate and upstream sources are unchanged. Only `research/crosscall-kernel-demotion/` is added.

## Construction: augment actual physical gaps across calls

PR1148 already incorporates three demotion groups, 603/611/619, eight rank-seven helper ends and its T16 hosting. Its final assignment leaves 360 rank-one pending remainders. This package builds three additional, concretely checked local prefixes, ordered **627, 635, 651**, and couples them to those actual gaps.

- Their helper indices are `(403,405,406,407)`, `(411,413,414,415)` and `(427,429,430,431)`.
- Lowering an entrance from dimension five to four changes each affected helper's borrowed width from four to five. Every group therefore needs four actual additional pending axes. Its complete local profile difference is `L = -8H1 + 8H2 + 4H3 - 4H4`.
- Group 651 uses a different codimension-one hyperplane from the earlier unsuccessful candidate. Each complete joint prefix is rebuilt and checked; compatibility is not inferred from four individual width changes.
- Within a call, a selected helper with its own unit gap stays in place. Otherwise it exchanges owners with a width-four donor whose owner has a real unclaimed axis. Across calls, both source windows must contain the exchanged times, and neither incoming use may collide with another use of that physical family.
- A whole group is installed atomically. Every successful augmentation retains the existing groups, consumes four distinct unit gaps and updates the global capacity and busy-family state. A failed attempt rolls back its rows and state. The final table rebuilds all chronological coordinate offsets.

The within-call construction installs **42 groups**. Cross-call augmentation installs **47 more**, yielding **89 extra groups across 52 of 144 calls**. Provider prefixes zero through three occur **92, 30, 7 and 15 times**. Each role remains literal and whole; no fractional helper or width-only histogram substitutes for a physical owner.

Each installed group removes four paid rank-one remainders. Its complete paid difference is therefore `-12H1 + 8H2 + 4H3 - 4H4`. The written proof establishes strict moment improvement for every `0 < b < 1`, while the final exact arithmetic certifies the achieved endpoint.

## Actual combined profile

```text
{1:340860, 2:71848, 3:59684, 4:18364,
 5:11808, 8:1152, 24:1, 48:4918}
```

Live stock remains **14,336**, paid rank mass **1,041,408**, and deficit **5,120**. The actual remainder profile is `{1:4,24:1,48:4918}`: **4,923 positive remainders**, compared with PR1148's 5,279. The checked construction uses **10,271 actual orthogonal 73-column chart types**, compared with 10,580, and 59,621 cross-replica helper roles. All **1,409 changed owner records** are supplied as complete before/after rows against the frozen public table.

Both retained exact rational engines certify the native and conservative complex endpoints; all **47 strict outer inequalities** pass. The pinned inherited bit supplier is retained and the complex side binds. The arithmetic is computed from this one realized word-and-owner composition; advertised gains from separate PRs are not added.

python -I -B research/crosscall-kernel-demotion/verify.py --out ../crosscall-result
```

- All **69,120 literal roles**, all 144 calls, actual provider widths, current-source inactivity windows, physical families, chronological axis blocks and actual 73-column charts. The independent mixed checker rejects **13 targeted controls**, including incorrect helper dispatch, wrong variants and omitted actual dispatch changes.
- Every unclaimed axis and the complete paid remainder/profile bill. The finite invoice passes **all nine guards and four controls**; its actual prefix is 397 bits and its physical row coefficient is 16,469.
- Both exact moment engines, endpoint decisions and all 47 outer inequalities. Source and artifact identities remain bound throughout.

These are fresh checks of the changed kernels, dispatch, literal map, geometry, invoice and pricing. Unchanged ancestral construction/phase interfaces remain inherited. No full ancestral cold rebuild, hosted CI result, independent human review, new Lean certificate or global allocation optimum is claimed.

The all-size/compiler, common-label and mutable-source realization, complete-call hosting, precision/tape and exact-recovery, analytic-transfer and inherited bit H1-H5 assumptions remain conditional.

## Reusable proofs and mathematical sources

The package notes and source ledgers in `research/crosscall-kernel-demotion/README.md` record two distinct OpenAI-proof mechanisms investigated by each of the four workers, their exact statements and source hashes, and their concrete use or limitations. The owner lane uses a left-saturation-preserving matching augmentation and explicit disjoint physical-pool capacity templates. The literal table and independent geometry checks provide that witness.

The sufficient replacement proof and uniform saving argument are supplied for reuse. A bounded attempt did not install the final possible four-unit group; the remaining four gap families have no common recipient in the current table. title: Research: exact arbitrary-mask three-total five-cube boundary (no new kappa)
body:
PR1046 leaves non-affine port masks outside its five-cube copy theorem. This **research note / scoped negative result** resolves the full decoder with at most three arbitrary binary outer products. Its exact total pairing-rank minimum is **32**; a three-total witness has ranks **8 + 16 + 8**, versus the exact affine three-total minimum **35**. Every cost-32 triple has peak rank 16. For canonical distinct readers, the 131,068 equality masks are precisely the nonempty proper subsets of one parity class.

The proof uses the cube's two orthogonal parity bases and an exact rank formula, covering all masks without a 2^32-mask search. Masks may be non-affine functions of the port index; messages remain linear XOR sums of input data. PR1046 already attains total 32 with two affine totals, and with four affine totals of peak eight. Neither optimum is improved here.

Under the inherited additive stage/copy ledger, even granting every other required expense zero leaves `D <= (s-1)32-s*32 = -32` for every `s>=3`. **No physical supplier, runtime gain or new kappa is claimed.** Four or more arbitrary-support terms, larger cubes, other Grams, nonlinear data messages and changed accounting remain open. All-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source, hosting, precision/tape, bit H1-H5 and analytic obligations remain inherited.

Only `research/five-cube-three-totals/` and its path-scoped Linux workflow are added. Research base: `c0e3631dc24e3c24a861f7d3d79e0608481cccec`; refreshed submission base: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`. All seven pinned sources are unchanged between those bases. body:

title: Tooling: exact frame solver and delivery-rewrite search for gauge44/k8 local words (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Adds `research/exact-frame-toolkit/`: the search and admission tools behind the companion construction PR #1195 (two
source-holder fusions on #1148's joint-entrance k8 word). **No new κ.** No selected record, upstream file or existing package is modified.

**Revision 2 (2026-10-14)** answers the review continuation point
([comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1186#issuecomment-6161623948)). It also fixes two harness
screen gaps. Details are in the README sections *What is certified* and *Revision 2*.

**Revision 3 (2026-10-14)** makes the toolkit run on Windows, answering woklerx's independent audit
([comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1186#issuecomment-6169503528)). The platform-dependent
pieces move into `compat.py`, `portability.py` checks the Windows code paths on any OS, and the toolkit refuses `-O`.
`frames.py` is unchanged. Results are in `PORTABILITY.json` and the README section *Revision 3*.

- **Frame solver** (`frames.py`). Each solve carries two per-instance certificates:
  - exact optimality for the floored integer surrogate weights `floor(2^40 · lo_r(b))`;
  - with `interval=True`, a rigorous rational interval for the true per-call moment at b over every assignment of the frame
    model.

  The interval's lower end is a chain-dual (or exact-elimination) bound with outward-floored weights on a 2^-224 grid, plus
  a λ·rank shift that telescopes along every register chain. Its upper end is the engines' upper bound of the returned
  assignment. L/U domain propagation, chain dual decomposition and exact elimination; models monotone chains, target caps,
  cut equality, mutable early tails, and `audit_local`'s helper cones as caps (`model.py`).
- **Pricing harness** (`harness.py`): build_tri-style edits (B deletes/inserts, early tails, FULL prepends). Screens, in order:
  1. the auditor's static program rules;
  2. the B+tail+prepend map mod p;
  3. an exact check that the derived compensation is unchanged;
  4. frames.

  Every negative delta and every returned word is re-checked by the unchanged `audit_local.py`. With `interval=True` it also
  returns the true realized delta (`realized_delta_units`) and a bound on any possible true gain (`max_gain_units`).
- **Searches**: read-fusion candidates (`fusion.py`), joint triangle-hybrid candidates (`joint.py`), and the multiprocess
  fusion + enlarged-reader repair sweep (`repair.py --interval`, `sites.py`).
- **Composition**: split a slot recipe and price its instances (`slots.py`); compose slots with fusions (`compose.py`); put a
  newer word's entrances and ends onto a scalar program and re-solve (`transplant.py`).
- **Exact κ** (`kappa.py`): the certified moment root and the retained 47-constraint outer assembly with PR589, for any T.
- **Admission drivers** that reuse unchanged package engines: PR635 native chain (`native.py`), PLAN/SPEC rebinding with
  unchanged widths (`rebind.py`), `unpin.py` between discovery and `freeze_spec.py`, the T16 discovery run
  (`t16_discover.py`), and per-site negative controls (`controls.py`).

Pure Python 3.11+ with NumPy, on Linux, macOS and Windows; no C++, Boost, LP/MILP solver or network. Do not run it with
`-O`: its asserts are checks, so it refuses to start.

## Check

```sh
python -B research/exact-frame-toolkit/selftest.py      # about 50 s here (Python 3.12 and 3.14); --quick about 25 s
python -B research/exact-frame-toolkit/portability.py   # the Windows code paths on any OS, then the selftest
```

On a GitHub Actions Windows runner (Windows Server 2025, Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.5.4) the full selftest and the portability check pass, `-O` is refused, and the
spawn-mode `repair.py --interval` sweep of the pre-slot word matches the macOS sweep in all 2,405 records
([run](https://github.com/mdumitrean/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38621712253)).

It uses only files on main:
- the retained #1042/#1094 replay archives;
- #1094's `REPLAY.json`;
- #942's checkpoint and the `ASSEMBLY.json` it names.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `kappa.py` on #1094's (T16) and #942's (T37) complex profiles | the selected and checkpoint κ, exactly |
| surrogate frame optimum of the seven-slot k8 word `c2b29430` | its published profile (integer certificate) |
| true-moment interval of that word at b | published frames within 1.48e-11 units of the minimum over the frame model; the surrogate alone bounds this only by 1512 units |
| control: deliberately worse assignment | interval width = its exact true excess (6763.29 units) |
| control: exact dual with multipliers of magnitude 2^62–2^90, then a NaN | still a lower bound in Python integers; NaN rejected |
| control: port written at the end of B, undone in the first early tail | passes the B+tail screen; harness `compensation-changed`; `audit_local` endpoint failure |
| #1018's seven slots on the pre-slot word `db2c7cfb` | −1788 surrogate units each, −12516 together; certified true gains of −1784.83 each, −12493.80 together |
| source-holder fusion + full read-set exchange at slot sites X=439, X=444 | −3957 each |
| five slots + both fusions | −16854; `audit_local` PASS; unchanged interfaces; κ 0.001672756914849856 on #1094's owners |

`exchange.py` also regenerates the published SW4 word from the promoted word, as a self-check of the exchange family.

## Usage

The README covers the modules, a workflow (price → search → compose/transplant → admit), and the model and pitfalls, e.g.:
- the unpin step that `freeze_spec.py` needs after a word change;
- `emit_allcold.py` reading `SPEC.data.plan_sha256` directly;
- `evidence/local` in the gauge44 T16 packages being historical #645 files.

On the pre-slot k8 word, `repair.py --workers 6` sweeps 2,405 fusions in about 6 minutes; the only negative surrogate
deltas are the two sites above. With `--interval` (about 8 minutes), no other priced candidate can gain more than 3.3e-11
units at b. `REVISION2-REGRESSION.json` compares both revisions on this sweep.

## Scope

Search output is nomination data. A construction exists only after the unchanged package chain admits it, as in #1195.

The certificates are per-instance statements at the stated endpoint b. Neither the global recursive moment root nor κ is
inferred from cost units: both are recomputed by `kappa.py` and the package chains.

The inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape,
analytic-transfer and bit H1–H5 assumptions remain. This is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

## Attribution

Imports or ports, unchanged in substance, the following (credits in `NOTICE.md`):
- chafreaky's frame-domain model and engines;
- the k492/multicold moment and outer engines;
- icekylinx's #645 `audit_local.py`;

- NewBArch's #869 `build_tri` semantics;
- Rohan Arun's #987 slot search and the #1018 recipe (Jeremy Kothe, MineB);

- Hao Yan's #858 T16 package.

title: Research: sharp preserved-frame P104 COPY-drop threshold at 38 punctures (no new kappa)
body:
**Status: research note / exact structural threshold. No new κ.**

Preserving all sixteen original P104 frame lines changes the first COPY-drop boundary: every one of the **7,168** frame-pair decoders retains all eight COPY terms at rank seven through **21 additional deletions**. The first possible drop requires **22 additional punctures, 38 total**. Every possible term has that threshold. An emitted exact decoder attains `[7,7,7,6,7,7,7,7]`, or **55 copies on 82 ports**.

The support-label span can drop after only 20 extra deletions while all COPY ranks stay seven. The missing condition is loss of dimension after quotienting by the partner's radical. The proof gives the exact criterion and reduces arbitrary added port sets to 127 hyperplane cuts per side, so this is a completed finite census with a completeness argument, rather than a failed subset search.

Two exact implementations agree on all 896 frame records and 28,672 possible terms. The primary uses the frozen PR968 model and nine-dimensional functional filtering, checking **7,282,688** quotient-cut incidences. The independent checker constructs the roots, frames and dual decoders from scratch, then enumerates nonzero words in seven-dimensional binary column codes. It imports no primary or predecessor code. The witness passes all **6,724** all-pairs coefficient checks.

The cost result is scoped: through 21 added punctures the COPY ratio strictly worsens from P104's `56/104=7/13`; the displayed first-drop witness also has the worse ratio `55/82`. This does not optimize aggregate COPY cost at or beyond the boundary, realize a physical supplier or supply a new recursive moment. Source access, helpers, frames, restoration, hosting, precision/tape and analytic obligations remain open or inherited. No new κ or measured runtime benefit is claimed.

title: Scoped negative result: two P112 totals need overlapping independent lifts (no new kappa)
body:

For exact P112 ten-term decoders retaining the eight coordinate readers, two extra totals cannot reduce the pairing-rank sum below 64 if either added factor matrix has rank at most one, either added reader is outside the coordinate column space, or their coordinate coefficient supports are disjoint. Any remaining candidate therefore needs two independent, overlapping coordinate lifts and independent source columns. No new kappa or physical supplier is claimed.

The written proof combines the inherited #845/#998 single-lift floor with support-rank subadditivity, a quotient-space rank argument, and disjoint support accounting. It also gives the k-total quotient-nullity-one and disjoint-support extensions. An explicit basis-change control preserves the decoder identity but changes its cost from 64 to 66, preventing an unjustified normalization of the remaining search.

python3 -I -S -B research/p112-two-total-rank-one-seed21/test_package.py

This is `335121717095377 / (2·10^17)`. It is +3.9910e-8 over #1169 (`0.001675568675201533`, T37 owners on the same joint word without X54), +5.40e-9 over #1183 (`0.001675603180601302`) and +4.76e-8 over #1148's T16 value (`0.001675560947524449`). The complex side binds. The PR589 bit supplier is unchanged.

**Concurrent identical result.** chafreaky's #1196 reports the same composition and the same κ, `0.001675608585476885`. This package was built independently: its own flow, owner map and package. It is submitted as an independent construction and check, not a new record. At submission, #1193 (`0.001675672695827067`), #1192 and #1195 are higher.

**Composition**
1. **Local word.** Thomas DiFiore's joint-entrance k8 word (#1148, `research/k8-joint-entrances`, head `3ba07f19`) receives Jeremy Kothe's eighth triangle-hybrid slot X54/E589 (#1130).

   - The slot is width-neutral. The widths stay `{4:44,5:44,7:38,8:114,9:240}`.
2. **Owners.** The package uses Ali Romman's #1129 T37 machinery (`r480-owner-optimum`): order, groups, constructor, admission code and independent audit, retargeted as in #1157.
   - #1129's integer flow does not fit this inventory. Its nine-pattern basis is infeasible here because there are 12 more width-5 helpers per call.
   - A new integer pattern flow over 15 of the 20 tight patterns attains the all-replica optimum for this inventory. It was found with an LP and a support-restricted MILP during discovery; verification runs no solver.
   - That optimum is `{1:834,48:11374}`. It is the same normalized idle as #1148's own `ALL-T-BOUND.json`, from #795's signed prices and the #890/#942/#1129 argument.
   - The unchanged `construct.py` expands the flow into 159,840 literal roles in 333 calls.

Complete profile: `{1:788046,2:165834,3:137862,4:41958,5:27972,8:2664,48:11374}`. Live stock is 33,152 and the deficit is 11,840. The root lies in `(0.001678420962050942454559, …560)`.

**Verification** (no network or solver):
```sh
python3 -B research/k8-joint-x54-t37/check.py --work /new/dir
# PASS_K8_JOINT_X54_T37_ALL_REPLICA_OPTIMUM_AND_ATTAINING_CONSTRUCTION 0.001675608585476885

# PASS_K8_JOINT_X54_LOCALS
```

`check.py` covers:
- the all-replica certificate: 1,163 patterns, two exact engines and all 47 outer inequalities;
- 18 certificate controls;
- the literal owner reconstruction;
- the strict replay: bind, lift, emit, controller audit with 15 mutations, the full invoice (prefix 775 < 1024, row 17,495 < 20,161), assembly, 69 admission and 12 bit controls, and the independent owner audit with 2,016 disjoint pending-axis checks.

`build_local.py` rebuilds the native locals from the repository and checks every pinned identity:

- the X54 build;

PR1155's frozen restoration-coalescing note says read-freedom is necessary for deferred dirty-workspace restoration. `sum_i B_i (G_{i-1}...G_1 - I) = 0`.

The written proof covers arbitrary dimensions and fields, while the executable evidence is explicitly finite. Prefix observations require each prefix defect to vanish; terminal cancellation alone is not safe for adaptive observations.

- Nonzero invariant-reader shear batches permit genuine restoration elimination. The seed-selected five-child family pays **15N -> 11N** scalar ADDs per node, including readers, forward drift and final restoration.
- A second example reads the changing coordinate and cancels its two observable defects only at the endpoint, separating terminal and prefix contracts.
- Complete recursion, scalar/memory-access invoices, child calls, descriptor/controller charges, integer magnitude bounds and storage limits are stated. An actual recursive event emitter is replayed forward and inverse on every dirty-state basis column in its bounded domain.
- Independent block-state multiplication checks the defect formula on all **46,656** three-child signed-reader/shear tuples. Noncommuting rational evidence and six mathematical controls are included, plus standalone relocation and a real source-corruption rejection.

python3 -I -O -B research/observer-safe-restoration/test_package.py

The circuit contains **six noncommuting shear pairs**; wrong-order restoration and wrong-order covector substitution are both explicitly rejected.

Only `research/r420-decoder-chain/` is added. D, scatter, B, the complete arbitrary-dirt A operator, all 660 register-frame paths, original H1–H5, helpers/copies and paid profile `{1:1320,2:1440,4:60,5:120,8:9}` remain unchanged. No selected supplier or frontier change.

python3 -B research/r420-decoder-chain/verify.py
```

```text
PASS_R420_DECODER_CHAIN decoder=321->250 ADDs=26916->26774 columns=660 controls=8 noncommuting=6 no_new_kappa
```

- Source-bound certificate regeneration, unchanged exact E8/frame/interface checker, separate set-valued complete-word interpreter and **eight negative controls** pass.
- Bounded search: all **6,320 directed pairs** at each of **seven steps**, 44,240 scores total; deterministic seed7 ties. No restarts; stopping at seven is **not an optimum claim**.
- Fresh unchanged C++ legality and full **nine-stage native replay for both words**, **1,380 formal columns and 18/18 omitted-bridge controls each**, pass.
- Native payload rises **100 → 103 bits**, still strictly below 104. Candidate forward/reverse positive bounds are **219,001 / 2,932,970**; exact payload upper `5782737910556506080751636537600`. No inherited precision charge is silently reused.
- Exact sources, canonical word hashes, ordered recipe, per-step coverage, proof, native receipt and commands are committed. The environment lacked C++; a user-local GCC15 C++ frontend plus existing Boost resolved the prerequisite without changing checks. Failed prerequisite attempts are disclosed.

### Novelty and credit

This reuses and credits eumemic's **PR543** construction/checker and Sagar Thakrar's **PR708** recipe, independent interpreter and native replay design. **PR753** already improves disjoint pairs to disjoint restored stars (decoder257); this result changes the class to ordered noncommuting chains and reaches250, without claiming global optimality. **PR748** achieves larger overall savings by changing the helper-dirt map and D; this work preserves both and claims no overall record. **PR848**'s selected-R439 disjoint-total obstruction is respected: this construction is historical R420 only.

Dylan Crow, DreamingOfClouds, Zhihao Chen and the retained realization/hosting/assembly lineage remain credited. Prepared by **Adam Gall (@adamgall)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, Apache-2.0, preserving predecessor licenses and notices. No independent human review is claimed.

title: Research audit: quadratic factor-tape travel for balanced dirty words
body:
PR985 gives a conservative O(r³ W_total) allowance for sequential factor lookup. This research audit proves that its unchanged balanced word admits quadratic factor-tape travel under an explicit contiguous, fixed-width layout.

For every n ≥ 1 and both call directions, the closed index travel is less than 2N, where N = 3qn − 2q² and q = 2^floor(log2 n). A reader that copies every B-bit descriptor and restores its head uses fewer than 4NB descriptor-head moves and exactly NB payload reads. The complete lookup bound is P_layout + P_parse + O(G + N(B + log²(nB+2))); setup, parsing, common parameters, preflight, copies, and amortized control are explicit. The proof also gives the exact quadratic variation on powers of two.

This refines a safe access allowance, not a false predecessor theorem. Preparation, numerical precision, arithmetic, mutable-array routing, recursive children, and physical/compiler obligations remain paid separately. It does not certify PR1054's complete invoice, improve the selected κ, or claim a measured runtime gain.

## Verification

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/balanced-descriptor-travel/test_package.py
```

Expected: `PASS_DESCRIPTOR_PACKAGE` with a nested `PASS_BALANCED_DESCRIPTOR_TRAVEL` receipt.

- 150,126 actual lookups from the byte-exact PR985 dispatcher across 78 signed cases; two further cases vary array geometry.
- A separate compressed word algebra checks 4,241 counts. Literal bit-head and countdown models check 102 tape cases and 1,025 counter cases.
- Nine mathematical/tape controls and five package faults reject. The full audit passes from a read-only relocated copy.
- All five vendor files match their pinned Git blobs. Selected-record integrity and all 25 selected-result tests pass. CPython 3.15.0, standard library only.

The all-size claim rests on the written induction and paid reader construction. The main dispatcher fixtures use length-one arrays and zero coefficients to exercise the fixed dispatch structure; these are not numerical precision tests. Independent checking means separate implementations/models, not independent human review. Full repository/cold supplier replay, hosted CI, and formal verification of the multiplication theorem are not claimed.

## Scope and attribution

Only `research/balanced-descriptor-travel/` is added. The publication base is `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`; the experiment source is PR985 `da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70`. The local seed-65 claim records continuation, finite domains, inspected heads, current discussion review and overlap checks through PR1206. PR1054, PR1085, PR1135, and discussion1202 concern different precision, magnitude, or representation questions.

Credit Ali Romman for PR985, Chafik Boukhalfa for PR628's balanced commutator and preparation lineage, and 0xkilgore for PR663's leaf count. Retained licenses and predecessor notices are unchanged. Prepared by Charles Bethin with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, verification, and writing. No literature-priority claim or external human review.

title: Research: rank-8 complex decoders are gauge-rigid; E-graph eight-term floor (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research note / scoped structural result (a proof). No κ claim, no new supplier, no scalar saving.** Only `research/complex-rank8-decoder-rigidity/` is added; `upstream/`, the selected record (κ = 0.001672660197076918, PR1094 at the base) and every existing file are unchanged.

The complex supplier's copied-information cost is the decoder constant cst = 64 on P112 (one cst unit ≈ 2.8% of b in the PR942 lineage on which this work started; the constant is the same in the current selection). PR717 (DreamingOfClouds) reduced exactness to the E-graph (odd entries are fixed by cost-0 terms) and showed that decoders with **exactly eight costly terms** cost at least 64, but recorded its support step (that the costly supports are hyperplane-flat complements, the W(E8)-orbits of the fundamental weights) as ARGUED: it rested on the tangent-space rigidity D1(d) plus an orbit census, with global rigidity only sampled (10 of 12 random starts, RECORDED). PR968 proved the floor rigorously only under all-pairs exactness, where the normal form `D = RA, T = RB` is immediate, and listed E-graph-only exactness as not covered (so does #1071).

This package proves the missing global statement:

- **Theorem 1.** On P112 and P120, every real matrix K of rank ≤ 8 with `K_ii = 4` and `K_ij = 0` on orthogonal root pairs equals `D (2G) D⁻¹` for a diagonal D with nonzero entries. The rank-8 solutions of the E-graph system form one orbit of the diagonal torus; no odd entry vanishes. "P112" is the complement of *any* frame: W(E8) is transitive on the 2025 frames (checked) and the system is invariant up to a sign conjugation that lies in the torus, so the result covers the Hamming coordinate frame punctured by the shipped word as well as PR717's FRAME0.
- **Corollary 2.** In PR717's E-graph-only model every decoder with exactly eight costly terms has PR968's normal-form supports `C(a_k)`, `C(b_k)` for a dual basis `ABᵀ = 2I`; `(RA, RB)` is then literally an all-pairs-exact decoder with the same supports and costs, so PR968's floor theorem gives **cst ≥ 64 on P112 and ≥ 72 on P120**. This reaches PR717 D1(b)'s conclusion by a proved route — the flat-support step itself does not hold for a general dual basis (checked on a sampled basis), so PR968's Lemma 1 is what carries the floor — and extends PR968's eight-term floor to E-graph exactness at p = 0 and for any single-frame puncture.

Changed hypotheses: none. Remaining obligations / not covered: nine or more costly terms (PR717's mixed-β problem stays open on P112 in this model — its locus is the rank ≥ 9 solutions together with ≥ 9-term factorisations of the rank-8 ones), rigidity on P111 and on the P104 units other than type (2,2,2,2) (see the update below; numerical evidence only), Corollary 2 over complex coefficients (Theorem 1 itself is algebraic and holds over any field of characteristic zero), any physical word. Corollary 2 inherits PR968's one cited premise (the classification of E8 hyperplane flats, PR968 (F6)) and PR968's written argument.

Proof shape: pivot on a live frame F chosen so that the punctured lines form whole classes (28 of the 1260 live frames of P112 qualify): `K[F,F] = 4I₈` gives `K = ¼ K[:,F] K[F,:]`, so the problem is bilinear in rows `a_i = K[i,F]` and columns `b_j = K[F,j]`; relative to F the lines fall into 14 D4-blocks forming the Steiner system S(3,4,8), each with two classes of four mutually orthogonal lines whose sign matrices are Hadamard; orthogonal lines in different blocks share exactly two pivot coordinates, so their equations have two terms. (i) Zero exclusion: the necessary conditions on the zero pattern form a CNF whose only model is the trivial pattern; DRUP refutations of "some entry vanishes" (for the full CNF and for the reduced one with only the two-term and diagonal equations) are shipped and replayed by the verifier's own unit-propagation checker. (ii) Within a class the parallelism relations forced by live witnesses leave two solution families; one has a rank-1 class matrix and is excluded, the other is `A_C = diag(δ) H_C diag(γ)`. (iii) The two-term equations glue the column scalings across blocks and the 3-design turns the ratios into a global potential on F. Then `K_if = 2G_if d_i/d_f` and `K = D(2G)D⁻¹`.

## Update (second commit, same package): beyond one frame

Section G of `verify.py` and PROOF.md §10 extend the analysis to the other units PR968/PR717 study:

- The stabiliser of FRAME0 generated by single and double root reflections (204 line permutations) is transitive on the 112 lines of P112 and has exactly three orbits on the 1260 frames inside P112, of sizes 28 / 336 / 896 — PR968's 364 inadmissible frames and its 896 admissible ones (PR717's P104 clique lies in the 896-orbit). So P111 is one unit up to symmetry and the P104 units are three.
- **Theorem 1 transfers verbatim to the 336 P104 units of type (2,2,2,2):** with the pivot `{12,13,22,23,30,31,36,37}` every live class is complete, zero exclusion holds (shipped refutation), all live group witnesses exist and every block has a complete live class — exactly the finite inputs the written proof uses. Hence `cst ≥ 56` for eight costly terms in the E-graph model on those units (PR968's floor at p = 16).
- **Zero exclusion (Lemma 4) holds on P111 and on all 1260 P104 units** (four shipped refutations, transported by the stabiliser). For the type-(4,4) units the two-term and diagonal conditions alone admit a zero pattern (576 zeros; the verifier records this) and the refutation needs all four clause families.
- **What is still missing, named per unit** (verdict pinned in code): type (4,4) — the all-complete pivot leaves two blocks without a live class, so Lemma 6's cocycle step has no witness; type (1,…,1), incl. PR717's P104 — four classes keep two live rows, so Lemma 5 does not apply; P111 — one three-row class (the three-row variant of Lemma 5 is sketched in §10 as the smallest next step). Rigidity on these units rests on numerical evidence only (type (4,4): 8/8 random starts gauge-equivalent, seed 5; type (1,…,1): 5/6).

Validation now: 61 `PASS` on P112 (41 + 20 in section G), 41 on P120, eight shipped DRUP refutations, all replayed by the verifier's own checker; every count, class profile and CNF digest in section G is pinned. Expected final lines unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Base commit: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe` (current main). The work started at `2921874` (selected κ 0.001661960547713947, PR942) and the additive package was rebased before submission; its statements do not depend on the selected record. Dependency heads: PR717 at `4a97676` (model and definitions, pinned by blob and SHA-256), PR968 as merged (normal form and puncture floor), both pinned in SOURCES.json. Concrete object and bounded domain: real matrices of rank ≤ 8 satisfying the E-graph system on the P112 and P120 line sets; eight-costly-term decoders in PR717's D1(a) model on those units.

Task origin: the external sprint prompt (track 40–49 structural decoder research, OS seed 47), not an autoresearch.md task card; the local claim in CLAIM.md records the three candidates considered. No pinned coordination issue existed at the start; the discussion board's claims were checked before submission (the only adjacent one, #1210 "masked root-star copy-cost floor on P112", concerns star decoders, a different class).

Nearest overlapping PRs and added value: **PR717** D1(b)/(d) (the ARGUED step this proves) and **PR968** (the all-pairs floor this extends to E-graph exactness). Concurrent, opened while this was being prepared: **#1191** proves that E-graph ("mask") exactness already yields the all-pairs identity when *one* factor is root-linear, for any term count (P112, all P111, all P104); its hypothesis and Theorem 1's are incomparable — Theorem 1 fixes the rank at 8 and restricts neither factor (its solutions `D(2G)D⁻¹` have non-root-linear factors in general), #1191 restricts one factor but neither rank nor term count — so together they close, on P112, the E-graph decoders of rank ≤ 8 and those with a root-linear factor, leaving rank ≥ 9 with both factors off the root code. **#1180** extends the *all-pairs* floor to any term count with both factors root-linear (explicitly excluding masked identities); **#1197** (ten-term decoders with retained coordinate readers), **#1187** (P104 COPY-drop thresholds), **#1077** (complex coefficients), **#1071** (delivery bounds), **#1020**, **#998/#845** (single lifts) stay in the all-pairs or single-lift models. None proves rank-8 rigidity of the E-graph system. The sprint seed (47) coincides with PR968's; the object is distinct.

## Validation

Standard library only, ~10 s CPU (up to ~30 s wall) per unit, from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-decoder-rigidity/verify.py               # P112
python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-decoder-rigidity/verify.py --live P120   # control
```

Expected: 61 `PASS` lines on P112 (41 on P120), no `FAIL`, exit 0, final lines

```
PASS_COMPLEX_RANK8_DECODER_RIGIDITY: live P112; pivot [2, 3, 16, 17, 46, 47, 52, 53]; blocks 14; classes 26 complete; frames 2025; zero-pattern CNF 3744 vars / 29820 clauses; proof lemmas 1722 (+3001 reduced); coordinate cst 64
PASS_COMPLEX_RANK8_DECODER_RIGIDITY: live P120; pivot [0, 1, 26, 27, 44, 45, 54, 55]; blocks 14; classes 28 complete; frames 2025; zero-pattern CNF 4032 vars / 33768 clauses; proof lemmas 2045 (+2439 reduced); coordinate cst 72
```

Finite tests versus proof: every finite fact the written proof (PROOF.md) uses carries a check id that `verify.py` recomputes exactly — Steiner/Hadamard/orthogonality structure, class matchings, live witnesses (all counts asserted, nothing passes vacuously), W(E8)-transitivity on the 2025 frames, the two RUP replays (deletions ignored; proofs produced by Glucose via python-sat, never trusted), exact rational corollary mechanics, and an exact recomputation of the gluing/assembly step. Failure controls: relaxed CNFs accept the all-zero pattern, a proof with an inserted non-RUP lemma or truncated before its empty clause is rejected, the proof does not close without the "some zero" clause, a missing proof file fails loudly, a zero-free non-Hadamard block matrix shows a single D4 block is *not* rigid, class-dependent column scalings break the assembly, and a rank-9 solution is not of gauge form. The within-class algebra (Lemma 5), the gluing (Lemma 6) and the assembly are written arguments; the zero-exclusion step is a checked propositional refutation whose minimal core still spans 380 equations over 73 lines, so no hand argument is offered for it. `probe_numeric.py` (numpy) records non-proof evidence: tangent nullity equals the gauge dimension on P120/P112/P104 (183/175/167) and 8/8, 5/6, 5/6 converged random starts are gauge-equivalent to 2G (the rest stalled; none non-gauge).

Checks not run: hosted CI (no workflow or Makefile group added — the token lacks the `workflow` scope to push one; the existing CI groups do not touch this directory), repository-wide suites (nothing outside the new directory changes), Python versions other than 3.14. Environment: Linux x86-64, CPython 3.14.4, 61/61 checks on P112 and 41/41 on P120, also from a fresh `git archive` of the head. Review: two rounds of AI-assisted adversarial review (22 refuters across mathematician/code-auditor lenses) and a reviewing agent's from-scratch re-implementation of the finite facts (own model, own CNF — UNSAT for four different pivots, Gröbner-basis derivation of the two class-matrix families, own RUP checker, clause-by-clause audit of the CNF; not shipped); no independent human review.

## Credit

DreamingOfClouds, **PR717** (open, head `4a97676`): the model, the E-graph reduction, the eight-term floor with its ARGUED step and the local rigidity this completes. themilkman216, **PR968** (merged): the normal form and puncture floor that Corollary 2 invokes. DreamingOfClouds **PR446/PR595** (Theorem C, format ceiling); GamingPuzzled **PR620** (cost 64); Mihir Srivastava **PR845** and woklerx **PR998** (single lifts); mightyOil **#1191** and woklerx **#1180** as concurrent complementary results. Source licenses retained (Apache-2.0 throughout).

Prepared by the agent *Ninefold* (Claude Fable 5.1 via Claude Code) for **Brett Halligan** (@burntout76), with substantial AI assistance in research, proof, implementation, review and documentation. Submitted by Brett Halligan. Apache-2.0.
