title: Research: classify the P112 masked decoder coordinate component (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Masked decoders leave the odd-pair entries unconstrained, so the existing all-pairs copy-cost floor does not directly apply. This scoped research result classifies the entire complex connected component containing the standard P112 eight-term decoder: every point is a factor-basis change and reciprocal row scaling of an all-pairs decoder. Consequently every continuous path of exact eight-term masked solutions from that starting point retains copy cost at least 64.

Both factors may leave the root-coordinate space. The exact 6,720 × 1,792 Jacobian has rank 1,617 and nullity 175. A written open-and-closed orbit argument extends the tangent calculation to the whole component, including exclusion of escape through deficient-rank factors. This is stronger than the trivial local floor from support persistence.

**No new κ or physical supplier is claimed.** Disconnected components, discrete/approximate searches and decoders with nine or more terms remain open. The cost corollary inherits PR1077/968's geometric classification premise and separate-term pairing-rank convention. All physical/compiler, hosting, precision/tape and analytic obligations remain unchanged.

The research package and its path-scoped `.github/workflows/p112-masked-tangent-audit.yml` workflow are added. Start with README.md and PROOF.md; the selected frontier, upstream and frozen inputs are untouched.

## Task and overlap

Base: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`, verified as current main before submission. Task selector: `complex-masked-decoder`, nonce `c4cb3fadd3712193711993a2fb0dac76`; TASK.md records the bounded domain and method.

PR1191 (`640b43bb13d3d476a2d83b74ef0d33f14d1b5711`) proves one-sided root-linear masked rigidity for arbitrary term count. This result instead treats two unrestricted factors, eight terms and one connected component. PR1180 (`75b408646d558147a4eb250fc407d1fbfcb8df4e`) treats overcomplete all-pairs root-linear factors. Discussion1210 proposes an arbitrary-term root-star support census; it is complementary and remains provisional. Exact predecessor heads and source hashes are in SOURCES.json. The final overlap scan covered 820 open PRs including drafts through #1211 and all six active discussions.

## Validation

Python 3.10+; standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/p112-masked-tangent-audit/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/p112-masked-tangent-audit/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/p112-masked-tangent-audit/test_package.py
```

Passed on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.14.7:

- Primary sparse F101 elimination checks a 1,617-square minor and 175 independent integer kernel directions; nine semantic controls pass.
- Separate symmetric/antisymmetric F3 bitset implementation obtains ranks 868 + 749, integer kernel dimensions 28 + 147, and six control groups.
- Five package tests cover optimized isolated relocation, read-only replay, corrupted evidence, changed/missing proofs and omitted source pins.
- PR1077's complete scoped verifier, selected-record integrity, five named selected-record tests and whitespace checks pass.

The proof and code received separate AI review; the identified source-inventory hardening is included. No Lean, full selected-supplier cold replay or independent human mathematical review is claimed. VALIDATION.md records commands and limits.

## Hosted CI

[The focused GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/DavidAriasC/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38462049339) **passed** on Ubuntu 24.04 with **Python 3.10 and 3.14**, for PR head `8867cf20fbe0d3960f68bcffca118a5ac0624f7f`. Both jobs passed the primary and independent certificates, optimized relocation/rejection controls, inherited complex-floor replay, selected-record integrity/regressions, and unchanged-tracked-files check. No test failures required mathematical or verifier changes.

These are **fork-hosted** results. Upstream fork workflows remain behind GitHub's maintainer-approval gate; they are not represented as passed. The unfiltered historical fork suites were canceled because they do not cover this package. Their workflows and tests were not changed.

## Credit

DreamingOfClouds (PR717/595), themilkman216 (PR968), woklerx (PR1077 and complementary PR1180), Philipp / mightyOil (PR1191), Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (PR620), icekylinx (P112), and the retained supplier lineage retain attribution. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, mathematics, both implementations, review and writing. Apache-2.0.

title: Finite construction: exact two-helper k8 gauges save 576 scalar primitives
body:

Scaling L251 and L427 saves 576 scalar primitives per complex invocation in each orientation. This is optimal among dyadic gauges on at most two of the 237 eligible helpers, with ADD topology and existing SCALEs fixed. Each pair's cost is affine between vertical, horizontal and diagonal break lines. Boundary charges make it coercive; unit discounts lower boundary values. A minimum therefore occurs at an integral intersection. Independent integer-grid enumeration confirms every pair minimum. Exact replay checks all 712 input columns. Native hosting remains unchecked; no new kappa is claimed. Hanson Sun, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, credits @woklerx's PR1161, Sagar Thakrar's lowerer and the retained supplier lineage.

title: Scoped negative result: restored dirty borrowing cannot match CK/JP8 scratch prices
body:
Restoring borrowed dirty registers cannot replace the disposable coefficient-work register at the existing CK/JP8 boundary price. This scoped negative result proves minimum costs **4**, **6**, and **9..10** for a two-cycle, three-cycle and disjoint two-plus-three-cycle, even with **any finite number of restored dirty donors**. The disposable-scratch comparators cost 4, 5 and 8. **No new kappa.**

The new step is a write-count/read-only-specialization lemma: at the relevant short budgets at most one donor can be written, and donors that are only read can be specialized away for a lower bound. Complete GL(3,3), GL(4,3) and GL(6,3) radius-four searches then exclude the cheaper words. Python and separately represented C++ implementations compare every one of **2,373,527 states and minimum distances**; exact Fraction witnesses supply upper bounds.

For all **168** frozen historical boundary records, the resulting lower bill is **238 versus 224 primitives per real component**, at least 28 extra real primitives per orientation under separate component lowering. This is a local scalar-interface obstruction, not a physical row-saving result or a selected-supplier change. Nine versus ten for the combined cycle remains open.

Review `research/complex-restored-borrowed-boundaries/PROOF.md` for the reduction and its hypotheses; README, exact source pins, complete receipt, controls and validation are in the same package. Research and refreshed submission base: **1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe**. OS assignment seed 33. Selected PR1094 remains unchanged.

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/complex-restored-borrowed-boundaries/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/complex-restored-borrowed-boundaries/test_package.py
```

Expected marker: `PASS_COMPLEX_RESTORED_BORROWING boundaries=168 states=2373527 costs=4,6,>=9 arbitrary_restored_donors no_new_kappa`.

Validation: complete replay and all 11 test groups pass on CPython 3.14.6 and 3.9.6/macOS arm64; 37 gate omissions, dirty-donor destruction, seven source corruptions, receipt corruption, dense matrix/product oracles and offline relocation are covered. Byte-identical receipt regeneration and a full six-register UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer replay pass. Selected-record integrity and its five tests pass. Added focused Linux workflow is pending; no hosted CI pass is claimed. No full native/phase/hosting/precision/tape/all-size/outer-theorem replay is claimed.

Credit **ToikY's PR969** (`d1ee3f46a6167ea54913e070af3161c71a99e1f2`) for the actual deferred-swap construction; PR1145's narrative called it PR971 incorrectly. The retained source bytes are unchanged. This adapts Ross Richardson's PR1145 (`fd4d5ffc448361297e717aa30eafed578caf8e61`) checkers to the explicitly excluded borrowed-register contract and adds the universal reduction. **woklerx's PR1095** addresses the distinct monomial-prefix/disposable-workspace class. Credit also Sagar Thakrar PR696, faw01 PR839, Chafik Boukhalfa PR626, Jeremy Kothe PR622, icekylinx and the retained supplier lineage.

title: Tooling: 1.70x faster exact historical ternary frame checks (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Tooling improvement; no new kappa.**

This opt-in tool speeds up the historical ternary frame checker by caching results for exact ordered frame pairs. It retains both orientations, every physical edge, and the existing rational arithmetic. Complete matrix-and-edge transcripts and published small-control fields for h=8 and h=9 match the retained checker. Timings use alternating fresh processes. The h=29 construction is not replayed, and kappa is unchanged.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`. Seed: **93**.
- Scope: `ternary-h8-h9-physical-edge-pair-memoization`; [task card](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/cb5a79f12531022c6fcd2fe592b5030d4e3ae9e7/research/ternary-frame-cache/CLAIM.json), [20 exact source pins](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/cb5a79f12531022c6fcd2fe592b5030d4e3ae9e7/research/ternary-frame-cache/SOURCES.json).
- Nearest work: #154 (scheduling/paired-cube frames), #367 (PR364 integer elimination). Object here: historical `ternary_side.verify_invocation_frames`; original rational routines and full schedule retained.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/ternary-frame-cache/verify.py --out /tmp/ternary-frame-cache-93 --pairs 3
```

Expected: `PASS_IDENTICAL_TERNARY_FRAME_REPLAY 84672 edges; ... ratio of medians`. Fresh output directory required.

| Local Python 3.14.6 / macOS arm64, three alternating pairs | Reference | Cached |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median wall seconds | 11.525 | 6.775 |

title: Research audit: exact interior-carry criterion for compact controls (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Mathematical audit / research note; no new kappa.** Outside the retained good set, the earlier-source compact-control word can get the target right while corrupting a dirty temporary. `g_i + z_i*t_i < A` for every `i < n-1`, where `A=2^(K-1)` and `B=2^G`.

The final outgoing target carry is harmless. The resulting invariant good fraction is exactly `((B-1)/B)^n * (1-(B-2)/(4*A))^(n-1)`. title: Research: nine-term complex E8 decoders are one-sided overcomplete representations (seed 42, no new kappa)
body:
**Status: research note / scoped structural result. No κ claim, no supplier word.** Only `research/nine-term-decoder-normal-form-seed42/` is added. The selected record (PR1094), `upstream/` and every existing file are unchanged.

## What was learned

PR968 and PR1077 prove the punctured complex E8 copy-cost floor for **exactly eight** all-pairs terms. Nine or more terms remained open (PR968 §6, PR1071, PR1077, PR717 mixed-β). The live roots span R^8 throughout, which holds for p ≤ 56. The statements below hold over R or C with ordinary transpose:

- **Theorem A (any m).** D = RA + N1 and T = RB + N2 with RᵀN = 0. Exactness ⇔ ABᵀ = 2I, N1Bᵀ = 0, AN2ᵀ = 0, N1N2ᵀ = 0. The pairing ker A × ker B is nondegenerate.
- **Corollary B (m = 9).** At most one factor leaves the live root code. An exact ten-term decoder with outside-code columns on both factors is checked, so this is specific to nine terms.
- **Corollary C.** A one-sided nine-term decoder is the same as an overcomplete representation. Choose nine column normals b_k with one dependency z, and give each live line *any* coefficient vector with Σ d_ik b_k = 2r_i.
- **Lemma D.** Proportional column normals merge without increasing cost. So |supp z| ≤ 2 reduces to eight terms, where PR968/PR1077 give cst ≥ max(72−p, 56) for p ≤ 24.
- **Propositions E–G.**
  - Terms outside the dependency are rigid.
  - Each line avoids exactly one ratio class of masked terms.
  - A line avoiding two masked terms is orthogonal to a canonical nonzero vector.
  - On P120 all 511 codeword supports span R^8, so a one-sided nine-term decoder costs exactly 81 − Σ δ_k. Beating 72 needs Σ δ_k ≥ 10, which forces a masked row support of ≤ 36 lines.
  - A census of all 130,305 support pairs shows that 39,255 do not span. So the pairwise argument alone cannot close P120; this is recorded as open.

**Residual class.** For p ≤ 24, the floor can fail at nine terms only for decoders with one factor outside the root code and |supp z| ≥ 3. "Exactly one" uses the open PR1180 for the both-root-code case; it is cited, not re-verified.

**Evidence, not proof.** Exact nine-term decoders were built from weight frames of maximal subsystems. In the A8 frame every root is 2- or 3-sparse. The decoders cost 76–81 on P120. A bounded annealing search (27 runs, seeds 0–2, 3000 moves) found best ratio 67/111 = 0.6036, nothing below 64/112 or 7/13. This is a failed search over the stated domain, not an impossibility theorem.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/nine-term-decoder-normal-form-seed42/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_NINE_TERM_NORMAL_FORM_S42 checks=80 pairs=130305 frames=5 A8_cost=81` (~35 s, stdlib only). It also passes under `-O`, from a relocated `git archive` copy, and alongside `scripts/verify_selected_result.py`. `search.py` reproduces `SEARCH.json`. Not run: hosted CI, repository-wide suites, Lean.

## Scope, overlap, credit

- Not covered: a floor for the residual class, m ≥ 10, masked/E-graph-only decoders, p > 56, physical realization. All selected-record conditions are inherited.

## Result

Conditional **κ = 0.001675608585476885** (exact `335121717095377/200000000000000000`).

- Over #1169 (`0.001675568675201533`): **+3.9910275352e-8**, i.e. **0.0023819%**.
- Over #1148 (`0.001675560947524449`): +4.76e-8.
- Conservative endpoint: `0.001675608582632503`.

## Construction

The base is #1169: #1148's joint entrance groups 603/611/635 with an exact T37 owner flow. This PR adds one ingredient to it: jeremykothe2's width-neutral eighth triangle-hybrid slot **X54/E589** (holders 335, 367) from #1130.

- **Recipe.** The edits and frames are identical to `RECIPE-X54-ends7.json`, rebased onto `k8-joint-entrances/FULL-WORD.json.gz` (content `1f666402…`). The joint-entrance recipe changes only frames, and none of its 39 changed B frames lies on an X54 position.

  - the 159,840 whole-helper roles in 333 calls;

- **Provider identity.** This is the only new identity. It is rebound name-by-name (15 identities) to a fresh native replay of the new word, and the SPEC is re-frozen through the unchanged discovery/freeze path.
- **Ceiling.** #1148's all-T signed-dual bound, pinned to the X54 plan, gives a grid ceiling of exactly `0.001675608585476885`. The construction attains the fixed-family ceiling for this local word and inventory.

The global profile is `{1:788046,2:165834,3:137862,4:41958,5:27972,8:2664,48:11374}`, with live stock 33,152 and deficit 11,840.

## Validation (passed)

- **Local audit.** The independent exact local audit of the X54 word passes on all 704 columns in both orientations (`PASS_INDEPENDENT_EXACT_FORWARD_AND_DUAL_ENDPOINT_FRAMES_ENTRANCES_CONES`).
- **Local controls.**
  - #1148's 27 entrance controls.

- **Native replay.** A fresh five-stage native replay of the new word.
- **Strict T37 admission** with the retained #1129 engines:
  - bind, emit, audit, invoice and assembly;
  - 69 admission and 12 bit controls;
  - the independent owner checker with 7 controls;
  - all 47 outer inequalities;

- **Fixed-family upper bound.** `PASS_ALL_T_K8_JOINT_X54_SIGNED_DUAL_UPPER_RELAXATION 0.001675608585476885`.

title: Research: masked root-star trimmed-star census on P112; exact covering bound 784/13, 64 falsified for beta-7 atoms (no new kappa)
body:
## Status

**Scoped research result / method-obstruction on the masked decoder model; no new kappa, no supplier.** Only `research/masked-root-star-floor/` is added. The selected record (kappa 836330098538459/5e17), `certificates/selected-result.json`, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

## Task and scope

Task selector draw: track `complex-mechanisms`, OS-random seed `b27e6ad9fd261c4b4134d5d02523a8a1`, card `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `7acfe4d9cac04f7ba4cb`), refined to the trimmed-star mixed-beta slice of CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#717's D1 open problem. Base `e208d5e77a204252f92b395aae271679cc3a56f0`; the full task card is `research/masked-root-star-floor/CLAIM.md`. Coordination claim: [discussion CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1210](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1210).

Object: on P112 in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717's B14 model, masked E-graph identity (exactness only on the 6720 even-pair entries, `x_i.y_j = 0` off-diagonal, `x_i.y_i = 4`; the 5824 odd entries fixed by cost-0 singleton terms), root-star decoders with trimmed supports `N(alpha)` — the pairing-rank-7 mixed-beta atoms excluded from CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#717 D1(b)'s flat-support census — with **unrestricted real coefficients on both factors and any number of terms**.

## What this establishes

1. **Complete census.** All 240 root-star supports (120 normals x {untrimmed `C(alpha)`, self-trimmed `N(alpha)}`) and all **57,600** ordered support pairs with exact F2 pairing ranks and exact frame-hit counts over the 1260 E-graph 8-cliques. Rank histogram: beta 7: 7,616 atoms; beta 8: 37,440; beta 9: 12,544.
2. **Exact covering bound for the family.** Every frame is an 8x8 rank problem, so >= 8 terms meet every frame; `cst >= 10080 * min(beta/hit)`. The complete minimum is `beta/hit = 7/1170`, so the frame-substitution bound over the whole root-star family is exactly **784/13 ≈ 60.31** (vs the ~43.8 of CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#717 D1(e)'s sampled general-support bound).
3. **The hoped-for 64 bound is falsified.** Beta-7 trimmed atoms meet **1170** of the 1260 frames (the card's threshold for a 64 bound was 1102), e.g. `(N(f), N(beta))` with `f` a frame normal and `<f,beta>` odd; the eight best atoms are recorded in `RESULTS.json` as leads. So nine or more cheap trimmed stars at total cost 63-64 are **not** excluded by frame counting; the family's assembly question is pinned to the exact window `[784/13, 64]`.
4. **All the slack lives in the trimmed atoms.** Over atoms of pairing rank >= 8 the bound is **exactly 64**, sharp: the eight coordinate stars `d_k = t_k = (<r_i,f_k>)_i` are trimmed root-star atoms of the census, satisfy `sum_k <r_i,f_k><r_j,f_k> = 2<r_i,r_j>` on every entry, and cost 8 per term (cst 64). Any root-star decoder whose terms all have rank >= 8 therefore costs >= 64 at any term count, masked or not.

The written argument (covering lemma, reduction lemma, falsification record, scope) is `research/masked-root-star-floor/PROOF.md`.

## Reproduce

Python 3.10+, standard library only, from the repository root:

```text
python research/masked-root-star-floor/verify.py
```

Expected: 28 PASS lines and `FAILS: none`, including

```text
PASS C.bound-beta-ge-8-is-64 | bound over beta>=8 atoms = 64
PASS C.census-complete | max hit/beta = 1170/7 at (a0,tr=False,b2,tr=True) beta=7 hit=1170; bound = 784/13
PASS E.coordinate-cst-64 | cst = 64
```

The run rebuilds the 120-line E8 model and the full 57,600-pair census from scratch and compares every field of the recomputed receipt with the committed `RESULTS.json`. A corrupted receipt (altered hit count) is rejected with a field diff and exit 1 (checked); the run also passes under `python -O`. Exact integer and F2 arithmetic throughout; no network, no third-party packages.

## Overlap and credit

- **DreamingOfClouds** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717 https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/595 https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/604: the B14 model, the masked reduction D1(a), the mixed-beta open problem, and the sampled covering bound D1(e) whose exact family value this PR computes.
- **woklerx** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968 https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1077 (with the seed44/seed48 packages): the eight-term all-pairs floor and its complex extension; both explicitly defer masked E-graph identities, which this PR addresses in one bounded family. **Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/620: star floors and the complex frame decoder of cost 64. **Mihir Srivastava** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/845: fixed-reader ninth total (scope excludes masked completions).
- **Concurrent masked results found in the final overlap refresh, all complementary.** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1212 (E-graph eight-term floor via rank-8 gauge rigidity) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1213 (masked coordinate component, eight terms; it cites [discussion CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1210](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1210) as the announced scope of this census) both leave nine-or-more terms open. https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1191 closes masked identity at arbitrary term count when one factor is root-linear; the trimmed, non-root-linear star atoms censused here are outside that hypothesis. Bit-side star label-code results (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/631 https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/669 https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/725 https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/732 https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1171) are a different model and are not imported.

## Remaining obligations and limits

No construction below 64 is claimed or attempted; the assembly of the recorded beta-7 leads (nine or more terms, every frame met by a rank-8 restricted block) is the open step, in the exact window `[784/13, 64]`. Not covered: deeper trims, unions of stars, non-star supports (CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#717 D3's P111/P104 hits are non-star), general supports, punctures other than P112. The favorable-cost accounting is unchanged (one cst unit is +2.81% of `b`; complex-side changes are capped by the CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#589 bit supplier at kappa 0.001730427469823602); nothing here lowers cst, and realization charges (centre reads, frame legality, dirty restoration) are not priced because no construction is offered. Finite replay is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem; the all-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source, hosting, precision/tape and analytic obligations of the selected construction remain inherited and unchecked here. The repository-wide suite and the selected cold replay are not rerun for this isolated additive package.

Prepared by **Navinor** with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

title: Research construction: sharp restoration cost for fixed readers
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Research construction and sharp boundary cost; no new kappa. Fixed children
`C_i(D,W)=(D+R_i W,-W)` can keep their readers unchanged while the parent
negates the smaller output between calls. The exact uniform boundary minimum
is `(k mod 2)N + 2 floor(k/2) min(N,d)` in the declared complete-register
negation alphabet. A full two-pass dirty echo makes the returned output depend
only on the source and restores all incoming scratch.

The seed-selected five-child, width-eight, one-output example uses **200
scalar instructions versus 256 eager**, saving 56 negations. The package
includes the written proof, recursive ADD/NEG and storage recurrences, source
copies, both child directions, data accesses, descriptor reads and preparation
charges. All ten added files are in `research/output-sign-restoration-seed51/`.

**The child boundary is a real restriction.** A compiler allowed to rewrite
inside the explicit matrix leaves can beat both words. No optimal matrix
algorithm, physical supplier, runtime gain, tape realization, rounding theorem,
or complete multiplication proof is claimed. Intermediate observers also need
an additional priced interface because the physical output can be negated.

[Proof and scope](https://github.com/thakrarsagar/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f39574ae9b2e3cceb01e29cf48e134f409ec1b0f/research/output-sign-restoration-seed51/README.md) ·
[Exact certificate](https://github.com/thakrarsagar/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f39574ae9b2e3cceb01e29cf48e134f409ec1b0f/research/output-sign-restoration-seed51/CERTIFICATE.json) ·
[Source pins](https://github.com/thakrarsagar/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f39574ae9b2e3cceb01e29cf48e134f409ec1b0f/research/output-sign-restoration-seed51/SOURCE-PINS.json)

## Task and overlap

The user's recursive-interface assignment was refined to this exact immutable
reader contract. OS-random assignment seed **51**; local claim made within the
first eight minutes. No scope change after the claim and no pivot.

Investigation base: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`. The final fetch
found upstream `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`, with unchanged selected
PR1094 evidence. Its new submission guidance was inspected. This standalone
archive format retains its own exact replay and source pins, rather than
inventing a catalogue assignment for the user's explicit track.

Nearest predecessors are #1155 at `9821c6e9388f3fc097e94b72be9fa7b41a849527`,
#1199 at `85ac2880ea5bda44f28632b71ffa2b4e35ec6b7d`, #1203 at
`38459854fd5bb93099871a84324413bd0e338d8e`, and #1205 at
`e2008d7ffcad464da7ec21c69e8d8a8c91de4930`. Compatible nonzero readers and
observer distinctions are already their results. This package adds paid
output sign changes, the sharp uniform boundary count, and a recursively
executable source-only echo. It does not claim priority for dirty echo
cancellation, which also appears in #889.

Immediately before submission, checked 834 open PRs through #1225. The broad
keyword match #784 optimizes leaf-call counts for ordered echo trees, a
different object. #1211 prices balanced factor-tape travel; #1216 excludes
cheap restored CK/JP8 donors. No matching wrapper was found. All five current
discussions were checked; no pinned sprint issue existed, so the claim is local.
This is bounded overlap evidence, not proof of novelty.

## Validation

Standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/output-sign-restoration-seed51/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/output-sign-restoration-seed51/test_package.py
```

Expected: `PASS_OUTPUT_SIGN_RESTORATION ... saved_NEG=56 source_pins=3 kappa=unchanged`
and `PASS_OUTPUT_SIGN_PACKAGE relocation=1 corruptions=4`.

Passed with CPython 3.14.8 in normal and optimized mode and CPython 3.11.17
in optimized mode. Evidence includes all 21,840 gap schedules through six
children, 384 exact price comparisons, 384 recursive cases on all 3,168 basis
columns, literal inverses, rational dirty probes, depth-two/three dense cases,
seven mathematical controls and seven invalid-input controls. The standalone
package test rejects four real on-disk corruptions. Certificate regeneration
is byte-identical; all retained source hashes and base-context hashes match.

These are finite implementation checks alongside the written general proof,
not formal verification of the full multiplication theorem. The selected cold
replay, Linux execution and human peer review were not run. Hosted CI status
must be assessed separately. No selected construction or upstream file changed.

## Open next questions

The [next question](https://github.com/thakrarsagar/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f39574ae9b2e3cceb01e29cf48e134f409ec1b0f/research/output-sign-restoration-seed51/README.md#open-next-questions)
is whether a supported supplier has an indivisible sign-drifting child with
fewer outputs than workspace coordinates. First trace one candidate's complete
source-return map and retained boundary, then price routing and precision. No
such supplier has been identified here. If its terminal negation can simply be
removed, reject that candidate immediately.

## Credit

Prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in algebra,
implementation, verification and writing. Credits Aaron Wang / navinor for
#1155, Sagar Thakrar for #1199, mightyOil for #1203, Adam Gall for #1205, and
CubeJerry for #889. Three predecessor notes are retained byte-for-byte with
their notices; no predecessor implementation is imported. New material is
Apache-2.0 under the repository license. The selected Rohan Arun / Jeremy Kothe
construction and its earlier contributor chain remain unchanged.

title: Independent verification: derive PR540's pending ranges [15,22) and [1,29) from PR442's schedule (no new kappa)
body:
**Scope:** an independent source-binding check for open #540. No new κ, and the selected record is unchanged.

## Task card
- **Card:** `formal-interface-lemma` (independent-verification track, chooser seed `89b099639256052efb5bbfd359684b0f`). Scope is **refined** to "audit one theorem-to-source binding".
- **Base:** `49b3157d`. **Audited head:** #540 `acc1917034d10f464271ab115fda314fd4eee7a3` (`PhysicalSourceConnection.lean` blob `9a78d48f`, `generate_ownership_data.py` blob `63703310`).
- **Question:** #540's `pendingTag` gives idle child 1 the axes `[15,22)` and child 2 the axes `[1,29)` by hand. Lean checks only that these ranges contain the targets, and the extractor hard-codes the bases 15 and 1. Are these the actual pending sets from the source schedule? This is the next task named in the [handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166).

## Result
Both ranges are **exactly** the derived pending sets.

| Child | Pair | Levels | Window | Derived | #540 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1→2 | {2} | E₂ = `[15,22)` | `[15,22)` |
| 2 | 2 | −1→3 | {0,1,2,3} | q⊥⊕E₁⊕E₂⊕E₃ = `[1,29)` | `[1,29)` |

## Method
The checker is standard-library only and imports nothing from #434, #442 or #540.

- The hosted template is bound to `bit_template_sha256` in #442's `EXPECTED.json` on main, and the geometry is bound to the template.
- The exterior 7-block layout is read from all 120 ports' routes.
- Each `[q/2 | A_q]` chart is checked to be exactly orthogonal.
- Level model (from PR386): L₋₁ = span(q), L_ℓ = Q⁸⊕E₁..E_ℓ. All 10 idle ranks are checked against it.
- The windows are recomputed from the schedule.
- All 747 hosted routes `(child, off, w)` are mapped to `pending[off:off+w]` and compared with #540's `base+off`.

Six mutations are rejected: previous-level block, a range that includes the q axis, swapped children, L₋₁ = {}, an offset past the pending rank, and stage 2 removed from the window.

## Not covered
- This is a Python derivation, not a kernel proof.
- The ranks fix only dimensions. Identifying L₋₁ with span(q) relies on PR386's route identity, which is not re-proved here.
- The ascending order of axes within a child is a convention shared with #540's extractor; PR442 does not fix it.
- Only one invocation is checked.

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 -I -B research/pr540-pending-range-derivation/verify.py      # ~0.5 s
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr540-pending-range-derivation
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'     # 20 OK, 1 skipped
```
The two vendored inputs are byte-identical to #540's `inputs/` files of the same names; the SHA256 pins are in `verify.py`.

**Credit:** construction and hosting rule from #434/#442; bit geometry from PR386; the Lean formalization and gap identification are cheesegrader's #540. Prepared by Douglas Colkitt with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance. Apache-2.0.

**Feedback:** the endpoint-moment card (`independent-moment`) is already covered for the selected record by three code-disjoint engines (Mercator, base-two, atanh prime chain). The handoff thread was a better source of an unmet independent check.

title: Research consolidation: exact rational numerator and residue contracts
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Add `research/rational-residue-scope/`, an executable comparison of PR1057 exact additive borrowing, Ali Romman's PR1135 common-numerator/rounded contracts, and PR1159 binary residues. Exact rational factors with odd reduced denominators can use the same residue kernel when the completed map is integral and the signed endpoint has a strict recovery bound. This does not contradict PR1135 or implement rounded leaves.

On the frozen 52-factor, 1,376-call word, alternating central scales 1/3 and 3 preserve the complete integer product. The least common denominator of every formal rational prefix is exactly **9**, with an explicit `-2584/9` witness. The common-numerator data bound is **94 bits** using denominator 9 (194 using the conservative `3^65`); residue data need **56 bits**. The numerator widths are sufficient bounds, not minima.

Residues incur **2,406 additional preparation commands**, including inverses and all 208 coefficient conversions: **54,698 kernel-plus-preparation commands**, using 283 private bits. The package prices the original descriptors, inverse table and external routing. Admission/normalization, generic product-check workspace and coefficient-height costs, input/output conversion, controller dispatch and physical implementation remain separately charged obligations. No runtime, supplier-adoption or κ improvement is claimed.

## Task and overlap

Discussion/claim: #1202. Consolidation seed 99 was drawn before detecting the revised donation prompt; the existing assignment was retained. Card `scope-navigation`, **scope changed**: PR1159 already links PR1135, so a navigation-only edit would add little; the useful result is the source-bound representation comparison and finite construction. Its connection is a possible precision representation at exact additive boundaries, with no changed paid supplier profile.

Experimental base: `1b59b624d21924f8e3537cdc1ac52d3be6eda2fe`; submission base: `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`. Exact dependencies:

The changed hypothesis is simultaneous sharing at one station, extending independently chosen pairwise completions. Two separately implemented exhaustive censuses agree on every legal frame maximum. title: [Lean] Derive #540's pending ranges from the PR442 schedule (stacked on #540; no new kappa)
body:
**Stacked on #540** (base branch `stack/pr540-base` = #540 head `acc19170`). Once #540 lands, this PR retargets to `main`. It adds one directory, `research/lean-pending-derivation/`. **No #540 file is changed**, so #540's hashed manifests and receipts stay valid.

## What it closes
#540's `PhysicalSourceConnection.pendingTag` supplies the pending ranges `[15,22)` and `[1,29)` by hand. Its README notes that "neither Lean nor the source-extraction check binds these ranges to the source schedule". #1228 derived them in Python. This PR does the derivation in Lean 4.21 and proves it equal to #540's actual definition.

## Theorems
All are proved by `decide`, using only `propext` and `Quot.sound` (some use no axioms).
- `PendingDerivation.idle_ranks_and_nesting`: for all 10 idle events, levels nest and the derived pending size equals the scheduled rank.
- `pending_child1 / pending_child2`: `[15..21]` and `[1..28]`.
- `hosted_windows`: for all 16 tags, stage 2 is in the child's window, the host pair is not pair 0, and `offset+width ≤ |pending|`.
- `target_derived`: every extracted `targetMask` is exactly the `[offset, offset+width)` slice of the derived pending axes. This also checks the extractor's hard-coded bases.
- `PendingBinding.pendingTag_derived` and `pending_eq_derived`: #540's `pendingTag` and `pending` equal the derived masks.
- `PendingBinding.selected_invocation_completion_derived`: #540's completion theorem, restated with the derived mask.

Definitions: L₋₁ = {0}, L_ℓ = [0,8) ∪ E₁ ∪ … ∪ E_ℓ (E_s = exterior axes of the stage-s route), pending = L_target \ L_source, and windows follow PR442's last-touch rule. The schedule and blocks are a Python-extracted literal (`generate_pending_schedule.py --check`, byte-exact against #540's pinned inputs). This is the same trust boundary as #540's other literals.

Six mutation controls each fail because `decide` refutes the mutated statement:
- L₋₁ empty;
- L₋₁ set to the whole local block;
- exterior blocks off by one stage;
- the first two blocks swapped;
- child 1 advanced before the selected call;
- child 1 claimed on the previous block.

## Not covered
- The level model is a definition. Its agreement with the PR386 frames (L₋₁ = span(q) in the `B_port ⊕ I₅₆` chart) is not proved. It is constrained only by ranks, nesting and the extracted target masks.
- Ascending axis order within a child is the offset convention shared with #540's extractor.
- Only one invocation is covered. No cost, all-size or κ claim.

## Reproduce
```sh
cd research/lean-multi-host-source && lake exe cache get <the five Mathlib modules in BUILD.md>
lake build PhysicalSourceConnection     # 3m24s measured on Apple silicon with the Mathlib cache
cd ../.. && python3 research/lean-pending-derivation/verify.py   # ~17 s, prints PASS_PR540_PENDING_RANGES_DERIVED_IN_LEAN
```
`verify.py` runs the generator check, compiles the three modules against #540's build through `lake env`, audits the axioms of all seven theorems and runs the controls.

**Credit:** the Lean formalization, ownership literals and gap identification are cheesegrader's #540. Construction and hosting are from #434/#442, and the bit geometry is from PR386. The Python predecessor is #1228. Prepared by Douglas Colkitt with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance. Apache-2.0.

title: research: reduce calibrated endpoint gauges to exact source tours
body:
Restored target phases can appear to make separately addressed pair readouts cheaper. A constructive detour moves each target's visited gauge to its declared source at no greater phase-moment cost, preserving every old input and both individual read calibrations. This closes arbitrary endpoint-gauge timing within a specified family, rather than only one phase window.

For even h >= 6, separate restored sources, separate dirty ordered within-half pair targets, exactly two individually calibrated reads per target, and no role mixing, the written proof gives exact minima for every 0 <= p <= 1:

- Oriented coordinate phases, rank cap h-2: `2h(h-2)^p + h(h-4)`.
- With binary translations separately counted but assigned zero phase-moment charge: `2h(h-2)^p + h(h-4)2^(p-1)`.

Translations are not declared free machine operations. At h=10 the attaining translation-closed word has 50 phase calls **plus 30 translations**, compared with 80 oriented phase calls; both have rank mass 220 and 80 scalar ADDs. The translation identity is inherited elementary algebra, not a new supplier mechanism. No new kappa, multiplication speedup or full formal proof is claimed.

## Evidence

Only `research/calibrated-endpoint-gauge-tours/` is added. Python standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/calibrated-endpoint-gauge-tours/test_verify.py
python3 -I -B research/calibrated-endpoint-gauge-tours/verify.py NEW_RECEIPT.json
```

- Twelve complete words at h=6,8,10: direct, translation-closed, overlapping endpoint gauges with late negative reads, and normalized source detours.
- Sparse integer Laurent-monomial replay and independently implemented dense Gaussian-integer/projector replay agree on **11,371,520 old-input operator entries**.
- Exhaustive oriented phase-group searches cover **4,352 states** at h=4,6.
- Eight test groups pass in optimized isolated Python mode, including twelve record corruptions, changed readouts, source/dirty-target restoration failures and existing-output preservation.
- Fresh patch application and relocation to a path containing spaces pass; the complete regenerated receipt is byte-identical. The relocated replay took 14.43 seconds, peak RSS 15,548 KiB, Linux x86_64 / CPython 3.10.12, one low-priority CPU and a 4 GiB address-space limit. These are resource observations, not a matched speed comparison.

The all-p all-size theorem is a written argument. The executable detour normalizer certifies rank mass (p=1); it is not a general all-p shortest-path solver. Finite replay is not formal verification of the universal theorem or the multiplication algorithm.

## Scope, credit and overlap

The coordinate-phase and rank-priced residual framework is inherited from the project's stopped/partial-gauge lineage, including icekylinx's #104. The phase/translation identity is not claimed novel.

Inspected 823 open PR titles/bodies, active discussions, nearest public proof notes and later arrivals through #1227. Exact heads are recorded in `SOURCES.json`. Eumemic's #288 and CubeJerry's #907 concern broader abelian-metric claims; this proof derives its explicit coordinate metric and uses no general l1-embeddability premise. Navinor's #825 treats rational-frame XOR common flags, outside the present complex-phase model. #1227 prices fixed-child sign restoration and dirty echo, not calibrated pair-port tours. title: Research: close the masked root-star assembly gap with sharp cost 64 (no new kappa)
body:
PR #1226 leaves open whether nine cheap trimmed-star atoms can assemble into a masked P112 decoder below copy cost 64. This package closes that question: **the exact minimum for its entire root-star support family is 64**, for any finite term count and arbitrary real or complex coefficients. The existing coordinate decoder attains the bound.

The new constraint is simultaneous frame coverage. Every live orthogonal eight-frame needs eight rank-one contributions. Nine cost-seven atoms would need pairwise disjoint missed-frame sets; selecting one live normal from each produces nine pairwise nonorthogonal E8 lines. A short primitive-integer-dependence parity argument rules those out. Eight terms cannot include a cost-seven atom, and ten already cost at least 70. This strengthens #1226's correct averaged bound `784/13` without relying on pending eight-term rigidity proofs.

The supports must be **exactly** `C(alpha)` or their self-trimmed versions `N(alpha)` on the specified P112. Arbitrary free cost-zero corrections are allowed. Deeper trims, arbitrary subsets, non-star supports, other punctures and shared-copy pricing remain outside the theorem. **No new kappa, physical word or supplier admission is claimed.**

Only `research/masked-root-star-assembly/` is added. Start with its `README.md` and `PROOF.md`. The base is current main `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`; the selected record, upstream and frozen packages are unchanged. title: The end-cap wall: why copies are forced in the E8 skeleton's verifier model (no κ claim)
body:
> **What is claimed, and what is not.**
> **Scope.** The k8 / #1018-type local word of the E8 complex unit: 112 targets with ports u_t ∈ F₂⁹ (distinct, odd weight, u·u = 1), frames that are subspaces of F₂⁹, the verifier rules R1 (an ADD climbs both operands to one frame), R3 (frames are monotone) and E (every target register ends in perp(u_t)); fixed ports, fixed decoder, fixed targets (`gk_word.py:116`, `:102`, `:117`; `audit_local.py:137-138`, `:122`, `:115`, `:142`). The deletion experiments run on the gauge-forward word of that skeleton (the stage before the port, cold44 and layer stages), regenerated by `verify.sh` from vendored inputs; the census, bound and window rows run on the #1018 word.
> **Result.** (T, argued from the cited rule lines; instances checked) A direct read `y_t += s` at time τ forces the end frame of y_t to contain D_s(τ), the join of every frame register s had before τ; y_t must end in perp(u_t), so the read is legal only if D_s(τ) ⊆ perp(u_t), and otherwise one of four prices is paid: (a) a version of s (held or reconstructed), (b) a reorder that puts the offending operations after τ, (c) a FULL end or descent on the target (a rank unit per call), (d) a descent on s. (M) Deleting any of the 24 legal single S3 packet copies, the 16 hub copies or any of five larger families (up to 80 copies) leaves 4 to 64 targets ending FULL, one dimension outside perp(u_t), and no complement sink can host a FULL frame; all 30 distinct regenerated words pass the generator's own frame check and fail the verifier's end rule E (`gk_word.profile` run on two of them, the end-cap replay on all). (P) One unit costs −2.819% κ per call (linear to 32 units; no exact certificate at 35) against a helper worth ≈ +0.15% and a ceiling of +3.5152% for all 112 S4 copies, so a copy is about 19 times cheaper and the copies are economically forced where the obstruction fires. (E) The escapes we built are closed in their stated models: one-accumulator version reconstruction (0 orders, exhaustive over the 20-21 op cluster, four absorption variants), the snapshot hoist and slide (0 of 64, 0 of 86), rematerialising the 161 never-read helpers (0 of 65), coded target pairs and cold-slot holds (0 of 224), and the frame-conflict bound (111 helpers forced, 113 attained; #1140 proves a stronger 224 on the same word).
> **Not claimed.** No κ gain, no word, and no proof that the 268 S3/S4 copies are necessary for every skeleton or op multiset. The theorem is a necessary-condition and pricing statement for the verifier model above. It does not exclude **two accumulators** (+1 helper per group; not searched), a **new h = 8 family** (needs a different decoder; C.6 gives none at window ≤ 9 for the current one), **joint deletion and reordering** at scale (only single hoists and slides were run), asymmetric pairings that unpin Lemma R, non-projection rational labels, or helpers (arbitrary ends via `helper_final`). No deletion word passes the chain, so no κ is computed for one.

title: Research note: packing ceiling (+0.87%) and 1/99 budget for the selected complex local word (no new kappa)
body:
**Scope:** a scoped obstruction plus a screening tool. No new κ, and the selected record is unchanged.

## Task card
- **Card:** `complex-new-helper-inventory` (complex-mechanisms track, chooser seed `f10085bdeb241ba1cd1390dfec98a448`, base `e3bb23b4`). Scope is **refined** to the card's first experiment: an optimistic exact relaxation that rejects routes without headroom. It is applied to packing of the incumbent word and turned into a calculator for proposed inventories.
- **Question:** with the selected #1094 local word fixed, how much can any hosting, owner or idle-remainder repacking gain? What would a changed helper inventory have to pay to reach a = 1/99?

## Result
- The selected local word pays `{1:2412, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8}` per call (mass 5,586). Live stock is 896 data families per nine-stage replica, with all helpers hosted.
- PR1012's coverage identity (`mass = 72W + 64N`, re-checked on the selected profile) fixes the idle mass at 1,646 per call. Cost per unit mass `r^(-a)·73^(a-1)` does not increase with r, so the best idle histogram puts all idle mass at the halving-guard maximum rank, 51, with fractional counts allowed.
- **Packing ceiling:** a < **0.001690054109089**, so κ < **0.0016872026** (**+0.869%**). This is certified with exact rational intervals.
- **Previous record #1042:** it splits as the same local word plus an admissible idle histogram. The derived idle histogram `{1:2249, 2:1, 3:400, 7:3, 16:47, 48:4850}` matches its README exactly, and its endpoint lies below the same ceiling. So all of #1042→#1094 was packing, and less than 0.87% of that headroom remains.
- **Planning target a = 1/99:** written as `Σ n_r p_r(a) ≤ B(a)`, the word's excess spend is **20.4 times** the per-call budget (2.597 against 0.1275). Deleting all rank-1 children cannot reach it. A target-scale gain needs about 95% lower fully priced local excess spend, or a changed coverage law: unpaid coordinates per family, the 64-per-call centre charge, or families per call.
- **Tool:** `ceiling.ceiling(local, 73, 896, 9, 64)` screens any proposed per-call local profile in about a second.

## Not covered
- This is one local word, port count, template, coverage law and outer recipe.
- Open claims that change the word (#1148's joint-entrance word and its descendants, all ≤ 0.0016759) are **not** bounded by it. Their ceilings are an open question in the README.
- Fractional counts and every repacking are allowed, and realizability is not checked.
- `κ < a/(1+a)` is the retained planning ceiling.

## Controls
- An idle-rank cap of 52 is rejected by the halving guard.
- A local mass beyond the coverage law is rejected.
- One extra rank-1 child lowers the ceiling.
- 25 sampled integer idle histograms all have exact moment > 1 at the ceiling.

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-local-word-ceiling/verify.py   # ~10 s
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-local-word-ceiling
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
```

**Credit:** the coverage identity is PR1012's. The fixed-word packing-ceiling lineage is static44, PR525 and PR643; the catalogue mixture bound is Ali Romman's heterogeneous-owner-assembly. The construction credits are in the selected review. Prepared by Douglas Colkitt with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Change and mathematical scope

**Independent verification / scoped negative result; no new kappa.** This package independently corroborates the cost-64 floor for P112 masked root-star decoders with exact `C(alpha)` / self-trimmed `N(alpha)` supports, arbitrary complex coefficients, any finite term count and free rank-zero corrections.

The final overlap refresh found David Arias's #1236, which had already submitted the same theorem while this work was underway. Credit belongs to that concurrent submission; this PR adds independent evidence, not a stronger theorem or priority claim. Navinor's #1226 supplies the preceding support-family census and assembly question.

The distinct implementation generates E8 roots by Weyl reflections, checks pairing ranks by column elimination and exhausts maximal cliques with pivoted Bron-Kerbosch. It imports neither predecessor code nor the new primary checker. The primary checker separately reconstructs roots, uses row elimination and enumerates every clique. Both reconstruct all 57,600 ordered support-pair costs and 1,260 frames, verify frame annihilation and extension, exclude nine compatible live normals, and check the cost-64 coordinate decoder on all 12,544 entries. title: Research audit: ordered-subset bounds allow quadratic interval amplification
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Adversarial mathematical audit / scoped negative result; no new kappa.**

The retained PR905 precision proof bounds an interval by two prefix bounds. This package proves that the resulting quadratic dependence on an ordered-subset norm budget cannot be replaced by a linear dependence for general noncommuting factors, even with invertible factors and a disturbance on a real leaf destination.

In the unchanged PR628 seven-factor word, every ordered subset product has norm at most `G=M`, but the interval `[13,27)` has diagonal block `I-JD` with norm `1+M^2`. The complete ideal word has norm two and restores all dirty arrays. The README supplies an exact parametric proof for every real `M>=1`. A smaller four-factor example distinguishes arbitrary register perturbations from actual leaf-destination support.

This is evidence for retaining the generic conservative bound, not a bug in PR905 or a lower bound on the working precision of its cyclic leaves. The family violates their common-operator/commutation assumption. No actual deterministic rounding-failure trace, physical implementation, supplier admission, full theorem verification or new exponent is claimed.

## Task and overlap

Base: `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`. Assignment seed **64**, adversarial audit; the `uniform-transfer-audit` card is refined to this exact two-cut implication. Only `research/dirty-interval-propagator-audit/` is added.

The source pins are PR628 `0768f97d06c623b8211e651543c66135796b62bf`, PR905 `aab6c0b8f4574cb36285ab5dab3fcfad0cd2b69e`, and PR877 `80a60c0da2b916798167deb0ce3a5ef22fda147a`; consumed bytes also have base Git-blob and SHA256 bindings. Current main was refreshed to `dd6403f774a0891093a006ae9716c02e371b1fdb`; consumed sources and selected certificate are unchanged from the experiment base.

The final textual overlap refresh covered all **843 open PRs** and **16 discussion records**, with complete pagination reported and no warnings. Nearest overlap is [PR1085](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1085), which sharpens prefix coefficients. This contribution instead gives an explicit interval obstruction and the distinction between arbitrary and leaf-supported perturbations. PR1054, PR1093 and PR1211 cover different accuracy or tape obligations. No literature-priority claim is made. The local claim, bounded domain and coverage are in TASK.json; no pinned sprint issue was present.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-interval-propagator-audit
```

Expected: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/dirty-interval-propagator-audit outcome=negative-result`.

- All **9,772** nonempty intervals through eight factors, both signs; **9,342** preceding-leaf destination columns. The first unordered monomial appears at four factors generally and seven for destination-supported inputs.
- **26** literal dispatcher comparisons; **16** exact dense cases; independent full-matrix multiplication, Gauss-Jordan two-cut reconstruction and dirty vector trajectories.
- Positive prefix/inverse-prefix controls at **446** boundaries; **six** mathematical separation controls; **seven** passing package tests, including source/receipt faults and read-only relocation.
- Python **3.12.13** isolated optimized replay matches the receipt generated under **3.14.6**. All **25** selected-record tests pass. Canonical mathematical receipt SHA256: `1cd6367958cd6eb107840c79190409c22ac11aad9a7d9278b4b4ed5a2f2d98ad`.

The finite census supports the written argument; it is not an all-size formal proof. The selected cold replay, repository-wide historical suites and hosted CI were not run for this local scoped package.

## Credit

Credit Chafik Boukhalfa for PR628/905, Gareth Davidson for PR877, and the retained predecessor lineage. Prepared for **Hanson Sun (@bbMisk)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in research, proof, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0; predecessor files and attribution remain unchanged. No independent human or proof-assistant review is claimed.

title: Research audit: two-pass compact-control guard and exact later-source density
body:
**Mathematical audit / research note; no new kappa.** Checking the sharper earlier-source guard only before the first call can miss dirty-field corruption in the later-source routine. For `n=2,K=6,G=2,rho=1`, the unchanged physical word takes `(x,y,t,u,b)=(2,124,1,0,7)` to `(2,126,5,0,7)`: the target is right, but the temporary should remain 1.

This adds a proved two-pass invariant sufficient guard and its exact correlated density. With `B=2^G`, `A=2^(K-1)`, source bits `c_i`, control parities `p_i=u_i mod 2`, and target segments `2g_i+a_i`, require:

```text
t_i <= B-2                         for i < n
u_i + c_i < B                     for i < n-1
g_i + (p_i OR c_i)*t_i < A         for i < n-1
```

The complete-rectangle good fraction is `((B-1)/B)^n * (1 - 1/(2B) - (3B-2)*(B-2)/(8*A*B))^(n-1)`. At the example geometry it is **1971/4096**, versus **81/1024** for the retained later-source guard and **63/512** for PR763's source-dependent carry condition with the original target guard. All twelve swaps, ten rotations, source access, highest-bit completion and full exceptional-repair costs remain.

The original construction is correct. PR1219 explicitly excludes later-source calls, and PR763 retains the old target guard. This contribution composes their results and adds the correlated density and full-map controls. The guard describes individually safe subcalls with no interior source-load carry; it is **not the global exact agreement set**. No production predicate, supplier, selected frontier or `upstream/` file changes.

title: Research audit: exact phase criterion for selected PR1094 residual charts
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

An orthogonal rebase can preserve the active projector, every spectator axis, support and amplitude magnitudes while changing the selected supplier's exact complex residual. Add `research/selected1094-chart-phase/`, a source-bound adversarial audit of this implication. **The selected construction passes, and its existing stronger chart binding rejects the demonstrated mutant. No production defect or new κ is claimed.**

For orthonormal active columns U and V=US with S orthogonal over F2, the products of the inherited `C_q=((1+i)I+(1-i)X_q)/2` gates agree exactly iff every row of S has weight **1 modulo 4**. The proof derives the phase character for every dimension. The four-axis `I+J` rebase is the smallest bad case: `i/4` becomes `-i/4` at one displacement while the diagonal stays `-1/4`. A six-axis nonpermutation rebase supplies a positive case. The quadratic-refinement principle is classical; the scoped application and executable evidence are the contribution.

## Task and overlap

Card `supplier-boundary-audit`, **refined** to normalized physical residual charts and exact phase. Random chooser nonce `08486e2f4cb05dd9e1b849fa4eff7033`, priority revision 2. Scoped claim: #1237. Experimental base `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`; submission base `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`, with scientific inputs unchanged.

Selected PR1094 source `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810`, parent PR1087 `589d1cedf5ef5f231182f4ec86408616311a8af0`. The inputs are the actual selected replay archive and literal owners, not historical copied evidence directories. SOURCE/TASK metadata pins all inputs and the original task.

PR1209 (`d1ba263139ceb6eb811628b7560a3f87f3c9652e`) audits pending-axis independence and chronology, excluding spectator charts. PR1149 (`f66dd4019d67a9660921bc204532306b47f4196e`) audits canonical-frame rank. PR702/712 audit historical local wrapper phases. This contribution checks the normalized residual's physical active-basis phase refinement and current emitted-chart binding; it does not replace those distinct checks. Exact parallel heads and credit are in NOTICE.md.

The final 21:05 UTC overlap snapshot covers all 844 open PRs through #1247, nine Discussion threads/comments and 324 local records, with complete pagination and no refresh warnings. Declared literal-search coverage is recorded; no matching investigation was found. Historical PR407 is a separate entrance-frame construction. This is not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/selected1094-chart-phase/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/selected1094-chart-phase/production_check.py
python3 -I -O -B research/selected1094-chart-phase/test_package.py
```

All 69,120 roles /144 calls /10,002 emitted charts pass. The check covers 53,300,658 Gram entries and all 10,008 `(chart,width)` signatures. Literal physical convolution, an independent subset formula and chart transport agree on 5,348,224 coefficients in both signs. All 23,817 orthogonal matrices in dimensions 1–6 pass the exact criterion over 2,996,852 coefficient comparisons. Six semantic controls and eight package tests cover operator columns, spectator fibers, enumeration completeness, and actual optimized source/container/receipt corruption.

Separately, unchanged source `orthobasis`/`audit` function ASTs and the chart-table assertion pass their original input and reject two mutations. The verbatim source C-only evaluator matches 512 complete input columns. This is an **isolated source-predicate replay**, not the top-level admission driver. The mathematical verifier imports no predecessor executable code.

Complete registered Python 3.12 replay and a read-only relocated Python 3.14 replay pass with identical mathematical and production receipts. Mathematical receipt: `34f3fc87deac2e04323d140b490133f7ebe2788c66143c926b5e266126993269`. The selected-record check and metadata/Git pins also pass. Exact commands, limits and corrected harness issues are in VALIDATION.md. Hosted PR CI is reported separately.

The normalized local endpoint is inherited. Full scalar/native/phase-wrapper replay, cost/precision/tape invoices, all-size compiler, physical cover realization, analytic transfer and the multiplication theorem remain outside scope. No faster algorithm or improved paid profile is claimed.

title: Independent verification: the selected frontier1094 complex rank ledger, rebuilt from its emitted program (no new kappa)
body:
**Independent verification. No new κ, and no check is changed or weakened.** Card: `independent-moment` (ledger method), scope refined (see `TASK.json`).

## What this closes

The selected certificate `research/community-frontier1094-audit/ASSEMBLY.json` (`1122cb3a…`) prices an aggregate complex profile: `{1:349604, 2:60192, 3:62585, 4:20448, 5:11808, 7:7, 8:1152, 48:4866}`. The selected κ omits the complex surcharge. The PR552/PR559 review (`vendor/pr559/PROOF.md`, `d5d498ed…`) rests that on two premises: **(a)** an exact exhaustive recursive-child profile (lines 17, 24), and **(b)** no good/bad q-adic selector (lines 9, 24).

This package rebuilds that profile **from the emitted program the certificate binds**, using code-disjoint standard-library code that imports nothing from the repository:
- the hosted `GLOBAL-TEMPLATE`;
- both dispatched `LOCAL-PROGRAMS`, which must equal the copy embedded in the template;
- `CANONICAL-WORD` and `DATA-PHASES`, read from the committed capsule.

It then requires the rebuilt profile to equal the certificate.

It checks part of (a) at source level: the priced aggregate equals the emitted recursive children of the bound program. It does **not** address (b), and it does not re-prove the classification rule or the hosting semantics.

## Checks

**New in this package**
- **Byte binding (B1–B9).** The checks cover:
  - the capsule pin and safe tar members, with tar parsing restricted to the hashed bytes;
  - certificate ↔ record (a checkpoint once the frontier moves);
  - the template and owner-audit digests;
  - the dispatched inputs and the local-replay receipt, which names the same programs and word;
  - the owner map and its manifest;
  - the literal remainder frames;
  - `FULL-WORD`.
- **Dispatch (L1–L3, L9–L12).**
  - Each `(stage, replica)` is called once.
  - **The schedule's local sweeps dispatch exactly the calls**, each sweep acts on one replica, and there is one provider.
  - Orientation and pair follow the recipe.
  - The program hashes bind the calls, and the programs equal the copy embedded in the template.
  - The 704 distinct live route families include the data routes of the active pair.
  - **Every owner-map slot is executed by exactly one call route** in a live replica, and each helper route equals its slot.
- **A code-disjoint frame replay of the dispatched programs, bound to those calls (L4–L7).**
  - Each register runs from start to final.
  - Each climb leaves the register's current frame for a strictly larger nested frame, in its phase. F2 ranks are recomputed.
  - Each centre is bound to its frame, its carrier and the `centers` phase.
  - **Adapters, residual adapters and every scalar operand are checked at their registers' replayed frames.**
  - The phase sequence and the vocabularies are closed.
- **Chain to the certificate (L23).** The rebuilt ledger equals `ASSEMBLY.complex_profile`, the owner-audit profile and `INDEPENDENT1094`.

**Cross-checks of existing work, not claimed as new**
- Against #1209: helper widths, joint orthonormality of sibling pending axes, contiguous prefixes, and the idle-remainder recount, matched one for one with the emitted `idle_children` and literal frames.
- Against the in-lineage replay receipt: the per-call ledgers.
- Against #1091 R7 and `INDEPENDENT1094`: the mass and deficit identity.
- Against #1012: its coverage identity, checked per family (72 units per live family).
- Helper climb totals match the `FULL-WORD` width vector.

| Case | W | N | Rebuilt ledger | Remainders | D |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **frontier1094 (selected)** | 14336 | 144 | {1:349604, 2:60192, 3:62585, 4:20448, 5:11808, 7:7, 8:1152, 48:4866} | 7526 | 5120 |
| frontier1042 (checkpoint) | 14336 | 144 | {1:349577, 2:60193, 3:62608, 4:20448, 5:11808, 7:3, 8:1152, 16:47, 48:4850} | 7550 | 5120 |
| slots T8 (1042 capsule) | 7168 | 72 | {1:174763, 2:30105, 3:31283, 4:10224, 5:5904, 7:54, 8:576, 16:23, 48:2419} | 3783 | 2560 |
| leaver T8 (1042 capsule) | 7168 | 72 | {1:174763, 2:30105, 3:30275, 4:12240, 5:4896, 7:54, 8:576, 16:23, 48:2419} | 3783 | 2560 |

All four rebuilt ledgers equal their assemblies. The last two cases are in-capsule ancestor assemblies, bound only through the capsule pin. The receipt also carries the values that #1200 (item 3) asks for: `local_profile_per_call`, `idle_histogram` and `live_families_per_call` (W, N, 896 live families per replica, 9 stages).

**Controls:** 43 tests, about 10 s. There are 36 semantic controls; each asserts the first check that rejects it.
- **Frame replay:**
  - descending, chain-broken and register-moved climbs;
  - a flipped centre;
  - an adapter or scalar at the wrong frame;
  - an extra phase marker.
- **Dispatch:**
  - a repointed local sweep, which leaves one call run twice and one never;
  - a foreign provider;
  - a multi-replica sweep;
  - **a slot parked in a phantom replica, with a ghost copy left behind**;
  - a whole stage dropped.
- **Hosting:**
  - a label-disjoint dependent axis;
  - a rank-0 child made pending through an orthonormality-preserving axis;
  - slot gaps;
  - duplicate or dependent remainder frames.
- **Certificate tampering.**

There are also 6 packaging controls (decoys, a foreign replay receipt, a foreign owner map, a flipped byte, unsafe tar members) and the positives.

A post-PR soundness review (second commit) found that slot execution, sweep dispatch and non-paid event frames were unchecked. No committed result was affected, and all are now closed with controls.

## Overlap and credit

- **#1209** (akiva8201-dotcom, `d1ba2631`) already checks the pending-axis independence, helper widths, prefixes and idle-suffix profile from package inputs. Here they are **cross-checks, not claimed as new**.
- **The in-lineage `hpe_audit_local.py`** (receipt in the capsule; ported by **#1184**, woklerx) already frame-replays both programs, including scalar and wrapper frames. Ours is code-disjoint, adds the binding to the template's calls, sweeps and owner map, and checks scalar frame tags, not arithmetic.
- **The coverage identity** comes from our **#1012**. **#1240** (Douglas Colkitt / Mister-Meeseeks) uses it as a premise.
- **Charts and phases** belong to **#1255** (bitplane) and are not validated here.
- **Complementary:** #1112, #1142, #1149 and #1198.
- **`INDEPENDENT1094`** takes the local factor from the word's self-reported `local_profile` and hard-codes W and N. This package derives both from the emitted program.

title: Review aid: packing ceilings of 14 open complex kappa claims (stacked on #1240; no new kappa)
body:
**Stacked on #1240** (it reuses `research/complex-local-word-ceiling/ceiling.py`). Once #1240 lands, this PR retargets to `main`. No new κ. **No claim is accepted, rejected or reviewed by this PR.**

**Card:** `complex-new-helper-inventory` (complex-mechanisms, chooser seed `9fe32a6efcf929bf30bb65fb781eb095`, base `dadfea6e`). Scope is refined to the card's "reject routes without headroom" step, applied to inventories already in the review queue. This answers #1240's first open question.

## What it does
30 open PRs state κ above the selected 0.001672660197076918. For each, I searched one package for:
- a complex profile whose κ equals the title κ;
- live stock W and call count N;
- an idle histogram consistent with the coverage law `mass = 72W + 64N`.

**14 claims** qualify. They are pinned by head, path and Git blob in `SNAPSHOT.json`; `rebind.py --fetch` re-reads every blob. Each profile splits into local word plus idle, and #1240's exact relaxation caps any repacking of that word.

## Result
All 14 obey the coverage law at 896/9 families per call, and every endpoint lies below its own cap. They use **9 distinct local words**:

| Word family | Caps on κ | Claims | Headroom left |
|---|---|---|---|
| selected-type (W1, W2 = selected, W4, W5) | 0.0016872026–**0.0016873148** | #1124 #1129 #1130 #1131 #1152 #1157 | 0.77–0.86% |
| #1148 joint-entrance (W3, W6–W9) | 0.0016836800–0.0016843188 | #1148 #1178 #1193 #1195 #1196 #1204 #1225 #1239 | 0.47–0.52% |

- **No repacking of any covered word passes κ < 0.0016873148.**
- The leading #1148 line sits on words whose caps are **0.17–0.21% below** the selected word's. Those words move local mass from rank 1 to rank 2 (5,590 against 5,584–5,586 per call). The line leads because it packs closer to its cap. Its gain is in realizability, not in a better paid profile.
- For reviewers: claims on the same word differ only in packing. A claim on a lower-cap word can never overtake the best packing of a higher-cap word. The largest remaining packing prize is about +0.7%, for packing W1 or W2 as tightly as the #1148 line packs its own words.

## Not covered
- 16 claims (#1104 #1107 #1111 #1117 #1121 #1150 #1154 #1169 #1172 #1175 #1176 #1183 #1192 #1201 #1207 #1218) do not record a profile matching the title κ together with an idle histogram in one package. They are listed in `SNAPSHOT.json`.
- #1172's head moved during the snapshot, and the fetched head was used.
- Caps are planning bounds (`κ < a/(1+a)`). They allow fractional counts and ignore helper widths, windows and chronology.

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-queue-ceiling-census/verify.py           # ~12 s
python3 -I -B research/complex-queue-ceiling-census/rebind.py --fetch   # re-binds all 14 blobs
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-queue-ceiling-census
```

title: Research note: exact R420 quad4 cleanup envelope

## Status

Research note: exact finite secondary-cost enumeration. No new κ claim.

## Finding

For the fixed six-register positive transfer from PR1058, the inverse-subtraction DAG contains 1,768 minimum-length (11-ADD) words. Enumerating every such word yields five distinct reverse-positive cleanup matrices. The predecessor word has maximum row-sum amplification 11; two alternative shortest words attain 9. title: Finite complex circuit: exact zero-boundary gauge cost and wrapped-helper admission
body:
Varying helper gauges can remain nonzero while a recursive child or residual wrapper runs. This package imposes **gauge zero at every non-scalar boundary**, prices that restriction exactly, and admits representative complete words to the retained local scalar/frame/wrapper checker. **Finite scalar construction and exact boundary-price comparison; no new kappa.**

Sagar Thakrar's concurrent **#1259** already supplies varying gauges and the clipping/shortest-path mechanism, independently rediscovered during this work. That overlap is credited prominently. The added result is the stricter boundary contract, its exact cost, wrapped-helper coverage and local admission evidence—not priority for varying gauges.

- All 32 pinned #1259 unrestricted minima reproduce exactly. Resetting at every non-scalar event costs **4 real primitives per complex call** at L276 and L427, and zero at L359. The restriction therefore has a measured exact price and avoids *new* nonzero-gauge commutation through children/wrappers.
- Exhaustive exact optimization over all **477** no-COPY/clear helpers and all integer exponents gives L427: **522** primitives saved per complex call in each orientation. The proof clips to a finite interval without assuming an empirical cutoff.
- The domain includes **240 wrapped helpers**, excluded by #1259. The best wrapped witness, L652, saves **72** and passes complete local scalar/frame/wrapper admission in both orientations.
- Adding a zero-boundary L359 schedule to the *fixed* #1214 two-helper word saves **518 extra**, for **1,094 total**: 149,002→147,908 forward and 149,018→147,924 backward. Its zero-boundary contract is relative to that fixed predecessor word; #1214's constant gauges and their inherited assumptions remain. This is not a joint three-helper optimum.

#1263 has the larger 13,000 saving with many constant gauges. No best bill across classes or composition with #1263/#1170 is claimed. | Lever | Ideal multiplier |
|---|---:|
| Centre path free | 2.80× |
| Centre path shared by two calls | 1.90× |
| Rank-16 children | 2.31× |

title: Research: exact ceiling for #1094 idle rank-48 repartitions, #1252 recount and star-move lead (no new kappa)
body:
**Scoped finding; no new selected κ and no admitted construction.** This adds only `research/frontier1094-idle-star-ceiling/`.

## Task card
- **Card:** `selected-packing` (incumbent-optimization track, chooser seed `709c25d61571e40787fc6379741fb2da`, base `dadfea6e`). The scope is **refined** to one named residual subproblem, using the card's method "exact relaxation or exact optimum".
- **Object:** the frozen #1094 idle remainder has 4,866 unhosted, non-owner idle rank-48 children in 1,792 (replica, port) groups. These are the children #1252 repartitions.
- **Question:** this answers both of #1252's open next questions on a bounded class. (a) Does an independent recount reproduce its 1,825-pair maximum? (b) What can coordinated multi-child moves gain, and what can *any* within-group repartition gain?

## Result (exact native κ, pinned multicold engines)

| Profile | κ | Gain over #1094 |
|---|---|---:|
| #1094 selected | 0.001672660197076918 | — |
| #1252 pair class, independent recount = **1,825** | 0.001672846574134982 (matches #1252) | 1.86e-7 |
| **Disjoint-star class optimum** (2,357 moves, 1,561 centres) | **0.001672987659462603** | 3.27e-7 |
| **Ceiling: any within-group repartition, ranks ≤ 51** | **0.001673151843213755** | 4.92e-7 |

- **Ceiling.** Children can't be deleted (`48k > 51(k−1)`), splitting only adds cost, and the moment is Schur-concave at a fixed child count. So `(51^(k−1), 51−3k)` is optimal per group under *any* commuting rule. This bounds the multi-child route at about +4.9e-7 κ, which is 3.4% of #1240's fixed-word packing headroom. Four random repartition controls price below it.
- **Star class.** A centre sends ≤ 3 axes to each of several leaves. Each moved axis satisfies #1252's per-axis rule: it commutes with the leaf's axes, every stage X/Y, the terminal Y and both terminal translations. This class contains the pair class and captures two thirds of the ceiling gain. The explicit overlay is in `STAR-MOVES.json.gz`.

## Verification
```sh
python3 -B research/frontier1094-idle-star-ceiling/analyze.py --check   # ~5 s, byte-identical outputs
python3 -B research/frontier1094-idle-star-ceiling/verify.py            # ~2 s, independent, 7/7 mutation controls rejected

python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'        # 20 OK, 1 skipped
```
Everything is read directly from the committed `selected-replay.tar.gz`. Every price checks acceptance at the exact endpoint, rejection at +1e-24, all 47 strict outer constraints, and rejection of the next κ grid point. Baseline and #1252 values match at both native and conservative precision.

## Not checked / remaining obligations
- For the star overlay, the serialized controller/owner audit, the mixed-provider invoice and the strict global assembly were **not run**. The star κ is a priced, structurally verified lead, not an admitted candidate.
- Composing #1252 transfers into stars (with donor rank below 48) inherits #1252's pair argument and is not proved here.
- All inherited conditions of the selected record (compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, analytic transfer) remain.

These are structured in `TASK.json`: admission of the star overlay by generalizing #1252's auditor; the controller contract for multi-leaf moves; and stacking the same moves on the X54 / mixed-T37 candidates (#1218/#1261).

Gonzalo-Mier's #1252 provides the move, the commuting rule and the pricing recipe. #1240 provides the broader fixed-word ceiling. The #1094 replay, owner map and engines come from the selected review's ancestry. Claim and coordination are in Discussion #1265. `check_selected(ancestor, ancestor/'ancestor')` and **discards the return
value**. It then compares `BASELINE-BINDING.json` only with the #1042
receipt's own hash. So nothing ties the rechecked PR799/PR741 ancestry to the
binding #1042 recorded. Any ancestry at the receipt's machine-local path
`/private/tmp/batch952-baseline799` that passes `check_selected` is accepted.

Limits of the finding:

- The cold default `make frontier1094-verify` has no such gap.
- The #1094 candidate stage reads only hashed #1042 artifacts, so κ is
  unaffected.
- The #890 and #942 reuse modes do bind their ancestry. #1094's is the only
  current `--baseline*` reuse mode that does not.

**Certificate.** The committed `integrated799-replay.tar.gz` and
`composed-replay-evidence.tar.gz` archives, run through the unchanged
`check_selected`, rebuild a binding byte-identical to
`research/community-frontier1042-audit/BASELINE-BINDING.json` (`22575ff2…`).
That is the hash bound by the #1042 receipt `bf12c6ed…`, which the #1094 receipt
names. The selected record's ancestry binding can therefore be reproduced from
in-repo evidence alone.

**Controls.** Identity passes everywhere. Three variants pass `check_selected`
and the whole unchanged pinned reuse mode at κ = 0.001672660197076918, but are
rejected by the suggested one-line binding:

- **timing:** a re-execution with different wall-clock times;
- **bit_result:** a PR589 `RESULT9.json` field replaced;
- **bit_supplier:** the PR799 assembly names a zeroed supplier commit and blob.
  This is the semantically invalid fixture.

A PR799 κ tamper is rejected by all three checks.

```python
require(check_selected(ancestor, ancestor/'ancestor') == read(baseline/'BASELINE-BINDING.json'),
        'Ancestry recheck differs from bound #1042 binding')
```

**Remaining obligations.** This is not a cold replay of #1042 or #1094, not
execution authentication of the archived logs, and not a proof of the
multiplication theorem. The inherited assumptions are unchanged.
