title: Research audit: linear subset-budget bound for commuting dirty intervals
body:
PR1244 leaves open whether commuting factors admit interval amplification linear in the subset norm budget. This research audit supplies an all-size induction for the unchanged PR628 balanced dirty word, including its shared deeper scratch.

For every n >= 1, every pair of complete-leaf cuts, and both signs, every surviving free-algebra monomial uses each factor index at most once. Thus pairwise commuting bounded linear factors with every subset product bounded by G >= 1 satisfy

`||P_t P_s^-1|| <= C^2 G`, where `C = 2 * 3^ceil(log2 n)`.

The safe generic PR905 bound was `C^2 G^2`. The new step is a six-case decomposition: intervals spanning two occurrences of the same child become a child interval plus a rank-one term with disjoint factor supports. The proof covers both cut orders and preserves reused scratch. It retains PR905's coefficient bound; PR1085's sharper prefix count is not needed.

**Status: research audit / all-size lemma. No new kappa.** PR1244's noncommuting obstruction remains valid. The conditional error-transport inequality improves, but no new rounded implementation, working-precision formula, cost invoice, or supplier adoption is asserted. Preparation, internal leaf growth, source access, copies, restoration, recursive children, physical/compiler and analytic obligations remain separate.

## Verification

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/commuting-interval-audit/test_package.py
```

Expected: `PASS_COMMUTING_INTERVAL_PACKAGE`.

- 2,154,828 exact free-algebra intervals for n=1..24 and both signs; 108 sampled two-cut cases through n=129. Repetitions remain in the polynomial representation.
- Independently constructed words match 57 executions of the pinned source dispatcher.
- Full dense rational matrices and Gauss-Jordan inversion check 144 scalar cases and nine noncommuting block cases.
- A separate model constructs no recursive word and checks 108 induction identities on constrained child matrices with shared scratch.
- Five mathematical controls, four actual package corruptions, and full read-only relocation pass on CPython 3.15.0.
- All seven vendor files match pinned Git blobs. Selected-record integrity and all 25 related tests pass.

The all-size claim rests on the written induction, not finite extrapolation. The source replay instruments `compose`; numerical leaves do not run. Independent models mean separate implementations, not independent human review. No hosted CI, full supplier cold replay, or proof-assistant multiplication theorem is claimed. VALIDATION.json records two corrected harness/invocation issues.

## Provenance and contribution

Only `research/commuting-interval-audit/` is added. Base: `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`. OS seed 64, adversarial audit. The local claim records three candidates and bounded selection. The final refresh covers 866 open PRs, 29 discussion records and 325 local records, with complete pagination and no warnings; PR1244 explicitly identifies this open follow-up.

Credit Chafik Boukhalfa (PR628/905), Hanson Sun (PR1244 and PR1085), Gareth Davidson (PR877), and their retained lineage. Exact sources, licenses and notices remain unchanged. Prepared for Charles Bethin with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, code, verification and writing. No literature-priority or external human-review claim.

Open next questions identify the rounded-contract substitution and sharper interval coefficient bound, with concrete first steps and remaining blockers. The selected frontier and `upstream/` stay unchanged.

title: Research: X54 mixed-T37 saturation — exhaustive local sweeps, exact Φ packing invariant and width/Φ prices (no new kappa)
body:
**No new κ.** Scoped negative result and screening tool for the X54 mixed-T37 line (#1193/#1218, κ = 0.001675809683500501). Package: `research/x54-mixed-t37-saturation/`.

**Superseded in part during this session:** #1274's helper-donor kernel found a local gain outside the #1186 move families. #1252/#1268/#1280's idle-axis exchanges (48+48 → 45+51) work outside the bin-remainder model used in (2). The README says exactly what still holds.

## Results
1. **Exhaustive local sweeps on both final words (D3 = #1207 BASE-X54, D4 = #1193 FOUR-WORD), #1186 toolkit unchanged, exact frame pricing.** #1195 swept only the pre-X54 words. Results per word:
   - fusion + repair (`repair.py`): 2,238 candidates, 969 feasible, **0 gains**;
   - read-set exchange (all subsets of swappable reads, 14 copy pairs): 50 candidates, 0 feasible;
   - joint triangle-hybrid (≤3 fused reads, partial swaps, both restore modes): 161 candidates, 24 feasible, **0 gains**.

   The baseline frames are exactly optimal.
2. **Exact width-class invariant (stdlib).** Put φ(4) = φ(8) = 0, φ(5) = 3, φ(7) = 1, φ(9) = −1. A full bin of capacity 8, 16 or 32 has Φ ≥ 0, and a full capacity-48 bin has Φ ≥ −4. The 125 D3 / 208 D4 inventory has Φ = −20,814, which is tight. So the two leftover rank-one idle units cannot be merged into one rank-two child, even with time windows, ports and family rules relaxed. That rules out the only cheaper idle histogram in the bin-remainder model (a gain of about +3.3e-10).
3. **ILP screening (SciPy/HiGHS) over demotion-count mixes k ∈ [−3, 3] and all 1,163 bin patterns.** The integer optimum equals the incumbent. The LP duals have the exact form π_w = −λ·w − μ·φ(w), with λ = 11.73 and μ = 25.04. This gives a **screening rule for proposed inventory changes**: an extra entrance group is break-even (which is why the mix stops at 208), 9→8 earns 13.3, 4→5 earns 86.9, and Δκ ≈ −1.03e-11 × score.

title: Research: masked rank-8 complex decoders are locally rigid on all P104 frame-pair punctures (no new kappa)
body:
**Status: scoped structural result (exact infinitesimal certificate) plus a seeded finite sample. No new κ, no supplier change.** Only `research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity/` is added; the selected record (κ = 0.001672660197076918), `upstream/` and every existing file are unchanged.

## Question

The masked (E-graph) decoder model of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717 fixes a costly part K only on the diagonal (K_ii = 4) and on orthogonal live pairs (K_ij = 0); odd entries are free and are repaired by cost-0 terms. Can masking deform the frame-pair decoders of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968, which attain the 7/13 copy ratio on P104 = P120 − F0 − F1, away from the all-pairs normal form? https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1212 proves global rank-8 rigidity on P112/P120 and lists P104 as numerical evidence only.

## Result

For P120, P112 and **every one of the 1260 frame-pair punctures**, the tangent space at K0 = 2G of {rank K ≤ 8, masked entries fixed} is exactly the tangent of the diagonal-torus orbit D(2G)D⁻¹. The solution set therefore coincides with that orbit near 2G. A masked eight-costly-term decoder close enough to 2G has the normal-form supports, so the #968 floor (cost ≥ 56, ratio ≥ 7/13 for p ≤ 24) still applies.

The certificate is exact:

- After eliminating N, the M-system has rank 7v − 63 over F_p (p = 2³¹ − 1). Since rank over F_p is at most rank over Q, the kernel is at most v + 63.
- The explicit gauge (64) and torus (v − 1) directions lie in the kernel and span 64 + v − 1.
- 66 Schreier elements fixing F0 (products of root reflections, checked) merge the 1260 frames into the 896/336/28 classes of #968; one certified representative covers each class, with full row insertion giving rank exactly 665.

Controls and sample:

- The decomposable live set D4 ⊕ D4 is rejected (its torus splits).
- 64 of 64 seeded random punctures with 24 to 80 lines pass. This is a finite sample only.
- The P112 tangent rigidity recorded in #717 D1 is reproduced by a separate exact method.

## Scope and obligations

- **Local only.** Components away from the torus orbit on P104 are not excluded (open question 1 in the README).
- **Not covered.** Nine or more costly terms (open question 2), other punctures beyond the sample, and physical copy trees, frames, restoration and hosting.
- **Inherited.** The decoder consequence uses #968's floor and its cited flat classification. All selected-record obligations remain. This is not a formal proof of multiplication, and there has been no independent human review.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity/verify.py        # ~70 s, stdlib only
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity
```

Expected final line: `PASS_P104_MASKED_LOCAL_RIGIDITY: P120, P112 and all 1260 frame-pair punctures (3 classes) infinitesimally rigid at 2G; D4+D4 control rejected; seeded sample p=24..80 rigid 64/64; local only, no new kappa`.

- `research_package.py` check-only and the full 3.12 replay pass (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`).
- `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` passes.

Four come from the host's system `core.autocrlf=true`, and disappear with `core.autocrlf=false` for the process. The fifth uses `os.killpg`, which does not exist on Windows. Linux CI was not run.

## Result

For the priced bill `f(a) = (1/(mW)) Σ n_r r (m/r)^a + c_s m^a`, convexity gives the diagnostic rigorously: with `D_eff = mW − Σ n_r r − c_s mW` and `E_eff = Σ n_r r ln(m/r) + c_s mW ln m`, the exact root satisfies **`a* < D_eff/E_eff` strictly** whenever `D_eff > 0` (tangent at `a = 0` reaches 1 at `D_eff/E_eff`; `f` lies strictly above its tangent). For `c_s = 0` this is exactly the stated `a < D/E` with `D = mW − Σ n_r r`, `E = Σ n_r r log(m/r)`.

| Ledger | recorded endpoint `a` | moment residual at `a` | at `a + 1e-24` | certified `D/E` ceiling | `D/E ÷ a` | screening extremum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| complex (m=73, W=14336, N=144, no surcharge) | 0.001675462676808103522925 | −1.304215e-24 | +1.624723e-24 | **0.001680590709754321699421** | 1.003061 | 0.013708749 (cap 51) |
| bit (m=64, W=28416, bad-residue surcharge) | 0.001733427039589844234749 | −1.598690e-24 | +1.669360e-24 | **0.001738557248401367986042** | 1.002960 | 0.016127138 (cap 45) |

- The independently computed residual intervals agree with the recorded `mercator` and `base_two` intervals of ASSEMBLY.json and reproduce the accept/reject sharpness at the next grid point; the complex values match `research/community-frontier1094-audit/INDEPENDENT1094.json`'s `moment_minus_one` digits.
- The diagnostic overestimates the exact root by about 0.30% (complex) and 0.29% (bit): nearly sharp in this small-saving regime, so it is a safe screen here.
- Ledger aggregates are reconstructed from the published histograms and checked against both coverage identities: complex `D = 73W − Σ n_r r = W − 64N = 5,120` (which also re-derives `W = 14,336` from the histogram and `N = 144`), bit `D = 64W − Σ n_r r = T(2Kv − L·cst) = 32(2·4·111 − 9·63) = 10,272`.
- **Screening extremum** (screen only, not realizability): rank-mass-preserving repackings up to the halving-guard cap could push `D/E` to about 0.0137 (complex) and 0.0161 (bit); both exceed `1/99 ≈ 0.010101`, so the screen alone does not decide the planning target there. For the complex local word the realizability-aware ceiling of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240 (0.001690054109089) supersedes the per-histogram ceiling and already rules out the target; the bit word has no such analysis (open question in the README).

## Method and independence

`research/selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic/verify.py` imports nothing from the retained engines (`moment.py`, `base_two_moment.py`, the atanh prime chain of `research/pending-claims-independent-pricing`, or the Mercator/base-two transcriptions under `research/community-batch970-audit/submitted/957/`). Exact rationals throughout; every enclosure comes from an explicit inequality; no floating point.

- `ln` by **rational square-root bisection** (`x^(1/2^k)`, k = 112, 2^-320 dyadic grid; `u − u²/2 ≤ ln(1+u) ≤ u`), cross-checked by **bisection inverting a certified Taylor exponential**; both must agree on every used log (ln 2 correct to 30 printed digits).
- `exp` by Taylor partial sums with an explicit rational geometric tail bound (order 48; tail below 1e-150 at the largest exponent used). This matches the standard approach of the retained engines and is disclosed as such.
- Positive fixtures: exactly solvable single-rank ledger `H={1:1}, m=2, W=1` with root `a* = 1 < 1/ln 2 = D/E`; agreement with recorded residuals; reconstructed coverage identities.
- 12 positive/negative controls, each required to be rejected or hold: tampered pin; bit ledger at wrong width m=73; one-count histogram mutation breaking the coverage identity; out-of-range rank; zero deficit; endpoint shifted two grid steps (must break acceptance); doubled bit surcharge (must break acceptance); negative surcharge.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic --check-only
```

Observed (Python 3.12.10, Windows, stdlib only): `PASS_INDEPENDENT_DE_DIAGNOSTIC`, 12 controls, and `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS` / `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic outcome=completed` from the package runner. Machine-readable output: `research/selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic/RESULT.json`.

Repo test suite `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 18/20 pass here. The 2 failures are pre-existing Windows platform issues in `tests/test_research_onboarding.py`, unrelated to this package: (a) the fixture's `Path.write_text` writes CRLF while system `core.autocrlf=true` normalizes the committed blob, failing the fixture's own pin check in `setUp`; with `core.autocrlf=false` those 6 setUp errors disappear; (b) `scripts/research_package.py`'s timeout path calls `os.killpg`, which does not exist on Windows. This package is not touched by either path.

## Not covered / limitations

- Paid profiles are taken from the published ledgers (ASSEMBLY.json `complex_profile`; `EXPECTED.json` `nine.profile`, git-blob pinned by the assembly's `bit_supplier` block). This package does not rebuild either word from its original operations.
- The conservative (surcharge-on-complex) endpoints of ASSEMBLY.json are not rechecked.
- `D/E` bounds one fixed histogram's root; it is not a repacking bound and not a realizability statement.
- All inherited all-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, analytic transfer and bit H1-H5 obligations remain assumptions. Not a multiplication theorem.

## Overlap, credit and coordination

Nearest concurrent work (all distinct): https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240 (complex local-word packing ceiling via idle-mass optimization), https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1264 (packing ceilings of open complex claims) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1276 (#1094 idle rank-48 repartition ceilings) — the repacking-ceiling lineage; none proves the `a < D/E` diagnostic or covers the bit ledger. Endpoint certification lineage: `research/pending-claims-independent-pricing` (Sagar Thakrar's atanh prime chain) and the Mercator/base-two audit of PR957's lineage. Ledger reconstruction for the complex owner map: Josie Elliston's and Sagar Thakrar's audits composed in `research/community-batch1099-audit/check_frontier1094.py`.

Predecessor credit: the pricing model and the `a < D/E` diagnostic are Douglas Colkitt's (`autoresearch.md`, `research/pending-claims-independent-pricing`); the complex ledger is Rohan Arun's #1094 construction on Jeremy Kothe's packing chain (selected review: `docs/research/community-batch1099-review.md`); the bit supplier is the PR589/PR555 lineage, retained unchanged by the selected record; the fixed-word packing-ceiling lineage is static44, PR525, PR643 and the author of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240.

Contributor: **Navinor**, with substantial AI assistance ("with help from opencode"). Apache-2.0. Claim thread: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18909718 (updated with FINDING/DONE alongside this PR). Priority revision 3 (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1272) landed after this assignment (drawn under revision 2); per `autoresearch.md` section 6 this completed evidence is preserved and submitted unchanged.

**Optional feedback:** the saturation of `independent-moment` on the selected record (already noted in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200#discussioncomment-18909265) is confirmed; a per-card "existing checks for the current selected record" field would have redirected this session earlier. title: Independent verification: universal dirty phase identities with four explicit invariants
body:
This independently certifies the local phase algebra used by Charles Bethin’s PR1278. All 16 ordered phase pairs and the completed parent map/inverse hold as universal noncommutative block-polynomial identities, with an opaque shared scratch block of arbitrary dimension.

The check needs only four one-sided invariants: `P e_y = Q e_y = e_y` and `e_x^T R = e_x^T S = e_x^T`. All other blocks are independent indeterminates; no P/R or Q/S inverse cancellation is assumed. Four explicit invertible shear counterexamples show that omitting one of these invariants can break the displayed family while retaining the other three. The stronger source/target and factor-support conditions remain inputs to PR1278’s separate induction.

**Status: independent algebraic verification; no new kappa.** PR1278 already supplies the all-size interval theorem and phase formulas. This contribution replaces finite matrix sampling for this local obligation with exact typed free-polynomial normal forms and isolates weaker sufficient local hypotheses. It does not certify the full induction, rounded leaves, precision costs, supplier admission or multiplication theorem, and is not a proof-assistant formalization.

python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/universal-dirty-phase-identities

title: Scoped proof: R420 quad4 all-length cleanup minimum is 9
body:
PR1266 establishes reverse-positive cleanup norm 9 among shortest 11-ADD words for Chris Barber's fixed R420 quad-4 transfer, while leaving longer words open. This contribution proves that **every finite positive-ADD factorization of that same ordered six-register integer target has norm at least 9**. The existing 11-ADD witness attains the floor, so the all-length minimum is exactly 9. No new circuit witness or kappa is attributed here.

The proof combines three necessary invariants: the reverse-positive matrix Q majorizes the entrywise absolute signed inverse, Q has positive diagonal, and Q is congruent to the signed inverse modulo two. In inverse row `[-1, 0, 1, -3, 1, -1]`, the zero diagonal forces an even positive Q diagonal of at least two, raising the former absolute-inverse row floor from 7 to 9. The argument covers arbitrary word length without enlarging the predecessor search.

Reproduce the registered package (Python 3.12, standard library only):

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r420-all-length-cleanup-floor
```

The core command is `python3 -I -O -B research/r420-all-length-cleanup-floor/verify.py`, which prints `PASS_R420_ALL_LENGTH_CLEANUP_FLOOR lower=9 attained=9 adds=11 columns=6 boolean=64 controls=5`.

Validation passed on Python 3.14.7 and the full registered Python 3.12.15 replay. Two exact engines check the target, signed inverse, bound and witness. Eight mathematical/package tests include all 9,331 three-register words through length five, an actual 19-ADD same-target word, a free-SWAP scope counterexample, archive/receipt corruptions, refused receipt overwrite and relocated optimized replay. These finite checks validate implementation and the numerical instance; the universal statement follows from PROOF.md. The portable runtime was checked against its published digests. Staged whitespace and archive-to-Git provenance checks pass.

Exact base: `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`. Target source: PR1058 head `d148d200f2d64c90504fa3a9608e455aaa4c0c21`. Reused witness receipt: PR1266 commit `8edfb5d97aea03d26316964f35359d1864731dbe`, unchanged by its later attribution fix. Git blobs, source hashes, scope change and open next question are recorded in the package. [Discussion 1279](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1279) is the coordination claim.

The theorem fixes the exact integer lift, six ordered registers and positive ADD alphabet, excluding workspace and permutations. It optimizes the positive bound map for a common incoming coordinate budget. The matrices trade entries, so the result does not establish an improvement for the full circuit's nonuniform entering bounds. Whole-word native pricing, selected-supplier adoption and outer assembly remain integration obligations; no new kappa or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

Credit: **Chris Barber (@cbarber1)** for PR1058's target, circuit minimum and DAG; **Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337)** for PR1266's reused witness/envelope; **eumemic** for the underlying PR543 R420 architecture, with full inherited credit retained in the frozen NOTICE. title: Tooling: Windows portability for research onboarding scripts and tests (no new kappa)
body:
## Tooling: Windows portability for the research onboarding scripts and tests (no new κ)

**Track / card:** `verifier-engineering` / `portable-replay` (helper seed `326311449640c5859b8c989bfb6ffb4d`). Scope **unchanged**: reproducible environment failures repaired with minimal cross-environment fixes.
**Base:** `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. Work started at `dadfea6e`; none of the touched files changed in between. The selected record is unchanged.
**No mathematical claim.** No certificate, frozen source, pin, catalogue or selected-record change.

### Findings at base (Windows 11, CPython 3.14.8, cp1252 locale, Git for Windows `core.autocrlf=true`)

`python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` → **6 errors / 20 tests**, plus two bugs in the overlap helper:

1. **`research_package.py --check-only` depends on the host locale.** It read `README.md`, `TASK.json` and `VERIFY.json` with the locale codec. A package whose README contains `“quotes”` (U+201D contains byte 0x9d, which cp1252 leaves undefined) **crashed on Windows and passed on Linux or in UTF-8 mode**. Most other non-ASCII text (κ, —) silently turned into mojibake instead. `test_documented_allocation_matches_catalog` failed the same way on `autoresearch.md`.
2. **`find_overlap.py --refresh` never worked on Windows.** `gh api` ran with `text=True` and the locale codec. Open-PR bodies contain byte 0x81, the subprocess reader thread died, `stdout` came back `None`, and both sources reported `the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not NoneType`. Coverage stayed `null`.
3. **`find_overlap.py`'s human report crashed** (`UnicodeEncodeError … 'κ'`) when printing an excerpt to a cp1252 pipe.
4. **Test fixture, CRLF:** the temporary fixture repo has no `.gitattributes`, so with Git for Windows' default `autocrlf=true` it stores LF blobs while `write_text` leaves CRLF on disk. `new_research_package.create` then refuses with `source has uncommitted changes…` (5 `setUp` errors). The main repo's `* text=auto eol=lf` hides this for real checkouts, so this part is test-only.
5. **`run_command` timeout:** it calls `os.killpg`, which does not exist on Windows. The child leaked and blocked temp-dir cleanup.

### Changes (6 files, +69/−15)

- `research_package.py`, `find_overlap.py`, `new_research_package.py`, `choose_research_task.py`:
  - `encoding="utf-8"` on every text-mode file read/write and text-mode subprocess call.
  - The scaffold also writes `newline="\n"`.
- `find_overlap.py`: the human report uses `errors="backslashreplace"`, so it never crashes and the output encoding consumers see is unchanged. `--json` is already ASCII via `json.dumps`.
- `run_command`: where `os.killpg` is unavailable, end the timed-out child **tree** with `taskkill /F /T /PID`. The POSIX branch is byte-identical.
- Tests:
  - The fixture repo pins `core.autocrlf=false` next to its pinned user identity.
  - The assignment tests read UTF-8.
  - Three new tests:
    - `test_utf8_metadata_validates_under_any_locale`: κ, an em dash and curly quotes in TASK.json and README must validate and round-trip.
    - `test_report_survives_a_cp1252_stdout`: runs `find_overlap.py κ --offline` with `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252`, which reproduces a Windows pipe **on any host**.
    - `test_onboarding_text_io_does_not_depend_on_host_locale`: an AST check that every text-mode `read_text`/`write_text`/`open`/`NamedTemporaryFile`/`subprocess.run|Popen|check_output` call in the five onboarding scripts names an encoding. It is needed because a UTF-8 Linux CI host cannot observe locale-codec bugs behaviourally.

### Evidence

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Base, Windows cp1252 | 6 errors / 20 |
| Patched (rebased on `bce54fb3`), Windows cp1252 | **OK, 23 tests (1 skipped: 3.12-only replay)** |
| Patched, `python -X utf8` | OK, 23 (1 skipped) |
| Control: `scripts/` reverted, new tests kept, cp1252 | static check fails, UTF-8 metadata errors, killpg errors |

title: Tooling: preserve replay assertions despite inherited PYTHONOPTIMIZE
body:
An inherited `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1` or `2` makes the registered-package launcher print `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` after skipping a verifier's false assertion. This reproduces through the complete CLI with a valid, source-pinned package fixture. With the same files and `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=0`, that fixture correctly fails.

Remove only `PYTHONOPTIMIZE` from each launched command's environment. Ordinary Python verifier children and their subprocesses then retain assertion checks. Preserve other environment settings, the caller's environment, command arguments, timeouts, and explicit `-O`/`-OO` options for intentional controls. This is a tooling repair; no mathematical result, supplier certificate, frozen source, selected frontier, or kappa changes.

Validation:

- `python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v`: all **23 tests pass** on CPython 3.12.12. They also pass with the test driver launched using `-OO`.
- CPython **3.15.0** via the research wrapper: **21 pass, two skip** because full generic replay explicitly requires 3.12. The same result holds with inherited `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=2`. Python.org confirmed 3.15.0 as current stable; 3.12 is a compatibility exception for the pinned replay contract.
- The new tests execute actual interpreter children, nested children, and the full registered-package CLI. False assertions reject; true assertions pass for environment values empty/0/1/2. Explicit optimization remains observable, the parent's setting is unchanged, and an unrelated environment sentinel survives.
- Restoring only the original launcher makes all three new test groups fail (seven failing subcases). The unchanged and patched CLI probes use identical fixture bytes. A separate `compile(..., optimize=0/1/2)` oracle, independent of the launcher, confirms why assertion removal changes the outcome.
- The selected-record check and all **25 selected-record tests pass**. No selected cold replay, hosted CI, Windows execution, or external human review is claimed.

Scope: this prevents accidental optimization inherited from the invoking environment. It does not prevent a manifest from explicitly requesting optimization or verifier code from changing its own subprocess environment. Those remain explicit package-author choices. Python documents the environment/flag behavior at https://docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html#envvar-PYTHONOPTIMIZE.

title: Scoped negative result: restored 2+3-cycle boundary costs exactly ten
body:

title: Research: sharp A8 simplex P112 copy floor 71 on matching-frame punctures (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #1248 left the fixed A8 simplex decoder on a P112 frame puncture open. This package proves that the minimum separate-term copy cost is **71** for the specified matching-frame puncture, over arbitrary complex row shifts, and for its 945 coordinate-permutation images. All nine terms can be active, with costs `(1,8,8,9,9,9,9,9,9)`. Since 71 exceeds the standard P112 cost 64, this family cannot provide the contemplated copy saving.

**Status:** scoped proof with exhaustive finite certificates, a negative result for this route. It bounds copy cost only: no scalar saving, paid-profile or κ improvement, physical supplier or complete moment invoice is claimed.

Only `research/a8-p112-decoder-screen/` is added (10 files). All finite lemmas are recomputed. The selected frontier, frozen sources and existing packages are unchanged.

**Precise delta.** The P112 column supports still have binary label rank nine, but partner deficiency spaces can now have dimension two. The P120 dimension-one lemma fails after the puncture, so it is not reused. A complete subspace-product check proves total deficiency at most ten, hence cost at least `81-10=71`. The primary check covers 390,915 planes, 19,299 partner-space tuples and 462,141 compatible choices. The separate checker rebuilds labels from the Gram matrix, uses annihilators and Cartesian products, and verifies a puncture stabilizer transporting two anchor representatives to all nine. Both check all 12,544 entries of the active witness, and the separate checker prices the actual pairing submatrices. The written argument in `PROOF.md` covers all complex row shifts, not sampled coefficients. This is a scoped proof with finite certificates, not formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

**Remaining obligations.** Not covered:
- other P112 frame orbits, other normal frames and masked identities;
- two unrestricted factors and shared-copy billing.

Not produced:
- a physical supplier;
- a delivery, restoration, frame, hosting or precision invoice;
- a new moment or κ.

Not run or proved:
- the selected cold replay (`make frontier1094-verify`);
- native or Lean builds, and hosted CI;
- the all-size compiler and the complete multiplication theorem.

All inherited analytic, realization and bit H1-H5 conditions remain.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `complex-masked-decoder` / `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`, refined to `a8-simplex-matching-frame-p112-all-complex-shifts`. Chooser nonce `a57142e8e77d6c0af036ca35809daf69`, track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2.
- **Base and exact heads:** base `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`; contribution `a052f0da36a3845c2ec785fd44e5b9e50de3b688`. PR #1248 `f226f4329a996b0a1bea8794179a91b5d0ed80bf`; PR #1224 `00e6ed0810b8ebc7f6133e2c036d0f1c9a3a4162`. Both predecessor heads were fetched and rechecked. They provide method and question attribution, not imported code or assumed finite lemmas. Main-tree source pins are in `SOURCES.json`. Selected PR #1094 `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810` is context only.
- **Concrete object and question:** roots `e_a-e_b` and `1_S-(1/3)1` in the sum-zero subspace of Q^9, with fixed `T_ik=r_ik` and `D_ik=2r_ik+t_i`. Remove frame indices `[0,15,26,33,42,89,112,119]`. Can arbitrary complex shifts reduce total binary pairing-rank cost below 64?
- **Scope status:** refined, to the card's overcomplete branch and PR #1248's explicit next question. Coordinate permutation gives a corollary for the 945 matching-frame punctures; no other frame orbit is claimed. Nine overcomplete terms are allowed, and P120 is replaced by the specified P112 puncture.
- **Method and bounded domain:** all 511 nonzero binary functionals, all 43,435 binary planes for each of nine anchors, and every subspace of each partner space (proved to have dimension at most two). Exact integer and rational arithmetic, with a separate Gram-derived implementation. No floating-point search or solver dependency.
- **Optimistic budget:** a cost of at most 63 would be the necessary first saving against 64 under separate-term billing. The sharp floor 71 rejects the route before any delivery, frame, restoration or hosting synthesis.
- **Nearest overlap and added value:** PR #1248 proves P120, and PR #1224 supplies the normal form and bounded searches; this proves the fixed P112 optimum for one frame orbit. PR #1212/#1213 and PR #1292 (discussion #1275) concern eight-term masked rigidity. PR #1236 and discussion #1267 concern root-star and co-star supports. The claim is in [discussion #1241](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1241#discussioncomment-18909913). A live overlap check just before submission (796 open PRs and 45 discussion records at 22:12 UTC, complete pagination) found no competing fixed-simplex P112 result.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-decoder-field-extension-seed44/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_baseline.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a8-p112-decoder-screen --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a8-p112-decoder-screen
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
python3 -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py
```

All pass on CPython 3.12.3 / Linux x86_64, standard library only. The registered replay runs both checkers and the six package tests in about 58 seconds. All 20 research-workflow tests pass without skips. Coverage includes:
- optimized replay, from a relocated copy and read-only;
- the separate checker run without the primary code;
- changed, missing, incomplete or malformed receipts;
- eight semantic rejection controls: a coefficient error, a deleted term, corrupt labels, a nonorthogonal puncture, the false inherited dimension-one lemma, missing mutual compatibility, a false cost of 70, and a valid non-real shift.

The registered replay and the metadata/pin check were run again on the final commit before submission, and both passed.

Expected markers:

```text
PASS_A8_P112_DECODER_FLOOR planes=390915 configurations=19299 compatible_leaves=462141 cost=71 controls=8
PASS_A8_P112_INDEPENDENT anchors=2 transported=9 planes=86870 compatible_leaves=92317 cost=71
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/a8-p112-decoder-screen outcome=negative-result
```

## Credit

- Philipp/mightyOil (PR #1248) for the deficiency method and the open P112 question.
- joaqcoo (PR #1224) for the A8 frame and the one-sided normal form.
- DreamingOfClouds (PR #717/#595/#446) for the decoder and label-cost model.
- themilkman216 (PR #968) and woklerx (PR #1077/#1180) for the surrounding bounds.
- Classical E8/A8 geometry.

New work is Apache-2.0.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the research, the proof, both implementations, the verification and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. The separate implementation comes from the same assistant, so it is not independent human review.

## Open next questions

From the package README:
- **Other frame punctures relative to the fixed simplex.** Do they also cost at least 64? First step: enumerate the orthogonal frames and their S9 orbits, then recompute column ranks and partner dimensions for a representative outside the matching-frame orbit. Blocker: the present enumerator rejects partner dimensions above two and may need extending.
- **Another specified nine-normal frame.** Can PR #1224's A7+A1 or A2+E6 family reach copy cost below 64 on a named P112 puncture? First step: establish its exact ratio classes, column spans and a favorable complete cost budget. Blocker: the simplex's common kernel vector and compatibility census do not transfer automatically, and physical realization remains a separate obligation.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

- **Helped:** PR #1248's explicit open next questions gave a distinct, bounded task right after the overlap check. The package generator and the registered Python 3.12 hook made the result easy to package and replay.
- **Friction:** the broad card's overlap terms returned many masked and overcomplete families. Title-level similarity did not distinguish the remaining puncture question, and `--all-terms` queries did.
- **Suggestion:** show one or two source-linked, bounded successor questions from recent packages beside the chooser's broad card, keeping the warning that they may already be claimed.

title: Finite certificate: no D-local feedback saving for 3x3 binary shears (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #1194's semantic D contract keeps the prohibition on targets feeding helpers, even inside its source-free zero-frame prefix. This package states the complete boundary condition under which that local restriction could be dropped, and finds its exact price. For all 512 binary 3-by-3 K, unrestricted single-source XOR circuits have the same minimum cost as circuits without target feedback. Both alphabets restore every helper and every target input basis, and the largest minimum is seven gates. The smaller shapes with 1 <= H,T <= 3 bring coverage to 682 labeled maps.

**Status:** finite exact certificate plus a conditional prefix-substitution lemma, a negative result for this relaxation. No scalar saving, supplier change, paid-profile or κ improvement is proposed.

Only `research/bit-zero-frame-feedback/` is added (7 files). It holds:
- the lemma;
- the exact shortest-circuit certificate;
- a packed-row verifier and a truth-table checker that shares no code with it;
- the source pins and the registered replay.

**Precise delta.** The endpoint is T_K = [[I,0],[K,I]] on arbitrary dirty inputs. Both alphabets charge every ordered single-source XOR one unit; the restricted alphabet excludes only helper destinations with target sources. There are no extra registers or other event types. Complete radius-four BFS balls meet radius-zero-through-three spheres at B = A T_K. Every word of length at most 7 has such a split, so an attained minimum of at most 7 is globally shortest, and every target has an attaining word. For costs 0 through 7, the six-wire minimum histogram is `[1,9,36,84,126,132,96,28]` in both alphabets, so feedback saves zero gates in this domain. Every actual preparation and restoration gate is charged. The boundary-substitution argument applies to any F2 module at a common zero frame with no other state changes or interior observers. It leaves the literal continuation unchanged, and does not relax its H1/H3 or projected-cleanup conditions.

**Remaining obligations.** Not covered:
- an equality theorem beyond H,T <= 3;
- other fields, weighted or multi-source alphabets, extra registers and nonzero frames.

No R439 or R420 word was changed. Not checked:
- native replay and full hosted-supplier emission;
- the all-size, compiler and common-frame realization;
- intermediate precision and tape bounds;
- the outer analytic transfer.

The selected frontier's cold replay was not rerun for this independent finite package. Binary endpoint equality does not establish physical precision bounds or a new paid recursive moment.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `bit-helper-contract` / `3475f46c8358c6a9211b`, refined to `zero-frame-H1-feedback/GL6-F2/3x3-unit-CNOT-exact`. Chooser nonce `e1ba96fa16219472c5ab32da75a99c6f`, track bit-mechanisms, priority revision 2, no reroll.
- **Base and exact heads:** base `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`; contribution `0d4c0069f1f4592833304a9ea6e61e676c566113`. No pending PR is imported or assumed accepted. The inherited checker and the PR #1062 documentation are hash-pinned context, not executed supplier dependencies. Context predecessors: PR #1194 `2e39c98238f543d988f9efc1b076590a4b780dca` and PR #1105 `20a960b545f4b0ade4f26922ef686bd5eaf275f4`, both by @woklerx. Their proof-document blobs and SHA256s are in `SOURCES.json`.
- **Concrete question and changed restriction:** may target feedback inside a fully restored, source-free, common-zero-frame D prefix lower its unit XOR cost? Only D-local H1 is relaxed.
- **Scope status:** refined. PR #1194 already treats the card's original H2/K question but explicitly keeps H1 in D; this isolates that retained condition and its cost, with a full boundary argument.
- **Method and bounded domain:** exact matrix BFS and meet-in-the-middle over all binary H-by-T K for 1 <= H,T <= 3. No ancillas, source reads, copying, erasure, allocation or frame changes; all inputs arbitrary.
- **Optimistic budget:** every actual XOR is paid, including restoration. A local success required a strict reduction against the restricted optimum, and none occurs. Recursive charges stay conditional on the common-frame realization and are not inferred to improve.
- **Nearest overlap and added value:**
  - PR #1194 treats a fixed word while keeping D-local H1.
  - PR #1105's obstruction concerns raw A/scatter/B feedback and projected cleanup, not a completely restored D prefix.
  - PR #1188 (`6e142e72e94515566e87c964c0fca39eea93156f`) applies GL5 shortest-word synthesis to other local endpoints.
  - PR #1122 (`a2551e70fce0cc34348f50f1a94e7cc4c80bbcbf`) and PR #1208 (`24c45725f7b9ffca4529b46661acf343ce93cee3`) optimize fixed R439 words.
  - This account's PR #794 (R420 target-basis compensation) is separate and was not redone.
- **Claim and final check:** the claim is in [discussion #1290](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1290). A live overlap check just before submission (797 open PRs and every discussion record at 22:14 UTC, complete pagination) found no competing work on zero-frame target feedback.

## Validation

From the repository root, Python 3.12 with its standard library:

```sh
timeout 60s python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-zero-frame-feedback --check-only
timeout 300s python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-zero-frame-feedback
timeout 120s python3 -I -O -B research/bit-zero-frame-feedback/verify.py
timeout 120s python3 -I -O -B research/bit-zero-frame-feedback/independent.py
```

All pass. The registered replay takes about two seconds, and the largest child process used about 50 MiB. Expected output includes:

```text

PASS_INDEPENDENT_ZERO_FRAME_FEEDBACK labeled_maps=682 dirty_inputs_per_six_wire_map=64 full_GL4=20160
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/bit-zero-frame-feedback outcome=negative-result
```

**Controls.** The primary verifier runs two positive and eight negative semantic and search controls. The independent checker uses complete truth tables and searches every labeled K without orbit reduction for its lower bounds. It transports restricted witnesses for the upper bounds. Ordinary full-group BFS for H,T <= 2 is an additional check, covering 20,160 unrestricted and 576 restricted four-wire states. In isolated copies, both checkers also rejected three corrupted certificates: a missing orbit, a false minimum, and a witness that leaks initial target dirt.

Both implementations rest on the same proved meet-in-the-middle principle, so they are separate code, not independent mathematics. The registered replay and the metadata/pin check were run again on the final commit before submission, and both passed.

No novelty is claimed for elementary matrix substitution, CNOT synthesis or meet-in-the-middle search. Existing licenses, source archives and selected artifacts are unchanged; new work is Apache-2.0.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the research, the proof, both implementations, the verification and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. No independent human review is claimed.

## Open next questions

From the package README:
1. **Does equality persist beyond three helpers and three targets?** A strict advantage would make the D-local feedback relaxation economically relevant. First step: one pinned 3-by-4 K, with a restricted upper bound and an unrestricted shorter candidate, followed by exact exclusion of shorter words. Blockers: the larger ball sizes, and having no candidate yet. This result supplies no general no-feedback theorem.
2. **Could a legal supplier instance realize such a prefix with its full physical costs?** If a larger strict gain is found, compare its complete prefix matrix against the original D, then recount the actual intermediate precision envelopes, paths and hosting. Blocker: no shorter candidate or physical bridge exists yet.

Extending the same 3-by-3 search is not useful: its exact no-gain result is complete.

title: Audit: selected PR589 bit-hosting pending projectors across all hosted helpers (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The selected PR #589 bit supplier's slot counts and borrowing windows do not, by themselves, specify the physical pending subspaces. This package independently reconstructs the frozen allocation and checks its geometric binding across all 126,432 helper occurrences. An exact equal-rank substitution keeps the counts, relative slots and windows but changes the address operator, which shows how far the weaker implication reaches.

**Status:** finite audit with a scoped counterexample. The audit is clean: it confirms the existing protection and finds no production acceptance bug. No new κ, scalar saving, paid-profile change or supplier adoption is proposed. The production pipeline does not accept the alternate chart.

Only `research/selected-bit-hosting-audit/` is added (7 files). It holds:
- a written projector argument;
- a standard-library verifier and a deterministic result receipt;
- source pins and package/task metadata;
- six focused tests.

No existing repository file changes.

**What is checked.** The audit derives ten idle children, expands 3,951 slots per replica, checks all 111 port projectors and 32 replicas, and recounts the complete paid histogram. 14,208 physical families host helpers from more than one idle child, and their hosted supports are disjoint. Every selected slot contains either the whole seven-dimensional q-perp block or none of it, so its projector does not depend on the choice of orthonormal completion. The complete profile agrees with the selected receipt: rank mass 1,808,352 and deficit 10,272.

**The counterexample.** It exchanges exterior axes 8 and 36 in child 7's realization only. Its rank, helper assignments, slot widths, within-child disjointness and windows stay unchanged, while its support overlaps child 0's. The idle-factor products differ exactly on axes 8 and 36. The README separates this product witness from a replay of the whole interleaved supplier.

**Remaining obligations.** Not established:
- the complete-call correlated-helper realization and injective cover-class compilation;
- local scalar correctness and H1-H5;
- the actual emitted or native word replay and all-size compilation;
- precision and tape bounds, the analytic transfer, and the full multiplication theorem.

No complete cold replay, Lean proof or recertification of the moment endpoint was run. Mixed-width slots that split q-perp fall outside the completion-free argument.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `supplier-boundary-audit` / `dcdb0fa8e49b08a958d0`, refined to `selected-PR589-nine-stage/ambient-pending-axis-disjointness/all-32-replicas`. Chooser nonce `a5c234473782f78e2b63b17f1efbf42b`, track adversarial-audit, priority revision 2, no reroll.
- **Base and exact heads:**
  - base `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`; contribution `4cb255ef445e2abc3ff8845fa01210b974e2cf6c`;
  - selected context, PR #1094: `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810`;
  - retained bit source, PR #589: `a5afc8c6169ea61ba7c51dfd3cade02cc7b13b46`, merged as `b3eb785ac5b4b1ca2beea0f80db078a505626a90`;
  - the PR #545 adapter predecessor: `376426f3b2b26ab430d10baf16bbd9ff42990a7c`;
  - the PR #589 receipt Git blob: `e293ddc557742637f9f679f083a1a282d87b1b13`.

  `SOURCES.json` pins 14 live input files and two historical provenance records. No pending PR is a dependency.
- **Concrete object and question:** does the actual R439 allocation have disjoint physical pending projectors across idle children of a shared family, and what geometric binding is needed beyond counts and windows?
- **Exact claim audited:** the implication from per-child cardinality, slot and timing checks alone to the required coordinate-factor product. No production predicate is weakened.
- **Scope status:** refined, to one current bit-supplier geometric premise. It is distinct from the historical PR #626 bridge omission and from the current complex-supplier audits. Confirming the selected binding is useful even without finding an acceptance bug.
- **Method and bounded domain:** exact integer support masks and rational projectors, over:
  - 111 ports, nine stages, ten idle children and four pairs;
  - 32 replicas, 64 axes, and 439 width-eight helpers per call.

  The source recipe and level convention are declared inputs. The allocation, timing, masks and profile recount are implemented independently, with the source's `windows` and `expand` used as comparison oracles.
- **Nearest overlap and added value:**
  - PR #1228 (`28243acfc6b54273ebcf3cb11edef25df09c8d95`), PR #1231 (`448690c3b7e5c2b5975b760075b162fe0a8cfb03`) and PR #540 (`acc1917034d10f464271ab115fda314fd4eee7a3`) treat one historical PR #442 invocation.
  - PR #1209 (`d1ba263139ceb6eb811628b7560a3f87f3c9652e`) treats the complex supplier's pending axes, and PR #878 (`7b3241566ddfd50548e6b113ede9333826b86313`) treats bit B boundaries.
  - The retained `bit589-width-packing` audit already supplies slot counts and a restricted packing optimum; here those counts serve as consistency checks.

  This PR adds the census of the selected allocation's projectors across all children, plus the geometric counterexample.
- **Claim and final check:** the claim is in [discussion #1289](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1289). A live overlap check just before submission (799 open PRs and 50 discussion records at 22:17 UTC, complete pagination) found no competing work.

## Validation

On Python 3.12.3, with no third-party dependencies:

```sh
timeout 120s python3 -B research/owner-boundary-audit/verify.py
timeout 120s python3 -B scripts/research_baseline.py
timeout 120s python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-hosting-audit --check-only
timeout 180s python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-hosting-audit
```

**What passed:**
- The first two commands passed the card's historical positive control and the selected binding baseline. Neither is a new finding or a cold replay.
- The package metadata and pins passed.
- The registered package replay ran `python3 -I -B research/selected-bit-hosting-audit/verify.py` and the whole focused test file under `-I -O -B`. All six tests passed, covering dense rational matrix composition, noncommuting and split-complement boundaries, altered source bytes and an altered receipt.
- All 12 semantic fault controls were rejected: geometric overlap, wrong source axes, duplicate axes or helpers, omitted helpers, slot collisions, timing, extent, width and copy errors, and a nonempty zero-rank child.

The registered replay and the metadata/pin check were run again on the final commit before submission, and both passed. The metadata pass certifies packaging and pins, not the mathematical conclusion.

```text
PASS_SELECTED_BIT_HOSTING_AUDIT: 126432 helper occurrences; 111 port projectors; 12 controls rejected
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-bit-hosting-audit outcome=completed
```

## Credit

- The PR #1228/#1231 auditors, Josie Elliston and Rohan Arun.

Existing licenses and source attribution are retained; new material is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

From the package README:
1. **Can the all-call pending-projector statement be connected to a typed physical realization of the actual PR #589 emitted word?** That would narrow the gap between finite placement and complete-call hosting. First step: export these source-bound slot masks into the PR #540/#1231 multi-host contract with the R439 word. Blockers: extracting the current word, and the correlated-helper realization; the historical Lean data cannot simply be renamed.
2. **Which mixed-width selected or proposed bit allocations split q-perp?** The completion-free argument would then need explicit local projectors. First step: run the `mask & 255 in {0,254}` gate on one pinned candidate's slices. If it fails, obtain the actual source orthonormal complement before testing orthogonality. No such mixed-width source is admitted or excluded here.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

- **Friction:** locating the exact current geometric boundary through the historical template, the punctured-word adapters and the selected assembly. Broad `hosting` overlap terms also returned hundreds of older candidates, and the card's historical first-step control helped orientation but did not point at this current bit boundary.
- **Suggestion:** add a current-source trace example to this card. It would name the selected assembly, the frozen R439 selection and the level-to-projector contract, with a narrow overlap query. It should say plainly that a clean finite audit is neither a production acceptance bug nor a full hosting theorem.

title: [Lean] Prove unitary prefix bounds on the existing Lemma G semantics
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This proves the quantified norm implication requested by PR1282 directly on the unchanged `LemmaG.Stream` event semantics. For every finite event word and prefix, norm-preserving label maps, exact relabel recipes and `WellLabelled` execution transfer the exact scalar row bound to the physical register norm. Zero private inputs are omitted from the active-input sum. An all-prefix row certificate remains an explicit premise.

The package also proves the Euclidean partial-store bound, including independent real/imaginary write masks: endpoints bounded by `L` imply squared norm at most `2 L²`, with a strict binary envelope from `2 L² < 2^(2b)`. The 13 core and 20 example theorems include exact witnesses for mismatched labels, incorrect recipes, nonunitary labels and a `41/25` partial-store overshoot.

This is a scoped formalization, not a new conjugation theorem or numeric replay. The selected PR1094 word, concrete row certificate, exact physical recipes, coefficient scratch implementation and full precision/analytic transfer are not instantiated in Lean. The 18/21-bit numerical examples explicitly assume their endpoint bounds. No selected record, production precision charge or kappa is changed.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `bdd4c63ac7c5d8a46ce070ba133df8d7ba9cb92c`; refreshed main: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. Relevant guidance, selected record and all five live source inputs are unchanged; the focused patch applies cleanly.

title: Research: independently check semantic-D bridge for composed R439 word
body:
PR1194's proposed semantic-D substitution contract is applied there to the 11,500-ADD PR1062 word. PR1122 changes A and cleanup as well, and retains the H2/K interface-adoption obligation. This package independently checks the contract's exact antecedents on PR1122's pinned **10,652-ADD candidate**, including the unchanged chronological continuation after a proof-only original-D prefix.

The independent set-valued calculation covers all **661 arbitrary dirty input columns**: semantic D compensation equals the raw continuation's K, with V=J=I and no target contribution to the source/helper block. The original-D splice passes every original H1–H5 and U/J/K/C flag through the unchanged owning checker. The actual candidate retains exactly its documented syntactic H2/K failures. The README gives the inherited substitution argument and names its common-frame assumptions. This is a scoped application of the predecessor's proposed proof, with no new circuit, saving, or κ.

Complete forward/reverse COPY/ERASE replay and local recount agree with the predecessor: **10,652 ADDs**, D 5,548; nine rank-seven copies/erasures; rank mass 5,129; identical ordered frame paths; F=15,223, B=3,910,388; strict 92/176-bit envelopes below the retained 104/192 caps. Nine mathematical controls reject dirty-restoration, compensation, source/target response, forbidden operand/frame and stale-cleanup faults. The stale cleanup passes the binary endpoint but fails H4, demonstrating why the bridge cannot be inferred from endpoint equality alone.

### Sources, task and overlap

- Start: current main `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`.
- PR1122: `a2551e70fce0cc34348f50f1a94e7cc4c80bbcbf`; exact candidate blob `0ab597fefd68bfefecc85d631b172d174bdaeb70` copied with original notice/license. PR1194 proof: `2e39c98238f543d988f9efc1b076590a4b780dca`. Both heads rechecked unchanged.
- Card `bit-helper-contract`, refined; OS nonce `09c41251dd3913927a6d642281ba7824`, priority revision 2. TASK.json records scope, sources, stop rule and follow-up.
- Refreshed overlap helper at 2026-10-13 22:24 UTC: 803 open PRs including drafts and 53 Discussion records, complete pagination. Literal searches exclude arbitrary diffs/nested sources and do not prove novelty. PR1194 owns the lemma; PR1122 owns the candidate and its native replay, including the PR1062 corner. PR1208 changes the word further; PR1306/discussion1290 instead examines target feedback. This independent check preserves H1.

### Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-abc-semantic-bridge
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
python3 -B scripts/research_baseline.py
```

All pass: registered replay and optimized relocation/corruption subprocess tests; 20 research tests with one skipped; selected-source bindings. Python 3.12.14 matches the deterministic receipt generated under Python 3.14.7. Three real package corruptions are rejected. Metadata/pins and staged whitespace checks pass.

Native replay, changed-word hosted emission/invoice, all-size compiler/common-label realization, precision/tape, recovery, analytic transfer and proof-assistant formalization are not executed or established here. PR1122's native evidence is credited, not freshly reproduced. Supplier adoption requires maintainer acceptance of the replacement interface and complete physical evidence; the selected frontier is unchanged. README/TASK give the concrete hosted-admission next question.

Arham Tahir, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review. Credit woklerx / PR1194; Gareth Davidson / PR1122; Sagar Thakrar / PR1062; Sricharan Vagvala / PR967; Aaron Wang / PR1015; Ross Richardson / PR923; DreamingOfClouds / PR589; eumemic / PR555/543; Zhihao Chen / PR425 and the retained scalar/checker lineage. Apache-2.0.

title: Research audit: X2 acceptance boundary for the selected owner map (no new kappa)
body:
**Adversarial audit of one selected supplier obligation; no new κ.** Navinor, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

Task selection: `adversarial-audit` track via `scripts/choose_research_task.py` (OS-random nonce `ca8debca8488dd850dd6c0afb7398632`), card `supplier-boundary-audit` (scope key `dcdb0fa8e49b08a958d0`), refined to one named condition. Base commit `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; audited source head `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810` (the selected owner map, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094).

## Question and answer

The card asks: does one selected supplier obligation follow from its actual source-bound checks?

**Obligation X2:** pending axes of distinct idle children of one physical family are disjoint, so a family's hosts on different children never share a cell (stated and checked in Josie Elliston's owner audit, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1091).

**Answer: no.** X2's acceptance does not follow from the selected record's `reproduce` command. It is enforced exactly once, at batch1099 review time, by `research/community-batch1099-audit/check_frontier1094.py` (pinned in the record's `proof_supplements`). Neither `make frontier1094-verify` (stages `historical-source`, `baseline1042-cold`/reuse, `rare-pattern-exchanges`) nor `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` (record and hash validation only, no subprocess execution) nor the `community-batch1099.yml` CI job (which runs `research/t16-owner-audit-seed67/verify.py --fetch` for its pinned claim list, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1022 through https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1087, excluding the selected supplier) executes that composition. The frozen verifier chain the replay does run (`upstream1087.tar.gz`, Hao Yan's https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/858 lineage) keys hosted cells per `(owner, child, port)` in `t16/indep16.py` and asserts only `len(pending) == rank` per child in `code/audit_allcold.py`; cross-child cell sharing is outside its rule set.

## Minimal adversarial instance

One integer in the pinned `DATA-PHASES.json` pending axes: child 1's axis 131072 at port 0 replaced by 13, already pending for child 0 (children 0 and 1 are distinct idle children of the same physical family place). Exactly one differing integer; every rank, window, role count, width and profile aggregate is preserved.

- `geometry()` rejects it: `X2: children [0, 1, 14] share axes at port 0`.
- With only the X2 check suppressed, `geometry()` returns an identical geometry object and the complete R1–R7/X1 rule set accepts the fixture. The X2 rule is the only rule that reads pending axes.
- Concrete damage: roles at time 3 and time 6 (both helper 476, owner replica 0, family 224, port 0, offset 0, width 8) resolve the same pending axis 13 of family 224 — one physical cell written twice — while every role-level rule accepts both.
- A second mutation (one axis duplicated inside a single child's list) is rejected at X2 as well. Both are failure controls with single-locus, rank-preservation and null-mutation guards.

The existing rejection batteries contain no X2-directed mutant: the owner audit's 11 controls and the frozen chain's 6 independent-t16 controls. This PR supplies the first two, answering the card's method ("construct one semantically invalid but superficially well-formed fixture and test rejection").

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_PR1094_X2_ACCEPTANCE_BOUNDARY_AUDIT`. Fresh run on Python 3.13 (Windows) in this session returned that status with both mutants rejected at X2. Deterministic record and exact input pins in `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/RESULT.json`. The repo suite `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` (with `PYTHONUTF8=1`) runs 20 tests with 5 errors and 1 skip — identical with this change stashed. The 5 errors are pre-existing environmental failures in `test_research_onboarding.PackageTests` on this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf=true` breaks the temp-fixture scaffold commit comparison); they do not involve this package.

## Files changed (new package only; `upstream/`, frozen pins and selected record unchanged)

- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/README.md` — task card, trace table, evidence, open next questions.
- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/verify.py` — stdlib-only harness (positive control, M1/M2 mutants, cell-collision witness, blindness measurement, control inventory, enforcement trace).
- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/RESULT.json` — deterministic record with source pins.
- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/TASK.json`, `VERIFY.json`, `SOURCES.json` — scope metadata and replay manifest.

## Remaining obligations (not claimed)

- The full `make frontier1094-verify` cold replay with the mutated phases was not run (needs the published frontier1042 baseline artifacts and cold replay time); frozen-chain acceptance of the mutant is code-trace evidence, not execution.
- No claim other than the selected inputs was re-audited; the historical owner-boundary-audit package was used as a method example only.
- This is a checker-coverage audit of one named obligation: not a construction, not a supplier change, not a κ claim, and not a proof of hosting soundness (X2 itself is enumerated on the pinned phases, not proved universally).

## Credit and predecessor attribution

X2's rule wording and the independent owner audit are Josie Elliston's (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1091), reused unchanged as a library. The selected owner map is Rohan Arun's https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094 on Jeremy Kothe's T16 owner-map lineage (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1050 and successors); the frozen verifier chain is Hao Yan's https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/858 lineage; the batch1099 composition and review are Douglas Colkitt's; independent endpoint pricing is Sagar Thakrar's https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1069. Nearest concurrent findings: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1277 (the reuse replay discards its ancestry recheck) — same replay-coverage class, different obligation, credited for the direction; https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1209 audits pending-axis independence of the selected data semantically, while this PR tests which checkers reject a corrupted fixture at all.

Audit by Navinor with help from opencode.

title: research: prove six calls for a three-source shear with one four-valued phase
body:
Three independent dirty-source transfers y_j += (C-I)x_j require exactly six C/C^-1 calls when C has all four character values 1,i,-1,-i. The lower bound permits arbitrary constant invertible complex role mixing and any number of restored arbitrary-dirty helpers. It excludes other phase functions and additional character-dependent gates, including free C^2/Pauli/address operations. This is a scoped written theorem with exact canonical checks; no new kappa or supplier admission.

The proof reduces a four-call candidate to phase-direction span three or four. Laurent interpolation excludes the four-dimensional case. The three-dimensional case forces two alternating target loops whose simultaneous constant-transfer images have ranks one and two. Six direct calls attain the required complete map. Eight binary-spectrum four-call words remain valid positive controls, showing why the full-spectrum premise matters.

Only research/four-spectrum-shear/ is added: README, proof, verifier/regenerator, exact certificate and attribution notice. Python 3.10+ standard library:

    python3 -I -B research/four-spectrum-shear/verify.py

Expected: PASS_FOUR_SPECTRUM_SHEAR minimum=6 binary_minimum=4 controls=7 no_new_kappa.

Validation: separate native and Python exact engines agree on all mathematical certificate fields; normal, isolated optimized, relocated and applied-patch replay pass; deterministic regeneration is byte-identical; seven mathematical mutations and two on-disk/output controls reject. The general case split is not proof-assistant formalized. No selected supplier/record, frozen package or framework is changed; full selected replay is outside this standalone change.

Prepared by Richard Hoekstra with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; no independent human peer review or literature-priority claim. Context and distinct model boundaries are credited for PR1235, PR836, PR800, PR720 and PR990. Open next questions cover the three-value spectrum and explicitly paid additional character-dependent gates.

title: Prove a nine-root obstruction for one masked P112 co-star decoder
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The fixed rational masked P112 decoder with co-star normal groups `[0,1,56,87]` and term capacities `[3,2,2,2]` cannot satisfy the required equations. This package gives a reusable rank-two crown lemma and a nine-root certificate explaining the obstruction, including when coefficients may vanish and left/right factors differ.

Six roots exclusive to one two-term group force its factors onto two distinct lines. Three further mutually orthogonal roots then lose that group's contribution, leaving two terms that would have to realize `4I₃`. The contradiction is rank at most two versus rank three.

The 12-file package contains the written proof, explicit E8 model and source-order provenance, exact certificate, deterministic expected result, standalone verifier, portability tests and task/replay metadata. Standalone replay needs only Python 3.10+ and the package directory. It has no runtime dependency on the historical search, census, pricing code or selected result.

## Task and overlap

Task `complex-masked-decoder`; scope **refined** from constructing a changed masked decoder to an exact obstruction for this one nine-term co-star assignment. It changes the eight-term/all-pairs assumptions rather than re-running their known bound. Base: `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`; exact historical model commit/blob/SHA-256 and the original task card are retained in `SOURCES.json` and `TASK.json`.

Nearest adjacent work: [#1292](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1292) (head `7a8325f6c8e5a6830ce919965a2959ac459e010a`) concerns eight-term P104 rigidity; [#1304](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1304) (head `a052f0da36a3845c2ec785fd44e5b9e50de3b688`) concerns a fixed A8 family. Their stated scopes differ from this two-sided co-star crown obstruction. Current [Discussion #1316](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1316) mixes one coordinate term with a free rectangle, also a different mechanism. These pending claims are overlap context, not theorem dependencies. Pre-submission refresh covered 807 open PR titles/bodies and all 26 Discussions without truncated threads; no direct duplicate was identified within those limits.

## Validation

Accepted by the final independent package review:

- Exact checker: 39 proof equations and 13 controls.
- Portability suite: 24 checks, including standalone copies with no checkout, spaces in paths, read-only deterministic runs, and malformed/missing/tampered inputs.
- Clean patch application and all registered Python 3.12 checks passed on original base `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8` and main `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. Both applied trees matched all 12 reviewed file hashes.
- A separate mathematical reviewer accepted the written proof and independently reconstructed its finite premises.

Reproduce with `python3 -I -O -B research/p112-costar-crown-obstruction/verify.py` and `python3 -I -O -B research/p112-costar-crown-obstruction/test_portability.py`.

Only this normal/capacity assignment is excluded. Other co-star candidates remain open; no decoder, physical realization or κ improvement is claimed. The verifier checks finite premises of the written proof, not a proof-assistant formalization.

## Credit

Coordinated in [Discussion #1267](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1267). Model attribution to PR717 and the retained PR968 adapter is recorded in `SOURCES.json` and `NOTICE`. Substantial AI assistance: Astra developed the proof/package, a separate Astra agent reviewed the mathematics, Fable 5.1 implemented preceding exploration, Gemini 3.8 Flash contributed brainstorming, and Codex coordinated. Separate-agent review is not human peer review.

## Open next questions

`README.md` and `TASK.json` record the smallest follow-up: freeze another co-star assignment and test whether its exclusive-root graph has a rank-two crown and residual rank obstruction before coefficient synthesis. No other assignment has been classified here; an exact surviving decoder and fully charged physical realization would still be needed for any κ claim. Full multiplication/selected-supplier replays were not run because this scoped proof changes neither.

title: Scoped bound: P112 star copy-cost drops need at least 20 trims
body:
The exact C/N root-star cost-64 theorem leaves further support trims outside its scope. This contribution answers the first-drop question raised by PR1242: **every original cost-seven P112 atom needs at least 20 total row-plus-column support deletions before its copied-information rank can fall**. The exact per-parent thresholds are 20 for 5,376 tagged pairs and 22 for 2,240. The recorded witnesses attain rank six. A frame-hit change is possible after only four deletions while the copy price remains seven; one extra trim changes neither quantity.

The proof reduces arbitrary erasures to minimum nonzero column-code weights, then uses rank factorization to handle simultaneous cuts on both factors. Both engines agree on all 7,616 tagged cost-seven parents (6,720 distinct support pairs), all 967,232 codeword cases, every threshold/witness/minimizer count and the complete code digests. title: Research theorem: exact paid cost for binary affine register words
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

In an explicit nonabelian binary-affine address model, noncommuting labels and arbitrarily many restored dirty registers cannot reduce the direct paid-call bill. The exact minimum for `diag([g_1],...,[g_w],1,...,1)`, with `g_i=(A_i,b_i)`, is `sum rank_F2([A_i-I|b_i])`.

The complete alphabet is formal `F2[AGL_d(F2)]` register words, free scalar `GL_r(F2)` basis changes, and unit paid calls `I+([g]-1)N` with binary rank-one idempotent `N` and rank-one homogeneous affine displacement. Nonzero translations are **paid** units; no address map is free. Every extra register must be restored on arbitrary dirty inputs. The attaining construction uses no extra register or scalar preparation. This is an optimistic screening model; real scalar work/storage and physical interfaces still need their own bill.

The written proof normalizes free scalar maps by augmentation, derives the lower bound from a homogeneous representation, and constructs an attaining factorization in the **formal group algebra** for every address dimension. A concrete triple of mutually noncommuting dimension-three targets requires nine paid calls for any restored dirty-register count; its nine-call formal construction with a fourth dirty register is checked.

This changes the address group and price rule from the card's rational abelian starting model. It does not reduce rational frames modulo two, prove a selected-supplier improvement, or claim a universal barrier for every nonabelian model. No kappa, frontier, physical supplier or multiplication-runtime improvement is claimed. The proof is written, not Lean-verified.

## Task and overlap

- Base and refreshed main: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; the patch applies cleanly. No guidance or selected inputs changed.
- One OS nonce `5d737eb3d3ab653b8a6a9411d0753d36` selected bit-mechanisms, card `bit-new-register-model`, scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f`, priority revision 2. Scope is refined to the complete binary-affine alphabet and arbitrary restored register count.
- PR468/720 concern the rational abelian three-register model; PR288 has related rank methods and a different nonabelian solvable-quotient setting; PR836 gives a complex/unitary obstruction. Their exact context and heads are recorded in `SOURCES.json` / `OVERLAP.json`.
- PR1194/1306 already cover the other suggested helper-contract card's immediate questions, so those investigations were not repeated.
- Final live overlap: 818 open PRs and 67 Discussion records, complete pagination, 2026-10-13 22:49 UTC. This is bounded overlap evidence, not a novelty certificate. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317 .

Only `research/binary-affine-register-bound/` and its dedicated full-census workflow are added.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -I -B research/binary-affine-register-bound/verify.py --full --work /tmp/binary-affine-full
```

Python 3.12+ and C++17 are required. The independent C++ Cayley BFS visits all **323,930 affine maps** through dimension four and **72,642,074 directed transitions**, without rank pruning. Python checks every distance, reachable state and explicit attaining factorization. The dimension-four histogram is `[1,225,11830,124200,186304]`. This enumerates address maps; the unlimited-register conclusion comes from the proof, not a claim to have enumerated all register circuits.

Additional evidence: 44,020 elementary rank checks; 96 exact formal words / 576 prefixes; 56 formal identities; 32 larger fixtures through dimension 32; seven boundary controls and five package tests. Controls distinguish dirty-helper correctness, noncommuting order, omitted calls, underpriced rank-two operations, translation offsets and the nonfaithfulness of the natural representation on the group algebra. Five packaging tests cover source/certificate/distance corruption, isolated read-only relocation and output preservation.

Registered Python 3.12 replay passed. A complete read-only exported replay under isolated optimized Python 3.14 rebuilt the C++ checker and produced the same canonical receipt, with all 14 input files unchanged:
`e95e3af2f484cb03f600c8d669354465f4812a1316e842e248fc81a48d5a30d0`.

The generic hook runs **quick coverage only**, explicitly omitting the full dimension-four native census; the dedicated workflow runs `--full`. Selected-record/source/provenance checks pass. Hosted CI is separate from these local results. No selected supplier cold replay, physical/native supplier, hosting, precision/tape/compiler or outer analytic admission was performed.

## Credit

Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, implementation, validation and writing; no subagent or independent human review. Apache-2.0; predecessor files/notices are unchanged. Credit eumemic, Ali Romman (PR468), David Govea (PR720), the retained rank-method lineage, and the helper-contract predecessors listed in the README.

The rank and reflection-length methods are classical; the proof credits Huang/Lewis/Reiner and delMas/Lewis with primary references. No new reflection-length principle or literature priority is claimed. The contribution is the explicit register-model cost statement, complete attaining construction, boundary audit and independent exhaustive certificate.

## Open next questions

A smaller coordinate-only paid alphabet can make direct target lengths exceed this rank floor; a dimension-three target with that gap is a concrete next search. Separately, any proposed physical escape should name the primitive/free-operation hypothesis it changes and price the full boundary. Natural representation equality alone cannot certify a formal word.
