title: Research: certified bit-side lever budgets for PR589 at a = 1/99 under the proposed revision 3 (no new kappa)
body:
**This PR has scoped obstructions and a screening table. There is no new κ, and the selected record is unchanged.**

- Track: bit supplier, seed 3.
- Card: `bit-helper-contract`, with the scope **changed**. The card question is saturated, and the register-model card is done in #1333.
- Base: `bce54fb3`.

## Why

The **proposed** priority revision 3 (open #1272, stacked on open #1240) prices the centre-path, rank-shape and coverage-law levers for the complex supplier only. This PR adds the bit-side numbers for the selected PR589 supplier.

## Model and premises

The arithmetic uses exact rational intervals, standard library only, and imports no repository engine.

It is #1240's coverage-law relaxation, applied to the bit side:
- Per call, the paid mass is (m−u)w + cst, with m = 64, w = 888/9 and cst = 63. This gives D = W − 63N, as in format-limits (Dfc).
- Local children are either the replayed word or the most favorable in-window shapes: each data register is one rank-7 climb, and each helper is one climb whose rank equals its width.
- Copies are carried at rank 7. This is a premise; at rank 8 nothing changes.
- Idle mass goes to the halving-depth cap, with fractional counts and no surcharge. Each of these steps can only lower the bill, so a certified fail rules out every construction that meets the premises.

**The idle cap is a premise tied to the halving depth.**
- `global_k.py` raises the halving depth until 2·maxchild^HD < m^HD.
- The row bound limits HD:
  - The record uses HD 2 under the PR510 bound (row 18355), so the cap is 45.
  - The merged elementary-cover bound (`row_bound.py`) admits HD ≤ 4, which gives caps 50 and 53.
- Results are reported at caps 45, 50 and 53. Cap 63 is a robustness bound only.

## Results (certified at a = 1/99)

| Bit lever (cap 45) | root a | × | 1/99 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Packing ceiling (reproduces merged #1023's free concentration) | 0.0019559 | 1 | fail |
| Centre path free | 0.0054196 | 2.771 | fail |
| Centre path shared by two calls | 0.0036864 | 1.885 | fail |
| Two unpaid coordinates | 0.0073120 | 3.738 | fail |
| Rank-8 children / rank-16 children | 0.0032114 / 0.0047309 | 1.642 / 2.419 | fail |
| Centre free + rank-8 (shipped helper mass) | 0.0089383 | 4.570 | fail |
| Centre free + rank-16 / + two unpaid | 0.0131671 / 0.0107587 | 6.732 / 5.501 | pass |
| Centre free + ideal data + ≤ 332 width-8 helpers (in window) | 0.0101021 | 5.165 | pass |
| Two unpaid + ideal in-window shapes (copies kept) | 0.0117941 | 6.030 | pass |

The fail rows also fail at caps 50, 53 and 63.

**O1 (copy charge 63).**
- Even with no helpers and ideal data, the bill exceeds 1 at a = 1/99 at every cap from 42 to 63.
- The ceiling is 0.006794 at cap 45 and 0.009665 at cap 63.

**O2 (centre path shared, copy charge 31.5, full-frame width-8 helpers).**
- The maximum helper count is 104, 131 and 145 at caps 45, 50 and 53. Each count k is certified: k passes and k+1 fails.
- The strict design-free floor of format-limits section D is 138. It applies to full-frame helpers and is cited as an argued premise.
- **The obstruction holds at halving depth ≤ 3 and flips at depth 4.**

**Joint surface.** The README has the table of copy charge × full-frame helper count at caps 45, 50 and 53, for ideal and shipped data shapes.

**What it does not say.**
- With the shipped helper mass, centre free needs rank-16 children or a second unpaid coordinate.
- But in this relaxation, fewer helpers (≤ 332) or a second unpaid coordinate reach 1/99 *inside* today's windows.

**Complex side.**
- #1240's ceiling is reproduced.
- #1272's ×6.5 combination (0.011008) needs rank-16 children beyond the window h = 9.
- Inside the window, centre free + rank-9 gives 0.008128 (fail), and two unpaid + rank-9 gives 0.010911 (pass).

## Checks

- **Bindings.** Selected record → frontier1094 certificate → `PR589-EXPECTED.json` → bit word, endpoint, halving depth and row coefficient. The row-bound and halving-depth source lines are pinned.
- **Positive controls.** The selected bit endpoint is accepted and the next 1e-24 point is rejected, with the surcharge. #1240's complex ceiling is reproduced.
- **Replay.** The local histogram equals the record: mass 5,129 and the class split. The profile equals 288 local words plus idle.
- **Tests (15).** They cover:
  - the interval engine and the endpoint;
  - the relaxation steps;
  - the guards and the halving-depth cap table;
  - the O1 and O2 boundaries at each cap;
  - the in-window centre-free boundary (332 passes, 333 fails);
  - tampering.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-revision3-levers-seed03/verify.py           # ~13 s; PASS_BIT_REVISION3_LEVERS
python3 -I -B -m unittest discover -s research/bit-revision3-levers-seed03 -p test_package.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-revision3-levers-seed03
```

## Overlap

- #1240 and #1272 (Douglas Colkitt / Mister-Meeseeks): this is the bit analogue, in independent code.
- #1293 (navinor): reconciled in the README.
- Merged format-limits sections A, A.4, A.7 and D. A.7's ×2.79 cross-checks the centre-free row.
- #974 (avirazza).
- #1023 (ours, merged): the packing ceiling is reproduced, not claimed as new.
- #1281 (mightyOil).
- #1194, #1311, #1179, #1253 and #1128.
- #1333 / #1317 (bitplane).

## Disclosure

Prepared by Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. Parallel read-only scout and judge subagents ranked the question. A post-PR adversarial review found the halving-depth error and two overclaims; all are corrected in the second commit. No claim was posted to Discussions. Apache-2.0.

title: Scoped negative result: no further helper-donor kernels or exact read re-timings on the #1297/#1305/#1324 words (no new kappa)
body:
## Summary

Scoped negative result, **no new κ**. **Revision 2 (`9e944899`)** adds a rigorous true-moment bound and narrows the optimality wording, in answer to the review continuation point; details are below. **Revision 3 (`c9da5f27`)** follows #1186's portable revision 3 (`c37dfb07`), so `regenerate.py` keeps working if #1186 merges as is; the evidence is unchanged.

The census runs on #1297's two local words. #1305, #1324 and #1319's T74 exact fill use the same Git blobs. #1305 and #1324 were later withdrawn by their author, because their idle overlays move axes across Z4 families. Kernels in richer families were later found on these words: #1625 (pivot 566) and #1672 (pivot 554). Both lie outside the two families searched here.

On those words, two kernel families give **no further gain** over **all 306 helper pivots read before their first B write**, where #1297 searched four:
- #1274/#1297's two-shock helper-donor kernels, with both restoration rules;
- exact re-timing of early reads.

Every neutral candidate is surrogate-optimal with a certificate, and none can lower the per-call moment at b by more than **1e-6 cost units** (rigorous). #1305's idle overlay is the exact optimum of the donor-star class its own verifier admits; that is now a statement about a withdrawn class.

Package: `research/frontier1305-kernel-census/`. Claim and results: [discussion #1314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1314).

## Starting point, validated locally (before the withdrawals)

- **#1324 @ `43c19465`:** a fresh checkout ran `verify.py`, including fresh native replays of both words and strict admission. Result: `PASS_GLOBAL_MIXED_X54_IDLE_EXCHANGES_NATIVE_AND_STRICT_ADMISSION 0.001677380107853623` (156 s, no Boost).
- **#1305 @ `a96a5d95`:** the same run gives `... 0.001677162029073474` (127 s).
- The #1186 `kappa.kappa(H, 37)` pricer reproduces both κ values, and #1297's, exactly from their profiles.

## Results (identical on both words)

Pricing uses #1186's harness, pinned at revision 3 (`c37dfb07`; its pricing code is revision 2's, `3855fd41`):
- the auditor's static rules;
- an exact program-map screen;
- an unchanged derived compensation;
- recomputed cone caps, tail-mutable frames and cut equality;
- the surrogate optimum certified by integer duality;
- `audit_local` on every negative delta;
- a true-moment interval certificate for every priced candidate.

| Family | Candidates | Neutral (Δ = 0) | Frame-infeasible | Inexact | Gains |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| #1297 relation rule, restore at end of early cleanup | 61 (25 pivots) | 32 | 8 | 21 | **0** |
| Same relation, restore just before the pivot's first write (exact by construction) | 292 (43 pivots) | 52 | 240 | 0 | **0** |
| Exact early-read re-timings within the target's suffix segment (152 pivots) | 803 | 635 | 168 | 0 | **0** |

- **True-moment bound (revision 2):** this covers all 1,438 neutral candidates, both words:
  - the realized true delta is exactly 0, because the paid profile is unchanged;
  - no candidate can lower the per-call moment at b below the base word's frames by more than 1e-6 units, where one unit is 2^-40 of that moment. The exact rational bounds are about 1e-11 and are rounded up.

  Infeasible and inexact rows involve no cost. Every verdict, delta and profile equals revision 1's.
- **Positive control:** on #1297's input word, the census reproduces its 5+5 hooks for pivots 555/567, including the committed donors 620/628. Each is priced at −11,707 surrogate units (H1 −3, H3 +1), the realized kernel worth 2.616e-7 κ. Its true value is −11,707.88 units, a certified gain, and `audit_local` passes all ten.
- **Robustness:** all base-word verdicts and profiles are identical at #1324's endpoint weights.
- **Idle:** exact backtracking over every assignment in all 3,687 (replica, port) groups gives the optimum, and it equals #1305's selection. No size-4 group admits a three-receiver donor in that class. #1324's simultaneous swaps are the larger class that does reach (51,51,51,39).
- **Deletion screen:** prices the word with a pivot's early reads deleted and no compensation. The largest prices are pivots 439/444 (−67,944), 438/440 (−62,316) and ten pivots at −51,648 (≈ +1.16e-6 κ). This is reported as a screen, **not a bound**: on the control word the uncompensated deletion of 555/567 is frame-infeasible, while the kernels are feasible and gain.

## Evidence and reproduction

- `python3 -B research/frontier1305-kernel-census/verify.py`: standard library, ~30 s. It checks the input pins, replays all five censuses exactly in rational arithmetic, binds every priced record to exactly one census match, and recounts all evidence against `RESULT.json`. It also checks every candidate's true-moment bound against `RESULT.json` and runs the positive control. It rejects five failure controls: a one-byte input change, a changed early-read coefficient, a forged negative price, a priced edit absent from the census, and a forged bound. It is a **recount**: it does not rerun the frame optimization or the interval certificates. Registered: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result` under Python 3.12.13. `tests/test_research_*.py` passes (20 tests, 1 skipped).
- `regenerate.py --toolkit <PR #1186 at c37dfb07>/research/exact-frame-toolkit --out NEW` reruns pricing, re-timing and deletion; with `--idle-run` it also reruns the idle check. It first checks the toolkit's pinned `MANIFEST.json` and every file that manifest lists. Two consecutive revision-2 runs reproduced all 15 toolkit-dependent evidence files byte for byte, in about 9 minutes each on 12 workers. Against revision 1's evidence, 8 files are byte-identical and the other 7 differ only by the added bound fields.
- **Revision 3:** `regenerate.py` now pins #1186 revision 3's `MANIFEST.json`. `deletion.py` used the harness's private SIGALRM handler, which revision 3 replaced with `compat.deadline`; it now uses the toolkit's `compat.deadline` and `Timeout`. `verify.py` and `regenerate.py` now refuse to run under `-O`; before, `verify.py`'s guard was itself an `assert`, which `-O` strips, and `regenerate.py` had none. A fresh regeneration with revision 3, including the idle check, reproduced all 16 evidence files byte for byte (about 8 minutes on 12 workers). `RESULT.json` changes only in its toolkit pin.

## Limitations

- These are finite searched families on two fixed words in #1186's frame model, at the stated b. The surrogate optimum is certified and true gains are bounded by 1e-6 units; exact true-moment optimality is not claimed.
- Not covered:
  - compensations with three or more shocks;
  - window donors on helper readers;
  - cleanup-side corrections;
  - other words, owner maps or hosting.
- Nothing is admitted, so no native or strict replay of candidates was needed or run.
- The idle statement holds only inside #1305's `verify_idle_overlay.py` class.
- The pricing scripts need #1186's toolkit (open PR); `verify.py` does not.

## Open next question

Do three-shock or window-donor relations exist for the high-screen pivots, 438/440 and the ten −51,648 pivots? #1625 and #1672 have since found kernels in such richer families, at pivots 566 and 554.
- **First step:** extend `census.py`'s dictionary to windows `x += c·q … x −= c·q` on any register x, closing before the first write. Solve sparse dyadic combinations of at most three terms, then price with `price.py`.
- **Blocker:** about 2,500 distinct suffix vectors per pivot, so the search needs support-guided pruning.

## Credit

- rohanarun: #1297 words, relation rule and edit format (`search_relations.py`).
- Jeremy Kothe: #1274 helper-donor mechanism; #1305/#1324 idle compositions and strict packages.
- Gonzalo-Mier: #1252 idle exchanges and verifier.
- The #1218/#1193/#1148/#1195 lineage.
- Wronskode: #1288 saturation sweeps on the #1218 words.
- PatatePatatePatate: #1276 idle ceiling on #1094.
- Pricing harness: #1186.

Vendored inputs are unmodified Apache-2.0 copies; see `NOTICE.md` and `inputs/PINS.json`.

Prepared by Marius-Paul Dumitrean with substantial AI assistance (Anthropic Claude, via Claude Code). Apache-2.0.

**Workflow note (optional feedback):** this used the `selected-packing` card with the scope changed to local-word kernels on the highest open claim. The main friction was that the frontier moved during the session: #1324 landed with the same words, which was easy to check with blob ids. One suggestion: the overlap helper could list open PRs that share Git blobs with a package's inputs.

title: Tooling: exact helper-donor cold-kernel search — rediscovers #1297's kernels, census on #1305/#1324 words (no new kappa)
body:
Adds `research/helper-donor-kernel-search/`, the first published search tool for the helper-donor cold-kernel mechanism. That mechanism was introduced by #1274 (pivot 531) and extended by #1286/#1297; it is the largest local gain on the X54 line. **No new κ.**

## How the search works
For every write `p += k·Y` that has earlier reads of p, the tool:
- deletes a subset of those early reads;
- cancels p through Y at a cut, with an early-cleanup tail restore;
- computes the exact program-map change D mod 2³¹−19;
- solves a single-donor relation `q·v_hook = −D` with dyadic q;
- prices each candidate exactly with #1186's frame solver.

## Results
- **Positive control.** On #1218's word (no kernel yet), the tool rediscovers #1297's pivot-555 kernel exactly: delete reads 466/502/734, donor 620 with coefficient 2 at hook 112, cost −11,676, profile H1 −3, H3 +1. It also finds the five equivalent donor hooks.
- **Census.** On #1305's final words, which #1324 (the current best claim) uses unchanged, I searched every register and write: 1,048 write instances per word, both words. **No further single-donor kernel exists.** Further local gains need two-donor relations or other cancel forms; see Open next questions.
- **Negative control.** The already-applied pivot 555 gives no gain.

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 -B research/helper-donor-kernel-search/verify.py --toolkit <PR1186>/research/exact-frame-toolkit   # ~1 min
```
Output: `PASS_HELPER_DONOR_KERNEL_SEARCH_CONTROLS`. Inputs are vendored and pinned: #1305 `a96a5d95` and #1218 `0aa14797`.

A candidate the tool finds is nomination data, not an admitted construction. All inherited conditions remain.

title: Research: sharp ten-query mutable-source connector (no new kappa)
body:
PR943's read-only five-source connector needs an extra pair of map calls. This contribution adds one explicitly paid operation family: temporarily XOR source rows, then restore them. For a common exact F2-linear B and arbitrary A_m, all 31 nonzero five-source output patterns use **10 B queries, 62 readouts and 12 source XORs**, preserving arbitrary dirty inputs and scratch. The common-B and temporary-source-ownership assumptions are essential.

**Scoped recursive-interface result; no new kappa or supplier adoption.** Ten B queries are sharp when each output is read twice, even allowing arbitrarily many source shears. The proof reduces nine-query coverage to all 2,600 normalized nine-point sets in F2^5; direct pair-set and separate integer Walsh-autocorrelation checks agree on the complete histogram. Twelve XORs are an attained count, not an optimum.

The full five-factor recursive word includes every child and inverse: 2,016 arbitrary-map leaves plus 12 identity-row XORs, versus 2,072 leaves for each literal PR943 repair, with four borrowed dirty rows throughout. The invoice separately counts 648 versus 666 internal nodes and 84 versus 74 root instructions. A declared positive tariff paying leaves, XORs, nodes and root dispatch gives **2,760 versus 2,812** units. This is an abstract complete price fixture; no physical runtime advantage follows. PROOF.md states the general price inequalities and a dense implementation with separately charged access, travel, preparation and control obligations.

Only `research/mutable-source-connector/` is added. Start with README.md and PROOF.md; SOURCES.json pins the three live predecessor inputs. Base/current main: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; contribution: `f1dcab36fa63f8226f70dd07e26f44afb9d39b51`. Selector nonce `a083d7387e219510c2de83d13581da77`, recursive-interfaces track, refined `connector-alphabet-change` card. TASK.json includes the question, pilot, stop rule, local claim, exact overlapping heads and next steps.

## Validation

Windows 11 / CPython 3.12.14, standard library:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mutable-source-connector --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mutable-source-connector
python3 -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py
```

All pass, along with the card's unchanged PR943 positive control and staged whitespace checks. Evidence includes exact free noncommutative replay of all 40 incoming dirty rows in both directions, both predecessor repairs, the complete 2,600-set census, **3,024** separate dense matrix executions, nine primary mathematical controls, two concrete oracle controls and four package test groups covering optimized relocation, deterministic regeneration, occupied-output preservation and eight source/certificate corruption cases. VALIDATION.md records an initial Windows temp-directory failure and its passing scratch-directory correction.

## Scope, overlap and credit

The selected record and frozen inputs are unchanged. No selected cold replay, fresh native supplier run, complete repository suite, Lean, hosted CI pass, physical supplier instantiation, ownership/frame admission, precision/tape realization or analytic-transfer proof is claimed. The next practical task is to locate an actual common-B boundary and price one source XOR completely; source immutability or an unfavorable tariff should stop that adoption attempt.

Final overlap refresh covered **821 open PRs including drafts**, with complete public REST pagination at 2026-10-13 23:03:34 UTC. The repository helper searched their titles/bodies and local notes/ledger. Public discussion listing, start-here, handoff and mechanism pages were inspected; complete Discussion pagination and a connected Discussion-write tool were unavailable, so the claim is local. This is bounded overlap evidence, not proof of novelty.

Credit **Ross Richardson's PR943/934**, **shhxera/CubeJerry's PR889**, **Chafik Boukhalfa's PR628**, Douglas Colkitt and the retained framework. PR1185 at `4a60772285ce70f6414458f6d3a54948652bbed0` extends the unchanged alphabet to six sources; Hanson Sun's PR1215 at `8870e80d720ffa3a666bb5496c33373c45b90751` checks its free-algebra word. They are complementary and no pending code is imported. PR1103/982 borrows outputs; PR1318 concerns a different four-valued complex-phase model. No priority is claimed for classical finite-group difference bases or dirty echo cancellation.

Prepared by **Arham Tahir** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in research, algebra, both implementations, tests and writing. No subagents or independent human review. New work is Apache-2.0; predecessor sources/notices are retained unchanged.

title: Scoped negative result: R439 quad17 minimizes positive ADDs and reverse envelope
body:
Gareth Davidson's retained PR952 R439 quad17 circuit already attains the exact minimum of 12 positive ADDs for its six-register integer transfer. This contribution certifies that minimum and proves its reverse positive envelope equals the entrywise absolute inverse, so it is the smallest valid endpoint envelope for every independent incoming coordinate budget. **Scoped negative result; no new kappa or supplier adoption.**

Two separately implemented complete searches remove gates from opposite ends. Each exhausts 9,739 states / 43,454 edges and counts 1,008,032 shortest ordered programs. Their independent row/column reverse censuses agree on all 57 matrices and multiplicities; the parent's matrix is the sole entrywise Pareto minimum, attained by 767,232 programs. The reverse-envelope floor also has a written algebraic proof covering all exact realizations of this fixed inverse.

Base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. OS assignment seed 17, bit-supplier track. Actual input: PR952 head `11d24706f06e95271804c9438869546724c67aab`, source-bound committed artifact, `A[854:866]`, frame283, registers 312/355/412/429/434/490. Exact Git blob and SHA256 pins are in `SOURCES.json`. The selected result at the base is PR1094, conditional kappa 0.001672660197076918.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r439-quad17-seed17/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_R439_QUAD17 minimum=12 shortest_programs=1008032 reverse_endpoints=57 sharp_absolute_inverse controls=8 no_new_kappa`.

Passed direct certificate replay, registered package metadata and replay, research baseline bindings, selected-record inventory/supplement checks, and diff whitespace checks. Eight controls reject gate deletion, noncommuting reorder, a Boolean-equivalent integer lift, a false minimum, an envelope below the inverse, both resource caps and a false path multiplicity. No complete supplier/native replay is claimed. A complete live overlap refresh covered 822 open PRs and 73 discussion/comment/reply records with no quad17/frame283 match; its coverage limits and the installed gh --slurp workaround are recorded in `OVERLAP.json`.

The gate minimum fixes the exact integer map, six labels and positive ADD alphabet; it excludes signed forward gates, other Boolean lifts, extra wires and free permutations. The envelope theorem fixes this inverse and independent coordinate budgets; it does not optimize full-word correlations or intermediate prefixes. The existing pair costs 12 forward plus 12 mandatory literal cleanup ADDs. Paid profiles, decoder costs, recursive children and the selected frontier are unchanged. All-size/compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, analytic and H1-H5 assumptions remain inherited.

Credit PR952/904 (Gareth Davidson), PR936/925 (Ross Richardson), frame272 PR1002 and frame281 (woklerx), earlier factorization/guard work, and the R439/PR589/selected construction lineage. This is new exact evidence about an existing construction, with none of its previous savings claimed anew. Prepared by Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0; no independent human review claimed. The package includes concrete open next questions.

title: Independent verification: exact replay of one P112 asymmetric unit (no new κ)
body:
## Result

Adds an independent standard-library replay of the `d0=76` member of the off-pattern P112 two-sink unit recorded in `research/format-limits` C.6. It reconstructs the E8/Hamming lines and labels, checks all 12,544 entries of the decoder/pairing support identity, and recomputes the COPY ranks and correction supports.

The checked witness has window rank 9, 24 shared extra sources, coordinate COPY ranks 8 each plus extra-total rank 1 (sum 65), and correction supports 28+28 versus 52+52 for the corresponding coordinate rows. Two mutations fail exactness. The certificate records the witness parameters, source set, supports, counts and matrix hashes.

This is an exact finite audit of one supplied witness. It does not establish a complete supplier invoice, a cheaper recursive profile, or a new κ.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/p112-off-pattern-unit-audit-seed52/verify.py
```

Expected marker:

```text
PASS_P112_ASYMMETRIC_UNIT_AUDIT seed=52 d0=76 ports=112 entries=12544 window=9 extra_sources=24 copy_ranks=8x8+1 copy_cost=65 corrections=28+28 baseline=52+52 controls=2 no_new_kappa
```

The command passed under Python 3.14.7. The research-package metadata/pin check also passed. The repository package wrapper requests Python 3.12, which is not installed in this environment.

**Scope.** Bit side does not bind the selected kappa (a_c = 0.0016754627 < a_b = 0.0017334270, 3.46% slack) — no new kappa, same scope as the accepted seed-16 bit-track precedents. Simultaneity certified for pairs, not triples+ (giant components); Steinberg/structural moves out of scope.

body:
## Result and scope

**Research note / scoped structural proof. No masked decoder, physical supplier, or new kappa.**

For every arbitrary rank-six support restriction of an original cost-seven P112 C/N root-star atom, at most **1,120 of the 1,260 live orthogonal frames** can be met on both factors. A rank-factorization lemma reduces all joint cuts to maximal one-axis codeword cuts. The complete census covers **7,616 tagged parents and 967,232 maximal slices**; two separately implemented engines agree on every maximum, attaining cut, minimizer count, full codeword/hit digest, and certificate field.

The sharp per-parent joint maxima are 1,080 for 5,824 tagged parents and 1,120 for 1,792. The uniform averaged frame bound is 54. The simultaneous integer **frame-demand relaxation has sharp copy bill 60**: the inherited nine-root obstruction excludes nine terms, while the exact certificate supplies ten rank-six terms meeting every frame at least eight times.

The recorded cover leaves **21 diagonals uncovered**, so it cannot satisfy the masked identity for any coefficient choice. This is a concrete negative control, not a proposed decoder. A single 120-second refinement requiring diagonal coverage returned no feasible incumbent; it did not exhaust the search or establish infeasibility. That refinement retained one support representative per frame-hit pattern and excludes other representatives even with identical frame hits.

## Result (all brackets certified, exact rational intervals, code-disjoint from CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1240)
Positive control: `a* = 0.001690054109088696` reproduces https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240's grid ceiling `a < 0.001690054109089` within one 1e-15 step. The incumbent ceiling is **below the unbinding target**, so pure repacking cannot unbind the complex side; an interface change is required even for the near target.

| Lever (others at the selected line) | T2: unbinding | T1: `a = 1/99` |
|---|---|---|
| unpaid coordinates per family `u` | `u* ∈ (1.009826689, 1.009826689)`, least integer 2 | `u* ∈ (2.804078009, 2.804078010)`, least integer 3 |
| centre charge `c` (from 64) | `c* ∈ (63.021698514, 63.021698515)` | **impossible**: sup `a* = 0.004711142955614` at `c = 0` |
| families per replica `F` (9 stages) | least met 906 (905 fails) | least met 3093 (3092 fails) |
| paid-word count scale `s` | met iff `s ≤ 0.969437086` | met iff `s ≤ 0.049110034` |

Pair points at `F = 896`: `(u=2, c=0)` gives `a* = 0.009357801683738 < 1/99` — unpaid relief up to 2 with **any** centre charge fails T1 (sup over `c` is at `c = 0`); `(u=3, c=64)` gives `a* = 0.011001994530886 > 1/99` (optimistic sufficiency). The 4.911% word-scaling threshold independently matches https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240's "about 95% lower fully priced local excess spend". The `a* < D/E` diagnostic inequality is certified at four points (incumbent `D/E = 0.001695287130359` vs `a* = 0.001690054109089`).

## Not covered / limitations
- Necessity holds inside the stated model only; sufficiency is optimistic-relaxation (fractional counts, all idle at rank ≤ 51, no added charges). **No physical realizability, owner map, finite invoice, cold replay or new kappa.** The card's acceptance gate (a new physically realizable contract) is not met by this PR.
- `u`, `c` and the pair points are at `F = 896`; `F`, `s` at `u = 1, c = 64`. `u > 1`, `c ≠ 64` are what-if coverage laws needing their own admission. `κ = a/(1+a)` is the retained planning transfer; T2 uses the bit supplier pinned at the base commit.

The total scalar saving against the original 149,002 / 149,018 word is 13,182 per orientation. Paid recursive profiles are unchanged; selected κ remains 0.001672660197076918.

OS seed 27 assigns the complex-supplier track. The object was selected as index `27 mod 218` in PR1263's sorted forward gauge support: helper L253. The other 217 gauges stay fixed. For each orientation, all 96 incident ADDs are optimized by an exact sequence DP over every integer schedule. The proven finite exponent domains are [-2,4] forward and [-4,2] backward; each DP checks 4,662 state transitions and attains a -91 real-primitive delta. All transition scales and changed coefficients are charged. The resulting schedules add 21 scale macros in each orientation.

The verifier replays the complete word over all 712 formal data, helper and center columns in both orientations; checks source/frame/paid-event identity, complete scalar invoices, paid-profile equality and the local 192-bit payload limit; and authenticates the selected certificate. This result uses seed-selected L253 over PR1263's 218-helper constant-gauge word. title: Tooling: preserve registered replay coverage for input and workflow changes
body:
Registered packages can declare proof inputs anywhere in the repository, but the workflow currently filters events before that declaration reaches the planner. A change confined to a declared certificate or review file can therefore skip replay. Two later selection gaps also lose required checks: Git's default rename detection reports only the new path, and a change to the replay workflow selects no packages.

This tooling repair closes those three gaps in the same invalidation path:

- Run the planning job for otherwise eligible pull requests and pushes to `main`, without path filters. The manifest-aware selector still produces no replay jobs for unrelated changes.
- Use `git diff --no-renames --name-only -z` so renaming an input invalidates consumers of its old path as well as its destination.
- Treat the replay workflow, like the runner, as a shared control that selects every registered package.

The claim concerns packages present at the compared head, with canonical declared input paths and a valid comparison base. It does not infer undeclared imports or bypass GitHub event eligibility/permissions. Package verification, source pins, exactness checks, job timeouts and concurrency limits remain unchanged. No mathematical or κ claim changes.

**Concrete evidence:** pending PR1262 at `4b196b40dcac3ec40f62ec285babac53a1b5a3c5` declares 16 inputs. Four fall outside both former event filters: the selected certificate, the #1042 checkpoint, and the #1047/#1099 integration receipts. The base main tree has zero registered `VERIFY.json` files; this establishes a defect in the registration contract, not an observed missed hosted run. PR1262's mathematics is not evaluated here.

Validation:

```sh
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v
```

Expected: **26 tests pass**. On the primary CPython 3.15.0 research runtime, **25 pass and one skips** because full generic replay explicitly requires 3.12. The compatibility run uses installed CPython 3.12.12. Python.org confirms 3.15.0 remains current stable.

- Six new regression groups execute the actual planner CLI in temporary Git repositories. They cover inputs under certificates/docs/src, paths containing spaces, deletion, a Git-detected rename, both shared controls, unrelated edits, and new package-local artifacts. The JSON matrix and GitHub output count must agree.
- Restoring only the original workflow and runner causes **three regression groups to fail**. A separate before/after Git-tree-object model, which neither calls `git diff` nor imports the planner, agrees on ten seed-94 scenarios, including shared consumers.
- A separate Ruby YAML parser plus a bounded event model finds four excluded PR1262 inputs before the patch and none after. It is not a general Actions emulator. The no-path-filter regression is an explicit static policy guard.
- **actionlint 1.7.12** passes for the changed workflow (`-shellcheck='' -pyflakes=''`). The selected-record check and all **25 selected-record tests** pass. No hosted CI execution, selected cold replay, Windows run, or independent human review is claimed.

Cost: the existing planning/helper-test job now runs on all otherwise eligible events, including unrelated edits. Expensive package jobs remain selective; changing the workflow deliberately replays all registered packages. Hosted startup cost was not measured.

Base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; OS seed **94**, verification engineering. Final overlap covered 834 open PRs, 76 discussion records, and 325 local records, with complete remote pagination and no warnings. No pinned coordination issue exists; the claim and evidence are saved locally. PR474 concerns a historical gen4 workflow. PR1298 and PR1299 change other launcher behavior; this adds a separate test file and does not include their pending fixes.

Credit Douglas Colkitt for the package tooling and Sagar Thakrar for PR1262's concrete manifest example. Existing Apache-2.0 attribution is preserved. Prepared for Charles Bethin with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in diagnosis, implementation, tests, and writing. The guide describes the revised contract. GitHub's documented path-filter behavior: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore.

title: Scoped negative result: no extra singleton 4-to-6 B-frame in selected k8 word
body:
## Result

This package proves a scoped obstruction for one precise change to the selected PR1094 complex supplier: no single unchanged B-gate output frame on its selected k8 word can be enlarged from dimension 4 to dimension 6 while preserving the later frame chains.

There are 147 unchanged 4D B-gate frames. Each has 155 possible 6D superspaces in `F_2^9`, for 22,785 candidate gate/frame pairs. The exact intersection of all later paid frames on both affected register chains, early cleanups, and terminal frames has dimension 4 at 122 gates and 5 at 25 gates. Every legal enlargement would have to fit in this common suffix cap, so no 6D candidate exists. title: Scoped proof: exact 3-ADD minimum for PR1221's R439 frame-509 endpoint
body:
## Result

For the fixed R439 frame-509 Boolean endpoint on `(a,b,h,c)=(33,38,468,77)`, the minimum in the scalar one-destination ADD model is exactly **3**. The endpoint changes three distinct destinations, so fewer than three scalar ADDs cannot realize it. PR #1221's three-ADD word attains the lower bound. An exact four-register CNOT census has 1, 12, 97 and 626 distinct maps at lengths 0–3, with exactly three target words at length 3.

The four-ADD and three-ADD integer transfers are different by exactly `2 e_468 e_33^T`; this is a Boolean endpoint result, not integer-map equality.

## Relationship to concurrent work

Hanson Sun's open [PR #1221](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1221) provides the witness and explicitly makes no minimum claim. Concurrent [PR #1344](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1344) independently verifies the maps, full splice, and invoice, also without claiming a minimum. This package adds the local lower bound and exact shortest-word classification; it does not repeat PR #1344's full replay.

## Provenance and scope

- Base commit: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`.
- Selected conditional result stays `κ = 836330098538459/500000000000000000`; the complex supplier remains binding.
- PR #1221 head `6deda901721316fcb61c6e2a6dd6b537de183452`; parent circuit PR #973 head `c05dc72734c25dd069077157224d4dd30c6e8c19`; selected PR #589 head `a5afc8c6169ea61ba7c51dfd3cade02cc7b13b46` on PR #555.
- Source pins and overlap notes are in `research/r439-b509-local-minimality-seed06/`.

This does not establish a shortest factorization for the full frame-509 block, reprove H1–H5, establish hosted supplier admission, change the paid recursive profile, or claim a new κ.

title: Tooling: fast guard for the 35 live-checkout files the selected #1094 replay hash-asserts, plus complete replay triggers (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Tooling only. No new κ, and no change to any construction, certificate,
selected record, pinned document or pinned verifier.** Three files:

- `scripts/check_selected_ci_inputs.py`: a new standard-library guard.
- `tests/test_selected_ci_inputs.py`: 21 tests, about 3 s. `make verify-tests`
  picks them up automatically in the generic matrix's `tests` group, on every
  Python version.
- `.github/workflows/frontier1094.yml`: new path filters only; nothing existing
  is removed.

**Gap.** `make frontier1094-verify` passes `--main ROOT` to package stages. Those
stages hash-assert **35 repository files outside the selected package roots**
through each root's `data/UPSTREAM-PINS.json` and `construction/INPUTS.json`
`files.main`. The replay's first stage also checks the #1042 checkpoint record
(`certificates/checkpoints/frontier1042.json`), meaning its certificate and its
12-root inventory.

The per-PR check of the selected record (`verify_selected_result.py`) covers
neither, and at `dadfea6e` none of these files triggers `frontier1094.yml`.
Which checks those files triggered:

- **13 baseline558 files under `community-k492-audit/pr622` and 2
  `structural-gain` files:** no fast check fired.
- **The #1042 checkpoint's certificate and inventory:** no fast check fired.
- **The other 20 (`complex-k492-owner-repair/**`):** caught only by that
  package's own manifest workflow.

So a one-byte change could pass every fast check and surface only inside the
roughly 2-hour cold replay. Reproduced on a scratch worktree by appending one
byte to `.../baseline558/.../split-centres/CLIFFORD-RECIPES.json`:

- `verify_selected_result.py` printed PASS, and `tests/test_selected_result.py`
  passed.
- `research/gauge44-slots-t16/verify_t16.py --main .` raised
  `AssertionError: Upstream dependency changed`.
- The new guard printed `FAIL_SELECTED_CI_INPUTS` with that file in its drift
  list.

**Guard.** Everything is derived from `certificates/selected-result.json`.

*Hard checks (exit 1):*
- Every live pin matches the checkout.
- No two roots pin different bytes, and any in-root pin equals the selected
  source inventory.
- Every selected-result-format record named by the driver's static script
  closure passes `verify_selected_result.check`. Today those records are
  `checkpoints/frontier1042.json` and `selected-result.json`.

*Advisory, enforced by `--require-triggers`:*
- The one workflow whose `run:` commands invoke the driver, or its make target,
  must trigger on push and pull request for every required path:
  - every live pin;
  - every inventoried root file;
  - the driver's script closure and the files it names;
  - each named record's certificate, manifest and inventory.
- Trigger forms the minimal reader cannot evaluate exactly are reported, never
  assumed. These include `paths-ignore`, `types`, `tags`, branch filters
  without `main`, flow-style `on:`, and `? + [] {}` globs.
- The test enforces complete coverage only while #1094 is selected, so a future
  selection commit is not blocked by trigger bookkeeping.

**Remaining obligations / scope.**
- This is a drift and trigger guard, not a replay or a mathematical check.
- The driver closure is static: imports plus string-literal repository paths.
- Inputs read only by stages that route no pin through these manifests are out
  of scope.
- I did not run the cold `make frontier1094-verify` (2 hours, and it needs
  Boost).

## Task and overlap

- **Base and track:** base `dadfea6e`. Seed 94 → verification engineering. Card
  `portable-replay`, scope **refined**: the "environment failure" addressed is a
  CI drift and trigger gap in the selected reproduction chain.
- **How it was chosen:** five explorers covered stage profiling, canonical
  payloads, dependencies, CI workflows and control-suite memoisation. Judges
  scored their candidates for impact, rigor and novelty, and this one ranked
  highest.
- **Overlap:** none found. `find_overlap.py` ("path filter", "frontier1094.yml",
  "UPSTREAM-PINS", "live checkout") and open-PR searches turned up only #474
  (historical gen4 path filters).
- **Different objects:**
  - #1277 (mine): the #1094 reuse-mode ancestry binding.
  - #1142: #1042 capsule closure.
  - #1073 (mine): T37 log coverage.
  - #1101, #1137, #1156, #1151, #1184: runtime work.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/check_selected_ci_inputs.py --require-triggers
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_selected_ci_inputs.py
```

- **Current tree:**
  - Guard: `PASS_SELECTED_CI_INPUTS` with 35 live pins, 0 drift, 2 named
    records, 0 record failures, and 0 uncovered paths across 1,669 required
    paths. Takes about 0.8 s.
  - Tests: 21 OK on Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.8, about 3 s. Both files parse with
    `feature_version=(3, 11)`.
- **Failure controls in the tests:**
  - every single-byte change to each of the 35 pins;
  - a missing pinned file;
  - a conflicting pin and an in-root pin that differs from the inventory;
  - path-escape pins;
  - a later `!pattern` dropping a pull_request trigger;
  - `paths-ignore`, `types`, `tags` and a non-main branch;
  - quoted keys;
  - workflow detection: unrelated comments are ignored, and a second workflow
    with a compact `- run:` or `make <target>` is rejected;
  - a changed checkpoint certificate on a synthetic root;
  - exit codes, with triggers advisory unless required.
- **Mutation testing of the guard:** 21 of 22 mutants killed. These include
  dropping either pin manifest, emptying the closure, ignoring records,
  negation or unsupported filters, push-only events, and `*` matching `/`. The
  survivor is equivalent: the closure names the selected record itself, so its
  inventory already reaches the required set through the record check.
- **YAML reader:** agrees with PyYAML on all 134 evaluable `(workflow, event)`
  blocks in the repo. The 10 it refuses are genuinely different forms: eight
  push filters on `codex/*` branches and one flow-style `on:`.
- **Historical selections:** the guard exits 0 at #617, #626, #741, #799, #890,
  #942, #1042 and the #1094 integration commit. Hard checks hold at all of them,
  and trigger gaps there are only reported. That is why trigger coverage is
  advisory.
- **Related tests still pass:** `tests/test_selected_result.py`,
  `test_pr_reconciliation.py`, `test_isolated_test_runner.py`,
  `test_selected_inventory_links.py` and `test_selected_proof_binding.py`.
  `scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py` also passes.
- **Pre-PR review:** a three-lens review (soundness, claims, acceptability)
  found one blocker, which is fixed. `docs/ci-verification.md` is pinned by
  CONTENT-COVERAGE, so the stale "current selected replay" section there is
  **left for a maintainer**. Its #626 description is out of date. The review
  also drove four other fixes:

title: Research: audit P104 tangent-to-orbit local regularity (no new kappa)
body:
## Status

Independent proof-step audit; no new κ, decoder construction, supplier, or selected-frontier change. This is a second review following the completed claim [#1275](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1275) and [PR #1292](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1292). It does not repeat the tangent-matrix census: it checks the local regularity implication and exhaustively verifies the displayed P104 kernel generators against the pinned reduced systems.

## Finding

For each of the three P104 representatives, the pinned certificate gives tangent dimension 103 at `K0 = 2G`, equal to the dimension of the diagonal-torus orbit `O`. Since `O` is smooth and contained in the masked rank-eight variety `X`, `dim_K0(X) >= 103`; the certified tangent dimension gives `dim(T_K0 X) <= 103`. Thus the local ring is regular and `X` is smooth near `K0`. The inclusion `O -> X` has an isomorphism on tangent spaces between smooth 103-dimensional manifolds, so the inverse function theorem gives equality of their germs.

This supports the stated **local** conclusion. It does not rule out distant off-orbit P104 components or rank-nine costly parts and does not change the selected κ.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/seed38-p104-orbit-regularity-audit/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/seed38-p104-orbit-regularity-audit --check-only
```

The verifier replays the pinned PR #1292 certificate, including its D4⊕D4 negative control and seeded sample, then checks all 168 gauge/torus generators against all 4,992 reduced rows in each of the three P104 classes modulo `2^31 - 1`. It reports tangent/orbit dimension 103. The proof argument is in `PROOF.md`.

**Status:** verifier tooling and a scoped audit finding about receipt comparison on its own. The original runner independently pins its sources and actual inputs and executes the original wrapper. No incorrect owner result was demonstrated, and that protection was not bypassed. No new circuit, supplier, speedup or κ is claimed. Frozen predecessors, including `research/t37-slice-bitmaps/`, and the selected frontier are unchanged.

**Precise delta:** eight new files under `research/t37-receipt-role-binding/`:
- `receipt.py`: explicit path/role normalization and complete comparison.
- `verify.py`: checks the pinned inputs, the exhaustive collision domain, the relocation and failure controls, and both fresh T37 engines.
- `test_receipt.py`: six focused test groups.
- README, RESULT, TASK, SOURCES and VERIFY carry the contract, the evidence and the registered replay.

**Evidence.**
- **Legacy comparison:** all 40,320 of 40,320 hash permutations compare equal.
- **Strict comparison:** it accepts the one identity assignment and rejects the other 40,319. The smallest witness exchanges the word and local native-replay hashes, with every other receipt field fixed.
- **Both fresh complete engines agree** on 167,832 roles, 333 calls and all 14 inherited controls. The complete canonical receipt has SHA256 `1a0e4a30fc8b18c3db52cde322fc2a7646462497186cc6276e056b58253532fd`.
- **Controls:** five accepted layouts plus a check that the caller's data is not mutated, and eleven role, path and field rejection cases. Both fresh receipts reject a swapped association.

**Remaining obligations.**

- **Not checked:** the native compiler, whole-hosted emission, the invoice, moments, outer assembly, Lean, remote CI, and any other interpreter or operating system.
- **Still open:** the inherited compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, analytic and bit-interface obligations.

title: Scoped negative result: P112 GL3 COPY floor with three active projections
body:
Mixing two original P112 coordinate terms with one nonzero free odd rectangle through GL(3,C) cannot improve the COPY bill when all three replacement terms retain original-coordinate components on both sides. For the fixed pair (4,6), each term costs at least six; the whole decoder costs at least **66 versus 64**. If both projected coordinates are present in every factor, the whole floor is **72**. At unchanged width/normalization and `0<q=1-a<=1`, the full COPY power bill is at least **33/32** of the baseline, even granting all added preparation, source access, frame, mixing, restoration, hosting and child-management expenses zero.

**Scoped negative result; no new kappa or physical supplier.** The result leaves the exactly-two projected-product branch open. The identity `sum q_j p_j^T=I_2` proves that at least two products must be active, so it identifies the remaining algebraic boundary for this mechanism. Zero rectangles, other coordinate pairs and changed normalization are outside this theorem.

The proof reduces arbitrary complex original-coordinate normals to five exhaustive support classes. Two independently implemented exact engines cover all 25 class pairs and all 5,824 ordered odd port pairs: **145,600 records**, with refined survivor minima 6/7/8. Their cost bytes are compared directly, alongside every histogram, witness and slice dimension. A support-containment argument then handles arbitrary nonzero free rectangles and complex coefficients. Four Q(i) fixtures check all 12,544 entries each. Two concrete `(8,8,0)` boundary identities demonstrate why the hypotheses cannot be removed.

OS assignment seed **46**, structural decoder track. Exact base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; selected conditional kappa there is 0.001672660197076918, PR1094. Actual model input is retained PR845 geometry, derived from PR717 at `4150829a2cb66b823f4282da98985959ee448a90`. title: Research audit: quadratic dirty-interval amplification for commuting isometries
body:
The sharp dirty-prefix coefficient does not transfer to a linear joint-interval bound, even with commuting scalar isometries and subset budget G=1. This package proves an all-height family in the unchanged PR628 reserved-depth word: at n=2^h, one chronological interval has target-row absolute sum floor(h²/2)+h+2, while every prefix/inverse prefix is bounded by h+2. Together with the existing squared-prefix upper bound, the worst interval growth is Θ(h²). The four-factor example gives 6>4 with full arbitrary-dirty restoration.

The result addresses PR1278/1295's explicit sharp-interval follow-up. It does not contradict their valid sufficient bounds or assert an actual rounded failure. Destination-supported errors can behave differently; the proof states that boundary explicitly. No production precision, supplier, selected record or kappa changes.

Only `research/dirty-interval-coefficient-boundary/` is added: complete proof and first counterexample in README, task/scope card, exact source pins, two checking representations, deterministic certificate, failure controls and registered replay. Base main is `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; coordination claim is [Discussion #1357](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1357). Final overlap refresh covers 843 open PRs and 93 Discussion records, complete pagination, without warnings.

Validation on macOS arm64:

- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-interval-coefficient-boundary` passes on CPython 3.12.14: 272,012 complete free-algebra intervals at n=1..16 in both signs; exact scalar attainment of every finite maximum; 87,380 literal family leaf events through h=8; independent recursive dense/Gauss-Jordan family checks through h=20; seven mathematical controls and six test groups.
- The separate literal scalar check enumerates all 510 sign assignments and 1,553,988 intervals at n=1..8. Full inverse-cut recurrence, actual source/receipt corruption and complete read-only relocation pass.
- Isolated optimized CPython 3.14.7 reproduces the same full mathematical receipt. Package metadata/provenance, `make selected-record-check` and patch whitespace pass.

The all-height conclusion rests on the written recurrence, not finite extrapolation. Hosted CI, full selected cold replay, numerical cyclic kernels, physical/compiler/hosting/caller admission and proof-assistant verification were not run for this local lemma.

title: Research: COPY floor 64 for two-coordinate P112 mixing with small free rectangles (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Coherently mixing two P112 coordinate terms with a free rectangular correction cannot lower their COPY bill in the certified small-support domain. At least two replacement terms keep pairing rank at least eight. So the whole decoder keeps COPY cost **64**, and its separate COPY power bill cannot improve. This answers part of the two-coordinate handoff left by PR #1331.

**Domain:** arbitrary `GL(3,C)` and all 28 coordinate pairs, with one of:
- a **nonzero** free correction with at most **23 rows and 23 columns**;
- supports of at most **11 per side**, including zero factors.

Identity mixing attains the floor with a rank-nine masked completion.

**Status:** a scoped proof with exact finite premises, a negative result for this route. No physical supplier, improved κ or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

**Precise delta:** adds only `research/p112-two-coordinate-small-rectangle/`. It holds:
- a written quantified proof and a deterministic exact certificate;
- two differently implemented finite-premise checks, with failure controls;
- source, task and replay metadata, and a validation receipt.

Selected and frozen sources are unchanged.

**The certificate:**
- All 140 projective support strata are classified over C.
- The 71,540 nonzero functional evaluations give ordinary erasure distances 24/24/12/12/24 and free-compatible distances 24/24/34/34/40.
- All 700 ordered support pairings have rank at least eight (448 rank 8, 252 rank 9).
- A coefficient-rank identity forces at least two active products, which preserves the two-child power bill and not just the sum of ranks.

**Witnesses:** a 12-row span-loss witness has no common odd neighbor, and a compatible 24-row witness has neighbor {0}. These mark the edges of the span-preservation premises. They are not the sharp decoder threshold, and neither is a gain.

**Remaining obligations.**
- **Not covered:** larger nonzero supports, zero-factor cases above eleven, more mixed coordinates, other punctures, and shared-copy accounting.
- **Unchecked:** physical gathering, frame and owner legality, restoration, hosting, precision/tape, the all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source conditions, the analytic transfer and bit H1-H5.
- **Not claimed:** a selected cold replay, a proof-assistant check, independent human review, hosted CI or maintainer acceptance.

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `complex-masked-decoder` / `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`, refined to `p112-two-coordinate-small-rectangle/GL3C/all28-pairs/nonzero-support23-or-support11`. Chooser nonce `44ef721f92930cbeabe2df5c07bc184b`, track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2.
- **Base and exact heads:**
  - base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; contribution `4a533aff2a7a87c9b36e077a31774b332a7f64bd`;
  - Arham Tahir's PR #1331, head `f08b698cc2bd74e2425486728a008e531fc35f0e`, fetched and rechecked; it is context, not a code or theorem dependency;
  - the live PR #845/#717 geometry and the PR #968 model proof, pinned by Git blob and SHA256 in `SOURCES.json`;
  - selected PR #1094, head `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810`, accounting context only.
- **Question:** can a small free correction, mixed with two original coordinate terms, reduce the complete separate COPY bill?
- **Scope status:** refined. The claim began as the singleton follow-up to the discussion #1316 handoff. The same exact erasure calculation then extended it to the two support domains above. It changes the masked/overcomplete assumptions rather than repeating the eight-term all-pairs theorem.
- **Method and domain:** a complete five-stratum classification for every coordinate pair, an exact F2 census of minimum-support functionals and pairings, and a quantified coefficient-rank proof for every complex invertible factor change. No random search and no floating-point acceptance.
- **Optimistic budget:** six unchanged rank-eight COPY terms plus three replacements. At least two replacements individually have rank at least 8, giving at least `2*8^(1-a)` for `0<=a<1`, with the same width, normalization and multiplicity. All added gathering, frame and restoration costs are optimistically zero for this rejection screen.
- **Nearest work:**
  - PR #1331 treats one mixed coordinate with arbitrary rectangles.
  - Discussion #1360 independently considers every nine-term factorization of a singleton completion and explicitly leaves larger free rectangles out of scope. This package treats larger rectangles with two original coordinates mixed, so the two are complementary.
  - PR #1212/#1213 concern rank-eight masked rigidity, PR #1224 nine-term all-pairs normal forms, and this account's PR #1304 fixed A8 simplex normals.

  None supplies an assumed pending theorem.
- **Claim and final check:** the claim is in [discussion #1316](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1316#discussioncomment-18911259). A live overlap check just before submission (847 open PRs and every discussion record at 23:45 UTC, complete pagination) found no competing two-coordinate result.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-two-coordinate-small-rectangle
python3 -I -O -B research/p112-two-coordinate-small-rectangle/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/p112-two-coordinate-small-rectangle/independent_check.py
```

The registered replay checks the metadata, provenance and live pins, then runs both checkers in about four seconds. It ends with `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-two-coordinate-small-rectangle outcome=negative-result`.

- **Fixtures:** nine exact Gaussian-rational fixtures check 112,896 scalar entries in all. They include nonreal coefficients, ordinary transpose, cancellation, a 23-by-one rectangle and zero-factor cases.
- **Controls:** nine primary and nine separate-checker mutation controls pass.
- **Separate checker:** it builds Euclidean E8 roots and a binary dual evaluation code without importing the primary checker or the predecessor geometry. Both optimized-mode checks pass.
- **Orientation:** the card's first working example also passed (`PASS_COMPLEX_DECODER_FIELD_EXTENSION_S44`).

The registered replay and the metadata/pin check were run again on the final commit before submission, and both passed.

```text

PASS_P112_SMALL_RECTANGLE_INDEPENDENT strata=140 characters=71540 pairings=700 boundaries=12,24 controls=9
```

## Credit

- Arham Tahir (PR #1331) for the one-coordinate predecessor and the two-coordinate question.
- DreamingOfClouds (PR #717) for the masked B14 model, and PR #446/#595 for the separate-total lineage.
- Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (PR #620) for the coordinate COPY64 decoder.
- Mihir Srivastava (PR #845) for the exact P112 geometry.
- themilkman216 (PR #968) for the pairing-cost model.
- woklerx (PR #1077) for the task's complex-coefficient positive control.

Apache-2.0; source attribution is retained.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the mathematics, both implementations, the verification and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. Both implementations come from the same AI-assisted contributor, and no independent human review is claimed.

## Open next questions

From the package README:
- **Can a nonzero free rectangle with at least 24 indices on one side exploit a span-losing coordinate support to reduce the two-coordinate COPY moment?** This is the first size the proof leaves open. First step: take the recorded 24-row `free_boundary` witness and its common odd neighbor {0}, then solve the actual GL(3,C) cancellation constraints while pricing every term. Blocker: a free support rectangle with span loss does not by itself satisfy the coupled inverse-factor identities or establish any gain. The 12-row unrestricted witness has no common odd neighbor and should not be used for a nonzero correction.
- **Zero-factor cases above eleven per side** are a separate open branch of this proof. Larger rectangles, three or more mixed coordinates, other punctures and shared-copy objectives remain outside scope.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

- **Main detour:** the first twelve-erasure boundary had no common odd neighbor. Conditioning the erasure distance on an actual free rectangle produced the useful 23-per-side bound and a compatible 24-row witness.
- **Suggestion:** decoder-support task cards could suggest checking the common odd-neighbor set before proposing a span-loss witness as a free-correction candidate. That separates a linear-algebra boundary from a realizable masked support at once.

title: Audit: recursive parking boundaries and exact fixed-tape overhead (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The retained tape package proves individual push/pop round trips but leaves recursive handoffs open. This package supplies a scoped written proof and an explicit park/call/restore controller. Arbitrary dirty roles are restored around a length-preserving child, and the wrapper costs exactly `5V - n_active + 9W - 2` transitions. Equal positive roles give child volume `V/W` and a wrapper cost of at most `14V`, independent of the length of the parked ancestors.

A separate all-length counterexample shows why restoring every byte and head is not enough for a uniform time bound. The same finite child can scan an arbitrarily long parked ancestor and return unchanged, so the child contract needs the distinction. This is not a defect claim against the manuscript, which explicitly forbids ancestor scans.

**Status:** a scoped written proof with exact finite checks, plus the counterexample, for an interface (transfer) result. No eliminated recursive calls, exponent gain or new κ are claimed.

**Precise delta:** only `research/recursive-parking-boundary/` is added (eight files). It holds:
- the written quantified proof;
- a source-table extractor and a literal tape simulator;
- an explicit active-stream move and a finite phase controller;
- a deterministic replay receipt, six focused semantic test groups, and standard package metadata.

No existing source, selected record, frozen artifact or supplier profile changes. The first-done and trace-locality arguments are written proofs, and no new Lean theorem is claimed.

**Cost accounting:** the exact cost includes one stationary dispatch per phase, including the child's return. Child execution, row splitting, descriptors and marker lifecycle costs are separate. Empty streams have charge `9W-2`; they are not covered by the positive-volume `14V` inequality. Unequal role lengths keep the boundary semantics but do not imply `V/W` child volume.

**Remaining obligations.**
- The nested fixture uses abstract row split/merge shims and does not price or implement them.
- Still open:
  - physical complete-row routing, descriptors and recursive call-stack control;
  - the concrete selected-call binding and a uniform child-time proof;
  - new Lean composition and trace proofs;
  - a full native or selected cold replay, and the precision and analytic transfer.
- Source extraction is a restricted parser, not a Lean elaborator.
- The selected κ is unchanged, and no full multiplication theorem or runtime speedup is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `uniform-transfer-audit` / `ce7411fb7cf6f3460bfc`, refined to `fixed-tape-parking/dirty-role-boundary/all-length-locality`. Chooser nonce `e101f9f408701b26cf61d9bd1f07e040`, track adversarial-audit, priority revision 2. It passed over `supplier-boundary-audit` because this account's PR #1307 and the active selected-geometry claims cover nearby ground.
- **Base and exact dependencies:**
  - base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; contribution `3a45bd089ad56c38b55da8d80d7b056f2d90e5fa`;

  There is no pending PR dependency.
- **Concrete object and question:** the fixed-W inactive parks, the active move, the child boundary, the active return and the reverse-order pops. The aim is to separate semantic restoration, intermediate locality and uniform cost.
- **Exact implication audited:** do literal primitives plus child endpoint restoration suffice for the normalized recurrence's equal-volume and linear-overhead premises? The counterexample disproves the weaker endpoint-only time implication.
- **Scope status:** refined. It takes the card's tape/restoration branch and the composition boundary the retained README explicitly names as missing. The finite tests support the written all-length proof; they do not replace its quantifiers.
- **Method and domain:** four-symbol, head-local, unit-move multitape semantics, with a written theorem for every fixed W >= 2, arbitrary lengths and finite ancestor contents. Source extraction covers all 12 push and 384 pop state-symbol entries. The exact finite domains and mutation controls are in `RESULT.json`.
- **Expected cost:** `(W-1)(5n+7) + 4n+4 + (2W+1)` for equal lengths. Exact restoration, the original stream order and ancestor independence are all required.
- **Nearest work:**

title: Scoped negative result: orthogonal P120 shared-total pairs fail diagonals
body:
## Result

**Scoped negative result; no exact decoder or new κ.** This changes the relative root geometry from PR #1366's fixed odd-pair pencil `e=L51,d0=L1` (`<e,d0>=2`) to the seed-selected orthogonal pencil `e=L48,d0=L91` (`<e,d0>=0`). The ordered orthogonal partner is selected reproducibly as index `48 mod 63` in the sorted list of orthogonal roots.

The exact finite census tests all 120 targets and 511 nonzero sink words, retains 65 calibrated rows with nonzero target diagonals, and examines all 2,048 distinct-target pairs. The union correction total is available at both sinks for 1,056 pairs; every one cancels at least one target diagonal (1,024 cancel both; 32 cancel one). There are no exact pairs in this family.

The obstruction is exact: if target `t_a` belongs to the other row's required-total set, then `p_e(t_a)=0`, `p_d(t_a)≠0`, and the total subtracts `p_d(t_a)`, making the required diagonal zero.

## Why this family was tested

A successful unit with the same C.6 accounting would cost one rank-one shared total plus eight rank-eight coordinate totals, or 65 local COPY-rank units, against the P120 all-pairs floor of 72. The result rules out that potential saving only for this pencil and total rule. It does not cover other orthogonal pencils, uncalibrated rows, different total directions, multiple totals, or a complete recursive supplier.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/seed48-p120-orthogonal-shared-total/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/seed48-p120-orthogonal-shared-total --check-only
```

The exact verifier replays PR #1366's odd-pair obstruction, the full P112 C.6 112-by-112 positive control, a required-total-source deletion control, and a label mutation control. Source/base pins are in `SOURCES.json`; proof and limitations are in `PROOF.md`.

title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on P111 and type-(4,4) P104 units (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p111-p104-44/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

PR #1212 (burntout76) proves rank-8 gauge rigidity, K = D(2G)D⁻¹, of the masked (E-graph) system on P112, P120 and the type-(2,2,2,2) P104 units. Its PROOF.md §10 leaves two gaps, and this PR closes both:

- **P111 (all 112 units):** Lemma 5′ covers a class with three live rows. Case (ii) has rank 1 < 3, as #1212 noted. The new part is the `b` side: the three pairwise sign products span the non-trivial characters, so γγ′ is constant.
- **Type-(4,4) P104 (28 units):** Lemma 6′ is a gluing lemma. It needs only connectivity of the usable classes through each pivot pair, plus an explicit three-triple path. The argument is multiplicative, so it holds over any field of characteristic 0. It works with 12/14 usable blocks.

**Consequence.** In the E-graph model, decoders with exactly eight costly terms have cst ≥ 63 on every P111 unit (attained by PR717's P111 decoders) and cst ≥ 56 on every type-(4,4) unit. Sharpness of 56 on the type-(4,4) units is not checked.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p111-p104-44/verify.py` runs 26 exact checks and 4 controls in about 1 s. It is an independent implementation with its own E8 model, classes, witnesses, gluing and assembly, and imports nothing from #1212. The controls show:
  - two-row classes are not forced;
  - P111 needs Lemma 5′;
  - the path condition rejects a rank-17 block set;
  - a perturbed entry breaks (2).
- `--pr1212-dir <checkout of 57099cb5>` checks the git blobs of #1212's `verify.py` and its two `.drup` files. It then replays their `G.P111.zero-exclusion`, `G.P104-44.zero-exclusion`, `G.line-orbits` and `G.frame-orbits`, and matches the pivots by root vectors. All pass locally on Python 3.14.
- `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

## Not checked or not covered

- **The 896 admissible P104 units**, which have two-row classes. This is the open next question. PR #1292 gives only local rigidity there.
- **Nine or more costly terms.**
- **Zero exclusion** is #1212's DRUP result, replayed but not re-derived. PR968's F6 premise is inherited.
- There has been no independent human review of the written proof.
- All inherited conditions of the selected record remain.

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`), refined to the #1212 §10 obligations on P111 and type (4,4). Chooser nonce `118c1c4d3856655a6b7cb222d8d50aef`, track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2.

A five-child interface carries a paired order-four frame across the child calls and pays it back at the end. The optimized root echo raises the exact prefix row-L1 peak from 11 to 20.

The quarter-turn is explicitly emitted using 9 ADD and 1 NEG per four-cycle, with the inverse at the same cost. The recurrence is exact in the declared macro alphabet of whole-register powers `P^u` and `Q^v`; it is not an unrestricted primitive-word lower bound. title: Research/pr1048 certified two transports
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR1048 compares profiles at a fixed exponent without establishing the ordering of their actual roots. This package reproduces the maintainers' counterexample, supplies a certified surcharge-inclusive reference-root comparator, and independently excludes improvement by at most two transports in the explicitly frozen PR589 domain.

The complete census contains **1,452,893 legal single transports** and **59,998 distinct overlapping ordered operation pairs**, giving **1,379,084 final pair representatives**. Singles have 1,227,676 exact ties and 225,217 strictly worse outcomes; pair representatives have 1,282,055 exact ties and 97,029 strictly worse outcomes. Both implementations report **zero better and zero unresolved cases**. Repeated-operation and register-disjoint pairs are covered by the accompanying reduction proof; operation-pair counts are not literal path counts.

The comparator encloses signed `J_delta` over the entire verified reference-root bracket using outward rational transcendental bounds. It fails closed on uncertain signs. This is a finite audit, with no new construction or κ improvement. Three or more moves, growing catalogues, arbitrary subspaces, other circuit identities, illegal intermediates, and full multiplication-theorem/native/precision obligations remain outside scope.

Start with [the result and exact domain](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/README.md) and [the proof](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/PROOF.md).

## Task and overlap

Explicit Brian Ross assignment: repair PR1048 pricing and independently check post-first-move coverage. Scope was refined from a bounded diagnostic slice to complete exclusion in the declared frozen domain: 3,064 elementary A/B operations; frames from the original 636-frame catalogue plus each current slot's own rational lower-span closure; legal intermediates and resulting retained COPY constraints.

Base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. Retained dependencies: #1048 at `07730cd8302c378607259a9ad0efb73e0b57a2f2` and #1182 at `0213b8911bfeefd5c81ddf320bac6a0fb7e86215`, with unchanged sources and notices. Four additive research directories; no existing upstream source or selected construction changes. Earlier package narratives and receipts are preserved as historical evidence.

Ian Libânio's #933 at `b9348c6907516e55dc07e135ad4d7a480d4f9840` already reports broader relocation/all-frame negative results and a 2,000-pair independent sample. This contribution claims no first-negative priority or equivalence with that larger domain. Its added value is corrected reference-root pricing, the explicit pair-projection completeness argument, and a full separate replay of this narrower domain. See [publication checks and overlap](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/PUBLICATION.md).

## Validation

CPython 3.13.2 on macOS. Reproduction commands and pinned receipts are in the README and [independent review](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/REVIEW.md).

- All 36 mandatory input pins pass. Separate implementations agree on every single-operation domain, the full pair transcript, all 93 pair delta/count/status records, and enclosing price intervals.
- Complete primary/independent pair scans took 372.174/125.896 seconds. A fresh isolated independent full replay on the submission base took 119.384 seconds and matched the saved complete result.
- Transcript SHA256: `b39d6d23210ab7eee24c04e165b078e39ea00053e4be4b523f7c793e24b79679`.
- Existing root-ordering and bracket defects reproduce. Semantic corruption controls fail closed. A synthetic strict-improvement control demonstrates why equal first-state profiles cannot justify discarding continuation neighborhoods; it is not an improving PR589 witness.
- `python3 -I -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py` and diff whitespace checks pass.

No full selected cold replay, native admission, repository-wide historical suites, hosted CI, proof assistant, or independent human proof review is claimed.

## Credit

Prepared by Brian Ross with OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate GPT-6 Astra review and rerun. Credit flemhhh's original search; Douglas Colkitt/the maintainers' existing counterexample; woklerx's reused #1182 bracket repair; Ian Libânio's #933; and DreamingOfClouds, eumemic, and retained supplier lineage.

Brian Ross's [Krenn independent verifier](https://github.com/brianross93/Krenn/blob/ab446724a61a293a3268c63b9e9e721c6a360561/experiments/krenn_quantum_graph/independent_verifier.py) and [semantic-corruption tests](https://github.com/brianross93/Krenn/blob/ab446724a61a293a3268c63b9e9e721c6a360561/tests/test_krenn_artifacts.py), plus [ThetaTwist exact-arithmetic discipline](https://github.com/brianross93/thetatwist/blob/b4ec6c13088b89961834cc675b44b81372199b02/src/thetatwist/core.py), inform the methodology. This is methodological adaptation, with no copied code from those projects or PR933. Existing licenses are retained; new material is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The [smallest useful follow-up](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/README.md#open-next-questions) is a correspondence audit of PR933's first-slot equivalence and post-first neighborhoods against the pair-specific projection here. Different move primitives and global frame reoptimization prevent assuming equivalence. No defect in PR933 is asserted; no larger search is justified without a new completeness argument.
