title: Scoped obstruction: helper468 must end at rank eight after B88's target MOVE
body:
## Result and scope

**Scoped negative result / exact boundary certificate. No new circuit, supplier or kappa.**

For helper **468** in the fixed PR589 R439 bit word, the first rank-eight two-sided boundary footprint occurs at **cut 177**, when zero-based **B gate 88 moves target 208 from frame 0 to frame 152**, before its ADD. Applying Ali Romman's PR1128 boundary lemma, **any permitted reversible linear suffix starting there or later must end helper 468 at rank eight**. The class allows arbitrary rational frames, arbitrary suffix length, target access and extra restored dirty auxiliaries, with common-frame scalar operations and monotone frame changes; it excludes new COPY/descent/reset or altered prefixes.

All **4,697 later cuts** have that general rank-eight obstruction. The earlier 177 cuts pass the two-sided rank-seven test and are not existence certificates. At those earlier cuts, an arbitrary **one-common-frame restore-and-isolate block** of rank at most seven is separately excluded because it would promote target 208 into an incompatible frame.

The complete ledger covers **4,874 boundaries**, including the initial post-scatter cut and every **1,310 MOVE / 3,563 individual ADD** boundary through original B/C and final MOVEs. Two different engines agree on every event, cut, restoration/dirty mask, geometry case and all 661 final forward/inverse columns.

| Exclusion | Cuts |
|---|---:|
| Rank-seven footprint forces target 208 into an incompatible frame |177|
| Footprint already spans rank eight |1557|
| Helper468 already has rank eight |3140|

Nine explicit frame-join certificates use nonzero integer minors and exact annihilating/separating normals. At the critical MOVE the scalar restoration row and dirty column remain unchanged, while the join's rank grows 7→8; its eight-line determinant is -32.

## Task, predecessor credit and delta

Fresh OS seed **17**, bit supplier track. Exact base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. [Claim/discussion1362](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1362).

[PR1256](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1256), pinned at `d6d5a994fcdcd8d04ec439ff988daa8f37b17ece`, supplies the initial-cut fixture and explicitly leaves later target-read cuts open. [PR1128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1128), pinned at `df29b159239b79d7e451d6ddda826a73e0e50a67`, owns the general two-sided restoration/erasure lemma and its two earlier boundary analyses. **The new result is its complete later-cut application and the exact B88 transition, not a new general lemma.** Its earlier exploratory single-register readout scan did not supply this whole-cut restore/isolate theorem or earlier general-suffix cutoff.

This changes the card from the already covered H2/K repair (PR1194/1311) to a residual/H4 boundary audit. It retains the assigned bit track. PR1253's fixed first-contact kernel entrances are a different question. Refreshed overlap covered 861 open PR bodies and 108 discussion/comment records, plus 60 recent all-state PRs; dependency heads were rechecked before submission. Coverage limits are recorded.

Only `research/r439-helper 468-late-cut/` is added. The first 177 cuts remain open for staged mechanisms; new transport or a changed earlier prefix is outside the theorem. Any staged attempt keeping the original prefix must start before the target 208 MOVE. No selected frontier or frozen source is changed.

## Accounting and validation

The README/proof gives a favorable ideal two-slot width-seven invoice: retain all nine COPY/ERASE pairs, return all eight freed old host coordinates, consume an idle rank-seven slot, and account for the changed helper path. Both ideal deltas preserve rank mass and lower child count/moment. Preparation, source/storage, restoration and frame overhead are optimistically free in that screen. It is not an implemented invoice or physical host assignment; the boundary failures remain even under free added work.

PASS_R439_HELPER468_LATE_CUT cuts=4874 excluded=4874 joins=9 arbitrary_suffix_from=177 new_kappa=false

Four source archives match exact Git blobs. The card's original R439 working example also passes.

title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on the 896 admissible P104 units (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p104-admissible/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

PR #1212 (burntout76) proves rank-8 gauge rigidity, K = D(2G)D⁻¹, of the masked (E-graph) system on P112, P120 and the 336 type-(2,2,2,2) P104 units. Its PROOF.md §10 leaves the **896 admissible P104 units** open (PR717's P104 among them). On #1212's pivot there, four classes keep only two live rows. For those classes Lemma 5 leaves a one-parameter family. This PR closes that orbit.

- **What already holds.** On #1212's admissible pivot, all 14 blocks carry a complete class, so Lemmas 5–6 fix the global scaling `g` on the 22 complete classes unchanged. #1212 §10 records that (I2), (I3) and (I4) hold; only (I1) fails.
- **New: Lemma 9 (propagation).** A two-row line `i` needs no in-class argument. Take a witness `j` in a complete class with `T_i ∩ T_j = {k, k′}`. Then (E2) gives `a_ik ε_ik / g_k = a_ik′ ε_ik′ / g_k′`, and the reverse order gives the same for `b`. If the witnessed pairs connect `T_i`, then `a_i ∝ ε_i ∘ g` and `b_i ∝ ε_i / g`, and (E0) fixes the product. On this unit, every two-row line has all six pairs witnessed, with 40 witnesses each. The lemma is linear, needs no zero exclusion for `i`, and uses no equation inside its class.

**Consequence.** In the E-graph model, every decoder with exactly eight costly terms has cst ≥ 56 on every admissible P104 unit, and PR717's P104 decoders attain it. With #1212 (type (2,2,2,2)) and #1389 (type (4,4), unmerged), rigidity then covers all 1260 P104 frame complements.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p104-admissible/verify.py` runs 11 exact checks and 4 controls in about 0.1 s. It is an independent implementation (own E8 model, classes, witnesses, gluing, propagation) and imports nothing from #1212. It recomputes the orbit type of the punctured frame. It cross-checks Lemma 9's algebra on the actual (E2) equations: rank 3, with the gauge vector as kernel. The controls show:
  - in-class conditions admit a non-gauge two-row solution;
  - witnessed cross-block equations reject it (28/40);
  - removing the witnesses at one column leaves a 2-dimensional family;
  - a perturbed entry breaks (2).
- `--pr1212-dir <checkout of 57099cb5>` checks the git blobs of #1212's `verify.py` and `proof-P104-11111111.drup`. It replays `G.P104-11111111.zero-exclusion`, `G.P104-11111111.class-witnesses`, `G.frame-orbits` and `G.pr717-p104-orbit`, and matches the unit and pivot by root vectors. That is 22 checks, all passing locally.
- Passes on Python 3.10.21, 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

## Not checked or not covered

- **Nine or more costly terms** (PR717's mixed-β problem).
- **The intermediate punctures P105–P110.** This is the package's open next question. Lemma 9 makes incomplete classes free once `g` is fixed, but each orbit needs its own zero-exclusion certificate.
- **Zero exclusion** is #1212's DRUP result, replayed but not re-derived. PR968's F6 premise is inherited.
- There has been no independent human review of the written proof.
- All inherited conditions of the selected record remain.

This is an exact census of the Cartesian product of three fixed, individually legal single-move option lists for the seed-selected simultaneous A-operation triple `(927, 928, 930)` in the selected PR589 `v=111`, `R=439` word. title: Scoped proof: two coordinate swaps need six paid coordinate-CNOT calls (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Two coordinate-SWAP targets cannot share paid coordinate-CNOT work in the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` model. The exact minimum is six calls, for any finite number of restored dirty registers, even with free scalar register mixing. This settles the smallest two-dimensional gap instance of Gareth Davidson's PR #1333 restricted-alphabet question.

**Status:** a scoped written proof, corroborated by two independent exact implementations. It is a negative result: no saving exists in this model. No new supplier or κ is claimed.

**The proof:** only `research/coordinate-cnot-register-bound/` is added. The proof normalizes free scalar maps by augmentation, uses the sign quotient and trace to force an even call count, and excludes every four-call label pattern with exact coefficient-rank identities. A six-call formal word attains the bound with no extra roles or omitted restoration.

**Independent corroboration:**
- A formal-coefficient implementation and a faithful left-regular implementation agree on every state through radius three: 559 states for two registers and 47,203 for three. Both radius-two/radius-three target intersections are empty.
- The replay also verifies:
  - 31 symbolic noncommuting label patterns, 36 sign products and 4,704 scalar conjugations;
  - identity and one-swap positive controls, the six-call witnesses, and 14 semantic scope and failure controls.

**Remaining obligations.**
- The all-register statement is a written proof, not checked in Lean or by an independent human. The finite replay covers exactly `r=2,3`; the proof supplies the unrestricted-register conclusion.
- Still open: three or more swap targets and higher-dimensional coordinate-CNOT targets.
- Not covered: clean-only endpoints, other free operations or a different paid alphabet.
- Not run: any physical, compiler, common-label, hosting, precision/tape, analytic-transfer or selected-supplier cold replay.
- No selected frontier, multiplication exponent or runtime change is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `bit-new-register-model` / `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f`, refined to `coordinate-CNOT / GL2F2 / two-SWAP / arbitrary-restored-dirty-registers`. Chooser nonce `30b6519a75b5dea27cbfaca91b7e00af`, track bit-mechanisms, priority revision 2. The selected method is a target-specific relaxation bound for an explicit alphabet. The other suggestion, `bit-helper-contract`, was passed over because PR #1194 and this account's PR #1306 already address its immediate direction.
- **Base and exact heads:** base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; contribution `9e1640094f649ba6db9742796825a8d6c238989b`. PR #1333 (`7f25b6d0e1d7e995d4d2840f231d98b1a1a9fec2`) is the research lead and the predecessor for the augmentation argument. PR #720 (`a942c0ae1b463710ca535c1fba1b07b6431b5a86`) is nearby rational-model context. No pending implementations are imported; exact contextual blobs and SHA256 values are in `SOURCES.json`.
- **Concrete object and question:** `diag([s],[s],1,...,1)` over the formal group algebra of `GL_2(F2)`, where `s = aba = bab` is the address-coordinate swap. Can it beat the direct paid bill of 3+3?
- **Scope status:** refined. The card permits a specified nonabelian family. PR #1333 prices every affine rank-one address label as one unit, so the swap itself costs one there; this work restricts labels to the two coordinate CNOTs. The initial `r=2,3` question was strengthened to every finite `r>=2` on the same target and alphabet, and the finite counts remain corroborating evidence.
- **Alphabet:** paid `I+([g]+1)N`, with `g` one of the two coordinate CNOTs, `N=uv^T` and `v^T u=1`. Scalar `GL_r(F2)` changes are free, and arbitrary dirty extras are restored. No free address maps, translations, COPY, erasure or clean allocation.
- **Optimistic budget:** six paid calls is the complete direct baseline, including every undo, so a saving would mean at most five calls with full dirty restoration. The theorem excludes that for any number of dirty extras. Free scalar work and role availability make this an optimistic relaxation; physical implementation is not claimed.
- **Nearest work:**
  - PR #1333 and discussion #1317 explicitly leave the restricted alphabet open.
  - PR #468/#720 concern rational abelian labels, and PR #680/#705/#800/#836 use other Clifford and complex models.
  - This account's PR #1306 is a dirty XOR shear census and is not repeated.
- **Claim and final check:** the claim is in [discussion #1317](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18911765). A live overlap check just before submission (817 open PRs and 141 discussion records at 00:28 UTC, complete pagination) found no competing work. `OVERLAP.json` records the lane's own snapshot coverage and its limits.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/coordinate-cnot-register-bound/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/coordinate-cnot-register-bound --check-only
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/coordinate-cnot-register-bound
```

The registered replay and all six focused tests pass in about ten seconds. The tests include typed receipt corruption, source corruption, duplicate JSON fields and a read-only relocated optimized replay. They were run again on the final commit before submission. `VALIDATION.md` lists the checks and the remaining obligations separately.

```text
PASS_COORDINATE_CNOT_REGISTER_BOUND minimum=6 dirty_registers=arbitrary census_r=2,3 symbolic_patterns=31 controls=14 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/coordinate-cnot-register-bound outcome=completed
```

## Credit

- Gareth Davidson (@bitplane) for PR #1333, its open question and the augmentation normalization; none of its implementation is imported.
- eumemic, Ali Romman and David Govea for the register-model lineage.

New work is Apache-2.0; predecessor sources and notices are unchanged.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the proof, both implementations, the verification and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. No independent human review is claimed.

## Open next questions

From the package README:
1. **Three or more swaps in the same alphabet.** A general direct-sum bound would say how far this obstruction scales. First step: three swaps. The sign trace permits only odd lengths, so seek a seven-call identity or a coefficient obstruction against the direct nine. Blocker: longer alternating words and arbitrary dirty-register counts need a new argument, which the present four-call proof does not supply.
2. **A three-dimensional coordinate-CNOT target with a rank/length gap.** This tests the higher-dimensional branch of PR #1333's question. First step: pin a target in `GL_3(F2)` and certify its direct coordinate-CNOT length, then test a two-role formal word below twice that length. Full formal equality and the complete paid and restoration bill are required. Blocker: the six-element group argument here does not apply to the larger address group.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

- **Most useful lead:** PR #1333's explicit open next question. The catalogue's broad entry point had already been answered by that pending contribution, so the overlap check before starting was essential.
- **Suggestion:** link a verified restricted-alphabet follow-up next to this card's broad affine-model overlap, so that later sessions pick a higher-dimensional target or the three-swap question.

title: Conditional lemma: linear transport of single-register leaf errors
body:
PR1374 leaves open the growth of errors supported on an actual completed leaf destination. This contribution proves that the worst amplification has order **Theta(h)** in the balanced PR628 word of height h, even though arbitrary joint-register errors can have quadratic amplification.

For every factor count, either call direction, every ordered pair of complete-leaf cuts, and any single input register:

- Contractive factors give an upper bound **h+2**, without commutation.
- Commuting factors with every subset product bounded by G give **(h+2)G**.
- For every h>=2, PR1374's existing scalar-isometry family attains **h-1 on the actual preceding leaf destination**. The new address argument identifies that destination as z_(h-1).

The upper argument uses PR1085's one-monomial-per-prefix-entry invariant; the commuting subset case additionally uses PR1278's squarefree intervals. At most h+2 terms contribute to one matrix entry, and a single-register input uses a column rather than the full row sum. The lower family and coefficient formula remain credited to Arham Tahir's PR1374. The exact optimal constant remains open.

**Status: conditional lemma and independent verification; no new kappa or implemented precision reduction.** A conditional variation-of-constants corollary is included. Actual destination support, negative-leaf preimages, coefficient preparation, internal growth, and the complete cost bill must be checked before changing numerical precision. No supplier or selected record changes.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/single-register-interval-transport/check.py
python3 -I -B research/single-register-interval-transport/test_check.py
```

Expected: JSON status `PASS_SINGLE_REGISTER_TRANSPORT`, then six passing tests. Standard library only; checks ran through the project's current stable CPython 3.15.0 wrapper. The exact runtime and executable are recorded.

- 816,036 chronological destination intervals at n=1..16, both signs and three concrete factor patterns. This does not exhaust all sign patterns.
- 276 ordered-cut comparisons through n=83 between literal source-dispatcher impulses and a separately implemented recursive prefix model with exact Gauss-Jordan inversion. The latter skips completed subtrees using their endpoint shear; it does not import the source traversal or predecessor checker.
- Lower-family address and coefficient checks through h=8; handwritten four-factor control, wrong-destination distinction, omitted-restoration failure, inadequate-singleton-budget example, actual source-corruption rejection, and optimized read-only-file relocation.
- Six tests pass normally and optimized; selected-record binding and its 25 existing tests pass. The clean patch applies to refreshed main.

The written proof, not the finite checks, establishes the all-size conditional claims. No proof assistant, external human review, hosted CI, selected cold replay, or numerical leaf execution is claimed.

### Sources and overlap

Base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; refreshed main `cd91ac8e2652bfee6bf09da3b8724253bcf78f5f` leaves the selected record and relevant guidance unchanged. Only `research/single-register-interval-transport/` is added. Consumed sources retain SHA256 and Git-blob pins.

title: Scoped obstruction: sharp P112 endpoint dimension and complete linear-lift cost
body:
The proposed second unpaid endpoint direction must change more than the rank budget. This package proves that every nondegenerate two-plane representation of the selected P112 graph needs dimension at least 18, with equality attained by the tensor representation. It also proves an all-size cost obstruction for arbitrary coupled linear endpoint lifts of the retained supplier and controller.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c755bf393bea26d2275e1516b0560ca92de7a52e/research/p112-linear-endpoint-lifts/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c755bf393bea26d2275e1516b0560ca92de7a52e/research/p112-linear-endpoint-lifts/CERTIFICATE.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c755bf393bea26d2275e1516b0560ca92de7a52e/research/p112-linear-endpoint-lifts/SOURCES.json).

The cost theorem permits arbitrary native factorizations of each retained role-stream edge, rank-zero adapters, and arbitrarily many extra coordinates with slanted or nonmonotone frames. It derives the tensor form from 80 independent graph-edge constraints and then uses exact Fourier rank and live-stream accounting. If M(p) is the full reference moment, every such padded lift satisfies M_lift(p) >= lambda M(p) + 1-lambda. Thus the optimal complex moment exponent cannot increase. An exact rational cap also excludes the next selected kappa grid point, 0.001672660197076919. No new kappa is claimed.

The sharp dimension theorem covers nonlinear plane assignments. The cost theorem does not cover new scalar words, new controllers, or joint children across separate arrays or frozen edges. Nonlinear dimension 18 assignments with a different complete word remain open. [PR #791](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/791)'s warning that arbitrary rank-two projector penalties need not double is respected: rank scaling is used only after linear-lift rigidity and exact frame-distance checks.

The source-bound verifier checks the selected canonical/program/archive bytes, all 3,494 local native edges in each orientation, all 7,526 idle children, the 144-call owner chronology, the full 510,662-child histogram, rational moment bounds, five rejected mutations and small exact lemma controls. body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-extension/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

Rank-8 gauge rigidity of the masked (E-graph) system, K = D(2G)D⁻¹, is known on every P104 frame complement: #1212 (type (2,2,2,2)), #1389 (type (4,4)) and #1399 (admissible). #1399's open next question is the intermediate punctures P105–P110. This PR settles the ones a linear argument reaches and counts exactly what is left.

- **Lemma 10 (extension).** Suppose L ⊂ L′, L is rigid, L spans R⁸, and for each new line `i` the lines of L orthogonal to `i` span `r_i^⊥`. Then L′ is rigid. K′[L,L] already has rank 8, so each new row is `2uᵀRᵀD⁻¹` on L. The orthogonal zeros force `u ∝ r_i`, and the diagonal fixes the scale. There is no DRUP, no zero exclusion and no class argument.
- **Theorem.** E8 \ S is rigid whenever S lies in the union of two disjoint frames.
- **Census for P112 minus X:**
  - It is covered exactly when X lies in a frame inside P112.
  - Every line, and every orthogonal pair, lies in a type-(2,2,2,2) frame. So **P111 and all 3304 orthogonal-pair P110 units are rigid from #1212 alone**. For P111 this is a second proof of #1389's result, by a different route.
  - For |X| = 3, …, 7 the covered counts are 29232, 77868, 70560, 35280 and 10080. PROOF.md splits them by which predecessor they need.

**Consequence.** On each covered unit, every decoder with exactly eight costly terms has cst ≥ 72 − p in the E-graph model, with p = 8 + |X|. This is #968's Theorem 4(b) via #1212 §8.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-extension/verify.py` runs 9 exact checks plus 5 algebraic checks and controls in about 1 s, standard library only. It has its own E8 model and recomputes:
  - the 2025 frames and W(E8) transitivity on them;
  - the three FRAME0-stabiliser orbits of the 1260 P112 frames (28/336/896), matched to their types;
  - the span condition on all 1260 × 16 new lines, with at least 52 orthogonal live lines each;
  - the bi-frame cover census, the P111 cover, the P105–P110 table, and the odd-pair P110 orbits (224 and 2688).
- Its controls show that both hypotheses of Lemma 10 matter:
  - a rank-9 solution escapes;
  - dropping enough lines to break the span condition admits a rank-8 non-gauge extension;
  - a perturbed orthogonal entry is rejected.
- Passes on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14. `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

## Not checked or not covered

- **Punctures containing an odd pair.** No frame contains an odd pair. This is most of P105–P110. At P110 it is 2912 pairs in two stabiliser orbits, and that is the package's open next question. Each orbit needs its own zero-exclusion certificate.
- Orthogonal X that do not extend to a frame inside P112, for example 1792 of the 31024 orthogonal triples.
- **P104 rigidity is cited, not recomputed.** #1212, #1389 and #1399 are all open. P111 and the covered P110 units need only #1212.
- Nine or more costly terms. #968's premise (F6) is inherited. Attainment of 72 − p on these units is not checked. There has been no independent human review.

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`), refined to #1399's open next question. Chooser nonce `35f10aeb31e6ffea65d714368cb51223`, track complex-mechanisms (the donor asked to continue this line), priority revision 2.
- **Heads:** base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. Cites #1212 `57099cb5`, #1389 `5480912a` and #1399 `4e1ba3a1`. No code is imported from any of them.
- **Claim:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1411
- **Overlap:** no other claim or PR on P105–P110 or on an extension argument. The overlap search was refreshed at 00:33Z (783 open PRs and 143 discussions, complete pagination).

## Credit

- **burntout76 / Brett Halligan (#1212):** the rigidity theorem, (E), the type-(2,2,2,2) units, the transport and §8.
- **themilkman216 (#968):** the floor 72 − p.
- **DreamingOfClouds (#717):** the E-graph model.

Substantial AI assistance: Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code (lemma, verifier, write-up). Submitted by the account holder. Apache-2.0.

**Feedback.** #1399's handoff proposed a per-orbit DRUP route for P105–P110. A five-minute census showed that a linear lemma covers the partial-frame punctures with no certificate at all, and that the real gap is the odd pairs. A quick "what does the cheapest argument already reach" census before planning per-unit certificates saved most of the session.

title: Research: P112 frame subsets miss 35,232 orthogonal rank demands
body:
Two nine-term P112 support layouts with binary pairing-rank bill 63 pass all 227,696 orthogonal-set demands obtained from full eight-root live frames, yet cannot be decoders. Conditional κ = **0.001676855229071321886206381217337893**, an absolute increase of **6.2381217337893E-23** over PR1377 (0.001676855229071321886144). **Certificate refinement only: the construction, scalar words, provider inventory, owners and paid profile are unchanged.** This is a tiny numerical improvement, not a new kernel or practical speedup.

The recurrence is a_(j+1) = (1-s)s + s a_j. Its closed form is a_j = s - (s-a_0)s^j; 0 < a_0 < s < 1 gives a finite increasing chain below s. title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on P112 minus an odd pair — completes P110 with #1419 (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p110-odd/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

#1419 shows that rank-8 rigidity of #1212's system (E) passes to supersets. That makes P112 minus any **orthogonal** pair rigid. It cannot reach an **odd pair**, because no frame contains one. The 2912 odd pairs of P112 form two FRAME0-stabiliser orbits, of sizes 224 and 2688. This PR proves rigidity on both, by #1212's method plus #1399's Lemma 9. For each orbit representative it ships a pivot and a new zero-exclusion certificate.

title: Research audit: averaged-height bounds for certified composite radices (no new kappa)
body:
PR1025's prime-power Fourier average uses `q/phi(q) <= 2`. That intermediate step fails outside its stated domain, for example `134/phi(134) = 67/33`. This package replaces two by `r/phi(r)` and carries the factor through the resultant estimate, where it cancels the field degree. This is an extension of the predecessor's domain, not a reported defect in its prime-power theorem.

**Status: mathematical audit / conditional precision bound; no new kappa.**

For `n=r-1`, `D=phi(r)` and `ell=ceil(log2 r)`, the written proof gives

```text
T = min(n D r, 3 n r (ell+1)^2 / 2 + 2 n D ell),
d_r = 1 + 2 ell + T,
|P_k(z)| >= 2^(-d_r) on |z|=1,
||P_k(tau Z_L^w)^(-1)||_infinity <= 2^(2 d_r + r + 2).
```

The resultant must be nonzero. PR666's seed-2 lifting argument supplies that condition for every `r=2*p^a`, prime `p>=5`, `a>=1`; its specialization is written out and credited here. Both exponents remain `O(r^2 log^2 r)`. At radix 8,978 the sufficient gap exponent drops from the common coarse dyadic envelope 356,393,327,561 to 28,312,479,536. These are analytic bound values, not executed working precision or runtime savings.

title: Prove complete moment optimality of fixed eight-helper complex blocks
body:
The twelve late eight-helper blocks in the selected complex word cannot reduce the recursive moment through any finite rational refactorization with their retained input/output frames. The proof permits arbitrary order and length, repeated input reads, changed helper coordinates, and fusion with later work within each block. The current native words attain the complete lower bound, including helper completion to rank nine.

title: Audit: quadratic rounding accumulation and linear-error Neumann evaluation (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Adversarial audit / conditional precision refinement; no new κ.** The retained Gaussian inverse evaluation sums separately rounded powers. Its stated absolute-error interface permits quadratic accumulation even when the exact operator is positive and the approximation is odd and zero-preserving. An all-length exact family establishes that boundary; it does not contradict the existing `3p²/4` allowance or claim a defect in actual Gaussian rounding.

A fixed-source Horner replacement keeps every intermediate in the disk grid and has error `<p·2^-p`, using exactly the same `k−1` complete E calls. The written proof assumes `p>100`, `||E||≤0.42`, oracle error `<(p/3)2^-p`, and `||E^k||≤2^-p`. It includes initialization, exact subtraction, residual error, all stream scans and the complete wrapper cost. A separate counterexample shows why merely `||E||<1/2` does not suffice for the disk invariant.

At p=128 and k=64, the same valid contract fixture gives power-sum error `10528/3` grid units and Horner error `166/3`, with 63 calls each. The old error remains within the old allowance.

Only `research/neumann-rounding-audit/` is added (eight files). The alternative is implemented at its abstract oracle boundary. Actual Gaussian execution, analytic estimates, PR371's separate block-rounding repair, and physical integration remain open or inherited. No selected supplier, source, precision charge or exponent changes. No benchmark or new mathematical-method priority is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Research base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; seed **68**, adversarial-audit track; card `uniform-transfer-audit`, scope **refined** to this rounded precision implication.

- Exact Git-blob/SHA256 source pins, three candidate tasks, bounded domains, stop rule and next questions are in SOURCES/TASK/VALIDATION. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1409.
- Fresh complete overlap snapshot: 791 open PRs and 148 discussion records. PR684 audits domain/windows, PR902 improves exact-power decay, and PR1243 audits inner packing. This adds rounded-error placement and a source-compatible abstract evaluator. None of those pending implementations is imported. Search coverage is not a novelty proof.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/neumann-rounding-audit
```

Expected: `PASS_NEUMANN_ROUNDING_AUDIT fixtures=648 family=326 controls=6`, ten passing tests, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`.

On macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.13:

- 648 fixed matrix/oracle cases, all 35,640 states compared between integer and separate Fraction/block-matrix implementations; dense exact elimination supplies the final inverse oracle.
- 326 complete adverse-family cases through p=1024; six semantic controls cover wrong sign, missing half, omitted tail premise, overwritten source, weakened contraction margin and an unsupported linear bound for the old evaluator.

title: Scoped negative result: one frame relation cannot save paid rank at any register count
body:
**Scoped negative result; no new kappa.**

This extends Ali Romman’s PR #468 at-most-one-relation argument from three scalar registers to arbitrary register counts in the abelian rational-address bit model. If the k paid rank-one frames have rational span at least k−1, every diagonal monomial target is a sum of a disjoint subset of the paid frames. Thus the sum of target ranks is at most k, including any extra registers restored on arbitrary dirty inputs. Targets need not be invertible or triangular.

For example, four rank-four targets cannot use 15 paid calls in this class. A 16-call attaining fixture is included. Two or more frame relations and different operation alphabets remain outside the result. The proof handles cyclic projector patterns with incoming-only or outgoing-only extra roles; a zero projector diagonal does not make such a role inactive.

The package includes a uniform written proof, exact source pins, and two separate implementations: packed coefficient matrices versus per-entry Laurent exponent sets, with different catalogue and rational-rank algorithms. They agree on all 155 projectors at sizes 1–4, 577 conjugations, 13 rational formal-word fixtures and nine hypothesis/scope controls. These finite checks support the proof; they are not a formal verification of its arbitrary-register statement.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-one-relation-seed04
```

title: Tooling: accelerate exact historical frame containment
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in exact containment adapter for the historical rational-frame checker. It tests integer membership equations instead of rebuilding a combined row basis. The original checker, selected construction, frozen inputs and upstream/ remain unchanged.

Verification engineering, OS-random assignment seed 90. No new κ. The selected conditional κ at the starting commit remains 0.001672660197076918.

## Result

For a canonical primitive reduced target basis with pivot columns p_i and positive pivot values d_i, set D=lcm(d_i). A source row u belongs to its rational span exactly when, for every nonpivot coordinate j:

D*u[j] = sum_i u[p_i]*(D//d_i)*v_i[j].

The adapter retains the original predicate's rejection of noncanonical target representations. Its bounded caches retain immutable inputs; no complete audit verdict is cached.

Nine alternating fresh-process pairs on Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12.14, CPU 0:

| Complete h=10/h=12 audits | Reference | Adapter |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median process wall time | 3.158709 s | 2.726833 s |
| Median peak RSS | 88,852 KiB | 70,512 KiB |

title: Scoped negative result: arbitrary free rectangles retain COPY64 for P112 pair (4,6)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Scoped negative result; no new kappa.** This closes the exactly-two projected-product branch left open by Cinna Davis's PR #1373. For the fixed P112 pair **(4,6)**, arbitrary GL(3,C) mixing of two coordinate terms with one nonzero free rectangle retains sharp whole-decoder COPY sum **64** and cannot lower the separate COPY power bill for `0 < t <= 1` at unchanged width and normalization.

The new compensation argument gives `|U| <= 2^(r_comp+1)-1`. If the compensation rank is at most one, at most three rows can disappear, preserving both other ranks. Otherwise the ranks dominate `(7,7,2)`, whose concave power bill is at least that of `(8,8,0)`. The three-product argument belongs to PR #1373; both new implementations replay its finite premise before combining the branches.

A literal failure control shows why all terms matter: omitting compensation falsely reports **63**, while the complete bill is **70**. Identity mixing attains 64, including a rank-nine masked completion.

Only `research/p112-two-product-compensation/` is added. The [written proof](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/8d53667d9bb09d9b1ffb0f865b5c8dc230eb02f6/research/p112-two-product-compensation/PROOF.md) states all hypotheses. Other coordinate pairs, zero-factor families, more mixed coordinates, multiple rectangles, shared copies and changed normalization are outside scope. No physical supplier, full paid recurrence, new multiplication bound or formal multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- OS seed **46**, structural decoder track; `complex-masked-decoder` card, scope refined to the open two-product branch. Three candidate tasks and the local claim are in TASK.json. No pinned sprint issue existed.
- Exact base: `cd91ac8e2652bfee6bf09da3b8724253bcf78f5f`; contribution: `8d53667d9bb09d9b1ffb0f865b5c8dc230eb02f6`. Refreshed upstream `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983` preserves every live source pin and the selected record.

- PR #1331: `f08b698cc2bd74e2425486728a008e531fc35f0e`, Arham Tahir's one-coordinate predecessor and survivor-containment method.
- PR #1375: `4a533aff2a7a87c9b36e077a31774b332a7f64bd`, @commdata2338's all-pair small-rectangle result. This contribution removes the support-size cap for nonzero rectangles on (4,6).
- Concurrent PR #1432: `4bcc49e3f4041018b0607da46a87d8928a6e0fd0`, Hanson Sun / bbMisk's fixed 24-row (0,1) result, including zero amplitudes. Its reported `(7,8,7)` pattern is independently corroborated here; the new contribution is the arbitrary-support compensation-rank argument. It is not a code or theorem dependency.
- The final recorded overlap scan completely paginated **797 open PRs and 149 discussion records**, without warnings; nearest heads were rechecked before submission. Source SHA256/Git-blob pins and source-specific notices are retained.

## Validation

Python **3.12.13**, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-two-product-compensation
```

Expected: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-two-product-compensation outcome=negative-result`.

Both exact engines agree on all five strata, **2,555** character evaluations, **2,800** one-sided ranks and **145,600** credited three-product records. They also check all eight baseline coordinate charges. The primary checker verifies eight Gaussian-rational fixtures (**100,352** entries) and eight semantic controls. The separate label-based checker verifies five sharp erasure boundaries and an affine omission control.

The registered replay, optimized Python **3.14.6** checks, three CLI corruption/export test groups, **20** repository workflow tests, selected-record integrity and whitespace checks pass. Receipt SHA256: `8ee4249397f879fecfac63695fe547badddd8492533279689c71079ae943aa1b`. VALIDATION.json binds the proof and executed checkers.

The independent implementation covers the finite premises; it does not separately replay the Gaussian-rational fixture implementation. Both implementations have the same AI-assisted author. Full selected-supplier cold replay, native admission, hosted CI and proof-assistant checking were not run locally. The compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, analytic and bit-interface obligations remain inherited.

## Credit

Credit Cinna Davis / PR1373; Arham Tahir / PR1331; @commdata2338 / PR1375; concurrent Hanson Sun / bbMisk / PR1432; Mihir Srivastava / PR845; DreamingOfClouds / PR717 and PR446; Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled / PR620; and the wider lineage in the retained notices.

title: Tooling: exact annihilator containment for historical frame audits

## Change and mathematical scope

Add an optional, source-pinned adapter for the historical h=10/h=12 mixed-point frame audits. title: Research audit: exact truncation transport boundary (no new kappa)
body:
The retained synthetic-transform proof moves componentwise truncation across a signed coefficient permutation to charge one truncation per round. This audit characterizes the maps for which that equality holds on every disk input and gives exact counterexamples to extending it using unitarity alone.

For a complex linear map, each output must select one input with phase `1`, `-1`, `i` or `-i`, or equal zero. For a square unitary map, this means a permutation with those phases. The package also bounds the commutation error by `sqrt(2) * 2^-p * (1 + ||A||_infinity)` and gives rational orthogonal witnesses with discrepancy proportional to `sqrt(n)` grid units, while both displayed arrays stay in the disk.

The source's signed-permutation argument remains valid. This is a scoped precision-boundary result, with no alleged production defect or new kappa. Only `research/truncation-frame-transport/` is added.

title: Research: independent COPY floor for arbitrary one-column P112 corrections
body:
An arbitrary free correction on one P112 column can invalidate the earlier rank-eight-per-child argument. This independent proof still bounds the **complete COPY power bill** when any two original coordinate terms and that correction are mixed by any `GL(3,C)` change of factors. All **28 coordinate pairs, 112 singleton sites, arbitrary complex amplitudes and every subset of the 52 odd neighbors** are covered; transposition gives one-row corrections. Six original terms remain fixed.

The three replacement ranks satisfy `sum r_j^q >= 2*8^q` for every `0<q<=1`. The complete COPY sum has sharp floor **64**, and the complete power bill has sharp floor **8*8^q**, attained by identity mixing for every allowed correction. The proof accounts for the pure correction factor through lower envelopes `(8,8,0)`, `(6,6,6)` or `(6,6,4)` and uses the coupled inverse-factor identity. title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on every P109 unit — 19 new orbit certificates (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p109/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

#1419's extension lemma makes P112 minus X rigid whenever X lies inside a frame of P112. For three-line punctures that leaves **198688 of the 227920 triples**, which fall into **19 FRAME0-stabiliser orbits**: 18 contain an odd pair, and one (1792 triples) is pairwise orthogonal but lies in no P112 frame. This PR proves rigidity on all 19 with #1425's per-unit method. Each orbit representative gets:

- a pivot frame passing #1212's (I3) and (I4) with gluing, with 18 to 24 complete classes;
- #1399's Lemma 9 connectivity for the 5–29 lines outside complete classes;
- a new DRUP refutation of #1212's zero-pattern CNF for (I2) zero exclusion, of 1595 to 2945 lemmas.

**Consequence.** With #1419, **every P109 unit** (P112 minus any three lines) is rigid. Every decoder with exactly eight costly terms in the E-graph model there has cst ≥ 61, which is #968's 72 − p at p = 11.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p109/verify.py` runs 25 exact checks in about 15 s, standard library only. It is self-contained:
  - **Census.** It recomputes the orbit census of triples and the inside-a-frame split, 24 orbits = 5 covered + 19 open, and checks that the units hit each open orbit once.
  - **Per unit.** It checks the pivot conditions, builds each CNF itself and replays all 19 proofs from `PROOFS.json.gz` (658 KB) with its own two-watched-literal RUP checker. The SHA256 of each decompressed proof and each CNF is pinned.
  - **Controls.** The gauge pattern satisfies each CNF. Each proof fails without the "some entry vanishes" clause. An empty-clause-only proof is rejected.
- **Cross-checks, run once:**
  - #1212's own `rup_check` (head `57099cb5`) accepts all 19 proofs, with identical lemma counts, and rejects every one without the zero clause.
  - A census written independently by OpenAI Codex, from a specification only, matches the orbit table exactly: every (size, odd pairs, inside-a-frame) triple, plus |H| = 344064.
  - A read-only adversarial review, also by Codex, found no soundness gap. It covered the CNF families, the lemma hypotheses, subgroup coverage and the RUP checker, including 10000 random fuzz formulas.
- `make_proof.py` (python-sat 1.9.dev15, Glucose 4.1) regenerates `UNITS.json` and `PROOFS.json.gz` byte-identically in about 4 s.
- Passes on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14. `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

title: Scoped audit: PR1417 P112 tensor rank is field-specific (no new kappa)
body:
**Status: scoped independent field-sensitivity audit. No new κ and no counterexample under PR #1417's stated `F2` assumptions.**

PR #1417's graph certificate reports that 5,824 ordered P112 edge tensors span rank 80 in an 81-dimensional matrix space. This package independently rebuilds all rows from the selected port word and distinguishes the result by field:

- rank is **80 over `F2`**, matching the stated binary-field claim;
- rank is **81 over `F1009`**; the package gives an explicit 81-by-81 pivot minor with determinant `548 mod 1009`;
- since 1009 is prime, that minor is nonzero over the integers, so the same tensor matrix has rank 81 over `Q` and `C`.

For the identity form, port 0 has integer self-dot 3 and edge `(0,1)` has integer dot 2. These reduce to the required values 1 and 0 modulo 2. The pinned PR #1417 proof explicitly declares `F2^9` and uses characteristic two, so the odd-characteristic result is a portability boundary, not a refutation of the theorem as written.

- Research/source base: `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`.

title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on every P108 unit — 168 orbit certificates, census-free coverage (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p108/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

#1419's extension lemma makes P112 minus X rigid whenever X lies inside a frame of P112. For four-line punctures that leaves **168 of the 180 FRAME0-stabiliser orbits**, 6132952 of 6210820 quadruples: 166 orbits contain an odd pair and 2 are orthogonal but lie in no P112 frame. This PR proves rigidity on all 168 with #1425's per-unit method. Each representative gets:

- a pivot passing #1212's (I3) and (I4) with gluing, with 16 to 24 complete classes;
- #1399's Lemma 9 for the other 4–36 lines;
- a new DRUP refutation of the zero-pattern CNF for (I2), of 1373 to 3168 lemmas and 361027 in total.

**New: coverage without a census.** The verifier does not enumerate the 6.2 million quadruples:

- Every quadruple contains a triple, and the 24 triple orbits are cheap. So every quadruple is equivalent to a *candidate*, a triple-orbit representative plus one line. There are 2517 candidates.
- 49 candidates lie inside a P112 frame, which is #1419's case; that property is invariant, because the group fixes FRAME0.
- For each of the other 2468, `COVER.json` gives a word in the generators, of length at most 10, that carries a unit's quadruple onto it. `verify.py` replays every word.

**Consequence.** With #1419, **every P108 unit** (P112 minus any four lines) is rigid. Every decoder with exactly eight costly terms in the E-graph model there has cst ≥ 60, which is #968's 72 − p at p = 12.

This is the follow-up to #1469 (P109) mentioned there. The two packages are independent, since neither uses the other.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p108/verify.py` runs 174 exact checks in about 2.5 minutes, standard library only:
  - **Self-contained.** It has its own E8 model, triple orbits, cover-word replay, pivot conditions, CNF builder and two-watched-literal RUP checker. It replays all 168 proofs from `PROOFS.json.gz` (about 6 MB), and the SHA256 of each decompressed proof and each CNF is pinned.
  - **Controls.** The gauge pattern satisfies each CNF. Each proof fails without the "some entry vanishes" clause. An empty-clause-only proof is rejected.
- **Cross-check, run once:** an independently written census (OpenAI Codex, from a specification only) finds the same 180 quadruple orbits. It has 12 inside a P112 frame (77868, matching #1419's census) and 168 open, 2 of them orthogonal. The coverage argument does not need it.
- **AI review:** a read-only adversarial review, also by Codex, checked the coverage argument and the P108 edge cases (classes with a single live row). It found no soundness gap. Its one wording point, that `verify.py` does not prove the 168 units lie in distinct orbits, is applied: the PASS line says "168 rigid units cover every P108 quadruple outside a P112 frame", and distinctness is credited to the census. This is not a human review.
- `make_proof.py` (python-sat 1.9.dev15 with Glucose 4.1, plus numpy and scipy) regenerates `UNITS.json`, `COVER.json` and `PROOFS.json.gz` byte-identically in about 40 s. numpy only proposes the orbit grouping; the verifier checks every word.
- Passes on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14. `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

## Not checked or not covered

- **Inherited steps**, cited and not re-derived:
  - #1212's Lemmas 5–6, §7 and transport;
  - #1399's Lemma 9;
  - #1419's Lemma 10 and its P104 inputs, for frame-contained quadruples.

  All of these PRs are open. #968's (F6) is inherited. Attainment of 60 is not checked. There has been no independent human review.
- **P107 to P105** are the open next question. Per-orbit certificates already take about 6 MB here, and P105 has on the order of 10⁵ orbits, so going deeper needs a structural replacement for the DRUP step (I2).
- **Nine or more costly terms.**

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`), refined to #1469's open next question. Track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2. The task was assigned by the donor as "the open thread".
- **Heads:** base `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`. Cites #1212 `57099cb5`, #1399 `4e1ba3a1`, #1419 `81b8997b` and #1425 `4b707c22`. It imports nothing from them.
- **Claim:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1411#discussioncomment-18912490 (P109; updated for P108 in the same thread).
- **Overlap:** none beyond my own claim and #1469. Refreshed at 01:20Z (819 open PRs and 166 discussions, complete pagination).

## Credit

- **burntout76 / Brett Halligan (#1212):** the theorem, (E), the CNF families of Lemmas 4/8, the pivot reduction, Lemmas 5–6, §7 and the transport.
- **themilkman216 (#968):** the floor.
- **DreamingOfClouds (#717):** the E-graph model.

Substantial AI assistance: Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code (proof, coverage argument, verifier, write-up); OpenAI Codex (independent census and read-only review). Submitted by the account holder. Apache-2.0.

title: Research audit: maximal invariant compact-control guard with saturated digits
body:
Saturated temporary digits can be safe for one earlier-source compact-control call and fail on the next. This audit derives the exact complete-map agreement set and its largest subset invariant under the intended XOR, with an explicit carry predicate and exact all-n transfer counts.

At `n=2,K=6,G=2`, the invariant good fraction is **1499/2048**, versus PR1219's **567/1024**. The full agreement fraction is `6841/8192`, but that set is not invariant and cannot be used blindly as the current-address repair guard. The retained construction and predecessor guards are correct.

**Mathematical audit / research note; no new kappa.** Only `research/compact-saturation-audit-seed69/` is added. The source word, production predicates, selected result and `upstream/` are unchanged.

The written proof covers `n>=1,G>=1,K>=G+1,0<=rho<K`. It retains all four swaps, four rotations, highest-bit completion and the complete exceptional-repair charge. Maximality applies to invariant agreement guards for this fixed word and complete rectangle, not every repair method.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/compact-saturation-audit-seed69
```

Expected: `PASS_COMPACT_SATURATION_AUDIT states=1196544 physical=1536 controls=7 headline=1499/2048 no_new_kappa`, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`.

Verification covers all 1,196,544 quotient states in six domains, 38,080 carry-transition cases, every permutation/inverse and sorted repair payload, plus 1,536 original physical-interpreter comparisons. Seven mathematical controls run in the committed verifier. Eight algorithm corruptions, six source corruptions and two receipt corruptions were also rejected locally. Python 3.14.8, optimized 3.12.15 and optimized 3.11.15 agree; 17 existing compact-control tests, five selected-record tests and selected integrity pass. Finite replay supports the all-n written proof; it is not formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

Research base: `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`. Refreshed main: `4040a0f46d67b41c36a472a7cd4af791fd4c36cc`, with all inputs and applicable rules unchanged. The final overlap snapshot covers 828 open PRs, 162 discussion records and 328 local records; no matching saturation/invariance audit was found.

Credit Douglas Colkitt and OpenAI's original framework, Hanson Sun / bbMisk's PR1219 and adjacent PR1247, and @martinxxx9's PR1108. The new scope removes PR1219's nonsaturation restriction and follows compact carries across multiple digits. No pending implementation is imported. title: Research audit: phase-weighted Fourier layout criterion (no new kappa)
body:
Reusing a phase-weighted Fourier routine for both forward passes and conjugating it for the final pass preserves the retained convolution identity only when every phase is 1 and the read map is a self-adjoint group automorphism. Even the constant phase i produces i times the desired answer. With separate forward and inverse weights, affine layouts work under an exact character-phase condition.

This **mathematical audit / scoped interface theorem** extends Ross Richardson's [PR940](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/940) from unweighted permutations to three monomial maps. It proves the full necessary-and-sufficient criterion, including agreement of the two forward address maps and the weighted adjoint for unequal cyclic factors. The original source's coordinate multipliers remain valid; no source defect or new kappa is claimed.

Only `research/weighted-fourier-layout/` is added: written proof, independently implemented literal cyclotomic oracle, verifier, deterministic receipt, source/task/replay metadata and focused tests. No pending code is imported, and the selected frontier and frozen sources are unchanged.

- Eleven focused test groups, including all 32,768 unreduced two-point cases, arbitrary reciprocal phase controls, correct affine and non-involutive source examples, false classifiers, source drift and output preservation.
- Registered Python 3.12.13 and isolated optimized Python 3.14.2 checks passed on macOS arm64. An offline source export in a path with spaces passes; corrupted source and expected certificate are rejected. Selected-record integrity and clean patch application to refreshed main pass. title: Research: eight-call UT3 commutator floor with one dirty register
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Two central commutator targets require exactly eight paid calls in the formal F2[UT_3(F2)] model with r=2 or r=3 registers. The paid address alphabet is a=I+E01 and b=I+E12 only; c=abab=I+E02. Each I+([g]+1)N costs one, with N a binary rank-one idempotent. Scalar GL_r(F2) mixing is free; the third register is arbitrary dirty and restored. The complete attaining bill is four calls per data role, with no clean allocation, free address maps or uncharged undo.

A C2-quotient determinant argument excludes odd lengths. Two separately implemented exhaustive radius-three censuses exclude every length at most six; together these prove the stated fixed-register minimum. This is a scoped computer-assisted obstruction, with no selected supplier or kappa claim.

## Task and overlap

Base main: `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`; head: `b30fdba48f3db70e3589ba740b0782b56ec0ba2e`. Task `bit-new-register-model`, scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f`, priority revision 2; scope refined to this group, alphabet, target and r=2,3. [Claim and coordination](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18912406).

This follows Gareth Davidson's #1333 (`7f25b6d0e1d7e995d4d2840f231d98b1a1a9fec2`) and the three-dimensional next question in commdata2338's #1414 (`9e1640094f649ba6db9742796825a8d6c238989b`). Their S3 coordinate-swap result and this D8 central-commutator result have distinct groups and targets. No pending implementation is imported. The overlap helper's remote refresh was unavailable (no gh CLI); live PR/Discussion searches were checked, including a fresh zero-match UT3 PR search. Coverage is incomplete; no novelty assertion. Main was rechecked before submission.

## Validation

`python3 -I -B research/ut3-commutator-register-bound/verify.py`

`python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut3-commutator-register-bound`

Python 3.12.14 registered replay passes. The formal-coefficient and dense faithful-regular engines agree on entire state sets and minimum distances: 565 states for r=2 and 47,231 for r=3, with empty two-target intersections. Both check eight-call witnesses; identity and single-target controls recover distances zero and four. Includes 37 algebra/boundary controls, including omitted calls, wrong labels, dirty leakage/restoration and a nonfaithful natural-representation fixture. A relocated, read-only Python 3.14.7 optimized replay passes (28.42 s), and a corrupted receipt is rejected. All eight uploaded files were fetched and verified byte-for-byte against the tested package; the diff adds only this directory.

The full selected baseline was attempted but its complete inventory is unavailable in the sparse checkout. No supplier cold replay, physical/compiler/hosting, precision/tape, analytic transfer or Lean verification is claimed. Hosted Linux CI is separate. Details and exact receipts: `research/ut3-commutator-register-bound/{README.md,EXPECTED.json,VALIDATION.md}`.

## Credit

Prepared for juper997 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review. Credit Gareth Davidson for the affine/restricted-alphabet question and augmentation normalization, commdata2338 for the adjacent investigation and faithful-census approach, and eumemic (PR288), Ali Romman (PR468), David Govea (PR720) and retained register-model lineage. Apache-2.0; frozen sources and selected frontier unchanged.

## Open next questions

The package README and TASK.json specify r=4 (two dirty extras) and an all-register six-call coefficient obstruction. First steps are a packed radius-three census, or classification of the 64 six-label patterns; state growth and noncommuting coefficient cancellations are the blockers. The current bound does not extend to arbitrary dirty-register count.

title: Scoped audit: cyclic product gaps cannot replace contraction guards
body:
The weighted two-scan inverse needs bounds on individual coefficients and intermediate prefixes. A fixed gap in the complete cycle product preserves invertibility but cannot preserve its inherited precision or magnitude guard: an exact family has closure gap 3/4 at every length, while every scan cut has error at least 2^(k-w)/3. Thus target error 2^-p requires w >= p+k-1. The retained full caller rejects this family; no current acceptance bug is alleged.

**Status: mathematical audit / scoped negative result; no new kappa.** This adds one source-pinned package, a written all-length/all-cut proof, and a sufficient relaxed-scan certificate that includes both rounded first-pass quantities, the closure denominator, all second-pass prefixes and stored-state height. An in-memory observer checks literal reads, writes, coefficient queries and roundings. No existing source, supplier, selected record, upstream file or frozen artifact is edited.

Validation:

- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/cyclic-product-gap-audit` passes: 16,800 family executions, 240 separately implemented real-block rational solves, 24 valid full-caller executions, nine semantic controls and nine focused test groups.
- 311,880 rounding events are observed. Of the family cases, 9,932 receive a sufficient certificate and 6,868 remain explicitly uncertified; every case satisfies the lattice obstruction.
- Optimized Python 3.14 replay produces the same mathematical receipt. A read-only relocated package, source/receipt corruption controls, an uncharged-read control and `make selected-record-check` pass.
- The final patch applies to refreshed main `e6f9716621f4e01fc190617934cdfaf072bd976f`; all four consumed inputs and selected kappa are unchanged. Hosted CI is separate from this local evidence.

Base: `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`. OS assignment seed: **73**, adversarial-audit track. No pinned sprint issue existed; the local claim, three candidate tasks, stopping rule and completion are recorded in TASK.json. Source Git blobs and SHA256 pins, exact witness, finite domain and remaining obligations are in the package.

Nearest overlap: #764 at `983d66f0f2e48ee500ec7eee2da9244c001c5064` sharpens the bound under pointwise contraction. This changes that hypothesis and proves why choosing a different cut cannot supply a product-gap-only guard. The final overlap snapshot covered all 812 open PRs and 166 discussion records, with complete reported pagination; it found only that predecessor and the local package.

Credit Chafik Boukhalfa's PR628/PR905 scan and wrapper, Ali Romman's PR621 kernel lineage, and Charles Bethin's PR764 bound. Prepared for Charan (@theon199) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, code, testing and writing; no subagents, independent human review, formal verification or complete multiplication theorem are claimed. Coefficient preparation, arbitrary dirty storage, tape/physical integration and supplier adoption remain outside this audit. Apache-2.0.

[Proof, sources, exact receipt and open next questions](https://github.com/theon199/integer-mult-bounds/tree/753c1b60eaf6ef464e258ca1fc022e53b5032cff/research/cyclic-product-gap-audit).

title: Research: two-mask five-cube cost 47 versus 48 under rank cap 14
body:
With every term capped at pairing rank 14, the five-cube code `C=span_F2{1,p,x0*x1,(1+x1)*x2}` has exact minimum total cost **47**, while every common one-mask subcode of this C either cannot decode or costs at least **48**. The attaining word has ranks **7+13+13+14**. This is a **scoped structural result / research note**, not a new kappa or physical supplier.

The package also certifies the complete rank-cap table for all **720** codes generated by two signed coordinate-product masks on distinct supports. There are three verified isometry classes. All retain unrestricted minimum 32; even the optimistic inherited stage budget is at most -32, so the constrained gain does not admit a positive supplier saving. An outside-family two-quadratic-mask fixture attains `8+8+8+8`, showing why the cap penalty cannot be generalized to arbitrary quadratic mask pairs.

The certificate covers arbitrary finite term counts through the complete 65,536-state dyad graph. A separately written checker uses Walsh-feature Gram construction, exact Fraction elimination, checked edge potentials and binary separating functionals. It imports no generator or predecessor code. Coverage: **675 ordered rational ranks, 737,280 transport-pair checks, 55,934,976 undirected edge inequalities, and 11 negative controls**. Attaining words are checked on all 1,024 port pairs.

Reproduce offline with Python 3.10+:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/five-cube-two-product-masks/verify.py
```

Expected final marker: `PASS_FIVE_CUBE_TWO_PRODUCT_MASKS codes=720 orbits=3 ranks=675 controls=11 pins=2 no_new_kappa`.

The [proof, scope, and rank-cap table](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4faed28a0e6c8a0aa5faa87b281b9373fb5d8403/research/five-cube-two-product-masks/README.md), certificate, readable receipt, exact source pins, task card, overlap record and execution logs are all in the package. The registered Python 3.12 replay passes, as do four package tests, selected-record integrity, and five selected-record regression tests. Regeneration is byte-identical; optimized standalone relocation and source/certificate corruption controls pass. No full selected-supplier cold replay, hosted CI pass, proof-assistant verification or independent human review is claimed.

Base **410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983**; OS seed **44**, structural decoder track. Only `research/five-cube-two-product-masks/` is added. Final overlap checks covered 798 open PRs and 168 discussion records with complete pagination, and reconfirmed main at `e6f9716621f4e01fc190617934cdfaf072bd976f`. The selected result and pinned inputs are unchanged. No pinned sprint issue existed, so the donor's local-claim fallback was used.

Credit @martinxxx9's **PR1046**, Ross Richardson's **PR958/1177**, **PR1222**, Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled's **PR231**, icekylinx/eumemic and the retained DreamingOfClouds/Jacob Sussman/Zhihao Chen copy/frame lineage. PR1222 at `c6fe323581d3803a080b000b263a07edf2b00b54` treats one quadratic mask; PR1177 at `e878ef36109bc6d7e21e62d03c22d8ec36f6f936` allows at most three terms. The four-term two-mask witness and its exact comparison are outside both scopes; neither pending result is a theorem premise.

Prepared by **Hanson Sun (@bbMisk)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in research, proof, both implementations, verification and writing. Apache-2.0. Physical realization, all-size/compiler, hosting, precision/tape, bit interfaces and analytic transfer remain outside the result.

title: Research: compose a 43-XOR R480 Q-node6 with reviewed node circuits
body:
The historical PR503/510 bit R480 word admits a shorter Q-node6 circuit: 51 → 43 XORs, saving 16 complete ADDs after rebuilding literal reverse cleanup. Composing it with the reviewed Q-node2 and Q-node5 circuits reduces the complete word from 33,958 to 33,904 ADDs.

This is a finite construction and composition certificate. No new κ.

**Exact result**

- Q-node6: phase A, frame 488, original slice [2460,2511), twelve fixed physical outputs.
- New saving: 16 ADDs. Predecessor savings: 38 ADDs. Combined saving: 54 ADDs.
- All eight subsets of the three replacements pass complete checks.
- All 720 persistent register frame paths, 480 helpers, nine COPY/ERASE pairs, and paid rank mass 5,592 remain unchanged.
- Paid histogram remains {1:1200, 2:1440, 4:180, 6:120, 8:9}.
- Combined positive bounds: F=176135 and B=3638746, versus baseline B=3751204.
- Exact combined local payload bound:
  64 F^3 B^2 = 4630420660642035956595446624000.
  Every subset uses 102 bits, below the strict 104-bit cap.

All preparation, source access, frame movement, copy and cleanup operations are charged. These are instruction savings, not measured runtime savings.

**New evidence and attribution**

The new contribution is the Q-node6 witness and complete admission of all eight compositions. Precision effects are not additive, so each combination is checked separately.

ToikY's PR1003 supplies Q-node2 (52 → 43); martinxxx9's PR1089 supplies Q-node5 (51 → 41), the unchanged synthesis algorithm, and reusable replay functions. Their 38-ADD saving is credited separately. No new synthesis algorithm or optimal circuit claim is made.

The bounded search uses assignment seed 6 and exactly 1,000 trajectories with seed 2026101406. Trial 625 supplies the 43-gate witness. Candidate acceptance checks the complete precision bill in all four predecessor backgrounds.

**Base and pinned dependencies**

Starting commit:
410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983

PR1003:
b0eda846c34413dabd1e75402b8ad730f8940ff2

PR1089:
9f33d4d10e59a7575d28378e63c033a4b0c13d3f

Original bitE8mut-r480.json.gz SHA-256:
92e399e9a486b55229b5624632ac54f800dd9e022f2aee97f1e5f264bbc0ef5c

SOURCES.json records SHA-256 and Git blob identities for every consumed dependency. Both predecessor heads were unchanged at the final Git refresh. Public PR/discussion searches found no matching Q-node6 composition; coverage was partial and establishes no priority claim.

**Reproduce**

From the repository root, Python 3.11+:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r480-qnode6-composition/verify.py --replay-search
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_R480_QNODE6_COMPOSITION Q6=51->43 ADDs=33958->33904 subsets=8 columns=720 controls=179 no_new_kappa
```

**Tests executed — PASS**

- All 4,096 Boolean inputs and inverses for each replacement.
- All 720 dirty-input columns for every composition.
- Original H1–H5, PR425 predicates, exact record export and frame accounting.
- Python and unchanged C++ 5/9/11-stage checks for all eight subsets.
- 179 Python controls, including every replacement-gate omission, missing compensation, illegal frame descent, endpoint-valid stale cleanup, precision overflow and bridge omissions.
- 384 native bridge-omission controls.
- Clean source export without Git metadata, in a path containing spaces, under optimized Python, including native replay.
- Six package corruption/output-preservation controls.
- Selected-record integrity and git diff --check.

Environment: Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.14, GCC 14.2.0, Boost 1.83. Add --native to the reproduction command for C++ replay; set BOOST_INCLUDE when headers are outside the system include directory.

**Limits**

This historical bit R480 word is distinct from the current complex provider also called R480. The selected conditional κ remains unchanged at 0.001672660197076918.

No hosted-parent invoice, selected-frontier cold replay, repository-wide suite, remote CI or Lean proof was run. Boolean equivalence does not assert equality of the old and new integer matrices. All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, uniform precision/tape and analytic transfer remain inherited obligations. No selected certificate, frozen predecessor or upstream/ file is modified.

Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, implementation, verification and writing. Credit also belongs to eumemic, DreamingOfClouds, Dylan Crow, DaysSky, Zhihao Chen and the retained E8 lineage. Original licenses and AI disclosures remain intact; new work is Apache-2.0. title: test: cover Linux descendant cleanup in research replay
body:
The research replay timeout test currently checks one sleeping process and the exception. It can miss a regression that kills the immediate verifier while leaving its child solvers running. This adds a Linux-only regression test with a real parent/child/grandchild tree.

The fixture waits for both descendants before starting the timeout, verifies their PID/group/session relationship, and checks that no recorded process remains live. A normal-completion control passes; replacing group termination with parent-only termination is detected by the same assertion. Teardown retains the real group kill and the fixture has a bounded lifetime. Only `tests/test_research_process_tree.py` is added; the existing research workflow discovers it automatically. Production code, frozen inputs and the selected frontier are unchanged.

### Evidence

- Linux/WSL2, CPython **3.12.14**: `python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v` — **23 passed, no skips**, including all three new tests.
- Linux/WSL2, CPython **3.14.4**: focused module — **3 passed**.
- Windows, CPython **3.12.14**: focused module — **3 explicit Linux-only skips**.
- Independent compatibility check of PR **#1298** at `e76026571dbfa7299bf474b941c9abeb5bd556b3`: its six changed files were overlaid on 34 source files exported from main `4040a0f46d67b41c36a472a7cd4af791fd4c36cc`, with each Git blob and SHA-256 checked. All **23 existing tests passed**, then **26 passed with this module and `-X utf8=0`**. The original Windows audit did not cover Linux. This is corroboration of that implementation, not another portability fix.
- Separate agent source review found no actionable issue; `git diff --check` passed.

Reproduce the added coverage on Linux with Python 3.12+:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_process_tree.py -v
```

### Scope, coordination and credit

[Claim and audit: Discussion #1472](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1472). Initial main: `4040a0f46d67b41c36a472a7cd4af791fd4c36cc`; submission base: `e6f9716621f4e01fc190617934cdfaf072bd976f`. The guidance, selected record, launcher and existing test sources did not change between these bases.

Task scope **changed** from the selector's `bit-helper-contract` suggestion (nonce `06351c3b61dce7f1b61b1a4517a5f6c9`) to a `portable-replay` verification audit after the prescribed overlap check encountered the known Windows Unicode failure. The original card's positive control passed. Live PR-body/Discussion/README/ledger searches found #1298's fix and @woklerx's independent Windows Python 3.12 audit; this adds the missing Linux execution evidence and descendant cleanup regression. Budget/stop rule: one bounded exact-head audit; no mathematical construction or search.

Credit Douglas Colkitt for the launcher and onboarding tests, @rtyu193-rgb for #1298, and @woklerx for the prior Windows audit at `a6f02272aed71a70c8107cc61bce763267fa2656`. Prepared by Paul Romeo (@p-romeo) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in investigation, implementation, testing and writing. Apache-2.0; no independent human review is claimed.

### Limits and open next questions

This checks ordinary descendants that stay in their inherited process group/session. It does not test escaped daemons, Windows `taskkill`, macOS, or the full selected mathematical cold replay. No kappa improvement is claimed. Hosted CI is separate from the local Linux results.

A useful next check is the same readiness-based descendant assertion for #1298's Windows branch. It would cover a behavior the current platform-specific test skips; the first step is a Windows process-state observer and parent-only failure control. That platform-specific observer is outside this PR.
