title: Tooling: exact sparse phase recipes reproduce the three frontier1042 phases pins, 12x on a shared host (no new kappa)
body:
**Tooling (verification engineering). No new κ. No pinned file changes, and no check is weakened.**

## What

A cold `make frontier1094-verify` runs `verify_frontier1042.py` as its `baseline1042-cold` stage. That replay calls the pinned serial `phases_full.py` three times, in the cells, chain and slots stages. In the maintainer's recorded run these three steps take **469 s of 1162 s** (199.4 + 134.4 + 135.3). #1151 parallelised the five layer-end-control steps and states that it does not re-measure these three.

Two merged exact fast paths already exist: Ali Romman's sparse compiler (#1029, `research/selected-replay-fastpath/`) and thakrarsagar's parallel runner (#1041, `research/phase-recipes-parallel/`). Both were measured only on the PR942 U8 word. `research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath/` checks them on the three k8 words of the selected chain.

## Result

The three canonical words come from `research/community-frontier1042-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz`. Their decompressed digests equal the `canonical_sha256` in LEAVER-PINS-k8, CHAIN-PINS-k8 and SLOT-PINS-k8. For each word:

- **Recipes.** `selected-replay-fastpath/run.py --engine sparse` writes a `CLIFFORD-RECIPES.json` that is **byte-identical** to the archived maintainer recipes. Its digest is the pinned `clifford_recipes_sha256`: cells `aab63b0a…`, chain `e3bfdfa2…`, slots `d0768f21…`.
- **Review.** Every `CLIFFORD-REVIEW.json` field except `seconds` equals the archived review.
- **Other engines.** The dense PR662 evaluator and `phases_parallel.py --engine dense662` reproduce the same bytes.

Same-host timings, macOS arm64, 10 cores, Python 3.14.7. The host was shared, with load average 10–29. The receipt is `BENCHMARK-macos-arm64.json`.

| Command | cells | chain | slots | Total wall (CPU) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| maintainer recording, pinned serial (other host) | 199.4 | 134.4 | 135.3 | 469.1 |
| pinned serial `phases_full.py` via `run_portable.py` | 80.3 | 82.4 | 88.2 | 250.8 (250) |
| `run.py --engine dense` (PR662) | 11.7 | 14.2 | 13.8 | 39.8 (39) |
| `run.py --engine sparse` (PR1029) | 7.9 | 7.8 | 5.0 | 20.7 (19) |
| `phases_parallel.py --jobs 10 --engine dense662` (PR1041) | 2.8 | 2.9 | 3.1 | 8.8 (70) |

All times are in seconds. On this host the sparse compiler is 12× faster than the pinned serial step in wall time, and uses one core. The parallel dense runner is 29× faster but uses about 10 cores.

## Controls

`verify.py` runs two controls on a corrupted cells word. Neither may reproduce the pin.

- **C1.** One one-dimensional frame is changed to a different line. It must be rejected by an `AssertionError`, with no recipes written.
- **C2.** One edge is redirected to a frame of a different dimension. It must compile, but to different recipes.

Both behaviours are asserted exactly.

A bit flip inside a *full-rank* frame keeps the span, so it is not a corruption. My first draft control did this and was replaced. `-O` is refused. #1029's package keeps its own controls, proof and gate tests, and this PR does not repeat them.

## Wiring (maintainers' call, not done here)

Later stages consume these outputs. `verify_slots.py` asserts both recipe digests, and `verify_t16.py` copies both CLIFFORD files forward and binds them.

- **cells.** `reproduce_leaver.py --skip-phases` works with an external `run.py` call and pin assertion.
- **chain.** `reproduce_leaver_chain.py --skip-phases` **fails**: it ends with `assert got == pins` over the whole CHAIN-PINS dictionary.
- **slots.** `verify_slots.py` has no switch.
- The T16 provider binder asserts the review's status, digests, global-phase flag and adapter count. The fast-path review matches on all of them, and `verify.py` checks this.
- All these scripts are manifest-pinned. The serial path stays the reference.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath/verify.py              # ~20 s; PASS_FRONTIER1042_PHASE_FASTPATH
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath --check-only
python3 -B research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath/bench.py NEW_DIR sparse,dense,par-dense662,pinned   # ~6 min
```

The package uses only the standard library. `verify.py` passed on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14, and the registered package check passes.

## Scope and limits

- The recipes are compiled from the **archived** words, which the canonical pins bind. A cold rebuild that reproduces those pins feeds the lowering identical input.
- Scalar-interface integration and the global emitted program are unchanged obligations.
- The host was shared during the timings (load average 15–23), so the numbers are descriptive only.

## Task, overlap and credit

- **Task.** `replay-runtime` (scope key `a76657a85478d269d19f`), refined to one stage. Chooser nonce `893f17f4197754c213cbf77d6bf6fe19`, priority revision 3. Base `858771bc`.
- **Claim.** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18915285
- **Overlap.** The overlap check was refreshed at 2026-10-14 05:04Z, covering 591 open PRs and 288 discussions with complete pagination. #1151 (head `99d4f42f`) covers the layer-end controls only. No open PR or discussion references these three recipe digests or the phase steps of the frontier1042 replay.
- **Credit.**
  - Ali Romman (#1029): the sparse evaluator.
  - thakrarsagar (#1041): the parallel runner.
  - Charles Bethin (#662): the gate tables and dense evaluator.
  - icekylinx and the PR425/PR531 ancestry: `phases_full.py` and `clifford_exact.py`.
  - LeaverSAT and LeaverSAT2: the k8 cells and chain.
  - The gauge44 slots authors.
  - Douglas Colkitt: the replay archive.
  - #1151: identifying this gap.
- **AI disclosure.** Prepared by Josie Elliston's donated session with Claude Code (Claude Opus). A Codex read-only review caught three problems. My first wiring note wrongly said chain `--skip-phases` would work; it fails its whole-dictionary pin check. The controls' pass condition was loose, and the credit was incomplete. All three are fixed. That review is separate AI review, not independent human review. Contribution head `3f21415b`.

**Open next questions** (also in TASK.json):

1. Should the cold replay use the sparse compiler for these three steps? Scaling the measured 12× ratio, it would save about 430 s on the recorded machine, and with #1151 the frontier1042 run would drop to roughly 300 s.
2. Do other archived replays spend comparable time in the 23 byte-identical `phases_full.py` copies?

Workflow feedback: the generated `TASK.json` stub sets `outcome` to `in-progress`, but `research_package.py` rejects that value with only "declare outcome". The accepted values (partial, completed, blocked, negative-result) appear nowhere in the stub or the guide.

title: Research: screen the queue-ceiling census's uncovered sixteen claims (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**No new kappa; no claim is accepted or rejected.** The selected record, `upstream/`, the frozen source pins and the task catalogue are unchanged. This PR adds only `research/complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered/` (README, SNAPSHOT.json, RESULT.json, verify.py, rebind.py, TASK.json, TASK-CARD.md, SOURCES.json, VERIFY.json).

It is the second follow-up of the [census handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18909652): https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1264 screened 14 of the 30 open complex kappa claims and listed 16 as not covered ("no profile whose kappa equals the title kappa, with live/calls and an idle histogram in the same package"). **All 16 are screenable at their snapshot-pinned heads.** The census's extraction condition missed them because of field naming, not absence: the same four inputs are recorded under `global_profile` / `profile`, `idle_profile`, `complete_invocations`, inside `expected/` blocks, or (for https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1175) README prose.

## Result

- **30 of 30 census-listed claims are now screened** (this package's 16 plus the census's 14). The 16 sit on **11 distinct per-call local words** (7 new against the census's nine), listed with exact ceilings in `RESULT.json`.
- **No newly screened word raises a cap.** The highest cap among them is **0.0016872744** (word N1, identical to the census's W4; claims CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1104, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1107, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1117, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1121, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1150, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1172), **+0.004%** over the selected word's cap 0.0016872026 and below the census's best cap 0.0016873148 (W1). The whole covered queue remains a packing contest inside the +0.87% band above the selected kappa 0.001672660197076918.
- **https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1175 is the selected word with a new idle packing.** Its recorded global profile splits into the selected local word exactly (`1:2412 2:418 3:432 4:142 5:82 8:8`, 72 calls on 7,168 live) with idle remainder `{1:1214, 2:1, 32:1, 48:2443}`; its recorded kappa 0.001674083482880778 sits 0.78% below the W2 cap. This is the "pack a selected-type word tightly" route from the handoff, already pursued there.
- **Review flag:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1175's PR-title kappa (0.001675338871723469) differs from every kappa its package records (headline 0.001674083482880778). The screen uses the recorded value and pins the mismatch; which profile the title value belongs to is for the claim's authors to say.

Every claim's recorded endpoint lies below its own word's exact relaxation and every recorded kappa below its cap, as for the census's 14. Each recorded profile satisfies the coverage law `mass = 72*live + 64*calls` exactly.

## Method and evidence

- `SNAPSHOT.json` records, per claim at its pinned PR head and Git blob sha1: the global paid profile, the idle-remainder histogram, live stock W, call count N (`complete_invocations`, or the census's `live*9 == 896*calls` rule), the recorded kappa and complex lower endpoint, and the exact field paths used (README prose for CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175).
- `verify.py` repeats the census's checks with `research/complex-local-word-ceiling/ceiling.py` ([CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1240](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240)): coverage law, idle split (idle <= profile, idle ranks <= 51), 896/9 live families per call, the per-word exact packing ceiling, endpoint below its word's relaxation, kappa below its cap, exact rational title/record kappa agreement (with CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175's pinned mismatch), and a byte-identical `RESULT.json`. Five rejection controls mutate the snapshot (coverage law, idle split, families per call, endpoint above relaxation, title mismatch) and must fail.
- `rebind.py --fetch` re-reads every pinned blob from its PR head and checks the recorded values (network; not run in the registered replay).

## Task card

- **Card:** `complex-new-helper-inventory` (complex-mechanisms track; chooser OS-random nonce `03cd0e6ed50226c5f8024d8ad5618d79`, priority revision 3, base `0a201997097b8a89b638f3a2afcb35db4184c8b2`). Scope **refined**: the card's first experiment ("write the candidate per-call local profile and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's") applied to the queue claims the census could not cover. Reason recorded in `TASK.json`; full card in `TASK-CARD.md`.
- **Exact heads:** branch `research/agent-21-queue-uncovered-03cd0e6e`, head `9efe15ab79b669c99d1e95dcc4a50e2d3ad71a9c` on base `0a201997097b8a89b638f3a2afcb35db4184c8b2`. Two claim heads (CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1172, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175) moved since the census listing; the pinned heads were current at snapshot time (2026-10-14T05:10Z).

## Overlap

Final `find_overlap.py` refresh (2026-10-14T05:03Z, complete pagination, 591 open PRs / 287 discussion records) for `uncovered sixteen`, `queue ceiling`, `local_profile_per_call`, `CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175`, `complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered` found only this package and its own claim. Nearest work: [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1264](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1264) (the 14 covered claims and the Not-covered list this fills), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1262) (supplies `local_profile_per_call` / `idle_histogram` fields on its own receipt — this is the consuming reader those fields were requested for), philippeVV's fork-only `k8-inventory-screens` (leaver-line words; different claims). Claim: [discussion 1166 comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18914889).

## Reproduce

Standard library only, from the repository root (about 9 s):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered/verify.py
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_COMPLEX_QUEUE_CEILING_UNCOVERED claims=16 words=11 new=7 max_cap=0.0016872743702513531 controls=5
```

Registered replay (run here on CPython 3.12.14) and metadata check both pass:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered
# PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered outcome=completed
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered --check-only
# PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

`python3 -I -B research/complex-queue-ceiling-uncovered/rebind.py --fetch` re-reads the pinned PR blobs (network).

## Limitations

- Caps are planning bounds (`kappa < a/(1+a)`) for hosting, owner and idle repacking of each claim's own recorded word under the coverage law, 896/9 live families per call and the halving guard. They ignore helper widths, windows and chronology and do not bound changed words, templates or outer recipes.
- The screen reads what each package records; it does not re-derive any profile from a circuit, re-run any claim's replay, or validate helper placement. A recorded profile could in principle disagree with its own construction.
- Several screened packages carry the status "pending native and strict admission"; nothing here strengthens those statuses.
- No new kappa, no selected-record change, no claim acceptance, no hosted-CI run and no independent human review. The repository test suite shows 20 tests with the same pre-existing `test_research_onboarding.PackageTests` scaffold-fixture errors (unrelated files, untouched by this diff).

## Credit

Every construction belongs to its claim's authors: G. V. Chudnovsky (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1175), tomdif and the CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1148-line authors (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1169 lineage), jeremykothe2 (CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1183/#1192/#1201/#1207/#1218 lineages), and the authors of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1104, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1107, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1111, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1117, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1121, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1150, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1154, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1172, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1176 as cited in their packages. The coverage identity is CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1012's; the ceiling model and queue-census method are Douglas Colkitt's ([CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1240](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1264](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1264)).

title: Research: connected E8 frame subfamilies need not saturate diagonal incidence
body:
## Result and exact boundary

347 genuine E8 frames on the fixed P107 live set have all 28 two-point
frame-intersection graphs connected, but their coordinate-2 diagonal-incidence
matrix has rational rank 43 instead of the required 44. An explicit +/-1
vector supplies an eighth independent kernel direction. This refutes
**(G) implies (D) for selected frame subfamilies**, not for the family of all
live frames.

The complete 877-frame family satisfies all eight required ranks. Adding one
explicit omitted frame, whose extra-vector sum is 2, already repairs all eight
ranks. No nongauge decoder, supplier, copied-information floor, physical
adoption, new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. In particular this
does not refute the predecessor theorem, which assumes (D) independently.

## Task card and sources

- Assigned track: complex-mechanisms; OS nonce
  `0d6468a107c6f96e18bdef01e3e8f622`; original card
  `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, scope key `02b31ebd160542c86299`.
- **Changed scope** to the connectivity-versus-rank handoff:
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18914508.
  This is prerequisite-verification side work, not satisfaction of the card's
  physical rank-shape acceptance gate. No proposed supplier means no replacement
  moment or a<D/E invoice; selected baseline bindings and the card's ceiling
  positive control were replayed.
- Base: `858771bcca3b8dd5d4ef4aa682a13cc9b7e23920`.
- Concrete object: FRAME0=(0,1,6,11,20,29,106,119),
  X=(32,45,73,78,88), F=(2,5,8,9,30,41,108,117); coordinate 2;
  select all live frames annihilating the recorded signed vector.
- Criterion/fixture: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1560
  at `eb9f6f15f15704949cbd25ca8fbf58063084dd8e`.
- Open implication question: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1616
  at `7b3e4624e31647fc2a8b777a181823739b12b36e`.
- Entry and immediate refined-object overlap checks were run before computation.
  Final refresh at 2026-10-14T05:10Z covered 593 open PRs and 292 discussions,
  complete pagination, plus local notes and ledger. Relevant heads were unchanged.
  No competing selected-subfamily investigation was found; unsearched diffs and
  closed work outside local notes remain coverage limitations.
- Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18915387.

## Files and verification

Only `research/e8-connectivity-incidence-boundary/` is added:
`README.md`, `TASK.json`, `SOURCES.json`, `VERIFY.json`, `CERTIFICATE.json`,
`verify.py`, `test_verify.py`. Frozen inputs and selected record are unchanged.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/e8-connectivity-incidence-boundary --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/e8-connectivity-incidence-boundary
```

Observed locally on Windows, Python 3.12: metadata/pins PASS; registered replay
PASS; 2 unittest groups PASS, including five semantic/receipt rejection cases.
Verifier output:

```text
PASS_E8_CONNECTIVITY_INCIDENCE_BOUNDARY live=877 selected=347 graphs=28 rank=43 required=44 canonical_kernel=7 extra_kernel=1 full_family_control=PASS one_frame_repair=PASS
```

Integer kernel identities supply exact upper rank bounds, modular nonzero minors
supply lower bounds, and the bounds meet. No floating point or predecessor
checker imports. A separate read-only AI review independently regenerated the
geometry/graphs and used Fraction elimination to reproduce selected/full ranks
43/44, canonical/augmented kernel ranks 7/8 and repaired rank 44. Its two minor
test-feedback items were addressed and the registered replay rerun.

## Remaining obligations and credit

The **all-live-frame-family** implication remains open and is the next question
in the README/TASK. No downstream rigidity, cost-floor or full multiplication
proof obligations are discharged. No full selected cold replay, independent
human review or hosted-CI success is claimed.

Credit Andrey Mas / an664 for the criterion and fixture, Josie Elliston for the
handoff and modular-rank methodology, and Brett Halligan / burntout76 /
Ninefold (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1212),
DreamingOfClouds (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717),
themilkman216 (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968)
for the retained geometry/decoder lineage.

Prepared by **Aaron Wang / navinor, with help from chatgpt**. Substantial AI
assistance includes research, implementation, writing and read-only review.
Apache-2.0.

Workflow feedback: the concrete-term recheck found the precise open handoff;
the annihilator-selected first vector falsified the broader implication without
a larger search. The supplied Python-3.12 path lacked a backslash: the working
path here is `C:\Users\warha\.local\bin\python3.12.exe`. PowerShell 5's default
redirection writes UTF-16; avoid it for JSON intended for UTF-8 tools. No packages
were installed.

title: Research: rank-8 rigidity on every P105 unit via #1560's criterion, and (G) does not imply (D) for frame sub-families (no new κ)
body:
## Scope

`research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p105`: a finite verification of a conditional theorem. **No new κ, no
construction, and the selected frontier is unchanged.** It answers the first open question of #1616 (P105) and
extends #1616 by one level.

## Result

#1560's Corollary 2 gives K = D(2G_L)D⁻¹ for any live set L whose pivot frame satisfies (D), (G), (W) and all 14
blocks nonempty. This package checks those premises, exactly and in the standard library, for **all 242802
orbits of 7-subsets of P112** (P105) under the 8-generator FRAME0-stabiliser subgroup H. **So with #1560, every
P105 unit is rigid**, and through #1212 §8 PR968's floor for masked decoders with exactly eight costly terms
reaches 57 = 72 − 15 at P105, the bottom of its 72 − p range.

## How the replay became affordable

#1616 left P105 open because a stdlib replay cost about 25 ms per unit plus 1.65 million coverage words. Here:

- **Per unit, about 5 ms** instead of 17 ms (one Apple-silicon core). The tests are #1616's. Rows are int
  bitmasks over deduplicated frame traces, (G) uses union-find with early exit, and (D)'s modular elimination
  first takes a greedy chain of rows that each add a new column. Those rows are independent over every field;
  only the row order changes. A GF(2) rank never reaches the target, so there is no binary shortcut.
- **Coverage transporters** are element indices into H, which `verify.py` rebuilds by breadth-first closure (8 s,
  about 700 MB), instead of words. `COVER.bin.gz` is 5.1 MB; `UNITS.json.gz` is 0.7 MB.

## Evidence

- `verify.py --cover`: 13 exact checks. Model and the frame identity (6) on all 2025 frames; generators; H (172032
  elements fixing FRAME0); triple orbits; four coverage levels (2517 → 180, 18782 → 1614, 156627 → 19295,
  1651528 → 242802), each candidate the image of its unit under an indexed element of H; #1560's fixture and
  control; (G) and (D) fail on deficient frame families; a first-frame control.
- `verify.py --part i/3`: every P105 pivot is a live frame passing (D), (G), (W) and nonempty blocks, ranks
  modulo 1000003 as lower bounds with the seven kernel vectors as the matching upper bound. All 242802 pass.
- The registered replay passes on head `d960f8a2` (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`, about 4 min wall on 10
  cores; timeouts 120 + 3 × 340 s assume a 4-core runner). Also: Python 3.10 and 3.14 on `--cover` and a 1/50
  part, and the 20 `tests/test_research_*` tests.
- Mutation controls: a non-live pivot, a (W)-failing pivot and one changed level-7 element index each fail.
- In scratch comparisons the new criterion matched #1616's exactly (verdict and statistics) on 300 P105 pivots,
  1200 random (unit, frame) pairs and 800 sub-family controls with (W), (G) and (D) failures.
- `make_units.py` (numpy) regenerates the data from scratch with an exact pivot search (about 9 min on 10 processes) and reproduces both committed data files byte for byte. Its census sums orbit sizes to exactly
  C(112,k), k = 4..7, and reproduces #1616's unregistered P105 census and float-rank pivots exactly.
- A read-only adversarial review by OpenAI Codex found no soundness defect in the criterion, rank bound,
  coverage induction or part split. Its one low-severity point is addressed (see below). This is not a human
  review.

**#1616's question "does (G) imply (D)?": no, for arbitrary frame families.** New `control.g-without-d`: on
P105 unit (2,3,7,12,13,30,45) at pivot frame 543, an 80-frame sub-family of the live frames passes (W), nonempty
blocks and (G), but its incidence matrix on I_3 has rank 39, not 40. The certificate is exact: the integer vector
−1, −1, +1 on lines 42, 66, 93 kills every row and is independent of the seven h_3l. With all live frames the pivot
passes. So a structural (G) ⇒ (D) lemma would have to use that the family is all live frames. (Found by a random
scratch search: one hit in 16416 sub-families of 20–300 frames at 608 P105 pivots.)

**Observation for the full-family question.** `tally_earlier.py` (unregistered, stdlib, seconds) reruns the exact
criterion on all 17429 live frames that precede a pivot: 17210 fail (W) and 219 fail nonempty blocks. So in every
P105 unit the first frame passing (W) and nonempty blocks also passes (G) and (D).

## Not covered

title: Construction: four paid transfers for the signed connector (no new kappa)
body:
Charles Bethin's PR1637 signed 3×3 connector uses twelve child queries and six paid root transfers. This contribution supplies a **four-transfer word**, retaining all twelve queries, both arbitrary-dirty roots, source preservation and the complete output map. The two root-doubling passes disappear.

**Status: finite complex circuit construction and scoped minimum theorem; no new kappa.** At exactly twelve signed child queries, four transfers are minimal for arbitrary fixed **one-way** root shears over Q or C. A short-transfer height argument reduces the lower bound to Ross Richardson's PR944 one-root obstruction, freshly replayed over all 720 paths by two implementations. Opposite-direction shears, scaled queries, more child calls and selected-supplier admission remain outside the result.

Both fully expanded 2/3/4/5/6/7-factor fixtures use 300 factor calls and five borrowed dirty rows (two roots plus three child rows). Total instructions fall from 306 to 304. In the matched dense integer tape model, including changed port bindings, the saving is `24 L^3 + 4 L^2 + 20 L - 4` head moves for every integer `L>=1`, plus `2L` fewer source reads, target updates, additions, work clears, root doublings and root negations. title: Research: sharp COPY64 and COPY71 for all-nine-factor uniform P112 columns
body:
Rescaling all 52 free entries of one P112 column creates a rank-nine masked completion. This proves that **every exact nine-term complex factorization still has separate COPY cost at least 64**, with sharp power floor `sum rho_j^q >= 8*8^q` for every `0<q<=1`. When all nine terms have nonzero original coordinate projections on both sides, the sharper bounds **71** and `8*8^q+7^q` are also attained.

The family is `K_lambda = XX^T + lambda*(X X_v^T - 4e_v)e_v^T`, for every one of the 112 live columns and every nonzero complex lambda. Lambda=-1 clears the free column entries. All nine factors may vary, with ordinary transpose; the transposed row family follows. Only `research/p112-uniform-column-rank9/` is added.

### Mathematical contribution and credit

Arham Tahir's #1591, pinned at `264b8dcfc56584797ebf36d69ee35de18313fd27`, handles one changed odd entry. Its complete punctured support classification is explicitly credited and independently replayed here; no priority for that lemma is claimed. The new 52-entry family has the same anchor on both sides, so singleton terms can pair at zero cost and the predecessor's distinct-anchor charge does not apply. The written proof resolves both zero-cost residuals using the actual coefficient matrix. Cross-duality permits at most one cost-seven mixed term, giving the sharp all-nine-mixed floor 71.

Gareth Davidson's #1468 and Hanson Sun's #1613 cover arbitrary column amplitudes while mixing two or three coordinate modes, respectively. The latter head is `a34723742801f877c9636ed72f176a7ffa7bf005` and credits Andrey Mas's parallel claim. This package restricts amplitudes but frees all nine factors. #1612's separate COPY71 result fixes nine simplex normals and all-pairs exactness, a different domain. The multiline and compensation lineage, Mihir Srivastava's #845 geometry, DreamingOfClouds' #717/#446/#595 model, GamingPuzzled/#620, themilkman216/#968 and woklerx/#1077/#1180 are retained in NOTICE.md and the unchanged source copies.

### Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-uniform-column-rank9
```

The complete registered replay passed:

- All 57,232 puncture/character cases, the unpunctured classification, and 13,552 support-class pairings.
- Fourteen exact Gaussian-rational factorizations, checking 175,616 matrix entries, including dense nonreal changes and attaining COPY64/COPY71 examples.
- A separate geometry/rank implementation and 37,632 independently computed integer compensation entries. Dropping the final paid term suggests COPY63 but corrupts a constrained diagonal.
- Eight external corruptions rejected for the intended reasons, plus optimized read-only relocation. Both checkers also passed isolated read-only Python 3.14 execution with identical primary receipt `c9c67a0d484f8e9cbc05d9aab592b57df5eb3a70bf9ccc53d0ebbc7d2ccacb79`.

Source pins, authenticated remote Git blobs, metadata, clean patch application and changed-package discovery passed. Mathematical commit: `6b05c428fcfdc5d860c30baa00d3b6fdc41da050`.

One OS-random selection, nonce `c3d61d9333f4d9682ef1c24c486cd260`, chose revision-2 `complex-mechanisms / complex-masked-decoder`; both prescribed starting checks passed. Base `ef5f39403610d231a0c27e8a6b4f08c10209bcd6`. Priority revision 3 was read on resumption; the assignment was retained. Final overlap covered 594 open PRs and 293 discussion records with complete pagination; the closest predecessor heads were unchanged. [Scoped claim and finding](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1639).

This is a scoped COPY-component obstruction with a written quantified proof and exact finite premises. It does not supply a physical decoder, whole local paid profile, 5% ceiling-gate improvement or new kappa. title: Research: sharp residual guard count for the seeded reciprocal
body:
PR1638 proves three reciprocal guard bits suffice but leaves open whether its **actual seeded routine** works with two. This contribution settles that question: with the unchanged seed 5/8, six-bit warm-up, floor rounding, exact products and capped doubling, target p=15 and c=127379/65536 return x=67435/131072. The residual exceeds 2^-16 by exactly 655/8589934592.

**Status: scoped mathematical result; no new kappa.** The complete reachable trace and an exact interval of failing inputs are proved in the README. Actual seeded failures also exclude zero and one guard. Combined with the explicitly credited PR1638 upper proof, three is therefore the least uniform nonnegative integer guard count for this fixed residual contract. All earlier stages satisfy their bounds. This is not a counterexample to PR1638's theorem, a minimum failing-precision claim, or optimality for arbitrary schedules or absolute-error-only approximations.

The proof is short enough to check directly. An integer-significand evaluator corroborates the witnesses. A separate rational certificate checker validates floor inequalities, row connections and a schedule derived from powers of two; it does not execute the recurrence or import the evaluator. This avoids treating two arithmetic representations with a shared traversal as independent validation.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/reciprocal-seeded-guard-boundary/verify.py
```

title: Bounded decoder experiment: 296 pair-total replacements fail the cost screen
body:
Adding one mixed centre could replace two scatter contributions with one. This bounded experiment checks that idea on the actual selected PR1094 delivery cut before attempting physical synthesis. **All 296 clean proportional pair-sharing variants fail the cost screen, even with additional implementation costs granted free.**

The precise mechanism is `H=C_i+lambda*C_j`: on a nonempty subset where `d_j=lambda*d_i`, replace both old contributions by `d_i*H`; retain all coefficients elsewhere, the other six centres and all non-centre paid work. All 28 unordered centre pairs, induced ratio classes and their nonempty subsets are covered. This changes the term count and cut supports; it is not another eight-term all-pairs search.

## Result and evidence

- 296 exact candidates; 265,216 rational carrier-basis coefficient checks. Canonical cut coefficients are cross-bound to the emitted forward program.
- Only four candidates tie total centre mass at 64. Each replaces two rank-eight children by `(7,7,2)`, a strictly more expensive recursive profile. All other cases pay 65–68 centre units.
- Best favorable primitive ceiling: bracket `(0.001689680763861, 0.001689680763862)`, below the selected word's relaxation bracket `(0.001690054109088, 0.001690054109089)`. These are packing-relaxation ceilings, not attained kappa or runtime measurements.
- All candidates fail the predeclared 5% gate and even the zero-percent comparison of those relaxed profiles. The written concavity argument shows their moment is pointwise worse for `0<a<1` under the fixed retained-work model.
- The complete candidate table is canonically hashed. A separate integer/explicit-vector implementation reconstructs every case, the six rank patterns and the best witness without importing the primary or supplier modules. Numerical roots use the credited, pinned PR1240 engine; independent numerical repricing is not claimed.

## Sources, scope and coordination

Seven new files only in `research/centre-cut-pair-sharing/`: two checkers, exact compact receipt, README/proof, TASK, SOURCES and registered VERIFY manifest.

Base main: `99aea7503041c2bd559e69bacb7ef12b4fa9a552`; contribution `9fca8c97`. Selected PR1094 source head: `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810`. The selected 480-helper word is read from the reviewed replay archive and bound to the slot recipe's canonical payload pin. No ancestor evidence/local word, upstream file, frozen package or selected record is modified.

The user selected a changed-decoder follow-up to [our PR1643](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1643). The exact refinement, favorable budget and stopping rule were recorded before computation. [Discussion1645](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1645) holds the claim and handoff. Complete pre-submission metadata pagination covered 532 open PRs and 300 Discussion records; the focused search found our package/claim only. Metadata search does not establish novelty over all historical/private code.

This is the selected sparse 176-edge cut acting on prepared carrier values. PR845/1071 concern a full P112 Gram fixed-coordinate-reader family, and PR1633 concerns all-pairs excess-rank classification; neither result is claimed anew.

## Verification and limits

The registered Windows CPython 3.12.14 replay passed all three commands:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-cut-pair-sharing
```

Primary normal and optimized checks pass with eight semantic/accounting controls. Secondary optimized replay passes with three separate failure witnesses. Metadata/source pins and staged whitespace checks pass. Repository onboarding helpers were unchanged; their previously observed Windows portability errors were not rerun or folded into this result. Hosted Linux CI is separate.

The budget counts every residual and added COPY, all retained non-centre work and ideal idle mass, while granting zero extra preparation, carrier-frame promotion, dirt repair, phase/precision/scalar and physical hosting overhead. This rejects the declared fixed-profile mechanism; it is not a completed physical invoice. No native A/B/cleanup redesign, target waiting schedule, full local phase/scalar replay, owner admission, global exact moment, outer composition or cold supplier replay was performed. The comparison is to the selected word's packing relaxation, not a general exclusion of improvements to its currently attained packing.

One-sided cancellation, direct regathering that changes the source frame, multiple added totals, altered non-centre work and other coverage laws remain outside scope. The next question is recorded with a first step and blocker, rather than supplying an unverified promising candidate. No new supplier, kappa, formal multiplication theorem, merge or closure is requested.

title: Tooling: compile reader tables for a 1.40x faster PR845 replay
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Tooling improvement; no new κ.** PR845's complete P112 single-lift verifier repeatedly evaluates the same reader forms. This adds an opt-in engine that compiles the exact eight-by-112 table with the original evaluator, then generates every original ordered constraint row. The frozen package is unchanged.

title: Research: UT4 central-target tariff bound with arbitrary dirty workspace
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Price the new class-three UT4(F2) central-target alphabet with arbitrary finite restored dirty workspace and every nonzero binary rank-one scalar coupling, including nilpotents. Every full formal word for w central targets requires n_a,n_c >= 2w and n_b >= 3w+[w=1]. The complete positive uniform tariff is at least 2w(alpha+gamma)+(3w+[w=1])beta; the explicit upper word costs 2w(alpha+gamma)+4w beta. One target is exactly eight calls; two targets lie between14 and16.

The new step combines a middle ker(X)/im(Y) quotient with degree-three mixed coefficients forcing both middle spans to have rank w. PROOF.md supplies the uniform rank argument; quotient.py certifies its fixed17-dimensional homomorphism lemma on all4,096 group products. A separate construction attains the necessary four-matrix relaxation for every w, without claiming a chronological word. Full endpoint acceptance uses the formal group algebra and an independently implemented faithful regular operator.

Only research/ut4-central-tariff-relaxation/ is added (13 files). This is a scoped lower theorem/relaxation, not a physical supplier, rational-frame identity, multiplication theorem or new kappa. The selected frontier is unchanged. Full multi-target optimality, proof-kernel formalization and physical/compiler/hosting/precision/tape/analytic transfer remain open.

## Task and overlap

Base main c24fb5e6537d19d79c62265e4a12781aef9309cb. Revision3 task bit-new-register-model, nonce825a224ec7f742d396fd07c46cd8f17c, scope7084092dd726e7ba1f2f; refined to the specified nonabelian-family variation and target-specific relaxation method. TASK.json and SOURCES.json record the card, exact source bindings and limits. [Claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1647).

Entry checked591 open PR bodies including drafts; pre-submit numbered pagination found532 distinct open PRs with no UT4 match. Main changed during paging, so this is not an atomic snapshot. The helper searched local metadata/ledger; live UT4 Discussion search found only our claim. Full Discussion pagination and all code diffs were not covered; no novelty guarantee. Guidance/catalog/selected/model blobs were rechecked unchanged at2de86c77b4127d2f01f504e0c7c5e4db737caa3c and again before publication at a18b4b0136d647529971e9fcb99fa83f5b9a0b81.

## Validation

Run python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-central-tariff-relaxation. Final registered replay passed in34.38s on Python3.12.14/macOS26.5.2 arm64 with standard library only. Optimized isolated verification passed;20 research workflow tests passed; staged whitespace check passed.

Exact finite evidence:30 full formal/faithful witnesses and7,040 basis columns;729 expanded ordered pairs;19,683 three-factor coefficient cases;128 attained factor fixtures throughw64;4,096 quotient products/4,913 algebra triples; separate literal4,096 group products/262,144 group triples and42 rank-one factors. Eight test groups cover actual failed words, omitted calls, dirty restoration, nonfaithful common kernels, source/receipt corruption, illegal domains, occupied outputs and read-only optimized relocation. VALIDATION.json records omissions. Finite role fixtures do not establish the uniform theorem; its written rank argument uses only the separately scoped fixed-group lemma. Selected cold replay was not needed or run.

## Credit and next question

Credit steph4n-gh/#1573 at0b8c5a69297c794f2de22c04494c83e41300ae36 for all-register UT3 zero-sum ranks; Arham Tahir/#1589 at010ec8c01c0edbbb08b541be236ab78d096f2ca1 for nilpotent couplings; Hanson Sun (@bbMisk)/#1607 at9d6117918025cee6a0c5b7ef30ff8d936ca0621f for coefficient-span tariffs, plus retained lineage listed in README. No predecessor executable is imported and no literature-priority claim is made. Apache-2.0; prepared for @ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including two bounded subagents. No independent human or kernel review claimed.

Next: decide whether two central targets attain14 calls, starting with six middle factors whose two spans have rank two, then imposing chronological and full formal endpoint conditions. The relaxation provides headroom, not an implementation.

title: Independent audit: PR1624 fixed paired26 minimum 62 (all 256 classes, PR1020 binding)
body:
This is a separately written audit of [#1624](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1624) (an664 / Andrey Mas, head `712a9b9a`). #1624 proves that PR1020's fixed 26-line puncture with designated pair (48, 0) has an eight-term separate-COPY minimum of **62**, with 256 optimal classes and a sharp branch bound of 67. #1624 itself notes two limits on its evidence: both of its checkers came from one session, and its 69 baseline was replayed from transcribed data rather than with PR1020's program.

**Result: corroborated, no gap found.** Only `research/paired26-independent-audit/` is added. The selected frontier and κ are unchanged.

## What it checks

- **Finite premises.** `verify.py` was written from proof.md's prose only; #1624's `verify.py`, `audit.py` and certificate were not read. It recomputes every finite premise of §§2, 4–6, 8 and 9 with exact integer and Fraction arithmetic:
  - the label basis and the 14,400-entry bilinear identity;
  - the −256 minor;
  - 511 kernels: 482 of rank 8, 29 of rank 7, on 27 lines `P ∪ {30}`, cross-checked mod p, with no rank ≤ 6;
  - the §5 table row for row, with each annihilator also found by enumeration;
  - the 13 + 1 perp candidates and the `c·r_j` list;
  - the 62 witness on all 8,836 entries, and the §8 table;
  - 256 independent seven-sets, matching the structural formula.
- **Beyond #1624.**
  - Each of the 256 optimal classes is expanded entrywise; all cost 62. #1624 left these unexpanded.
  - A branch-67 witness is built here rather than taken from #1624.
  - The §10 complex example is checked over Q(i): cost 63, and the real look-alike has the same 16 supports.
- **Binding to PR1020.** Merged PR1020's own `decoder_check` prices its decoder at 69 and #1624's witness at 62. PR1020's root indexing, pairing and puncture equal #1624's spec. This stage imports predecessor code on purpose and is labelled as binding, not independence.
- **Written audit.** The README reviews the §3 normal form, the §4 reduction over C, the (2.1) bound, both §7 cases and the §9 converse step by step. No missing implication was found.

## Commands

All run on macOS arm64, about 30 s each. Seven rejection controls run in normal and `-O` modes.

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired26-independent-audit   # PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE
python3.12 -B research/paired26-independent-audit/verify.py      # also 3.10, 3.14, and -O
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired26-independent-audit --check-only
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' # 20 tests OK
```

A read-only OpenAI Codex adversarial review found no problem in the mathematics or the main gates. It flagged two tautological controls, an unchecked support premise in the §10 control, and an overbroad independence claim. All four are fixed in `99a8cd75`.

## Limits

- The spec (P, `J_label`, tables, matrices) is transcribed from #1624's proof.md and compared against recomputation.
- One Claude session wrote this audit. It is not a human review and not a proof-assistant proof.
- Not checked: #1624's own certificate bytes, its 14 controls, and its external GPT-6 Pro review. None of these is needed for the theorem as written.
- The theorem's scope is unchanged: one puncture, one ordered pair, COPY-only. No physical decoder, moment or κ.

## Task and overlap

- Chooser nonce `37b2c62ff85db7b743acb46efb8fc1d1`: track independent-verification, card `formal-interface-lemma`, priority revision 3.
- The scope is changed to this audit. The reason is recorded in `TASK.json`.
- `independent-moment`, the other card offered, is saturated for the selected record.
- Base: main `a73173f7`.
- Claim: [1570 comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1570#discussioncomment-18915746).
- Overlap refresh at 05:41 UTC covered 535 open PRs and 306 discussion records, with complete pagination. The only matches were #1624, its discussion, and this claim.

## Credit

- an664 / Andrey Mas with GPT-6 Pro (#1624): the theorem and proof.
- woklerx (PR1020): the puncture, the cost-six pair, and the 69 decoder.
- themilkman216 (PR968) and DreamingOfClouds (PR717): the model.
- Hanson Sun / bbMisk (PR1521): the question that #1624 answered.

Prepared in JosieElliston's donated Claude Code session, with substantial AI assistance. Apache-2.0.

title: Consolidation: overlap receipt for the fourth100 witness-MANIFEST pin family (#636/#638/#639/#640/#642/#644/#646) — one drifted larger_gain pin, partial retention, credit intact (no new kappa)
body:
**Card:** `overlap-receipt` (consolidation track, priority revision 3, chooser nonce `6bc45fb7886eb99e0494a94781da0e58`, scope key `757723e3fd38f20fa774`), scope **refined** to one small named PR set. Base main `1f7a934975e5eacaf83511c9ac870263bf095e05`. No new kappa, no construction, no disposition changes; all seven PRs stay open and the selected frontier is unchanged.

**Object:** the seven entries of the fourth100 reconciliation whose contributed-package replay fails at `verify.py` line 39 with `AssertionError: larger_gain manifest pin` — https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/636 , https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/638 , https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/639 , https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/640 , https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/642 , https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/644 (vectorsss / Chi Zhao) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/646 (jeremydiviney). This is a source-bound disposition receipt: a finite certificate of git-blob identities plus one diagnosed source-pin defect, auditing the existing fourth100 receipt (`research/community-reconciliation-fourth100-audit/`, `docs/research/community-reconciliation-fourth100-review.md`, `docs/research/pr-ledger.json`).

## Findings

**F1 — the seven failures share one cause: a drifted `larger_gain` pin.** All seven SPECs register `larger_gain` with `manifest_sha256 = 54d67f45ad520f4a134e069336bd0ff639aaeada28d13539298e4f2655c9692d`, which is exactly `research/larger-gain/MANIFEST.json` at the pinned PR569 revision `897213a855b7fb8a1b8b0e552a2f5c42e6c1b326`. The same path as staged into main (commit `df417acd`, "Stage frozen PR family through 588") hashes `73c186c2807c703e43293c7cf785557a046958c245fa812e433f7fe208cdef6d`, and this drifted copy is what all seven recorded heads carry in their base trees (checked at each head via the contents API). The two manifests differ in exactly two `files` entries, `NOTICE` and `README.md`; both are 40,559 bytes. The staged package is self-consistent at its own revision (main's `NOTICE`/`README.md` hash to the staged manifest's values). The other five pinned sources (`multicold`, `structural_gain`, `joint_prefix`, `frame_coalescing`, `direct_delivery`) still match their pins in the live repository packages.

**F2 — the six vectorsss packages vendor the pinned revision byte-exactly.** For each, every source pin resolves to its own `vendor/<name>/MANIFEST.json` and matches its registered digest in raw bytes (zero CRLF anywhere; the repository's text normalization is not involved). All pinned files match too. Run through their own `verify.sh` source overrides, the six pass the pin block the reconciliation recorded as failing; they evidently ran with sources resolved to live repository packages (as #646's defaults do), where `larger_gain` is the first failing pin. #646 has no vendored copy: its default resolution of `larger_gain` is the live `research/larger-gain`, which reproduces its failure on any checkout of main.

**F3 — retention is partial and dominated by re-vendored predecessor content** (exact blob identity against main at `1f7a9349`; no path matches at the same path and no path exists in main with different content):

| PR | changed paths | byte-retained in main (other path) | not byte-retained |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| #636 | 348 | 285 | 63 |
| #638 | 347 | 281 | 66 |
| #639 | 340 | 281 | 59 |
| #640 | 339 | 282 | 57 |
| #642 | 354 | 281 | 73 |
| #644 | 355 | 280 | 75 |
| #646 | 186 | 77 | 109 |

The unretained remainder is each package's own witness/tools/data/result files (path lists in `evidence/pr{N}-audit.json`).

**F4 — the six vectorsss members share their vendored core** (250-268 shared blobs pairwise; #646 shares 31-33 with each): one content family plus six small per-PR deltas.

**F5 — predecessor credit is present.** `CONTRIBUTORS.md` credits vectorsss for #636/#638/#639/#640/#642/#644 (line 835) and jeremydiviney for #646 (line 833). No missing attribution found for this family.

## Delta and evidence

New package `research/pr636-family-witness-manifest-receipt/` only (plus the local task card `notes/task-card-agent-22.md`): README with Open next questions, `TASK.json`/`SOURCES.json`/`VERIFY.json` metadata, `RECEIPT.json`, per-PR evidence (`evidence/pr{N}-audit.json`: pin tables and every changed path with its blob identity and class), two byte-exact `MANIFEST.json` evidence copies, and tools (`tools/audit_witness_pins.py` fetch-side, `tools/build_receipt.py`). No existing file is modified; `upstream/`, frozen sources and pins are untouched.

## Checks

- `python3 -B research/pr636-family-witness-manifest-receipt/verify.py` passes: drift identity (entries `NOTICE`, `README.md`), all per-PR pin verdicts and retention classes re-derived against `git ls-tree -r 1f7a9349` (2,269 changed paths), cross-PR shared-blob counts, one positive fixture and four failure controls (tampered digest, substituted manifest diff, omitted row, substituted class), each rejected.
- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr636-family-witness-manifest-receipt` → `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`; `--check-only` → `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.
- `python3 -B scripts/research_baseline.py` → `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 15 passed, 1 skipped, 5 errors in `test_research_onboarding.PackageTests.setUp` (Windows CRLF fixture: `write_text` CRLF vs normalized blob in a temp repo). The same module errors identically on a pristine `git archive` extract of the base commit, so these are pre-existing environment failures, not caused by this change.

## Limitations (not checked)

Head-side blob identities rest on the GitHub pulls/contents APIs at the recorded head SHAs (PR trees are not fetched locally; `verify.py` re-derives the main-tree side). The `multicold` `full_tree` manifests were not recomputed file by file. The seven packages' full contributed replays were not executed; this receipt resolves the recorded pin failure and the retention/credit question only. That the fourth100 harness resolved sources to live packages is inferred from the uniform `larger_gain manifest pin` assertion plus the pin data; the harness invocation was not recorded. Retention matching is byte identity.

Five alternating same-input pairs on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.12 measured complete three-case suite medians **32.61348 s → 5.90754 s (5.52066x)**. All samples, including slower pairs on the shared host, are retained. This is a historical verifier improvement, not a selected-replay or multiplication-runtime claim.

## Task and overlap

title: Research: (G) does not imply (D) for full live families at eight deletions (no new kappa)
body:
## Scope

`research/full-family-g-without-d`: an exact counterexample to a proposed verification shortcut, plus scoped
search evidence. **No new κ, no construction, and the selected frontier is unchanged.** It answers open question 1
of #1650: does a pivot that passes (W), nonempty blocks and (G) always pass (D) when the frame family is **all**
live frames? The earlier counterexamples (#1650's `control.g-without-d`, navinor's #1649) use sub-families.

## Result

**No, once eight lines are deleted from P112.** Fixture 1: X = (3, 4, 8, 9, 107, 108, 117, 118), pivot
F = (19, 25, 37, 47, 67, 82, 94, 115), all 784 live frames of P112 \ X.

- Nonempty blocks, (W) and (G) hold.
- (D) fails at pivot k = 2: the live-frame incidence on I_2 (52 lines) has exact rank 44 over Q, not 45.
- Certificate: x = +1 on lines {30, 31, 40, 41} and −1 on {2, 5, 7, 10}. Every live frame is orthogonal to x, and
  x is outside the span of the seven h_2l, which also lie in the kernel. So the kernel has dimension at least 8.
- **Mechanism.** Every one of the 2025 E8 frames meets the coordinate-half D4 subsystems (lines on coordinates
  0–3, and on 4–7) in equally many lines. FRAME0 removes 4 lines from each and X removes 4 more. The 4 lines left
  in each are all odd to F[2], and x is the difference of their indicators.
- Restoring any one of the eight deleted lines makes the same pivot pass all four conditions.
- The unit is still rigid through other pivots: 674 of its live frames pass all four conditions.

Fixture 2 has the same pattern at another pivot, using a non-coordinate pair of D4 subsystems. Its
certificate is checked the same way.

## Evidence

- `verify.py` (standard library, about 3 s): both fixtures. It checks the premises on the full family, exact
  Fraction ranks for every k (only the stated k fails), the ±1 certificates, and the D4 frame identity on all
  2025 frames. Controls: 8 restore checks per fixture, a mutated certificate, and the pivot alone failing (G). Its
  conditions are re-typed from #1650's `criterion`, so it does not depend on that unmerged package.
- Unregistered search (`search/`, imports #1650's `verify.py` through `PR1650_PACKAGE`):
  - Deletion walks: fix a pivot and delete lines while (W) and blocks hold. 176 of 5000 walks reach a
    (G)-pass/(D)-fail step. Greedy restoration shrinks them to locally minimal sets of size 8 to 28, **none below 8**.
  - D4-mechanism census: all 7 D4 pairs that contain FRAME0 as 4 + 4, all 1260 pivots disjoint from FRAME0, all k.
    The deletion this mechanism needs has size 4, 6, 8 or 10, and **(D) fails only at size 8** (32256 cases).
  - Random 8-, 9- and 10-line deletions, every live frame: no (G) or (D) failure.
  - Every live frame of all 1614 P107 units (1393377 frames): 1386438 pass all four, 6936 fail (W), 3 fail
    blocks, and **none fails (G) or (D)**.
- The registered replay and `--check-only` pass. `verify.py` also passes on Python 3.10 and 3.14 and refuses `-O`; the 20 `tests/test_research_*` tests pass.
- A read-only OpenAI Codex review found that the four conditions match #1650's `criterion` and that the rank-44 proof
  is exact. It independently reproduced both (D) verdicts and all 16 restores with #1650's code. Its three
  low/medium points (a placeholder, a search-script label, and two README counts not in `verify.py`) are fixed. This is not a human review.

## Not covered

- **|X| ≤ 7 (P105–P111) is still open.** The searches found no counterexample there, and the D4 mechanism needs
  exactly eight deletions, but neither is a proof. An every-frame census of the 19295 P106 units would take about
  40 CPU-hours (9 CPU-s per unit at P107).
- Nothing in #1616 or #1650 changes, since both check (D) explicitly.
- #1560's Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 are cited, not re-derived.

## Credit

an664 / Andrey Mas (#1560, criterion); navinor / Aaron Wang (#1649, the sub-family case and the full-family
question); #1650/#1616 (implementation and question); burntout76 (#1212), themilkman216 (#968) and
DreamingOfClouds (#717) for the model. Chooser nonce `083eb6ba0dd52fa857761981ccb9156c` drew recursive-interfaces.
Its three cards were crowded tonight (the plane-port lever is claimed in #1587), so this session took a recorded
open question instead. TASK.json records the scope as changed.

Prepared by JosieElliston with substantial assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code. Apache-2.0.

title: Independent verification: quadratic screening brackets sharpen selected D/E diagnostics
body:
## Result

Adds certified two-sided quadratic screening brackets for the three frozen
selected moment roots, retaining every modeled surcharge. The uncertainty
gap left by the linear `a < D/E` diagnostic shrinks by **more than 419x** for
native/conservative complex and **more than 418x** for bit.

This is a screening result, **not** a new kappa, endpoint-grid certification,
supplier improvement, speedup or selected-frontier change. The surrogate
gap is about 1.2e-8; containing the published 1e-24 endpoint intervals does
not independently certify their acceptance/rejection signs. It also cannot
resolve the much smaller native/conservative correction.

## Exact scope and method

- Track/card: independent-verification / `independent-moment`.
- OS nonce: `4fa6ddc953abae43610a0c49ace10c99`.
- Catalogue scope key: `c191650c0fa8d2fa514e`, refined to
  `selected1094:three-ledgers:quadratic-majorant`.
- Base: `2de86c77b4127d2f01f504e0c7c5e4db737caa3c`.
- Concrete ledgers: complex m=73,W=14336, native and conservative models;
  bit m=64,W=28416 with its surcharge. Profiles are read from pinned
  ASSEMBLY/INDEPENDENT1094/bit EXPECTED files, not from headlines.
- Selected complex source head: `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810`;
  bit source head: `a5afc8c6169ea61ba7c51dfd3cade02cc7b13b46`.

For `M(a)=sum c_i exp(lambda_i*a)`, use exact bounds on its first and second
logarithmic moments, E/F, and its maximum rate L. The factorial inequality
`n!>=2*3^(n-2)` gives
`1+t+t^2/2 <= exp(t) <= 1+t+t^2/[2(1-t/3)]` on `0<=t<3`.
The two rational gain surrogates bound the unique moment root, using the
correct outward bisection endpoints and the checked domain `Lhi*D/Elo<3`.
The surcharge is an exponential term and enters D, E, F and L.

No primary pricing/checking implementation is imported. The log primitive
uses an independently written positive atanh enclosure; that classical log
method is not claimed as novel. The different **moment-root enclosure** is
the rational surrogate comparison, not another full endpoint-series replay.
The first bounded computation succeeded; no pivot or large search was used.

## Verification and files

Adds only `research/selected-quadratic-root-brackets/`:
`README.md`, `TASK.json`, `SOURCES.json`, `VERIFY.json`, `RESULT.json`,
`verify.py`, `test_verify.py`. Frozen inputs and selected record are untouched.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-quadratic-root-brackets --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-quadratic-root-brackets
```

```text
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-quadratic-root-brackets outcome=completed
```

Twelve mathematical/control groups include an independent exact fixture
`M(a)=2^(a-1)` with root 1, pole/invalid-domain/unbracketed-root rejection,
and the surcharge's D/E/F/L effects. A separate read-only AI proof/code
review found no critical or important issue. Its minor maximum-rate coverage
point was addressed and replay rerun. A separate 100-digit Decimal root
calculation agreed with every bracket; that is a noncertifying cross-check,
not part of the exact acceptance argument.

## Overlap, remaining obligations and credit

Entry survey and immediate refined concrete-term search preceded computation.
Final refresh at 2026-10-14T05:58Z covered 518 open PRs and 316 discussions
with complete pagination, plus local notes/ledger. Closest work is the linear
diagnostic https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1293 at
`85a361233431befe4b11cf878f7b1b77a244d473` and TennisBowling's log-contract
audit https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1405.
Existing complete selected endpoint audits are credited, not replaced.
No matching quadratic screening package was found; no novelty certificate

title: Independent audit: #1560's zero-exclusion Theorem 1 / Corollary 2 and their use in #1616/#1650 (no gap; no new κ)
body:
Separately authored audit of #1560's Theorem 1 (structural zero exclusion) and Corollary 2 (gauge form), and of how #1616 and #1650 use them. **Corroborated; no gap found.** No new κ, bound or rigidity claim.

#1560 (@an664, with GPT-6 Pro) states no independent human review. #1616 and #1650 apply its criterion at hundreds of pivot frames for the P107, P106 and P105 rigidity results, and cite the theorem without re-deriving it. This package checks that step.

**What was checked**

1. **Written audit of proof.md §2–§4 and §6**, step by step, over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field (README table). No gap. One expository omission is filled: §6 says the pivot entries "have the required form" without the calculation. The README gives it, and Corollary 2 holds as stated.
2. **Implicit finite facts at every pivot.** The proof uses E8 facts relative to F that it never states. #1560's checker covers only its own pivot. `verify.py` was written from the prose alone and checks these facts exactly at **all 2025 frames**, in about 50 s, standard library only:
   - the expansion `2v_i = Σ G_ik v_k`;
   - `|T_i| = 4` and `G ∈ {0, ±1}` off the pivot;
   - the 14 blocks form an S(3,4,8) with 8 lines each;
   - 4+4 orthogonal classes by sign product, each completing to a frame;
   - Hadamard class rows;
   - every exceptional 4+1 configuration (3,628,800) gives `w_j = ±1/2`;
   - the class-sum dichotomy;
   - `Σ_k ε_ik ε_jk = 2G_ij`.

   Three negative controls are included.
3. **Binding.** Both `criterion` functions were read against §3. They test exactly (D), (G), (W) and nonempty blocks with the full live-frame family. For (D) they use a modular rank lower bound plus the seven kernel vectors, whose membership is identity (6), checked for every frame. `binding_crosscheck.py` compares #1650's `criterion` with a second implementation built on different exact methods: classes by orthogonality, Q-rank of `MᵀM` by Bareiss elimination, and BFS. All 4354 sampled cases agree (5–10-line deletions, including every live frame of five deletion sets), and so do 1503 thin-family cases (11–40-line deletions). The fixtures include session 13's full-family (G)-without-(D) pivot. The comparison is thin for (G) and (D), because #1650 stops at its first failing test.

**Not covered:** #1212 §8 (floor from gauge rigidity) and §10 (stabiliser transport), which #1616/#1650's floors also need. Not covered either: whether (G) implies (D) (session 13's claim in #1502), or a proof-assistant formalization. Part 3 is a same-account check, since #1616/#1650 came from earlier Claude sessions on this account. Parts 1–2 do not use that code.

**Task card:** `formal-interface-lemma` (chooser nonce `a2a3ecb2c0544e92b8d811b546d670c3`), scope refined to this theorem-to-certificate binding (TASK.json). Base main `a18b4b01`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1502#discussioncomment-18916028

- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/zero-exclusion-proof-audit --check-only`, plus the registered replay.
- The cross-check as stated in the README.
- A Codex read-only adversarial review found no mathematical gap. It raised three low-severity points (one control was really an illustration, the Python version was unstated, one overbroad phrase), all fixed in `c29103af`.

title: Conditional kappa = 0.001677160151714381 via capped phase-cell fusion
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This contribution replaces the repeated-axis outer Gaussian resampling cost by a capped, in-place tensor construction. With the unchanged pinned T74 supplier from #1661, the resulting **final** conditional bound is

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa=1677160151714381/10^{18}=0.001677160151714381.$$

The new outer argument combines shallow reversible Toeplitz circuits, a common Hadamard schedule, recentered/capped Gaussian interiors, and paid sparse boundary and routing operations. It improves the same supplier's #1661 outer result by approximately `2.6348269308e-7` in kappa. This is a proof/construction contribution with finite supporting checks, not merely a finer numerical grid or a new primitive supplier.

The package retains the original all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source, whole-call hosting, semantic precision (`C1=1`), fixed-tape/prime-packing, paid interchange, exact recovery and analytic assumptions. It does not claim an unconditional or fully formalized multiplication theorem. A separate supplementary `0.001677600129305161` corollary explicitly assumes `omega_C <= 9/4`; that premise is **not needed for the headline result**.

Review entry point: [package README](https://github.com/Vlado-V/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2569871ff906d2a2abfc86e97126ab9afe2e4a5a/research/capped-phase-fusion/README.md), [complete proof](https://github.com/Vlado-V/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2569871ff906d2a2abfc86e97126ab9afe2e4a5a/research/capped-phase-fusion/phase_fusion_note.tex), and [supplier substitution review](https://github.com/Vlado-V/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2569871ff906d2a2abfc86e97126ab9afe2e4a5a/research/capped-phase-fusion/frontier_fusion/INDEPENDENT-SUBSTITUTION-REVIEW.md). The selected frontier is not modified.

- Publication base: `a5d4f08ac102d1a6da301d89379c75285eca680e`; original research snapshot: `e6f9716621f4e01fc190617934cdfaf072bd976f`.
- Exact supplier dependency: #1661 at `f852af5e178ce035cd46181a29d9330bcbcaa206`, source manifest SHA256 `d90d49eaa68e48c6992a07972e736ef4b9cd80274361cbbc1ec980d43f29ad7f`.
- #489 already develops a branch-free Gaussian inverse; this contribution supplies a different in-place tensor compiler, capped gauges, and boundary/layout transfer. #1141's reversible phase stream is related background, not a dependency. #1661 supplies the unchanged finite construction. No global priority or optimality claim is made.
- Refreshed `find_overlap.py --task uniform-transfer-audit` and checked current PR/discussion material before publication; search coverage is not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

From repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -m pip install sympy==1.14.0
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/capped-phase-fusion
```

This registered replay **passed locally with Python 3.12.15 and SymPy 1.14.0**. It recreates and compares 21 exact algebra, tensor, Gaussian, layout, moment and outer-ledger receipts in a temporary copy. The headline ledger has 45 strictly positive exact inequalities and five rejecting variants. Additional publication controls reject an inert checker leaving stale evidence and altered native semantics.

The complete unmodified #1661 native replay also **passed afresh**, with no native reuse: 12 top-level stages, both new provider words, retained parent, 319680 owners, prefix 1441 charged at 2048, and row coefficient 19545 below 20161. Rejected controls: 114 admission, 12 bit, 15 controller, eight independent owner, six geometry. The portable binder checks all 58 receipt files and 46 canonical JSON receipt hashes. Python 3.14.7, NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1 and SymPy 1.14.0 were used for that local run; C++17 and Boost are needed for the native pipeline.

`PUBLICATION-CHECKS.json` records the exact evidence; the README gives the full pinned cold command. The 121 MB native assembly and vendor tree are reproduced externally rather than duplicated. body:

The new uniform lemma applies to every full formal UT4(F2) central-target word with r>=w>=2 and length L<=7w+1. Summing the six scalar span inequalities permits at most one extra span dimension. All factors therefore share a common upper/lower block orientation; active-corner compression preserves multiplication over the full noncommutative group algebra. Compressed nonzero rank-one factors remain legal, and zero identity factors are dropped. Every 14/15-call two-target word consequently reduces to exactlytwo roles. The direct 16-call two-role upper word then proves equality of the minima.

title: Scoped negative result: four-unit signed connector forces every root port

body:

This contribution audits its unchanged symbolic duals and proves that the same paid histogram minimizes the frame LP for **every `0 <= a <= 1/32`**. - Reconstructs all **23,004 LP columns, 17,507 rows and 135 component objectives**; a second column assembly works directly from the shared event graph and agrees on every cost and residual.

title: Scoped negative result: 72/77 copy-cost lower bounds for two masked Walsh P112 totals

Two masked Walsh source totals can leave the P112 coordinate column space, but this specific two-coordinate-reader family still cannot improve the copy-rank bill. A written support-cell reduction and exact finite premises give cost **at least 72 for every real coefficient matrix with two nonzero columns**, and **at least 77 when both masked sources are nonzero**, against the coordinate baseline 64. These continuous lower bounds are not asserted to be attained.

The separate exhaustive census covers all 28 coordinate pairs, 511 nonzero binary label cuts and 40 small unimodular matrices: **572,320 cases**, minimum 72 overall and 78 with both sources nonzero. The all-real argument reduces residual supports to six scalar representatives and added-reader supports to five types, then sums independent term minima as an optimistic lower bound. This is not an inference from a failed search.

Only `research/p112-masked-walsh/` is added. It contains the proof, source pins, deterministic certificate, geometry, two independent rank implementations, controls and local sprint claim. title: Research: no 14-call two-target UT4 word on two roles; with CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680, at least 15 calls for every r (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This adds only `research/ut4-two-target-r2/`. It is an exhaustive finite negative result in the explicit `F2[UT4(F2)]` alphabet of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1662. No new κ, no supplier, and no change to the selected record, `upstream/` or any frozen pin.

**Result.** With r = w = 2 (no extra roles), no word of 14 paid factors `I+([g]+1)xy^T` (g in {a,b,c}) equals the two-target endpoint `I+([z]+1)I_2`. No such word reaches even the degree-three quotient endpoint. This answers CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's open question for two roles.

**Every-r corollary, conditional.** @ToikY's concurrent https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1680 (head `a281330e`) proves in writing that every 14/15-call two-target word with any r ≥ 2 compresses to two roles. Together: two central targets need **at least 15 calls for every finite r**, so the interval is 15..16. That corollary rests on CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680's written lemma, which this package does not re-derive.

## Method

CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's written bound forces counts (4,6,4). The search then:

1. Enumerates the zero-sum six-call middle sequences up to GL2(F2) conjugation. The 5,582 representatives' orbits are checked to cover all 33,489.
2. Reduces each a/c placement to its prefix-sum profile at the six middle calls (20,791 profiles), screened by the a/b-only and c/b-only quotient coefficients.
3. Pairs profiles through the vectors `u_j = P_j x_j`, `w_j = P_jᵀ y_j`, on which `abc` and `cba` depend.
4. Expands every surviving pair into all concrete words. Each word is checked against the full quotient and, separately, the full formal group-algebra endpoint.

| Stage | Count |
|---|---:|
| Canonical middle sequences | 5,582 |
| Key pairs / profile pairs with `abc = cba = I` | 184 / 208 |
| Concrete words | 3,248 |
| Pass quotient endpoint / formal endpoint | 0 / 0 |

## Evidence

`python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-two-target-r2` gives `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/ut4-two-target-r2 outcome=negative-result`. Local run: CPython 3.12 on Windows x86_64, about 4 min (`verify.py` 227 s, then 14 tests in 12 s). `--check-only` also passes.

- `verify.py` independently checks:
  - that `g ↦ 1+g` is multiplicative from UT4(F2) into the quotient on all 4,096 pairs, with `z ↦ 1+abc+acb+bac+cba`;
  - GL2 orbit coverage;
  - CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's direct 16-call word as a positive control, with all 16 one-call omissions failing;
  - every stage count of the full search.
- `test_package.py` (14 tests):
  - the profile and key formulas against direct quotient products on random words;
  - indexed key pairing against brute force;
  - that the formal product is in word order;
  - planted-word completeness: random (4,6,4) words are regenerated by the enumeration;
  - a slow reference driver that finds `(abcb)^2` at r = 1 and nothing for counts (2,3,2).
- Six source mutations (operand order, the `bab` sum, cross order, quotient reduction, left versus right multiplication, the central target) are each killed by the tests. An earlier run showed the multiplication-order mutant surviving; the order test was added to catch it.

**Not checked:**
- CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's count lower bound and CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680's compression lemma are cited, not re-derived.
- No proof-assistant or independent human review.
- No physical, compiler, hosting, precision or analytic obligations; no selected cold replay (nothing in the selected chain changes).
- On this Windows machine, 6 of the 20 `tests/test_research_*.py` workflow tests error inside their own temporary repositories (`source has uncommitted changes ... input.txt`, a line-ending issue). The other 14 pass. The errors are unrelated to this package.

## Task and overlap

- Card `bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 3, chooser nonce `f9a363c919f7441f52bd6dbdade3397d`, scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f`. Scope is **refined** to CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's open next question with r = w = 2; see `TASK.json`.
- Base main `a18b4b0136d647529971e9fcb99fa83f5b9a0b81`.
- Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1647#discussioncomment-18916137.
- The final overlap refresh (07:06 UTC, 383 open PRs and 333 discussion records, complete pagination) found only CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662 and the complementary CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680, which cites this claim.

## Open next questions

1. Is 15 attainable at r = 2? By CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680 that decides the exact cost for every r. The first step is to run the pipeline on the splits (5,6,4), (4,7,4) and (4,6,5).
2. An independent check of CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680's compression lemma.

## Credit

@ToikY (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1662 for the model, bound and question; https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1680 for the workspace compression). Also steph4n-gh (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1573), Arham Tahir (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1589) and Hanson Sun / @bbMisk (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1607). No predecessor code is imported.

Prepared by Aaron Wang / navinor, with help from Claude Code. Apache-2.0. Not requesting merge; the selected frontier is unchanged.

title: Conditional κ = 0.0016769381110224387711...: stacked pivot 566 + 554 kernels with 470-digit grid and 450-digit endpoints over PR1672
body:
## Change and Mathematical Scope

This package establishes a new certified conditional upper bound for integer multiplication:

$$T(n) = O(n (\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa = \frac{k_{\text{num}}}{10^{470}}$$

where:
$$\kappa = 0.$$

and the conservative endpoint lower bound is:
$$\kappa_{\text{conservative}} = 0.$$

### Construction and Refinement
This package stacks the physical helper-donor kernels for cold pivots 566 and 554 (`k554-signed-001`, PR1672) on the T74 exact fill, and certifies the resulting complex moment using outward-rounded integer Taylor recurrence engines (`fine_mercator.py` with dyadic outward rounding $2^{-1800}$ and `fine_moment.py` with decimal outward rounding $10^{-550}$) with 450-digit endpoints, a 470-digit outer grid, 500-digit margin, and 190 bootstrap steps.

The global profile is:
`{"1": 1560432, "2": 336336, "3": 278724, "4": 84912, "5": 54612, "8": 5328, "48": 22748}` ($W = 66,304$, $m = 73$).

### Strict Improvements
- **Over PR #1672 (Jeremy Kothe)**: Strict **+404 decimal digit refinement**, resolving the exact mathematical root beyond PR1672's 66-digit grid and proving all 47 outer margin constraints positive and all 4 rejection controls strictly rejected on the stacked construction.
- **Over PR #1677 / PR #1661 (midhatn)**: Physical kernel addition of pivot 554 (**$+4.144 \times 10^{-8}$** in kappa).
