title: Theorem: common-flag frame obstruction for nonlinear gates
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR825 proves the common-flag rational-frame obstruction for XOR circuits and excludes nonlinear gates. This contribution removes that gate restriction with an information-flow proof.

For arbitrary deterministic pointwise gates over a finite alphabet, the outgoing transcript of a frame-label class must distinguish the independent input symbols whose required outputs leave that class. Weighted label partitions therefore give rank-cost lower certificates. Applying the diagonal characters of a common flag proves `s >= Wm`, including flags over characteristic-zero extension fields, commuting nonsplit frames and noncommuting triangular families. The optimistic recursive moment cannot contract in this class.

Full nonlinear semantics matter: a four-gate Toffoli/CNOT word realizes a CNOT through Boolean idempotence while its CNOT-only subword is identity. The verifier replays complete truth tables and cut transcripts instead of using linear columns.

This is a written structural theorem and exact finite evidence, with no new supplier, exponent or selected-frontier change. Only `research/nonlinear-frame-cut-bound/` is added. The weighted cut statement is proved in the README; the executable instantiates its unit-weight common-flag corollary.

## Task and overlap

- Base main: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; contribution: `78a1810e44bf08f845252cfe4c785ccc967c07a2`.
- Changed scope under `bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 3: arbitrary nonlinear scalar gates rather than a finite nonabelian address alphabet. TASK records the exploratory selection and rationale.
- Predecessor: Navinor's PR825, head `421db1ca2eb26056e82797f94b8c4eecd0120620`. SOURCES pins the current-main statement, upstream contract and finite XOR scorer.
- Active claim: [Discussion #1753](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1753), as **jmbarrancoml**.
- Final complete overlap snapshot covered 431 open PRs and 389 Discussion records. The nonlinear Gaussian/Hurwitz copy bounds and fixed-prefix cleanup obstruction have different contracts. An earlier joint-helper investigation matched PR1517 and is not claimed as new.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/nonlinear-frame-cut-bound
```

Registered replay passed on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.13. Optimized Python 3.14.6 produced identical JSON. Twelve cases cover 428 full input assignments, 3,830 outside-only simulations, exact rational edge ranks, a sharp equality case, nonsplit characters and eleven failure/boundary controls. Controls include a nonlinear gate that fools zero/one-hot endpoint checks and an omitted outgoing message.

PR825's fourteen examples and thirteen tests, source pins, metadata, selected-record integrity and staged whitespace checks also passed. Finite examples support the written proof; they are not a proof by exhaustive enumeration of arbitrary circuits.

Hosted status: GitHub reports `action_required` for the [registered package run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38538365638). Hosted verification remains outstanding.

## Limits and credit

The theorem retains fixed topology, independent inputs, complete all-role permutation endpoints, one common frame per gate and full edge charging. Arbitrary non-common-flag geometry remains open. There is no claimed full multiplication theorem, new physical/compiler admission, Lean proof, independent human review or hosted-CI pass at submission.

Credit Navinor/PR825, OpenAI's retained finite-shear contract, and the preceding routing and nonlinear cleanup audits. The cut-set counting principle is standard; no literature-priority claim is made for it. Prepared for **Jose Manuel (@jmbarrancoml)** with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, proof, implementation and prose, including read-only mathematical exploration subagents. Apache-2.0; source files and licenses remain intact.

## Open next questions

A five-role mixed nonlinear candidate must have a nonidentity endpoint verified on all 32 inputs, a nonroutable topology, and a rational two-dimensional frame assignment with total rank at most nine. The README gives a non-common-flag frame seed. No such complete witness has been found; a failed bounded search would exclude only its declared domain.

title: Research: q<=4 barrier for a noncentral UT4 root pair
body:
## Result

This package gives a complete q<=4 no-go for one fixed nonabelian four-register model. In the full formal algebra F2[UT4(F2)], with paid labels x=I+E12, y=I+E23, z=I+E34 and any binary rank-one idempotent N in M4(F2), no word of at most four calls D_N(g)=I+([g]+[1])N realizes diag([xyxy],[yzyz],[1],[1]). The direct word uses eight calls, so the minimum in this fixed model is between five and eight. Lengths five through seven are unsearched.

## Exact evidence

The package enumerates 120 rank-one idempotents and 360 factors, constructs all 129,600 ordered pair products in the full group algebra, then exhausts all 360 length-three endpoints and 129,600 length-four suffixes. It also cross-checks all 4,096 UT4 group products by ordinary 4x4 matrix multiplication, verifies both target roots are noncentral, checks the direct eight-call word, and rejects an omitted-call and wrong-label corruption.

Reproduce:

~~~sh
python3 -I -B research/ut4-noncentral-commutator-seedbfe59/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-noncentral-commutator-seedbfe59 --check-only
~~~

The exact result, stopping rule, source pins, overlap, and validation limitation are in research/ut4-noncentral-commutator-seedbfe59/README.md. Local mathematical verification passed under CPython 3.14.7. The registered generic replay requires Python 3.12, which was unavailable locally.

## Cost and scope

This prices one formal call as one unit: the direct construction costs eight, and a q<=4 identity would have halved that count. Natural-representation displacement rank gives a floor of two. The selected baseline positive control says the complex primitive remains binding; it also reports a 5.827190801985042 bit multiplier under retained planning assumptions. This finite bit-model result does not change the selected record or kappa. There is no physical supplier, recursive schedule, or complete interface invoice here.

PR #1333 established a rank-sum minimum with the full rank-one affine-label alphabet. This search restricts to three fixed generators and a noncentral two-root endpoint. Open PRs #1662, #1680, and #1690 concern UT4 central targets. No predecessor certificate or selected frontier was modified.

Prepared by Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematical framing, implementation, verification, and writing.

Coordination claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1759

title: Scoped exact minimum: even order-3 targets diag([ab],...) need 2t calls through t = 4 (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

In the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` rank-one-idempotent register model with free scalar
`GL_r(F2)` mixing (paid calls `I + ([g]+1)N`, `g in {a,b}`, `N = v phi` any binary
rank-one idempotent), the **even** order-3 diagonal targets
`T_t = diag([c],...,[c])`, `c = ab = (ba)^2`, at exactly `r = t` registers (all
registers arbitrary dirty inputs restored exactly) need exactly **`2t` paid
calls** for `t = 1, 2, 3, 4` (minima 2, 4, 6, 8). This is the first even-target
tuple class of the coordinate-CNOT line: since `c` is even, the sign quotient
maps the target to `I`, so the inherited invariants flip (`q` even,
`sum_i N_i = 0`) and no predecessor conclusion transfers. Cross-register
sharing does not beat the two-calls-per-target tariff through `t = 4`.

Written invariants (package README sections 2-3): L1' sign-quotient parity
(`q = 0 mod 2`); L2' free mixing forced to `U = I` with `sum_i N_i = 0`; and a
degree 1-3 free-layer system in `F_2<x,y>/(x^2,y^2)`, used only as a screening
filter. **Correction**
(https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1763#issuecomment-6172859400):
an earlier version of this paragraph called that system complete, and package
README section 3 called it necessary for any hitting word. Both claims are
withdrawn. At `r = 1` with every projector `[1]`, the word `b a b a` is an
exact target word (`(ba)^2 = ab = c`) with `sum_ba = 1`, so the condition
`sum_ba = 0` fails on a genuine target word. The corrected scope (package
README section 3): up to degree 3 the kernel of `F -> F_2[G]` is spanned by
`R = xyx + yxy + x + y` alone, the second claimed kernel correction
`Z = z + z^2 + z^3` having degrees up to 6 with a degree at most 3 truncation
outside the kernel, so the matched system is a necessary condition only for
words of length at most 3. The system remains a screening filter
(`layer_ok_even_target`): it holds on the attaining words used here and
rejects the wrong-target control, but it is neither necessary nor sufficient
and is never used to exclude candidates.

Exclusion evidence (`research/even-target-cnot-census/`, standard library only):
complete natural-image meets (a homomorphic image, so empty meets exclude the
formal word) give zero hits at `q = 2` for `t = 1, 2, 3, 4`, `q = 4` for
`t = 3, 4`, and `q = 6` for `t = 4`; the completeness argument for cross-depth
value recurrence (`C C = I`, `C C C = C`) is in README section 4. Every
attaining word is verified exactly in `M_r(F2[G])` by an independently written
formal-coefficient engine, with drop-one-call mutations failing. Engine B
agrees with engine A on every small meet (including the seven 2+2 pairs at
`t = 2`). Calibration: the exact-depth ball *value* counts at `r = 4`
(240 / 32,651 / 3,639,920) match the recorded counts in
https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1705 exactly.

Validation on the committed head:

- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/even-target-cnot-census`
  passes (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/even-target-cnot-census
  outcome=completed`), and `--check-only` passes metadata and pins.
- `python3 -I -B research/even-target-cnot-census/verify.py --check-receipt`
  prints `PASS_EVEN_TARGET_CNOT_CENSUS t1r1_min=2 t2r2_min=4 t3r3_min=6
  t4r4_upper=8 t4r4_excluded={2: 0, 4: 0, 6: 0} balls4=240,32651,3639920
  pr1705_ball_match=True no_new_kappa` (about 50 s).

title: Scoped proof: four fully occupied swaps require twelve calls
body:
Four coordinate-SWAP targets on exactly four roles require **twelve paid coordinate-CNOT calls** in the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` rank-one-idempotent register model, even with free scalar `GL_4(F2)` mixing. This closes the four-role balanced ten-call residual left by #1722 and investigated in #1755. All inputs are arbitrary; no extra dirty workspace is included in this minimum.

The new argument is short: at full occupancy `T=[s]I`, conjugating a paid call by `T` flips a↔b while retaining its scalar projector. A twisted cyclic rotation therefore converts a hypothetical `(5,5)` word into `(4,6)` or `(6,4)`, which the credited #1722 saturation theorem excludes. The README restates saturation with credit and retains its exact proof bytes. The same cut argument shows that any full-occupancy saving below `3t` needs at least `2t+3` calls; equality forces alternating labels.

A concrete four-active/one-dirty counterexample shows why partial-target conjugation leaves the paid alphabet. **Ten calls with active/dirty coupling on five or six roles remain open.** No supplier, selected-frontier, physical hosting or kappa change is claimed.

Only `research/four-swap-full-occupancy/` is added. It contains the proof, task and source pins, exact formal replay, a separately written faithful regular-operator checker, deterministic receipt and failure controls. Both implementations were written by the same assisted author; no independent human or Lean review is claimed. The preliminary SAT work led to the analytic proof and is not a replay dependency.

Validation on Python 3.12.12/macOS arm64:

- Registered replay passes: `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/four-swap-full-occupancy`.
- Both engines agree on 5,334 conjugations, 24 positive words, 288 chronological cuts, 264 omitted-call controls, 99,861 label patterns and the 992-factor partial-target boundary.
- Five test groups pass, including corrupt source/receipt rejection, natural-representation alias detection and optimized read-only relocation.
- `make selected-record-check` and whitespace checks pass. Full selected cold replay, physical/compiler/hosting/precision/analytic admission and proof-assistant verification were not run or claimed.

Exact base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. Exact predecessor heads and refreshed overlap coverage are in TASK.json. [Claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18919990).

title: Independent verification: stdlib re-certification of PR1615's eight-transfer threshold, with all 2,502 eight-transfer schedules (only port splits r=1, r=5) (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Independent verification. No new κ, and no change to any construction,
certificate, selected record or pinned file.** It adds one registered package,
[`research/two-connector-eight-transfer-census-seed58/`](research/two-connector-eight-transfer-census-seed58/README.md).

**Priority belongs to #1615.** The six-transfer exclusion and the sharp
eight-transfer threshold for the free-port two-connector family are
**#1615 (Hanson Sun / bbMisk)**. That family is the one from #1438/#1498: five
sources, every B and A called exactly twice, and paid one-way transfers
`C: z0 += z1`. The eight-transfer word is **Discussion #1412 (Cinna Davis)**.
This package was built concurrently without reading #1615's code. It agrees
with every #1615 number it overlaps.

**What it adds:**

1. **Re-certification in the generic CI hook.** #1615's registered hook is
   `--witness-only`, and its exclusion needs a native C++ workflow.
   - Here a gap-reduction lemma lets a pure-Python census certify the
     exhaustive `t ≤ 7` exclusion and the exact `t = 8` count. On 10 cores it
     takes about 20 s and 50 s, inside the generic Python 3.12 package hook.
   - The lemma: within one gap `z1` is fixed. So three transfers act like one
     and four like two, with coverage and restoration parities preserved.
   - Two further code-disjoint engines cross-check it: a full-placement C census
     and a numpy census with per-occurrence ports.
2. **All eight-transfer solutions.**
   - Exactly **2,502** canonical schedules are universal: **2,376 with one
     source on `z1`** and **126 with all five on `z1`**. The second class is
     Discussion #1412's restricted alphabet, up to renaming.
   - No schedule with any other port split is universal at eight transfers.
     The best coverages are 31, 31, 27 and 24 of 32.
   - So free ports enlarge the solution set but save no transfer.
   - All 2,502 replay as complete 80-call programs on dense random F2 maps with
     arbitrary dirt.
   - #1615's own census tool would give these counts with a small change. They
     are recorded here with replay evidence.
3. **#1498's four-transfer split bounds.** The r = 2 bound of 25 is **not
   attained**; the exact maximum is 21. The other bounds are exact, as #1498
   itself allowed ("need not be sharp").

**Scope.** The incidence-minimal 72-call family only. It is a finite census
plus a short reduction lemma. There is no supplier claim. The cost condition is
#1498's `t·σ` tariff at `t = 8`, as in #1615.

## Task and overlap

- **Base and track:** base `0b1cccf8`; catalogue priority revision 3 leaves the
  card unchanged. Seed 58 → recursive interfaces, card
  `connector-alphabet-change`, scope **refined** to independent verification
  and classification.
- **Overlap:**
  - **#1615 (head `96916897`):** the threshold theorem. Its files contain no
    eight-transfer count, no split classification, no `t = 4` split maxima and
    no stdlib exclusion; I checked every file.
  - **#1498 (`b7baacc8`):** the four-transfer obstruction and the question.
  - **#1438 (merged, read in-repo):** the interface and full-placement censuses.
  - No other overlapping work since #1615 was found among PRs or Discussions.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-connector-eight-transfer-census-seed58 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-connector-eight-transfer-census-seed58
```

**Registered parts** (standard library, parallel):

- **`controls`:**
  - #943's in-repo 105- and 945-word censuses, bin for bin;
  - #1438's in-repo full-placement `t = 2` censuses for 1 to 5 sources: every
    restored count and histogram;
  - complete per-split coverage histograms pinned at `t = 0` and `t = 4`, with
    no universal schedule;
  - no restored schedule for odd `t`.
- **`six`:** an exhaustive `t = 6` census over all 945 words and 32 splits.
  None is universal, and the per-split maxima equal #1615's
  (31, 31, 28, 22, 23, 31). The full histogram is pinned.
- **`eight`:**
  - exactly 2,502 universal schedules, with a pinned list digest `ba04f277…`
    and split counts;
  - each replays as an 80-call program (62 A, 10 B, 8 C);
  - Discussion #1412's pilot is included;
  - on three witnesses, deleting any C or A, or reading on the wrong port, fails.

**Offline receipts.**

- **`independent/census.c`** (every placement, no reduction) agrees exactly:

  | `t` | Candidates | Restored | Universal |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 4 | 30,270,240 | 10,402,560 | 0 |
  | 6 | 242,161,920 | 74,692,800 | 0 |
  | 8 | 1,323,241,920 | 384,199,200 | 2,502 |

  The `t = 6` totals reproduce #1615.
- **`independent/census_numpy.py`** (per-occurrence ports) gives 74,692,800
  legal schedules and 0 universal at `t = 6`.

**Pre-PR review.** A three-lens review covered the mathematics, verifier
soundness and the claims.

- The math reviewer's own fresh brute force reproduced every count:
  - full-vector, per-occurrence ports for n = 1–3;
  - a full-placement n = 5 C census, including all 2,502 at `t = 8`, each with
    maximum gap 2;
  - numeric readout equivalence over 92,772 checks.
- Fixes from the review are included:
  - complete-histogram pins, which catch an undercounting engine that the
    maxima alone miss;
  - live "none universal" checks and a `t = 0` all-split check;
  - mutation controls on three witnesses;
  - the merged #1438 read in-repo;
  - wording.

Tested on Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.8 (macOS, 10 cores). On a 4-core runner each
part fits well within the 600 s per-command limit.

## Credit

- **Hanson Sun (bbMisk), #1615:** the exclusion and the threshold, with

- **Gareth Davidson (bitplane), #1498:** the obstruction, source-port lemma,

- **woklerx, #1438:** the interface and censuses.

- **Ross Richardson, #943:** the universal connector and 945-word census.

AI disclosure: prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial Anthropic Claude
assistance, including explorer, judge and reviewer subagents. Two of those
subagents wrote the independent engines. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. **Is there a short structural proof of the six-transfer exclusion that also
   explains why only r = 1 and r = 5 reach eight?**
   - *First step:* classify the 2,502 witnesses by their transfer phases.

2. **Can extra A/B incidences lower the threshold?** This is #1615's question 1.

body:
This adds an exact weighted optimum for the pinned five-source dirty connector, with complete source leaf prices [1, 4, 10, 16, 28] and unit target readout prices across all 31 nonzero masks.

The predecessor's 12-source-call universal word repeats B2 and costs 200 leaf calls. The alternate 10-source word misses only mask 21; using four A21 readouts also costs 182. Both schedules are replayed on all 37 basis coordinates of the arbitrary dirty state.

With exactly 10 source calls, the pinned complete 945-path census forces at least one nonzero target mask to be absent, requiring at least two extra unit-price readouts. Any legal schedule with 12 or more source calls pays at least the cheapest restored source pair, also a surcharge of 2. The baseline invoice is 180, so the exact minimum is 182. The cheaper relabeling saves 18 against the published repeated-B2 schedule without changing the root record count or primitive alphabet.

title: Research: one connector is blocked by selected output caps
body:
## Result

Scoped negative result for one added dirty accumulator in the selected late complex block. If the single added array reads all eight independent external inputs and is the sole carrier of their `Qz` terms to the four retained additive ports, monotone frame growth makes the route infeasible: the joined input frame is not contained in any rank-eight target cap. Existing helpers may still carry the retained `Ry` and dirty-endpoint work, but cannot store external `Qz` terms. The last external input contributes to two distinct ports, so after the connector has read all eight inputs at least one required output update would force its target to rank nine.

The exact checker covers the 12 blocks in the selected word and 24 blocks from two pinned PR1319 comparison words: 36 block instances and 144 target-cap pairs. Every pair has `dim(span(F_1,...,F_8) + H_j) = 9`; the six rank-eight joins across the three words also differ from every cap. No scalar schedule, gate count or connector tour can evade this frame obstruction inside the stated class.

This is not a general connector lower bound, a result about multiple `Qz` accumulators or direct source-to-target routes, a selected-supplier replacement, or a new `kappa`.

## Provenance and scope

The exact base is `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; the selected-record SHA-256 is `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. `SOURCES.json` pins the selected review, source manifest, assembly certificate, task catalogue, block certificate and compressed block sources.

The closest neighboring constructions are PR #1522's centered BIT source tour, PR #1717's paired dirty-output delta, PR #1739's source/map transition, and PR #781/#855's separate six-source coded-helper packet cell and provider-cost analysis. Those results and their authors remain credited; this result is only the all-eight-input frame-join obstruction for the selected four-port block interface.

title: Research: four-role mixed D8 target has exact five-call minimum
body:
## Result

This adds an exact minimum for one four-role heterogeneous target in the formal group algebra `F2[D8]`, where `D8=<a,b | a^2=b^2=e,(ab)^4=e>` has order eight. Paid factors are `I+([g]+[e])N` for `g in {a,b}` and every binary rank-one idempotent `N` in `M4(F2)`. The target is `diag([a],[ab],[ba],[e])`.

The exact minimum is five. The package gives the direct word
`D_(a,E00) D_(a,E11) D_(b,E11) D_(b,E22) D_(a,E22)` and excludes every word of length at most four by exact coefficient arithmetic over all of `F2[D8]`.

## Verification

The replay enumerates all 120 idempotents and 240 paid factors, forms all 57,600 ordered pair products (32,651 distinct states), and checks the target-specific length 0–4 meetings. Matrix entries retain all eight group coefficients. It also checks the positive five-factor word and seven negative controls.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/d8-mixed-target-seeda97c8e
```

Local result: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`; `git diff --check` passes. Package metadata and exact base pins pass. title: Research: inverse-column cut forces R439 frame-508 source to rank four
body:
## Result

This is a scoped exact obstruction for the exceptional R439 phase-B frame 508 source. For the pinned 11-wire map, register 19 must visit the full rank-four block frame under any monotone same-wire XOR circuit whose operation frames stay inside that frame. The proof allows arbitrary circuit length and proper intermediate frames; it extends the predecessor's source-star-prefix obstruction.

The exact inverse column has support `{19, 35, 66, 89, 97, 466}`. Register 466 enters at the full frame. A cut/factorization argument shows that if register 19 never reached that frame, the inverse-column support would have to lie among wires entering in a proper low subframe, a contradiction. The other ten rows already force full-frame exits by dependency span.

Therefore the current direct block climbs remain moment-minimal for (q=1-a\in(0,1)). No new selected κ or supplier adoption is claimed; the selected complex supplier remains unchanged.

## Pins and reproduction

Base commit: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`  
Selected-record SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`  
Cycle seed: `3b2676afb1d8667edc131585f741d4b0`

Run:

```sh
python3 -B research/r439-bsection-stars-seed01/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/r439-frame508-inverse-cut-seed3b/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/r439-frame508-inverse-cut-seed3b/test_verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-frame508-inverse-cut-seed3b --check-only
```

The scalar positive control passes. The exact verifier emits `PASS_R439_FRAME508_INVERSE_CUT`; all five controls pass. Package metadata and pins pass. Direct replay ran with Python 3.14.7. The registered package replay requests Python 3.12, which is unavailable in this environment.

## Scope and attribution

This covers only the exact 11-wire frame-508 matrix with monotone frames inside its rank-four block frame. Added wires, COPY/ERASE, cross-block changes, frames outside the block, native/hosted admission, all-size realization, precision/tape, and analytic-transfer obligations remain open. Frame 509/source 22 remains a separate question.

The predecessor `research/r439-bblock-frame-barrier` settles eight blocks and leaves source 19/22 open; its simple source-star-prefix check does not contain this arbitrary proper-frame cut argument. Credit the R439 lineage: DreamingOfClouds (PR589), eumemic (PR555/543), Sricharan Vagvala (PR967), Aaron Wang (PR1015), Ross Richardson (PR923), and Arham Tahir's frame-barrier work. Prepared by OpenAI Codex with substantial Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review.

title: Research: source-bound screen of diagonal rank-16 child batches
body:
The selected #1094 gauge44 provider has 2,412 rank-one children per orientation. This package tests a cross-column construction: sixteen adjacent rank-one child climbs on distinct destinations can be represented by one rank-16 child using diagonal block matrices. The hash-pinned chronology permits eight such groups (128 rank-one children). Even after waiving every new interface expense, the best local ceiling rises only 1.7191%, below the task's 5% gate. The result is a scoped construction screen; it claims no physical supplier or new κ.

## Construction and bounded result

For block inputs `X_i,Y_i`, the exact identity

```text
M16(diag(X_1,...,X_16), diag(Y_1,...,Y_16))
  = diag(X_1 Y_1,...,X_16 Y_16)
```

preserves the sixteen requested products; all off-diagonal outputs vanish. The provider trace has one contiguous run of 16 and one of 112 rank-one climbs, partitioned into seven more groups of 16. Both forward and backward orientations have the same windows. No child crosses a scalar, adapter, centre, or other-rank event.

The mass-preserving profile changes from `{1:2412, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8}` to `{1:2284, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8, 16:8}`; both have rank mass 5,586. The exact ceiling upper endpoint moves from `1690054109089/10^15` to `1719107428154/10^15` (gain 1.7191%). The 5% target is `0.00177455681454345`, so the bounded family fails before adding the actual gathering, copies, frames, hosting, output storage, precision, or arbitrary-dirty restoration charges.

## Pins and overlap

- Seed `95da2249593d8218c4c1e30f471d675f`, track `complex-mechanisms`, card `complex-rank-shape-decoder` refined to contiguous cross-column diagonal batches, priority revision 3.
- Exact base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Selected replay archive SHA-256 `f1da80610bf33c58527f18ad63b4350d0b864e1d4486141ee17ac9bed4d529d6`; gauge44 provider member SHA-256 `241fde27d4e43f5a9cb6b128f9f76c5131a53d09f0371676163f914d0b0fef3a`.
- This complements Arham Tahir's open [PR #1605](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1605) (head `488f2ecf1835c6d813e96543656dddf0062fdc9a`) and [Discussion #1596](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1596): their integer reblocking price leaves chronological batches open; this package bounds a source-exact, cross-column diagonal subfamily. It is distinct from the same-column frame assignment screens in [Discussion #1659](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1659)/[PR #1686](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1686) and the one-touch same-column retiming of [Discussion #1693](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1693)/[PR #1703](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1703).

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-diagonal-child-batches-seed95da --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-diagonal-child-batches-seed95da
```

Local registered replay passes: `PASS_COMPLEX_DIAGONAL_CHILD_BATCH_SCREEN groups=8 rank1_repacked=128 profile_mass=5586 ... gain_percent=1.719076 target_percent=5 controls=3`.

The physical M16 interface remains unimplemented: it would need its input/output storage, source and copy schedule, frames, hosting, precision and restoration charged. The selected result is unchanged. Next, any larger gain needs a pinned operand-ready/use-window model for nonconsecutive buffered batches and an end-to-end invoice.

Credit Sagar Thakrar/PR1012, Douglas Colkitt/PR1240, Arham Tahir/PR1605, Josie Elliston/Discussion #1596, Navinor/Discussion #1659 and the selected construction lineage. title: Prove connector cost with source updates and delivery cuts
body:
Sequential output delivery prevents using an offline connector batch, and source updates make an open connector incur paid corrections. This package combines the distinct PR1439 and PR1442 contracts and proves the exact minimum query price, allowing arbitrary readout/source/correction call multiplicities.

For fixed complete prices, the optimum is

```text
2 sum a_i + min_{p_0=p_k=0} [sum b_i(2-(p_(i-1) XOR p_i)) + sum d_i p_i],
```

plus mandatory source updates and caller overhead. A coherent two-state word attains the coefficient/parity lower bound for arbitrary compatible F2-linear maps. Uniform source prices reduce to an adjacent matching problem; unequal prices can favor a longer open interval (32 versus 48 in the included tariff example). The bound also survives permitting past correction calls inside later requests at unchanged prices.

The literal three-output pilot costs **52 versus 64 scalar XORs**, with both source updates, the connector correction, all dirty restoration and every delivery included. This is optimal in its declared indivisible macro tariff, **not** unrestricted XOR-circuit synthesis. The earlier two-output 43-to-31 construction belongs to PR1439 and is reproduced as a control.

Review [the package proof and contract](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/15a91b5d634023a3a14129cbb240854c4b188111/research/mutable-connector-delivery-optimum/README.md), especially the fixed-call alphabet and the additional lifetime/hosting bill needed by a real caller.

Validation on CPython 3.12.12/macOS arm64:

- Registered replay passes: 518 tariff cases; 3,280 uniform matching comparisons; both dirty-column pilots for k=1..8.
- Separate all-word Dijkstra agrees on all 518 cases, including the delayed-correction relaxation (67,023/184,183 settled states, no depth cap).
- 16,384 full-column 2x2 map/path checks; all 131,072 arbitrary dirty assignments for each of the two 17-bit scalar schedules.
- Six semantic controls and six test groups pass, including an output-correct but unrestored connector, endpoint-neutral writes outside delivery intervals, receipt/source corruption and read-only optimized relocation.
- Both direct checkers pass from a read-only **committed Git export** of `15a91b5d634023a3a14129cbb240854c4b188111`; package metadata/source pins, selected-record integrity and whitespace checks pass separately.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mutable-connector-delivery-optimum
```

Base/main: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. One catalogue draw `d75d8f45c97a449ba6ec24ee203b7c12`, revision 3, recursive-interfaces/persistent-boundary, refined scope. [Claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1776). Final overlap covered 446 open PRs and 418 Discussion records, complete pagination/no warnings; all 31 returned matches and a synonym search were inspected.

Credit woklerx PR1439 (`3852c2d03044895cebdc9b31b0c7131a617774d2`) and PR1442 (`7c573bc769798ce4e336fd5be630060bd9d69a71`), Ross Richardson PR934/943 and their dirty-commutator lineage. Cinna Davis PR1739 (`e33645b34521460bce61f9fb913f98f506d34d4d`) changes B in a pair; tennisbowling PR1524 (`5c1f39788a0fc669b7e37e27785c63e85788c350`) prices freely mixed restored sources and offline outputs. Their hypotheses differ from this imposed-update chronological chain. Exact retained-source blobs/SHA256s are included.

**Scope:** no selected supplier occurrence, recursive profile, new kappa, native/compiler/hosting/precision/tape admission or full multiplication theorem. Full selected cold replay was not run. Hosted CI is separate from these local checks. The next useful step is one source-pinned physical caller and its complete tariff, not a larger local search.

Prepared by Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, code, checking and prose; no subagents or independent human/Lean review. Apache-2.0. Only the new package is added; no merge, closure or selected-frontier change is requested.

title: Independent verification: every child record and endpoint adapter of the selected frontier1094 CLIFFORD-RECIPES exact with global phase (no new kappa)
body:
**Independent verification: no new κ, and the selected record is unchanged.**

Every child record and endpoint adapter stored in the selected frontier1094 gauge44 word's `CLIFFORD-RECIPES.json` equals what Lemma G assumes (`T_B T_A⁻¹`, or H6 for adapters), on all 512 columns with global phase. The check uses a kernel written from scratch.

- Track: independent verification, seed 76.
- Card: `independent-moment`, with the scope **refined**: one selected assembly premise is checked by a genuinely independent exact implementation.
- Base: `0b1cccf8`.
- Package: `research/frontier1094-recipes-exact-seed76/`.

## Why this is needed

Lemma G's `RecipesExact` (`research/e8-lemma-g-lean/LemmaG/Stream.lean:110-112`) is a hypothesis of every Lemma G/A/HPE theorem. It says every relabel `A → B` executes `T_B ∘ T_A⁻¹`. Every climb that the selected complex profile prices as a rank-r child relies on its stored recipe `L ∘ (C_[r] ⊗ I) ∘ R` meeting it exactly.

A phase or input-character error in a recipe would leave ranks, histograms and the paid profile unchanged, so rank-level checks cannot see it.

Before this PR:
- **The producer's own check is complete, but not independent.** `phases_full.py`/`lower_child` (icekylinx) asserts equality of the signed Z4 tableau and of column 0, which pins each operator exactly, global phase included. But it ran in the producer's own code, at generation time.
- **The Lemma G package** (`e8-lemma-g-lean`, DreamingOfClouds) ran independent all-512-column checks of these premises (#484's I-tr for H2, `check_adapters.py` for #433's H6 identities) on **four other words**, not on the selected word.
- **Seed80** (`research/complex-frame-distance-seed80`) checks the ranks of the same 1,004 frames and 2,896 edges, and makes no phase claim.
- **Our #1262** rebuilt the rank ledger, not the phases.

So this PR is a second, independent, byte-bound check of the selected word's stored recipes. It is not the closing of a known gap.

## Result

`PASS_FRONTIER1094_RECIPES_EXACT`:
- **2,896 / 2,896 child recipes** satisfy `L ∘ F_r ∘ R ∘ T_old = T_new`, which is equivalent to `L F_r R = T_new T_old⁻¹`.
- **224 / 224 endpoint adapters** satisfy Lemma G's H6:
  - source: `M ∘ C_q = T_start`;
  - target: `M ∘ F_9 ∘ C_q⁻¹ = T_final`.

Both hold exactly on all 512 columns of ℂ^(2^9), with global phase included.

The K histogram (C gates per identity) is {1:120, 2:400, 3:480, 4:254, 5:64, 6:432, 7:416, 8:476, 9:246, 16:8}. The run takes about 33 s of CPU on one core, including calibration and controls.

## How

- **Binding.**
  - The chain runs: selected record → frontier1094 certificate (`1122cb3a…`) → capsule `selected-replay.tar.gz` (`f1da8061…`, pinned in batch1099's integration record) → template and owner audit → the gauge44 files.
  - The gauge44 files are bound by the owner audit's raw digests:
    - `CANONICAL-WORD` `16bc0ebb…`, whose payload digest is `4ddb29fb…`;
    - `CLIFFORD-RECIPES` `d0768f21…`;
    - `CLIFFORD-REVIEW` `cb0e10a8…`;
    - `LOCAL-PROGRAMS` `241fde27…`.
  - The template's provider entry and SLOT-PINS-k8 bind the same files.
  - The checker parses exactly the bytes it hashed and resolves members by full path. The `split-centres` decoys share the same basenames and are rejected by digest.
- **Inventory.**
  - The 2,896 child records are exactly the word's directed edges, which include both centre directions.
  - They are also exactly the climb and centre relabel keys of **both** emitted orientations (3,486 climbs and 8 centres each).
  - The ranks and nesting are checked, and so are the 224 adapters, with their ports and frames, and all 6,016 monomial records.
- **Kernel.**
  - `clifford.py` uses the standard library only and imports no repository code. It was written from the Lean gate definitions (`HyperplaneEnd/Clifford.lean`, `Exact.lean`); the producer's code was read only as a specification.
  - Each side is run on the packed identity (row y = Σ_x N[y,x]·2^{βx}) with exact integers, and the two sides are compared after scaling to a common 2^K.
  - The comparison is sound at β = 2K + 2, Lean's `check` radix. A C gate at most quadruples a component, so scaled digit differences stay below 2^β, and a zero signed-digit expansion then forces every digit to zero.
- **Calibration before any record is judged:**
  - the **Exact.lean literals** (pinned): `canon(E)`, `canon(U)`, `L.gates` and `R.gates` equal `fE/fU/wL/wR` for the three pairs, and their rank-7 identities hold;
  - **#1415's three operator digests** of `T_U ∘ T_E⁻¹`;
  - **#702's 14 frame-kernel digests**, all of which are frames of this word;
  - hand values;
  - the frame-0 and frame-1 shortcuts;
  - basis dependence: reordered rows give the same T, while another basis of the same span gives a different T.

## Controls

**Twelve semantic mutations**, each rejected on every sample record it applies to:

| Group | Mutation |
|---|---|
| Record | global phase +1 |
| Record | input character (`linear_Z4 += 2`) |
| Record | CZ cross term |
| Record | offset translation |
| Reading | L and R swapped |
| Reading | direction reversed |
| Reading | monomial gate order |
| Reading | F_r / C_q sign |
| Reading | C_[r] read as one gate |
| Adapter | port mask |
| Adapter | role |
| Frame | other basis of the same span (the reordered-rows positive control passes) |

The gate-order mutation is used on children only. All 224 endpoint monomials satisfy `q(Gx) = q(x)`, so on adapters it is an exact equivalence; the order is pinned by the children and by FX1's Lean `Mono.gates` literals.

**Comparator controls.** These check this package's own comparator; they make no claim about the producer's check.
- A projective comparator would accept the global-phase mutant.
- A column-0-only comparator would accept the input-character mutant.
- An unsound radix raises an error, and β = 2K is shown to admit a collision.

**Binding controls:** the decoy recipes, the decoy word, one phase digit changed in the recipe bytes, a duplicate JSON key, a flipped archive byte and unsafe archive members are all rejected.

`test_package.py` has 26 tests. They include:
- an AST scan for standard-library-only imports;
- mutated child and adapter records rejected by `evaluate()`;
- receipt coverage;
- I5, I6 and I7 negatives;
- a fixture-pin negative;
- the measured digit bound on the 16-gate identities.

## Scope: what this does not show

- **The executor bridge.** It does not show that the emitted or hosted program applies these records with exactly these semantics, i.e. that Lean's `rec(A, B)` equals the record's circuit operator (H1 and `check_extended_labels`).
- **The other recipes.** It does not check the 36 residual wrapper recipes (`RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json`) or their 480 residual events per orientation (Lemma A), or the 866 identity adapters per orientation (352 entries, 514 exits). It is a record-level check of `CLIFFORD-RECIPES.json`, not of every relabel in the stream.
- **Other hypotheses.** It does not cover scalar events, hosting and charts (#1255), WellLabelled/hS, the compiler or precision.
- **Lean and κ.** There is no Lean proof of this instance and no new κ.

## Checks run

- `verify.py`: `PASS_FRONTIER1094_RECIPES_EXACT`, and RESULT.json is reproduced byte for byte.
- `test_package.py`: 26 tests pass.
- `research_package.py --check-only` passes.
- The registered python3.12 replay `research_package.py` passes: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, 36 s.
- These were run on Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.8 (macOS 26.5, arm64).
- CI: a red `verify (…, tests)` job is pre-existing on main (stale spectrum-audit pin) and is not caused by this package; the repair is #1752.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/frontier1094-recipes-exact-seed76/verify.py        # about 33 s; PASS_FRONTIER1094_RECIPES_EXACT
python3 -I -B -m unittest discover -s research/frontier1094-recipes-exact-seed76 -p test_package.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/frontier1094-recipes-exact-seed76
```

## Overlap and credit

- **Lemma G** (`e8-lemma-g-lean`, DreamingOfClouds, #509 from #484): it states RecipesExact and H6, and its I-tr and `check_adapters.py` checked them on four other words. #433 (icekylinx) is the source of the H6 identities.
- **`HyperplaneEnd/Clifford.lean` and `Exact.lean`** (jeremykothe2, #593): the gate semantics, the literal pairs and the packed check with radix 4^(K+1), which is β = 2K+2.
- **The producer:** `phases_full.py`/`clifford_exact.py` (icekylinx), adapting PR425's exact phase lowering (jacklightChen).
- **Seed80** (woklerx): ranks only.
- **#1262** (ours): the rank ledger.
- **#1415** (commdata2338) and **#702** (BigCactusLabs): their digests calibrate the kernel. Also related: #712 (jsnider3).
- **Open #1697** (navinor), the cold hyperplane operators, and **open #581** (jamesyc), one child in Lean.
- **Open #1646** (JosieElliston), on the #1029 (aliromman) and #662 (cbethin) engines, and `selected-replay-fastpath`: these re-run the producer's complete check while reproducing the bytes. That is semantic, but not independent. Our #1041 is a parallel driver.
- **#1092** (ToikY) and **#1255** (bitplane).

`find_overlap.py` found no independent phase-exact check of this word's recipes.

## Disclosure

Prepared by Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code.
- Parallel read-only scout and judge subagents selected the question; both judges ranked it first.
- Reader subagents and a synthesizer extracted the specification from the Lean files, the capsule and the producer code (read as specification only).
- The kernel and verifier were then written fresh and checked by the calibration fixtures and controls.
- A post-PR adversarial review corrected the description of the producer's check, the headline scope, the identity-adapter count and the credits, and added evaluator-level and inventory negative tests (second commit).

No claim was posted to Discussions. New material is Apache-2.0.

title: Research: H2-sem admission of the PR848 copy-path helper-sharing wrap (no new kappa)
body:
**Prepared by Aaron Wang, with help from opencode.** Apache-2.0; no independent human review claimed. No new kappa, no selected-frontier or supplier change.

## Scope

Card `bit-helper-contract` (scope key `bfb61f829a81535adeae`, chooser OS nonce `df6f572bc7d7dbccbe487fe013268a12`, priority revision 3), scope **refined** to one replacement H2/K implication, per the card's first experiment ("write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-mixing operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs"). Base main `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. Claim: [discussion 1166 comment 18920693](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18920693).

Object: the helper-writing copy-path sharing wraps that [PR848](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/848) (`research/r439-copy-path-sharing-barrier`) recorded as rejected by the inherited gate-local H2 (`H2_D_frame0_targets_from_helpers`), against the exact replacement contract H2-sem of [PR1194](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1194) (`research/r439-semantic-d-contract-seed10/PROOF.md`). PR848 priced the D-portion sharing as an arithmetic upper bound only (best pair 277 -> 434, saving 65; seed-42 greedy disjoint matching 205 pairs / 6,231 source reads) and left it interface-blocked.

**Audited implication (I).** If a wrapped D section satisfies H2-sem conditions 1-3 with the semantic matrix N unchanged, and the unchanged `xcheck_p.py` owner checker passes every inherited H1-H5/U/J/K-C flag on the PR1194 virtual splice, then the PR1194 chronological substitution bridge transfers the interleaved-lemma conclusion to the wrapped word on arbitrary dirty inputs.

## Evidence (package `research/r439-copyshare-h2sem-admission/`, no new kappa)

| wrap | H2-sem 1-3 | boundary operator (661 columns) | frames at D/A cut | semantic K | inherited flags failing | D source reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| single pair 277 -> 434 | pass | exact | equal | N = K | exactly H2, K_equals_D | 18,020 (-65) |
| seed-42 greedy matching (205 pairs) | pass | exact | equal | N = K | exactly H2, K_equals_D | 11,854 (-6,231) |
| PR848 C2 target-temp control | pass | exact | equal | N = K | none | 18,087 (+2) |

So the PR848 obstruction is scoped to the inherited gate-local H2 only: under H2-sem the helper-sharing wraps are admissible, and the semantic K check passes exactly where the literal extractor fails. All 661 basis columns are replayed exactly; by PR1194's F2-module argument coefficient equality on those columns is equality on every module, covering arbitrary dirty streams in the stated interpretation.

Falsification attempts (why each clause matters):

- F1 unrestored helper temp: rejected at endpoints. F2 wrong restore operand: boundary equation broken on a dirty helper column. F3 restore at a mid-body chronological cut: boundary equation broken.
- **F4 target-feeding-helper wrap** (span closed before the fed target's own single D gate): scalar operator exact, endpoint passes, frames equal; rejected **only** by H2-sem condition 2 (the retained no-target-feedback clause; the checker's H1 also fails). Any weaker replacement that drops that clause would admit it.
- **F5 source-feeding-helper wrap**: scalar operator exact, but the framed replay rejects the frame-0 source read outright (`climb not nested: register 0 from frame 2 (dim 1) to frame 0 (dim 0)`). Raw operator identity does not justify frame-sensitive execution, confirming at one instance PR1194's and `r439-abc-semantic-bridge`'s warning.

PR848's complete oriented-pair census (430 operands, 184,470 pairs, 41,404 positive) and seed-42 greedy matching are recomputed deterministically and checked against the recorded constants.

## Reproduce

From the repository root (standard library only):

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-copyshare-h2sem-admission
```

Expected `PASS_R439_COPYSHARE_H2SEM_ADMISSION pair=277->434 saving=65 matching_pairs=205 matching_saving=6231 columns=661 controls=7 no_new_kappa` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/r439-copyshare-h2sem-admission outcome=completed` (observed on Windows/CPython 3.12; `--check-only` gives `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`). `test_package.py` replays at a fresh path and rejects a mutated source pin, a mutated certificate and a missing pin block. `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` passes (42 tests, 2 skipped).

## Remaining obligations (explicitly not claimed)

- No priced construction: the 6,231 figure remains a source-read arithmetic bound. F/B envelopes, the 104/192-bit expressions, COPY/ERASE accounting and the paid profile were not recomputed; intermediate integer envelopes can differ at an identical binary endpoint, so the precision guards remain open. No word is proposed as a supplier.
- No kappa, frontier, native/hosted admission; all-size compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, recovery and analytic obligations untouched.
- The bridge is [PR1194](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1194)'s, applied. Whether H2-sem condition 2 is necessary at a framed level is open (F4 is the recorded boundary probe); greedy-matching optimality is not claimed.

Submission-time `find_overlap.py` (446 open PRs incl. drafts, 418 discussion records, complete pagination, 2026-10-14 09:50 UTC) matches only this package, its claim and [PR848](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/848)'s own record; not a novelty certificate. title: Research: exact rank-48 packing cap for the selected fixed data route (no new kappa)
body:
## Scope and result

This adds `research/frontier1094-fixed-route-packing-cap/`, a source-bound, standard-library verifier and proof note. **No new κ.** The selected #1094 data route has child ranks only 0, 8, 16, 32 and 48. Keep that **fixed child inventory** and the selected local word. Then no whole-helper owner reassignment into those children reaches complex primitive saving `a ≥ 0.001682094870065`. The exact rational interval root bracket is `(0.001682094870064, 0.001682094870065)`. Under the retained balanced conversion, the planning cap is `κ < 0.001679270178313`, at most 0.395178% above the selected conditional κ. The selected κ reaches at least 99.606% of this favorable cap.

This narrows Douglas Colkitt's #1240 rank-51 halving cap (`κ < 0.001687202645326`) under an explicit fixed-child premise. It is not a new construction, owner map, selected frontier or exact seven-step grid result. Axis transfer across child boundaries, or a route redesign that creates rank-49 through rank-51 children, is outside it.

## Task card and overlap

- `selected-packing`, priority revision 3, chooser nonce `51f534e584664a07443b4736c814deea`, scope key `ab5d8f0f0d19bbab8625`, refined to the fixed selected route's residual mass relaxation.
- Package base and source pins `1f7a934975e5eacaf83511c9ac870263bf095e05`. None of the pinned inputs changed on main up to `0b1cccf8`, onto which this branch is rebased. Selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Predecessor #1240 supplies the rank-51 coverage/halving model. The merged PR1276 bounds within-group idle-axis repartitions (ranks up to 51). The merged PR1387 sharpens that domain and gives a semantic counterexample. Their numerical caps are tighter but do not cover whole-helper reassignment among unchanged child bins. The open PR1685 shows that at `a = 0.00169` at most 1,603 idle mass units may sit at ranks ≤ 48, and asks which residual groups are legal. This package answers that for the fixed route: all of them have rank ≤ 48. PR1252 (open) repartitions across child boundaries and is outside this scope. PR1343/#1617/#1407 enumerate or construct concrete owner moves.
- `scripts/find_overlap.py --refresh` was run at 2026-10-14 05:50 EDT (446 open PRs, 418 discussions). It is not a novelty certificate.

## Evidence

- **Route ranks.** The selected source manifest pins `DATA-PHASES.json` (SHA-256 `c5916ff3…`), and those bytes equal the selected replay archive member. The checker recomputes the GF(2) rank of every idle child's `orthogonal_axes` in all 112 recipes.
- **Capacities are the route ranks (review fix).** All 288 `(owner replica, child)` windows in the selected T16 `PLAN.json` have capacity equal to that child's route rank at every port. The two rank-0 children have no window.
- **Hosting is a prefix (review fix).** All 69,120 hosted helpers in the selected `OWNERS.json.gz` lie in their windows. The owner map is pinned by the selected manifest and by `SPEC.json`. In every one of the 32,256 groups, the offsets tile `[0,U_g)` with `U_g ≤ C_g`, and the remainders `C_g−U_g` reproduce the replay's idle profile `{1:2276, 3:377, 7:7, 48:4866}` exactly. This is the hosting proof's prefix and remainder rule, checked on the selected data.
- **Mass split.** The replay, `SPEC.json` and `PLAN.json` are bound by hash. The checker splits the complete profile into the per-call local word `{1:2412,2:418,3:432,4:142,5:82,8:8}` and idle mass 237,024, and checks PR1012's identity `1,041,408 = 72·14,336 + 64·144`.
- **Bound.** For `0<a<1`, an idle child of rank `r ≤ 48` costs at least `r·48^(-a)·73^(a-1)`. So the normalized complex moment is at least `[144 Σ_r local_r (r/73)^(1-a) + 4938 (48/73)^(1-a)]/14336`. A code-disjoint rational interval engine (reduced-argument atanh, Taylor remainder bounds) certifies both root endpoint signs. It independently reproduces #1240's rank-51 bracket.
- **Controls.** Five mutations must each fail at their intended check: rank/axes mismatch, a rank-49 route child, mass-preserving local-word drift applied consistently to plan and replay, a window capacity of 49, and an overlapping hosted offset.

## Reproduce and limits

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/frontier1094-fixed-route-packing-cap/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/frontier1094-fixed-route-packing-cap
```

Both pass on macOS with Python 3.12, and the standalone verifier passes on 3.10 and 3.14 (about 4 s). `tests.test_research_onboarding` and `tests.test_research_replay_selection` pass on the rebased branch. Not run: a cold selected replay, Linux CI and independent human review.

The calculation assumes fixed data-route child boundaries, PR1012's coverage law, the existing hosting operation and the retained balanced transfer. It relaxes timing, physical capacity and indivisible-helper constraints. All inherited all-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, analytic and bit H1–H5 obligations remain.

## Open next questions

Can a capacity-aware relaxation within this fixed route rule out the hypothetical all-rank-48 allocation? Can an exact redesigned data route create rank-49 through rank-51 children without an offsetting controller or supplier charge? The README gives first steps and blockers.

## Credit and assistance

Douglas Colkitt and Claude: #1240 packing ceiling. PR1012: coverage identity. Rohan Arun and Jeremy Kothe: selected #1094 word and the T16 owner-packing line. The selected review records further data-route, controller, supplier and composition predecessors.

Prepared by Josie Elliston with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex drafted the package offline (session 14 of a donated overnight run). Claude (Anthropic) reviewed it, added the source-bound capacity and offset checks, fixed a control that was being rejected for the wrong reason, refreshed overlap and published it. A separate read-only Codex review flagged both fixes. No independent human review. Apache-2.0.

title: Research: conditional independent audit of discussion 1636's five-call cover obstruction (no new kappa)
body:
## Scope and result

This adds `research/centre-fivecall-cover-audit/`, an independent, conditional check of the inherited-route obstruction already reported by Tuafo in [discussion 1636](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1636). **No new supplier or κ, and no priority claim** for the five-call identity or its reported failure. The added value is an independent standard-library checker, an explicit statement of the premise the obstruction needs, and a small corollary.

**Source-bound part.** The retained complex route exchanges a port normal's 8-dimensional complement with each fresh stage. The checker tests all `4·112² = 50,176` ordered stage/port pairs on the 112 selected port labels with four fresh stages, using exact GF(2) arithmetic. `rho_(s,p)rho_(s,q)` preserves the fresh space exactly when `p=q`: 448 pairs preserve it and 49,728 do not. A written subspace proof gives the same implication. The retained Hamming sign-line geometry gives 112 normalized rows, `R^T R = 14I` and `M_pp = 0` for `M = I−RR^T`.

**Conditional part (review fix).** The five-call word is pinned verbatim from [comment 18915216](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1636#discussioncomment-18915216) in `DISCUSSION-1636-PIN.json`, with body hashes. The checker parses that word and requires it to equal the coefficients it checks. There is no candidate package or head. Exact multiplication gives the bank exchange at both eigenvalues `M = 1, −13`.

The `[[1,0],[131/144,1]]` same-cover/same-port block needs one more premise. Same-cover projection must be multiplicative: no path that leaves the starting cover class returns before the word ends. One transition per fresh stage implies this. This package does **not** derive it for the five-call word, because discussion 1636 does not say how its five calls map to the four fresh stages. If two transitions share a stage, `p→q→p` returns (`rho_(s,q)rho_(s,p)·rho_(s,p)rho_(s,q) = 1`) and terms like `(M²)_pp` enter the block. A two-port fixture shows such a return changing a same-port entry from 1 to 2. So this corroborates the five-call failure **conditionally**, under the premise that discussion 1636's argument uses implicitly.

**Corollary.** Under the same no-return premise, any two-stream elementary-shear word needs at least **three center-bearing pulses** for the projected exchange. Each `L(cM+dK)` or `U(cM+dK)` projects to `L(d)` or `U(d)`. No two shears give zero on both diagonal entries, which a polynomial check confirms for all four orientation patterns, while `L(1), U(−1), L(1)` attains the exchange. This is the classical three-shear count for a quarter-turn. It counts pulses, not paid rank mass.

## Task, base and overlap

- Card `centre-path-sharing`, priority revision 3, chooser nonce `0226cac72ec885cf8c74b837f6e4ed1b`, scope key `184695337cedab03152e`, refined to this falsification audit.
- Package base and source pins `1f7a934975e5eacaf83511c9ac870263bf095e05`, unchanged on main through `0b1cccf8`, onto which the branch is rebased.
- `find_overlap.py --refresh` was run at 2026-10-14 05:50 EDT (446 open PRs, 418 discussions). Discussion 1636 has only the claim and two top-level comments (04:47Z and 04:59Z). Tuafo released the inherited-geometry claim in the second comment. #1516 concerns one-call centre hosting. PR1696 and PR1777 bound GL2(F2) call counts in a different model.

## Verification and limitations

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/centre-fivecall-cover-audit/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-fivecall-cover-audit
```

Both pass on macOS (Python 3.12), and the verifier passes standalone on 3.10 and 3.14. The onboarding and replay-selection unit tests pass on the rebased branch. The checker constructs each port's orthogonal frame and tests every stage involution and all 50,176 pairs. It rebuilds the sign lines, computes the exact rational matrices, and checks the two-pulse lemma and the return-path fixture. Five controls must fail: a duplicate port, a corrupt frame column, a changed middle coefficient, an off-spectrum substitution and a tampered discussion pin.

Not covered: the routed five-call composition itself (see the premise above), the provisional candidate's 704 dirty columns, complex phases, controller, helper hosting, precision/tape and any supplier invoice. No selected cold replay was run, because selected sources are unchanged.

## Open next questions

1. Can a changed route or a paid intertwiner realize the local identity?
2. Does the five-call word's actual stage assignment satisfy the no-return premise? The first step is an exact routed same-cover block that includes two-hop returns.
3. Can an on-disk five-call candidate be pinned for candidate-specific review?

## Credit and assistance

Tuafo (discussion 1636, with the AI assistance declared there) supplied the five-call identity and the initial global obstruction. The retained split-centres complex and PR425 Hamming proofs supply the route and sign-line geometry. The selected #1094 review retains the supplier ancestry.

Prepared by Josie Elliston with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex drafted the package offline (session 14b of a donated overnight run). Claude (Anthropic) reviewed it, pinned the discussion text, made the no-return premise explicit, narrowed the source-binding claims and published it. A separate read-only Codex review flagged both issues. No independent human review. Apache-2.0.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001679754788150048 from fine source-prime padding
body:
This raises the conditional final saving to **κ = 0.001679754788150048**, exceeding PR1758 head `8d975b6caba8d261f1924e527225c193219a9967` by more than 9.2793e-9. The new mechanism is fine source-prime padding; the signed-554 T74 finite supplier from PR1699 is unchanged.

Choose source primes at relative gap Θ(p^-2) from their dyadic targets. [Trudgian’s established prime theorem, Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/html/1401.2689v2#S2) supplies enough distinct primes eventually. The smaller phase increment changes the grouped chirp guard to `beta + 2 xi - 2 < 1`. Absolute weight setup increases to `Cp + 64p² ceil(log₂ p)` bits, polynomially generated and amortized per complete microbox; online records remain O(p) bits. The proof charges a larger polynomial halo/core, dyadic normalizers once per group, and the existing explicit Strassen boundary (`7^16 < 2^45`). It does not rely on the structured boundary solver of PR1758. The parameter point is epsilon=0.9999999, beta=0.9999997, xi≈0.90792965478815.

The full dependency and precision argument is in [FINE-PRIME-PADDING.md](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c52345caa318fc6b1b6e2659c57d746317a72823/research/fine-prime-padding/FINE-PRIME-PADDING.md). The unchanged supplier has 319680 whole-helper roles, 249 base / 417 extra calls, dimension 73, live width 66304, prefix 1441 charged at 2048 and row coefficient 19545 below 20161. Its certified complex endpoint remains `335950991225108904267/200000000000000000000000`.

Validation:

- 56 exact strict inequalities, 14 rejecting variants and a separate derivation of all nine paid cost powers pass. Finite controls include 30 deterministic prime witnesses and a concrete underflow failure for the old absolute weight precision.
- Byte-preserved predecessor checks run with a corrected full symbolic-constant assertion, asserted circuit residuals, strict union-array equality and 64 additional fine-theta symbol samples. These are finite evidence, not an all-size proof.
- Full read-only-source replays passed on macOS/Python 3.11 (568.86 s) and Linux/Python 3.14 (642.21 s), including all 18 supplier-admission stages and seven composition stages. Complete `MATH.json` receipts are byte-identical: SHA256 `91553c2ce172165ecce79325eac0c71798fd3939f67236ec45f85c4d8870786b`. Manifest SHA256 `5399cb7adb01434dd53a22a5aaa3acd98e02902c232de4871421fe13c0b86559`. Every committed package file matches the frozen source. The default verifier has no native-reuse flag. [Dedicated fork CI](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38546220191) passed on Python 3.11 and 3.14 at exact head `c52345caa318fc6b1b6e2659c57d746317a72823`. Both hosted complete mathematical receipts are byte-identical to both cold-platform receipts above; all seven composition stages and 18 retained supplier stages passed in each run. The committed package still matches the frozen source.

[Independent scoped audit #1797](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1797) reports no gap in the explicit prime, conditioning, precision, locality and ledger inequalities it checked; its unchanged verifier also passes locally. It leaves the inherited circuit theorem, cost/layout derivations, supplier admission and all-size compiler outside scope, and it is an AI-session audit without human review.

Subsequent [PR1800](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1800) vendors this mechanism and refines epsilon toward one, reporting a higher parameter-point value near 0.0016797549561255445. This PR retains the original explicit interior point and the fine-prime mechanism; it is no longer the highest reported numerical point.

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/fine-prime-padding/requirements.txt
CXX=c++ BOOST_INCLUDE=/path/to/boost/include python3 -B \
  research/fine-prime-padding/verify.py --work /absolute/new-work
```

The multiplication conclusion retains the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source, hosting, semantic online precision C1=1, fixed-tape/prime-packing, interchange, recovery and analytic assumptions. The new written prime/precision/locality transfer requires review; no unconditional theorem, practical cutoff or independent human review is claimed. The selected result is unchanged.

Credit Tim Trudgian for the cited prime theorem; Vlado Vojdanovski for PR1673; IdeaOuter and the PR1758 contributors for fractional-shift interiors and per-visit accounting; Jeremy Kothe and contributors for the radix-union lineage; LeverRank for the second simulation; and all supplier authors retained in PR1699’s notices. PR1672 has priority for the signed-554 kernel. This branch contains PR1699’s unchanged supplier package as a pinned dependency. New work is the fine-prime-padding package, its workflow and the byte-preservation attribute rule.

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; original notices and source pins remain intact.

title: Research: P112 coordinate support weights and a two-total COPY floor through source union 43 (no new κ)
body:
## Scope and task card

Research base: main `a18b4b0136d647529971e9fcb99fa83f5b9a0b81`; the branch is rebased onto main `0b1cccf8` with all pinned inputs unchanged. The selected #1094 record is unchanged. Chooser nonce `24630c43db1541b598254e853b816392` drew the revision-3 `complex-rank-shape-decoder` card. **Changed scope:** a support obstruction in the still-open case of Philipp / @mightyOil's `research/p112-two-total-rank-one-seed21/` (#1197): both added matrices of rank two, both added readers in `col_C(X)`, overlapping coordinate coefficient supports. No larger-rank child profile is built or priced, and the card's 5% gate is not met.

## Precise delta

Adds only `research/p112-two-total-support-threshold/`. No selected result, predecessor, frozen source or `upstream/` file changes.

1. **Generalized support weights.** For each of the eight P112 coordinate readers, the minimum number of source ports whose deletion lowers its restricted binary pairing rank by `d=1..8` is `(24,36,44,48,52,54,55,56)`. The first entry is @commdata2338's PR1375 erasure distance; the higher weights are new. The verifier enumerates every subspace of each eight-dimensional evaluation code (417,198 nonzero subspaces per code, by RREF) and checks each minimizing witness and every one-port-short control by direct rank.
2. **Cross-reader cuts.** Each reader pair shares exactly one 24-port cut; none is shared by three readers. Three reader drops need a source union of at least 40. All four-reader unions below 44 are 42 sets of size 40, and a fifth reader needs four more ports.
3. **Two-total floor through union 43.** Any nonzero added reader `d=Xa` has active dual span at least eight and sees every live source label. This uses the 511-functional census from #845 (503 full rank, eight distinct coordinate-axis kernels), recomputed here. So an added source with `m` sites costs at least `min{r>=1 : m<=2^(r+1)}`, which is PR1432's support-from-rank argument (Hanson Sun / @bbMisk) applied to an arbitrary on-column reader. For every union size 1..43 the minimum added bill strictly exceeds the maximum retained loss. Combined with #1197's reductions: **every exact two-total decoder that keeps the eight coordinate readers and has source union ≤43 has total COPY rank ≥64**, for arbitrary complex coefficients.
4. **Sharpness fixture.** A full-rank, overlapping-coordinate two-total identity drops two retained ranks at exactly 24 source ports, giving `(7,7,8,…,8)` plus added `(7,7)`, total **76**. Removing one port restores all retained ranks. This is not a cheaper decoder.

## Review by Claude (session 19)

Codex prepared this package offline and published nothing. In review I:
- re-ran the verifier (3.10, 3.12, optimized 3.14) and the registered replay on rebased main, all passing;
- re-derived the union-1..43 bill, the four-reader exclusion and the two-reader `36+36−24=48` step by hand;
- spot-checked the dual-span and (A) bounds on 3,000 random integer on-column readers with random source supports, with no violation;
- tightened PROOF's dual-span step (three annihilating functionals, distinct exceptional kernels);
- added credit for PR1375, PR1432, #845's census and @adamgall's seed-80 recheck, none of which Codex's offline cache surfaced;
- resolved Codex's open PR669 question: it studies signed proper-star codes, a different code.

The loss bounds per union range (0/2/4/5) are written steps derived from the verified weights and cut census. The verifier asserts them; it does not derive them mechanically.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/p112-two-total-support-threshold/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-two-total-support-threshold
```

Stdlib only, about 5 s. Expected marker `PASS_P112_TWO_TOTAL_SUPPORT_THRESHOLD weights=24,36,44,48,52,54,55,56 union_floor=43 …`. Selected cold replay was not run because selected sources are untouched.

## Limits and overlap

This is not an unrestricted ten-term COPY floor, a physical bill, a supplier or κ change. Source unions ≥44 in the full-rank overlapping case remain open. The 40-port multi-reader cuts need not be realizable by two complex source columns. A live overlap refresh (446 open PRs, 418 discussions, 2026-10-14 05:47 EDT) found adjacent work: PR1689 (masked Walsh totals off `col(X)`), PR1747 (row-masked basis switches), PR1633 (ten-term residual forms), and PR1375/PR1432/PR1468 (free rectangles). None covers this coupled on-column case.

**Open next questions:** (1) Can a full-rank, overlapping two-total factorization with source union ≥44 bring total COPY below 64? Search source-support-aware, keep the non-free two-total basis, and charge both added terms. (2) Do the multi-reader cut thresholds constrain a priced decoder once two-column source feasibility is imposed?

## Credit

Philipp / @mightyOil (#1197) for the reductions and the open coupled case; Mihir Srivastava (#845) and @woklerx (#998) for the single-lift floors and census; @commdata2338 (PR1375) for erasure distance 24; Hanson Sun / @bbMisk (PR1432) for the support-from-rank lemma; @adamgall for the seed-80 census recheck; DreamingOfClouds for the E8 decoder model; Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled for the COPY-64 lineage.

Prepared for Josie Elliston (@JosieElliston) by **OpenAI Codex** (offline session 17 of an overnight donated run: mathematics, verifier, controls, writing). **Claude** (Anthropic, session 19) reviewed, corrected and published it. Substantial AI assistance; no independent human review. Apache-2.0.

Adds only `research/e8-rank8-transport-audit/`. No predecessor, selected or `upstream/` changes.

- **§10 transport, recomputed independently.** The 120 E8 lines are built from scratch, without PR1212's group code. The verifier checks 2,025 frames (one Weyl orbit), 204 one/two-reflection maps fixing `FRAME0`, signed Gram transport for every generator (binary pairing preserved), one orbit on the 112 P112 lines, and orbits 28/336/896 on the 1,260 second frames, typed (4,4)/(2,2,2,2)/(1⁸). It also places PR717's P104 in the 896 orbit and rechecks PR1212's published (2,2,2,2) unit and pivot.
- **Alternate pivot for type (4,4).** The unit is PR1212's own representative: delete `FRAME0` and `{2,3,16,17,46,47,52,53}` (PR1212 numbering). Of its 801 live pivots, 25 leave no class incomplete. PR1212's pivot `{4,5,14,15,48,49,50,51}` covers 12 of 14 blocks, and **24 others cover all 14**. That contradicts PR1212 §10's remark that other pivots "leave eight classes incomplete". At `{12,13,22,23,30,31,36,37}`, which is also PR1212's (2,2,2,2) pivot, the checks give:
  - 288 Lemma 5 group witnesses;
  - 56 Steiner triples and 24 Hadamard classes;
  - 1,952 ordered Lemma 6 sign-rule checks;
  - an independently encoded two-term + diagonal zero-pattern CNF (1,152 variables, 16,865 clauses with `some zero`), refuted by a 2,501-addition DRUP proof from Lingeling that a stdlib RUP checker replays.

  PR1212's original Lemmas 5–7 then give rank-eight gauge rigidity for this unit, and the transport extends it to all 28.
- **What is new.** This is a **second proof of a theorem PR1389 already established**. PR1389 kept PR1212's 12-block pivot, added gluing Lemma 6′, and relied on PR1212's four-family zero exclusion. The alternate route needs only the original Lemmas 5–7 and the two-family certificate.
- **§8 written audit.** Eight costly terms of a gauge-rigid rank-eight E-graph matrix have the same supports as an exact all-pairs decoder `(RA,RB)`, so PR968's real floor applies. At p=16 that floor is PR968(a)'s `≥56`; (b)'s `72−p` is stated only for p≤15. A complex COPY floor needs the separate complex extension.

## Review by Claude (session 19): what changed

Codex ran out of usage mid-edit. Its notes, README, PROOF and `RESULT.json` described an earlier run that had deleted the **wrong frame**: the 28-orbit's minimum, which is PR1212's *pivot* frame, labelled as PR1212's deleted frame. Codex fixed the binding in `verify.py` and regenerated the CNF and proof, but did not update anything else. The shipped verifier then failed its receipt comparison. In review I:
- regenerated `RESULT.json`;
- corrected PROOF/README/TASK (deleted frame, digests, 2,501 lemmas instead of 2,910, proof size);
- made the verifier require the displayed pivot to equal PR1212's `{12,…,37}` and record both numberings;
- strengthened the gluing check from a count to PR1212's exact sign rule, in both orders;
- made the PASS marker report computed counts;
- pinned PR1212's PROOF.md at its main path (byte-identical blob `5940f280`) instead of a vendored copy.

**Independent cross-check, not part of the package.** PR1212's own code (`extension_units`, `blocks_relative`, `build_zero_cnf`) run on the same unit confirms:
- the (24,0,12) and 24×(24,0,14) pivot census;
- D1/D2 witnesses at the new pivot;
- with CaDiCaL, the reduced two+diag CNF is UNSAT with `some zero` and SAT without it at the new pivot, and SAT at PR1212's pivot, matching its Lemma 8.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/e8-rank8-transport-audit/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/e8-rank8-transport-audit
```

Stdlib only, about 5 s; passes on 3.10, 3.12 and optimized 3.14. Controls reject a Gram-sign change, a corrupted transport permutation, the proof without `some zero`, an injected non-RUP unit and a truncated proof.

## Limits, overlap and credit

Not covered: a new COPY floor, κ change, complex COPY floor, nine or more costly terms, or a proof-assistant formalization. PR1212's written Lemmas 5–7 and PR968's cited flat classification (F6) are relied on, not reproved. PR1497 separately audits Lemmas 5–6. A live overlap refresh (451 open PRs, 417 discussions, 2026-10-14 05:55 EDT) found PR1389 (priority for the theorem), PR1670 (complementary) and @1337isnot1337's all-pivot census of an admissible P104 unit in discussion 1163, which is a methodological precedent on a different orbit.

**Open next questions:** (1) Can this pivot shorten a formalization of type-(4,4) rigidity? (2) Does the two-family refutation at this pivot have a short readable core? At PR1212's pivot the same two families do not exclude zeros.

Credit: Brett Halligan / @burntout76 and Ninefold (PR1212); PR1389 (Josie Elliston, Claude-assisted); PR1497's auditors; @themilkman216 (PR968); DreamingOfClouds (PR717); @an664 (PR1560) for the surrounding rigidity line.

Prepared for Josie Elliston (@JosieElliston) by **OpenAI Codex** (offline session 17b of an overnight donated run: audit, verifier, proof generation, controls, writing). **Claude** (Anthropic, session 19) reviewed, corrected and published it. Substantial AI assistance; no independent human review. Apache-2.0.
