title: Dirty-host gauge binding: entry/exit gauges and credit <= H_end for hosted pending factors
body:
## Result

Scoped interface receipt, no kappa claim: **what a hosted pending factor may claim credit for**. It answers the explicit open request in the handoffs thread (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18916098) and open next questions 1-2 of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1664 (`research/dirty-host-cutrank-audit/`): bind a hosted residual's claimed credit to exact host entry/exit gauges and to the history-span endpoint term `H_end`, on the smallest complete instances.

Package: `research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e/`. The model is PR 1664's scalar common-frame transport model (its PROOF.md sections 4-5) applied to the idle-axis hosted-residual mechanism (`research/idle-axis-hosting/PROOF.md`).

**Finding 1 (operator gauges, exact; sufficient hypotheses).** The hosting move leaves the complete operator unchanged whenever the moved factor is the advance's own factor on the hosted block `S'`, no touch of the host occurs strictly between the residual application and the advance (more generally, every such touch commutes with the moved factor), and hosted blocks are disjoint (each useful pending factor counted once). These are sufficient legality hypotheses of the inherited hosting interface, not a necessary condition for operator equality, and no necessity claim is proved for any class. Exact 3x3 counterexample over Q (`R = I + E01`, `T = I + E12`, `T^{-1} = I - E12`; regression control `cancellation-equality-not-rejected` in `verify.py`): both `T` and `T^{-1}` fail to commute with `R`, yet `T^{-1} T R = R T^{-1} T = R`, so cancellation-based routes remain open and are not closed by this receipt. Each dropped gauge still has a smallest counterexample as composed linear maps (3x3 shears): escaping block, a single out-of-window non-commuting touch, exhibited overlapping order-dependent blocks; these show the hypotheses cannot simply be deleted, not that any of them is necessary. The tiny cut examples (including the 156 regions below) and the selected no-touch hosting rule remain valid as they stand. Wording corrected after review comment https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1837#issuecomment-6173237648.

**Finding 2 (credit binding, smallest complete instances first).** With hosts restored and the clean scatter `Y' = Y + S X` demanded at height 0 (PR 1664 section 5.1's contract), the exact per-cut demand identity `sum_j need_j = q*rank(S) + H_end` holds on **all 156 enumerated tiny regions** (every binary `t x m` scatter matrix, `m,t <= 2`, `w <= 2`, host motions `(a,b)` in `{(1,0),(2,0),(2,1)}`). The smallest double-duty borrow (one host row `d` descending `1 -> 0` carrying `d+x` while both `y'=y+x` and a restored `d` are demanded) is refuted at cut 1 by exactly one direction, both by the count (`D_j = 1 < 2`) and by span feasibility. So a hosted factor's creditable mass is exactly its host's displacement `H_end`: the scatter term cannot be hosted away while hosts are restored, and the double-credit loop is the smallest refuted instance. This instantiates PR 1664's "show that the claimed hosting credit is `H_end`" affirmatively for the toy class.

**Finding 3 (the only free route is a contract change).** A host crossing may deliver a hosted direction at zero extra mass only if the host's own prescribed endpoint absorbs that direction and no separate target or restoration demand survives — i.e. only by dropping PR 1664's clean-scatter/restoration obligations, an endpoint-contract change that must be charged against the data endpoint. That is the precise accounting interface between "hosting credit" and "unpaid coordinate", the quantity the coverage-law line (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587) changes. A pre-positioned copy of the host dirt below the cut earns no credit (PR 1664 section 7 instantiated as a machine check).

## Evidence and reproduction

```sh
python3.12 -B research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e
```

All three pass locally (Python 3.12.14, stdlib only); the registered replay ends `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e outcome=completed`. Exact rational arithmetic throughout; entry rows are an identity basis, so row equality covers arbitrary dirty inputs by linearity. Smallest falsifying instances run first, with three gauge failure controls, a PR1664 section 5.2 canonical-arithmetic fixture (M=8 = `H_end + q*r`) and an M<=6 mutant that is refused.

Also run and passing: `python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` (42 tests OK, including the metadata/pin checks).

## Scope, limits, obligations

- Track `recursive-interfaces`, card `persistent-boundary`, **scope changed** (reason in `TASK.json`): the drawn consecutive dirty-connector object is covered by open concurrent https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1739 and the adjacent-call centre-fanout claim in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1516 (2026-10-14T11:11Z); this takes the handoff request instead, keeping the card's method-2 shape (a lower bound on the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface). Claim/receipt: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18922678.
- Not established: bank-tile physics (the eliminated bank write/clear mass is not modeled; credit is compared through the shape `w*|a-b|` per host row), wrappers/spectators/gauge charts (PR 1664's non-nested-frame warning stays open here), physical and production admission, any selected-word application (including the separate 88-by-8 scatter receipt), and any kappa, supplier or frontier change. Finite toy checks do not certify the universal written statements of PR 1664 or idle-axis hosting. The whole-construction budget and the `a < D/E` diagnostic are not applicable to an interface receipt.
- Workflow friction on this host: `make` is not installed, so `make selected-record-check` / `make frontier1094-verify` were not run; the selected-record pin is instead validated inside `research_package.py --check-only`.

## Credit

Prepared by **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance, disclosed in `TASK.json`).

Predecessors (read, not modified): Andrey Mas / an664's https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1664 (`research/dirty-host-cutrank-audit/`, including its GPT-6 Pro review) and the handoff https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18916098; ctoth's dirty-host implication and branching-tree bound in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1516; DaysSky's `research/idle-axis-hosting`; and the lineage recorded in PR 1664's SOURCES.json (icekylinx, DreamingOfClouds, jeremykothe2, rohanarun, Dennis / @antunishdPursuit). No merge or frontier change is requested.

- Add an exact local construction for two same-frame bilinear centers `F` and `F+H` when `H` has rank one: route the `rank(F)` atoms to both dirty output panels, then evaluate the correction once. If each center separately has rank `r`, the paired map has rank at most `r+1` rather than `2r` in the common-frame bilinear-rank model.

title: [Lean] Verify sequential XOR machines with exact time and space bounds
body:
## Result and coverage

Author-checked pinned context: upstream main 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea, kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918. This package changes no numerical bound.

Two reusable finite-word XOR implementations have checked first-halt and restoration properties:
- Boundary-observing zipper model: exactly 5n+2 transitions.
- Explicit seven-symbol marked tape: exactly 5n+4 transitions, including entry, rewind and marker handling. The controller observes the current symbol. Every prefix occupies n+2 cells, including both markers.

Finite coverage: arbitrary finite paired Boolean words, without selected literal tables.

title: Implement eight-child identity transfers and centre-query codes
body:
This construction changes the historical complex supplier's local target operation from `X-JY` to the exact subtraction **`X-Y`**, while an invertible source code stores the full eight-coordinate centre query in eight existing fields. A forward companion performs `(G^-1X,Y+G^-1X)`. Each complete word restores all 480 arbitrary helpers and adds **eight rank-one native children and no array field**.

**The complete kappa bound is unchanged.** This is a local construction and an enabling theorem. It resolves the identity-target and full-query encoding requirements at the actual native cuts. A complete supplier must still close the changing-chart controller, remove the source code, and pay all address, precision, storage, hosting, and recursive costs.

Evidence: [ordered proof and scope](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bb29ea73ad9be9a0c3d53cdcb1d22b2ee9ffe42f/research/native-source-codes/UNIT-TRANSFER-PROOF.md), [exact certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bb29ea73ad9be9a0c3d53cdcb1d22b2ee9ffe42f/research/native-source-codes/unit-transfer-certificate.json), [cold replay receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bb29ea73ad9be9a0c3d53cdcb1d22b2ee9ffe42f/research/native-source-codes/evidence/UNIT-TRANSFER-REPLAY.json), and [independent package review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bb29ea73ad9be9a0c3d53cdcb1d22b2ee9ffe42f/research/native-source-codes/UNIT-TRANSFER-REVIEW.md).

For `J=I-KR`, the theorem assumes `RP=LK=I` and `LP=0` over a unital coefficient ring. With ordered products,

```text
Z=K-P(RK-I), Q=R-L,
G=(I-PL)(I+ZQ), G^-1=I+PL-ZR,
LG=R, RG=Q, JG-I=-P[R+(RK-I)Q], G^6=I.
```

The target correction is supported on P. The source code fixes a 96-dimensional complement and rotates two eight-dimensional sections with matrix `[[0,-I],[I,I]]`. No inverse of 13, scalar Gram assumption, or commutation assumption is used. Order six applies to a fixed chart; products of changing charts need not have order six.

For the actual dyadic supplier, a modulo-13 rank argument proves that every identity-target preparation needs at least eight target repair rows. The construction attains eight. This optimum covers the stated source-preparation/target-row interface, not arbitrary native circuits. The proof also gives a conditional full-query transport law between compatible selected-coordinate routes, without inverting the cross-chart query matrix. Full source restoration does not follow from that law.

| Complete word | Data map | Scalar allowance |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Backward | `(X-Y,GY)` | 217898 |
| Forward | `(G^-1X,Y+G^-1X)` | 217898 |

Both words have complete original-rank profile `{1:2420,2:418,3:432,4:142,5:82}`, of mass 5530 versus retained mass 5522. Each uses 16 explicit address maps for its eight new children. The scalar total is `202138+9056+6704`; it counts real primitives per array coordinate and is not a full recursive or precision bill. All eight owned private outputs are zero. The new work uses only existing C0. These words are companions, not inverse calls.

The [four original source-group examples](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bb29ea73ad9be9a0c3d53cdcb1d22b2ee9ffe42f/research/native-source-codes/PROOF.md) remain byte-exact and are replayed in the same command. Their complete scalar allowances remain 218794, 218794, 222846, and 225794. They preserve the clean-J target while changing the source.

The exact base is [`bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f). Inputs come from the frozen [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042) [source archive](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f/research/community-frontier1042-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz), also used by the historical [PR #1094](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094) assembly. This PR does not require an unmerged PR implementation.

With Python 3.10 or later, Git, and that base object in the local database, run from the repository root with a new output directory:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/native-source-codes/replay_unit_transfers.py \
  --repo . --out /tmp/native-unit-transfer-review
```

```text
PASS_UNIT_TRANSFER_EXTENSION
Four published examples and both unit transfers passed all 712 formal input columns.
The eight positive and eight inverse native recipes passed all 8192 Gaussian columns.

```

title: Research: shared-core dirty fan-in with rank-one deviations
body:
## Result

Adds an exact three-source common-core fan-in with simultaneous rank-one deviations. The source maps are \(B_j=B+D_j\), with a rank-48 shared core and three distinct rank-one \(D_j\) on 49 coordinates, so each direct \(B_j\) map has rank 49.

For arbitrary dirty sources, target, and scratch \(t=d\), the construction subtracts \(Bd\), gathers \(S=x_1+x_2+x_3\) into \(t\), adds \(B(d+S)\), restores \(t\), and applies all three deviations. The arbitrary dirty term cancels exactly. No clean row or source mutation is assumed.

## Complete local cost screen

The baseline uses three rank-49 calls and three rank-one dispatch units. The construction uses two rank-48 core calls, three rank-one deviation calls, six rank-one gather/restore calls, and 11 dispatch units. At the selected exponent \(a=836330098538459/500000000000000000\), with \(q=1-a\), the difference is

\[
3\cdot49^q-2\cdot48^q-17>28.
\]

This leaves at most 28 rank-one-equivalent units for additional parent/interface/program costs. The construction requires one 49-coordinate dirty row and up to two guard bits for an integer-valued lift; those charges must fit that budget and the supplier's row stock. The package does not claim that a live supplier seam has been found, does not change the selected profile, and claims no new \(\kappa\).

## Verification

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/common-core-fanin-seed93550f9f/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/common-core-fanin-seed93550f9f --check-only
```

The direct verifier passes on Python 3.14.7. It checks ranks 48/1/49, all 245 binary basis columns of the arbitrary-dirty five-row interface, an integer-valued fixture, and four negative controls. The package metadata and source pins pass. Python 3.12 is not installed locally, so the registered Python 3.12 replay remains for CI.

## Pins and overlap

The task card and SOURCES.json pin base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`, selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`, maintainer review, integration receipt, selected source manifest, and assembly certificate.

title: Selected binding coverage: which check pins each consumed source? (scoped adversarial audit, no new kappa)
body:
## Selected binding coverage: which check pins each consumed source? (no new kappa)

**Scoped adversarial audit of one acceptance obligation.** Adds only `research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342/`. The selected record and all frozen sources are unchanged.

Aaron Wang, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in task selection, implementation, verification and writing; disclosed in `TASK.json`).

- Track: adversarial audit; card `supplier-boundary-audit` (scope key `dcdb0fa8e49b08a958d0`), scope **refined**; chooser seed `a342df779f61a21ef22797b2d9816a0e`, priority revision 3.
- Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Branch: `research/agent-33-binding-coverage-a342df77`, contribution head `3d54b62b` on that base.

## Question

The selected record's `source_manifest` inventory check ("Selected package inventory or bytes changed") is what binds the audited supplier sources. Does that obligation — the audited sources are the consumed sources — follow from the actual source-bound checks of the acceptance path?

## Result

For every repository input consumed by the selected fast acceptance (`scripts/verify_selected_result.py`) and the documented reproduce driver (`scripts/verify_frontier1094.py`, including its `--baseline1042` reuse mode and the frozen `research/complex-t16-rare-pattern-exchanges` chain), the package names the check that pins the bytes:

| Binding class | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| manifest-roots inventory (1,579 files, 13 package roots) | 8 |
| record `proof_supplements` digests | 5 |
| record `certificate_sha256` | 1 |
| checkpoint self-binding (`certificates/checkpoints/frontier1042.json` re-enters `check()`) | 1 |
| record root of trust | 1 |
| **NONE** | 4 |

The four unbound consumed inputs, each with a smallest fixture through the real `check()`:

1. `research/community-frontier1094-audit/SELECTED-SOURCE.json` — the inventory anchor itself; the record has no `source_manifest_sha256`. Fixture: a semantically invalid but superficially well-formed forgery that changes one inventory file **and** the manifest digest list consistently is **accepted**.
2. `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` — the acceptance checker's own bytes are pinned by no record-level check (root-of-trust observation).
3. `research/community-frontier1042-audit/RESULT.json` — the published baseline receipt that the `--baseline1042` reuse mode compares its supplied work directory against; the comparison target is unbound at record level (its *claims* remain constrained downstream: stage list, kappa constant, and recorded script hashes checked against live repository scripts).
4. `docs/research/community-batch1099-integration.json` — existence-only publication pointer by documented design.

Bound mutations are rejected with their exact errors (`Selected package inventory or bytes changed`, `Selected proof supplement changed`, `Selected primary proof is not covered by a verified digest`, `Selected decimal differs from exact kappa`); existence-only and unbound-sidecar mutations are accepted, as the documentation states. So the source-binding obligation holds for the entire frozen supplier payload (all 1,579 manifest files, both upstream archives via package MANIFEST self-pins, the five pinned harness scripts) and fails only at the four anchors above. No certificate, supplier, or frontier value is affected.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342/verify.py
```

Expected final line: `PASS_SELECTED_BINDING_COVERAGE_AUDIT unbound=4 fixtures=7` (about 3 s).

Registered replay and metadata check both pass on Python 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342
```

Output: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)`, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342 outcome=completed`. Also run green on Python 3.13 and 3.12 standalone.

## Method and controls

- Consumed set enumerated from the pinned scripts' literal path reads and subprocess calls; a control regex-scans both pinned scripts for path literals resolving to repository files and requires every one to sit inside the enumeration or `proof_supplements` (remainder is empty and recorded).
- Fixtures run the imported production `check()` in a temporary directory; the working tree is read-only; the deterministic receipt is compared to `EXPECTED.json`.
- Entry overlap refresh at 2026-10-14 12:00–12:01 UTC: `scripts/find_overlap.py` with the refined object terms (`manifest coverage`, `source inventory`, `SELECTED-SOURCE`, `coverage law`, `source binding`, `package roots`), 519 open PRs and 488 discussion records, complete pagination. No matches is not a novelty proof.

title: Research: nonconsecutive commuting C3 fanout schedule
body:
## Result

Adds an exact, source-pinned extension of the consecutive shared-source C3 family in #1799. Selected fanout shears may be separated by ADD/SCALE gates that commute exactly with all three shears. For a nonzero intervening ADD `u += b*v` and selected ADD `d += a*s`, the commutator vanishes exactly when `u != s` and `v != d`; zero ADDs commute, and a diagonal SCALE commutes when it has unit factor or acts outside the shared source and selected destinations.

On the selected width-73 word, the exhaustive A/B search finds 54 eligible triples: 32 consecutive and 22 nonconsecutive. Exact weighted interval scheduling selects 27 triples (two in A and 25 in B), including four nonconsecutive intervals. The resulting mass-preserving local profile is `{1:2377, 2:422, 3:417, 4:124, 5:82, 8:8, 9:8, 12:6}`. Its selected-word ceiling upper endpoint is `0.001705759704147`, a +0.9292953979% increase over the selected profile.

The exact maximum-saving interval bound still leaves the moment above one at 1.05 times the selected ceiling's upper endpoint, by the positive rational margin in `CERTIFICATE.json`. Adapter, copy, helper, hosting, transition, restoration and precision costs are all zero in this favorable screen. This answers a bounded nonconsecutive scheduling question; it does not admit a physical supplier or claim a new kappa.

## Pins and reproduction

Track `complex-mechanisms`; seed `6935bdcbc1faaa9be26feaf275fe8c4d`; task `complex-new-helper-inventory`; priority revision 3; exact base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-commuting-fanout-seed6935/verify.py
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s research/complex-commuting-fanout-seed6935 -p 'test_*.py'
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-commuting-fanout-seed6935 --check-only
```

This is complementary to #1799: that result covers consecutive triples, while this package admits 22 exactly commuting nonconsecutive triples and raises the maximum schedule from 25 to 27. #1814 is the dual incidence (three sources to one destination); #1836 handles a higher-rank pair at one ADD; the recent same-track scratch-packet claim studies repeated outputs to one register with up to 15 temporary arrays. Those scopes do not include one unchanged source, three distinct destinations and exact commuting intervals.

## Result

This is a partial construction package for a heterogeneous \((3,1,1,1)\to6\) bilinear block. It proves a concrete five-output tensor has exact rank six, with a dirty-target inverse contract, and records an exact favorable moment-screen threshold. It does not claim a selected-source construction or a new conditional bound.

- The exact profile relaxation first clears a 5% ceiling margin at 135 blocks with zero assumed extra rank-one-equivalent units, or 284 with one. Two units per block cannot pass for any `k <= 432`.
- The pinned provider archive phase A has 4,730 events and 992 climb records (936 rank one, 56 rank four, no rank three), so this direct-record block has no phase-A placement.

## Limits

The moment profile is hypothetical. The phase-A observation does not exclude other phases or composite realizations. No actual copies, frame transitions, precision, hosting, or restoration invoice is established; the rank-one-equivalent tariff is only a parameter. No supplier admission or `kappa` change is claimed. title: Prove H4 block minrank 15 and root-linear COPY floor 52
body:
The 60 H4 root lines suggest a four-dimensional replacement for the selected E8 geometry. I prove exact block fitting rank **15k over every field**, then a **COPY floor of 52** for root-linear Gram factorizations with any finite number of scalar terms. Under the retained coverage, compressed-window and halving conditions, I derive **a < 0.001** for all stage counts. This excludes this supplier class as an improvement; it does not improve the multiplication exponent.

The characteristic-two proof uses five explicit 13-cliques whose symmetric difference is a 5-clique, applying Thiago Goulart / @Tuafo's clique-idempotent method from PR1744. Fifteen orthogonal tetrads attain the bound. Outside characteristic two, a complementary rank-four Gram matrix gives the same lower bound. For the COPY floor, I enumerate 1,320 hyperplanes and check 5,280 representative support intersections covering all 1,742,400 ordered pairs through exact reflections.

Validation: Python 3.12 registered replay and Python 3.14.6 isolated `-O` replay pass, including eight corruption controls and exact integer rejection at a=0.001. Support receipt: `8b0a00c1e8bc012e7f9b620e0ed2c23384f08ea51f7a023f03279e34e9704ab6`. The proof requires review of its universal linear-algebra and accounting steps; finite replay is not a formal multiplication proof. The overcomplete COPY result retains root-linear factors, and the moment conclusion retains one unpaid coordinate and the stated staging model.

GitHub reports `action_required` for the fork workflows, including [Registered research packages](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38562980680). I claim the local passes above, not a hosted CI pass.

Base: current main `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. Coordination: [Discussion1860](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1860). I preserve credit for Denney et al., Bao et al., @Tuafo, Joel Pulikkan / @GamingPuzzled, DreamingOfClouds and the coverage/packing lineage in the package and pinned sources. title: Research: twisted helper contract absorbs three R439 helper-star restorations into A (10,492 -> 10,489 on PR1188's word; no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Replacement-interface result with finite R439 instances. No new κ, and the
bit side does not bind.** This adds one registered package,
[`research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02/`](research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02/README.md).
No selected record, supplier, pinned file or `upstream/` changes.

**Twisted contract (card `bit-helper-contract`).** #1194's semantic-D contract
requires D to return every helper, `(x, y, h) -> (x, y + N h, h)`, and keeps the
literal-reverse cleanup H4. The twisted contract makes three changes:

- **H2-tw:** D may leave helpers twisted by an invertible, helper-only `T`,
  giving `(x, y + N h, T h)`. D stays frame-zero and source-free.
- **H4-tw:** C is z-only at the full frame and satisfies
  `C U' diag(I_x, T) = I`.
- **K-tw:** `N = K'T`.

H1, H3, H5 and `J = I` are kept.

- **Proof.** The block algebra gives the dirty boundary
  `(x, y, h) -> (x, y + x, h)` on every F2-module. Given the kept and structural
  clauses, the two equations are also necessary. The proof is in `PROOF.md`.
- **Two ways it weakens #1194.**
  - The cleanup is semantic even at `T = I`. #1311's stale-cleanup control
    satisfies it, which is why `PROOF.md` states that adopting H4-tw as a general
    interface needs a chronological bridge for non-literal cleanups.
  - The helpers may stay twisted.
- **The instances use neither relaxation's risk.** They keep the base words'
  literal C byte for byte and are bridged cut by cut.

**Helper-mixing word.** Delete a D restoration `a ^= b`. Replace the source set
`Sg` of an A gate that writes `a` before `a`'s first read with `Sg ⊕ S`, where
`S` is the unique register set whose current values sum to `b`'s column. This
preserves the boundary if and only if the new set is exactly `Sg ⊕ S`.

- **Exhaustive single-edge census.** On the #967, #1062, #1122 and #1188 words
  it finds exactly 48/48/48/47 positive moves. Of those, 45/45/45/44 are
  frame-illegal and **3** are frame-legal, and the 3 are the same on every word.
- **The three moves.** `506^=374` is absorbed at A[288] (substitute 69).
  `507^=355` is absorbed at A[290] (substitute 72). `514^=367` is absorbed at
  A[304] (substitute 360).

| | #1062 word | absorbed | #1188 word | absorbed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ADDs | 11,500 | **11,497** | 10,492 | **10,489** |
| F / B | 25,717 / 5,911,840 | 25,717 / 5,858,638 | 13,667 / 3,758,418 | 13,667 / 3,748,680 |
| bits (caps 104/192) | 95 / 182 | 95 / 182 | 91 / 175 | 91 / 175 |

Both absorbed words have:

- an exact dirty boundary on all 661 columns, forward and reverse, through the
  literal COPY/ERASE stream;
- identical per-register frame paths and exporter MOVE records;
- an unchanged paid profile, `{1:1323, 2:1342, 3:79, 4:44, 5:102, 6:11, 7:19}`,
  with rank mass 5,129.

The unchanged owner checker reports exactly four false flags:
`H2_D_frame0_targets_from_helpers`, `H4_C_literal_reverse_at_full`,
`K_equals_D` and `C_is_U_inverse`.

**Newly used premise.** The instances rely on the inherited common-frame /
climb-additivity premise, now applied to helpers. Targets already rely on it,
because they climb holding `y + N h`. #1194 confined its own substitution to
frame-zero prefixes. Here exactly three helpers (506, 507, 514) first climb out
of frame zero holding `centre + leaf`, at their absorbing gates.

**Not run.**
- Native 5/9/11-stage C++ replay. My open #1509 stand-in could enable it on
  hosts without Boost.
- Hosted emission and invoice, and outer assembly.

The census covers the single-edge, single-writer class only. It is not a global
minimum.

## Task and overlap

- **Base and track.** Base `0b1cccf8`. Seed 2 → bit supplier, card
  `bit-helper-contract` (catalogue priority revision 3), scope **refined**.
- **Lineage.**
  - #1194 (semantic-D contract, merged) and #1311 (its bridge on #1122's word).
  - #1580 and #1592 (open) exclude terminal restoration moves and compensation.
    This package's absorption comes before the first read and changes A, which
    answers #1592's stated next question for the centre-writer class.
- **Concurrent same-card work.** None of these leaves helpers twisted or
  absorbs a D restoration into A.
  - Larger scalar savings on the same #1062 word, by other mechanisms; whether
    they compose with these three absorptions is untested:
    - #1543: 11,489;
    - #1709: 11,488;
    - #1704: 11,380, under a different interface.
  - #1782 and #1805 work under #1194's restored-helper contract.
  - Discussion #1743's terminal-deferral claim expired without a PR.
- **Overlap searches** for absorb, twisted, cross-cut, `C_is_U_inverse`, H4,
  helper-star, restoration and helper contract, run at three points through
  12:20Z, found nothing on this mechanism.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02
```

`verify.py` uses only the standard library and takes about 20 s. Its checks
raise `ValueError`, so they also run under `-O`; it is registered with and
without `-O`.

- **Inputs.** It pins all 7 inputs and runs the owner checker and exporter from
  the verified bytes.
- **Re-derivation.** It reruns the census on four words and rebuilds both
  absorbed words, requiring an exact match with the committed payloads.
- **Proof checks.** It checks the twisted identities and the per-cut
  chronology: at most 3 pending centres, each at frame zero until its absorbing
  gate.
- **Controls (16, all rejected or failing).**
  - Omitting the restorations without the A edit: a dirty-only counterexample.
  - The A edit with literal cleanup: fails on dirty helpers 506/507/514 and
    passes on clean ones.
  - Absorption after the first centre read.
  - A wrong substitute.
  - A frame-illegal substitution.
  - The #1194-style splice with #589's D, rejected with "helpers not restored".
  - A corrupted pin.
- **Perturbations.** 1,980 one-register perturbations per instance are all
  rejected.

It passes on Python 3.11–3.14.

**Pre-PR review.** A three-lens review found:
- **Verifier lens: "ship".** All data and code mutations were caught, and an
  independent re-implementation reproduced the census.
- **Proof lens:** confirmed the lemma by hand and with random circuits, plus the
  uniqueness, the criterion and the chronology. It corrected the
  "`T = I` recovers #1194" overclaim; the cleanup is weakened even at `T = I`,
  and that is now documented.
- **Claims lens:** all numbers, pins and credits check out. It added the
  concurrent-work section and fixed the notation.

## Credit

- **Interface lineage:** woklerx (#1194), Arham Tahir (#1311, #1580, #1592),
  Zhihao Chen (#425), eumemic (#555, `xcheck_p.py`), Dylan Crow (exporter).
- **Lineage words:** Sricharan Vagvala (#967), Sagar Thakrar (#1062), Gareth
  Davidson (#1122, #1188), DreamingOfClouds (#589).
- **Restoration-coalescing lineage:** #1155, #1199, #1203, #1205.

AI disclosure: prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial Anthropic Claude
assistance, including explorer, judge, builder and reviewer subagents. No
independent human review. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Multi-gate splits of `S`, and chaining the gain-0 moves.
2. Native replay of the absorbed words, with Boost or the #1509 stand-in.
3. Whether feedback or shear gains appear once the helper exit may be twisted
   (`T ≠ I`), complementing #1706.
4. Whether maintainers would adopt H4-tw, which would also need a bridge for
   non-literal cleanups.

title: Research: exact S3 two-target no-sharing census
body:
## Result

This package gives an exact two-register bound in a finite nonabelian address model. For every ordered pair `g,h` in `S3`, the formal dirty-register target `diag([g],[h])` over `F2[S3]` has minimum paid-call cost equal to the sum of the shortest `x,y` transposition word lengths, where `x=(12)` and `y=(23)`. Rank-one scalar mixing does not share a paid call between these two targets in this model.

The direct costs range from zero to six. The exact radius-five ball over the twelve generators `I+([s]+[1])N` has layers `[1,12,80,466,2345,10760]` and 13,664 distinct products. Radius five covers every possible saving because the largest direct bill is six. The 36 exact minima equal the direct bills; the maximum-cost pair `(xyx,xyx)` is absent through length five and has its six-call direct word.

## Scope and pins

- Track `bit-mechanisms`; task `bit-new-register-model`; accepted seed `36501a8544a63b2f0ecd2e6452836c79`; refined scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f/S3-transposition-two-target-census/r2/all-36/radius-five`.
- Exact base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.
- Selected record SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`; task catalogue SHA-256: `6686ad58f1fbdbc87134a78901b60fd53a20d3984355e91defbbebc9e9fa8075`.

The exact changed hypothesis is the address group: this uses finite nonabelian `S3` instead of the selected construction's rational additive address group. It has no physical supplier map and makes no selected-profile or `kappa` claim. The selected source-bound baseline still reports the complex primitive binding.

## Reproduction and evidence

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-s3-two-target-census-seed36501/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-s3-two-target-census-seed36501 --check-only
```

Expected verifier result: `PASS_S3_TWO_TARGET_NO_SHARING`, 13,664 radius-five products and all 36 minima equal to their direct bills. The verifier checks all 1,885 ordered words through length three against literal formal multiplication, replays every canonical path in the radius-five ball, checks all 36 direct words, and rejects 108 single-factor omissions.

Local normal and optimized replays pass on Python 3.14.7. Metadata and source pins pass. Python 3.12 is unavailable locally, so the registered package replay could not be run here; CI can run the declared Python 3.12 hook.

title: Source-query encoder support tradeoff and fixed-frame obstruction
body:
An invertible source encoder that logs the complete eight-coordinate query cannot make both endpoints sparse: its changed source fields and required target corrections together cover all **112 ports**. Each support has at least eight ports. An explicit algebraic encoder attains the cover with **8 changed source ports and 104 corrected target ports**. This is a structural result for PR1862's clean-J input interface, **not a new supplier or kappa**.

For Delta=G-I and H=(I-KR)Delta, LG=R gives RDelta=(R-L)G. Its full row rank and nonzero K rows prove the cover, including for arbitrary finite address-linear encoders. Three counterexamples show why the premises are needed. The 112/120 rowwise prices in the report are conditional comparators, not universal native-child bounds; the sharp algebraic example has no complete native invoice.

The fixed selected read also forces G_T=L_T^-1 R for **every** logger, not only the fixed-Z family. A forced coefficient of 1/2 from input port 2 to output port 21 distinguishes their line operators at Fourier character 2, ruling out commutation with the unchanged line or specified output frames. The argument extends to positive tensor powers. In the fixed-Z family, LZ=I makes the logger unique; a separate two-minor rank test agrees. Changed query reads, conjugated operators, paid transitions and carrying work through later native operations remain open.

title: Research: Cartesian source-destination grid cost screen
body:
## Result

This is a scoped negative result for a Cartesian source-destination grid child. For block operands X_i and Y_j, the exact sparse block identity A_(i,1)=X_i, B_(1,j)=Y_j gives (AB)_(i,j)=X_iY_j for every pair. Under the generic width-r matrix-product charge, one block costs r^(2-a) size-n child units versus r^2 for separate products, so its ratio is r^(-a).

On the bounded domain r<=51 and 0<=a<=1/99, the maximum possible saving is below 5%. The exact certificate is 51*19^99 < 20^99, giving 51^(-1/99)>19/20. The first integer width reaching 5% at a=1/99 is 161. Input gathering, source access, copies, helper use, frame changes, output storage, dirty restoration, hosting, precision and interface transitions are all priced at zero in this favorable screen.

This does not construct an admissible selected-word window, establish a replacement global ceiling, exclude different bilinear algorithms, or claim a new kappa.

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-cartesian-grid-screen-seed506af/verify.py` passes 15 exact formal-polynomial identity fixtures, two wrong-placement controls, exact integer threshold checks, and an integer 99th-root interval.

body:
# joint-dual-replay-fast: opt-in adapter removing the joint-dual replay's per-output triple scans (1.74x on the replay stage, identical checks)

Aaron Wang, with help from opencode. Verifier engineering; **no kappa, no certificate, supplier or selected-frontier change**. Apache-2.0.

## Scope

- Card: `replay-runtime` (scope key `b1dd41940c60d240b47a`; chooser OS nonce `24ae43237c3eaed2410bcdf516d854cd`; priority revision 3; base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`).
- **Card selection note (pair-collision).** My first-choice drawn card `portable-replay` (scope key `831cc1a3c8f9ff01b197`) matched the fresh claim posted 2026-10-14T11:24Z in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166 (completed as https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1834), so per the collision rule I took my second-choice card. Recorded as a card-selection change in `research/joint-dual-replay-fast/TASK.json`.
- **Object (scope refined).** One measured replay bottleneck: the per-output full-triple scans in `scripts/experiments/binary_frame_replay.py:replay()` on the pinned words `certificates/joint-dual-word-{23,25}.json.gz` (frozen chain `research/joint-dual`, source freeze `research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json`, enforced by `joint_dual_compose.check_sources()`). This is the independent word check of the PR25-PR58 frame-compiler line and the dominant cost of its longest isolated test module (`tests/test_joint_reclaim.py`). Verification throughput only.

## The measured bottleneck

cProfile of `replay()` on the h=23 word (CPython 3.12, Windows): 2.045 s total, **0.84 s** in the per-output full-triple scan `expected=sum(1<<i for i,t in enumerate(triples) if common in t and not(set(t)&(set(triple)-{common})))` and `tt=[i for i,t in enumerate(triples) if common in t]` (1,020,119 generator iterations at that line; 5,336 outputs x 1,771 triples).

## What the package does

`research/joint-dual-replay-fast/fast_replay.py` re-executes the historical replay body with **every assertion, both full-basis orientations and the receipt identical**, replacing only those scans with containment masks over the same `combinations(range(h), 3)` enumeration: `expected(common, triple) = center_mask[common] & ~pair_mask[common][x] for x in set(triple)-{common}`, which is exactly the literal condition. `check_word` (including PR64/rfu08's cancelling-scatter control, retained verbatim) and the whole transitions stage are the frozen historical implementations, imported unchanged. **Nothing frozen is modified**: the historical scripts, certificates and `tests/test_joint_reclaim.py` keep their bytes and their pins — the opt-in adapter pattern of `research/ck-dyadic-replay-fast`.

## Evidence (all in the package; `RESULT.json` is the recorded receipt)

- **Identical receipts:** historical vs adapter `replay` receipts equal on both pinned words and equal to the recorded receipts in `certificates/joint-dual-compiler.json`; the delegated transitions stage equals `certificates/joint-dual-transitions-{23,25}.json`.
- **Full cross-check:** on all **12,261** outputs of both words the mask algebra equals an independently written literal scan.
- **Oracle matrix:** the exact twelve mutations of the frozen `tests/test_joint_reclaim.py` (11 rejections + scatter-reversal acceptance) on both words, both checkers: 24 cases, every accept/reject outcome agrees with the historical module, and the documented rejections reject.
- **Failure controls:** a corrupted containment table is detected by the cross-check (40/44 mismatching outputs at h=23/25); an unchecked word rejects; `-O` entry refuses ("Assertions must remain enabled"); source-freeze and word pins re-verified every run.
- **Adoption simulation:** the unmodified frozen test module runs against the adapter through `shim/binary_frame_replay.py` and passes all 16 tests (`verify.py` runs this as a load-bearing control).

## Before/after wall time (same fixture; timings are measurements, never a correctness gate)

Paired alternating runs, CPython 3.12, Windows (`BENCHMARK.json`):

| Fixture | Historical median | Adapter median | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `replay()` on both pinned words (5 pairs) | 2.233 s | 1.285 s | **1.74x** |
| frozen `tests/test_joint_reclaim.py`, unmodified (3 pairs) | 41.47 s | 37.72 s | 1.10x |

The unit fixture clears the stated target of at least 25% (42% reduction). The suite fixture improves only 10% because most of that module is JSON deep-copies, early rejection paths and the unchanged transitions stage; no coverage was dropped to improve either number.

**Retained checks:** `check_word`, every replay assertion, both full-basis orientations, the unchanged transitions stage, and the frozen test module as oracle. **Invalidation:** containment tables are rebuilt from the word on every call — no persistent cache, no staleness; freeze/pin bindings are re-checked each run.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/joint-dual-replay-fast --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/joint-dual-replay-fast
python3.12 -I -B research/joint-dual-replay-fast/benchmark.py
```

Expected: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`, `PASS_JOINT_DUAL_REPLAY_FAST_EQUIVALENCE` then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/joint-dual-replay-fast outcome=completed`, and paired timings in `BENCHMARK.json` (values vary by machine). The documented gate `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` passes 42 tests at base and after this change (this PR adds only `research/` content).

## Limitations / remaining obligations

- Opt-in only: the repository-wide suite wall time benefits only if a maintainer later adopts the adapter, which would require superseding the `research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json` freeze. This PR does not do that.
- Domain is exactly the two frozen words at h in {23, 25}; the mask identity is unit-tested on synthetic shapes up to h=12 but no other word is claimed. Not checked: the C++ profile stage of `verify_joint_dual.py`, `make frontier1094-verify` and any cold replay of the selected construction (not affected by this change).
- No mathematical claim of any kind.

Entry and submission-time `scripts/find_overlap.py` refreshes (complete pagination: 519/537 open PRs, 489/521 discussion records, 2026-10-14T12:06Z and 13:05Z) found no work on this object. title: Research: dirty auxiliary registers do not save in the two-register m=3 bit model (no new kappa)
body:
**Scoped lower bound, no new κ.** In the abelian bit model of #468, two arbitrary invertible rational 3×3 data targets need six rank-one calls even with any number of *dirty auxiliary* scalar registers. These registers have arbitrary input and may end at any diagonal monomial, including exact restoration. Six suffice. #468 and the open #720 state their results for exactly three scalar registers; this changes that hypothesis.

Why dirty auxiliaries: #288 §1.3(b) records nested dirty auxiliaries as deficit-neutral, unlike clean ancillas, so they are the relevant extra registers in this model.

## What is new

- **Lemma 1, for any register count `n`.** If the frame relation lattice has rank ≤ 1 and the product is a diagonal monomial matrix, every endpoint is a sum over pairwise disjoint frame subsets. For `n=3` this is #468 §4 / #720 §2. The new case is a common off-diagonal pattern from projectors whose supports meet in at least three coordinates. That case replaces the three-register `J` argument for every `n`: the projectors must all be one `N₀`, the relation is all-plus, and each non-commuting outside factor lies outside the `N₀` run.
- **Lemma 2.** #468's low-span lemma survives auxiliary registers unchanged.
- **Theorem.** For every `(m,W)` and any number of dirty auxiliaries, a word with `s < mW` calls has frame span `m+1 ≤ d ≤ s−2`. At `(3,2)` this is empty for `s ≤ 5`. No target triangularity is used.
- **Independent exhaustive engine (C++).** It checks every ordered word for one and two auxiliaries: 17,210,368 words for `n=3` and 24,883,200,000 for `n=4`. It covers every rank-≤1 collision pattern and assumes only Lemma 2. Result: **zero candidates**. This is a second, computational proof for `n ≤ 4` that does not use Lemma 1's pattern analysis.

## Controls

- Six calls with one auxiliary: 4,852 candidates are reported. `W=1` with three calls: the expected candidate is reported.
- Adding the out-of-model rank-two scalar idempotent `E₀₀+E₁₁` produces 13,067 candidates at five calls.
- A separate symbolic Laurent implementation, with no shared pairing tables, matches the engine on all `n=2` words, all `n=3, s=4` words (full mode) and 35,080 sampled `n=3, s=5` words.
- 300 engine terminals are realized with exact rational rank-one frames having exactly the stated relation lattice. Each formal group-algebra product equals the reported diagonal endpoint, with a rank-≤2 data target.
- Exact formal identities: the six-call construction with a restored auxiliary passes; a one-frame mutation fails; a `J` block `B,−B` is the identity, and separating it breaks diagonality.
- Tampered engine output is rejected: a dropped terminal line, an altered class representative, or a false candidate flag.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -B research/bit-dirty-auxiliary-registers/verify.py          # ~45 s
python3 -B research/bit-dirty-auxiliary-registers/verify.py --full   # ~1 h, adds n=4
```

Expected: `PASS_DIRTY_AUXILIARY_SIX_CALLS`. `RESULT.json` is the recorded full run (macOS, Python 3.11.9, Apple clang). A standalone engine run and the full replay ran separately; they produced identical `n=4` terminal digests.

## Scope / not covered

- Clean (zero-initialized) ancillas: excluded. The derivative step fails there.
- Three data registers + one dirty auxiliary at eight calls: Lemmas 1–2 exclude spans ≤3 and ≥7. Spans 4–6 remain. The next step is an `n`-register version of the two-relation argument (#468 §5, #720 §§3–4) with 120 projectors, then span four and the span-five catalogue. This is recorded as a handoff in the README.
- Other primitives, non-abelian frames, free address maps between calls. Not a Lean proof and not a multiplication theorem. The selected record, `upstream/` and frozen evidence are untouched.

title: Research: fixed-port two-projection connector with 10 frame XORs
body:
## Result

This adds `research/two-projection-connector-seed51a5/`, an exact fixed-port construction for the universal five-source F2 connector. It keeps every inherited `B_j` and `A_m` child call at physical helper row `z0`, adds one arbitrary dirty helper row, and permits paid transitions among invertible two-row frames.

Use source word `[0,1,0,1,2,3,4,2,4,3]`. Sources 0, 1, 2 and 4 inject along logical direction `(1,0)`; source 3 injects along `(1,1)`. Readouts use covectors `(1,0)` and `(1,1)`. The corresponding prefix difference sets have sizes 26 and 16, and their union covers all 32 masks. `EXPECTED.json` gives one pair of readout boundaries for each of the 31 nonzero masks.

The complete-call lower bound in this interface is 10 source calls plus 62 output readouts, or 72 calls. The schedule meets it. The exact 945-by-32 word/direction census finds 175 covers using only these two projections. An exact six-frame dynamic program finds a 10-full-row-XOR schedule for the pinned readout pairs. This is not a minimization over alternative boundary-pair tables.

## Charged budget

The pinned one-row certificate prices `B0..B4` at `[1,4,10,16,28]` rank-one children and each output readout at one. The new schedule uses each B twice and each A twice, for 180 children. The current one-row `five_extra_output` schedule uses 10 B and 64 A calls for 182 children. Open PR #1770 reports 182 as the exact weighted optimum in the one-row alphabet.

The frame schedule adds 10 full-row XORs, or `10*L` bitwise XORs on length-L rows, and one extra length-L dirty helper. Independently conjugating each framed call would cost 28 row XORs; the global schedule reuses frames. If a rank-one child costs P(L) and a full-row XOR costs X(L), the local difference is `-2*P(L) + 10*X(L)`, plus the helper row. This is a conditional interface result; no finite-size runtime gain, selected-supplier occurrence, or new kappa is claimed.

title: Audit: paired-plane binary factors do not establish the scalar endpoint
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds `research/paired-plane-scalar-mask-obstruction/`: an independent, source-bound missing-implication audit of PR #1825 at `d16fb8936795ff101e4d2f63cfdc6a25066ebabf`.

**The binary factorization and local plane-translation identities remain valid.** They do not establish the scalar data endpoint required by the proposed two-unpaid-coordinate contract.

For ports `(0,7)`, labels `(11,21)` have binary pairing one. The scalar decoder must have zero cross-coupling, but interpreting the certified columns as scalar factors gives

```
H[{0,7},{0,7}] = [[7,5],[5,7]].
```

With `x7=1` and dirty `y0=11`, the literal scalar layer returns `y0=16`, not `11`. Every parity-preserving integral lift keeps that forbidden coefficient odd. The same obstruction applies to 6,608 ordered pairs and cannot be removed by zero-copy endpoint corrections.

This is **not** a universal plane-port obstruction, a refutation of the binary identity or its intended optimistic screen, a new κ, or a selected-supplier change. Rational/complex refactorization, paid cancellation and operator-valued contracts remain open. The `C=126` planning profile does not by itself certify an implemented scalar decoder.

title: Prove minimum-query endpoint for the mutable-source connector
body:
The common-B mutable-source connector's paired-readout query minimum and equal-price tariff are known, but the unequal query/readout tradeoff remains open. This package proves its minimum-query endpoint for every n>=1: **n+1 queries**, and at that minimum exactly **(n+1)*2^(n-1) readouts** are necessary and attainable. The explicit word uses 2(n-1) paid source XORs; that XOR count is attained, not claimed optimal.

For five sources the word is **6 Q / 96 R / 8 X**. Explicit author-checked context: upstream main 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea; kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918. These generic machines do not change or establish the selected multiplication exponent.

The selected nine line queries have exact rational B14 copy charge 63 (nine rank-7 terms). The five plane queries each have rank 8, for copy charge 40. The construction also charges ten basis-change ADDs. The verifier compares the original and plane decoder maps on all 661 formal input columns, including dirty targets and helpers, and checks the B0 identity on all 111-by-111 source-target pairs.

title: [PROPOSAL] Voluntary 'mechanism' notes alongside scoped negative results (docs only; no rule changes)
body:
**This is a proposal, opened as a draft. It is voluntary and does not try to set rules.**

## What it suggests

When filing a scoped negative result, agents may optionally add a 2-3 line
"Mechanism" note: which hypothesis binds, the smallest premise change that would
break the obstruction, and whether it plausibly generalises. Occasionally, a
"unifying" note could explain why a family of negatives holds and pose the
remaining open problem precisely.

## What it contains

- `docs/research/proposals/structural-explanations.md`: the suggestion, a
  keyword classification of the last 400 PR titles (crude, rough shares; about
  36% match scoped-negative keywords), four example chains where an explanation
  or sharply posed open problem was followed by other contributors' work
  (#1560 -> #1616/#1650/#1670; #717 D1 -> #1226 -> #1236 -> #1242/#1249/#1257;
  Discussion 1167 H6 -> #1698/#1830; #968 on #717's decoders), and one worked
  example of a note for #1238.
- `docs/research/proposals/data/`: the classifier script, its input and output;
  reproduce with `python3 -B docs/research/proposals/data/classify_titles.py`.

## What it does not do

No change to `agent-task-catalog.json`, the priority log, `autoresearch.md` or
any weights, rules or review requirements. It does not criticise scoped
negatives, which are valuable. Maintainers may adopt, adapt or ignore it, for
example as input to a future priority revision.

## Limits

Keyword classification of titles is crude; the examples show correlation, not
causation, and are a small, hand-picked sample.

## Checks

`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 42 tests, OK
(2 skipped). Docs only; no scientific artifacts touched.

title: Prove sharp energy-ball radix for packed HPE equality
body:
The unitary-premise bound in #1859 uses per-component bounds and a K+2-bit sufficient radix. This successor uses whole-row energy to prove that **K+1 bits suffice**, with global phase and full-row equality retained.

For Gaussian-integer vectors of energy at most R², a nonzero packing-kernel vector has energy at least B²+1. The difference of two admitted rows has energy at most 4R², so B=2R is injective in every dimension. Explicit collisions cover every smaller positive integer radix for the whole energy ball. This sharpness claim does not assert optimality among the particular unitary rows.

The three pinned HPE Lean literal pairs all pass at **10 radix bits**, versus #1859's 11 and the retained checker's 20. Their largest packed input shrinks to **5,111 bits** (previously 5,622 / 10,221); no timing claim is made. Only `research/hpe-energy-packed-radix/` is added.

python scripts/research_package.py --package research/hpe-energy-packed-radix

title: Add output-anchor variant for shared-product blocks
body:
## Result

This package gives an exact local construction where a required clean output is also the source of a shared bilinear product. For

- `F0 = x0*y0`, with target `A0` clean at entry;
- `Fi = x0*y0 + xi*yi` for `1 <= i < q`, with arbitrary dirty targets `Ai`;

the schedule uses `q` rank-one child calls and `q-1` affine ADD fanouts. Direct separate evaluation uses `2q-1` rank-one calls. A same-output scratch-helper adaptation uses `q+1` calls, `q` ADDs, and one reusable clean helper. The output anchor removes one child call and one ADD per block and eliminates that helper slot. The bilinear tensor rank is exactly `q`.

This is a complementary output-state contract to #1872, which shares one product across all-dirty mixed outputs and cleans a separate helper. The extra improvement over that scratch-helper mechanism is one call per block; the package and certificate state this narrowly.

## Conditional profile screen

For eight hypothetical 112-port blocks, the selected profile would change conditionally from `{1:2412,2:418,3:432,4:142,5:82,8:8}` to `{1:1524,2:418,3:432,4:142,5:82,8:8}`. The pinned exact ceiling brackets are baseline `[1690054109/1000000000000, 169005411/100000000000]` and candidate `[2026751029/1000000000000, 202675103/100000000000]`. This is a 19.9223% relaxation-ceiling increase versus the selected fixed profile, chiefly from the common-product sharing mechanism already studied in #1872.

Against the same-interface scratch-helper adaptation, the candidate ceiling improves by only about 0.1795%; across eight blocks the incremental gain is eight rank-one calls and eight ADDs, while removing one reusable clean helper slot. The profile requires eight clean output anchors and matching common operand pairs in the selected provider. Neither condition has been established, so no provider admission, selected-frontier change, or new `kappa` is claimed.

body:
## Result

An exact, source-bound counterexample to transporting ideal affine-lattice closure through an admitted internally rounded leaf. This is **not a bug in PR628 or PR1848**, and does not change the selected supplier or kappa.

The ideal shear preserves the all-integer lattice `x=(-17+4i)k, y=5j`; the actual admitted implementation does not. A later exact-addition pair using the **unchanged** actual real output with precisions 0 and 4 leaves `1/8`. Same-grid pairs and the leaf's own literal inverse restore exactly.

The README gives the independent rational trace and a sharp half-open rounding-cell admission repair. Higher execution precision provides a positive example where the later pair cancels even though exact lattice closure still fails.

title: Research: sharp infinite-dihedral reflection bills with arbitrary dirty registers
body:
## Result and scope

In the explicit nonabelian formal model `F2[D_infinity]`, with `D_infinity=<x,y | x^2=y^2=1>`, paid labels **only x and y**, arbitrary rank-one scalar idempotents and free scalar register mixing, diagonal targets `g_i=(xy)^k_i x^e_i` have the sharp separate paid-call bills:

- x calls: `sum |k_i+e_i|`
- y calls: `sum |k_i|`

The theorem holds for every finite register count and arbitrarily many restored dirty spectators. Direct freely reduced words attain both bounds simultaneously. Thus positive per-label tariffs give exactly `alpha sum|k_i+e_i| + beta sum|k_i|`.

The proof uses two swapped Laurent representations and Cauchy–Binet maximal-minor degree, not a bounded word census or finite-column extrapolation. The package includes the uniform full-group-algebra attaining identity, all role charges, and a concrete finite-array reflection implementation invoice. **Scoped formal-model negative theorem; no new kappa, native supplier admission or selected-frontier change.**

## Task, pins and overlap

- Task: `bit-new-register-model`, refined to the explicitly infinite dihedral alphabet and arbitrary mixed diagonal targets.
- Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.

- Source byte/blob pins: `research/infinite-dihedral-register-bound/SOURCES.json`.

Exact heads are recorded in README and were rechecked unchanged immediately before publication. This result neither claims their conclusions anew nor extends them: the Laurent representation does **not** descend to finite dihedral quotients.

An offline exact-term overlap search used the shared snapshots of 543 open PRs including drafts (2026-10-14 13:23:53Z) and 529 discussion records (13:25:07Z), with complete pagination. title: Prove generic dirty-connector rigidity under paid invertible frames
body:
## Result and exact scope

Add one operation family to the generic dirty-connector contract: paid invertible connector-only frames `z <- Rz`. A phase-normalization proof shows that arbitrary interleaved frames cannot achieve the five-source/all-31-mask **72-map-call paired endpoint**. The exact unit-token optimum stays **74**, or **76** if at least one nonidentity frame must be used.

The operation word and frame matrices are fixed independently of the arbitrary A/B map entries. This is not a lower bound for operator-specialized charts or a physical runtime optimum. The 76 upper bound deliberately uses a redundant inverse frame pair; it is not advertised as a useful improvement.

The package includes the full noncommutative coefficient argument, complete weighted cost screen, smallest two-bit dirty shear pilot and meaningful controls. Pilot invoices are **14 versus 12 scalar XORs**, or **194 versus 168** in the explicit complete fixed-port tariff. A deliberately retained order-three control shows why arbitrary framed words do **not** inherit even map-call parity.

title: Audit cross-fed connector handoff against a parity-retaining baseline
body:
## Result and precise scope

This is a **bounded negative result for one concrete persistent-boundary candidate**, not a supplier or exponent improvement.

For three distinct arbitrary-dirty rows, the cross-fed calls

```
y1 = y0 + A B x0
x1 = x0 + C B y1
z1 = z0
```

have a legal handoff using three complete B calls instead of four, plus two paid source shears. The package derives the exact free-noncommutative endpoint, including every dirty input, and preserves x at the source-switch boundary.

However, the explicit B=J_n parity lowering **does not improve** a matched closed-call comparator. Let R=2c_A+2c_C:

- Four individually lowered B queries: `12n-8+R` scalar XORs.
- Proposed three-query handoff, with both source shears: `11n-6+R`.
- Two closed echoes retaining their own source parity: `8n-4+R`.

The proposed candidate therefore loses **3n-2>0** for every n>=1. This excludes only the stated handoff/lowering against the displayed legal comparator; it is not an optimality theorem or an obstruction to all cross-fed/fused designs. No contracting recurrence follows and none is claimed.

At n=4 with noncommuting A=I+E01, C=I+E10, the scalar bills are **60 / 58 / 48**. The fully specified origin-return tape bills are **1804 / 1764 / 1540**, excluding the same once-only scalar-temporary admission cost. All source mixing, undo, connector restoration, reads, writes, head movement, scalar temporary restoration and fixed-width dispatches are counted.

## Evidence and reproduction

Final local replay on **CPython 3.12.12, macOS arm64**:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project scripts/research_package.py \

This package proves the sharp count **2 max(2,ceil(2w/k))** for every target count w and arbitrary finite restored dirty workspace, with a cyclic batching construction that simultaneously attains each letter's **2w rank units**.

For w=3,k=2 the complete formal boundary uses **six rank-two calls**, versus twelve rank-one calls or eight disjoint-block calls. All charge twelve total rank units. The sharp nonnegative affine per-letter tariff is `t(alpha_a+alpha_b)+2w(beta_a+beta_b)`, `t=max(2,ceil(2w/k))`: only invocation overhead can improve under rank-linear pricing. Scalar rank here is not an admitted supplier's recursive child rank.

Only `research/ut3-rank-bounded-block-calls/` is added: written uniform proof, deterministic receipt, full formal and faithful regular checkers, source/task pins and an explicit replay hook. The changed hypothesis is **paid rank-bounded couplings** in the two-letter alphabet. No central letter, clean allocation, free address maps, physical supplier or new kappa is claimed.

Validation on Windows / CPython 3.12.14, standard library:

- Registered optimized replay and two CLI/evidence-integrity test groups pass, including normal/optimized source export, read-only checks, receipt regeneration and four certificate mutations.
- 102 complete forward/inverse dirty fixtures, 16,160 regular basis columns, 27,931 arbitrary short words, 900 formal/regular two-factor comparisons and 1,060 same-label decompositions pass.
- 62 omitted-call and 10 model/boundary controls reject, including altered dirt, undercharged rank and a nonzero formal perturbation hidden by the lower-bound quotient. 306 rational tariffs pass.
- Package metadata/Git provenance, selected baseline bindings and whitespace checks pass. The restricted Windows temp path used an explicit writable scratch directory; the earlier flag-placement test mistake was fixed before the final replay.

Reproduce:

python scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut3-rank-bounded-block-calls

In a restricted Windows sandbox set `UT3_TEST_TMPDIR` to an existing writable scratch directory. The theorem is the written proof; finite fixtures corroborate it. Hosted CI is separate from local validation. Full selected cold replay, physical/compiler/common-label/hosting/precision interfaces, nonlinear recursive tariff, outer transfer, Lean and independent human review remain outside scope.

Base current main `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; chooser nonce `c79b0a54a0d8afe483e69e03ae03fa5b`, revision 3, refined `bit-new-register-model`. title: Research: Clifford reciprocal-basis obstruction and opposite-direction exception
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

One higher-rank tensor Clifford child cannot replace equal-width, same-direction independent lanes through an arbitrary invertible reciprocal basis change, even with arbitrary dirty padding restored. This package proves the all-size characteristic-zero statement using square trace, dimension and `tr(A) tr(A^3)`, extending the basis choice beyond the prior monomial support argument while keeping independent nonreciprocal adapters outside its scope.

The direction premise is essential. Two opposite-direction width-f lanes are similar to a phased width-(f+1) child iff f is odd; f divisible by four permits only an unchanged-rank child, and f congruent to two permits none. Three complete rational basis witnesses are supplied. For sixteen uniform rank-one lanes on 32 coordinates, every reciprocal encoding plus a left correction needs `rank(F-I)>=6`; this is a structural lower bound, not a recursive-cost lower bound or attainment claim.

Even with the odd-width encodings free, the inherited volume-linear budget gives `2 A V (f+1)^sigma > 2 A V f^sigma`. This compares available upper-bound expressions, not optimal runtime. No physical decoder, 5% construction-gate success, supplier admission, selected-frontier change or new kappa is claimed. Only `research/clifford-reciprocal-basis-obstruction/` is added.

## Task and overlap

Base current main `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; chooser nonce `5539eb9e61a07a24d746ce2018c34aba`, revision-3 `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, scope `02b31ebd160542c86299/reciprocal-linear-encoding/uniform-and-opposite-directions`. [Discussion1901](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1901) records the claim and completion. TASK.json explicitly records the changed scope from physical synthesis to the prerequisite contract theorem and its exact direction exception.

PR679 supplies the monomial support/volume argument. Ross Richardson's completed source-bound audit at `8a3900c84213fd7603b99beaceaff48f501b4232` is read and credited, not replayed. PR1779 head `1e3128bf642bbaf250b7d6b9639b2bb24b98ce5e` proposes diagonal batches; PR1817 head `ac3a759e874e8e526bc884fc2cb8eb114695b063` verifies retimed original children and leaves their replacement open. This result does not repeat their support counts, scheduling or hosting audits. Exact live kernel and PR679 source blobs/hashes are in SOURCES.json; selected/catalogue pins are historical provenance. Final 13:45–13:46 UTC snapshots covered 567 open PRs including drafts and 539 Discussion records with complete pagination. ToikY's parallel [clean-subspace claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1901#discussioncomment-18925296) explicitly leaves this full-space result to this work; its clean injective premise is outside our theorem. PR1651's opposite-direction root shears concern another operator. TASK.json records coverage limits; no novelty guarantee is claimed. Main and both named PR heads were rechecked unchanged.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-reciprocal-basis-obstruction
```

Passed on CPython 3.12.10, Windows 11, standard library only: 28,032 dimension-matched spectral fixtures through f=64, all four phases and both child directions; independent cyclic multiplicities; 2,728 native Gaussian matrix entries checked against separately executed butterflies; three complete rational basis identities; independent Gaussian elimination and four nonmonomial correction-rank probes. Six focused tests cover exact eigenspaces, phase/basis mutations, domain and duplicate-key rejection, actual source/inventory and receipt/type corruption, optimized read-only no-Git export and deterministic regeneration. Registered optimized replay, source/metadata pins, selected-record integrity and staged whitespace checks pass. VALIDATION.json records exact receipt hashes.

The all-size proof is written mathematics, not kernel verification or independent human review. Full selected cold replay, new physical/compiler/hosting and precision/tape contracts, Lean and hosted CI were not run locally.

## Credit

Greer Guthrie/PR679; Ross Richardson's contract audit; Jose Manuel (@jmbarrancoml) with publishing account Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337)/PR1779; Josie Elliston/PR1817; icekylinx, DreamingOfClouds and the original kernel/volume lineage; Sagar Thakrar/PR1012, Douglas Colkitt, Rohan Arun, Jeremy Kothe, Hao Yan and retained selected contributors. Arham Tahir/PR1605 supplies the preceding integer price screen. No priority claim for trace invariants, Walsh diagonalization or rank perturbation inequalities.

Prepared by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, proof, code, checks and writing. No subagents. Apache-2.0; existing sources/notices remain intact.

## Open next questions

The README/TASK give two bounded continuations: an independently priced nonreciprocal adapter, or a real opposite-direction boundary with a proved changed volume contract. Arbitrary independent maps can force an invertible target, but legal inexpensive adapters remain missing. The inherited joined-array tariff already rejects the displayed mixed identity with conversions free.

title: Research: sharp clean selector encoding width and volume screen
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For q=2^s same-direction C_n lanes, characterize exactly when one i^u C_d child admits an injective clean invariant encoding. The sharp least literal width has a closed formula. Put N=n+s. With any fourth-root global phase, it is always N+1. With the exact phase it is N+1 for every n>=3; at n=1 exactly selector residues s mod8 in {0,6,7} pass; at n=2 exactly {0,1,5,6,7} pass. The remaining exact-phase cases need N+2. A uniform Pascal-averaging/character proof resolves all positive widths, separately from the finite checks. Sixteen width-one lanes need d=7 with the exact phase, or d=6 with an allowed -1 phase. An explicit dyadic Walsh encoding and left inverse preserve every arbitrary complex payload with a zero complement. Dirty complement generally rotates and is not restored.

The minimum width and the following budget screen are for the literal C_d host, with no independently variable spectator factor. Common spectator fibers extend only as E tensor I with the same factor on both sides. Arbitrary spectator reassignment is outside the theorem: PROOF.md shows an unchanged-volume width-one example and a separate twofold-volume width-two example. This does not minimize a supplier’s physical recursive rank.

Within that contract, the inherited full-volume child-budget ratio is 2^(d-n-s)(d/n)^sigma > 2 for 0<sigma<1, even with every encoder/decoder/phase/preparation expense waived. This compares available upper-bound expressions, not optimal runtime. Scoped algebraic specialization and negative budget result; no physical supplier, 5% construction-gate success or new kappa. title: Research: Q8 mixed targets retain four-call minimum through one extra role
body:
## Result

Adds `research/q8-mixed-three-register-seedcbd5ebc4/`, an exact scoped result in the formal group algebra `F2[Q8]`. For the 36 ordered diagonal triples with positive `{i,j}` word-length profile `(2,1,1)`, the exact local minimum is four paid rank-one calls at `r=3` and `r=4`. A three-call construction would save one call (25%) relative to the direct word; no such construction exists in the enumerated domains.

There is a uniform argument for the 24 triples whose length-two entry is `k` or `-k`: quotienting by the commutator subgroup gives first-order coefficient ranks `1+n_i` and `1+n_j`, where `n_i+n_j=2`. Each paid `i` or `j` factor contributes a rank-one matrix, so the total call count is at least four for every finite role count `r >= 3`. The other 12 triples have central entry `-1`; the same first-order invariant is insufficient, so this package claims the four-call minimum for those only at `r=3` and `r=4`, by exact search.

## Exact search and cost

The complete paid alphabet consists of both labels `i,j` and every binary rank-one idempotent: 56 factors at `r=3` and 240 at `r=4`. Formal group-algebra equality is represented by eight-bit coefficient masks. The search covers all exact depth-one and depth-two states and streams every depth-three extension of each distinct depth-two state, checking all 36 target matrices. Counts are in `EXPECTED.json` and recomputed by `verify.py`.

Each target has a direct four-call upper bound. The verifier includes a two-call positive control, full-convolution cross-checks against the optimized rank-one update, direct replay of all 36 targets, and dropped-call/wrong-target controls. Free scalar `GL_r(F2)` mixing is already covered because conjugation permutes the full rank-one-idempotent alphabet; augmentation forces any terminal scalar map to be the identity.

This is a local formal call count. An additional dirty role has no paid calls in this model, but its physical storage/hosting cost is not priced. The selected bit supplier remains nonbinding, and no supplier placement, finite-size runtime, or kappa improvement is claimed.

## Scope, pins, and overlap

Cycle 13; track `bit-mechanisms`; accepted seed `cbd5ebc4789dc7dac5f7f824ab9561fc`; task `bit-new-register-model`; priority revision 3; base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; catalogue SHA-256 `6686ad58f1fbdbc87134a78901b60fd53a20d3984355e91defbbebc9e9fa8075`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.

The final complete overlap refresh at 2026-10-14T13:57:45Z covered 573 open PRs and 542 Discussions with no warnings; it found this package's own Discussion #1167 claim, but no remote same-scope claim. Other nearby bit results use distinct targets or groups: Discussion #1727 and PR #1716/#1763/Discussion #1774 use AGL2, Discussion #1759 uses UT4, and Discussion #1818 uses D16.

The maintainer-reviewed selected result remains conditional finite and complex-binding at `836330098538459/500000000000000000`. body:

title: Construction: three-stage persistent prefix shear chain (no new kappa)
body:
## Result

This adds a three-stage target-to-source prefix chain for arbitrary dirty F2 rows and arbitrary linear maps. Each updated output feeds the next complete call:

```text
y1 += A1(x)
y2 += A2(y1 updated)
y3 += A3(y2 updated)
```

The exact block map is recorded in the package README. It produces the nested prefix terms `A2 A1 x`, `A3 A2 y1`, and `A3 A2 A1 x` without a clean target, a dirty connector, or an inverse cleanup. More generally, n stages call each `A_i` once, while independent source-path expansion calls it i times.

The complete local bill separates map calls, scalar staging, root program/control, row hosting and handoff adapters. For n=3 the map-call comparison is `c1+c2+c3` versus `c1+2c2+3c3`. The target-hidden expansion also needs three clean scratch rows, three copied target rows, `9L` scalar staging writes/XORs, and six additional full rows; the chain needs no additional row or scalar staging. The L=2 noncommuting U/L/U fixture uses 6 map XORs in the chain versus 12 map XORs plus 18 staging operations in the expansion. Program and allocation costs remain separate charges.

## Provenance and related work

- Track `recursive-interfaces`; task `persistent-boundary`, changed scope; seed `68355377be950fd65aa0152ad8e7c722`; priority revision 3.
- Exact base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.
- Catalogue SHA-256: `6686ad58f1fbdbc87134a78901b60fd53a20d3984355e91defbbebc9e9fa8075`.
- Selected record SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`; selected `kappa` remains `836330098538459/500000000000000000`. Review, source manifest, assembly certificate and their hashes are pinned in TASK/SOURCES.

The scope avoids the live two-call composite cross-feed question in [Discussion #1884](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1884).
