title: Scoped census: late-compensated R439 helper entrances; only #1179's kernel pair survives the carrier-checked class, one triple stays open (no new kappa)
body:
**Scoped negative result with one open survivor. No construction, no new κ, and the selected record is unchanged.**

- Track: bit supplier, seed 9.
- Card: `bit-helper-contract`, with the scope **refined**.
- Base: `0b1cccf8`.
- Package: `research/r439-late-entrance-census-seed09/`.

## The open case this narrows

The inherited H2/K interface requires every helper to start at frame 0, so that a frame-0 prefix D supplies all dirt compensation. An entrance would let a helper start at a nonzero frame instead: a pivot p, with the gauge q ^= p on a support c. That changes the response by ρ = Kc, so the targets in T = supp ρ need compensation from somewhere else.

Merged work decides only T = ∅:
- **#1179** found the kernel entrance 444+470.
- **#1253** proved it unique among common-frame entrances (366 classes).

Two cases were left open by name:
- **#1128** PROOF §4 excludes "compensation moved after A".
- **#1179** says K e_J = 0 is "not a statement about arbitrary later compensation".

This PR **narrows** that case, for **compensation after the scatter** with A and the scatter fixed and one entrance at a time, to one open triple. It covers every one of #1253's 4,954 supports, plus 5,212 enumerated source-donor entrances (5,059 of them placeable), on the selected PR589 word and the four merged star words (#1062, #1122, #1188, #1208). The broader case of #1128 §4, compensation after A but before the scatter, is not covered.

## The test

For each target t, W_t is the **dirt-only space**: the helper parts of all source-free F2 combinations of the values that t can legally read after the scatter. A support is admitted only if every t ∈ T has some u ∈ W_t with u·c = 1.

There are three classes:

| Class | What t may read | Status of a REJECT |
|---|---|---|
| **LC-fav** | any register whose frame at the cut lies in t's final frame t⊥, plus the nine COPY snapshots | **Sound for the whole class** of post-scatter programs with monotone frames and the stated premises (`PROOF.md`: the cone lemma is #1128 §1's dependency-path argument; the monotone-span lemma is the dual of #1128 §2's erasure invariant). This is the necessary test. |
| **A6** | B ++ C unchanged, inserted target reads with a carrier check, read-only relays (reads during C reduce to the end of B: C is at FULL and touches no target, asserted) | Sound for A6. A6 is contained in LC-fav. |
| **A6R** | A6 plus storage relays, with restoration ignored | An over-approximation, used only to keep a survivor open. |

## Results

They are identical on all five words.

| | LC-fav | A6 |
|---|---|---|
| Admitted supports | 444+470 (T = ∅, #1179) and **444+470+578** (\|T\| = 8) | 444+470 only |
| Single helpers / new pairs | 0 / 439, 0 / 1,569 | 0 / 439, 0 / 1,569 |
| Source donors (5,212 enumerated, 5,059 placeable) | 0 kernel, 0 late | 0 kernel, 0 late |
| Relaxation (366 classes) | 1 nonzero class, kernel {444+470, 578} | 1 nonzero class, kernel {444+470} |
| max dim W_t | 5 | 4 |

**The triple 444+470+578 is OPEN.**
- A6 covers 2 of its 8 targets (150 and 197).
- A6R covers all 8.
- A6R restricted to relays inside T covers 4.

So, within A6R (B ++ C fixed, insertion-only target reads), covering all 8 needs storage relays outside T, which must later be restored. LC-fav also allows a rewritten B or C and fresh restored registers, which A6R does not model. It is handed on as open question 1.

**Why so little survives.** Every W_t is a *coordinate* subspace, spanned by at most 5 unit vectors (4 in A6). A target can compensate a support only where the support meets that set, and only 98 (47) of the 18,085 nonzero K incidences do.

## Correctness

- **Two engines.**
  - Engine 1 (`census.py`) does the packed-int replay and the parity census.
  - Engine 2 (`engine2.py`, no shared code) uses set-valued replay, rational annihilators, a kernel-method LC-fav and per-pair change points for A6.
  - They agree on K, the closure (which also equals **#1253's `CERTIFICATE.json`**), every W_t in both classes and every **support verdict**, on all five words. Engine 2 also checks that all 636 frames are closed, so label inclusion equals rational containment.
  - The source donors, the relaxation (checked to contain every admission), the scout class and A6R are computed by engine 1 only.
- **A realisable late entrance, on a synthetic word.** `W_syn` is PR589 with target 150's compensation of 470 moved after the scatter: three B reads into 150, and 470 dropped from D's row 150.
  - The census admits 444+470 there as a *late* entrance (T = {150}) in LC-fav and A6.
  - Its built witness passes the merged `wlib.replay`, and **fails at register 150 without its three late reads**. The witness is: start[444] = 79, the shear and its inverse, three post-scatter reads into 150, and D′ = PR589's D without 444.
  - Honest note: those late reads undo `W_syn`'s own moved compensation, so after B the witness carries the same values as #1179's prefix entrance on PR589. It shows that an admission can be realised; it is not a new construction.
  - Both words are rebuilt in code and checked by canonical sha256.
- **Mutations.** Flipping one K bit rejects the kernel pair. Letting register 77 be read at FULL admits the triple in A6. Emptying target 150's reads rejects the triple. A flipped word byte is rejected.
- **Sanity checks** of the census, true by construction:
  - with every unit vector added to every W_t, all supports are admitted;
  - the kernel pair is admitted;
  - clearing K's column 578 admits 578.
- **Checks run.**
  - `verify.py` gives `PASS_R439_LATE_ENTRANCE_CENSUS` in about 3 min, and RESULT.json is reproduced byte for byte.
  - 20 tests pass.
  - `research_package.py --check-only` passes.
  - The registered python3.12 replay gives `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` in 3 min 15 s.
  - These were run on Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.8 (macOS 26.5, arm64).
- **CI.** A red `verify (…, tests)` job is pre-existing on main (the stale spectrum-audit pin) and is not caused by this package. The repair is #1752.

## Scope

**Covered.** Single common-frame entrances, with fixed A and scatter and no pre-scatter wires, and with the endpoint required on all 661 columns.

**Not covered:**
- a changed A, targets leaving frame 0 before the scatter, a new COPY, or scatter changes beyond added snapshot terms;
- shears after A or at several frames;
- general source-dependent basis changes;
- simultaneous entrances (the joint test is stated in `PROOF.md` but not run);
- recursive interfaces and hosting.

**No κ.** The bit side does not bind, and an entrance's −H1 is cancelled by +H1 in width-8 hosting (#1179, #1253).

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r439-late-entrance-census-seed09/verify.py          # about 3 min; PASS_R439_LATE_ENTRANCE_CENSUS
python3 -I -B -m unittest discover -s research/r439-late-entrance-census-seed09 -p test_package.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-late-entrance-census-seed09
```

## Overlap and credit

- **#1128** (aliromman): this narrows the case its §4 names. Lemma 1 is its §1 argument, and Lemma 2 is the dual of its §2.
- **#1179** (adamgall): the kernel pair. Its stream checks are proposed for a future witness of the triple; they are not run here.
- **#1253** (mightyOil): the closure and its certificate, reproduced here.
- **#1194** (woklerx) and **#1311** (Arham-Tahir64): the semantic-D contract.
- **The star words:** #1062 (ours), #1122 and #1188 (bitplane) and #1208 (ToikY). The helper-star D comes from #967 (theon199), built on #915/#926 (bitplane).
- **The R439 word, scatter and `xcheck_p.py`:** eumemic (#543/#555). The A-section transports and `wlib.py`: DreamingOfClouds (#589).
- **The helper-470/source-77 boundary behind the survivor:** #1043 (aliromman, open), #1079 (bbMisk / Hanson Sun) and #1256 (RossRichardson).
- **Kernel-entrance precedents:** #254 (Dugongue) and #382 (chafreaky).
- **Different mechanisms:** open #1810 (RossRichardson) and #1580/#1592 (Arham-Tahir64).

`find_overlap.py --refresh` found no work on late compensation of R439 entrances.

## Disclosure

Prepared by Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code.
- Parallel read-only scout and judge subagents selected the question; both judges ranked it first.
- Reader subagents and a synthesizer audited the scout's criterion. They found the triple the scout had missed and the missing carrier check in its strict class.
- Both engines, the proof note and the controls were then written fresh.

- A post-PR adversarial review corrected the witness description, the open triple's scope, the citations and the controls (second commit).

No claim was posted to Discussions. New material is Apache-2.0.

## Result

The minimum for PR #1761's noncentral UT4 root pair is **exactly eight paid calls**, including arbitrary finite restored dirty workspace and every nonzero binary rank-one coupling (idempotent or nilpotent).

More generally, for `p` disjoint E13 target roles and `q` disjoint E24 target roles, the sharp separate bounds are

```
n_x >= 2p,  n_y >= 2(p+q),  n_z >= 2q.
```

The direct `xyxy` / `yzyz` coordinate words attain all three bounds. Nonnegative uniform per-label prices therefore give exactly `2p alpha + 2(p+q) beta + 2q gamma`.

This closes #1761's stated five-through-seven gap by a written all-register proof, not a larger finite search. Natural and contragredient representations force `C_xy=C_yx=P`, `C_yz=C_zy=Q`. The **same** middle-label column and row spans must each contain the direct sum of the disjoint target spaces. Their first-order projector sum is zero; rank-nullity then forces `n_y>=2(p+q)`. This is not addition of separate estimates on shared calls.

## Evidence

Only `research/ut4-noncentral-shared-middle/` is added, containing the proof, independent exact representations, complete certificate, source/task/selection/replay metadata and actual validation receipt.

- All 4,096 group products and 4,096 contragredient homomorphism checks.
- All 284 binary rank-one matrices at r=1..4, including 129 nilpotents; 852 formal involutions and 204,672 faithful single-call basis columns.
- All 20,440 two-register words of length0..3 verify coefficient recurrences and span inclusions. This is corroboration, not the universal lower-bound proof.
- 34 full formal/faithful attaining fixtures through eight roles; 8,896 dirty basis columns including two scalar-conjugated targets.
- 18 semantic controls, including omitted calls, dirty workspace restoration, a nonzero formal perturbation killed by both proof representations, a genuine higher-rank shortcut, and a six-call same-role uv witness showing why disjointness is essential.

Executed on CPython **3.12.12**, macOS27 arm64:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -O -B research/ut4-noncentral-shared-middle/verify.py
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-noncentral-shared-middle
```

Both pass:

```
PASS_UT4_SHARED_MIDDLE pair_minimum=8 witnesses=34 dirty_columns=8896 coefficient_words=20440 controls=18 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/ut4-noncentral-shared-middle outcome=negative-result
```

The coordinating parent separately reviewed the shared-span proof and controls and replayed the registered Python3.12 command before granting publication.

## Provenance and scope

- Exact baseline: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.
- Independent OS chooser seed: `5080ba3917adb12fda1e688c38733a49`; track `bit-mechanisms`; emitted card `bit-new-register-model`. Full chooser JSON is preserved. No reroll or seed-based novelty claim.
- Credit **Cinna Davis / @1337isnot1337, #1761** (`0f4f6d79b14573116e47d31d012f8e3f7a49cd87`) for the exact target, q<=4 result, upper witness and explicit gap; **steph4n-gh, #1573** (`0b8c5a69297c794f2de22c04494c83e41300ae36`) for the zero-sum rank method; **Arham Tahir, #1589** (`010ec8c01c0edbbb08b541be236ab78d096f2ca1`) for the nilpotent extension. Earlier register-model attribution is retained in the README.
- #1662/#1680/#1690/#1816 concern the different central E14 target. This is not their result restated.
- Targeted final live checks found the cited heads unchanged and #1761's gap still open.
- Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1759#discussioncomment-18925851 ; round coordination: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1929 .

**Scoped formal-algebra theorem; no new kappa or physical supplier.** All roles, allowed free scalar mixing and paid undo are explicit. No address maps, clean allocation or higher-rank calls are free. Physical/compiler/common-label realization, hosting, precision/tape, selected cold replay, outer analytic transfer, Lean and independent human proof review are not supplied. The two proof representations provide necessary conditions only; full-algebra witnesses are checked separately. No selected record, upstream or frozen source is modified.

title: Audit: P111 Parseval blocks cost 73 in the fixed-block scalar model
body:
## Result: an exact fixed-block scalar-copy obstruction

This independently audits PR #1900 at `9a891c9cb25b15f5a189bcad1d022198adeaf885`. Its **F2 Parseval identity is valid**: reconstruction agrees on all 111 targets and all 661 formal dirty input columns. This is not the complex-field issue in #1889.

The new question is the copy interface. Within each of #1900's five fixed rank-two coefficient blocks, allow any finite sum of inherited scalar copied totals, with factors in that block's two-dimensional binary source and target spans. All basis choices, asymmetric terms and repeated terms are allowed; cross-block rebasing and new operator-valued primitives are not.

The exact block minima are **16, 15, 14, 14, 14**, totaling **73**, versus **74** for the literal ten-channel Parseval expansion and **63** for the selected nine scalar channels. Every finite word reduces by parity to a subset of nine possible rank-one terms: the verifier checks all **2,560 subsets**, the **160 exact factorizations**, and all **30 ordered GL2(F2) bases**. Rational pairing ranks are independently cross-checked by modular elimination on the full Gram support matrices.

The sum of five union-support ranks is indeed 40, but it is **not the invoice of five ordinary scalar copies implementing these rank-two blocks**. Literal one-copy-per-union substitution gives 5,838 wrong source entries and 17,146 wrong full dirty entries. With source port 0 equal to one and all other inputs zero, target 0 receives zero instead of one. The package includes this counterexample and 45 two-bit single-channel witnesses.

**Scope is essential:** this is not a proof that a genuinely new physical block-valued copy must cost two scalar copies, nor a disproof of a possible plane-port supplier. The coefficient planes do not themselves provide physical data-port planes or justify `unpaid=2`. The all-length scalar P111 optimum 63 is credited predecessor work; the new result is the exact pinned five-block audit and its typed-interface counterexamples.

## Favorable paid screen

Keeping the incumbent non-copy children and line-port contract, the best fixed-block scalar interpretation replaces two rank-7 copies by three rank-8 copies. With every *additional* basis, routing, storage, restoration, hosting and precision charge optimistically zero, its exact ceiling is `a <= 0.001401325233`, compared with the original line relaxation `a <= 0.001947467559`. This screen does not treat omitted implementation charges as free in a completed construction. No new supplier, selected frontier, or kappa is claimed.

## Verification

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -O -B research/p111-parseval-copy-interface/verify.py
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python scripts/research_package.py --package research/p111-parseval-copy-interface
```

Observed locally on CPython **3.12.12**, Darwin arm64:

```text

PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p111-parseval-copy-interface outcome=negative-result
```

An isolated optimized generator smoke and registered replay passed. Positive controls preserve the original and Parseval dirty maps. Negative controls cover every one-channel choice, ten optimal-term omissions, a broken frame, omitted block, switched channels, and rational-versus-binary rank. The first metadata wrapper attempt rejected an invalid outcome enum; it was corrected before the successful registered replay. A second agent independently reviewed the scoped proof and ran the registered Python 3.12 replay before publication. No human proof review, full selected cold replay, or unseen CI result is claimed.

title: Research: certify complete multi-donor R439 star absorption linear system and gain-0 chaining (no new kappa)
body:
## Summary

**Scoped replacement-interface census and linear-algebraic exclusion; no new $\kappa$.** Prepared by **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0. Only `research/r439-multi-donor-star-absorption/` is added; `certificates/selected-result.json`, the selected bit supplier (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/589), and `upstream/` are unchanged.

Under the twisted helper contract (`H2-tw / H4-tw / K-tw` of Sagar Thakrar's [PR #1868](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1868), head `6b222d01fee072bcd3a680e6a96ae7d22e13bcac`), omitting a nonempty subset $L_a$ of terminal `D` helper-star restorations on a centre $a$ and toggling source/helper donors across existing pre-first-read `A` writes $W(a)$ restores $a$ before its first read.

This preserves the exact 661-column arbitrary-dirty boundary

$$
(x,y,h)\longmapsto(x,y+x,h)
$$

with unchanged literal `C` **if and only if** the binary indicator vector $c\in\mathbb{F}_2^{\lvert P(a)\rvert}$ over the frame-legal donor pool

$$
P(a)=\lbrace (i,r):i\in W(a),\ r\text{ legal at }A[i]\rbrace
$$

satisfies

$$
\sum_{(i,r)\in P(a)}c_{i,r}\thinspace\mathrm{val}_i[r]
=d_a
\quad\text{in }\mathbb{F}_2^{661},
$$

where

$$
d_a=\bigoplus_{b\in L_a}e_b.
$$

The exact net scalar ADD change is

$$
\Delta\mathrm{ADDs}(c)
=-\lvert L_a\rvert+
\sum_{(i,r)\in P(a)}w_{i,r}c_{i,r},
$$

with

$$
w_{i,r}=
\begin{cases}
-1 & \text{if }r\in S_i,\\
+1 & \text{if }r\notin S_i.
\end{cases}
$$

Open [PR #1868](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1868) tested single-writer substitutions and left open multi-gate splits of $S$ and chaining the gain-0 moves. Open [PR #1913](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1913) (Adam Gall, head `6cde2d14f0090f51672feae32a04f3145e70f595`) excluded two-writer single-donor-per-writer corrections ($\lvert D_i\rvert=\lvert D_j\rvert=1$) on the 11,500-ADD word and left open arbitrary multi-donor correction sets over full-itinerary-legal donors.

## Exact results across three pinned R439 star words

The package evaluates three pinned candidate words:

- **`pr967`**: `research/r439-helper-stars-seed19/candidate.json.gz` (11,783 ADDs, 221 edges, 157 centres).
- **`pr1062`**: `research/r439-bsection-stars-seed01/candidate.json.gz` (11,500 ADDs, 236 edges, 162 centres).
- **`pr1122`**: `research/r439-abc-semantic-bridge/inputs/candidate.json.gz` (10,652 ADDs, 236 edges, 162 centres).

For each word, the package solves the complete unconstrained-size multi-donor, multi-writer $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear system across all pre-first-read writes, with $1\le\lvert W(a)\rvert\le5$, in two modes:

- **`same_path`**: Full-itinerary-legal donors, keeping all 661 register frame paths and paid profile `{1:1323, 2:1342, 3:79, 4:44, 5:102, 6:11, 7:19}` identical.
- **`monotone_all`**: All fixed-gate monotone-climb-legal donors.

### Donor-pool census

| Word | Mode | Star edges | Two-leaf centres | Pool pairs | Zero-bit $b$ | Nonzero-bit unsolvable |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `pr967` (11,783) | `same_path` | 221 | 64 | 1,287 | 147 | 69 |
| `pr967` (11,783) | `monotone_all` | 221 | 64 | 1,744 | 146 | 70 |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `same_path` | 236 | 74 | 1,412 | 158 | 73 |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `monotone_all` | 236 | 74 | 1,894 | 157 | 74 |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `same_path` | 236 | 74 | 1,484 | 134 | 97 |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `monotone_all` | 236 | 74 | 2,013 | 133 | 98 |

Pool pairs are counted as $\sum_a\lvert P(a)\rvert$.

### Solvability and exclusion results

| Word | Mode | Solvable single edges | Solvable two-leaf pairs | Extra from chaining | Dual witnesses |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `pr967` (11,783) | `same_path` | **5** | **0** | **0** | — |
| `pr967` (11,783) | `monotone_all` | **5** | **0** | **0** | 280 |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `same_path` | **5** | **0** | **0** | — |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `monotone_all` | **5** | **0** | **0** | 305 |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `same_path` | **5** | **0** | **0** | — |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `monotone_all` | **5** | **0** | **0** | 305 |

### 1. 890 canonical dual-hyperplane witnesses

Every unsolvable single-leaf target $e_b$ (216 on `pr967`, 231 on `pr1062`, 231 on `pr1122`) and every simultaneous two-leaf target $e_{b_1}\oplus e_{b_2}$ (64 on `pr967`, 74 on `pr1062`, 74 on `pr1122`) carries an explicit dual vector $u\in\mathbb{F}_2^{661}$ in `CERTIFICATE.json`.

Each witness satisfies

$$
\langle u,d_a\rangle=1\pmod 2
$$

and

$$
\langle u,\mathrm{val}_i[r]\rangle=0\pmod 2
\qquad
\text{for all }(i,r)\in P_{\mathrm{mono}}(a).
$$

All witnesses are independently checked by a frozenset oracle in `test_package.py`.

### 2. Complete affine solution spaces on the 5 solvable edges

Exhausting all $2^{\dim\ker}$ solutions proves:

| Edge | Minimum $\Delta\mathrm{ADDs}$ | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| `506 ^= 374` | **-1** | No multi-donor or multi-writer split reaches -2 ADDs |
| `507 ^= 355` | **-1** | No multi-donor or multi-writer split reaches -2 ADDs |
| `514 ^= 367` | **-1** | No multi-donor or multi-writer split reaches -2 ADDs |
| `264 ^= 536` | **0** | Writers `[38, 346]` |
| `326 ^= 530` | **0** | Writers `[98, 334]` |

### 3. Why early `monotone_all` gain-0 moves worsen the paid profile

Under `same_path`, `264 ^= 536` and `326 ^= 530` have unique solutions:

- `264 ^= 536`: `A[346]` at rank-2 frame 153.
- `326 ^= 530`: `A[334]` at rank-2 frame 147.

Both preserve all 661 frame paths and the paid profile.

Their additional `monotone_all` solutions at `A[38]` (rank-1 frame 21) and `A[98]` (rank-1 frame 51) split a `0 -> 2` climb into `0 -> 1 -> 2`.

This changes the paid profile by $-H_2+2H_1$, raising child count from **2,920 to 2,921** at fixed rank mass **5,129**.

### 4. Cross-centre chaining and 5-edge composition

Adjoining all star-leaf vectors

$$
\lbrace e_{b'}:(a',b')\in E\rbrace
$$

of any unread centre $a'\in P_{\mathrm{mono}}(a)$, with `i < first_read(a')`, yields **zero additional solvable single-leaf or two-leaf targets**.

Composing all five `same_path` edges (`composed_all_5`) passes:

- The 661-column forward/reverse literal COPY/ERASE boundary.
- `H2-tw / H4-tw / K-tw`.
- `xcheck_p.py`.

The five-edge composition has identical ADDs (**11,780**, **11,497**, **10,649**), `F / B` bounds, and paid mass **5,129** as the three-edge composition.

## Task card and overlap

- **Track / task / scope key:** `bit-mechanisms` / `bit-helper-contract` / `bfb61f829a81535adeae` (chooser OS nonce `a1c179f07c59db9e5b8720002bb16ab1`, priority revision 3, catalogue SHA-256 `6686ad58f1fbdbc87134a78901b60fd53a20d3984355e91defbbebc9e9fa8075`), scope **refined**.
- **Base commit:** `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea` (`selected-result.json` SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`).
- **Claim:** [Discussion #1166, comment 18925672](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18925672).
- **Overlap refresh:** `scripts/find_overlap.py` refreshed at 2026-10-14 14:22–14:24 UTC (583 open PRs including drafts, 563 discussion records, complete pagination) found no competing multi-donor / gain-0 chaining package. Predecessor heads [PR #1868](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1868) (`6b222d01fee072bcd3a680e6a96ae7d22e13bcac`) and [PR #1913](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1913) (`6cde2d14f0090f51672feae32a04f3145e70f595`) were rechecked unchanged.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-multi-donor-star-absorption --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-multi-donor-star-absorption
```

Expected output:

```text
PASS_R439_MULTI_DONOR_STAR_ABSORPTION words=3 edges=221,236,236 pr1062_pools=1412/1894 solvable=5 two_leaf=0 chained_extra=0 duals=305 ADDs=11500->11497 controls=8 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/r439-multi-donor-star-absorption outcome=completed
```

## Remaining obligations and credit

**No new $\kappa$ is claimed.**

The package does not claim a selected-supplier change, native 5/9/11-stage C++/Boost replay (covered for the three-edge words by [PR #1902](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1902)), hosted emission/invoice, all-size compiler, precision/tape, or analytic transfer.

title: Research: COPY84 floor for low-rank matched P112 support frames
body:
## Result

One new exact package: `research/p112-matched-frame-copy-floor/`, on base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.

For any finite masked P112 decoder over C with ordinary transpose, suppose every paid rank-one term has **equal F2 source/target support spans** and pairing-rank COPY cost at most four. Actual supports need not coincide or be tetrad-local. Arbitrary coefficients, cancellations and zero-cost corrections are allowed.

The package proves

`n1 + 2 n2 + 4 n3 + 5 n4 >= 112`, hence **COPY >= 84**.

Its rank-relaxation optimizer is uniquely 28 rank-three terms; this is **not a constructed COPY84 decoder**. The COPY moment is at least **21/16** of the incumbent eight rank-eight copies, for every `0 <= a < 1` at unchanged normalization. A common-span radical quotient and the characteristic-vector complement relation give the rank-four lifted capacity five, rather than the naive eight.

The fully charged optimistic retained-template ceiling is `[0.000736244670745, 0.000736244670746]`, below the unchanged five-percent target `0.00177455681454345`. Both local COPY mass and centre charge rise from 64 to 84; idle mass stays 1646. Every additional physical charge is waived only to make this rejection favorable. **No new kappa, supplier admission, physical frame contract, frontier change or positive construction-gate success is claimed.**

## Exact evidence

- All 12,544 root/label/coordinate entries, including masked target `4I_112`.
- All **452** nonsingular nonalternating symmetric F2 forms through dimension four; lifted rank capacities **1,2,4,5**.
- Exact P112 witnesses attaining each per-term capacity, including distinct actual supports with the same label span.
- Fraction row elimination plus independent odd-prime column rank corroboration.
- Semantic controls for missing/wrong diagonal terms, wrong mask, arbitrary zero-cost correction and undercharged centre.
- Explicit unmatched-span rank-two/lift-three and matched rank-five/lift-ten counterexamples showing why the scope restrictions matter.

## Reproduction actually exercised

On **CPython 3.12.12**, Darwin arm64:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -B research/p112-matched-frame-copy-floor/verify.py --write
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -O -B research/p112-matched-frame-copy-floor/verify.py
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-matched-frame-copy-floor
```

Direct and registered replays passed:

`PASS_P112_MATCHED_FRAME_COPY_FLOOR forms=452 entries=12544 capacities=1,2,4,5 COPY>=84 moment_ratio>=21/16 controls=7 no_new_kappa`

`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-matched-frame-copy-floor outcome=negative-result`

The coordinating parent independently reviewed the quantified proof and repeated the registered Python 3.12 replay before granting publication. This is not independent human review or a proof-assistant theorem. Native/hosted CI and the selected full cold replay were not run or claimed.

## Selection, overlap and limits

Independent one-shot chooser seed **`5cee555544503585ad60b2631e790c0c`**; track **complex-mechanisms**; emitted and chosen card **complex-rank-shape-decoder**. Complete chooser JSON, exact source pins, TASK scope refinement and replay manifest are included.

This uses the card's allowed scoped support-alphabet lower bound, not its positive five-percent construction gate. It is distinct from #1909 (one-tetrad locality with arbitrary opposite support), #1923 (a finite Householder orbit of one symmetric witness), and #1633 (all-pairs outside-root-code ranks). Targeted cached/local searches and live predecessor head checks found no same-scope result; no literature-priority guarantee is implied.

Unmatched support spans, COPY rank at least five, other punctures, nonseparate copy accounting and changed role/coverage interfaces remain outside the theorem. A high-rank mask fixture is not a decoder. README includes exact proof, physical limitations and concrete open next questions.

Base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18925921

## Bottleneck

The selected record has one stage after #1042: `complex-t16-rare-pattern-exchanges/verify.py`, which runs the frozen PR1087 `verify_t16.py`. Its slowest sub-stage is `audit`: 32.6 s of 57.6 s in the maintainer receipt. The script is `audit_allcold.py`, SHA-256 `1467a2ac…`. The cold baseline1042 `t16` stage runs the same bytes from `research/gauge44-slots-t16/code/`.

cProfile puts about 80% of this sub-stage in `copy.deepcopy`. Each of the 15 mutation controls copies the whole hosted T16 template, and each of the 16 audits copies every source event: 4,838 top-level calls in total.

## Change

New package `research/audit-allcold-fast-copy/`. Its `fast_copy.py` is an opt-in drop-in for `python3 -B run_portable.py SCRIPT ARGS…`:

- It checks `run_portable.py` and the script against a SHA-256 allow-list, then runs the pinned `run_portable.py` unchanged.
- It replaces only `copy.deepcopy`. For a top-level dict or list, the copy is `marshal.loads(marshal.dumps(x))`. That copy is kept only if marshal accepts the value (core builtin types only), the copy has the same type, and it compares equal. Otherwise, and for any call with a memo, the original `deepcopy` runs.
- marshal keeps aliasing through back-references, as deepcopy does.
- No verifier source is edited, nothing is cached, and no check or control is skipped.

## Evidence (`verify.py`, registered replay)

1. **Fixture.** It extracts the archived gauge44 provider files from `selected-replay.tar.gz` and runs the unchanged selected final stage on them. The stage must print `PASS_T16_RARE_PATTERN_EXCHANGES 0.001672660197076918`, and its `ASYNC-AUDIT.json` must equal the archived selected receipt byte for byte.
2. **A/B.** It reruns the audit sub-stage on fresh copies of the same inputs with verify_t16's exact environment, alternating legacy and fast. Both must reproduce the in-stage outputs byte for byte: `ASYNC-AUDIT.json`, `OWNERS-AND-PROFILE.json`, `IDLE-REMAINDER-FRAMES.json`, the regenerated `IDLE-REMAINDER-FRAMES.json.gz` (same environment) and the merged stdout/stderr log. All 4,838 calls must take the marshal path.
3. **Controls.**
   - A tampered hosted template is rejected by both launchers.
   - An unpinned script is refused.
   - An identity copier (no copying) is detected. The pinned audit itself still exits 0 in that case, but writes a corrupted report (provider count 143 rather than 144, and one idle frame missing), so the byte comparison is load-bearing.
   - Copy semantics are checked: aliasing and independence, plus fallback for a dict subclass, NaN, a custom object, a cyclic list and an explicit memo.

Measured on macOS (Apple silicon), same host and fixture, 3 alternating rounds, with identical outputs every round:

| Interpreter | Legacy audit (s) | Fast audit (s) | Median |
|---|---|---|---:|
| CPython 3.12.13 | 22.37, 22.27, 22.50 | 9.05, 9.06, 9.21 | **2.47x** |
| CPython 3.14.7 | 17.85, 18.31, 17.79 | 9.43, 9.46, 9.47 | **1.89x** |

Commands run:
- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/audit-allcold-fast-copy`: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, about 80 s.
- `--check-only`: pass.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 42 tests OK, 2 skips.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

## Limitations / not checked

- **Not wired in.** The launcher is not used by `make frontier1094-verify`, because the frozen `verify_t16.py` calls `run_portable.py` directly. Wiring it in needs an opt-in driver or a maintainer decision (open question 1).
- **One script hash.** The allow-list has the single audited script. The nine other `audit_allcold.py` variants were not checked.
- **No fresh cold baseline.** The fixture's `--local` input comes from the archived selected replay. It is bound by the archived `ASYNC-AUDIT.json` equality, not by a fresh cold baseline1042 run. A full cold `make frontier1094-verify` was not rerun.
- **Indirect inputs.** verify_t16's own `UPSTREAM-PINS.json` dependencies are enforced by the stage itself, but they are not declared as this package's CI inputs.
- **Untested hosts.** Linux and Windows timings were not measured here.

## Credit

The audited code is from the retained gauge44 / PR1087 lineage:
- the `audit_allcold.py` controller audit and its mutation controls (OpenAI Codex in the original packages);
- Hao Yan's (@FanPUYen) PR858 T16 controller;
- the `run_portable.py` wrapper from `complex-k492-owner-repair`;
- PR1094 (Rohan Arun) on Jeremy Kothe's k8/T16 construction;
- the maintainer's frontier1094 audit receipt.

The opt-in, byte-identical adapter pattern follows #1880, #1874, #1646 and `frontier1042-lec-parallel`.

Prepared by jackmgaller with substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance. Apache-2.0.

**Workflow feedback (optional).** The task chooser and overlap helper worked well. The biggest friction was getting the final stage's `--local` input without a 20-minute cold baseline. The archived `selected-replay.tar.gz` provider files solved it. Suggestion: document that fixture route in the bottleneck brief for replay-runtime work.

title: Research: sharp even finite-dihedral tariffs with dirty workspace
body:
## Result

For every **even** rotation period `n`, the formal `F2[D_{2n}]` register model with paid reflections only `x,y`, arbitrary binary rank-one idempotents, free scalar mixing, and any finite restored dirty workspace has the sharp separate bills for heterogeneous diagonal targets `r^k_i x^e_i`:

- x calls: `sum d_n(k_i+e_i)`
- y calls: `sum d_n(k_i)`

Here `r=xy`, `e_i in {0,1}`, and `d_n` is cyclic distance to zero. Coordinate words simultaneously attain both bounds, hence all nonnegative per-letter tariffs are exact.

The uniform lower-bound proof uses two n-address permutation representations with offsets `c=n/2` and `c=n/2-1`, plus subadditive balanced-cut ranks. The offsets matter for `n=2 mod 4`; n=2,6,10 controls are included. Arbitrary scalar projectors contribute exactly their rank across the active cut, so this is not merely a coordinate-call argument or a finite-search extrapolation.

## What is new

This closes the explicitly open **finite-torsion** question in #1911 (`712593f8`): its infinite-dihedral Laurent invariant does not descend through `r^n=1`. The new finite cut invariant does. In particular #1821's D16 central pair retains its 16-call minimum with arbitrarily many dirty roles, and the theorem covers all even periods and heterogeneous endpoints.

The all-register **D8 central-target** special case was already proved by steph4n-gh in #1573; it is credited, not claimed anew. Arham Tahir's #1919 rank-bounded D8 invocation tariff is distinct and also credited. #1792's stale-handoff warning was checked, along with local/merged #1443 and live all-state overlap.

## Evidence and reproduction

Only `research/finite-dihedral-cut-bound/` is added: written proof, standard-library verifier, deterministic receipt, full chooser selection, TASK/SOURCES/VERIFY metadata, and actual validation record.

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -I -B research/finite-dihedral-cut-bound/verify.py
uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python scripts/research_package.py --package research/finite-dihedral-cut-bound
```

Both direct and registered optimized replay passed on macOS arm64 / **CPython 3.12.12**:

- 1,027 complete formal forward/inverse dirty fixtures; 134,864 faithful-regular basis columns.
- 9,420 complete short mixed words, 47,872 representation products, and 1,088 target cut ranks.
- 3,720 rank-one call checks over all 155 projectors through four roles; all 174 scalar invertible maps through three roles; 1,088 additional arbitrary-idempotent rank checks.
- 9,249 omitted-call controls and 13 semantic/model controls reject; a corrupted receipt also rejects under `-O`.
- A nonzero invertible dirty shear hidden by **both** proof representations is detected by full formal and faithful-regular checks, guarding against represented-endpoint false positives.

The universal theorem is the written proof, not inferred from finite checks. No native supplier, selected cold replay, hosted CI, Lean, or independent human proof review is claimed.

## Provenance and limits

- Exact base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.
- Independently sampled seed: `63537661f5ee8acaa486b70f82726911`; track `bit-mechanisms`; emitted card `bit-new-register-model`; target-specific relaxation method.

**No new kappa or selected-supplier change.** Odd periods, arbitrary free address maps, nonlinear invocation tariffs, and physical/compiler/frame/hosting/precision/tape admission remain outside scope. The lower bound grants scalar mixing free only as an optimistic formal relaxation; the attaining word needs no clean state, extra workspace, COPY, or uncharged restoration.

title: Construct shared-product fanout through dirty output anchors
body:
## Result

**Exact local construction; no selected-provider admission or new kappa.** This package fans one common bilinear product out to q arbitrary-dirty output rows without a clean anchor or helper. For

```text
A_i' = A_i XOR p(x,y) XOR t_i(u_i,v_i),  i=0,...,q-1,
```

it uses two row-XOR waves around one complete child that toggles p into A0, then computes the q private terms:

```text
for i=1..q-1: A_i ^= A_0       # compensate the old dirty anchor
child:        A_0 ^= p
for i=1..q-1: A_i ^= A_0       # deliver p from the updated anchor
for i=0..q-1: A_i ^= t_i
```

The exact invoice is q+1 child calls and 2(q-1) full-width row ADDs, versus 2q child calls directly. The net charged saving is (q-1)(mu-2 alpha(w)); no child/ADD price ratio is assumed. For q=112 this is 224 versus 113 child calls plus 222 row ADDs. A Hamming-weight argument proves that 2(q-1) row ADDs are minimal for one common child in the target-row XOR alphabet, without scratch, COPY or CLEAR.

## Conditional profile screen

If eight hypothetical 112-port blocks occur, the rank-one profile changes from n1=2412 to n1=1524. The pinned rank-only ceiling brackets change from [1690054109/1000000000000, 169005411/100000000000] to [2026751029/1000000000000, 202675103/100000000000]. The dirty schedule also adds 1,776 scalar XORs at width one, retained as a separate linear term. No matching selected-provider occurrence or finite base-width mu/alpha comparison is established, so no supplier, frontier or kappa claim follows.

## Evidence and reproduction

- `PROOF.md` gives the symbolic identity and row-ADD lower bound. `verify.py` exhausts 281,600 arbitrary child-output/dirty-target assignments through q=5 and widths one or two, checks inverse execution, rejects four malformed schedules, checks exact operation counts for q=2..112, and recomputes both pinned ceiling brackets.
- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-output-anchor-seed-da1ec3f0 --check-only` — PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS.
- `python3 -I -B research/dirty-output-anchor-seed-da1ec3f0/verify.py` and `python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-output-anchor-seed-da1ec3f0/verify.py` — PASS.
- `python3 -I -B research/complex-local-word-ceiling/verify.py` — PASS.

Local replay used CPython 3.14.7. The registered package workflow specifies Python 3.12, unavailable locally; hosted CI is not yet claimed.

## Provenance and distinction

Base commit `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. The package pins the selected review, source manifest, assembly certificate and the ceiling model. The selected result remains unchanged.

- PR #1907 uses a clean required-output anchor. This construction allows every output to be arbitrary dirty and pays a second fanout wave.
- PR #1872 uses a clean helper and inverse cleanup. This construction uses a dirty output and no helper.
- PR #1930 studies a three-stage linear prefix chain; PR #1917 studies a cross-fed parity connector.
- The adjacent active claim at Discussion #1167 comment 18926048 broadcasts a common linear map from a separate dirty scratch row across distinct source-prefix states, then restores that scratch with a second map call. This scope instead uses a required output row as the carrier for one common bilinear term, adds private products per output, requires no scratch or cleanup, and proves the minimum row-ADD count for the single-child target-row-XOR alphabet.

The final overlap refresh completed at `2026-10-14T14:34:38Z`, covering 590 open PRs and 567 Discussions with no warnings; the adjacent claim was manually checked at `14:35:43Z`. This is bounded overlap evidence, not a novelty certificate. The package is prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review is claimed. Apache-2.0.

title: Research: exact heterogeneous Clifford child interface classification
body:
## Result and exact scope

Adds only `research/complex-heterogeneous-child-interface/`: a complete **unequal-width** classification for one inherited Clifford tensor child under arbitrary reciprocal linear encoding, plus exact source and volume accounting.

For two equal-volume lanes with canonical operators `C_p` and `C_q^epsilon`, `1 <= p < q`, and a candidate child `lambda C_d tensor I_t` with positive integers **d>=1, t>=1**, arbitrary restored dirty identity padding does not help. Width-zero scalar children are outside this declared contract:

- Same directions never fit one phased child, even granting arbitrary invertible encoding and its inverse.
- Opposite directions fit exactly when `q=p+1` and `p=1 or 2 mod4`, or `q=p+2` and `p=1 mod4`. The child width is necessarily `q+2`, with the explicit phase in the proof, and its active volume is the sum of both original lane volumes.
- Three full rational basis witnesses attain the exceptional cases. For example, `(C_1 tensor I_4) direct-sum (C_2^-1 tensor I_2)` is similar to `-C_4` on 16 coordinates.
- Even with both encoders and every other extra charge free, the inherited available child expression `2 A V(q+2)^sigma` exceeds `A V(p^sigma+q^sigma)` for `0<sigma<1`. This is an **upper-bound-expression comparison**, not an optimal-runtime lower bound.

The proof uses Gaussian-prime valuation to force the new width and exact four-trace multiplicities for necessity/sufficiency. It is not extrapolation from the finite sweep.

title: Prove a diagonal-span projection barrier for the PR117 word
body:
Restricting a completed commuting phase word to fewer address coordinates preserves its algebraic identity, but can add internal frame cost. I prove that every nonzero binary row-isometric restriction within the 24 diagonal tensor axes fails positive coverage for the original PR117 carrier schedule.

For each nonzero projection column, the first-stage helper paths force at least 317,823,660 extra rank units. The data can save at most 32,388,554 units per odd-norm column. The resulting margin, 285,435,106 per nonzero column, excludes even the zero-saving moment. The proof grants free centres and permits constant gauges, bank concatenation and catalytic helpers; it retains the original scalar incidences and commuting frames.

The six-file package includes the proof, attribution and a standard-library verifier. It regenerates the exact 71,185-arc matching and 28,705 physical carrier paths from the pinned DAG, then recomputes all 24 coordinate defects. Reviewers need no C++ compiler or bundled matching fixture.

title: Audit: selected bootstrap cutoffs omit the carried constant (κ unchanged)
body:
**Scoped audit of one finite lemma instantiation in the selected record. κ, the certificate, the suppliers and the selected frontier are unchanged.**

Package: `research/bootstrap-cutoff-carry/`. Base main `0b1cccf8`. Card `uniform-transfer-audit` (chooser nonce `9c18a425e1fae055c7b797453ed1df50`, priority revision 3), scope refined. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18926613

## Question

The selected `research/community-frontier1094-audit/ASSEMBLY.json` records 14 finite bootstrap cutoffs, seven per branch. Frozen PR1087 `code/assemble.py` computes them as `max(ceil(36/gap^2), ceil(2*(4+512)/gap))`, which takes `ceil(log2 C) = 512` at every stage.

The lemma they instantiate appears in PR387's PROOF and in `five-stage-source527-banks/proof/FINITE_BIT_ACCOUNTING.md`. There, C dominates "previous ordinary constants", and the next constant is `C_large + C_old*2^(L*(a_(j+1)-a_j))`. Do the recorded cutoffs satisfy that rule once the carried factor enters the next stage's C?

## Result (exact rationals, stdlib)

- All 14 recorded cutoffs reproduce from the receipt and the formula. Stage 1 is valid in both branches.
- **Stages 2–7 fail in both branches (12 of 14)**, even with the most favorable carry (`C_old = 1`, no `C_large`, the recorded smaller previous cutoff). The shortfall ratio is 1.996649 at every failing stage.
- **Closed form.** The gaps satisfy `δ_(i+1) = sδ_i` and the steps satisfy `Δa = (1−s)δ/s`, so the quadratic cutoff `⌈36/δ²⌉` can never pay the carry when `s < 1/2`. The shortfall tends to `2(1−s)`. Every lineage that uses this formula with a fixed allowance should therefore fail the same way, including T37 (1024) and the deeper chains in #1424, #1586 and #1724. Only the selected record is checked here.
- **Corrected chain.** The exact minimal cutoffs that carry the constant are about `2^(i−1)` times the recorded ones; stage 7 has 48 digits instead of 46. This assumes fresh per-stage constants below `2^512`, as the receipt does.
- **The numerical κ calculation is unaffected.** The pinned outer engine takes no cutoff input, and κ reproduces exactly from the chain end. The asymptotic statement needs only some finite cutoff per stage, but it still rests on the bootstrap lemma under one of the repairs below.

This is a receipt/proof-text inconsistency, conditional on the lemma's wording. It does **not** establish that the bound fails. There are two repairs:

- (a) carry `C_old` into the cutoff, which gives the corrected chain above;
- (b) restate the lemma so that previous-algorithm tolls are absorbed against the new constant. This is the usual "large induction constant" argument, and we expect it to work. It would leave the recorded numbers valid, but it is **not** written here.

## Evidence

- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bootstrap-cutoff-carry` prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `--check-only` passes.
- `verify.py` passes on CPython 3.10–3.14.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 42 tests OK.
- Six controls are rejected: a tampered recorded cutoff, the next-grid κ, a shifted starting saving, a corrected cutoff minus one (which shows minimality), the recorded cutoffs under the carry rule, and an outer signature with a cutoff input. As a positive check, dropping the carry from the corrected chain reproduces the receipt's 14 cutoffs exactly.
- `scan_receipts.py` (supplementary, unregistered) checks stages 3 onward of every in-repo `research/*/ASSEMBLY.json` that records cutoffs: 12 receipts and 23 branches, including the #741–#1042 frontier audits and T37's 1024-bit receipt. It uses recorded exponents only. All 114 such stages fail the minimal carry.
- One independent read-only review by OpenAI Codex confirmed the lemma reading and the index (`L_j(a_(j+1)−a_j)`) and the closed form. Its must-fix and should-fix items are applied: the finding is stated as conditional on the lemma's wording, the closed-form scope is narrowed, "least" is qualified, the κ claim is narrowed to the numerical calculation, and a vacuous control was replaced by an in-memory mutation of the outer engine source.

## Not checked

- Whether repair (b) holds.
- The actual fresh per-stage constants.
- Open PRs' receipts. The in-repo scan covers stages 3 onward only and is unpinned.
- Every inherited all-size, precision, hosting and analytic obligation of the selected record.

## Overlap

`complex-t37-validation/check_bootstrap_reserve.py` (Tekalign) and `frontier1042-invoice-audit-seed81` (Wronskode) check the same cutoffs against a *fixed* allowance; those checks are correct as stated. `bootstrap-depth-audit` and `t37-bootstrap-depth-seed60` study depth, not cutoffs. A fresh overlap refresh found no work on the carried constant.

## Credit

The cutoff lemma and the next-constant rule are from rohanarun's PR387 and eumemic's five-stage bank proof. The chain and the 512 allowance come from the frozen PR1087 assembler (Jeremy Kothe's package and its lineage) and Rohan Arun's PR1094 receipt.

Prepared by Josie Elliston with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance.

title: Research: local-move exhaustion on the pivot-566+554 T74 supplier (0 gains in 4,461 exact moves, 107 compensation searches) and idle-optimal 249/417 dispatch (no new kappa)
body:
## Research: local-move exhaustion on the pivot-566+554 T74 supplier, and idle-optimality of the 249/417 dispatch (no new κ)

Since PR1800, κ ≈ b(supplier) up to the free slacks, so only a cheaper T74 supplier can raise it. This package gives exact, reproducible negative results for the cheap local move families on the current base and extra words, which are the same bytes as PR1839/PR1672. It also gives an ILP certificate that the owner packing's idle side is already optimal.

**Results** (`research/t74-k554-local-exhaustion/RESULTS.json`; raw data in `data/`)

- **Deletion relaxation of all 1,797 B reads** (exact frames). 1,002 deletions would lower cost.
  - Exactly 16 save one rank-2 split (−4,913 units): the early pivot reads of 448/450/452/454/585/587/589/591/473/497/521/545/586/588, plus the two costly reads inside the 566/554 kernels (B1, B3).
  - The rest are delivery reads, first writes and structural reads, from −3,050 to −26,389.
  - All 1,002 send value into target rows, so compensation must stay inside B. None can be moved to the frame-free cleanup prepends.
- **Frame-cost oracle**, calibrated exactly on PR1672's pivot-554 kernel. Its insert costs are `[0, 4913, 0, 0]`, so the kernel's whole cost is one rank-2 split. The cost-aware search rediscovers a −1,850 kernel by itself.
- **107 cost-aware compensation searches:** no negative delta. Every one-split read needs at least one split to compensate. Large-gain reads have single-window source values or rows that no candidate can reach.
- **Exact single-gate commuting-move sweep:** all 1,002 gain-carrying reads at all 4,461 window positions, exact solver. Results: 2,131 neutral, 2,330 infeasible, **0 gains**.
- **A section:**
  - A1220/1226/1232/1238/1244 are cold-pivot pre-cancels, each saving 6,763 if deleted. Compensating them across A, B and tails, with full-program exactness and the dirt rule, is infeasible.
  - 91 rewrites of a cancelling read pair into reads of the pivot's writer are all frame-infeasible.
- **Owner packing (aggregate ILP over all T74 child windows):**
  - Moving any K = 12, 24, … extra calls to base is infeasible.
  - Over every mix of the 0–4 entrance-demotion variants (W_res 3734–3738), the maximum number of empty rank-48 children is **22,748**. That is the current value, attained by 249 base / 417 extra.
  - So no supplier-mix or modulo-48 rebalancing can add idle rank-48 children.

**Reproduce:** `python3 -B research/t74-k554-local-exhaustion/verify.py --work /abs/new/work`. It takes about 5 minutes on 2 cores and checks:
- pins and profiles;
- the oracle calibration;
- 32+32 sampled exact re-solves;
- the 16 one-split searches;
- the packing ILPs;
- result consistency.

`--full` re-solves everything and takes several CPU hours. The receipt is in `evidence/`.

**Scope:** finite searches of the stated move families on two fixed words. This does not rule out multi-gate rewrites outside these families, new kernel mechanisms, or parent/centre-interface changes such as centre-path sharing (PR1708/1748/1791). No κ is claimed and no construction is changed.

**Credit:** PR1186 (toolkit, vendored verbatim), PR1625 (mdumitrean), PR1672 (jeremykothe2 / LeverRank), PR1319/PR1297/PR1193, and PR1839/PR1800. Prepared by Rohan Arun with substantial AI assistance (Anthropic Claude). Apache-2.0.

title: Audit: mutant coverage of the selected T16 controller/owner audit (no gap found, no new kappa)
body:
**Adversarial audit (card `supplier-boundary-audit`, scope refined), with no κ, certificate, supplier or frontier change.** Josie Elliston (JosieElliston), with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance, in a donated session.

Base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected record SHA-256 `10b9e340…`. Chooser nonce `5f419d173f49750373ab915c29fb04d7`, priority revision 3. Branch `research/t16-audit-coverage-s28`, head `6e66ea56`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18926402

## Question

The selected record's only post-#1042 stage, `research/complex-t16-rare-pattern-exchanges/verify.py`, runs the frozen PR1087 `code/audit_allcold.py` (SHA-256 `1467a2ac…`) through `verify_t16.py`, with 15 mutation controls. Which of the audit's acceptance predicates do those controls actually reach? For each predicate they miss, is a targeted semantic mutant rejected?

## Package `research/t16-audit-mutant-coverage/`

`verify.py` is stdlib only and takes about 70 s. The fixture is the selected hosted template archived in `research/community-frontier1094-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz`, so no cold run is needed. The pinned audit runs unchanged and in-process. The harness executes the shipped control block verbatim, with only `def reject` renamed, and records the `audit_allcold.py` line that rejects each mutant.

| Mutant set | Count | Rejected | Accepted | Further lines with an `assert` reached first |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shipped controls | 15 | 15 | 0 | 8 of 42 |
| New targeted semantic mutants | 35 | 34 | 1 | 20 |
| One-field template census | 111 | 92 | 19 | 6 |

- **Positive control.** The in-process audit reproduces every field of the archived selected `ASYNC-AUDIT.json` except the two mutation-run fields.
- **Shipped controls are concentrated.** Four of the 15 are rejected first by line 94 (the whole provider-registry equality). Three are rejected by line 152 and three by line 159.
- **First exercised here.** Each of these is rejected at the intended assertion:
  - the idle window from both sides (line 156);
  - the wrong side of the idle pair, and a helper past the child's rank (line 156);
  - overlapping axis cells across calls (line 163);
  - a gap in the pending prefix (line 178);
  - schedule list order and retiming (lines 114, 121, 122 and 129);
  - pooled-slot count, key and field binding (lines 169 to 173).
- **Accepted: 19 path mutations.**
  - Pooled-slot `time`: line 172 omits it, so the audit alone accepts changed times.
  - 15 fields `audit()` never reads, such as `cover`, `m`, `version`, `port_restriction`, `replica_lift`, `hosting.owner_map_sha256` and `hosting.rule`. A text search of the PR1087 archive and the maintainer frontier1094 scripts finds no reader of these in the hosted template after `emit`.
  - Three partial checks: appended text in `loop_order` (only one sentence is required), and an extra key in `hosting` or in `async_schedule`.
- **A cross-stage link that no selected stage checks.** The audit checks the hosted template, while `lift16`, `independent-t16` and the maintainer composition (PR1091 auditor) check the frozen `data/OWNERS.json.gz`. The verifier checks that the template's `pooled_slots` is exactly that owner list: 69,120 roles, with `time` fields included. It also checks that `owner_map_sha256` names the list's gzip. Both hold.
- **Unreachable by template-only mutation.** Eight of the 42 lines with an `assert` cannot be reached this way, each for a stated reason. Three depend only on base inputs, and five are implied by earlier assertions or by construction.

**Outcome:** no missing implication was found for the selected fixture. This is line coverage: a line with a compound condition, such as 94, 152 or 156, does not get one mutant per conjunct. The audit alone would accept changed pooled times. The fixture-level owner binding is a separate check in `verify.py`.

## Checks

- `python3 -B research/t16-audit-mutant-coverage/verify.py`: `EXPECTED.json` is byte-identical on CPython 3.10.21, 3.12.14 and 3.14.7 (macOS arm64).
- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t16-audit-mutant-coverage`, both the check and the replay, passes.
- The 42 research unit tests pass.
- An independent read-only Codex review found no outcome-changing discrepancy in the shipped-control wrapper, the line attribution, the new mutants or the eight unreachable-line claims. Its must-fix (line totals) and two should-fixes (narrower "no reader" wording, separating the fixture binding from what `audit()` implies) are applied.

**Not checked:**
- mutations of base inputs (DATA-PHASES, providers, parent);
- the module-level provider checks;
- the invoice, assembly and indep16 stages;
- the #1042 ancestry;
- Linux or Windows;
- a cold `make frontier1094-verify`.

## Open next questions

1. The same receipt for the nine other `audit_allcold.py` hashes in the repository (PR1939's handoff).
2. A successor driver binding template `pooled_slots` to `OWNERS.json.gz`. This needs a maintainer decision, because the frozen code stays unchanged.
3. Mutation testing for `invoice_allcold.py`, which carries the prefix and row inequalities and has no mutation-control block of its own.

## Credit

- Audited checker: the PR1087 archive's `code/`, byte-identical to Jeremy Kothe's #870 code. Its docstring credits OpenAI Codex, and it includes the T16 edits from Hao Yan's (@FanPUYen) #858.
- Selected exchanges and run: Rohan Arun's #1094, with the run archived by the maintainer's frontier1094 audit.
- Copy-cost observation: jackmgaller's PR1939. The harness copies by `marshal`, following it.
- Interpreter stability of the stage: session 26's PR1824.
- Independent OWNERS recount: PR1091.

## Change and mathematical scope

**Audit for the complex supplier. No new κ, and the selected record is
unchanged.** This adds one registered package,
[`research/selected1094-extended-labels-seed65/`](research/selected1094-extended-labels-seed65/README.md).
No selected record, supplier, pinned file or `upstream/` file changes.

**(a) H1 holds for the selected programs.** Lemma G's Theorem 1 (Lean
`LemmaG.Stream.conj_matrix`) needs two hypotheses:

- **H1:** the emitted stream is `WellLabelled` in the extended labels
  (tag × frame);
- **H2:** every recipe is exact.

The package regenerates the selected seven-slot word's emitted forward and
backward local programs from committed bytes, using the pinned PR635 tools. It
reproduces all four selected hashes: canonical `4ddb29fb`, programs `071ecdac` /
`f36c5831`, and `CLIFFORD-RECIPES` `d0768f21`.

An independent HPE-aware extended-label checker finds **0 violations in both
orientations**. That covers 24,767 events each, including 1,497 / 3,924 source
writes and 240 wrapped helpers, 48 of them cold hyperplane-ended. The result
holds under both the literal and the most permissive Lean reading of private
clears.

- **Lemma S.** A structural lemma extends the tag part to every word the pinned
  transport and emitter accept.
- **Theorem R.** With `conj_matrix`, the H2 recipe pin (independently checked by
  my open #1781) and an exact scalar shadow, this gives per-call common-label /
  mutable-source realization of the complex local programs. It holds on ℂ^{2^9}
  and ℂ^{2^9} ⊗ V for arbitrary dirty inputs.
- **Still inherited, named and not discharged:**
  - all-size recipe execution;
  - whole-call hosting (Lemma A (O′), (W));
  - cross-call composition;
  - precision and tape;
  - Lemma A (N);
  - the **bit supplier's** mutable-basis realization (#535's carryover note).

**(b) The selected chain runs no tag check.** Lemma G assigns the tag half of H1
to `check_extended_labels.py`, which cannot parse HPE words (see (c)). The HPE
package maps only G0 in `cleanup_tail` to the local audit, and every operand
there has tag T.

The chain's emitted-program check, PR635's frame-only `hpe_audit_local.py`,
does not substitute for a tag check. It **accepts three scalar-neutral mutants**
of the forward program (exit 0, PASS, 25 controls). Their scalar shadows equal
the honest data shear, yet each is physically wrong:

| mutant | `label_check` permissive / strict | patched Lemma G checker | exact witness |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| X: exit straddle, target 112 at frame 778 | 2 / 4 | 4 | target ends at `a`, not `N_t⁻¹ a`; at `a = e_0`, `i³e_1` is expected |
| Y: entry straddle, source 0 at frame 9 | 2 / 2 | 4 | `M_0` skipped; wrong at `h_0 = e_1` (`M_0 e_1 = i e_10`) |
| Z: exit adapters of registers 0..112 moved before a phase-B add on `L_112` | 113 / 113 | 113 (50 capped) | honest − mutant = `(I − A_t) b/2`; target ends at `(i³e_1 − e_0)/2` instead of 0 |

The pinned emitter cannot produce these mutants from any word, so κ is
unaffected. This is a coverage gap in admission.

**Recommendation.** Run an HPE-aware extended-label check next to the replay.
Forbidding scalars in the adapter phases is **not** enough, because Z has none
there. `verify.py` also includes a cheaper `adapter_rule`:

- every adapter and wrapper sits in its own phase at `cur[r] == f`;
- per-register adapter state is tracked.

The rule rejects all three mutants and accepts the selected programs. It is a
sketch, not proved sufficient.

**(c) The published Lemma G checker on the selected word.** Before this, only
#509 and #516 ran it, and never on an HPE word.

- **As published:** it fails with `ValueError` on the 5-field HPE wrapper events.
- **With the 5th field stripped:** 96 violations per orientation, which is the
  48 cold helpers × 2.
- **With a three-line marked cold-HPE patch** (rebuilt byte for byte from the
  pinned original): 0 violations. It still rejects its own five mutants and all
  three mutants of (b).

## Task and overlap

- **Base and track:** base `0b1cccf8`. Seed 65 → adversarial mathematical
  audit, card `uniform-transfer-audit` (catalogue priority revision 3), scope
  **refined**.
- **#1781 (mine, open)** checks **H2** on the same word. This package checks
  **H1**. They are complementary.
- **#1282 (merged) and #1309 (open), bitplane,** derive a Lemma G prefix-norm
  corollary on the same programs, with H1/H2 as premises.
  - This package discharges the H1 instance they assume, and the
    concrete-extended-label part of the Discussion #1291 / #1309 handoff.
  - The row certificate and recipes stay theirs and #1781's.
- **#1611 and #1697** bind wrapper pairs and cold operators (Lemma A / HPE (N)).
  They are used here only through the inherited helper-block evaluation.
- **#729** found a frame-history gap in a different component.
- **Overlap searches** of open and recent PRs for Lemma G, WellLabelled,
  `check_extended_labels`, `hpe_audit_local`, tag check, extended-label and
  exit adapter found nothing else on this proposition.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected1094-extended-labels-seed65 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected1094-extended-labels-seed65
```

`verify.py` uses only the standard library and takes about 85 s; recipe
generation dominates and runs concurrently. Its checks raise `ValueError`, and
it is registered plain and under `-O`. The pinned producer scripts run in
`-I -B` subprocesses from SHA-checked byte copies.

**Failure controls.** These test the checker; they do not prove it.

- **Rejected under both readings:** 28 forward and 27 backward edited programs.
  - Lemma G's five `mutants()` and two HPE edits.
  - Single-clause edits:
    - target exit and entry adapters at wrong frames or positions;
    - identity adapters added for wrapped or HPE helpers;
    - a post wrapper before the final climb;
    - a source entry adapter keyed away from its start;
    - centre steps and copies from wrong frames;
    - phase markers dropped or swapped;
    - unknown event kinds;
    - wrapper key and count edits.
- **Rejected under the strict reading only:** one edit, as Lean's `Admissible`
  intends.
- **Clause weakenings.** `verify.py` weakens each of the checker's 32 clauses
  alone and re-runs all 62 pinned inputs. **31 of 32** change a pinned value.
  The survivor is implied by the next clause and is pinned.

**Pre-PR review.** A three-lens review (proof, verifier, claims) returned
ship-with-fixes. It found mutant Z, which showed the earlier "forbid scalars in
adapter phases" fallback was insufficient. It also asked for the added
controls, the complex-supplier scoping, the credit corrections and the (b)
reframing. All are applied. Tested on Python 3.12.15.

## Credit

- **Lemma G / Lemma A Lean packages:** DreamingOfClouds (#509, #516, and #484's
  Lemma G stage and `lg_phys.py`).
- **HPE Lean packages:** jeremykothe2 (#593) and DreamingOfClouds (#599).
- **PR635 tools:** jeremykothe2 (#635). They adapt #433 (icekylinx), building on
  #425 (Zhihao Chen / jacklightChen) and #514 (Dugongue). They include:
  - jeremykothe2's HPE changes (#591, #592, #601);
  - DreamingOfClouds' GK (#484) and COLD-HPE (#604) changes;
  - `phases_full.py` (icekylinx, vendored via #558, eumemic);
  - `clifford_exact.py` (#531, icekylinx).
- **Slot / T16 lineage:**
  - rohanarun (#987; #1094, the selected record);
  - jeremykothe2 (#1005, #1018, #1022, #1087);
  - Hao Yan / FanPUYen (#858 controller).
- **Seven-slot word bytes:** Ali Romman.
- **Prefix-norm corollary:** Gareth Davidson / bitplane (#1282, #1309).
- **Bit-supplier carryover note:** icekylinx (#535).

AI disclosure: prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial Anthropic Claude
assistance, including explorer, judge, builder and reviewer subagents. No
independent human review. New work is Apache-2.0. The patched checker keeps its
original attribution, and its changes are marked.

## Open next questions

1. Wire an HPE-aware extended-label check into the selected local replay, with
   X, Y and Z as negative controls. Alternatively, prove that a cheaper rule
   like `adapter_rule` implies H1.
2. State the cross-call data-phase composition in Lemma G's event model.
3. Re-run the Lean builds of `e8-lemma-g-lean` and `hyperplane-end-lean`. This
   package checks statement text only.
4. Formalise Lemma S against an extended Lean emitter model.

title: Proof repair: bootstrap cutoffs need only a stock constant (repair (b) of #1956; κ unchanged)
body:
**Proof repair for one finite lemma: under a restated cutoff lemma, the selected bootstrap cutoffs reduce to an uncomputed space obligation with a large exact margin. κ, the certificate, the suppliers and the frontier are unchanged.**

Follow-up to #1956 (open question 1, "repair (b)"). That PR showed the 14 recorded `cutoff_log2` values of the selected #1094 `ASSEMBLY.json` fail the cutoff lemma *as written* (PR387 PROOF; `five-stage-source527-banks/proof/FINITE_BIT_ACCOUNTING.md`) from stage 2 on, because that lemma's C must dominate the carried time constant `C_old·2^(L·Δa)`. This PR proves a restated lemma under hypotheses (H1)–(H3), which are read from the retained sources but not re-proved. Under that lemma the same numbers are valid exactly when each stock coefficient satisfies `σ_j ≤ 2^(H_j−3)`, where `H_j` is that stage's headroom. This is plausible by a wide margin but is not verified here.

## Result

- **The time bound needs no cutoff.** Each lower-order toll is at most `M(δ)·e^(1−a_j)` for **all** `e ≥ 1`, where `M(δ) = max(2, 2/(ℯ·ln2·δ)) ≥ sup_t (1+t)2^(−δt)`. Hence `T_j(e) ≤ C_j·V·e^(1−a_j)` with `C_j = max(K(4+M), C_(j−1)·2^(L·Δa))`. Neither the previous time constant nor the new one enters L.
- **The cutoff only makes the borrowed stock fit**, `k < e/2` (`three-stage-cover-rows.tex`). With `C = 8σ`, where σ is the stock coefficient in `log_q S(e,w) ≤ σw(1+log2 e)`, the original 36/δ² and `2(4+ℓ)/δ` inequality chain gives `k ≤ e/64 + 1`. The induction stays sequential: `σ → L → C_j`.
- **Selected receipt, exact:** all 14 recorded cutoffs satisfy the fit-only rule with `log2(8σ) ≤ 512`. The exact headroom `H_j` (the largest `log2(8σ)` each cutoff supports) is **6,562,783 bits at stage 1** and about 3·10^23 bits at stage 7. The carried factor alone (`log2 C_old ≥ L·Δa`) exceeds every stage-2..7 headroom, which reproduces #1956's finding from the other side. An illustrative time-constant chain, under the extra modeling assumptions that fresh constants are below 2^512 and `K_j ≤ 2^512(1+C_(j−1))`, gives a 27-digit `log2 C_7`.

## Evidence

`python3 -B research/bootstrap-cutoff-time-space-split/verify.py` prints `PASS_BOOTSTRAP_TIME_SPACE_SPLIT recorded=14 fit_only_valid=14 written_rule_fails=12 time_constant_finite=2 controls_rejected=7`. It uses the standard library and exact Fractions, except for a floating-point sanity check of `M`, and runs in under 0.1 s. It passes on CPython 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14. `research_package.py --check-only` and the registered 3.12 replay pass, and the 42 research tests pass. The verifier source-pins the receipt, both lemma texts, `three-stage-cover-rows.tex` and the assembler formula in `upstream1087.tar.gz`. It certifies `ln2 > 693/1000` and `ℯ > 2718/1000` from series with tail bounds and checks the `3√t` step. The seven rejected controls are: cutoff −1; stock coefficient one bit over the headroom; `M/4`; the false bound `ln2 > 0.6932`; the false bound `ℯ > 2.719`; the carried time constant in the fit rule; and a tampered gap. A floating-point check at the maximizer is a sanity check only.

## Not discharged

- **(H3):** the stock coefficient σ_j contains no time constant and satisfies `log2(8σ_j) ≤ headroom_j`. This rests on the retained complete-row contract's logarithmic old-leaf reserve, which has the same bound shape at every stage, so the below-cutoff branch does not multiply it by `2^(LΔa)`. This PR does not compute σ_j.
- **(H2):** the retained stopped-leaf estimate holds whenever `k < e/2`, and its O-constant is independent of the cutoff. The sources state the estimate only asymptotically. Any further "sufficiently large e" condition in the inherited PR185 lineage is another fit condition, with its own coefficient to check against the headroom.
- Other lineages that use the same formula (T37, #1424, #1586, #1724): the argument applies, but their headrooms are not computed. All other inherited obligations of the selected record are also untouched.

## Scope and overlap

Chooser nonce `bff97872294a70402bf5bd4940f9436f` drew complex-mechanisms. I overrode it, by donor/coordinator preference, to #1956's open question. Card: `uniform-transfer-audit`, refined. One Codex read-only review was run. Its two must-fixes (narrow the receipt claim, and `σ ≤ 2^(H−3)` rather than `2^H`) and its should-fixes (qualify H2, label the time chain's assumptions) are applied. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18926910. The overlap helper found nothing beyond #1956. This PR and #1956 are complementary repairs, (b) and (a); maintainers can pick the wording. Base `0b1cccf8`.

**Credit:** rohanarun (PR387 PROOF), eumemic (five-stage bank proof), the retained `three-stage-cover-rows.tex`, Jeremy Kothe's PR1087 assembler and its lineage, Rohan Arun's PR1094 receipt, and #1956. Prepared by Josie Elliston with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance. Apache-2.0.

title: Research: sharp odd-dihedral joint tariffs with dirty workspace
body:
For odd finite-dihedral rotation periods, the two separate reflection bounds miss one joint call for each longest reflection. This package proves the missing joint constraint for every odd period and every finite dirty-register workspace, completing the odd-period question left by Adam Gall's [PR1941](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1941).

For heterogeneous formal targets `r^k_i x^e_i`, let `A=sum d_n(k_i+e_i)`, `B=sum d_n(k_i)`, and let `t` count the longest reflections. Every permitted word obeys `X>=A`, `Y>=B`, `X+Y>=A+B+t`; all pairs `(A+j,B+t-j)` are attained. The exact nonnegative tariff is `alpha*A+beta*B+t*min(alpha,beta)`. For example, two longest D10 reflections require ten calls even with arbitrary restored dirty workspace; separate cuts and parity alone permit eight.

The new proof uses a half of the faithful regular action whose crossing rank equals each target's shortest alternating-word length. It credits and extends PR1941's separate cuts. This is a written all-parameter theorem in the explicit formal `F2[D_(2n)]` reflection-only, rank-one-idempotent model with free scalar mixing. No new kappa, selected supplier, physical compiler/hosting/frame/precision/tape admission, or Lean multiplication theorem is claimed.

Only `research/odd-dihedral-joint-tariff/` is added. It contains the proof, full formal and separately implemented regular-action checks, independent specialist checker, failure controls, fixed receipt, exact source pins, task selection and limitations. No predecessor implementation is imported or frozen input changed. Credit Adam Gall #1941/#1911, commdata2338 #1414, Cinna Davis #1541/#1870/#1953, Ross Richardson #1766, Aaron Wang #1763, and the retained register-model lineage; their known special cases are not reclaimed as newly open.

Validation on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.12:

- Registered replay PASS: 510 complete single-target cases, all 155 projectors through four roles across five odd periods, 3,770 complete short words, 392 forward/inverse dirty pair words, and 84 larger mixed tuples. All 2,478 omitted-call controls reject.
- Separate Codex exact-verification specialist found no blocking proof/code defect; its no-import checker covers all 5,200 single targets for odd periods 3–101 and 216 full-matrix conjugations.
- Six package tests pass, including actual detector-removal sensitivity, source/receipt corruption, missing-evidence refusal, and isolated optimized read-only relocation. CPython 3.14.6 replay agrees; selected-record integrity and whitespace pass.
- Hosted CI and full selected cold replay are separate and are not claimed passed.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/odd-dihedral-joint-tariff`.

Exact contribution head: `691e6eb9417384d1820de4fdc167fc3e9797b75e`. Research base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; main advanced to `ecc75c79c22d909fd42aa68437eb77c4c1361835` during the run, with selected record, guidance, pinned inputs and package runner byte-identical. Final overlap refresh covered 535 open PRs and 592 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings; the precise scope is coordinated in [Discussion1955](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1955). No novelty guarantee is inferred from searches.

Prepared for Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including bit-supplier derivation and separate exact-verification review. This is AI-assisted checking, not independent human or formal-kernel review. Apache-2.0. The next useful mechanism must change the paid alphabet or supply a fully priced physical interface; another search in this same formal model cannot beat the direct bill.

title: Research: Heisenberg central-pair call floor (no new kappa)
body:
## Result

This package gives an exact call-minimum result for one new nonabelian register model. In the formal algebra `F2[UT3(F3)]`, with two scalar registers and paid shears over the four generator labels `x, x^-1, y, y^-1`, the endpoint `diag([z],[z])` for `z=[x,y]` needs exactly eight calls.

Applying the commutator word `x y x^-1 y^-1` once to each register gives the eight-call upper bound. A complete meet-in-the-middle search over all six binary rank-one idempotents and all four labels excludes every word of lengths 0 through 7. The exact sorted-state receipts cover 82,063 distinct length-four products; `EXPECTED.json` records hashes and every tested split. Free scalar `GL2(F2)` changes are absorbed because all rank-one idempotents are enumerated and the target is scalar.

## Verification

```text
python3 -B research/heisenberg-central-pair-seed0154/verify.py
PASS_HEISENBERG_CENTRAL_PAIR minimum=8 excluded_lengths=0..7 group_order=27 characteristic=2 registers=2 generators=4 idempotents=6 controls=6 matrix_crosschecks=144 state_counts=[(0, 1), (1, 24), (2, 413), (3, 5927), (4, 82063)]

python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/heisenberg-central-pair-seed0154 --check-only
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

The exact replay also passes under `python3 -I -O -B`.

## Scope and attribution

This is limited to the named finite group, two registers, four-label alphabet and endpoint. It rejects a commutator-sharing saving in this model; it does not bound other nonabelian groups or establish physical supplier adoption. No new kappa or integer-multiplication claim is made.

PR #1822 studies the related Q8 central pair. This changes the group to odd order 27 over coefficient field F2, and the central target has order three with a four-letter direct generator word. The full overlap refresh is recorded in `README.md`; the handoff is on [Discussion #1167](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-18926907).

Assignment base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; current PR base is the latest `main`. The selected record hash remains `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. Exact assignment and predecessor source pins are retained in `TASK.json` and `SOURCES.json`.

Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No predecessor code is copied. New work is Apache-2.0.
