title: Accumulate shared product sums before dirty-anchor fanout
body:
## Result

This package extends the one-common-product dirty-anchor schedule to a shared sum of `s >= 2` bilinear products. A required output accumulator with arbitrary dirty entry first compensates every other output for its old value, accumulates the entire common sum, and then broadcasts the updated anchor once. Each output receives the common sum plus its private product; reversing the schedule restores every arbitrary dirty accumulator.

For `q` outputs, direct evaluation uses `q(s+1)` product children. The anchor schedule uses `s+q` children and charges `2(q-1)` width-`w` row additions. Repeating the one-term dirty-anchor fanout separately for each common product uses `2s(q-1)` row additions, so the aggregate schedule saves `2(s-1)(q-1)` additions. For `q=s=3`, this is 12 direct children versus 6 children plus 4 row additions; separate one-term fanout would use 12 row additions.

The local bill is exact. If `mu` is one child cost and `A_w` one width-`w` row-add cost, the net saving against independent evaluation is `(q-1)(s*mu - 2*A_w)`. Eight hypothetical `q=s=3` groups would change the rank-only fixed-word ceiling by only 0.905971%, even before adding the 32 width-one scalar additions, and the selected trace does not establish that placement. No supplier or `kappa` claim is made.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/recursive-multiterm-anchor-seedb9a23 --check-only`
- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/recursive-multiterm-anchor-seedb9a23`
- `git diff --check`

The package symbolically checks forward/inverse maps for `2 <= q <= 5`, `1 <= s <= 4`, exhausts all 60,073 `q=s=2` dirty/input states over `F2` and `F3`, and tests both missing-wave and wrong-sign failures.

## Scope and overlap

This is a finite local construction. PR #1944 and active claim #18925817 cover `s=1`; this package changes the object to a shared multi-term sum and coalesces compensation across all common terms. PR #1907 uses a clean output anchor, PR #1872 uses a clean helper and cleanup, and PR #1155 treats generic linear restoration coalescing. Finding a source-incidence match in an admitted supplier remains open.

The work used substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Selected-word construction credit remains with its original authors.

title: Add native joint centre-query transfers on sixteen selected ports
body:
This **local construction and enabling theorem** uses two disjoint eight-port minors to carry centre queries in the joint X/Y state. It gives invertible forward and backward data maps, preserves all **sixteen selected X-plus-Y sums**, and allocates no new array field. Changing the selected source baseline permits a local query exchange without a Schur-unit assumption. The package supplies **37 complete native local words** for the actual historical complex supplier.

**The complete kappa bound is unchanged.** This is a reusable local operator interface, not a complete changing-chart controller. The package includes an exact witness against the current controller's selected-only recovery interface and states the remaining escapes.

Evidence at the reviewed commit: [ordered proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a6e6ad3936f67b8f63b5b68c5e75d540610a65e7/research/joint-query/evidence/JOINT-QUERY-TRANSFER.md), [literal native certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a6e6ad3936f67b8f63b5b68c5e75d540610a65e7/research/joint-query/certificate.json.gz), [independent package review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a6e6ad3936f67b8f63b5b68c5e75d540610a65e7/research/joint-query/evidence/PACKAGE-REVIEW.md), [replay receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a6e6ad3936f67b8f63b5b68c5e75d540610a65e7/research/joint-query/evidence/REPLAY.json), and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a6e6ad3936f67b8f63b5b68c5e75d540610a65e7/research/joint-query/SOURCES.json).

The ordered theorem uses disjoint selected sets A and T, their complement U, `K=K_A+P+K_U`, `J=I-KR`, `RP=LP=I`, and the stated support conditions, with `PL` the T-coordinate projector. The forward companion also uses `RK_A=I`. Put

```text
M=R K_U,  Z=K_U-PM,  H=I+ZR.
RZ=0,  H^-1=I-ZR,  JH=I-[K_A+P(I+M)]R.
```

No inverse of M and no interchange of ordered factors is used; M may be noncentral or singular. A future A-logger `E_t=I+N_t`, with only A output rows and no A input columns, supplies the second chart's record. In the conserved backward map, let `u=E_t y`, `a=ell_s x`, and `b=R_s u`. Its records are

```text
R_s y' = a,
ell_(t,A) y' = R_t y,
ell_s x' = b + M a.
```

The selected X record is `b+Ma`, not b alone. The ordinary target rows perform `x_U-y_U`. The forward companion puts the full current X query in T and moves the old T query into A. Both maps preserve each selected pair sum and have explicit algebraic inverses in both orders. The conserved sums are logical identities; their X and Y terms have different native endpoint frames. The words are companions, not inverse circuits. The actual instance has `R` of size 8 by 112, `K=R^T/4`, and `M=12I`. The general theorem is algebraic; the priced native instances use these actual dyadic matrices.

The [native contract](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a6e6ad3936f67b8f63b5b68c5e75d540610a65e7/research/joint-query/evidence/CONSERVED-QQ16.md) supplies all 28 `B_s_t` cases for `1 <= s < t <= 8` and all nine `F_s` cases for `0 <= s <= 8`. Its cover views change the owner and apply a separate payload translation on every tensor layer. Each full-cover sweep must finish before the next event. A private row body completes at one owner before C0 is reused at the next. The new work uses one existing owned C0 field. title: Prove an all-length balance law for native source-code controllers
body:
Ali Romman’s [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862) provides native identity transfers with an order-six source code, but a controller that restores the full source remains open. This adds a written, all-length conservation law for the fixed-code controller class: the signed count of forward/backward calls must be divisible by six, even with arbitrary invertible whole-bank scalar mixing, signs, scales, extra restored dirty banks and true inverse calls. Consequently every odd-call controller in that class is excluded, including a fixed-code substitution into the inherited nine-call skeleton. Coherently conjugated coordinate changes satisfy the same law.

A complementary theorem allows a different admissible chart at each call of an F-B-F exchange. Its unwanted diagonal block D satisfies `R D K = RK - 2I`; on the retained source this is `12 I_8`, so its rank is at least eight for every choice of those charts. This extends [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862)'s fixed-chart counterexample to all admissible selected rows in this architecture.

The contribution is one scoped proof package under `research/native-controller-congruence/`. It supplies a construction-level stopping criterion, rather than a bounded search or extra decimal digits. **The numerical multiplication bound is unchanged.** Port-dependent operations, non-equivariant physical chart transport, new clean workspace and paid repairs remain possible escape routes. The valid [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862) local construction is preserved; no native implementation or full supplier is claimed.

`README.md` contains the proofs and precise reopening conditions; `TASK.json`, `SOURCES.json`, `ARCHIVE.json`, `PREDECESSOR.json`, `RESULT.json` and `VALIDATION.json` record scope, source pins and replay evidence. title: Research: the 916 open mixed GL3 target pairs need exactly their direct cost (no new kappa)
body:
## Contribution

This closes open question 1 of `research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-seed18/` (Hanson Sun, on main). The model is the same: M_2(F2[GL_3(F2)]) with 36 paid involutions `I + N([g]+[e])`, where g is one of six coordinate CNOTs and N one of six binary rank-one idempotents. Free GL_2(F2) scalar mixing is allowed, and the target `diag([a],[b])` must hold with formal equality. Seed18 left 916 ordered pairs with direct cost 10..12 at "minimum >= 9". **Each of them needs exactly its direct cost d(a)+d(b):**

| direct cost | pairs | exact minimum | new exclusion |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 10 | 816 | 10 | no length-9 word |
| 11 | 96 | 11 | no word of length 9 or 10 |
| 12 | 4 | 12 | no word of length 9, 10 or 11 |

With seed18's table, all 28,224 ordered pairs cost exactly d(a)+d(b). Heterogeneous targets never share paid work in this alphabet. The four cost-12 pairs use the two 3-cycle permutation matrices, which are the only elements at distance 6.

**Bounded third-register probe.** `engine3.cpp` adds one extra dirty scalar register, which must be restored or may end at any monomial `[c]`. That gives 28 idempotents x 6 labels = 168 paid involutions. A radius-3 ball (2,705,791 states) plus 450,868,320 streamed distance-4 images covers every word of length at most 7. **No pair gets a word shorter than d(a)+d(b).** All direct words of length at most 7 are found as positive controls. So the extra register saves nothing for the 24,224 pairs with direct cost at most 8, and pairs with direct cost at least 9 still need at least 8 calls. Lengths 8 and above with a third register are not covered.

## Method and evidence

- `engine.cpp` is a new C++17 engine that shares no code with seed18. It builds the exact radius-4 ball and streams the distance-5 layer. It reuses seed18's row-orbit lemma: `A B^-1 = diag([a],[b])` exactly when each row of A is a left translate of the same row of B. It groups the 16,292,362 radius-5 states by canonical row keys, compared exactly with no digests. The join covers 1,119,282,418 ordered pairs, which is every word of length at most 10.
- **Length-11 stage, for the four cost-12 pairs only.** It streams all 562,639,176 images `hC`, with C at distance 5, and looks each one up exactly among the radius-5 groups.
- **Reproduces seed18.** The radius-4 layers 1/36/996/25,518/636,945, the 133,207 cosets and the table `min(9, d(a)+d(b))` all match at every pair.
- **Positive controls on the same code paths.** For the 27,308 pairs with direct cost at most 9, the radius-5 join returns exactly the direct cost. It finds a length-10 word for every cost-10 pair. The length-11 stage, run on all 96 cost-11 pairs, finds an 11-call word for each one.
- **`verify.py` is stdlib.** It has its own formal algebra. It re-derives the 916 pairs and checks all 816 + 96 recorded words and the four direct twelve-call words formally. It binds the receipt to seed18's pinned certificate and rejects tampered witnesses. Five tampered `RESULT.json` variants were also rejected by hand. `--full` compiles the engine with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, reruns it and requires the parsed output to equal `RESULT.json`.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10/verify.py          # quick, < 1 s
python3 -I -B research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10/verify.py --full   # C++17, ~3 GB RAM, 65-120 s
python3 -I -B research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10/verify.py --three  # third-register probe, ~35 s, 2.3 GB
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10 --check-only
```

One read-only OpenAI Codex review of the two-register part found no must-fix issues. It confirmed the coverage cases, the key, anchor and dedupe exactness, the length-11 binary search and the absence of data races. Its two should-fixes are applied: quick mode now pins the complete engine receipt and histogram and rejects duplicate rows, and the README wording on length-11 hits is corrected. The third-register probe was added after that review and was not part of it. Quick mode passes on CPython 3.10–3.14 and in the registered 3.12 replay (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`). `--full --three` passes on macOS with Apple clang in 114 s on 10 cores. Runs with 4 and 10 threads give identical receipts and tables. `--check-only` passes.

## Limits

- This is a finite certificate for exactly two scalar registers, this alphabet and these targets.
- It covers no extra or dirty registers, other labels, physical, compiler, hosting or precision admission, or transfer to the rational-frame supplier. No kappa or selected-record change is claimed.
- The lower bounds rest on one engine. Seed18's independent replay corroborates only the radius-4 part.
- No dedicated CI workflow is added, and the registered quick command does not compile C++.
- Seed18's README still says these minima are unresolved. It is a frozen predecessor, so it is left unchanged.

## Open next questions

The package README lists three: a dirty third register at length 8 or more, a written invariant for `min = d(a)+d(b)`, and a second independent radius-5 join.

## Credit and overlap

- Model, coverage lemma, radius-4 table and the question: Hanson Sun's seed18 package, with its retained lineage (eumemic PR288, Ali Romman PR468, Gareth Davidson PR1333).
- PR1804 (1337isnot1337, head `26f5ae8a`) treats one cost-6 pair, which is already inside seed18's exact table.
- PR1696 (same author, head `4dadd274`) studies heterogeneous GL2 targets, a different group.
- The overlap check was refreshed at 2026-10-14 15:38Z (540 open PRs, 602 discussions) and found nothing on the 916 pairs. That is not a novelty certificate.
- Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18927159

Task card `bit-new-register-model`, chooser seed `86b2fd3dcdd43a2916d120e0d0196837`, priority revision 3, base `ecc75c79`. Scope is refined: the same card and model, narrowed to the predecessor's own open question. Prepared for @JosieElliston (session 32 of a donated overnight run) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. No independent human review. Apache-2.0.

title: Research: Eisenstein E8 decoder copy floor 23 via submatrix-minrank certificates (past the clique-method limit; no κ claim)
body:
## Result

**Scoped lower bound; no supplier, no κ change, selected record untouched.**

In the abstract Eisenstein E8 scalar binary decoder model of `research/eisenstein-clique-copy-bound` (Jonathan Lam, PR798), every fitting decomposition costs **at least 23** pairing-rank units. PR798 proved 22 and showed that no weighting of cliques can prove more. Its PROOF.md says a stronger bound needs a new ingredient. This package supplies one: rank bounds on non-clique principal submatrices.

- **Lemma 1.** Zero-cost totals touch only free orthogonal entries, so they can be dropped.
- **Lemma 2.** Let `m(S)` be the least F2 rank of `B[S,S]` over fitting `B`. Then `m(S)` is at most the number of positive-cost totals meeting `S` on both sides. Weights satisfying `sum_S λ_S [F meets S][G meets S] <= c(F,G)` on every flat pair with `c >= 1` prove `C >= sum λ_S m(S)`. Cliques are PR798's special case. Asymmetric row and column sets add nothing.
- **New sets.** Take `S_uw = N[u] ∩ N[w]`, where `u,w` are nonorthogonal; there are 540 such sets of 20 lines each. Each splits as `I_2 ⊕ core`, with an 18-line core of clique number 5. An exhaustive normalized search (`U[Q]=V[Q]=[I_5|0]`) excludes every fitting completion of rank ≤ 7, and a rank-8 completion exists, so `m(S_uw) = 10`. Under PR798's optimal clique dual these sets are priced at 9.5. Five pinned automorphisms generate a group transitive on all 540 nonorthogonal pairs, so the search runs once.
- **Certificate.** Use weights `184/6835` (singletons), `13/13670` (2,880 seven-cliques) and `7/20505` (`S_uw`). They satisfy all 296,321 positive-cost flat-pair inequalities exactly, with 601 tight. The objective is `30200/1367 ≈ 22.092`, so **C ≥ 23**.

**Consequences.** The abstract optimum moves from [22,40] to [23,40]. PR1794's necessary window for an Eisenstein supplier shrinks from C ≤ 31 to 23..31. PR798's conditional three-stage Dfc window shrinks from 22..26 to 23..26. Neither route is closed.

**How far the method goes (exploration, not replayed).** I enumerated all 858,299 hit-maximal sets `⋂_{a∈A} N[a]`; every set has the same price as one of them and no larger minrank. They fall into 78 (|A|, |S|, price) classes. SAT minranks on class representatives and the class-uniform LP give exactly 30200/1367 again, and only the `S_uw` class beats the clique dual. If those classes are automorphism orbits (not checked), principal-submatrix certificates top out at 23.

## Verification

```sh
python3 -B research/eisenstein-submatrix-copy-floor/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/eisenstein-submatrix-copy-floor
```

- `verify.py` is standard library only. It passed on CPython 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14 in 35–58 s. The registered 3.12 replay, `--check-only` and the 42 research tests also pass.
- There are five rejection controls: the clique rank 6/7 search sanity check, a non-automorphism, a non-transitive generator subset, an inflated `S_uw` weight, and cliques-only weights falling below 22.
- Independent cross-check (SAT, not shipped): the normalized rank-7 instance is UNSAT for every one of the core's 112 five-cliques.
- One OpenAI Codex read-only review found no soundness issue (Lemmas 1–3, search completeness, automorphism reduction, i ≤ j symmetry, rounding). Its two wording fixes are applied: the positive-cost pair count, and an explicit `m(P,Q)` definition with the method-limit statement kept conditional.
- Not done: proof assistant, independent human review, any physical or supplier reading beyond PR798's premises.

## Scope and credit

The model, premises and geometry are PR798's; the pinned `geometry.py` is imported unchanged. Whole K-lines, scalar binary totals and the fitting pattern are essential. Nonlinear messages and sub-line operations are not covered.

Chooser seed `8bcd09ea00ac64eec3911b4b0c15e635` (complex-mechanisms / complex-rank-shape-decoder), scope **changed**; the reason is in `TASK.json`. Base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-18926981

Credit: Jonathan Lam (@jonathanlam, PR798: model, geometry, clique certificate, method-limit theorem); Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (PR620 geometry); Douglas R. Colkitt (PR703) and Sagar Thakrar (PR738) for the weighted-clique method; Maximooch (PR1794) for the window screen; DreamingOfClouds for naming the target. New material is by Josie Elliston, prepared with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code, with substantial AI assistance in search, proof and verifier. Apache-2.0.

title: Independent verification: exact enclosure of the pivot-566+554 T74 complex root behind the top pending kappa claims (no new kappa)
body:
## Independent enclosure of the pivot-566+554 T74 complex root (no new κ)

**Card:** `independent-moment` (independent-verification track, scope key `c6f2494b197df3bc3591`, chooser OS nonce `9dd43e38694b6907874fe4e993da7bf9`, priority revision 3). Scope **changed**, with the reason in `TASK.json`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18927871. Base `ae95f60feec79897b153dba6459bb3f9fd4d7b8e`. Adds only `research/t74-k554-root-enclosure/`.

### Why this object

The selected https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094 pricing already has independent ledger, moment, invoice and outer checks (frontier1094-emitted-ledger-seed78, selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic, pr1407-complex-moment-audit-seed39, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1735). So I applied the card's enclosure method to the pending supplier behind the highest open claims.

Every claim from https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1800 to https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928 prices the pivot-566+554 T74 supplier. At their "free ε → 1" point, κ approaches this supplier's complex moment root. https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928 sets b to its certified native endpoint minus 10^-10010. Until now, only the authors' own engines had certified that endpoint.

### What is checked

The inputs are the global profile `{1:1560432, 2:336336, 3:278724, 4:84912, 5:54612, 8:5328, 48:22748}`, m = 73 and W = 66304. They are pinned by Git blob and SHA-256 from `new/SPEC.json` at https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672 (head `b8ab040d`) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928 (head `07e4e423`). `extract_inputs.py --check` rebuilds `INPUTS.json` byte for byte from the fetched pull refs.

The moment definitions come from the written review rather than code: native moment from `research/native-complex-moment552/PROOF.md`, conservative fallback from `notes/three-stage-cover-assembly.tex`.

The method shares no algorithm with the authors' Mercator and binary-reduction engines or with earlier audits:

- ln 2, ln 3 and ln 5 are integer combinations of ln(16/15), ln(25/24) and ln(81/80). Each of these is 2 atanh(1/k), and the verifier checks the identities exactly.
- ln 73 = ln 72 + 2 atanh(1/145).
- exp uses argument halving, a Taylor polynomial with a tail bound, and repeated squaring.
- All values are outward-rounded integers. The final comparison is exact. Undecided signs fail closed.

| Case | Grid | Bits | M(e) | M(e + grid) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1672](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672) native | 1e-70 | 360 | below 1 | above 1 |
| [1672](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672) conservative | 1e-70 | 360 | below 1 | above 1 |
| [1928](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928) native | 1e-10000 | 33347 | below 1 | above 1 |
| [1928](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928) conservative | 1e-10000 | 33347 | below 1 | above 1 |

Also checked:

- For both models, the 1e-70 endpoints equal the 1e-70 floors of the 1e-10000 endpoints.
- At both heads, 249 gauge44 calls and 417 extra calls with their per-call profiles, plus 22,748 idle rank-48 children, sum to the global profile. Rank mass is 4,816,512 and the deficit is 23,680.
- The headline κ of CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1928 is 2.003e-10010 below its native endpoint, as its choice of b implies. CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1672's is 2.817e-6 below.
- Ten semantic controls are rejected: next and previous grid point as endpoint, one child moved from rank 1 to rank 2, m = 72, W − 1, and the surcharge omitted or added in the wrong model. Three are repeated at 1e-10000.

The optional `crosscheck_decimal.py` repeats the 1e-10000 case with Python's `decimal` ln and exp at 10,060 digits. It agrees on all seven log enclosures and all four signs. It takes about 4 minutes and corroborates the result; it is not a certificate.

**No discrepancy was found.**

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-k554-root-enclosure --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-k554-root-enclosure
```

Local results on Windows, Python 3.12, stdlib only:

```
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
PASS_T74_K554_ROOT_ENCLOSURE_INDEPENDENT | brackets 4 | nesting 2 | controls 10 rejected | 13.5 s
Ran 10 tests ... OK
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/t74-k554-root-enclosure outcome=completed
PASS_DECIMAL_CROSSCHECK | 7 log enclosures | 4 moment signs agree
PASS_INPUTS_MATCH_PINNED_PR_HEADS
```

`tests.test_research_onboarding`, `tests.test_research_replay_selection` and `tests.test_research_assignment` also pass (32 tests). `make` is not installed on this host, so no make target was run. Hosted CI has not run.

### Scope

This is a finite check of recorded endpoints and of the profile arithmetic. The following are taken as given:

- the profiles themselves;
- the native, surcharge-free complex recurrence;
- the outer reduction from b to κ, the fine source-prime padding and the ε → 1 transfer (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1797 audits the CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1786 lemmas on a different supplier);
- all inherited all-size/compiler, realization, hosting, precision/tape, recovery, analytic and bit H1-H5 assumptions.

No new κ is claimed and the selected record is unchanged.

1. Does CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1928's `outer/LEDGER.json` follow from this endpoint, checked by code that does not import `outer/*.py`?
2. Does the global profile equal the profile emitted by the T74 template and owner map? The seed78 emitted-ledger rebuild could be adapted to the two-provider layout.

- Supplier: mdumitrean (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1625), Jeremy Kothe (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1672 through https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1928), Rohan Arun (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1319) and their credited lineage.

title: Research: exact local gauge floors for P112 decoder
body:
## Result

Adds an exact lower bound for a local gauge-edit family of the coordinate-frame-plus-root nine-normal P112 decoder. The 112 live E8 lines are partitioned by an explicit increasing-index orthogonal-block rule. For each of 14 single blocks and 91 block pairs, the verifier holds every exterior coefficient row at its per-root sparsest gauge and sums the exact F2 ranks contributed by those unchanged rows.

The singleton floors are 67 twice and 68 twelve times. Pair floors are 64 once, 67 twenty-four times, and 68 sixty-six times. Since adding rows cannot reduce F2 rank, arbitrary rational null-dependency gauges on the selected one or two blocks cannot reduce the full copied-information bill below the known P112 cost 64.

## Scope and relation to prior work

This is a finite structural obstruction for one frame, puncture, 14-block partition, and at-most-two-block edit rule. It does not cover coordinated changes on three or more blocks, changed exterior gauges, another frame, or arbitrary masked terms. It makes no new kappa or physical supplier claim.

PR #1224 supplies the nine-normal dependency frame. Cycle 15 PR #1962 studies a shared ternary shift vector; this contribution instead permits independent rational gauges on any one or two blocks and uses a monotone exterior-rank bound. Open PR #1909 proves a different tetrad-local masked-decoder result and lists two-tetrad escape as a next question. This package fixes the coordinate-plus-root frame and all exterior rows, making its scope complementary and explicit.

title: Derive ordered decoding for the paired-log controller
body:
The paired dirty-log local words leave a global decoding obligation when successive calls use different charts. I give an explicit ordered inverse for the nine-call controller that restores all data and independent log inputs without assuming commuting charts or inverting an aggregate route matrix.

The decoder uses final X/log outputs and four stacked Y readers. I prove that their row space is exactly the information a fixed linear decoder needs to restore the initial logs. In a finite field-linear realization its dimension is `sum_j rank([R_(2j);R_(2j+1)])`, between `4r` and `8r`. This dimension is not a count of native Fourier children.

The five-file package includes the proof, exact source pins and a registered standard-library verifier. The verifier follows the pinned controller recipe, restores 290 input columns across common, mixed and noncommuting charts, compares the complete observation row spaces, and rejects 25 corruption cases. Registered Python3.12 and direct optimized Python3.14 replays pass; metadata/source pins and diff-check pass.

Native query acquisition, Y-hole injections, routed owner placement and the complete precision/recurrence invoice remain open. This result supplies scalar closure and its exact observation contract; it does not improve the multiplication exponent or change the selected frontier.

Credit Zhihao Chen's retained PR377 controller implementation, Ali Romman's PR1862/1969 source preparation and ordered local query inverses, Rohan Arun's PR1931 local instances, and their predecessor lineage. Query swaps, triangular elimination and row-space observability are standard linear algebra. Jose Manuel (@jmbarrancoml) prepared this contribution with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and read-only mathematical subagents; no independent human review.

## Change and scope

At base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`, three leave-two-style expected-support genexprs dominate historical verify wall time:

title: Audit: PR1866's one-unit block overhead passes only by idle credit (no new kappa)
body:
## Result

**Scoped audit of a pending screen. No new κ, construction or supplier; the selected record is unchanged.**

[PR #1866](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1866) (head `7d22d1d51eb6c0bc040f8181b6c5f83e051fb234`) screens a `(3,1,1,1) → 6` block with `e` assumed rank-one-equivalent overhead units per block. It reports first passes of the 5% ceiling target at k = 135 (`e = 0`) and k = 284 (`e = 1`), and none for `e = 2`.

Those numbers are arithmetically correct for the invoice it computes. However, the `e·k` overhead is added to the **local profile** passed to `ceiling.relax`. The ceiling model fixes paid mass at the coverage identity (7232 per call), so each overhead unit is subtracted from the idle remainder. It pays only its excess over ideal rank-51 idle mass. The merged [PR1605 rank-one block budget](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/main/research/complex-rank-one-block-budget/README.md) and the [block target screen](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/main/research/complex-block-target-screen/README.md) charge additional work **on top** of the unchanged idle bill. PR1605's replay includes this exact credited invoice as a false-pass control.

| Overhead per block `e` | PR1866 invoice (credited against idle) | Additional overhead (no idle credit) |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | first pass k = 135 (298 passing k) | first pass k = 135 (298 passing k) |
| 1 | first pass k = 284 (149 passing k) | **no k in 0..432 passes** |
| 2 | no pass | no pass |

- **Per-block saving.** One block saves `3 + 3^q − 6^q` rank-one calls (`q = 1 − a`), certified in `(0.013204, 0.013205)` at the target. With no idle credit, one extra call per block makes every block costlier than the children it replaces, for all `0 ≤ a ≤ a*`.
- **Why the credited invoice passes.** A credited overhead unit costs only about 0.006953 rank-one calls, roughly half the block saving.
- **Total uncredited budget.** At most **3** extra rank-one calls in total (not per block) with all 432 blocks, and **0** at k = 135.

## Task card

- **Task ID / scope key:** `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, scope key `cad3ba853d7f324f16fa`, chooser nonce `c3eec147a2cf20ef07d6ce3652384ebc`, priority revision 3.
- **Scope:** **changed**, to an independent audit of the newest pending screen on this card. The overlap helper reported 231 possible matches, so this session did not add another candidate block. The card's construction acceptance gate is not met.
- **Base:** `01a65937ece11b56d515c81f039464ae3043c1c1`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- **Audited head:** #1866 `7d22d1d51eb6c0bc040f8181b6c5f83e051fb234`. It was still open, with no comments or reviews, at submission.
- **Domain:** k = 0..432 blocks per call; `e ∈ {0,1,2}`; target `a* = 35491136290869/20000000000000000` (21/20 × the selected ceiling's upper bracket), the same target #1866 and PR1605 use.

## Evidence

`research/pr1866-overhead-idle-credit-audit/verify.py` checks every decision with two arithmetic engines:

- **Engine A:** the pinned `ceiling.py` enclosures.
- **Engine B:** a code-disjoint `decimal` engine (libmpdec correctly rounded `ln`/`exp` at 80 digits, widened by 4 ulps; directed rounding elsewhere).

Every decision must be strict, and the engines must agree. They agree on the selected ceiling bracket, all 2,598 scan decisions and both budget counts. Each passing set is checked to be an upper interval in k. Five controls pass:

- idle rank 52 is rejected by the halving guard;
- a coverage overspend is rejected;
- the two conventions agree at `e = 0`;
- k = 134 is rejected for `e = 0`;
- k = 284, `e = 1` passes when credited and is rejected as additional work.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/pr1866-overhead-idle-credit-audit/verify.py   # PASS_PR1866_OVERHEAD_IDLE_CREDIT_AUDIT, ~1 s
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr1866-overhead-idle-credit-audit --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr1866-overhead-idle-credit-audit
```

All three passed locally (Python 3.14.8 and 3.12). `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` also passes: 53 tests, 2 skipped.

## Limits

- This audits one pricing convention in one pending moment screen. It does not examine #1866's tensor-rank proof, dirty-target contract or phase-A placement scan.
- The `e` tariff remains a parameter. No copy, frame, restoration or hosting bill is established.
- If a construction proves a new coverage identity under which its overhead legitimately displaces idle mass, the credited column applies. That proof is its own obligation.
- All limits of the retained ceiling model apply.
- Engine B trusts libmpdec's documented correct rounding. Widening and agreement with engine A are the safeguards.
- No full selected cold replay was run: no supplier or selected artifact changed.

## Credit

The block, its tensor proof and its screen are by Cinna / commdata2338 (#1866). The ceiling model is Douglas Colkitt's (PR1240), built on PR1012's coverage identity. The uncredited-overhead convention and its false-pass control are Arham Tahir's (PR1605). The block target screen is Jose Manuel's (@jmbarrancoml), building on Ali Romman's PR1429.

Prepared by ianlibanio with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance via Claude Code, covering task selection, both engines, verification and writing. No independent human review. Apache-2.0.

**Workflow feedback (optional).** The biggest friction was that `ceiling.relax` cannot distinguish payload children from overhead children. Passing overhead inside the local profile silently credits it against idle mass. The package's second open question proposes a successor helper with an explicit extra-profile argument.

body:
## Result

Adds `research/sl2f3-conjugate-triple-seed592f/`, a scoped exact result in the full formal algebra `F2[SL2(F3)]`. For the three-role target `diag([i],[w],[w^-1 i w])` and four address labels `{i,i^-1,w,w^-1}`, the exact paid-call minimum is five. The separate direct word costs five; exhaustive exact coverage excludes every four-call-or-shorter word. This is a negative result for one new nonabelian alphabet, not a new `kappa` or supplier construction.

## Exact model and evidence

The group has order 24, generated by the pinned matrices `i=[[0,1],[-1,0]]` and `w=[[0,-1],[1,-1]]` over `F3`. The paid factor is `D_N(g)=I+([g]+[e])N` for each of the 28 binary rank-one idempotents in `M3(F2)`, giving 112 paid factors. Free scalar `GL3(F2)` mixing is included by augmentation/conjugation closure. Every paid factor costs one.

The verifier covers all lengths 0 through 4. The 12,544 ordered two-call words collapse to 8,905 exact states; each distinct state is checked as a suffix against the complete prefix set for both 1+2 and 2+2 splits. This exhausts all 1,404,928 length-three and 157,351,936 length-four raw words, as well as shorter lengths. All 12,544 two-call products are cross-checked by independent full coefficient convolution. The direct five-call word, all five call omissions, a mutated generator, the factor inverse law, group-table associativity, and a known two-call target control pass. `CERTIFICATE.json` records the two-call state digest `7313957379a9c51963604fae5f6a69edda1771006526c9c2ef4ab068e76bed95`.

The direct target costs five. A four-call factorization would reduce this finite model bill by 20%; the exact minimum remains five. The bit-model address labels have no priced implementation in the selected multiplication supplier, so this experiment yields no exponent change.

## Pins and overlap

Track `bit-mechanisms`; seed `592f04c45f93ecfac35ea0ab971b12ba`; task `bit-new-register-model`; priority revision 3; catalogue SHA-256 `6686ad58f1fbdbc87134a78901b60fd53a20d3984355e91defbbebc9e9fa8075`; exact research base `1c47876ef742ba64bf9140b0527d63acf656a3b4`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. ## Scope and result

**Exact scoped negative result; no new kappa.** In the formal group algebra `F2[C7 semidirect C3]` on three registers, the target `diag([a],[a^2],[a^4])` has exact paid-call minimum three in the declared alphabet. PR #1779 covers homogeneous rank-one batches; PR #1866 uses a different `(3,1,1,1)->6` tensor; open PR #1960 optimizes rank-two/rank-three blocks. title: Prove sharp cost 40 for Eisenstein binary decoders
body:
For the 40 Eisenstein lines, I prove that every binary scalar rectangle decoder has abstract pairing cost at least **40**, matching Jonathan Lam's row-star upper bound. I allow arbitrary asymmetric supports, any finite number of terms and XOR cancellations. This closes the interval left by the floor 22 in #798, the floor 23 in #1977 and the non-clean screen in #1794.

I normalize the Hermitian Gram matrix over Q(omega), prove that its entries lie in Z[omega,1/3], and reduce it to F4. For every fitting B, the entrywise product Hbar o B is I40. Vanishing minors and the trace-pairing identity bound each summand's F4 rank by its existing abstract pairing charge. Rank subadditivity then gives C >= 40.

I also derive the known binary minrank 10 without a SAT premise, rule out hyperplane-supported nonzero codewords in rank-10 fitting row/column spaces, and prove the fixed-support block-linear bound C >= sum_t b_t under per-bit pairing charges.

Validation: the registered Python 3.12 replay and the direct optimized Python 3.14.6 replay pass. I check 1,600 Gram entries, 6,400 trace identities, reduction arithmetic, 209 rank-conversion blocks, 40 hyperplane restrictions, matching cost witnesses, a rank-10 frame partition, mixed-bit controls and seven rejected assumption corruptions. The written radical/minor argument supplies universal support coverage; sampled rank checks do not replace it.

Scope: this is a sharp theorem for the specified abstract linear model. I do not supply a native multiplication construction, establish the physical COPY pricing premise, settle nonlinear encoders, or change the selected exponent. The consequence for #1794 remains conditional on that screen's accounting; I do not rerun the screen here.

Credit: Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (#620), Jonathan Lam (#798), DreamingOfClouds (#1590, Lemma B's same-field Hadamard argument), Maximooch (#1794), Josie Elliston (#1977), and Michael Fischler's fixed-support message model. I retain their files and attribution. I used substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation and prose; no independent human review.

title: Scoped proof: sharp 53-row rank-additivity boundary for P112 two-column masked completions (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

On the canonical P112 root lines, a genuinely masked rank-two correction on 53 rows and two columns raises the Gram matrix's rank from eight to nine, not ten. Within the complete two-column family, 53 rows are necessary: no correction with at most two changed columns and at most 52 rows fails rank additivity. The package classifies every column pair over arbitrary complex coefficients:
- orthogonal column pairs force rank ten;
- odd pairs admit rank nine or ten;
- every nonzero odd-only rank-one correction, with any column support, gives rank nine and fits inside 52 rows and 52 columns.

The last point closes PR #1447's suggested rank-one follow-up: the 53-by-53 odd rectangle it proposes cannot occur, because every odd neighbourhood has exactly 52 roots.

**Status:** a scoped proof with an exact finite certificate. The proof covers arbitrary complex coefficients without the predecessor's hyperplane-flat classification premise. The displayed nine-factor realization costs COPY65, so no COPY improvement, physical supplier or κ is claimed.

**The package:** `research/p112-two-column-completion/` holds:
- a written proof and the explicit 53-row, two-column witness, with attaining rank-ten examples;
- an exact census over all 112 singleton columns, all 6,216 unordered pairs and every projective cancellation stratum of the 2,912 odd-pair pencils (`CENSUS.json`, about 780 KB);
- a primary checker and a separately written independent checker, with focused tests.

Nine new files; selected and predecessor files are unchanged.

**Remaining obligations.**
- The theorem is about ordinary matrix rank. Not established: a COPY optimum, a paid local profile, physical source access, a frame or restoration contract, hosting, precision and tape, all-size compilation or the analytic transfer.
- Not performed: the full selected cold replay, Lean, hosted CI or independent human review.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `complex-rank-shape-decoder` / `02b31ebd160542c86299`, refined to `P112/odd-mask/two-column-completion-rank`. Chooser nonce `46dd6716742415eb113c9b4830c4ada9`, track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 3.
- **Base and exact heads:** base `1ff9c501b624ec354e1330b1b9be571a6adba9cb`; contribution `9943467c4b24d2050275a202e3866cfc522afbe7`. Predecessor: woklerx's PR #1447 (`5f784a84bbe80879b5bd7ae9b48dd28a5765863d`), retained on main as `research/p112-sparse-completion-rank`. The live root data and predecessor note are pinned by base-commit Git blob and SHA-256 in `SOURCES.json`. No pending implementation is imported; the selected PR #1094 (`0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810`) is context only.
- **Concrete question:** for G + Q, with G = XXᵀ = 2RRᵀ on canonical P112, Q_ij = 0 unless the corresponding roots have odd inner product, and at most two nonzero columns: what is the ordinary complex rank, and where does a mask-valid failure of rank additivity first appear?
- **Scope status:** changed, from physical block-climb synthesis to PR #1447's explicit masked-completion boundary. This is an algebraic side result; the card's five-percent construction gate is not met.
- **Changed restriction:** the predecessor's 52-row support cap is removed, while the genuine mask and the two-column limit are kept. The rank-one branch is checked with no column cap.
- **Method and complete domain:** all 112 singleton columns and 6,216 unordered pairs; exact integer minors, rational full-matrix witnesses and a finite projective zero-pattern classification, plus the written proof. No floating-point acceptance and no stochastic search.
- **Optimistic budget:** no physical charge is waived to claim an improvement, and ordinary matrix rank is not recursive child rank. The observable contribution is the exact masked rank boundary, not a packing-cap or κ claim.
- **Nearest work:**
  - PR #1447 proves the 52-by-52 sparse-block theorem and gives an unmasked boundary.
  - This account's PR #1375, and PR #1331, #1432, #1468 and #1473, study COPY costs under factor mixing. PR #1600 uses a binary cut-parent information bill. None classifies arbitrary two-column complex correction ranks.
- **Claim and final check:** the claim is in [discussion #2006](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2006). A final overlap check of the open PRs (368 at 17:15 UTC, complete pagination) and of the changed-file index found no competing work.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-two-column-completion --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-two-column-completion
python3 -I -O -B research/p112-two-column-completion/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/p112-two-column-completion/independent.py
```

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only. The primary checker recomputes the complete certificate. The independent checker imports neither the primary checker nor any predecessor's. It rebuilds the standard E8 roots and their exact isometry to the pinned input, checks 12,544 integer minors and all 2,912 pencils, and recomputes five full correction and completion ranks over Q. Eight built-in rejection controls and eight focused test groups cover source and receipt corruption, a finite-field rank-loss control, 19,683 small determinant fixtures and an exact Gaussian-integer realification test. Both optimized checkers also passed in a read-only relocated tree with every file hash unchanged.

The registered replay was run again on the final package bytes before submission, under an 8 GiB memory cap, and passed.

```text
PASS_P112_TWO_COLUMN_COMPLETION pairs=6216 odd=2912 orthogonal=3304 boundary_rows=53 correction_rank=2 completion_rank=9 controls=8
PASS_P112_TWO_COLUMN_INDEPENDENT integer_minors=12544 pencils=2912 witnesses=5 root_isometry=120
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-two-column-completion outcome=completed
```

## Credit

- woklerx: PR #1447, the sparse-block theorem this extends, and PR #1077.
- DreamingOfClouds (PR #717) and themilkman216 (PR #968): the geometry and model.
- The pinned root-data lineage (PR #523, #514, #507, #425 and #433).
- This account's PR #1375 is a different COPY-cost result.

New material is Apache-2.0; predecessor credit and licenses are kept.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the reasoning, the implementation, the testing and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. No independent human review is claimed.

## Open next questions

From the package README:
1. **Does another exact factorization of the displayed 53-by-2 completion improve on its direct COPY65 bill, perhaps approaching or beating the original COPY64 decoder?** First step: parameterize its rank-nine factors in the fixed nine-dimensional column and row spaces, then check the exact identities and all support-pairing ranks under candidate basis changes. Blocker: the coupled, support-sensitive factor search; rank nine alone proves no COPY saving, and a favorable bill would still need source access, frames, dirty-state restoration, hosting, precision and tape, complete recursive pricing and the inherited all-size and analytic obligations.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

- **What helped:** PR #1447's explicit next question pointed at a precise boundary.
- **Friction:** the physical batching and gather suggestions already have many nearby results, and the predecessor's proposed rank-one 53-by-53 odd rectangle turned out to be impossible, since every odd neighbourhood has size 52.
- **Suggestion:** before advertising a masked support search as an open next question, compute its elementary row and column cardinality constraints; here that check points straight at the useful change (rank two, two columns). Also, keep text overlap queries separate from `--path` queries: combining them suppressed Discussion matches, including this session's own claim.

title: Research: sharp 40-copy floor for the Eisenstein frame decoder with at most eleven totals
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove a sharp obstruction for the fixed Eisenstein orthogonal-frame decoder: **every binary decomposition into at most eleven totals costs at least 40 pairing-rank units**, even with non-clean supports and cancellation. Ten- and eleven-total witnesses attain 40. The inherited supplier screen needs at most 31, so adding one total cannot make this decoder viable.

The general theorem covers any number of orthogonal frames in any positive-definite dimension. Factor ranks reduce one extra total to a single frame-code coset; distinct supports in that coset have pairwise orthogonal geometric complements. Their aggregate rank deficit cannot exceed the ambient dimension. See `PROOF.md` for all hypotheses and cases.

Status: **research note / proved scoped negative result**. Other fitting matrices and twelve or more totals remain open. No supplier, new kappa, unrestricted decoder optimum, or full multiplication theorem is claimed. The selected frontier and upstream files are unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Base: `6aff82d6d346fb2238d061ef45066b82d48a9b67`. Task: `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, refined to this complete one-extra-total class. Actual originating task: `01a1335e-7a24-73c3-a549-9bcb5496a363`; OS seed22 selects the complex track. Source blobs and hashes are in `SOURCES.json`.

[PR798](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/798) supplies the geometry and general pairing-charge model. [PR1794](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1794) supplies the frame witness, clean-class floor and necessary cost screen. This theorem extends beyond clean supports for a fixed decoder and bounds every decomposition with one extra total. [PR1977](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1977), head `ea021c002e61fea7f2f9cd1b613f65b88f7eb7e9`, studies general minrank certificates; this package does not repeat or independently certify that pending result.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/eisenstein-eleven-total-seed22/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_EISENSTEIN_ELEVEN_TOTAL`.

- Exact-integer rank-adjoining traversal and separate modular generator-combination traversal agree on **all 164110 proper support ranks**. The independent traversal examines all 10700 generator sets; a Hadamard bound makes reduction modulo 65537 exact.
- Separate rational elimination checks **9200 complements and 5470 orthogonal pairs** across all 4360 nontrivial cosets.
- A direct four-port outer-product model checks all 225 rectangles and 50625 ordered pairs, recovering all six two-term and 618 three-term decompositions without using the proof reduction.
- Both sharp E8 witnesses, altered-frame/rank controls, normal and optimized CPython 3.15.0 runs, the explicitly pinned 3.12.12 registered replay, metadata/source pins, and read-only relocation pass. On-disk source and receipt corruption fail as intended.
- The inherited necessary-cost screen replays at 31. Selected-record checks and five unit tests pass. The full selected cold replay is not run because its sources are unchanged.

The implementations share pinned geometric input, not traversal or elimination functions. Expected outputs are regression receipts, not independent evidence by themselves. These finite checks corroborate the written argument; they do not prove its universal quantifier. No proof-assistant validation or independent human review is claimed.

## Credit

Jonathan Lam / PR798; GamingPuzzled (Joel Pulikkan) / PR620; Maximooch / PR1794; and Josie Elliston / PR1977. New work is Apache-2.0. Charles Bethin with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, verification and writing.

## Open next questions

A different fitting matrix or at least two extra totals must change the excluded contract. Start by pricing the complete optimistic invoice, then study a two-dimensional factor extension or a changed matrix. No obstruction or successful construction for that larger scope follows here. Details are in `TASK.json` and the package README.

title: Research: sharp mixed UT4 root tariffs with arbitrary dirty workspace
body:
Mixtures of the six noncentral UT4 commutator targets cannot reduce their direct per-letter bill through free scalar mixing or arbitrary restored dirty workspace. This adds the uniform proof and two exact checkers under `research/ut4-mixed-root-tariffs/` only; no selected frontier or frozen source changes.

For targets `u^s_i v^t_i z^h_i`, with u=I+E13, v=I+E24, z=I+E14 and support sets S,T,H, every word in the adjacent-letter alphabet satisfies

```
n_a >= 2|S union H|,
n_b >= 2|S union T union H|,
n_c >= 2|T union H|.
```

All three bounds are attained simultaneously when no role is pure z. This includes same-role uv and central twists uz,vz,uvz. The mixture `(u,v,uv,uz,vz,uvz)` has exact bill `(10,12,10)`, or32 unit calls, for every finite restored dirty workspace. Nonnegative uniform letter tariffs are therefore sharp. The general inequalities remain necessary for pure-z roles, but sharpness is deliberately not claimed for that family.

The paid factors are `I+([g]+1)xy^T` over the **full** F2[UT4(F2)], g in {a,b,c}, all nonzero binary rank-one couplings, including nilpotents. Every undo is charged. Scalar GL mixing is favorably free; address maps, clean allocation and higher-rank unit calls are absent. The proof uses both spans of each label and exact third-order coefficients, then gives full formal attaining words separately.

**Delta and credit.** Adam Gall/PR1935, head9bb74ff3597adfe6949d7b988698b06c0c99978b, already settles disjoint u/v roles and gives a six-call same-role uv fixture. This package adds the sharp overlapping/mixed target family with central twists. It applies ToikY/PR1662's degree-three quotient and middle-span method (head01cc02b164ecc4f9d84df3f56a1fe65b88daf390) and Hanson Sun/PR1607's heterogeneous coefficient-tariff method (head9d6117918025cee6a0c5b7ef30ff8d936ca0621f). Credit steph4n-gh/PR1573, Arham Tahir/PR1589, Cinna Davis/PR1761 and the retained register-model lineage. No new rank principle or literature-priority claim.

**Validation.** Registered CPython3.12.3 full replay passes, including eight control groups. Both checkers also pass isolated optimized read-only CPython3.14.4 relocation, all14 exported files unchanged. Exact evidence: all4,096 group products, all4,913 quotient associativity triples, all20,440 two-role coefficient words through length3, and402 complete formal/faithful operators on99,264 basis columns. The independent implementation derives a rank23 relation space on40 words and uses literal group matrices and faithful regular action; it imports no primary mathematical code. There are40 omitted-call controls plus dirty-kernel, paid-rank, source/receipt and optimization controls. All12 new files reproduce byte-for-byte from the clean patch.

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-mixed-root-tariffs
```

These finite checks support the fixed-group algebra lemma and written all-length/all-workspace proof; they do not extrapolate a universal theorem from a short search. The three conjugated-boundary fixtures explicitly use their conjugated restored complement, rather than claiming restoration of original coordinates.

**Scope and coordination.** One OS draw51b93dabe7190b9eb05c31682dd5750a, priority3 bit-mechanisms / bit-new-register-model; no reroll. Baseec94fd3d2fcad7ade8e72d6bcd8e223b7fdb3f30; current mainc676548106012571fefa1dce0ec16f1bcfe11dce preserves every input, instruction and selected record checked. Final overlap paginated356 open PRs and662 Discussions, no warnings, eight targeted matches all returned. Nearby heads are unchanged and claim [Discussion2019](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2019) had no replies. Search coverage is not a novelty certificate.

Mathematical/published commit `cd37822ee3523e53b645848644e0dae42d47abe7`. Primary canonical receipt `62fc9faf47d09649a98962d35922371368834e0b5452bd888f162213df7104b7`; independent receipt `407d4af5b31fd5bfebdc8cfe3e60201da5c14e662ea03a3530af2290c91eec1a`.

**No new kappa or physical supplier.** Pure-central mixed-family optimality, physical/compiler/common-label realization, hosting, precision/tape, selected cold replay and outer analytic transfer remain unproved or unrun here. - Track: adversarial audit, seed 62.
- Card: `supplier-boundary-audit`, scope **refined**.
- Base: `179089e4`.
- Package: `research/frontier1094-residual-wrappers-seed62/`.

## Why this is needed

Lemma A's exact part (`e8-lemma-a-lean`, `e8-lemma-g-lean/PROOF.md` §4) needs a stored wrapper (L, R) for every helper that enters at a nonzero frame E or ends at a hyperplane U. Each wrapper must satisfy `L ∘ (C_[w] ⊗ I) ∘ R = T_end ∘ T_E⁻¹`. For the selected word these are the 36 records in `RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json` (`383f40aa`).

Tracing the acceptance in the selected chain:
- **The bytes are pinned.** Both the owner audit and the certificate's fresh invoice (`input_sha256.fresh_invoice` → `PREFIX-AND-INVOICE.json` → `providers.gauge44.artifacts`) pin `RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json`. The fresh invoice also pins `WRAPPER-CHECKS.json`.
- **The chain's own audit checks structure only.** `gauge44-slots-t16/code/audit_allcold.py` (lines 56–61) checks only the wrappers' structural fields: frame, terminal, vectors and ranks.
- **Exactness is established only by the producer's own code.** `hpe_adapters_local.py` generates the wrappers and decodes them again with the same `clifford_exact` primitives, writing `WRAPPER-CHECKS.json` (`PASS_RESIDUAL_WRAPPERS_ARE_EXACT`).
  - The cold replay re-runs that producer (e.g. `gauge44-slots/construction/slots/verify_slots.py:103`).
  - No chain code reads the receipt's status or content.
- **Our merged #1781** checked the child and endpoint records but explicitly left these 36 open.

## Result

`PASS_FRONTIER1094_RESIDUAL_WRAPPERS_EXACT`:

| | Records | Kernel B | Kernel A |
|---|---|---|---|
| FULL-ended | 22 | exact | exact |
| Cold hyperplane-end `0:U` | 12 | exact | exact |
| Entering hyperplane-end (`2:999`, `3:998`) | 2 | exact | exact |

Every identity holds on all 512 columns, with the global phase included.

## How

- **Binding.**
  - The merged #1781 binding is imported with its digests pinned: selected record → frontier1094 certificate → capsule → owner audit → word and programs.
  - `RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json` must equal the owner audit's own digest.
  - The `split-centres` decoy has the same basename and is rejected by digest.
  - The certificate's fresh invoice pins both files' bytes.
  - The global8 twin is byte-identical.
- **Inventory.**
  - The 36 keys are exactly the word's entering helpers ending at FULL (key = start) and its hyperplane-ending helpers (key = start:final).
  - Every record's frames, vectors and ranks match the word, and all 72 monomials are well formed.
  - In both programs, each of the 240 wrapped helpers has exactly one `pre` and one `post` residual event, with the correct key. The `pre` comes first and the `post` last.
- **Kernel B** (`closed_form.py`, new, standard library only) works from closed-form amplitudes: the frame operator's closed formula, the closed form of the monomial records, and F_w as a product of √X gates. It uses sparse exact columns and evaluates no gate lists. Before judging any record:
  - its frame operator must reproduce #702's 14 frame-kernel digests and #1415's three operator digests;
  - its monomials and F_w must equal kernel A's on every column.
- **Kernel A** is #1781's packed evaluator. Both kernels must pass every record; RESULT records 36/36 for each.
- **Lean pairs.** `3:998` and `2:999` are field-for-field Exact.lean's pair 2 and pair 3.

## Controls

Each mutation is rejected on every record it applies to:

| Mutation | Rejected |
|---|---|
| Global phase +1 | 36/36 |
| Input character (`linear_Z4 += 2`) | 36/36 |
| CZ term in Q | 36/36 |
| Offset translation | 36/36 |
| Swapped wrappers | 36/36 |
| Width −1 and width +1 | 36/36 each |
| Transposed matrix | 36/36 |
| Hyperplane-end record against FULL | 14/14 |
| FULL-ended wrapper reused for a hyperplane end | 2/2 |
| Another basis of the same span (reordered rows pass) | 2/2 |
| Kernel B phase and width mutants | 8/8 |

The tests also reject:
- the decoy;
- a mismatched invoice;
- a flipped archive byte;
- a dropped `pre` event;
- a wrong event key;
- a wrong record vector.

In the inventory, residual events must be `pre` or `post` only, and every record must have exactly its expected fields.

## Checks run

- `verify.py` passes (about 40 s), and RESULT.json is reproduced byte for byte.
- All 17 tests pass.
- `research_package.py --check-only` passes.
- The registered python3.12 replay gives `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` (48 s).
- These were run on Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.8 (macOS 26.5, arm64).

## Overlap

- **The Lean pairs.** `2:999` and `3:998` are the Exact.lean pairs (#593, with #1415's binding). #1611 had tied `2:999` to pair 3 for this word.
- **The cold rank-4 records.** The eight records `0:124`…`0:327` are byte-identical to records in earlier provider files (e.g. `complex-sw4-frame8-validation`). #702 checked that family's cold wrappers by amplitudes, for PR626.
- **The four cold hyperplane-end records `0:1000`…`0:1003`.** They are hyperplane cases of #1697's audit of all 511 cold hyperplane terminals, which used wrappers generated by its own run.
- **What was producer-only.** The 22 FULL-ended entrance wrappers had only producer evidence.
- **What is new.** All 36 are now checked from the **selected** word's bound bytes, by two kernels, and tied to its programs.
- Open #1964 (ours, from another session) is about Lemma G H1 extended labels and wrapper placement; that is a different obligation.

## Scope

This PR does not show:
- the executor bridge (Lemma G's H1, and rec(A,B) = record circuit);
- the identity adapters;
- Lean proofs beyond the two Exact.lean pairs;
- any new κ.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/frontier1094-residual-wrappers-seed62/verify.py        # about 40 s
python3 -I -B -m unittest discover -s research/frontier1094-residual-wrappers-seed62 -p test_package.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/frontier1094-residual-wrappers-seed62
```

## Credit

- **Lean packages:** Lemma A (#516) and Lemma G (#509), both by DreamingOfClouds and formalizing #484.
- **The wrapper producer:** `hpe_adapters_local.py` (DreamingOfClouds, after PR #458 by chafreaky), using `clifford_exact.py` (icekylinx), which adapts PR425 (jacklightChen).
- **Exact.lean:** jeremykothe2 (#593).
- **Calibration sources:** #1415 (commdata2338) and #702 (BigCactusLabs).
- **Related checks:** #1697 (navinor) and #1611 (bbMisk).
- **The packed kernel and binding:** our #1781.

## Disclosure

Prepared by Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. Parallel read-only scout and judge subagents selected the obligation; both judges ranked it first. The closed-form kernel, the verifier and the controls were then written fresh. A post-PR adversarial review corrected the supplier trace (the fresh invoice pins the receipt's bytes), the overlap and the credits, and added the kernel cross-check and further controls; these are in the second commit. No claim was posted to Discussions. New material is Apache-2.0.

body:

Resolve PR1805's explicit open question 2 for one fixed pair, 277→434, on PR1062's exact 11,500-ADD R439 star word. Three literal splices are fully billed. A naive entry/exit wrap with target-only edits restores helpers but changes 68 target rows (first witness: target111, dirty input434). Correct whole-prefix conjugation costs +9 ADDs; the prepared-middle wrap costs +3. Their local/nine-stage precision bills are 96/182 bits, within the inherited 104/192 guards, and the paid profile/rank mass 5,129 is unchanged. No new κ, cheaper supplier, all-cut/all-pair exclusion or optimality claim.

The new value is the exact composed boundary, cut argument, counterexample and complete invoice. PR1805 already establishes its 65-ADD baseline-pair saving; PR1194 already supplies H2-sem. Those are credited, not claimed anew. The naive case deliberately violates the original constructor's target-only-D precondition; it is not a PR1805 software bug. PR1047 tests a different prepared-middle pair on PR967. All source blobs and hashes are in SOURCES.json. Current-main guidance and selected-result blobs remain unchanged at c676548106012571fefa1dce0ec16f1bcfe11dce.

## Validation

Separate dense GF2 conjugation, set-based column and Fraction rank oracles agree. title: Apply parallel worker memory budgets on Windows
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Native Windows has no `os.sysconf`, so `run_parallel.memory_gib()` returned `None` and the default worker count ignored the documented three-GiB-per-worker budget. On the tested Windows host, the old code chose 32 workers; querying 31.297 GiB of physical RAM now selects 10. The shared `verify_parallel.default_jobs()` also receives the detected capacity.

Use the standard-library `ctypes` binding to `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`, with the SDK's fixed-width fields and initialized structure length. Preserve the POSIX query, explicit `JOBS` overrides and unknown-memory fallback. This restores the existing **total physical memory heuristic**; it is not a free-memory reservation or a hard resource limit. No scientific input, certificate, selected result or kappa changes.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `c676548106012571fefa1dce0ec16f1bcfe11dce`.
- Card: `verifier-engineering / portable-replay`, priority revision 3, scope key `831cc1a3c8f9ff01b197`, chooser nonce `cdb3518b3b43e210c16c478540c21dea`. Scope **refined** to one native Windows resource-detection failure in the existing verification tooling.
- [Coordination claim #2030](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2030).
- The existing worker policy comes from eumemic's #154 and its integrated validation/snapshot hardening. Merged #1298 (`e76026571dbfa7299bf474b941c9abeb5bd556b3`) addresses Windows onboarding encoding/process cleanup in different files.
- Submission refresh at 2026-10-14 17:46-17:51 UTC covered 361 open PR bodies, 676 Discussion records, 362 open-PR file inventories and 1,448 local metadata records, with complete pagination and no warnings. Text search matched only this session's claim; no open PR reported either changed path. These are bounded text/file-list checks, not a novelty guarantee.

## Validation

The new tests produced **five failures against the unchanged base implementation**. After the fix:

| Environment | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows, CPython 3.12.9 | `python -X utf8 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_parallel_memory.py -v` | 11 pass, including the real Windows API |
| Windows, CPython 3.14.2 | Same command | 11 pass |
| Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, CPython 3.12.3 | `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_parallel*.py' -v` | 17 tests, one Windows-only smoke test skipped; all others pass |

Controls cover a fractional capacity above 4 GiB, total versus available memory, API failure with a populated buffer, zero/unknown capacity, CPU and minimum-worker bounds, explicit overrides, and the shared isolated-group budget. The existing Windows-safe scheduler tests also pass (four tests covering overrides, failure propagation, snapshots and invalid CLI/group inputs).

`python -X utf8 -B scripts/research_baseline.py`, `python -X utf8 -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py` and `git diff --check` pass. The source-bound baseline reports the unchanged selected record. No heavy audit workers were launched for the scheduler comparison. Full historical/mathematical replay was not run for this tooling-only change. Hosted CI is separate from these local results.

Hosted CI currently requires maintainer approval: [Verify research artifacts](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38610219719) reports `action_required` with no jobs executed. The local results above do not claim hosted CI success.

## Credit

Retain the existing Apache-2.0 notice and credit eumemic's PR154 worker policy and the integrated maintenance work. API layout and return semantics follow Microsoft's [MEMORYSTATUSEX](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/ns-sysinfoapi-memorystatusex) and [GlobalMemoryStatusEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-globalmemorystatusex) documentation. Prepared for Tairitsu-Aya with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

## Open next questions

This is an existing-tool repair, not a new research package. Accounting for competing processes, free RAM or container/job-object limits would require a separate scheduling-policy change; this patch preserves the current total-memory policy.

body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The bottleneck brief still sends contributors toward an R439 H2/K replacement lemma. Retained work already supplies it: PR #1194 proves the semantic D contract, PR #1311 checks its application to PR #1122's changed-A word, and PR #1806 supplies that exact word's complete finite nine-stage hosted invoice. This change links those results and names the remaining supplier-admission boundary.

**Status:** a navigation repair with a source-bound consistency checker (consolidation track). It changes no mathematical claim, frozen package, selected supplier or paid profile. The original syntactic H2/K flags stay false, and the replacement evidence does not make the word selected.

**The change:**
- `research/r439-semantic-d-navigation/` (six files) maps the five retained PRs and checks their exact heads and credit, the word and receipt bindings, literal versus semantic interface flags, recorded profiles, charged precision and the selected PR589 binding. It imports no predecessor mathematical engine: it checks the consistency of retained evidence, not a new native or hosted execution.
- `docs/research/bottleneck-brief.md`: the H2/K example now routes the reader through the evidence map. For the exact 10,652-ADD word, the remaining step is supplier-admission review under the inherited physical and all-size premises; for a different helper operation, first identify which hypothesis or boundary the existing contract does not cover.
- `docs/research/research-glossary.md`: the "H2/K gap" entry now distinguishes the original syntactic failure from the semantic replacement and its finite hosted follow-up.

**Remaining obligations.**
- Not run: a fresh native replay, hosted emission or audit, full invoice production, an independent moment enclosure or the selected cold replay. Their retained evidence is linked and bound.
- Still inherited: common-frame and label interpretation, all-size compilation, physical hosting, precision and tape, recovery and the analytic premises.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `scope-navigation` / `fff26335d457e528d9c4`, refined to `R439-semantic-D/1062-1122-1194-1311-1806/local-vs-hosted-vs-selected`. Chooser nonce `d2435983b76fd86391c83bd4a80e7e79`, track consolidation, priority revision 3.
- **Base and exact heads:** base `c676548106012571fefa1dce0ec16f1bcfe11dce`; contribution `d9d644185838aa0b126078e2735f3d582b4b1f9d`. All five predecessors are retained on the base, and no pending implementation is adopted:

  | #1122 | `a2551e70fce0cc34348f50f1a94e7cc4c80bbcbf` | Gareth Davidson (@bitplane): A/B/star composition and native evidence |

- **Concrete question:** which local, native and finite hosting obligations of the fixed word have retained evidence, and which adoption obligations remain?
- **Scope status:** refined to one five-PR chain and one onboarding ambiguity, following the card's bounded-family index method. No global survey and no priority revision.
- **Claim audited:** the brief's implied next task of deriving a replacement lemma for this fixed word.
- **Optimistic budget:** no circuit or moment change; the local rank mass stays 5,129 and the selected bit saving is unchanged. The required improvement is an evidence-backed corrected pointer with explicit remaining obligations.
- **Nearest work:** PR #1194, #1311 and #1806 supply the mathematics and the finite invoice and are credited, not repeated. The existing k8-catalogue, transport-domain, E8-decoder and R714 maps cover other interfaces. No open PR touches either document.
- **Claim and final check:** the claim is in [discussion #1796](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1796#discussioncomment-18930573). 1. **For an authorized supplier-admission review, does the exact PR #1122 word satisfy the maintained semantic-interface policy and all inherited physical and all-size obligations?** Start with PR #1194's chronological proof, PR #1311's changed-A bridge and PR #1806's complete invoice, then enumerate the remaining admission requirements. The blocker is accepting and fulfilling those requirements, not another derivation of the same scalar lemma or the finite nine-stage invoice. The unchanged paid profile supplies no exponent improvement.

title: test(connector): add direct C0 operation BFS test for small linear transformations
body:
Contribution: Extended the connector alphabet with a direct source‑to‑target operation (C₀: y₀ += x₀) and demonstrated that, under a unit‑cost model, this can strictly reduce the number of operations needed to realize certain small linear transformations (2 sources, 2 targets).

Evidence: The script research/universal-connector-boundary/comprehensive_test.py enumerates all 16 transformations where each yᵢ is a linear combination of x₀,x₁ (no z or y terms) and z is unchanged. Using BFS over operation sequences {B₀,B₁,A₀,A₁} (without C₀) and {B₀,B₁,A₀,A₁,C₀} (with C₀), it finds multiple transformations where the minimal operation count drops when C₀ is available. Examples:
- y₀ = x₀, y₁ = 0 (masks 01,00): without C₀ = 4 ops, with C₀ = 1 op (saving 3).
- y₀ = x₀, y₁ = x₁ (identity matrix, masks 01,10): without C₀ = 8 ops, with C₀ = 5 ops (saving 3).
- y₀ = x₀+x₁, y₁ = 0 (masks 11,00): without C₀ = 6 ops, with C₀ = 5 ops (saving 1).
The verification script research/universal-connector-boundary/verify.py continues to pass, confirming that the baseline universal‑connector boundary remains intact.

Remaining limitations:
- The test assumes unit cost for each operation; actual pricing in the universal connector boundary may differ, so the cost advantage depends on the relative price of C₀.
- Only the 2‑source/2‑target case was explored; the benefit for larger alphabets (e.g., the 5‑source boundary) remains to be analyzed.
- We have not verified that C₀ satisfies all structural constraints of the universal connector boundary (e.g., legal pricing, restoration properties).

Links: The test scripts are available in the current workspace at:
- research/universal-connector-boundary/comprehensive_test.py
- research/universal-connector-boundary/test_extension.py (initial simple test)

Process followed:
1. Read AGENTS.md and autoresearch.md to understand task selection and overlap rules.
2. Ran python3 -u -B scripts/choose_research_task.py → suggested task connector-alphabet-change.
3. Checked overlap with python3 -u -B scripts/find_overlap.py --task connector-alphabet-change (found only local README overlap, as expected).
4. Executed the first step (python3 -u -B research/universal-connector-boundary/verify.py) to confirm the baseline.
5. Conducted the first experiment: added one operation (C₀) and tested a tiny dirty‑input instance (identity matrix for 2 sources/2 targets) – saw a cost reduction.
6. Expanded to a comprehensive enumeration of all 2‑source/2‑target transformations, demonstrating systematic savings.
7. Created a focused branch, added the test files, committed with an atomic milestone scope, and pushed the branch.

title: Tooling: faster partial-swap SharedPoint verify digests and __init__ construction with identical receipts
body:
## Change and scope

At base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`, the partial-swap fork (`scripts/partial_swap/shared.py`) spends substantial wall time in two places on the historical `h=46` circuit:

1. `SharedPointCircuit.verify` — per-node / per-output `json.dumps` while building `circuit_sha256`
2. `SharedPointCircuit.__init__` — per-common sort/unpack/lookup in the merge/lookup loop

This PR applies the same byte-identical hand-rolled digest formatter used on the canonical producer in [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1994](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1994), then ports the merge/lookup construction rewrite from [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#2054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2054) onto this distinct producer fork (including `point_order` / sorted `pair_ids`). Support checks stay; `circuit_sha256` and the constructed DAG stay fieldwise identical. `certificates/partial-swap-network.json` updates only the `scripts/partial_swap/shared.py` `source_sha256` pin **once** for the combined file.

**Tooling improvement; no new kappa.** Selected frontier untouched.

## Result

On Linux / CPython 3.12.3 (Linux-6.12.94+-x86_64-with-glibc2.39), five alternating fresh-process pairs:

| Path | Median before → after |
|---|---|
| `partial_swap.shared.SharedPointCircuit(46).verify` | **2.176 → 1.050 s (2.07×)** |
| `partial_swap.shared.SharedPointCircuit(46)` construction | **0.771 → 0.523 s (1.47×)** |
