Independently corroborate the anti-Fano minimum raw pairing cost of 12, answering item 1 of the [independent-check request](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18934590).

```text
pinned twelve-line configuration
  -> three universal triangular minors
  -> 786,432 column-basis assignments and 12,288 row-basis assignments
  -> one rank-three completion per coordinate block
  -> credited exchange argument plus an admissible (4,4,4) witness
  -> minimum raw cost 12
```

The new package is `research/antifano-subspace-audit/`. It replaces the SAT uniqueness step of DreamingOfClouds' #2111 with two complete standard-library subspace censuses. No predecessor implementation is imported. The configuration, license and source notice are retained unchanged.

- #2111: `98da76c2839ba38538b510420dec54546ccabf0b`, configuration and credited exchange argument.
- #2162: `113a718265c62aec301c5695f4bfb9c421bef7ab`, configuration source and alternate jet proof.

The original `bit-helper-contract` draw is explicitly marked as a changed scope after existing H2/K and profile-audit coverage was found. This is an independent decoder-floor audit, not a helper-contract advance.

## Evidence

Before, #2111's uniqueness step used SAT factorization and enumeration. After, independent packed-column and packed-row implementations agree entrywise after complete finite censuses, without SAT, jet or floating-point dependencies.

title: Prove selected BIT packet integration and live-row layout
body:
I prove a selected BIT integration lemma over GL64(Z/q^w): complete local words preserve their COPY/ERASE guards and hosted endpoints when the caller batches all high matrices for one low cover class. I also give an explicit live-row layout that preserves the selected child-volume denominator and supplies complete descendant stock.

The packet distinction matters. Two owners can differ at each fixed matrix while their full high packets coincide. I prove low-packet separation for the selected helper completions and add an exact alias countermodel. I also reject transpose and reorthogonalization shortcuts that pass modulo 3 but fail over Z/9.

Evidence:

- 4,668 split-rank cases, 14,370 weighted transports and 181,056 selected same-family owner pairs.
- A sequential restricted-fibre XOR over all 3,888 GL2(Z/9) rows, moving 198,288 payload bits while preserving the other 47 low packets.
- An explicit mixed-radix layout with `lcm(28416,28425)`, complete child stock and the exact live denominator `28416*|GL64(Fq)|`.
- Registered Python 3.12 replay passed normally and with `-O`; source pins and deterministic receipt comparison passed.

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-local-ring-sweeps
```

I reuse alephnan's [PR1627](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1627) literal audit and whole-call proof, and credit eumemic's [PR490](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/490) for the generic GL argument. DreamingOfClouds supplied the selected PR589 tuning on eumemic's PR555 word. The package records exact predecessor heads, including the recent routing, stock, weighted-child and fallback work. I also credit commdata2338's concurrent [PR2188](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2188) mixed diagonal-pair descriptor and retain its remaining shear/physical integration question.

title: Research: exact S5 inverse 5-cycle minimum is eight
body:
## Scope and result

**Scoped exact minimum of eight paid factors; no new kappa.** In the full group algebra `F2[S5]`, generated by the four adjacent transpositions `s1=(12), s2=(23), s3=(34), s4=(45)`, the target `diag([c],[c^-1])`, where `c=s1*s2*s3*s4` is a 5-cycle, has no word of length at most seven in the 24-factor alphabet

```text
D_N(si) = I + ([si] + [1]) N,
```

with all six rank-one idempotents `N` in `M2(F2)` allowed for each generator. The direct independent-coordinate construction uses eight factors, so the exact minimum in this two-register formal model is eight. Equality in the full group algebra certifies the action on arbitrary dirty inputs for these two registers.

The complete radius-seven meet-in-the-middle search builds the prefix ball through length three and suffix ball through length four. It covers 14,425 raw prefix words and 346,201 raw suffix words before deduplication; the exact balls contain 6,505 and 93,121 matrix states. It finds zero target hits. The certificate records every per-depth state count and digest. All 24 factors are checked involutive; a planted three-call target is recovered; reverse-orientation, dropped-factor, and wrong-generator controls pass.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -I -B research/s5-inverse-fivecycle-seed52bf211c/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/s5-inverse-fivecycle-seed52bf211c --check-only
```

Both commands passed locally under CPython 3.14.7. The package metadata and source-pin check passed. The registered package runner requests Python 3.12, which is unavailable locally.

## Pins, costs, and limits

- Seed: `52bf211cbbc5cdf54a9c9460f2174659`; task `bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 4.
- Exact scientific base: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`.
- Selected-result SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Catalogue SHA-256: `d46eb6d5b3e279428753d770653663fbdf1063e55c255ea073d768f344927ef7`.
- Direct paid bill: eight factors; a shorter word would save one call, or 12.5%. The formal alphabet has no helper, recursive, frame, copy, restoration, precision, or hosting operations, so those costs are absent by definition.
- Merged PR #1911 proves sharp bills for two paid reflection labels in `D_infinity`; its Laurent argument does not descend to finite quotients. The completed free-group inverse-commutator claim in Discussion #1997 was released as implied by that theorem. This package uses four paid Coxeter generators in finite `S5`, which that two-label theorem does not cover.
- No native supplier mapping or selected-bound improvement is claimed. Physical implementation, precision, hosting, and assembly remain outside this formal model.

title: Bound QQ16 private d_A retention at the B1 cut
body:
## Result

This is a scoped negative result for one proposed QQ16 interface mechanism: retaining the post-`B_1_2` eight-coordinate `d_A = Y_A` observation in the existing owned fields `C0..C7`.

At the exact pinned cut, the private fields return in frame I, while the eight A-port Y outputs have frames `f117, f124, f137, f144, f153, f163, f174, f228`, each with 18 nonzero Z4 terms. An exact scan of all 3,650 registered cover maps finds no one-map normalization to I. In the one-term native-line model, matching the eight private fields to the source frames requires at least 144 rank-one line calls, with 288 associated full-cover map operations. The eight coefficient-one scalar copies cost 32 real scalar primitives. Terminal cleanup adds eight clear primitives; a following retained core can reuse its existing clears.

The current favorable rank-eight output envelope in [Discussion #2074](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2074) leaves at most two further rank-one-equivalent calls above the selected ceiling. The 144-line floor exceeds that planning allowance before charging the record handling, physical address/stream costs, global hosting, or recursive precision. This is scoped to the pinned single-map search and one-term line conversion model; it does not rule out a multi-map route or another state layout. No controller or new κ is claimed.

title: Negative result: calls-only centre-source rank census across all 144 selected calls (PR2048 Q2; no new kappa)
body:
**Status: Negative result** (scoped negative result / research note). This is a finite certificate in a declared scalar projection. It is not a native obstruction, not a formal proof and not a new kappa. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Summary

This addresses open question 2 of PR2048 (pairs whose centre sources depend on each other in time). PR1918's common-frame scalar projection is extended from one disjoint-data forward pair to **all 144 selected `local_cover_sweep` calls** (80 forward, 64 backward). The calls run in `execution_schedule` order from a formal vector over the 14,336 physical owners. **Only the calls run.** Bridge, idle_cover_sweep, terminal, padding and translate events are not executed; the number of them between the two calls of each dependent pair is counted.

New package: `research/selected-centre-chrono-source-census/` (verify.py, RESULT.json, README, TASK.json, SOURCES.json, VERIFY.json). No other files are changed.

Results, all in this projection:

1. **Global formal rank 1152/1152**, exact over Q and also mod 2^61-1 (forward 640, backward 512). No centre-source row is a linear combination of other calls' rows. This statement covers the formal rows only. It does **not** give PR1918's lemma bound (d >= rank) for groupings of calls. That bound would need a fixed-dirt, source-only output-increment rank on separate output panels, and this package computes neither. Some centre-scatter panels overlap.
2. **All 1,539 dependent pairs have rank 16.** The pairs are those that share roles 0..111 owners (96), pass a write to a later read (the same 96), or share formal support (1,525). Each has rank 16 formally and again when restricted to its own roles 0..223 owners. No deficient pair exists.
3. **PR1918's roles 0..111 column restriction does not hold up for dependent pairs.** On that restriction, 671 of 1,539 pairs fall below 16: all 96 shared-data pairs (six classes, rank 8 each), and 51 pairs at rank 0. For backward calls, roles 0..111 are the block the call writes, not source data. For the 16 same-block f0->b1 pairs, the verifier certifies `backward1 centre k |_D = (1/4) forward0 centre k |_D` with exact kernel witnesses. It also certifies that **zeroing only the target block keeps rank 16**, because forward0 also reads helper roles. So this identity is not a reuse lead on its own.
4. Two diagnostics fall outside the template semantics. Zeroing owners first touched as helpers drops the global rank to 570; zeroing owners not first touched in roles 0..111 drops it to 418. The full-rank result therefore depends on owner contents that the omitted events change.

## Reproduce

Base commit `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. Standard library only, about 30 s and under 200 MB of RSS. Verified under Python 3.14.4 only. The package hook declares Python 3.12 and was **not** run, because 3.12 was unavailable.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/selected-centre-chrono-source-census/verify.py
```

Expected output:

```text
PASS_SELECTED_CENTRE_CHRONO_SOURCE_CENSUS calls=144 rows=1152 global_rank_q=1152 global_rank_mod_p=1152 dependent_pairs=1539 formal_pair_rank_hist={'16': 1539} pair_local_rank_hist={'16': 1539} deficient_formal_or_pair_local=0 f0_b1_same_block_data_only_ranks=[(8, 16)] f0_b1_target_zeroed_ranks=[(16, 16)] controls=8
```

Pins (full digests and Git blobs are in SOURCES.json):
- `research/community-frontier1094-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz`: `f1da80610bf33c58527f18ad63b4350d0b864e1d4486141ee17ac9bed4d529d6`. Its members GLOBAL-TEMPLATE, LOCAL-PROGRAMS and CANONICAL-WORD are pinned in verify.py.
- `certificates/selected-result.json`: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- PR1918 receipt `research/selected-centre-composed-source-rank/RESULT.json`: `31555505a5eea8e54b3b04c67e4aefa495101f3b43d7fe9fa8dca90776dea668`.
- Each call is bound to its program through `local_program_sha256`.

Other checks: `scripts/research_package.py --check-only` gives PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS, and `unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` passes (65 tests, OK, skipped=2).

## Certificates and negative controls

**Internal controls**, run on every verification:
- PR1918's 16 source maps, rank 16 and roles 0..111 rank 16 are reproduced exactly.
- Duplicated rows give rank 8, and reversed-order rows give rank 8.
- The forward centre copies equal `word.centers = [92,57,81,224,11,240,9,256]`.
- A perturbed backward coefficient changes the program binding and changes or rejects the local map.
- Omitting one backward centre gather changes the centre input.
- Omitting the final private clear is rejected as a dirty exit.
- A one-bit flip changes the archive and member hashes. This is a hash-sensitivity check only.

**External controls**, run in scratch copies. Each was rejected as required:
- Tampered `global_rank_q`: `result receipt differs`.
- Tampered kernel-witness coefficient: `result receipt differs`.
- Tampered new target-zeroed rank field: `result receipt differs`.
- Flipped archive byte: `pin mismatch`.
- Edited PR1918 receipt: `pin mismatch`.

**Independent reviewer replay**, separate code using prime 2^31-1 and a different pivot order. It reproduced the global rank 1152, both endpoint transvections and the 1/4 identity. A semantic input mutation, swapping two owners in the last backward call with the archive re-pinned, was caught by the receipt check.

## Scope, inherited assumptions, unresolved obligations

**Inherited from PR1918:**
- clear, copy, scale and add are exact over Q;
- climb, adapter and residual_adapter act as the identity;
- the `center` event is the read cut;
- owners hold independent formal initial values.

**Not executed:** bridges (144), idle cover sweeps (160), terminal events, padding and translate. The native schedule is not a specialization of these formal variables, so the full-rank statements could fail natively, and the deficient restricted statistics could be higher or lower natively.

**Still open:**
- an owner-level replay of the bridge and idle events;
- the fixed-dirt source-only rank and panel separation that any grouping bound needs;
- a native 512-address lift (PR2048-style) of the D-block identity;
- a full storage, transport, restoration, hosting and precision invoice for any reuse.

No kappa follows from any outcome.

## Search record

- **Domain:** all 144 calls and 1,152 rows. All C(144,2) pairs were screened for the three dependency classes, giving 1,539 dependent pairs.
- **Ranking:** each dependent pair was ranked exactly over Q under five variants, plus a target-zeroed variant for f0->b1.
- **Seed:** sprint seed 50 chose the track only; the census itself has no randomness.
- **Stopping rule:** complete coverage, about 30 s, so no stop rule fired.
- **Pair loop:** the same-orientation pair loop was not needed, because full global rank implies full rank for every subset of rows.

"No deficient pair" holds in this projection only. It is not an impossibility theorem.

## Credit and overlap

- **Predecessor:** PR1918 (Adam Gall) supplied the projection, the replay logic and the lemma. This package reimplements the replay and pins PR1918's receipt.
- **Open question:** taken from open PR2048 (commdata2338).
- **Related work:**
  - PR2076 and #2058 (1337isnot1337), early-fanout and zero-storage; the census planned there was never run.
  - PR1829 (Cinna Davis) and #1963, owner aliasing.
  - #1986 (1337isnot1337), the same f0/b1 boundary studied as an F2 frame intersection.
  - Sharing budgets: PR1708 (1337isnot1337), PR1748 (ToikY), PR1791 (rtyu193-rgb), PR1664 (An664) and PR1888 (RossRichardson).
  - The selected #1094 lineage (Rohan Arun et al.).
- **Concurrent work:** a sibling local session drafted a similar card and aborted it unclaimed; nothing from it was reused.
- **What this adds:** the earlier work covers one disjoint-data forward pair. This package covers the dependent and shared-source class (mostly mixed orientation) and the global rank, and it records where the roles 0..111 restriction stops being robust.
- **Review:** three independent AI-assisted reviews (reproducibility, mathematical audit, provenance) were run before submission. The audit corrected the interpretation of results 1 and 3.

Sprint track: recursive interfaces (50-59), OS seed 50. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163#discussioncomment-18935621

Contributor: @thakrarsagar, with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code) running in an automated sprint loop. No independent human proof review is claimed. Licence: Apache-2.0.

title: Research: all-depth QQ16 cover-map parity floor at B1 cut
body:
## Scope and result

**Scoped all-depth obstruction; no new kappa.** At the exact post-`B_1_2` QQ16 cut, the eight `Y_A` output frames each have 18 odd Z4 terms, while the existing private fields `C0..C7` return in the zero frame. Every registered cover map applies an invertible binary owner transform and adds only coefficient 2. Modulo two, the payload shift vanishes and the owner transform preserves odd-support size. Therefore every finite composition of cover maps leaves all eight frames at odd-support weight 18; this rules out depth-one, depth-two, depth-three, and longer map-only normalization.

In the declared one-term native-line model, one rank-one correction changes at most one parity bit. Reaching the private zero frames requires at least 18 corrections per output, or **144 rank-one line calls** total. This exceeds by 72 times the favorable budget of at most two extra rank-one-equivalent operations after the rank-eight output charge. The bill also includes 288 associated full-cover map operations, eight scalar copies priced at 32 real primitives, and up to eight terminal clear primitives (zero additional clears if the existing next core follows). Further map implementation, hosting, source routing, and precision charges cannot lower the line floor.

This extends the released one-map / one-term result in PR #2197 with an all-depth invariant. It is limited to the pinned eight frames, registered invertible cover maps, and one-term Z4 corrections. Alternate field layouts and multi-term native operations remain open. No full controller, supplier admission, or selected-bound change is claimed.

## Exact evidence and reproduction

The source-pinned verifier reconstructs the eight port frames from the native recipes, checks all 3,650 owner maps for rank 73, applies every map to every port frame (29,200 checks), and validates a two-map positive control. Negative controls demonstrate that an odd coefficient shift could cancel a parity bit and that a singular owner map violates the invariant's hypothesis.

title: Research: exact rank-three common-sum anchor screen
body:
## Result

Adds an exact reversible **rank-three common-sum output anchor** for `q=2..112` and screens two disjoint `q=112` blocks against the pinned selected local-word ceiling. This is a local construction and conditional moment result. It does **not** claim selected-provider placement, a new `κ`, or a tensor-rank minimum.

For each block, the clean anchor is `F0=x0*y0+x1*y1+x2*y2`; each dirty output receives `F0+x_(i+2)*y_(i+2)`. The schedule uses 114 rank-one products and 111 explicit affine fanout additions, versus 447 rank-one products for separate evaluation. Two blocks save 666 rank-one products. Exact profile screening gives about a 14.2% ceiling gain; 411 added rank-one-equivalent child charges still pass the pinned 5% gate and 412 fail. Fanout ADDs remain a separate cost line.

## Evidence and reproduction

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-rank3-anchor-seed3f73/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-rank3-anchor-seed3f73 --check-only
```

Expected direct result:

```text
PASS_RANK3_SUM_ANCHOR q=2..112 products=114 fanouts=111 two_blocks_saved=666 cap_extra=411/412 local_only
```

The verifier symbolically checks forward and reverse schedules for every `q=2..112`, exhausts all 32,768 `q=4` input/dirty-output states, rejects three malformed controls, and recomputes exact rational ceiling brackets and the 411/412 boundary. The package pins the selected result, review, source manifest, assembly certificate, catalogue, and ceiling implementation. Local replay used Python 3.14.7; repository generic replay uses Python 3.12 and will provide the hosted run.

## Scope and limits

The provider source map is not established. A realization must bind products to the selected gauge44 program and invoice source access, helper operations, frame changes, copying, hosting, precision, restoration, interface transitions, and the 222 fanout ADDs before this profile can affect the selected construction. title: Research note (no new κ): orthogonal-pair bit decoders in the frozen PR555 L3 family — P102 unreachable, real helper counts erase the eleven-stage gain
body:
**Status: research note and scoped negative result (bit supplier). No new κ, no supplier change, and no selected-record edit.**

## Question

PR1084 (`research/bit-orthogonal-pair-decoders`, navinor) showed that a decoder term with orthogonal punctured reader and source lines costs 6 instead of 7. It reached P102 (cst 54) over all 120 lines, but left two open points:
- At nine stages, the inventory R = 439 exceeds the hosting wall 4v = 408.
- The shipped PR589 puncture admits only one such pair (P110).

This PR asks a narrower question. Inside the family that actually built the selected bit word (PR555's `gen_p3` on PR543's frozen L3 plan), how many cost-6 terms can a legal reader set reach? And what are the resulting units worth at the nine-stage template and at PR555's eleven-stage template, once hosting, idle children and the generator's real helper inventory are all priced?

## Result

1. **P102 is unreachable in this family; the maximum is j = 5 (P106).**
   - The frozen plan has 19 eligible pseudo-target lines. Of the C(18,9) = 48,620 subsets, 17,478 are admissible.
   - The root-dual count j is distributed `{0:4515, 1:7975, 2:3977, 3:929, 4:77, 5:5}`.
   - The shipped P has j = 1 (pair 66–87, i.e. PR1084's P110).
   - A second implementation, written before reading the first, agrees on all 127 compared fields.
2. **At R = 439, eleven stages would look favorable, but that premise is false.**
   - Eleven stages host every unit whole (11R ≤ 64v).
   - At R = 439 the j = 5 sets would gain +1.94% to +1.97% over the selected bit c.
   - Real `gen_p3` builds of 4,989 reader sets need R(P) = 446–472 helpers, against 439 for the shipped set. PR555's `choose.py` minimised exactly these extra carriers.
   - With their own R(P), all 82 j ≥ 4 sets price between **−2.78% and −0.21%**.
   - None of the 2,785 built j = 2/3 sets passes the nine-stage wall (min R 446 > 436 for j = 2; 448 > 432 for j = 3).
3. **The only hostable gain is the shipped P110 at nine stages, +0.70%.** That is below PR1084's recorded P104 line (+1.3294%) and below the same P104 gain re-based to the current selected complex b (+1.9829%, a stated transfer premise). The bit side does not bind today; its headroom is 3.46%.

Exact parts:
- the census;
- template parameters and walls;
- the certified idle optima and window max-flow;
- every c, as a certified lower bound from the pinned selected-record engine.

Positive controls reproduce, exactly:
- PR589 at nine stages and at eleven stages;
- PR555 at eleven stages;
- a byte-for-byte rebuild of PR555's word.

## Premises and open obligations

- No P(111−j) word with punctured duals is built, and `gen_p3` does not model dead non-reader lines.
- The asymmetric rank-6 COPY (PR620) is unrealised.
- Profiles are PR589-based proxies with an average-helper shift for R ≠ 439. The margin to the nearest threshold is at least 1.5 percentage points.
- The receiver search is bounded, not a proof of minimal R.
- j = 2/3 coverage is time-capped at 281/929 and 2,504/3,977 sets, with a two-receiver screen over all 4,906.
- Eleven-stage use would need a new assembly receipt.
- The census fixes the label-reader basis.

This is a finite result for the frozen plan, not an impossibility theorem for orthogonal-pair decoders. The README lists three open next questions: a jointly optimised plan, realising the shipped P110 word, and pricing the built-word profiles.

## Reproduce

From the repository root (Python 3.10+, standard library only, about 100 s):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-orthogonal-pair-stage-screen/screen.py --check
```

Expected last line begins `PASS_BIT_ORTHOGONAL_PAIR_STAGE_SCREEN rows=44 enum11=82 ...` and ends `| own_R: L11 j>=4 82/82 hostable, >=P104 0/82, >=rebased 0/82, best -0.211302% at R=451 ... checks=57`. It runs `census.py --check`, `independent_census.py` and `price.py`, and requires each of their PASS lines.

The build receipt `CARRIERS.json.gz` is regenerated by `carriers.py`. That needs numpy (2.5.4, verified PyPI wheel) and took 1,142 s on 4 workers; the README gives the exact command.

Checks run locally:
- All four scripts pass on CPython 3.14.4.
- `scripts/research_package.py --check-only` gives `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.
- The 65 `test_research_*.py` tests pass (2 skipped).
- The registered Python 3.12 replay was **not** run, because 3.12 is not installed here. The scripts parse under the 3.10 grammar.

title: QQ16: add an F0-B1 selected-state shear
body:
## New mechanism

This package tests the reversible selected-state shear

```text
X_T <- X_T + X_A
Y_T <- Y_T - X_A
```

between the fixed QQ16 F0 and B1 calls. It preserves each selected `X_T+Y_T` sum and uses existing fields. The exact source-pinned group-algebra replay propagates all eight directions of the retained selected-input erasure witness through B1. Without the shear the T output has rank 0; with it the T output has rank 8. The package includes a nonsingular exact 8-row minor with determinant `-1/4096` and its owner-map keys and rational coefficients.

This establishes a local interface mechanism for the fixed witness family. It does not establish that later events preserve these values, a complete controller, a supplier, or a new κ.

## Cost and validation

The shear adds 16 scalar additions per owner at the common `completed(0)` data frame. It uses no new helper, owner map, precision, temporary storage, or recursive child. It preserves selected sums and leaves the inherited helper-restoration contract unchanged.

Reproduce from the repository root:

body:
## Scope and evidence

**Research consolidation; no new $\kappa$.** Assigned by `scripts/choose_research_task.py` without rerolling (OS-random seed `a690c28b61e61a128b496b24d98aba3b`, track `consolidation`, task `overlap-receipt`, scope key `757723e3fd38f20fa774`), refined to Rohan Arun's (#211, head `c63e50a5dde96fe1459d6b29e55e47f42f104347`) complete 25-path / 13-direct-file source retention across incorporated #205, #210, and #217, Round-9 certificate reconciliation, and missing credit restoration in `CONTRIBUTORS.md`.

At base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, `docs/research/pr-ledger.json` lists #211 as `partially_reviewed` with `integration_location: []` because #211 was in draft state when the `next100` batch (`#153–#303`) selected 100 non-draft PRs—even though #211 had already passed `complete-changed-work-replay-passed` at the exact same head in `research/community-round9-audit/review-ledger.json` and its 6,191 cascade-optimized frame bases were incorporated into 42+ downstream PRs (`#210`, `#216`, `#217`, `#221`, `#227`, ...), with zero mentions of #211 in `CONTRIBUTORS.md`.

### What `research/pr211-retention-receipt` authenticates and reconciles

1. **Complete 25-path / 13-direct-file Git tree and blob proof (`SOURCE-PROOF.json`, 41 raw Git objects):**
   - **12 inherited #205 paths (`3b6b66891c..95c58706ad`):** All 11 files in `research/packed-diagonal-bit` (subtree `409a4737d6ca0aa6c59f40b732c5d4608e705246`) and `.github/workflows/packed-diagonal-bit.yml` (`b00ddc44b8f866f57a62a82dd7ba6b43894301b6`) are inherited unchanged from incorporated parent #205 (`95c58706ad231d532bd7038308946a0344d08186`, direct parent of `archive/pr-reconciliation-next100-20261013` `bd1b279e5e5449f81ca262c1647961e81dd69e50`).
   - **13 direct #211 paths (`95c58706ad..c63e50a5dd`):** #211 adds `research/cascade-frames-bit` (subtree `1708e493cbb1931e4fd11eca058b72193dfec3ac`, 12 files) and `.github/workflows/cascade-frames-bit.yml` (`aed05819ec6a716b8de02d243b447031ef1309a1`):
     - `opframe-bases.json` (4,977,602 B, Git blob `8433d7724cbed83401fa42beee8653c62657ec0d`, SHA256 `56b2ed0f6b867e8cafdc32ac70419cfda36d02838844572098b3fc77f8026e58`) is retained byte-identically in incorporated #210 (`b0c058ba979c748bb3a8604bfb6502e9fac9b84d:research/coordinated-crossover-pr200/search/pr211-frames.json`) and as gzip+base64 (`6b3b66eaa484a50f1f45ab9f7515a1b4ff26897f`) in incorporated #217 (`b739fc226a54a4a507989aa1bef092d491287451:research/butterfly-coordinated-bit-211/opframe-bases.json.gz.b64`), whose decompressed payload matches both digests identically.
     - `NOTICE` (`9edc2572378be7a7819f229de985eeaffa1173b6`), `banks.py` (`6505ebd37e3414016168511cca7c2f69216cc9f1`), and `controls.py` (`51235415282f631caa4402e80b72f84915ff977d`) match their retained copies in #205 (and `NOTICE` is also retained in #210, #217, and `UPSTREAM-NOTICE`).
     - All 9 remaining direct files (96,628 B total) are stored as authenticated raw Git blobs in `SOURCE-PROOF.json`.
2. **Saved-certificate and child-histogram reconciliation (`verify.py`, `RESULT.json`):**
   - Verifies all 6,191 replacement frame bases in `opframe-bases.json` (distinct operation indices in `0..40,265`, dimensions `3..21`, 65,501 total rows of length `h = 24`).
   - Reconciles all 5 sections of `fresh` (`admitted`, `physical`, `arithmetic`, `independent`, `bank_controls`) in `research/community-round9-audit/pr211-changed.log.txt` against #211's `certificate.json` (`pinned_bit_files = 2,242`).
   - Verifies the 34-sink terminal delta (`{"3": -102, "21": -102}`, rank reduction `2,448` from `1,486,160` to `1,483,712`), the internal/target physical histogram decomposition, the unpacked child-histogram delta `du` from #205 to #211 (`+531` children on internal ranks `1..19` in multiples of `3`, `0` rank-mass delta), and the 3-copy banked delta `dp = 3 * du` (`+1,593` children, `0` rank-mass delta at `W = 56,402`, `rank_mass = 4,055,136`, `deficit = 5,808`).
   - Re-verifies the 3-level ordinary-leaf rational recurrence and balanced assembly grid ceiling (`\kappa = 683847872495777/10^{18} > \kappa_{\text{PR207}} > \kappa_{\text{PR205}}$).
3. **Attribution repair (`CONTRIBUTORS.md`):**
   - Adds a concise credit paragraph for Rohan Arun's #211 alongside the existing #99/#1015 retention paragraphs without altering ledger dispositions or `certificates/selected-result.json`.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr211-retention-receipt --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr211-retention-receipt
```

Runs the standalone offline checker (`PASS_PR211_RETENTION_AND_CERTIFICATE_RECONCILIATION paths=25 direct=13 frames=6191 child_delta=531 mass_delta=0`) and 19 unit tests (1 positive case + 18 corruption, coverage, provenance, frame-base, and accounting rejection controls) under `-I -O -B`.

Original notice preserved verbatim in `UPSTREAM-NOTICE`.
